title: Use of artificial intelligence and other data-driven technologies for coastal management
abstract: Biogeochemical cycles occur naturally in coastal regions. Estuaries, wetlands, and tidal creeks assist these cycles. Since increased anthropogenic activities and naturally occurring events act as stressors, they impact physical, chemical, and biological processes in maritime spaces and hence these cycles. This makes existing ecosystems susceptible to trophic imbalance. Resultantly, researchers began monitoring and mapping coastal environments to understand how different stressors impact these biogeochemical processes using numerical and empirical models. abstract: Introduction Construction delays remain a challenge in projects, often resulting in cost overruns, disputes, productivity losses, and schedule inefficiencies. Growing project complexity has increased the need for data-driven approaches to delay analysis and management. This study reviews the application of artificial intelligence in construction delay analysis and management by examining application areas, techniques, project contexts, implementation maturity, and research gaps. abstract: Marine biofouling causes significant economic and environmental impacts by increasing drag, fuel consumption, emissions, maintenance costs, and material degradation. abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are changing Library and Information Science (LIS) by impacting on user services, cataloguing, and information retrieval; however, the literature on how this is happening has not been systematically catalogued. abstract: Sea surface temperature (SST) sits at the centre of the climate system, but estimating it accurately is hard because the oceanographic processes that drive it interact in complex, non-linear ways. abstract: Artificial intelligence has moved from science fiction into the clinic with remarkable speed. Machine learning systems now read medical scans, flag sepsis before symptoms declare themselves, draft clinical notes, and coach patients through their smartphones. abstract: Urbanization, climate change, increasing energy demand, and rapid infrastructure development have created significant challenges for achieving sustainable and resilient cities. title: Inter‐Comparison of Snow Depth Over Antarctic Sea Ice From Ocean Reanalyzes and Observations
abstract: Abstract Snow depth on Antarctic sea ice is a critical climate variable affecting energy and mass balance, yet its observation and modeling remain challenging. We present a systematic intercomparison of snow depth from six ocean reanalysis products, two satellite retrievals, and ship‐based and airborne observational constraints. Results indicate that reanalysis and satellite products show consistent large‐scale climatological snow depth patterns, with the highest depths in the Weddell Sea. However, substantial differences remain in magnitude, seasonal phasing, spatial variability, and trends.

abstract: This research analyzes the risks that the development and use of artificial intelligence (AI) may pose to the protection of human rights. Born from a persistent observation in the teaching of research methodology, it approaches the archive not as a mere repository of sources but as an operative category that condenses tensions between tradition and creation, canon and heterogeneity, epistemic authority and critical dimension. abstract: Flood-prone Bangladesh requires accurate short-term rainfall prediction, yet conventional numerical weather prediction (NWP) models remain computationally intensive and regionally limited in skill. abstract: In March 2026, the Wakashio-maru, a new training vessel for the National Institute of Technology, Toyama College, was completed. Operating primarily in Toyama Bay, which features deep-sea areas exceeding 1,000 metres, the vessel continues a tradition of marine surveys and observation activities carried out for many years by its predecessor. abstract: Fault slip modeling, based on laboratory-derived friction laws, has significantly enhanced our understanding of fault mechanics. abstract: Reliable detection of lit fishing vessels from night-time satellite observations is essential not only for monitoring fishing activity but also for investigating the distribution of fishery resources when integrated with marine environmental information. However, false detections caused by anthropogenic coastal illumination remain a major challenge for vessel detection using observations from the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS). abstract: ABSTRACT The genus Streptomyces is well known as a prolific source of many bioactive compounds. This review outlines the principles of Raman spectroscopy and its application to bacterial systems, with particular emphasis on the secondary metabolites produced by Streptomyces . Streptomyces are unparalleled chemical factories, producing over two‐thirds of all naturally derived antibiotics and bioactive molecules. title: Sudden collapse of ice mélange under increasing submarine melt at tidewater glaciers
abstract: Rapid ice loss from the Greenland Ice Sheet is responsible for roughly 20% of global sea level rise since 2002. Almost half of this loss is moderated by the presence of ice mélange, which influences glacial calving and melt rates. However, the seasonal to interannual drivers of ice mélange extent and collapse are poorly understood. Observations show a spread of behavior for ice mélange in different Greenland fjords, ranging from seasonal collapse each spring over a few days to perennial persistence. abstract: Coral reefs support marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of coastal communities, yet their condition in Indonesia, including Bali, continues to decline due to coral bleaching. Bleaching monitoring still relies largely on manual surveys that are time-consuming, costly, and require trained experts. This study develops a YOLOv10-based object detection model with transfer learning to automatically detect and localize bleached areas in underwater images. abstract: Weather prediction is crucial in agriculture, transportation, and disaster management. Accurate and timely forecasts are essential for making informed decisions and minimizing risks. This study proposes a hybrid machine learning approach for weather prediction, combining Ridge Regression for feature extraction and selection and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) for training and evaluation. title: Biophysical transport control in smart nanocomposite packaging under non-thermal food preservation technologies
abstract: Smart nanocomposite packaging has emerged as a promising approach for enhancing food preservation by improving barrier performance, enabling active functionality, and supporting intelligent quality monitoring. Its integration with non-thermal preservation technologies, including pulsed electric fields, cold plasma, ultraviolet irradiation, and high-pressure processing, offers new opportunities to extend shelf life while minimizing thermal damage to food products. abstract: Abstract. Projections of Antarctic mass loss and its contribution to sea-level rise are highly sensitive to the applied ocean-driven melting. As fully coupled continental-scale ocean–ice sheet models are scarce, ice sheet models are typically run in standalone configurations, forced with parameterised sub-shelf melting. title: The Impact of Earthquake Early Warning Systems on Smart Cities' Resilience: Conceptual Framework and Comprehensive Review
abstract: Earthquake Early Warning Systems (EEWS) are critical components of resilient smart cities, employing advanced digital technologies to reduce the impacts of seismic events and strengthen urban disaster preparedness. These systems integrate distributed Internet of Things (IoT) devices, wireless sensor networks, high-speed communication infrastructures, and machine learning algorithms to detect, analyze, and evaluate seismic activity in real time. title: Explainable artificial intelligence reveals spatially divergent effects of global change on mammals
abstract: Abstract Understanding how global change reshapes species distributions remains a central challenge in ecology, yet most global assessments treat environmental drivers as static, uniform, or aggregate influences. This obscures where, why, and how specific drivers generate ecological risk or opportunity. Here, we apply explainable machine learning to assess how climate averages, variability, extremes, and land cover are projected to reshape future distributions of 1,992 terrestrial mammals. title: Where freshwater meets the sea: satellite–model insights into salinity dynamics in the Venice Lagoon
abstract: Salinity is a key descriptor of transitional water bodies at the land–sea interface, and resolving its spatiotemporal dynamics is essential for understanding water-mass exchange, habitat distribution, and ecosystem functioning. However, available observations remain limited in their ability to resolve dynamic freshwater–marine interactions at relevant spatial scales. abstract: Strains of the picocyanobacteria genera Synechococcus and Cyanobium occur in cold-temperate zones, from coastal waters to the open ocean, spanning a range of salinities and water depths. To thrive across different salinities, picocyanobacteria strains acclimate internal turgor by expending metabolic energy to accumulate compatible solutes and extrude inorganic ions. abstract: ABSTRACT Reducing flood damage is a key challenge for both administrators and communities, particularly in the face of increasing climate‐related impacts. A fundamental prerequisite for effective damage reduction is a detailed understanding of the spatial distribution of territorial susceptibility to flood damage. abstract: Background Superficial fungal infections present a growing threat to global public health. Traditional diagnostic techniques, including microscopy and culture, are time-consuming and subjective, often limiting diagnostic accuracy. Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diagnostic tools offer a promising adjunct to improve efficiency and standardization of microscopic fungal detection. abstract: Comprehending bioconvection facilitates the modelling of natural processes in aquatic environments and improves the efficacy of systems incorporating microorganism suspensions. It connects biology with fluid dynamics, providing insights into the impact of living creatures on fluid flow behaviour. abstract: Rapid and accurate prediction of radial power distribution is crucial for the design and operation of space nuclear reactors. However, traditional Monte Carlo methods incur prohibitively high computational costs, while conventional data-driven surrogate models face severe overfitting and insufficient generalization capabilities under small-sample and data distribution shift conditions. abstract: The blue economy has emerged as a strategic framework for reconciling ocean-based economic development with marine ecosystem conservation and social well-being, particularly in maritime regions such as Southeast Asia. As one of the world’s most ocean-dependent regions, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) possesses extensive marine resources that support fisheries, marine tourism, shipping, offshore energy, and emerging marine biotechnology industries. abstract: Abstract The international community has committed to protect 30% of the ocean by 2030, and satellite monitoring can now detect industrial fishing inside marine protected areas (MPAs) at near-global scale. Yet remote detection establishes only a vessel’s identity, position, time, and movement; whether those facts can support enforcement action depends on how the law is written. abstract: Autonomous Underwater Vehicles have become essential platforms for ocean exploration, environmental monitoring, offshore engineering, and military applications. As the primary hydrodynamic component of an AUV, the hull significantly influences drag, endurance, maneuverability, and payload capacity. abstract: With the rapid advancement of digital technologies, such as artificial intelligence, big data, blockchain, and cloud computing, the traditional wealth management industry is undergoing profound transformation. abstract: Soil salinity poses a significant challenge to agricultural productivity and sustainable land management in coastal and semi-arid regions. abstract: Abstract Shifting technological landscapes have been shaping the epistemologies, methods, and workflows of classicists, historians, and archaeologists for more than a century. abstract: ABSTRACT Coral reefs are under increasing threat from local and global stressors, resulting in changes to the composition and spatial structure of benthic habitats. This study uses high‐spatial resolution satellite imagery and landscape metrics to analyse changes to the shallow, turbid reef at Sebastião Gomes on the Abrolhos Bank in the Southwestern Atlantic Ocean between 2010 and 2024. abstract: ABSTRACT Sponges, phylum Porifera, are long-lived and basal-branching metazoans that play important roles in ocean biogeochemistry and host diverse microbial communities. Siliceous sponges form a major clade of the Porifera; however, their microbiome is not well characterized, particularly in the deep ocean. abstract: Polar coastal waters are highly complex and productive ecosystems that experience increasingly higher average water temperatures, shallower and stronger stratification, and higher glacier-melting rates. Yet, the environmental complexity and high microbial diversity within fjords pose challenges to understanding the impacts of these changes and the ecological processes driving them. abstract: Concurrent local and global stressors are rapidly degrading marine ecosystems. Flag‐type triboelectric nanogenerators (F‐TENGs), which have been widely investigated for harvesting energy from low‐velocity ocean currents, generally rely on bluff body to induce vortex. This dependence limits their spatial utilization efficiency. abstract: Mussaenda wallichii G. abstract: Underwater images play a significant role in ocean exploration, but they frequently suffer from major loss of image quality due to light absorption and scattering in underwater conditions. However, underwater image restoration remains a challenging issue because of various distortions. The primary cause of information degradation includes wavelength-dependent color attenuation, light scattering effects, and blurring of objects. title: Asian new regionalism revisited: ASEAN–China interactions in the 21 st century
abstract: ASEAN–China interactions constitute a critical site for reassessing the contemporary dynamics of new regionalism in the 21st century. While scholarship has moved beyond state-led and Eurocentric paradigms, gaps remain in understanding how new regionalism evolves in Asia. This article revisits Asian new regionalism and reconceptualises it as a pluralistic, multi-actor, multi-layered, and rule-shaping form of regional configuration engulfed by internal and external challenges. title: Multimodal Machine Learning for Cloud-to-Ground Lightning Classification and Polarity Localization in Tropical Thunderstorm
abstract: Accurate classification and localization of Cloud-to-Ground (CG) lightning are essential for the development of reliable early warning systems in tropical regions and the improvement of thunderstorm monitoring. This study proposes a multimodal machine learning framework for CG lightning classification and polarity-based localization with synchronized atmospheric and electromagnetic measurements collected in Melaka, Malaysia, in 2024. title: Linking marine benthic biodiversity and ecosystem functions related to carbon cycling in a continental mud depocenter
abstract: Abstract. The importance of carbon storage in continental seafloor sediments is increasingly recognized, yet the role of benthic macrofaunal biodiversity in the regulation of these processes remains poorly understood. Benthic macrofauna contributes to organic carbon cycling through respiration and secondary production, while the sediment reworking (bioturbation) and ventilation (bioirrigation) of infauna promote the redistribution and remineralization of organic matter in sediments. abstract: Estimating room layout has become increasingly important in recent years because of its wide range of applications,particularly in marine environments such as ship interiors, offshore platforms, and maritime facilities. However, thistask is quite challenging due to factors like clutter, occlusion, and varying lighting conditions in room images, which are commonly observed in marine and maritime operational settings. abstract: Maritime engineering is rapidly transforming with the integration of intelligent computational technologies that enhance vessel operations, reduce operational costs, and improve overall system performance. However, unforeseen failures during mission-critical maritime processes—such as navigation, cargo handling, and fleet coordination—can significantly degrade system reliability. To address these challenges, this research proposes a novel Dynamic Clustering with Flamingo Searchbased fault-tolerant scheduling mechanism (DCFS-FTDSS) designed specifically for maritime applications. abstract: This study develops a hybrid analytical and computational framework for the (2+1)-dimensional Boussinesq equation, which models weakly nonlinear, weakly dispersive shallow-water gravity waves relevant to wave resonance and oblique interactions in coastal and ocean engineering. Using the unified Riccati equation expansion (UREE) method, five exact traveling-wave solutions are constructed: a bright soliton, a singular soliton, two periodic waves, and a rational solution. title: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation for treatment-resistant depression in Singapore: a retrospective, naturalistic study
abstract: Introduction Naturalistic repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) outcome data for treatment-resistant depression remain limited in Southeast Asia. This retrospective study describes such outcomes from a general hospital in Singapore. Method 28 outpatients received rTMS (10Hz high-frequency or intermittent theta-burst) targeting the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (F3 scalp position) between May 2022 and May 2025. title: An Optimized Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Short-Range Rainfall Forecasting in Mumbai’s Monsoon Regime
abstract: Abstract Short-range rainfall forecasting in tropical coastal megacities is a formidable challenge owing to the nonlinear dynamics, strong seasonality, and pronounced interannual variability that characterise monsoon precipitation regimes. This study develops and evaluates deep learning frameworks for multi-lead-time (D+1 to D+4) daily rainfall forecasting over Mumbai (72.88°E, 19.07°N), India, a densely populated coastal metropolis where accurate precipitation prediction is directly consequential for flood early warning. title: Explainable machine learning for predicting microplastic burden in commercially important freshwater fish and assessing dietary exposure
abstract: Microplastic (MP) contamination in commercially important freshwater fish represents an emerging concern for aquatic ecosystem integrity and human food safety. This study presents an interpretable machine learning framework for predicting and assessing MP accumulation in European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax), Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus), bighead carp (Hypophthalmichthys nobilis) and crucian carp (Carassius auratus) collected from four retail markets in Yichang City, Hubei Province, China. title: Intelligent Cyber-Physical Protection for Maritime IoT Ecosystems: Machine Learning-Based Intrusion Detection for Intelligent Marine Systems
abstract: In the modern network security study, the intrusion detection systems (IDS) play the central role in securing the Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructures against cyber-attacks like the Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) and the brute force attacks. But there are often difficulties of imbalance classes and high-dimensional data faced by traditional IDS.This study proposes a real-time, machine learning-based framework tailored for the maritime edge, delivering up to 99.8% detection accuracy while ensuring compliance with international cyber risk management guidelines. title: Attention-Guided Deep Learning Framework for Ovarian Cancer Subtype Classification
abstract: Ovarian cancer histotype classification is challenging because of substantial morphological heterogeneity and subtle subtype-specific features. This work presents a controlled evaluation of high-resolution pathology representations and slide-level aggregation methods for automated classification of five ovarian cancer subtypes from whole-slide histopathology images. Precomputed CONCH patch embeddings were aggregated using mean pooling, max pooling, gated attention-based multiple-instance learning, and a max-pooling cascade. title: Deep-Learning Error Correction of Regional Significant Wave Height Forecasts
abstract: Deep-learning post-processing can correct systematic errors in numerical wave forecasts, but its reliability under high-wave conditions remains unclear. We develop an error-correction framework in which deep networks predict the full future error trajectory of operational forecasts, and compare three architectures, a pure LSTM, a pure Transformer and a hybrid LSTM–Transformer, tuned identically with Bayesian optimization, using hourly observations from six buoys in the Bohai Sea and Yellow Sea over 2023–2025. abstract: BACKGROUND: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn's disease (CD), is becoming an increasingly important public health concern in Asia, with rising incidence and prevalence reported across the region. Despite progress in global burden studies, data gaps remain in Asia due to variations in healthcare and socio-demographic factors. This study aims to address these gaps by assessing the burden of IBD across Asia from 1990 to 2023, focusing on regional trends in UC and CD. title: Projected intensification of summer upwelling along the Southeastern Coast of China
abstract: Coastal upwelling is a key dynamical process along the southeastern coast of China, regulating regional circulation, biogeochemical cycling, and marine ecosystem dynamics. While previous studies have provided valuable insights into the mechanisms and variability of this coastal upwelling, its future evolution and underlying physical drivers under climate change remain unclear. title: Convolutional Neural Network-Based Classification System for Weld Radiographic Test Images
abstract: Steel pipes are widely applied in shipbuilding and marine engineering. Welded steel pipes undertake heavy loads inrelevant structures, so non-destructive testing of welded joints is necessary to ensure integrity. Traditional radiographic testing is time-consuming and complex, relying on manual operation and evaluation by qualified inspectors, which easily causes human errors. This study adopts EfficientNet with transfer learning and fine-tuning to classify the quality of welded steel pipe radiographic images as qualified or unqualified under limited data. title: An attention-enhanced residual network framework for structural damage detection based on structural health monitoring data
abstract: Local damage in steel structures often produces only subtle differences in vibration responses, and measurement noise can further reduce identification robustness. To address these challenges, this study proposes a structural damage identification method that combines Markov transition field (MTF) encoding with a coordinate-attention-enhanced residual network. abstract: Abstract Multi‐angle polarimetric instruments (MAPs) enable the retrieval of essential aerosol properties over oceanic regions. MAPs retrieval algorithms commonly use a 1‐parameter ocean bio‐optical model (OBM), based on chlorophyll‐a concentration only to represent optical properties over open waters (case‐1), whereas the coastal water (mixture of case‐1 and case‐2 waters) representation generally requires multi‐parameter models as demonstrated for sophisticated sensors such as SPEXone. title: A Hybrid Quantum Optimization Framework for Oil Spill Detection Using Marine Radar
abstract: Oil spills at sea pose a serious threat to marine ecosystems and coastal economic development. Therefore, rapid and accurate detection of oil spills is crucial for emergency response and environmental protection. Marine radar offers unique advantages in short-range, continuous, and all-weather monitoring, making it an important supplementary tool for oil spill detection. title: Integrating Remote Sensing, Geographic Information Systems, and Machine Learning for Environmental Monitoring and Sustainable Resource Management
abstract: Environmentally sensitive coastal areas are rapidly becoming urbanised, increasing pressure on vegetation, wetlands, surface-water resources and the natural resource base. The current study combines remote sensing, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and machine learning to evaluate changes in Land Use/Land Cover (LULC) and environmental conditions in the Lekki–Ajah axis of Lagos State, Nigeria. title: Cohort-level growth modeling of ethical engagement with artificial intelligence in education
abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in higher education, yet limited evidence explains how students’ ethical engagement develops over time. Existing research is largely cross-sectional and often treats ethical awareness, reflection, and responsible use as a unified competence. This study examined cohort-level changes in AI Ethics Awareness (AEAw), Responsible AI Use (RAIU), and AI-Driven Reflection on Decision-Making (AIRD), including relationships among their initial levels and growth rates. abstract: Underwater acoustic target recognition (UATR) is essential for ocean-intelligence sensing, but deep learning-based models often suffer from performance degradation under ocean acoustic domain shift. This problem arises because ship-radiated noise recorded under different propagation channels, vessel operating states, background noise levels, and recording configurations may exhibit substantial distribution discrepancies. title: Asymmetric bloom lengthening drives high-latitude ocean chlorophyll accumulation imbalance
abstract: Terrestrial ecosystems maintain a stable time-allocation budget between growth and senescence, but whether this applies to the ocean remains unclear. Using fused satellite LiDAR and ocean-color data (2007–2022), we show that marine phenology is variable and asymmetric. In high latitudes ( > 50°N), the bloom growth-to-decline ratio (RGD) is declining by ~5.3% per decade. While the chlorophyll-increase phase has lengthened by 2.3–5.5 days, the post-peak chlorophyll-decline phase has extended disproportionately by 5.7–6.2 days. abstract: The growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping hotel marketing and guest-service delivery, yet empirical evidence on its implications for guest satisfaction and loyalty in developing hospitality markets remains limited. This study examined AI applications in selected international hotels in Abuja, Nigeria, focusing on their perceived contribution to marketing performance, guest satisfaction and loyalty, as well as barriers to adoption. title: Spatiotemporal Precipitation Trends and Hybrid Machine Learning Prediction in the Humid Rainforest Climatic Zone of Nigeria
abstract: This study investigated the spatiotemporal trends and hybrid machine learning prediction of precipitation in Nigeria’s humid rainforest climatic zone using 45 years (1981–2025) of monthly rainfall data from Calabar, Yenagoa, Benin City, and Ikeja. Data obtained from the NASA POWER database were analyzed using statistical, spatial, and machine learning techniques. abstract: Despite the availability of safe sanitation access, this issue remains a major challenge in many developing nations like South Africa where there are challenges associated with the fragmented data gathering, manual reporting, and lack of interoperability and real-time monitoring of the sanitation service chain. abstract: El estudio tuvo como propósito determinar la relación entre el uso de la inteligencia artificial y el desempeño laboral del personal administrativo en una Universidad Pública de la ciudad de Trujillo, 2024. title: Tornado damage prediction using machine learning
abstract: Tornadoes are the most violent of all atmospheric windstorms. Although they occur throughout the world, the highest frequency is observed in the US, where over 1,700 tornadoes were recorded in 2024 alone. Intensity measures that characterize tornado damage, such as the Enhanced Fujita (EF) scale, are derived from post-event assessment on the ground. This somewhat circular aspect of damage characterization and EF scale determination remains a major limitation for long-term prediction of damage. abstract: ABSTRACT Digital elevation models (DEMs) are widely used to characterize terrain and support applications ranging from geomorphology to environmental management. While traditional analyses rely on handcrafted geomorphometric features, advances in machine learning enable richer, data‐driven representations of topographic surfaces. title: A Cluster-Based Technology Roadmapping Approach for Strategic Management of Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare
abstract: Technology roadmapping is a key strategic concern for companies. The aim of this study is to propose a cluster-based technology roadmapping approach using patent documents. The proposed approach is applied to artificial intelligence (AI) technology. The proposed approach provides evidence-based decision-making in healthcare management by identifying and prioritizing artificial intelligence (AI) technology domains with high long-term success potential. title: Predicting long-term degradation of prestressed bridge girders using a hybrid finite element and deep learning approach
abstract: Prestressed concrete girders are widely used in bridge and railway infrastructure. However, their long-term performance is highly vulnerable to environmental effects, particularly corrosion, which significantly compromises structural serviceability and durability. Accurately quantifying corrosion-induced deterioration over extended periods remains challenging due to the substantial time and computational demands of conventional finite element analyses. title: Marine Mammal Monitoring Research from 2014 to 2023: A Bibliometric Analysis of Collaboration, Technological Trends and Research Themes
abstract: Marine mammal monitoring research has expanded considerably alongside developments in acoustic, remote-sensing, telemetry, molecular, and computational approaches. This study used bibliometric analysis to characterise the structure and evolution of research published between 2014 and 2023. A total of 2586 peer-reviewed publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection were analysed using CiteSpace to examine publication trends, collaboration networks, keyword co-occurrence, temporal clusters, and citation bursts. abstract: La creciente incorporación de herramientas de inteligencia artificial en el ámbito educativo ha transformado la forma en que los estudiantes acceden al conocimiento, ofreciendo oportunidades para personalizar la enseñanza y apoyar el aprendizaje. title: Deep-learning climate emulator ACE2 reveals a global decrease in 15th-century tropical cyclone frequency under El Niño-like sea surface temperatures
abstract: Abstract The relatively short modern observational record limits our understanding of the relationship between global tropical cyclone (TC) frequency and sea surface temperature (SST), resulting in uncertain future TC projections. Using novel deep-learning-based past-millennium simulations with the Ai2 Climate Emulator version 2 (ACE2), we provide insight into the connections between SSTs and TCs. abstract: Intrinsic differences among individuals can shape how marine predators forage in heterogeneous environments. For emperor penguins at Cape Crozier, the southernmost breeding colony in the Ross Sea and a potential climate refuge, the influence of sex, size, and body condition on at-sea behavior during late chick-rearing is unknown. title: Urban growth-induced surface thermal dynamics: an integrated deep learning assessment for Colombo, Sri Lanka
abstract: Abstract Urban growth is a major driver of land surface temperature (LST) change, yet most LST forecasting studies do not explicitly incorporate future urban expansion. To address this gap, we develop an integrated deep learning (DL) framework that couples urban growth simulation with LST prediction for Colombo, Sri Lanka, and benchmark our proposed ResNet+Transformer model against six comparison models (four DL architectures and two machine learning methods) across both tasks. title: Bearing capacity and safety factors of ring foundations in spatially variable soils: a hybrid FELA-machine learning approach
abstract: Abstract Ring foundations efficiently support axisymmetric structures like silos, storage tanks, chimneys, and cooling towers with reduced concrete volume compared to solid circular foundations. Their ultimate bearing capacity is strongly affected by asymmetric loading and spatial variability in soil properties. This study presents a hybrid machine learning framework to predict normalized bearing capacity factors and safety factors for ring foundations in spatially variable cohesive-frictional (c-φ) soils. abstract: Abstract. Storms and associated marine hazards pose a environmental risks, particularly under long-term changes driven by anthropogenic climate change. This study assesses the potential impacts of future climate change on annual median and extreme wave conditions in the North Sea and the Baltic Sea using a ensemble of up to 14 and 8 regional projections, respectively. title: Resilience assessment and prediction of fresh agricultural product supply chains using variable fuzzy recognition and machine learning
abstract: Fresh agricultural products are highly perishable and sensitive to transportation, storage, and handling conditions, which makes their supply chains particularly vulnerable to disruptions. Such disruptions can interrupt product flows and reduce both quality and availability. Traditional risk analysis methods mainly focus on uncertainty and the probability of adverse events, but they do not adequately capture the ability of supply chains to recover and adapt following disruptions. title: Multi-objective optimized signal decomposition with explainable and reliable hybrid models for multistep significant wave height forecasting in ocean wave energy applications
abstract: Accurate forecasting of significant wave height (Hs) is vital for marine safety, coastal engineering, and renewable energy production. This study presents an effective integrated model system to forecast Hs for two distinct sites in Australia, Gladstone and Palm Beach, over various time horizons from 30-min to 24-h ahead during the period of 2018 to 2022. abstract: Introduction Marine buoys are essential aids to navigation, yet their positions can vary continuously under dynamic environmental forcing. It is therefore important for navigational safety, maintenance planning, and reducing search-and-recovery costs to achieve accurate short-term prediction of buoy displacement. abstract: Significant wave height (SWH) is a fundamental parameter for ocean engineering, maritime safety, and climate studies. Although spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) wave mode observations provide global, all-weather coverage, accurate SWH retrieval remains challenging due to the complex ocean-to-SAR imaging mechanism. This paper presents an explainable machine learning algorithm for retrieving SWH from Sentinel-1 SAR wave mode data. abstract: Coastal segmentation struggles with complex terrain configurations and discontinuous edge demarcation. title: FPGA-Based Neural Network Accelerators for Space Missions: A Survey
abstract: Space missions are growing ever more ambitious, placing greater demands on onboard computing. Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) have garnered interest due to their reconfigurability and cost-effectiveness. At the same time, neural network (NN)-based methods are proving invaluable for critical spacecraft tasks such as autonomous operations, remote sensing, selective downlink, and data compression. abstract: Groundwater dynamics in South Florida play an important role in shaping the hydrologic balance of the region. abstract: Trigonium zonatulatum (Greville) A. Mann, originally described as Triceratium zonatulatum Greville, was previously known solely from the Indo-Pacific, Indian Ocean, and Bering Sea. Here, we report the first record of this diatom species from the Atlantic Ocean (Caribbean Sea), based on material collected at Boca Chica Beach, Dominican Republic. abstract: Cross-border artificial intelligence (AI) cooperation is expanding, but evidence on its effect on domestic technological capability in recipient economies is scarce. Drawing on absorptive capacity theory, we create a composite AI absorptive capacity index for 10 Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) economies, encompassing innovation foundations, application foundations and industrial support. abstract: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is a well-known sleep disorder that can lead to major health consequences if left untreated. abstract: ABSTRACT Social and environmental accounting provides accountability mechanisms through which organisations communicate their sustainability practices to stakeholders. However, the increasing volume, complexity and diversity of sustainability disclosures make manual content analysis both labour‐intensive and susceptible to subjectivity. This review synthesizes 173 studies published from 2002 to 2025 and retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, and PubMed. abstract: Anti-tropically distributed species have long intrigued biogeographers. abstract: Reverse osmosis (RO) is widely used for seawater desalination, water treatment, and product concentration, yet long-term performance degradation remains difficult to predict because fouling and membrane deterioration arise from coupled physical, chemical, and biological phenomena under variable industrial conditions. We developed a hybrid modeling (HBM) framework combining a first-principles RO model (FPM) with a deep neural network and applied it to an industrial two-stage RO system concentrating byproducts from methionine fermentation. title: Sentiment analysis and satisfaction evaluation of ecotourism consumption under a multi-source deep learning framework
abstract: Ecotourism promotes sustainable development, but evaluating tourists’ experiences becomes difficult because of different multi-source feedback. Traditional methods using text or rating have been inaccurate. Research incorporates textual reviews and numerical ratings to enhance precision, depth and interpretability in ecotourism sentiments and satisfaction evaluation. abstract: Abstract Meteorological seasons are typically defined through fixed calendar intervals or region‐specific thresholds, yet such approaches fail to capture the actual variability of the annual cycle. Here we present a machine learning framework that objectively detects meteorological seasons and projects their future evolution. abstract: Abstract Mangroves are important coastal blue carbon ecosystems, but future sediment GHG emissions remain uncertain because global projections have largely emphasized atmospheric climate drivers, with less attention to coastal hydrology, particularly sea-surface salinity and tidal range. title: Determinants of Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Construction Project Delivery: Evidence from Large Construction Firms in Nigeria Using the TOE Framework
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly recognized as a transformative technology for enhancing construction project delivery. However, empirical evidence explaining the factors associated with its adoption remains limited, particularly in developing-country construction contexts. This study investigated the determinants of AI adoption across construction project delivery functions among large-scale construction firms in Nigeria using the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework. abstract: The increasing accumulation of plastic waste has encouraged its reuse as a partial aggregate replacement in concrete, offering a sustainable alternative to conventional construction materials. title: From publication to action: connecting science, policy, and public attention for ocean-related climate mitigation
abstract: Ocean-related options (OROs), including marine renewable energy and ocean-based carbon dioxide removal, are emerging as promising climate mitigation actions. OROs vary widely in technological maturity and risk acceptability, yet as scientific literature exponentially increases, synthesising the current state of evidence is a major challenge. abstract: The rapid expansion of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems has increased the cyber-attack surface of critical infrastructure, requiring intrusion detection systems (IDS) that are accurate, robust, and efficient under resource-constrained edge environments. abstract: Concrete industry has widely incorporated fibres in mixes due to their potential to improve concrete mechanical properties, enhance the toughness and durability of concrete reinforced members, and their ability to control crack widths in reinforced concrete members. abstract: Groundwater nitrate contamination is a major water-quality concern, with implications for drinking water supplies and groundwater-dependent ecosystems. abstract: The intersection of NANO+AI+ML is a novel approach for environmental risk governance, pollution control and disaster management. This study investigates the amalgamation of AI-enabled nanotechnology that unites extremely sensitive environmental sensing technology with predictive analytics to bolster detection, assessment, prevention and mitigation of environmental hazards. title: Lithostratigraphically-constrained landslide susceptibility modeling in red-bed basins using a bayesian probability-based mixture probabilistic neural network
abstract: Regional landslide susceptibility prediction commonly treats diverse failure mechanisms as a single statistical entity, an oversimplification that fails in lithologically complex red-bed basins, where retrogressive and translational landslides follow fundamentally distinct hydromechanical laws. Here we develop a mechanism-divergent framework that integrates frequency ratio factor screening, Bayesian probability for uncertainty-aware dataset construction, and a mixture probabilistic neural network to explicitly fuse multi-modal susceptibility indices. title: Design of a Robust Embedded Sensor Network for Real-Time Hull Structural Health Monitoring in Marine Vessels
abstract: This research introduces a robust sensor network that is embedded in the hull of a marine vessel for real-time structural health monitoring. The system involves strain sensors, an (MEMS) accelerometer, and the wireless communication modules for securing data of structural behavior under different conditions. title: Non‐Perturbative Bacterial Identification Directly From Solid Agar Plates Using Raman Micro‐Spectroscopy and Machine Learning
abstract: Raman spectroscopy is a promising tool for microbial identification, yet its implementation in microbiology and clinical workflow is still restricted due to the accompanying additional preparation required to focus on microbial signals. Here, we demonstrate Raman-based bacterial identification directly from unopened, inverted agar plates, the same conditions used during incubation. title: Satellite LiDAR reveals patterns in water table depth and flood risk in SE Asia coastal lowland and peatland plantations
abstract: Agriculture in SE Asian coastal lowlands is vulnerable to inundation and associated crop production loss. Quantifying and managing flood risk, surface subsidence, and carbon emissions (in peatlands) requires an understanding of water table depth patterns and controls, for which no comprehensive data currently exists. Here, we present a dataset of 15,575 measurements of canal water table depth below the soil surface (CWD) in large-scale industrial tree plantations across the islands of Sumatra and Borneo, derived from ICESat-2 satellite LiDAR data. abstract: Underwater images are affected by spectral attenuation, particulate scattering, and nonuniform illumination and therefore often exhibit color shifts, reduced contrast, blurred edges, and local darkening. Existing public datasets provide limited coverage of degradation types and intensities, while frame extraction from continuous videos introduces many similar backgrounds, making it difficult for detection models to fully learn object variations in complex waters. abstract: Abstract Video auditing can provide vital insights into complex industrial operations where quality, safety, and compliance are critical. However, there is a need to develop explainable artificial intelligence frameworks capable of recognising workflow steps and producing interpretable reports from long, untrimmed video sequences. abstract: Hail is a small-scale hydrometeorological phenomenon threatening disaster-prone regions of Indonesia, yet understanding of its atmospheric dynamics and deep learning-based radar nowcasting remain limited. This study characterizes the atmospheric conditions of the Depok City hailstorm on 28 October 2024 and evaluates a hybrid UNet-ConvLSTM2D model in predicting radar reflectivity. abstract: Underwater surveillance and inspection relies on interpretable images, however, underwater images are prone to haze, colour casts, and poor scene detail. This paper proposes a two-stage single-image enhancement framework which first restores the image using an autoencoder and then refines it using a generative adversarial network (GAN). title: Regulating Marine Mammal Tourism Management: Challenges and Opportunities for Effective Enforcement in Aotearoa/New Zealand
abstract: Marine mammal tourism (MMT) in Aotearoa/New Zealand operates under one of the world’s most established environmental protection regimes, centred on the Marine Mammals Protection Act 1978 (MMPA) and Marine Mammals Protection Regulations 1992 (MMPR). Despite this reputation, persistent non-compliance and weak enforcement have raised concerns about the long-term sustainability of the MMT industry and the effectiveness of existing regulatory tools. abstract: Salinity stress constrains medicinal plant productivity, particularly in coastal and salt affected agroecosystems where rapid, deployable diagnostics are essential. Here, we develop an AI‐enabled RGB light‐to‐frequency proximal sensing platform integrated with Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) for nondestructive, real‐time salinity discrimination. title: MobiDerm-Fisher: Transfer Learning-Based MobileNetV3 Model with Cost-Sensitive Learning for Skin Disease Classification in Coastal Fishermen
abstract: Skin disease monitoring among fishermen in remote coastal areas remains challenging due to limited access to medical facilities and delayed clinical assessment. This study proposes MobiDerm-Fisher, a transfer learning-based skin disease classification framework utilizing the MobileNetV3Large architecture combined with cost-sensitive learning to address class imbalance. The model was trained on 4,564 dermoscopic images from the DermNet dataset covering five classes: Psoriasis, Eczema, Atopic Dermatitis, Poison Ivy, and Urticaria, using a stratified 80:20 train–test split. abstract: INTRODUCTION: Reef restoration practitioners aim to preserve coral genetic diversity by protecting reefs and cultivating diverse genotypes in coral nurseries. However, cryptic genetic lineages in most corals complicate restoration strategies, as the role of between-lineage genetic divergence remains unclear regarding adaptation. In Montastraea cavernosa, researchers have identified cryptic lineages, some strongly segregated by depth. Efficient exploration of the vast possible synthetic space is nevertheless hindered by the slow pace of manual experimentation. However, these benefits depend on daily accessibility. In compact coastal metropolises, extensive nature may coexist with highly unequal residential access. This study investigates whether socially vulnerable residential areas in Shenzhen experience reduced exposure to public green and coastal blue spaces. However, the nonlinear and hysteretic behavior of Magnetorheological elastomer materials poses challenges for achieving robust vibration suppression under varying excitation conditions. abstract: The events such as earthquakes, tsunamis and underwater landslides occur; communication reliability becomes a big challenge in Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks (UWSNs). abstract: Underwater bridge crack detection remains challenging because underwater optical images are often degraded by light absorption and scattering, leading to color distortion, uneven illumination, low contrast, and complex background interference. In addition, annotated underwater crack samples are scarce. abstract: Abstract Despite the widespread need to map the abundance of invasive quagga and zebr mussels ( Dreissena spp.) in lakes and reservoirs worldwide, current methods remain limited by data collection and analysis bottlenecks. abstract: Chemical heterogeneities in Earth’s deep mantle may record either preserved primordial reservoirs or later core-mantle exchange, but distinguishing between these origins remains challenging. title: Push and pull factors of relocation in the coastal zone: what matters most?
abstract: Abstract Permanent relocation is increasingly proposed as an effective long-term strategy for coastal areas affected by recurrent flooding. While the literature on coastal relocation has been steadily growing—particularly on policy processes, financial mechanisms, and lived experiences—less attention has been given to understanding the reasoning behind relocation decisions. This study provides empirical evidence on the factors that drive willingness to relocate from a telephone survey administered in high-risk coastal settings on the Delmarva Peninsula in Maryland and Hampton Roads, Virginia.

abstract: Mass coral bleaching events are intensifying under climate change, yet their ecological consequences remain highly context dependent. We quantified shifts in benthic community structure, coral diversity and reef functionality during the 2023–2025 Fourth Global Mass Coral Bleaching Event (GCBE) in Tela Bay and Roatán, Honduras, two traditionally high-cover reef systems within the Mesoamerican Reef (MAR). abstract: Three marine protected areas, i.e., Borkum Reef Ground, Sylt Outer Reef, and Dogger Bank, have been established within the European NATURA 2000 program in the German Exclusive Economic Zone of the North Sea. Within them, we analysed the effect of the varying impact of mobile bottom-contact fishing on infauna communities in selected focus areas as a baseline study prior to the exclusion of mobile bottom-contact fishing since 2023. This study compares a one-dimensional Residual Network (ResNet1D) and a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT)-inspired model for one-hour-ahead water-level prediction using Marine Automatic Weather Station (MAWS) observations from 2020–2024. abstract: Extreme precipitation events increasingly threaten historic buildings in river basins, yet existing studies lack a basin-scale perspective on nonlinear flood risk mechanisms. Taking the Minjiang River Basin as the study area, this research integrates hydrological simulation (SCS-CN), machine learning (XGBoost-SHAP), and spatial autocorrelation analysis to assess flood risk for 5482 historic buildings. abstract: Abstract Tropical ocean evaporation is the dominant source of moisture for global precipitation. However, the dependence of evaporation‐temperature sensitivity on ocean surface radiative properties has not been quantified in the fully coupled modeling framework. abstract: Early and correct detection of cancer regions in histopathology images is important for timely diagnosis and treatment. title: Physicochemical and urban land-use characteristics associated with resistance to precipitation in estuaries vary across scales
abstract: Estuaries are subject to frequent stressors, including elevated nutrient loading and extreme hydrologic events, which impact water quality and disrupt ecosystem stability and function. The capacity of an estuary to resist changes in function in response to precipitation events is an important descriptor of ecosystem response dynamics, especially when interpreted within the context of baseline system condition and ecological state. abstract: Total Suspended Matter (TSM) is a primary indicator of water quality. abstract: A new species of the arcid genus Anadara is described from intertidal and shallow subtidal habitats in Kuwait, northern Arabian/Persian Gulf. abstract: The focus of this panel report is to present evidence of a panel discussion that took place in October 2025 on the use of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) in academic research and publishing. title: Deciphering Precambrian Litho-structural settings and barite-associated mineralization through integrated hyperspectral and geophysical datasets
abstract: Effective lithological mapping and mineral exploration remain challenging in geologically complex and underexplored Precambrian terrains. abstract: Predicting marine engine wear based on the analysis of used lubricating oil samples is an important task in predictive maintenance.However, conventional forecasting methods are often ineffective in this context because of irregular sampling intervals, the limited number of observations available for establishing reliable relationships, and the apparent "improvement effect" in oil condition caused by oil replenishment or changes in engine operating conditions.This study proposes a methodological approach based on topological data analysis.Its distinctive feature is the identification of hidden

title: The Navier–Stokes Equations: A Critical Review of Theory, Computation, Turbulence, and Data-Driven Frontiers
abstract: The Navier–Stokes equations describe the motion of viscous fluids and stand at the center of modern fluid mechanics. They also define one of the hardest open problems in mathematics, for the question of whether smooth three-dimensional solutions can develop singularities in finite time remains unresolved. This review provides a critical, evidence-based synthesis of the subject from its foundations in the work of Leray and Hopf through the mathematical, computational, and data-driven landscape of 2026. title: Declining Surface Solar Radiation Resources in Polar Regions Under Global Warming
abstract: Abstract Surface solar radiation is a key component of the polar energy budget and solar energy resource availability, but biases in climate models limit confidence in future projections. We developed a U‐Net deep learning framework to correct surface solar radiation from 12 Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 models using the European Centre for Medium‐Range Weather Forecasts Reanalysis v5 as reference. abstract: Background Nitrogen availability strongly regulates growth and biochemical accumulation in marine diatoms, but the magnitude and direction of these responses are strain-specific. abstract: La heterogeneidad demográfica, financiera y territorial de los Gobiernos Autónomos Descentralizados (GAD) municipales plantea la necesidad de disponer de herramientas que permitan caracterizar conjuntamente las diferencias existentes entre los cantones del Ecuador. abstract: The rise of generative artificial intelligence forces a revision of assumptions that have become entrenched in contemporary pedagogical discourse: that activity by itself produces learning, that projects automatically develop critical thinking, that student autonomy requires reducing teacher intervention, and that competency development can be conceived separately from knowledge construction. abstract: Katablepharids (or kathablepharids) are plastid-less, biflagellate protists widely distributed in marine and freshwater environments. Here, we report a new katablepharid species, Katablepharis ulleungensis sp. nov., isolated from a black sandy beach in Ulleung-do, South Korea. The stock strain was co-cultured with a small bicosoecid flagellate, serving as its prey. title: Seabirds and native vegetation drive ecosystem processes that support atoll island resilience
abstract: Ecosystem restoration is expected to enhance ecosystem resilience to climate change, but few empirical and mechanistic demonstrations of such assertions exist. Here, we explore this topic for tropical atoll systems, combining science on nutrient subsidies and geo-ecological functions through a unifying ecological energetics lens. title: Effects of el niño and avian influenza on the trophic niche of the South American Sea Lion (Otaria byronia) in the central-southern Humboldt current system
abstract: Large-scale climatic variability and emerging diseases can reshape trophic interactions and ecosystem functioning in highly productive upwelling systems. Here, we evaluate how El Niño conditions and the 2022–2023 avian influenza outbreak affected the population trophic niche of the South American sea lion ( Otaria byronia ) across the central–southern Humboldt Current System. abstract: Abstract. In the Namib Desert, fog is an essential water source and occurs when and where advected marine stratus clouds intersect with the land surface. However, the meteorological controls of the cloud base height are still insufficiently understood. This study aims to develop a basic understanding of the relevant processes. title: The History and Labor of Web Scraping
abstract: Abstract Both the free labor of generating data online and the importance of data work which cleans, labels, and verifies these data are required for producing artificial intelligence (AI) systems. Between these two essential moments in AI production, we identify web scraping as the intercalary process of extracting data from the internet at scale. abstract: Silk fibroin, a natural textile material spun by silkworms over millennia, is emerging as a transformative platform for integrating human intelligence with artificial intelligence. Its core innovation lies in the meso-functionalization strategy, which precisely programs protein refolding and hierarchical assembly. title: Agaricia spp. recruitment failure and subsequent recovery in the wake of mass bleaching and disease outbreak on reefs of St. Thomas, US Virgin Islands
abstract: Caribbean coral reefs have declined severely under cumulative stressors including hurricanes, thermal anomalies, disease outbreaks, and local anthropogenic impacts. abstract: Riverine (fluvial) flooding remains a significant climate-related disaster in many countries. Extreme rainfall events caused by climate change cause significant damage and disruption to communities living near riverbanks or neighboring land areas, particularly when risk-sensitive development is ignored. abstract: Effluents generated in the food and beverage industry typically contain elevated concentrations of organic carbon sources and inorganic nutrients, representing a significant environmental burden as global food demand continues to rise. Owing to their capacity to effectively assimilate carbon and nutrients while simultaneously generating biomass with potential valorization pathways, Chlorella spp. offers a dual benefit of contaminant removal and resource recovery. abstract: Abstract. The skill of climate projections depends on the ability of models to reproduce the long-term and low-frequency variability of the system. In this paper, a method is proposed to estimate directly the low-frequency component of the ocean variability from native observations using statistics from a prior long-term simulation. abstract: Abstract Membrane-exposed ligand binding sites in membrane proteins are emerging as important modulatory targets in drug discovery, however, their prediction remains challenging due to limited structural data. Here, we present DeepPocket-Mem, a deep learning-based approach that applies transfer learning to a convolutional neural network originally developed for soluble protein binding sites. abstract: Abstract The tropical Pacific plays a pivotal role in global climate. Changes in its mean state and El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) could significantly alter regional hydroclimates, causing major economic and societal impacts, yet its response to different emission pathways remains poorly constrained. abstract: Tourism in Goa is concentrated along the coastal belt, generating congestion, environmental stress, and uneven spatial development. This study develops a spatial decision-support framework to identify areas where tourism pressure should be contained and areas where diversification is more feasible. This study proposes the density and temporally aware filter (DTF‐Filter), which combines local density‐adaptive thresholding with temporal consistency across consecutive frames. title: A new species of sole (Pleuronectiformes, Soleidae), Soleichthys labyrinthus, from the China Sea
abstract: The genus Soleichthys (Soleidae) suffers from taxonomic confusion due to morphological similarities. In this study, a new sole species, Soleichthys labyrinthus sp. nov ., is described based on the holotype and 24 paratypes collected from the northern South China Sea and the East China Sea. title: Transformer-Based Bias Correction of ERA5 Winds over the East China Sea and Wind Resource Trend During 2016–2025
abstract: Accurate wind information is essential for offshore wind-resource assessment in the East China Sea, yet global reanalyses remain poorly constrained in this region. title: Similar degenerative patterns of olfactory receptor genes in the giant panda and marine carnivores
abstract: Olfactory receptor (OR) genes constitute the largest mammalian gene family and are critical for olfactory perception and ecological adaptation. OR gene variation is associated with interspecific differences in habitat, diet, and sensory reliance, yet the relative contributions of these ecological factors to OR evolution remain unclear. abstract: Glycosylated phosphoisoprenoids constitute valuable bioactive molecules and starting materials for complex glycosylation cascades. Herein we report the identification and the functional characterization of a newly identified polyprenyl phosphomannose synthase from the marine microorganism Rhodococcus erythropolis PR4. abstract: Reliable wave forecasts are a cornerstone of coastal risk management and offshore operations, yet operational products remain expensive to generate at high resolution and can be insufficiently calibrated for decision-making under uncertainty. abstract: ABSTRACT Fracto‐mechanoluminescence (FML) materials have recently demonstrated great potential as next‐generation interactive optoelectronic systems, while they generally suffer from irreversible fatigue degradation under long‐term cyclic stress, severely limiting their practical applications. abstract: This research highlights the need to incorporate the teaching and learning of artificial intelligence, particularly big data, into the educational process. In addition to developing digital literacy, students must acquire knowledge of the technological tools required by companies, which may become their future sources of employment. abstract: Lead-free double perovskite solar cells (DPSCs) have emerged as attractive alternatives to conventional lead-based perovskites because of their superior environmental compatibility, enhanced chemical stability, and reduced toxicity. abstract: Abstract: Climate-induced disasters, including floods, cyclones, and droughts, have increased in frequency and severity in coastal Odisha over the past few decades. Recurrent crop failures, livelihood disruptions, and loss of income have heightened economic stress and reduced the resilience of vulnerable communities. These impacts are often gender-differentiated, influencing how men and women respond to and cope with disaster-related challenges. abstract: This study examines how the Montreux Convention shapes NATO’s defense posture on the Eastern Flank within the Black Sea security environment. abstract: Nearshore hardbottom (NSHB) habitats occur in shallow coastal waters throughout the Florida Keys and support sessile benthic invertebrate communities dominated by sponges and octocorals. abstract: Land use and land cover (LCLU) classification from multispectral satellite imagery is important for applications such as urban planning, environmental monitoring, agriculture, and disaster management. abstract: Introduction: The growing integration of generative artificial intelligence into higher education has transformed the way students access, process, and produce information, creating new learning opportunities while also raising risks associated with cognitive dependence. abstract: On 29-30 October 2018, an extreme sea level occurred in the Adriatic Sea, driven by a combination of long-period (storm surge) and short-period (meteotsunami) oscillations. abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate prediction of the drilling rate of penetration (ROP) is crucial to optimizing drilling performance, wellbore stability, enhancing operational efficiency, and reducing the overall cost of hydrocarbon exploration. abstract: Against the backdrop of global climate change and the increasing frequency of extreme rainfall events, rainfall-triggered clustered landslides have become a major concern in mountainous disaster risk management due to their sudden occurrence, regional clustering, and high destructive potential. abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) models have transformed weather forecasting, but their skill for unprecedented weather extremes is unclear. abstract: Energy wells underpin critical technologies in the global energy transition, including geothermal energy extraction, carbon capture and storage, and underground hydrogen storage. In recent years, digital twin (DT) concepts have been increasingly explored to support well design, monitoring, and integrity management. abstract: Critical transitions can irreversibly change complex systems, making anticipation a fundamental challenge. abstract: Long-term time series forecasting is important in energy, transportation, and meteorology, yet existing methods struggle to model multi-scale features and preserve local sequence structure. We propose PatchRNN, a decomposition- and structure-aware framework for multivariate forecasting. abstract: Agricultural green transformation is important for achieving economic growth and environmental sustainability. abstract: Multi-predator feeding aggregations (MPFAs) are ocean events whereby two or more species forage on the same or co-occurring prey. abstract: This study explores the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in enhancing STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) education and workforce readiness in Nigeria. Amid rapid global technological change, Nigeria faces critical challenges in aligning its education system and labour market with AI-driven demands, including outdated curricula, infrastructural deficits, limited digital literacy, and underinvestment in teacher training. abstract: Abstract Liquid-phase separation underpins numerous sectors of modern chemical industry, yet achieving high selectivity for separation of mixtures of organic compounds remains a persistent challenge. abstract: Abstract Interpretable machine learning (ML) is crucial for gaining insight into complex ML models. abstract: Salt marshes are increasingly recognized as important sources of total alkalinity (TA), contributing to coastal carbon sequestration. abstract: Lichens are widely recognized as biological indicators of environmental quality because their physiological condition reflects long-term atmospheric and ecological changes. abstract: The transformation of higher education has increased the need to articulate classroom-based innovation with institutional management and governance processes. abstract: Abstract Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is being investigated for renewable-energy forecasting, optimisation, predictive maintenance, synthetic-data generation, and infrastructure planning. This study reviews global advances and critically assesses their implications for Africa's sustainable energy transition. abstract: Introduction Harmful algal blooms of Alexandrium monilatum and Margalefidinium polykrikoides are a common occurrence in the tributaries of lower Chesapeake Bay, United States of America. abstract: Environmental processes often exhibit complex, non-linear patterns and discontinuities across space and time, posing significant challenges for traditional geostatistical modeling approaches. To overcome this weakness a hybrid modeling strategy can be proposed. abstract: Abstract Mixotrophs, phytoplankton capable of both phototrophy and heterotrophy, serve crucial yet complex roles in ocean food webs and carbon cycling. As climate change is expected to reduce iron bioavailability within upwelling zones, mixotrophs may have an advantage due to an array of possible iron acquisition strategies. title: Evaluation and bias correction of reanalysis wind data for resource assessment and long-term power prediction
abstract: Reliable long-term wind-power prediction requires linking short-term mast measurements with long-term reanalysis data. This study developed integrated methodology using measurements from five coastal and near-coastal sites, four reanalysis datasets, seven Power Law exponent methods, and seven bias-correction techniques. The proposed Day–Hour Lookup-Table Power Law produced lowest average mean absolute error, root mean square error (RMSE) and standard deviation of error of 0.23, 0.35 and 0.33 m/s, respectively, and maintained relative RMSE of 4.31–6.30% during chronological hold-out validation.

abstract: Abstract Floods increasingly interact with anthropogenic pollution sources, remobilize legacy pollution, release emerging pollutants and harm critical infrastructure, transforming hydrologic extremes into compounding pollution disasters. abstract: Infected bone defects are not simply bone defects complicated by bacterial infection; they are dynamic pathological niches in which biofilms, intracellular bacterial persistence, oxidative stress, dysregulated immunity, vascular failure, and pathological bone remodeling are mutually reinforcing. abstract: Cryogenic Electron Tomography (cryo-ET) is an emerging experimental technique used to visualize cell structures and macromolecules in their native cellular environment. title: A South Atlantic atmospheric river dipole as a key precursor of Amazon wildfires
abstract: Wildfires in the Amazon have far-reaching climatic and ecological impacts, yet their predictability remains limited. Here we identify a large-scale atmospheric precursor of August–September Amazon wildfires: a June–July dipole mode of South Atlantic atmospheric rivers (ARs), characterized by suppressed AR activity in the north and enhanced activity in the south. abstract: ABSTRACT Skin‐friendly ionogels with multi‐scenario adaptive, high‐fidelity, and self‐healing performances were critical building units in wearable signal transmission devices. title: A review of forest innovation: Technologies and sustainable practices for environmental conservation
abstract: Forests play a crucial role in climate regulation, biodiversity conservation, ecosystem service provision, and sustainable socio-economic development. However, increasing deforestation, climate change, habitat fragmentation, and unsustainable resource exploitation continue to threaten forest ecosystems worldwide. title: Beyond production: understanding aquaculture narratives, public engagement, and visibility on TikTok and Instagram
abstract: Public acceptance and societal trust are increasingly recognized as critical challenges for sustainable aquaculture development. While previous research has examined consumer perceptions and social acceptance, limited attention has been given to how aquaculture narratives are constructed, circulated, and gain visibility within contemporary digital media environments. This study examines how thematic patterns, sentiment, audience engagement, and narrative construction shape aquaculture communication on TikTok and Instagram. title: Physics-informed CNN and SCS unit hydrograph modelling for urban stormwater discharge prediction in Kolwezi sub-catchments, Democratic Republic of Congo
abstract: Rapid urban expansion in tropical mining cities is increasing stormwater volumes, shortening runoff response times and exposing drainage systems to recurrent surcharge. This study evaluates two contrasting approaches for urban stormwater discharge prediction in the Musonoi sub-catchment of Kolwezi, Democratic Republic of Congo: a physics-informed one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), in which SCS-CN rainfall excess is incorporated as an input feature to constrain learning with hydrologically meaningful runoff-generation processes, and the classical Soil Conservation Service (SCS)

title: Feasibility study of using magnetic and thermoelectric methods for the assessment of storage-induced changes in flux-cored welding wires
abstract: The lack of knowledge regarding whether a welding consumable remains suitable for the welding process or has undergone degradation that precludes its further use constitutes a significant challenge. Appropriate control procedures and effective evaluation methods may contribute to addressing this issue. This study presents the results of investigations concerning the applicability of magnetic and thermoelectric methods for such an assessment. title: Wastewater Generation and Environmental Pathways in Libya: An Evidence-Based National Accounting Framework
abstract: Reliable national wastewater accounts are difficult to construct where direct flow measurements, treatment-plant records, and discharge inventories are incomplete. This study develops an evidence-aware accounting framework to estimate domestic wastewater generation and distinguish sewer-connected from non-networked sanitation pathways across Libya’s 22 administrative areas. title: The furnace of crisis: assessing the European Union’s trajectory toward strategic independence and global actor in the shadow of the Russo-Ukrainian war
abstract: Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine has removed the assumptions on which the post-Cold War European security order rested and has increased pressure on the European Union to act as a provider of hard security rather than primarily as a regulatory and geo-economic power. This article examines whether that pressure is producing meaningful strategic autonomy and a more consequential global role. title: Too little too late? Nationwide carbon trading in China
abstract: China launched a nationwide, rate-based carbon market in 2021. Covering the world’s top C O 2 emitter, compliance depends on the intensity of carbon emissions rather than an absolute cap. We draw on the theoretical literature on rate-based systems to provide the first empirical evidence on an early adopter. Using plant-level data from satellite imagery and machine learning methods, we find that high-efficiency power plants increased electricity generation and C O 2 emissions by approximately 5% relative to low-efficiency plants. title: SAMWater: a prompt-guided multimodal framework for transferable water mapping with the segment anything model
abstract: Accurate and transferable surface water mapping is critical for water resource assessment, flood monitoring, and aquatic ecosystem management, but remains difficult because SAR speckle, optical contamination, heterogeneous backgrounds, and scarce high-quality pixel-level annotations limit robust large-scale mapping. We propose SAMWater, a prompt-guided multimodal framework that integrates Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical imagery, the Segment Anything Model (SAM), and Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3). title: Silica nanoparticles antagonize while titania nanoparticles synergize silver nanoparticle toxicity in zebrafish
abstract: This study investigated the individual and combined toxicity of silver (AgNPs), titanium dioxide (TiO₂NPs), and silicon dioxide nanoparticles (SiO₂NPs) in zebrafish (Danio rerio), with emphasis on acute/chronic mortality, oxidative stress, bioaccumulation, and histopathology. In vitro stability tests showed that SiO₂NPs reduced AgNP stability more strongly than TiO₂NPs, leading to greater sedimentation and a lower silver concentration in the water. title: Isolation and characterization of human skin-derived bacteriophages with antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against coagulase-negative staphylococci
abstract: Abstract Coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS), particularly Staphylococcus epidermidis and Staphylococcus capitis , are significant opportunistic pathogens associated with biofilm-related infections and antimicrobial resistance. Although bacteriophage therapy is a promising alternative to antibiotics, human skin-derived phages targeting clinically important CoNS remain poorly characterized. Four bacteriophages were isolated from facial skin swabs of healthy volunteers, and two (phages Se_20 and Se_42) were selected for detailed characterization. title: Integrating Solid Waste Management into Urban Flood Risk Reduction: A Resilience Framework for Lagos, Nigeria
abstract: This study examines how solid waste management influences urban flood risk in Lagos, Nigeria, and develops an integrated resilience framework connecting waste governance, drainage management, and flood-risk reduction. An integrative evidence synthesis and comparative case-study approach was used to assess peer-reviewed studies, institutional documents, policy materials, and recent reports concerning waste disposal, drainage obstruction, flood exposure, and government and community responses. Quantitative evidence was compared descriptively, while qualitative findings were synthesized thematica

title: Measuring destination image dissonance: A compositional data analysis of cross-media representations in Sanya’s Tourism
abstract: This study examines Sanya's tourism image disparities across cognitive, spatial, and affective dimensions in Press Generated Content (PGC), Tourist Generated Content (TGC), and Official Generated Content (OGC) (2013-2022), comparing pre-pandemic (2013-2019) and COVID-19 (2020-2022) periods. Results show: cognitive consistency in "tourism/hotels" but TGC focusing on "coastal + food" vs. PGC/OGC emphasizing policy elements; spatial misalignment between policy-driven spaces and tourists' preferred spaces, revealing a systematic dissonance between institutional promotion and on-the-ground practice
