title: Anthropogenic sinkholes in the urban fabric of Messina (Sicily, Italy)
abstract: Urban anthropogenic sinkholes are increasingly reported in Messina (Sicily, Italy), where culverted torrents, legacy underground works, and dense utilities intersect a Holocene coastal/alluvial plain. We present an updated, georeferenced inventory of sinkholes within the municipal urban area, built from local press/ web sources and field cross-checks, and we assess spatial relationships with culverted drainage and known urban cavity entrances. title: A global base temperature dataset for residential building energy demand modelling
abstract: Abstract. Accurate building energy demand modeling is critical to decarbonizing regional energy systems. The cooling and heating degree-day models are widely used due to their simplicity and low data requirements; however, the lack of accurate base temperature data limits their performance. In particular, the scarcity of high temporal resolution building energy demand data constrains regional-scale base temperature estimation through conventional methods such as the energy signature method and the performance line method. To address this limitation, this study develops a global regional-scale

title: Every Public Servant Was Once a student: Reimagining Education for Ethical Leadership, Public Service and Good Governance in Fiji and the Pacific
abstract: Not every student will become a public servant, but every public servant was once a student. This simple proposition raises a significant but insufficiently examined question about the wider purpose of education: to what extent does education contribute to forming the values, ethical judgement, critical consciousness and sense of public responsibility of those who later serve within public institutions? title: Hyperspectral Satellite Imagery for Digital Twinning of Boreal Forests
abstract: Digital twins of the Earth require Earth observation data streams that are both spatially continuous and informative about the state of the modelled system. For forests, the standard optical data source is Sentinel-2, whose 10 m multispectral imagery trades spectral detail for spatial resolution; the forthcoming operational imaging spectroscopy missions CHIME and SBG will offer the opposite trade-off with 30-m pixels and hundreds of spectral bands. title: Multidirectional acoustic wave transmission via artificial periodic structures
abstract: This paper presents a unified artificial periodic structure for multidirectional acoustic wave transmission along complex pathways. The structure employs a two-dimensional, three-component unit cell—consisting of a lead core, rubber cladding, and epoxy matrix—whose resonant dynamics are captured by a double-spring model extended with nonlocal inter-cell coupling corrections. title: Identification of Novel PFAS Transformation Products in AFFF-Impacted Surface and Groundwater
abstract: Abstract The widespread use of Aqueous Film-Forming Foams (AFFF) has left thousands of contaminated “hotspots” across North America. In Canada, only 25 per-/polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are regulated in drinking water at 30 ng/L. title: Feature-engineered physics-conditioned DNN with validation-selected ridge residual correction for pore water pressure prediction in clays
abstract: Introduction Accurately predicting pore water pressure is important for evaluating effective stress, deformation, and stability in clayey soils. Methods This study develops an interpretable feature-engineered physics-conditioned DNN with validation-selected ridge residual correction using 42 complete curves from kaolin clay and Mercia Mudstone clay. Complete curves were divided into training, validation, and testing subsets. title: 6PPD-quinone exposure impairs erectile function through dysregulation of the HIF-1α/eNOS/NO axis: multi-omics and in vivo evidence
abstract: Background 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q), a transformation product of the tire antioxidant 6PPD, has emerged as an environmental contaminant with potential reproductive toxicity. However, its role in erectile dysfunction (ED) and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Methods This study integrated network toxicology, transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, machine learning, Mendelian randomization, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and animal experiments to investigate the potential mechanisms linking 6PPD-Q exposure to ED. title: Changes in Physicochemical Properties, Volatile Flavor Compounds and Microbiota in Phascolosoma esculenta Muscle During Frozen Storage at −20 °C
abstract: Phascolosoma esculenta is a valuable marine seafood, which suffers quality and flavor deterioration with the extension of frozen storage time. To reveal the degradation mechanism, physicochemical properties, microbiota, metabolites, and volatiles were investigated in P. esculenta muscle during frozen storage (−20 °C). Water-holding capacity (WHC) decreased to 77.87%, while the content of total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N) and thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARSs) increased to 18.85 mg/100 g and 1.18 mg MDA/kg, respectively. title: SLA-YOLO: A Lightweight SAR Ship Detection Model
abstract: Reliable ship detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery is challenged by speckles, coastal clutter, scale variation, dense berthing, weak target responses, and limited computing resources. SLA-YOLO is a lightweight YOLO11n detector that coordinates established mechanisms across the backbone, neck, and head. title: Shifting mosquito vector ecologies pose new risks for new stakeholders
abstract: Mosquito-borne infectious disease is a major cause of mortality and a significant economic burden worldwide. Variable regional and seasonal patterns make proactive intervention challenging. Here we introduce a machine learning approach trained on satellite and mosquito observational data, improving generalizability to sparse observations while retaining similar positive performance characteristics of models used in standard practice. title: A performance-based multivariable weighting framework for WRF parameterization-scheme selection
abstract: Abstract. The selection of optimal physical parameterization schemes is a major source of uncertainty in WRF model simulations. A comprehensive evaluation of model performance requires simultaneous consideration of multiple output variables. However, existing multivariate approaches often rely on subjective or overly simplistic equal-weighting strategies and lack an objective mechanism to quantify variable importance. title: Landslide susceptibility modelling in Cianjur Regency using landslide numerical risk factor
abstract: Cianjur Regency was often hit by landslides. In 2022, this regency was affected by landslide, leading to several civilian deaths, injuries, along with damaged houses and infrastructure. To minimize the impact, determining landslide susceptibility level was proven to be an essential step in maximally plan- ning disaster management. Therefore, this study aimed to develop landslide susceptibility model in Cianjur Regency using the Geographic Information System (GIS). title: Development of an AI-assisted maritime poetry writing book using tourism posters for junior high school students
abstract: Background- Poetry writing is an important productive literacy skill in the Merdeka Curriculum, yet instruction remains predominantly theoretical. Students may experience difficulties in idea generation, diction, and imagination due to limited contextual and visual support. Objectives- This study aimed to (1) identify instructional needs; (2) develop an AI-assisted maritime poetry writing book integrating illustrated data cards and marine tourism posters; and (3) evaluate its effectiveness. abstract: Traffic-related air pollution constitutes one of the primary threats to public health and environmental sustainability in urban centers worldwide.Historic centers face particular challenges because their narrow streets, irregular urban configuration, and high vehicle concentration during peak hours hinder the implementation of conventional environmental monitoring systems.This research assessed the pollutant emissions generated by vehicular traffic in the historic center of Ayacucho, Peru, an Andean city located at 2,761 meters above sea level with approximately 29,476 inhabitants in the study

title: Core–Shell Molecularly Imprinted Polymer@SiO 2 @Fe 3 O 4 for Low‐Cost and Selective Electrochemical Sensing of Paraquat
abstract: The widespread use of the water‐soluble paraquat (PQ) herbicide has found to be linked with numerous toxic outcomes to humans as well as aquatic animals, while the on‐site and rapid measurement is still challenging due to unsuitability and lack of selectivity of the existing techniques. This study presents a selective, sensitive, and low‐cost electrochemical sensor for detecting residual PQ in water by combining a core–shell molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP)@SiO 2 @Fe 3 O 4 material with a portable screen‐printed carbon electrode (SPCE). title: Quantification of wave–current interactions in a tide-dominated harbour: A fully coupled modelling study of Darwin Harbour, Australia
abstract: The present work investigates the effects of wave-current interactions in a tidally dominant harbour, using Darwin Harbour in Australia as a case study. Numerical experiments were performed using a two-way coupled FVCOM modelling system across five distinct configurations: a hydrodynamic model, a fully coupled wave-current interaction model, a wave model, a fully coupled model excluding wind forcing, and a fully coupled model without swell input. title: First record of the non-native leafhopper Hishimonus hamatus Kuoh, 1976 (Hemiptera, Cicadellidae, Deltocephalinae, Opsiini) in Bulgaria
abstract: We report Hishimonus hamatus Kuoh, 1976 from Bulgaria for the first time. We collected 36 specimens, including a nymph, at eight localities in six widely separated cities. All records originated from urban parks and gardens. Identification was based on external morphology and the male genitalia. The broad geographic spread of the records, from the Black Sea coast and southern Bulgaria to the Danube region in the north-west, suggests that this adventive East Asian leafhopper is already more widely distributed in Bulgarian urban areas than currently documented.

title: Industrial Paradigm of Multidimensional Poverty in Karawang Regency (Determinant Analysis and Policy Implementation)
abstract: Karawang Regency is known as one of the largest processing industry centers in West Java, with the sector's contribution of around 71 percent to GDP on a Constant Price Basis in 2024. However, the dominance of the industrial economy has not been followed by an inclusive poverty reduction: the number of absolute poor people will increase by March 2024, the open unemployment rate remains above the West Java average, and the inequality of expenditure between the poor is widening. title: Influencing factors and genetic model of low-resistivity shales: a case study of the Longmaxi Formation, Southern Sichuan Basin, China
abstract: Low-resistivity anomalies are widely developed in the Wufeng–Longmaxi Formation marine shales of the Sichuan Basin, but their complex conductive mechanisms remain poorly understood, hindering accurate reservoir evaluation. abstract: This study investigates the improvement of a low-plasticity silty soil (ML) sourced from the Gölveren region of Kastamonu province, Türkiye, using lime-based hybrid binders partially replaced with glass powder (GP), blast furnace slag (BFS), and seashell powder (SSP) within the Deep Soil Mixing (DSM) framework. The experimental program was designed using the Taguchi L18 orthogonal array method to determine the effect of control parameters and optimum mixture ratios. title: An adaptive behavioural zero-trust security framework with proactive cryptographic caching for continuous authentication in 5G non-terrestrial networks
abstract: Abstract 5G non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) are key to future global broadband and military communications, but their high latency and dynamic topologies require security approaches beyond perimeter defences and static authentication. To overcome these vulnerabilities, we propose an adaptive behavioural zero trust security framework (BZTSF) for continuous 5G NTN authentication. Our method continuously evaluates node trustworthiness using network signal information processed by an isolation forest machine learning algorithm. title: Mapping Fuel Categories in Mediterranean Regions with Sentinel-2 and PlanetScope Satellite Acquisitions
abstract: Accurate and spatially explicit mapping of forest fuel types is essential for developing integrated wildfire risk management strategies, estimating fire danger, and modeling fire propagation in fire-prone Mediterranean ecosystems. While time series of Copernicus Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery at 10 m spatial resolution have proven effective for regional fuel mapping, severe spectral and spatial ambiguities persist in distinguishing complex canopy structures, heterogeneous shrublands, and pastures. abstract: Industrial and port areas require integrated air quality assessment methods combining monitoring observations, meteorological conditions and atmospheric dispersion modeling. In this study, we have investigated the pollution behavior and industrial source contributions in the Sohar Port and Freezone industrial area of Oman for a multi-year period of ambient air quality monitoring data and meteorological observations and AERMOD dispersion modeling results for PM 10 , NO 2 , SO 2 and CO. title: Water-rich sub-Neptunes and rocky super-Earths around different stars: Radii shaped by volatile partitioning, formation, and evolution
abstract: Despite precise characterization measurements, the nature of planets with radii between 2 and 4 Earth radii -- sub-Neptunes -- remains unknown due to degeneracies in interior models. Nevertheless, the field has compiled an impressive ensemble of small planets with measured masses and radii orbiting different stars. This dataset can be used to test the prediction of large water reservoirs on sub-Neptunes, as proposed by planet formation theory with orbital migration. title: The Struggle for Dominance in the Central Harşit Valley in the XIIIth-XVth Centuries
abstract: The Seljuks arrived in Anatolia long before establishing an official state, during Chaghri (Çağrı) Beg’s western expedition in 1018. After the establisment of the Seljuk State in 1040, the Kelkit Basin, which constitutes the eastern section of the Northern Anatolian route, emerged as one of the primary regions of initial activity during the era of Anatolian conquests. title: Compact target-aware stability-based feature selection for cross-dataset wearable activity monitoring
abstract: Wearable activity-recognition models may lose reliability when transferred across participants, sensor placements, sampling rates, acquisition protocols, and activity definitions. This study evaluates a compact unsupervised target-aware feature-selection strategy for cross-dataset wearable activity monitoring under a pre-specified MHEALTH→PAMAP2 transfer protocol. title: Insights into energy consumption and carbon emissions from freight industry in China
abstract: Against China’s commitments to peak carbon emissions before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2060, the freight industry, a major energy consumer and emitter, demands attention. This study estimated the energy consumption and carbon emissions from the freight industry in China based on the data of 2022–2024 official turnover, energy source types and IPCC “top-down” CO 2 emission factors. title: Equivalent force-based Kalman-type filter and reduced system function for full-field response reconstruction
abstract: Abstract In structural health monitoring, full-field response sensing and monitoring are essential to establish a digital twin model. However, directly measuring all required structural loads and responses is costly and impractical. Simultaneous estimations of structural loads and responses are consequently developed, which is, however, an ill-posed problem. title: Recombinant bacterial β-galactosidases for lactose bioconversion and galacto-oligosaccharide production: a comparative overview
abstract: The increasing demand for lactose-free dairy products, sustainable whey valorization and high-value prebiotic ingredients has intensified the need for efficient bacterial β -galactosidases capable of both lactose hydrolysis and galacto-oligosaccharide (GOS) synthesis. title: A scalable low-supervision framework for longterm land cover mapping: Automated training sample generation and independent validation
abstract: Reliable long-term land cover information is essential for environmental monitoring, yet many regions still lack dedicated datasets. Main obstacles are assembling training labels at national scale without extensive manual annotation and obtaining reference data sufficiently independent of the mapping process to support credible accuracy assessment. Here, we present a scalable, low-supervision framework for national land cover mapping addressing both limitations. title: Rhein-induced free fatty acid generation cooperates with silver ions for biofilm-infected diabetic wound healing
abstract: Diabetic foot infection (DFI) significantly increases the risks of hospitalization and amputation, with biofilm infections caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and carbapenem-resistant Escherichia coli (CREC) being key drivers of treatment failure. Here, we analyzed MRSA/CREC biofilm-infected ulcer tissues from patients using proteomics and metabolomics. abstract: As core infrastructure for global energy distribution, onshore long-distance crude oil pipelines face multiple challenges, including wax deposition, structural stress concentration, and H 2 S release. Traditional non-destructive testing (NDT) techniques, such as eddy current testing and magnetic flux leakage (MFL), suffer from limitations including low spatial resolution, limited penetration depth, and directional blind spots, making high-resolution and omnidirectional defect identification difficult. title: Amine-terminated zirconium metal-organic framework as an efficient adsorbent for lanthanum removal
abstract: The current study developed an amine-terminated zirconium metal-organic framework (UiO-66-NH2) to effectively adsorb lanthanum (La3+) from water. The UiO-66-NH2 was confirmed by various analytical techniques. The optimization of La3+ removal was achieved through response surface methodology. title: Efficient zinc ion biosorption on the biomass of Ericaria selaginoides algae following response surface methodology optimization: uptake behaviors and mechanisms
abstract: Background Biosorption using marine algae biosorbents is a sustainable and effective method for removing of heavy metals from aquatic environments. Methods This study explored the biosorption of zinc ions from aqueous solutions using the biomass of the brown alga Ericaria selaginoides . The impacts of biosorbent dose, pH, and biosorbate concentration were optimized using the Response Surface Methodology (RSM) and 3-D surface plots generated via Design-Expert software. title: Physics-informed parameter identification of fractional-order battery models using Nyquist-based initialization and two-stage metaheuristic refinement
abstract: Accurate parameter identification (PI) of fractional-order models (FOMs) from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) data is essential for battery state estimation but is challenged by nonlinearity, parameter coupling, and local optima. This study compares ten metaheuristic (MH) algorithms for FOM PI, identifying the Marine Predators Algorithm (MPA) as the most robust, with a mean RMSE of 1.09×10⁻⁴ and the lowest standard deviation (1.0×10⁻⁵) over 20 trials. title: Energy Production and Economic Feasibility of a Tidal Barrage System in the Gulf of Khambhat
abstract: Rising need for clean and reliable energy has raised tidal power system interest. The large tidal range in the Gulf of Khambhat has good potential for the extraction of tidal energy. To assess the feasibility of a proposed tidal barrage using harmonic tidal reconstruction and dynamic basin modelling techniques for the purposes of estimating the hydraulic head, turbine discharges and the power production. title: Four Quality-Control Failure Modes in Public Wireline-Log Archives: Measured Effects and a Reproducible Workflow, With Examples From Wyoming and Kansas
abstract: Public wireline-log archives are widely reused in petrophysical and machine-learning studies, yet the processing steps required to make them analytically usable are rarely reported. We processed 1,210 logs from the Teapot Dome archive in Wyoming, together with a 300-well pilot drawn from 29,089 Kansas Geological Survey records, and found four processing failures, each of which produced an error larger than the signal it was supposed to resolve. title: No critical slowing down in the Atlantic Overturning Circulation in historical CMIP6 simulations
abstract: Abstract. The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a key component of the Earth’s climate system, and is theorized to have multiple stable states. Critical slowing down (CSD) can detect stability changes in Earth system components, and has been found in sea-surface temperature (SST) based fingerprints of the AMOC. We look for CSD in simulations from 27 models from the sixth Climate Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP6). title: Limits of questionnaire-based prediction of oral health-related quality of life in non-smokers
abstract: BACKGROUND: Oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) reflects the perceived impact of oral health on daily functioning, psychosocial well-being, and social interaction. While clinical symptoms strongly influence OHRQoL, it is unclear how well OHRQoL can be estimated using only non-clinical information, particularly in non-smoking populations. This study evaluated whether sociodemographic, behavioral, and self-perceived health variables can predict OHRQoL in non-smokers. METHODS: This cross-sectional study recruited 130 adults. title: Catastrophe theory and AHP modelling of landslide susceptibility using multi-source geodata in southwestern Nigeria
abstract: Landslides are among the most destructive natural hazards in mountainous and structurally complex terrains, posing significant threats to lives, infrastructure, and sustainable development. Accurate Landslide Susceptibility Mapping (LSM) is therefore essential for hazard mitigation and land-use planning. This study develops a Catastrophe Theory (CT)-based Landslide Susceptibility Mapping Index (LSMI) that integrates surface and subsurface conditioning factors derived from geological, geomorphological, geophysical, and climatic datasets. title: ACANTHUS ILICIFOLIUS L: ETHNOBOTANY, PHYTOCHEMISTRY, PHARMACOLOGYAND SYNTHESIS OF SILVER NANOPARTICLES (AGNPS)
abstract: Acanthus ilicifoliusbelongs to the family Acanthaceaeis a medicinal plant widely distributed in the coastal areas of tropical and subtropical regions. It has been traditionally used in various systems of folk medicine for managing conditions such as wounds, fever, inflammation, and respiratory problems. Phytochemical investigations have revealed the presence of several biologically active constituents, including flavonoids, alkaloids, phenolic compounds, and terpenoids. These constituents are associated with a range of biological effects, particularly antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and immuno

title: Estimating Twomey forcing sensitivity to aerosol plume spreading rates
abstract: Abstract. The amount of sunlight that reaches Earth's surface can be reduced by increasing cloud droplet number and decreasing droplet size (i.e., Twomey forcing), a central idea underpinning the Marine Cloud Brightening strategy. Cloud albedo depends nonlinearly on cloud droplet concentration, meaning the spatial extent of aerosol plumes could be an important constraint on the brightening potential. title: One health perspectives on pharmaceutical and clinical effluents driving multidrug resistance in aquatic ecosystems: a comprehensive review
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has emerged as one of the most pressing global health challenges, yet the contribution of environmental reservoirs to the spread of multidrug resistance (MDR) remains insufficiently integrated into mainstream discussions. This systematic review synthesizes evidence from 167 peer-reviewed studies published between 2000 and 2026 to examine how pharmaceutical manufacturing effluents and clinical waste drive the dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and multidrug-resistant bacteria in aquatic ecosystems. title: Separating Environmental Modulation From Source Intermittency in Methane Leakage From a Legacy Well in British Columbia
abstract: Abstract Legacy oil and gas wells are an incompletely quantified source of greenhouse gas emissions and offer leakage pathways for subsurface gas migration if inadequately isolated. We present a high‐resolution, process‐based characterization of leakage dynamics at an integrity‐compromised legacy gas well in northeastern British Columbia using five spatial flux surveys and approximately 70 hr of continuous hotspot measurements of methane (CH 4 ) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), integrated with co‐located soil and meteorological observations. title: Intensifying compound drought–heatwave events weaken ecosystem water-use efficiency in the Nile River Basin
abstract: Climate warming has intensified compound drought-heatwave (CDHW) events worldwide, posing growing threats to ecosystem carbon-water dynamics. However, the impacts of CDHWs on ecosystem water-use efficiency (WUE), particularly event sequencing, drought memory, and climatic heterogeneity, remain poorly understood at large river-basin scales. title: Probabilistic Digital Twin Framework for Climate-Resilient Offshore Infrastructure under Coupled Corrosion–Fatigue Degradation and Environmental Uncertainty
abstract: Offshore assets deteriorate through mechanisms that reinforce one another: corrosion removes section and raises the local stress, the elevated stress accelerates fatigue, and fatigue damage exposes fresh metal to the marine environment. title: Geospatial suitability of cacao in Amazonas (Peru): An ensemble predictive modeling approach (BIOMOD2) integrating multisource data, territorial management, and plant health
abstract: Identifying climatically suitable areas for cacao cultivation (Theobroma cacao L.) is essential to guide sustainable intensification, territorial planning, and compliance with emerging environmental standards in tropical regions. This study assessed the current climatic suitability of cacao in the Amazonas department (northwestern Peru) using an ensemble modeling approach implemented in biomod2, integrating bioclimatic, topographic, and edaphic predictors with spatial biophysical exclusion criteria, legal conservation constraints, regulatory eligibility associated with the European Union Defor

title: Stable core rhizosphere microbiota across the entire wheat growth cycle mitigates cadmium accumulation via reducing rhizosphere cadmium Bioavailiability
abstract: Reducing crop cadmium (Cd) uptake via beneficial rhizosphere microbes offers a low-cost, sustainable strategy for ensuring agricultural product safety. Most prior investigations have largely focused on mechanisms examined at single time points or individual functional strains, leaving the stable core microbial taxa that persist throughout the plant growth cycle and the synergistic potential of multi-strain consortia in alleviating Cd stress largely underexplored. title: Predicting environmental health-related search patterns using freely available digital and reanalysis data: A critical evaluation of Google Trends and global datasets for Morocco
abstract: Climate change and environmental degradation increasingly threaten urban public health, yet monitoring infrastructure is often unavailable in resource-constrained settings. This study develops and critically evaluates a machine learning framework that predicts environmental health-related search behavior , used as a low-cost digital proxy rather than a measure of clinical burden, in Morocco using exclusively open-access global datasets. title: How does energy transition in China amidst climate risk shocks influence residents’ welfare?
abstract: China regards energy transition as a significant measure to handle global climate change and foster the harmonious coexistence of human beings and nature. This article matches the urban energy transition index with China Family Panel Studies data to systematically examine and evaluate the impact of energy transition on residents’ happiness. The baseline results indicate that energy transition has improved residents’ happiness. title: Efficient Harmonic Generation Toward High Power Femtosecond Blue‐Green Laser From a Thulium‐Doped Fiber Amplifier
abstract: ABSTRACT Blue‐green ultrafast lasers offer great potential for oceanic optical communication, laser fabrication, and scientific research. title: A comprehensive review of underground CO2 storage and associated risks
abstract: Geological carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) storage has emerged as one of the most promising technologies for mitigating greenhouse gas emissions and achieving global carbon neutrality. This review provides a comprehensive overview of CO 2 geological storage with emphasis on storage formations, trapping mechanisms, storage capacity assessment methods, monitoring techniques, risk assessment, mitigation strategies, and the key factors governing long-term storage security. title: A parametric Morison-inspired model for wave-induced torque fluctuations on a vertical axis tidal turbine
abstract: This paper investigates the effect of surface waves on the hydrodynamic torque fluctuations of vertical axis tidal turbines. Wave-induced orbital velocities and accelerations are shown to generate periodic variations of the incoming flow, leading to significant unsteady torque loads. title: Characteristics and simulation of ozone pollution in Haikou City under combined effects of meteorological factors and pollutants
abstract: Ozone (O 3 ) pollution has become a central concern in regional air-quality management. title: Strategic implications of China-India geo-economic competition for Pakistan (2015-2025)
abstract: The increasing geo-economic competition between China and India has significantly reshaped South Asia’s strategic landscape, positioning Pakistan at the center of an evolving regional power contest. This study analyses the fundamental drivers of Sino-Indian geo-economic competition and its strategic ramifications for Pakistan’s economic development, security posture, and foreign policy orientation. title: Manganese-modified biochar enhances white-rot fungi-mediated lignocellulose humification: insights from molecular transformation and multi-omics analyses
abstract: Humic substance formation is essential for soil health, yet natural humification is slow, and synthetic production is often inefficient. White-rot fungi (WRF)-mediated lignocellulose humification shows potential but is limited by slow substrate degradation. Given the high biocatalytic potential of Mn(II) and its compatibility with the enzyme system of WRF, manganese-modified biochar (MBC) was utilized to enhance the degradation and conversion efficiency of lignocellulose. title: Tampa Bay observing network: a continuous data acquisition system in support of science and environmental management
abstract: The Tampa Bay estuary is a vital ecological and economic hub, whose productive, shallow-water habitats are highly vulnerable to both chronic anthropogenic stress and acute environmental disturbance events (e.g., extreme weather, human incidents). Historically, the bay's health was monitored primarily through low-frequency, monthly field sampling that has provided a foundational baseline of water quality for the last fifty years. title: Implementation Of International Maritime Organization Standards In Seaworthiness Supervision Of Indonesian-Flagged Vessels At The Tanjung Priok Main Port Authority Office
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of implementing International Maritime Organization (IMO) standards in supervising the seaworthiness of Indonesian-flagged vessels at the Tanjung Priok Main Port Authority Office (KSOP), identify the inhibiting factors, and analyze the efforts undertaken by KSOP to ensure compliance with seaworthiness requirements. The study employs a qualitative descriptive approach with a case study at the Tanjung Priok Main Port Authority Office. title: Land suitability analysis for taro (Colocasia esculenta) cultivation based on topo-edaphic variables in a smallholder farming system
abstract: Taro ( Colocasia esculenta ), one of the neglected and underutilized crop species (NUCS), is regarded as a climate-smart crop due to its ability to tolerate harsh environmental conditions associated with climate change. The crop plays a critical role in enhancing food and nutritional security while promoting resilience through crop diversification, particularly in smallholder farming systems in developing countries. title: Beyond Vulnerability: Women’s Water Stewardship and Adaptive Agency in Climate-Vulnerable Bangladesh
abstract: Abstract In Bangladesh, the climate crisis manifests through acute water scarcity, which profoundly disrupts social reproduction, particularly for women. Using a Feminist Political Ecology (FPE) lens, this study explores women’s adaptive agency in daily water management practices at both household and community levels. The study was conducted in three climate-vulnerable regions of Bangladesh: Mongla (cyclone-prone coastal Bagerhat), Naogaon (drought-prone), and Cox’s Bazar (flash flood- and landslide-prone). title: Time capsules of infection: Updating the distribution of Aphanomyces astaci in Croatia using archived crayfish specimens
abstract: The crayfish plague pathogen Aphanomyces astaci Schikora, 1906 is one of the most damaging invasive pathogens affecting European freshwater ecosystems, causing declines in native crayfish populations. In Croatia, crayfish plague was first reported in the late 19 th century and was subsequently molecularly confirmed in 2016. title: Ground-based spectral irradiance for intra-hour photovoltaic power forecasting
abstract: Electricity markets worldwide are shortening their settlement intervals, with Australia adopting 5-minute settlement in 2021 and the European Union now mandating a 15-minute imbalance settlement period across Member States. Shorter intervals sharpen the value of accurate intra-hour photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting at the timescale of cloud-induced ramp events, which broadband irradiance cannot fully resolve. title: Optimizing Logistics Ecosystems: Evaluating the Performance of Smart Port Enterprises
abstract: Abstract The rapid development of smart ports has revolutionized the maritime industry, leveraging advanced technologies and data analytics to enhance efficiency, productivity, and sustainability. However, assessing and optimizing the performance of smart ports remains a complex challenge. This study proposes a comprehensive framework for evaluating and improving smart port efficiency using a Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) approach. title: Detection of old-growth forests using airborne laser scanning and other auxiliary data combined with National Forest Inventory field plot data
abstract: Accurate detection and mapping of old-growth forests (OGFs) are essential for biodiversity conservation and forest management, yet remain challenging due to their structural complexity, rarity and varying definitions. In this study, we developed a framework for classifying OGFs in boreal forests by integrating airborne laser scanning (ALS) data, and multispectral Sentinel-2 imagery and aerial imagery with different modelling approaches. title: Characteristics of Staphylococcus haemolyticus Isolated from Humans and Animals
abstract: Staphylococcus haemolyticus is an opportunistic coagulase-negative staphylococcus increasingly recognized as an important reservoir of antimicrobial resistance within the One Health framework. However, comparative studies simultaneously evaluating isolates from humans and companion animals remain limited. This study characterized 113 S. haemolyticus isolates recovered from clinically healthy and affected humans and cats and from clinically healthy dogs using phenotypic, molecular, proteomic, and genomic approaches. abstract: Introduction High-altitude (HA) illness threatens health after acute high-altitude exposure, but its molecular mechanisms and effective interventions remain unclear. Drug–food homologous (DFH) substances have potential for HA illness intervention, yet their active components and targets are unknown. title: GIS-based assessment of population and dwelling exposure to landslide-prone areas in the Valencian Community (Spain)
abstract: The spatial identification of population exposure to landslide-prone areas is essential for risk-informed territorial planning, particularly where impacts affect peri-urban and dispersed residential areas rather than consolidated urban centres. title: Passive acoustic monitoring for the estimation of density of the singing lemur ( Indri indri )
abstract: Abstract Passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) has emerged as a valuable tool for estimating animal density and abundance, particularly in challenging environments where traditional methods face limitations. In this study, we applied PAM techniques to study the indri ( Indri indri ) in the Maromizaha New Protected Area, a tropical forest in Eastern Madagascar. abstract: Introduction International assessments of maritime cities have shifted from hard infrastructure indicators toward institutional quality metrics such as maritime finance and law and attractiveness and competitiveness. The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA), with its distinctive “one country, two systems, and three jurisdictions” configuration, faces gaps in cross-jurisdictional rule connectivity that may limit its maritime soft power—a challenge that existing single-jurisdiction assessment frameworks do not fully capture, highlighting the need for rule-of-law coordination. abstract: Dental students often experience stress due to the curriculum’s theoretical and practical demands, whichcan negatively affect their well-being. Previous research suggests that room colors and images can reduceanxiety in certain populations. However, no studies have examined this effect among dental students. abstract: The implementation of the policy of direct settlement of cross-provincial medical expenses in China has effectively improved access to medical care for vulnerable migrant groups. Using data from the 2012–2022 China Family Panel Studies (CFPS), this research applies a generalized Difference-in-Differences (DID) model to examine the impact of the policy on poverty among rural older adults, with Propensity Score Matching–Difference-in-Differences (PSM-DID) used as a robustness check. title: Bebas-Aktif and Pragmatic Assertiveness: Continuity and Change in Indonesia’s Foreign Policy under Prabowo Subianto
abstract: This article examines whether Indonesian foreign policy under President Prabowo Subianto (October 2024–August 2026) represents a doctrinal departure from bebas-aktif or a programmatic reconfiguration of strategic autonomy. It develops the Doctrinal Continuity–Instrumental Reconfiguration (DCIR) model, integrating foreign-policy-change theory, role theory, leader-centered Foreign Policy Analysis, and hedging. abstract: We report 100 individuals of the Longfin Batfish, Platax teira (Forsskål, 1775), from the Mexican Pacific. Records include first reports from the Revillagigedo Islands and Michoacán, as well as additional sightings from Baja California Sur, Jalisco, Colima, Guerrero, and Oaxaca. abstract: ABSTRACT Organizations face growing pressure to respond to environmental and social challenges, yet research has not sufficiently explained how organizational actors mobilise dynamic‐capability microfoundations across the development of sustainability‐oriented innovations. Drawing on 68 semistructured interviews conducted between March and November 2024 across 18 EU and UK marine firms, this qualitative study examines how innovation champions and related actors support sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring. title: Hymenoptera of Galápagos: diversity and distribution of one of the most species-rich insect orders in the archipelago
abstract: Despite the importance of the Galápagos archipelago as a key site for the study of biodiversity and evolution, significant components of its invertebrate biodiversity, particularly Hymenoptera, remain insufficiently documented. Occurrence records of Hymenoptera from 1959-2025 were combined from structured surveys of non-formicid Hymenoptera, long-term ant sampling, museum collections, literature, and online sources to assess the richness, distribution, and species composition of hymenopterans across the archipelago. abstract: Accurately detecting shrimp targets in EK80 acoustic echogram images is challenging due to their small size, high-density aggregation, and strong background clutter, which collectively hinder conventional object-detection models. To address these issues, we propose an enhanced detection framework based on RT-DETR. abstract: Monitoring water coverage in intertidal zones is challenging due to the lack of satellite sensors that simultaneously provide both high spatial and high temporal resolution. Landsat offers detailed spatial information but is limited by its 16-day revisit cycle, whereas Himawari-8 provides frequent observations but at coarse spatial scales. title: Impact of Radio Wave Refractivity on Mobile Network Portability Threshold in Bayelsa State, Nigeria
abstract: This study investigates the influence of radio wave refractivity on mobile network portability thresholds in Bayelsa State, Nigeria, focusing on the effects of radio refractivity (W-unit), atmospheric temperature (K), relative humidity (%), and atmospheric pressure (hPa) on mobile network signal strength. A mixed-methods approach was employed, combining field measurements and statistical analysis to assess the Quality of Service (QoS) of GSM network providers in Biogbolo and Etegwe, Yenagoa. title: Colorimetría y atmósfera como constructores de percepción emocional audiovisual: una revisión sistemática.
abstract: El cine y los contenidos audiovisuales están cambiando gracias a la evolución del color y las tecnologías visuales. abstract: Concept Drift Detectors are the methods that are used to identify the patterns and behaviors of data that changes over time. These methods are tested separately on different datasets, which makes it difficult to compare which detector is suitable for particular situation. title: Spatial spillover effects of urban forest policy on urban green production efficiency: evidence from China’s National Forest City Construction
abstract: As environmental constraints tighten and urban green transformation continues, whether National Forest City Construction (NFCC) can improve urban green production efficiency (GPE) and generate cross-regional spillovers remains an important theoretical and policy question. Using panel data for 277 cities at the prefecture level or above in China from 2006 to 2024, this study applies a spatial Durbin difference-in-differences (SDM-DID) model to estimate the effect of NFCC on GPE. abstract: Türkiye’s thermal insulation standard, TS 825, was reissued in its 2024 edition with six climate zones and, for the first time, a cooling component, and it has governed all new building permits since April 2025. abstract: Within the first few years of life, children go from nonverbal infants to fluent users of hundreds of words. abstract: The crucian carp ( Carassius carassius ) has declined markedly in recent decades due to the ongoing invasion of its congeneric species complex, the gibel carp ( Carassius gibelio ) and widespread habitat degradation. In Europe, the crucian carp occurs in two highly divergent phylogenetic lineages: the northern lineage distributed across northern and central-eastern Europe and occurs in the Elbe (Labe) and Oder (Odra) River Basins and the Danubian lineage restricted to the Danube (Dunaj) River Basin. abstract: Background The fucoidan extracted from sea cucumber Pearsonothuria graeffei (Fuc- Pg ) has beneficial anti-inflammatory and lipid-lowering effects, suggesting its potential anti-atherosclerotic properties. Methods ApoE −/− mice were fed a high-fat diet (HFD) for 12 weeks. Fuc- Pg (20 mg/kg and 80 mg/kg) was administered by oral gavage once daily. title: Impacts of needle-leaved forests landscape pattern and environmental factors on the spatial differentiation of pine wilt disease in China
abstract: Following its emergence in China, pine wilt disease (PWD) has continuously expanded, creating substantial risks to regional forest ecosystems. However, most existing research emphasizes climate and other macro-scale associated factors, and lacks long-term and systematic analysis approached through the lens of forest landscape patterns. The research focuses on describing the spatiotemporal dynamics of PWD in China across the period 1982–2020 and identifying the dominant factors influencing its distribution. title: Analysis of amplifying effect of antecedent drought on rainfall-induced shallow landslides
abstract: Abstract Rainfall-induced shallow landslides are typically attributed to short-term meteorological triggers such as rainfall intensity and duration. However, the influence of antecedent hydrological conditions, particularly prolonged dry spells, has received limited attention despite their potential to alter soil behavior significantly. This study investigates the role of antecedent dry spells on landslide occurrence in the clay-rich terrains of the eastern Black Sea region of Türkiye. title: Natural Hazards, Critical Infrastructure Systems, and Resilience Enhancement: A Structured State-of-the-Art Review and a Synthesis-Based Rapid Assessment Framework
abstract: Abstract Critical infrastructure systems (CISs) are increasingly exposed to natural hazards whose impacts are amplified by infrastructure interdependence, urban complexity, and the growing prevalence of compound and cascading events. Existing research provides valuable insights into individual hazards, infrastructure components, modeling methods, and resilience metrics, but these insights remain difficult to translate into preliminary decision support because they are organized across different hazard types, sectors, analytical scales, and decision contexts. abstract: The present overview raises questions regarding the degree of regulation of educational network cooperation between domestic and foreign universities. title: Remote sensing of aquatic nutrients from proxy estimation to integration with process models
abstract: Leveraging its capability for large-scale, repeated monitoring, remote sensing has increasingly supported nitrogen and phosphorus estimation in surface waters. However, the evolution of this field from proxy-based nutrient retrieval to integration with process-based models remains insufficiently synthesized. Here we review remote sensing approaches for estimating aquatic nutrients, with emphasis on their roles in supporting process-based modeling, and compare their methodologies, applications, and limitations. title: Joint determination of factors influencing adoption of climate smart agricultural practices in modern rice production in Southwest Bangladesh: a multivariate probit approach
abstract: Climate change and environmental degradation are increasingly threatening rice production in the coastal regions of the developing world, where the goals of raising productivity and building resilience became a joint priority. Climate smart agriculture offers a portfolio of practices that serve both goals, yet knowledge on how farmers in saline rice systems combine these practices, and why adoption remains often partial, is still limited. abstract: Extended abstract 7-265-26 Reference Dwellings (RDs) underpin Dwelling Stock Energy Models (DSEMs) used to inform national retrofit and decarbonisation strategies. abstract: Abstract: Background: Liraglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA), has preclinical anti-inflammatory and barrier-protective effects, but its safety profile and potential favorable reporting associations in ulcerative colitis (UC) remain uncertain. Objectives: To characterize liraglutide-associated reports in patients with UC and explore biological pathways that may contextualize the observed pharmacovigilance signals. abstract: Background Human leukocyte antigen class II (HLA-II) genes mark several microglial states in Alzheimer’s disease, but it remains unclear how their average transcription relates to tau measured in the same brain region. Methods We used a locked 13-gene HLA-II panel selected by biological function, cross-cohort detection, and variance, without considering effect estimates. abstract: Incorporating the perspectives of local fishing communities and their ecological knowledge (LEK) can enhance policymaking and improve wildlife and economic management strategies. This study aimed to evaluate the local ecological knowledge of fishermen at Beni Haroun Dam regarding the Great Cormorant (Phalacrocorax carbo) a species legally protected under Algerian law, and to reveal their conservation attitudes toward this species. title: Deep protected habitats in the Gulf of Cádiz reveal an overlooked Iberian distribution of Pagurus chevreuxi (Bouvier, 1896) (Decapoda, Paguridae)
abstract: We report Pagurus chevreuxi (Bouvier, 1896) for the first time from Spanish waters of the Gulf of Cádiz, filling a gap in this species’ documented distribution along the Iberian Atlantic margin. The specimen was collected at 418 m depth on Gazul mud volcano during the CIRCASUR2025 survey and identified using diagnostic morphological characters and mitochondrial 16S rRNA sequence data. title: GIS-based spatial prioritization of natural-hazard exposure and recorded COVID-19 case counts in Lemery, Batangas, Philippines
abstract: Local governments often maintain separate natural-hazard maps and health-surveillance records but lack a transparent method for identifying areas where these concerns overlap. This study applied a Geographic Information System (GIS) sieve-mapping approach to prioritize the 46 barangays of Lemery, Batangas, Philippines using 2,505 confirmed COVID-19 cases and ten natural-hazard layers covering seismic, landslide, coastal, flood, and volcanic hazards. abstract: Background. Ginger is a horticultural commodity and a biopharmaceutical crop with many benefits and high economic value. Ginger is widely used as a raw material in the functional food, cosmetics, and herbal pharmaceutical industries. Water content is a critical parameter affecting the quality, storage stability, and activity of bioactive compounds in ginger rhizomes. Purpose. abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive empirical analysis of the economic impact of submarine cable (SMC) infrastructure, which is critical for global digital connectivity and carries almost all intercontinental data traffic. Despite their fundamental role in the digital economy, robust evidence on the economic returns of SMC investments is very scarce. abstract: This study compared three models-a literature-guided, a large language model (LLM)-assisted, and a data-driven model-all developed using Bayesian networks as the framework for predicting angler pressure measured by the number of boats observed in aerial surveys. The models used meteorological data from 98 lakes in Ontario, Canada, during 2018 and 2019, as well as platform-derived variables, including angler-reported fishing trips, fishing duration, and catch rate, together with lake webpage views. title: New Δ246p53 isoform responds to DNA damage to enhance p53 family functions in cellular senescence
abstract: ABSTRACT p53 is with little doubt one of the most powerful genes in our genome, as it makes growth vs arrest, repair vs replacement, catabolism vs anabolism, life vs death decisions in the cell. An alteration or malfunction in p53 may lead to cancer, degeneration or premature ageing. So, it is not surprising that p53 is also one of the most complex and tightly regulated genes, encoding for at least 10 RNA variants and 12 widely accepted protein forms. title: Evolution of Research on Satellite-Based Monitoring for Algal Blooms in the African Great Lakes
abstract: Abstract Algal blooms pose significant environmental and economic challenges worldwide. As their impact increases, there is an urgent need to improve forecasting models that predict their occurrence, development, and trends. Understanding recent research developments in satellite-based monitoring of algal blooms in the African Great Lakes provides a vital foundation for creating effective early warning systems and improving both short- and long-term prediction accuracy. abstract: Background Rising global temperatures and precipitation variability are intensifying extreme weather events and threatening human health worldwide. In Kenya, climate change is projected to significantly alter the distribution and severity of climate-sensitive diseases, particularly affecting vulnerable populations. This study projects climate extremes and associated health impacts in Kenya through 2050 under two emission scenarios: SSP245 (moderate mitigation) and SSP585 (high emissions). abstract: Objective: This study was conducted to determine the mediating role of fall risk in the relationship between loneliness levels and quality of life among older adults living alone.Materials and Methods: The research was a correlational descriptive study. It was carried out with older adults individuals living alone in a provincial center in the Eastern Black Sea Region. The study sample consisted of 131 older adults. title: Ulvan, carrageenan, and fucoidan: comparative immunomodulatory mechanisms and future directions in major algal sulfated polysaccharides
abstract: Sulfated polysaccharides derived from marine algae have attracted considerable interest in innate immunity research due to their structural diversity and pronounced immunomodulatory activities. Ulvan, carrageenan, and fucoidan, derived from green, red, and brown algae, respectively, represent three paradigmatic classes of algal sulfated polysaccharides. Histopathology remains the reference standard, but it does not provide immediate information at the point of surgical specimen assessment. abstract: Any-angle path planning extends traditional graph-based path planning by allowing movement between any pair of vertices, rather than being restricted by predefined edges. It can find straighter and shorter paths in continuous space with graphs, making it particularly suitable for navigation in open areas such as airspaces, warehouses, and oceans. abstract: Extreme salinity is a major environmental constraint affecting plant growth and physiological performance in coastal ecosystems. Although mangroves are naturally adapted to saline environments, their tolerance and physiological responses vary among species, and the effects of exogenous melatonin (MT) under different salinity levels remain insufficiently understood. title: Active Visual Perception: Opportunities and Challenges
abstract: Active visual perception enables an intelligent system to improve perception by controlling how visual evidence is acquired. However, differences in how studies define active perception and evaluate its benefits make approaches difficult to compare across tasks. The study aims to analyze policy implementation based on George C. abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are not environmentally static particles; aging, fragmentation, contaminant acquisition, organic conditioning, and microbial colonization progressively convert them into dynamic particle–chemical–microbial interfaces. abstract: BACKGROUND: Self-rated health (SRH) is a validated holistic indicator of health, yet evidence among seafarers is limited. We examined how health conditions and lifestyle factors relate to poor SRH and whether perceived stress modifies these associations in active-duty seafarers. abstract: Introduction Enteropathy is a significant and under-recognised complication of inborn errors of immunity (IEI), frequently misclassified as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) or coeliac disease due to overlapping and non-specific histopathological findings. Diagnostic criteria remain poorly defined, contributing to substantial diagnostic delay and associated morbidity. abstract: Modelling how mangroves disperse can help prioritize site restoration selection by identifying source populations and linking appropriate restoration efforts with potential site-specific propagule availability. Dispersal modelling approaches are particularly impactful in regions with limited empirical data, like the Middle East. abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the main factors that influence the issuance of green and sustainable sukuk (GSS). Specifically, it investigates how institutional, environmental, and economic pressures shape GSS issuance across countries that have developed this market. abstract: Aerosol–cloud interactions represent a major uncertainty in climate projections. Cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) are particles upon which cloud droplets form, yet in situ CCN measurements remain scarce. Aerosol chemical component exerts important control over CCN activity. abstract: Abstract. Accurate spectral transformation across satellite sensors with similar but different spectral response functions (SRFs) are essential for applying the same retrieval algorithms. abstract: Seagrass restoration increasingly relies on seed-based approaches, yet optimal seeding densities and deployment methods remain poorly resolved. abstract: Microplastics (MPs) have transitioned from a predominantly marine concern to a defining threat facing terrestrial agroecosystems, where croplands now function as one of the largest global reservoirs of plastic particles. abstract: Automatic Identification System (AIS) data provide a large-scale record of maritime vessel movements, yet learning reusable port representations from these routes remains underexplored. This paper investigates whether unsupervised graph representation learning can produce meaningful and operationally useful embeddings for ports in a global maritime port network. abstract: Background Secondary hypertension is under-recognised despite the availability of mechanism-based diagnostic tests and, for several aetiologies, potentially curative or highly targeted therapy. The clinically important question is not only which causes exist, but how reliably mechanisms translate into diagnosis and cause-directed treatment. abstract: Although condition monitoring systems (CMS) provide detailed information about the health of critical wind turbine components, their practical application in wind farm operations and maintenance (O&M) remains limited, significantly diminishing their value. abstract: Tipping points are abrupt, drastic, and often irreversible changes in the evolution of nonstationary and chaotic dynamical systems. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper proposes a Causal‐Aware Dynamic Knowledge Graph (CA‐DKG) framework that systematically fuses FMEA domain knowledge with data‐driven causal discovery from SCADA time series. abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop a modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system and validate its diagnostic performance. abstract: Governments around the world have identified distant water fleets (DWFs) as a key threat to ecosystem health, domestic economic opportunities, and food security. With a high prevalence of undernutrition and micronutrient deficiencies in countries where DWFs operate, the aquatic foods caught by DWFs represent a vital opportunity to shift policy and improve nutrition outcomes. abstract: Local erosion around foundation elements, generally referred to as ’scour’, is of major concern when designing hydraulic structures. When placed in natural open water systems, these structures influence the local dynamics of the flow and bed, which could result in lowering of the embedment level, with potentially severe consequences. To improve the nowcasting accuracy by leveraging complementary information from multi-source data, this study proposes a precipitation nowcasting model based on multi-source data fusion and efficient additive attention (EAA-MNFP). abstract: Abstract There is increasing attention paid to the manipulation of ships’ Automatic Identification System (AIS) signals, with implications for maritime safety, law enforcement, and security. Based on the literature and narrative reports, this paper proposes a framework that answers why and when ships engage in AIS manipulations by tracing the purpose, goals, and strategies of their operators. abstract: High-severity traffic accidents impose substantial human and economic burdens, necessitating proactive and data-driven risk forecasting mechanisms within intelligent transportation systems. This study proposed TRIDENT-Risk, a temporal risk-driven imbalance-optimized ensemble framework for high-severity accident prediction using the eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model. abstract: Introduction Ovarian cancer is the most fatal gynecologic cancer, contributing to approximately 207,000 deaths per year worldwide, largely due to late-stage diagnosis and considerable histopathological diversity across subtypes. Accurate subtype classification is clinically important for prognosis and treatment planning, but remains challenging due to high inter-class morphological similarity and the scarcity of adequately labeled histopathological datasets. abstract: To address the potential data leakage associated with overlapping slicing and the limited generalization capability of rolling bearing fault diagnosis models under strong noise, small-sample, and class-imbalanced conditions, a parallel CNN–BiLSTM–CBAM method based on time-isolated slicing and multi-domain feature fusion is proposed. title: Feature-level fusion of Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical imagery for crop-type mapping in humid tropical mountainous terrain
abstract: Accurate crop-type mapping in humid tropical mountains is challenged by persistent cloud cover, rugged topography, and fragmented smallholder parcels. This study evaluates a feature-level fusion workflow that integrates Sentinel-2 optical indices and Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter for crop-type mapping in Candipuro District, Lumajang, East Java, Indonesia. abstract: An accurate and timely flood prediction that relies on streamflow information is important for developing an early warning system to minimize the negative effects of floods. This paper proposes a new Steam flow-based Flood prediction model using a Fine-tuned MTV19ANet architecture (SFFPM-FTA). abstract: Flood evacuation is an effective protective action, yet decisions to evacuate are shaped by complex interactions among risk perception, household characteristics, and contextual constraints. Empirical evidence on household evacuation during rapid-onset riverine floods in Bangladesh remains limited. Guided by the Protective Action Decision Model (PADM), this study examines determinants of household evacuation during the August 2024 flood in south-central Bangladesh. abstract: Purpose: This study aims to develop a novel nature-inspired metaheuristic optimisation algorithm based on the semi-aquatic behaviour of the red-eared slider (Trachemys scripta elegans). abstract: Abstract. Deterministic model predictions can struggle to adequately capture extreme events such as floods and droughts, which are of particular relevance in hydrology. abstract: Although loss of control (not under command, NUC) is one of the leading triggers of maritime accidents, the quantitative role of human and organizational factors in the process by which it evolves into a risk of grounding and collision has been largely neglected. title: An interaction perspective on situation awareness in human–AI teaming: A scoping review
abstract: Situation awareness (SA) is crucial for effective teaming and is becoming increasingly relevant in human-AI teaming as AI systems take on more active roles. AI systems rely on designed interactions to communicate information and coordinate with humans, which may influence how human teammates perceive, interpret, and anticipate task situations. abstract: Extreme congestion occupies only a small portion of traffic records but carries disproportionate operational consequences for traffic-management systems. abstract: GIScience is crucial for spatial understanding, analysis, and decision-making across multiple sectors. abstract: Chili pepper productivity in Indonesia is highly sensitive to climate variability, particularly solar radiation. This study aims to predict solar radiation to optimize chili pepper productivity across four distinct topographic zones in the Special Region of Yogyakarta. abstract: Abstract Northern Hemisphere snowmelt phenology has shifted earlier over the past 37 years, but Eurasia and North America have followed markedly different trajectories. title: Phytoplankton community composition and environmental associations in Liujiaxia Reservoir under a reverse seasonal water-level background
abstract: In regulated reservoirs, actual water-level dynamics do not always coincide with conventional hydrological periods, yet phytoplankton community variation under such conditions remains insufficiently understood. We investigated phytoplankton communities and environmental conditions at 21 fixed sites in Liujiaxia Reservoir during conventional wet, normal, and dry periods, while water level increased progressively across the three surveys. title: A lightweight residual multilayer perceptron method for geomagnetic matching navigation
abstract: Abstract To address the inherent challenges of localization in regions with weak or ambiguous magnetic gradients, this paper proposes a lightweight residual multilayer perceptron (MLRP) method for geomagnetic matching navigation. By establishing an accurate nonlinear mapping between geomagnetic vectors and spatial coordinates, the proposed method prevents gradient degradation and the consequent decline in accuracy and stability observed in existing geomagnetic matching methods. title: A Simulation‐Based Selective Maintenance Framework for Mission‐Oriented Equipment Systems Using Real‐Time Condition Mapping
abstract: ABSTRACT Selective maintenance for mission‐oriented equipment systems is often simulated from fixed lifetime distributions or static initial ages, which can obscure component‐specific degradation before a mission. This paper proposes a simulation‐based selective maintenance framework that incorporates real‐time condition mapping into mission reliability evaluation. Multi‐domain monitoring features are reduced by kernel principal component analysis and used as health covariates in a Weibull proportional hazards model (PHM) to estimate component‐level equivalent ages. title: Revealing hydrochemical regimes and health risks in an urban karst spring system
abstract: Groundwater in urban karst spring systems is increasingly impacted by coupled natural processes and anthropogenic nitrogen loading, yet the linkage between hydrochemical evolution, nitrate-related health risk, and contaminant transport remains insufficiently resolved. This study develops an integrated framework for the Baiquan spring system by combining hydrochemical analysis, entropy-weighted water quality index (EWQI), probabilistic health-risk assessment, numerical transport modelling, and multivariate clustering. title: Positive-unlabeled graph ranking for assembly-center-oriented resilience-green sustainability evaluation of China Railway Express node cities
abstract: China Railway Express (CR Express) has become an important rail-based logistics corridor for improving Eurasian connectivity, regional openness, and sustainable freight organization. However, evaluating its node cities remains challenging because assembly-center labels are incomplete, city performance is network-dependent, and logistics development is increasingly shaped by resilience and green-sustainability requirements. title: Multi-Isotope Analyses of Colonial Sheep from the Sydney Region, Australia: Implications for Husbandry Strategies
abstract: Abstract Stable isotope analyses of faunal remains have demonstrated significant potential to enhance understandings of human-animal relationships during periods of European colonization. Isotopic analyses enable reconstructions of historical livestock management practices, including diet, provenance, and mobility, while also providing insights into past climatic and environmental conditions. title: FUSED-Net: Detecting traffic signs with limited data
abstract: Automatic Traffic Sign Recognition is paramount in modern transportation systems. However, curating large-scale datasets for diverse traffic sign detection remains impractical. In this context, we present FUSED-Net, a novel approach that enhances Few-Shot Object Detection (FSOD) for traffic signs using limited data. FUSED-Net integrates Faster RCNN with Unfrozen Parameters, Pseudo-Support Sets, Embedding Normalization, and Domain Adaptation to improve detection accuracy. title: Spatio-temporal analysis of land use/land cover (LULC) changes using GIS techniques in Upper Bhavani River Basin, Nilgiri Hills, India
abstract: The study investigates the land use and land cover (LULC) changes in Upper Bhavani River basin of the Western Ghats over the past four decades (1989–2019) using remote sensing (RS) and geographic information system (GIS) techniques. It also explores the correlation between LULC changes and population growth during this period. The study highlights the importance of mapping and monitoring LULC changes in developing better management strategies for the sustainable development of natural resources. title: MontClouDifuser: A diffusion-inspired denoising framework for parcel-level crop type recognition
abstract: High-accuracy crop distribution information is essential for precision agriculture and food security. However, parcel-level crop mapping remains challenging in mountainous terraced regions of southeastern China, where extreme parcel fragmentation and frequent cloud contamination lead to discontinuous optical time series. Here, we proposed SatDiFuser, an end-to-end diffusion-inspired framework for parcel-level crop type recognition from multi-temporal Sentinel-2 imagery. title: TriAlign UDA for hybrid domain adaptation of frozen histopathology foundation model representations
abstract: Foundation models produce strong patch-level representations in histopathological image analysis; however, domain shifts across different centers, staining protocols, and scanner conditions can limit the direct generalizability of these representations. In this study, a hybrid feature-level unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) framework called TriAlign-UDA, which operates on frozen histopathology foundation model representations, is proposed. title: Invited perspective: Uncertainties in natural systems may be uncomfortable, but ignoring them would be absurd
abstract: Abstract. Uncertainties in natural systems are pervasive, varied, and unavoidable due to inherent open system complexity and limited knowledge. Therefore, the evolution of a natural system cannot be predicted deterministically and probabilistic forecasts are commonly used to account for these uncertainties. As the Voltaire-inspired title suggests, representing and quantifying all uncertainties in hazard and risk forecasting is difficult yet essential for an effective risk-cycle management and for a meaningful scientific evaluation of forecasting models. title: MSAL-YOLO: a YOLOv8-based detector for small and densely distributed object detection in UAV aerial imagery
abstract: Abstract Object detection in UAV aerial imagery is challenging because of small object scales, dense distributions, occlusions, and complex backgrounds. To address these issues, we propose MSAL-YOLO, an improved YOLOv8-based detector for aerial object detection. Specifically, a Spatial–Channel Mixed Convolution (SCMConv) module is introduced to enhance local feature extraction by combining standard and dilated convolutions. title: Deer disturbance influences avian acoustic activity across functional groups in temperate forests
abstract: Cervid overpopulation is increasingly altering temperate forest ecosystems worldwide, when browsing pressure exceeds ecosystem resilience, with consequences that extend beyond individual species to the structure and functioning of entire communities. While the impacts of deer ( Cervidae ) on specific bird species are well studied, there remains a critical gap in understanding how deer influence avian communities across a spectrum of functional traits. title: Wetland loss amplifies regional heat exposure: insights from the 2023 Southeast Asia heatwave
abstract: Wetlands play a crucial role in regulating regional climate through their effects on surface energy balance and evapotranspiration. However, rapid wetland loss in Southeast Asia has raised concerns about its potential to intensify extreme heat exposure during heatwaves. This study investigates the impact of wetland loss on regional temperature and human heat stress during the 2023 heatwave in the Cambodia Lower Mekong Delta (CLMD). title: ST-FGDIR: Spatiotemporal Traffic Forecasting with Forecast-Gain-Guided Deviation–Invariance Routing
abstract: Accurate multi-step traffic forecasting requires models to respond to genuine traffic-state transitions while resisting deviations caused by missing or noisy observations. Existing deviation-aware methods characterize departures from recurrent patterns, but deviation magnitude alone does not indicate whether the resulting correction will improve a node-wise forecast. Guided by the insight that correction strength should depend on forecast gain rather than deviation magnitude, we propose Spatiotemporal Traffic Forecasting with Forecast-Gain-Guided Deviation-Invariance Routing (ST-FGDIR). abstract: System prompts have become a consequential behavioral control layer in large language model applications and agentic AI systems. They shape instruction adherence, task completion, tool selection, verification, safety boundaries, escalation, style, and resource use. title: Interpretable water and agricultural land cover in urban landscapes using CNN–ViT framework with Grad-CAM for agricultural sustainability
abstract: Abstract Accurate land-use and land-cover classification in hyper-arid environments is challenging because several surface types can exhibit overlapping spectral and spatial characteristics in Landsat imagery. These surfaces include water, irrigated agriculture, moist soil, barren land, and built-up areas. This study proposes an interpretable hybrid framework for classifying six land-use and land-cover classes in Najran, Saudi Arabia, using seven-band Landsat 8 imagery. abstract: Abstract. When modelling ice flows there are several aspects which are poorly constrained by observations, in particular parameters related to ice rheology and basal sliding. In computational ice flow models, inversion methods are frequently used to estimate the spatial distribution of these hidden fields. abstract: Methanogenic archaea, capable of producing organic matter from hydrogen and CO 2 emanating from the mantle, constitute one of the key functional groups of microorganisms in the deep subsurface. Although the diversity of methanogenic inhabitants of the deep biosphere has been studied in detail, the activity of methanogens in these biotopes remains virtually uncharacterized. title: The prospects of Vietnam’s niche diplomacy in the era of national advancement
abstract: Niche diplomacy is a notable characteristic of the foreign policy of middle powers - states that have the capacity to play a prominent role on the international stage, but are not powerful enough to impose their will on others. Therefore, middle powers need to rely on their ability to identify and fill in “niche spaces” through diplomatic methods and skills, that is, choosing a few specific issues, institutions or areas to specialize in and orient them as important foundations in its foreign policy. title: Enhancing Antarctic terrestrial conservation through biodiversity informatics
abstract: Area-based and species-specific protection provide complementary benefits for biodiversity conservation. Yet, their application to key Antarctic terrestrial invertebrates has been hindered by biodiversity shortfalls, including the prevalence of cryptic species. Here, we use a biodiversity informatics approach combining a new spatially-explicit occurrence database of Antarctic Collembola, comprising 3457 georeferenced records of 22 nominal species, eight of which have cryptic taxa, with a new bioregional ecosystem habitat classification and putative cryptic species information, to assess occurr

abstract: Groundwater is a major water resource for irrigation and domestic use, especially in arid and semi-arid regions where freshwater is scarce and the total amount of rainfall is limited. Hence, monitoring both quality and quantity parameters of this source is necessary for optimal water resources management, environmental studies, and ecosystem modeling, as well as ecological planning. abstract: Object detection in complex scenes requires models that can maintain precise spatial attention and reliable query representations. However, existing CNN and DETR-based detectors often exhibit diffuse cross-attention, weak query initialization, and limited robustness in cluttered or dynamic environments. This paper proposes HyMTAS-GBM, a hybrid multi-head transformer architecture that integrates attention-consensus learning, semantic-guided query selection, and gradient-boosting classification to improve detection reliability across image and video domains. abstract: Over the past decade, artificial light at night (ALAN) has become one of the most spatially extensive anthropogenic disturbances along coastlines worldwide, yet whether its capacity to alter predation is a fixed property of illumination intensity or depends on the ecological context in which it occurs has received little attention. abstract: Dam-break flow modelling involves a trade-off as resolving steep gradients requires high-order discretisations, yet these tend to generate spurious oscillations near discontinuities. Moreover, classical limiters used to suppress such oscillations rely largely on single-parameter algebraic indicator rules.
