title: From concept to action: Driving impact through responsible research practices in the International Polar Year 2032–2033 An early career perspective
abstract: Regions at the poles are warming at rates two to four times higher than the global average, driving profound environmental, societal, and geopolitical changes. As Polar Early Career Researchers with careers extending into and beyond the 5th International Polar Year in 2032–2033, we have a responsibility to shape research practices that are impactful, ethical, and sustainable. We argue that current definitions of research impact often prioritize narrow, quantifiable metrics, overlooking cultural, environmental, and long-term consequences. title: Mathematical Foundation of Digital Twins
abstract: A digital twin (DT) is a computational model that evolves over time to persistently represent the structure, behavior, and context of a unique physical system or process. DTs are characterized by a dynamic and continuous two-way flow of information between the computational model and the physical system. Data streams from the physical system are assimilated into the computational model to reduce uncertainties and improve predictions of the model, which in turn is used as a basis for controlling the physical system, optimizing data acquisition, and providing decision support. abstract: Climate change has intensified the frequency, severity, and geographic reach of extreme weather events, posing growing risks to human and environmental health worldwide. This study is a descriptive-analytical systematic literature review (PRISMA), combined with a case study of an interdisciplinary research group, examining scientific production and official data on global climate-related disasters from 2004 to 2024, with emphasis on historical trends and geographic distribution. abstract: The prediction of compressive strength of ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) is essential for optimizing mix ratios and supporting engineering applications. Traditional testing methods are costly and time-consuming, while empirical formulas often lack generalizability, limiting their effectiveness for precise design requirements. abstract: Low-cost minidrone platforms are increasingly used in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) research for safe indoor experimentation, controller development and engineering education. The Parrot Mambo Minidrone is particularly attractive because of its compact size, onboard sensing, MATLAB/Simulink compatibility and suitability for real-time validation. abstract: Rapid urbanization has altered rainfall–runoff processes in many cities and increased the hydraulic burden on urban drainage systems during short-duration, high-intensity storms. Taking a representative drainage system in Dongxihu District, Wuhan, as a case study, this study investigates urban waterlogging under a 20-year return-period design storm. abstract: Forcing together with radiative responses and natural variability has sharply increased Earth’s energy imbalance (EEI), a key driver of climate change, between 2003 and 2023. Declining anthropogenic aerosol emissions and increasing greenhouse gas concentrations are the leading contributors to the forcing. title: Nanomaterials for Water Purification Towards Global Water Crisis Sustainable Solutions
abstract: Providing the world's increasingly growing population with clean, affordable water is an unprecedented challenge for the 21st century. In the face of climate change and failing water quality, nanotechnology has become the center piece in innovation in this global crisis. This article discusses the ways in which nanomaterials are leading the way in the revolution of the water purification techniques and are providing sustainable means to increase access to safe drinking water around the world. abstract: Remote sensing-based hydrothermal alteration mapping plays an important role in regional mineral prospectivity analysis but remains challenging in structurally complex regions because of spectral mixing, weak peripheral anomalies, and fragmented spatial distributions. This study proposes an integrated spectral–semantic framework that combines Landsat-8 OLI multispectral imagery with AlphaEarth Foundations (AEF) semantic embeddings for hydrothermal alteration characterization and prospectivity evaluation in the Tuwu copper belt, Eastern Tien Shan, China. abstract: Search and Rescue (SAR) robotics increasingly depends on collaborative intelligence to operate effectively in dynamic, uncertain, and time-sensitive environments. Modern SAR missions require coordinated interaction among heterogeneous robotic agents as well as structured collaboration between humans and intelligent systems for perception, decision-making, and adaptive mission execution. title: Wind gusts prediction using multivariate time series classification
abstract: Wind speed intermittency is a key challenge for integrating wind energy into the energy mix. Accurate wind power forecasting in wind farms is crucial for mitigating this issue. A major source of uncertainty in nowcasting and short-term wind power prediction arises from wind gusts. title: Physics-informed uncertainty-aware patch-level graph temporal network for aero-engine remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of the remaining useful life (RUL) of aero-engines is critical for improving system reliability and reducing maintenance costs. However, during operation, aero-engines are inevitably affected by multi-source uncertainties such as sensor noise, operational fluctuations, and external disturbances, leading to complex and non-stationary degradation patterns. abstract: Research on Arctic securitization centers on the Arctic states; non-Arctic observers have received less systematic attention. This article examines Germany, an Arctic Council observer since 1998, and asks how its official framing of the Arctic changed between 2013 and 2024. abstract: Understanding the spatiotemporal association between ecosystem service value (ESV) and human activity intensity (HAI) is essential for coordinating regional ecological protection with sustainable socioeconomic development. Using geospatial data for the Chengdu Metropolitan Area from 2000 to 2020, this study estimated ESV and HAI with an ESV accounting model and an HAI assessment model, and examined their spatiotemporal patterns and associations using bivariate spatial autocorrelation and coupling coordination degree models. abstract: Smart system and participatory process become buzz words in disaster risk management highlighting the importance of those concepts in reducing the impact of disasters effectively. Surabaya, like other cities, put a lot of effort to implement them in their administrative process especially in flood risk management. title: Variability in blue carbon stocks across mangrove forest types in Jamaica
abstract: Mangroves are among the most carbon-rich tropical forests, with much of their carbon stock located in underlying sediments. They play a vital role in climate mitigation and adaptation by offsetting carbon dioxide emissions linked to global warming. Despite their importance, blue carbon ecosystems remain poorly represented in climate policy across the Caribbean, with Jamaica and Belize being the only Caribbean countries to incorporate blue carbon stock values into their Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). Limited standardized information on mangrove carbon stocks across representative f
institutions: University of the West Indies System

title: Cost-driven design and optimization of steel support structures for offshore energy platforms: a review of CAPEX cost models
abstract: Steel support structures for offshore energy platforms require large volumes of steel and complex manufacturing, making them one of the most expensive elements of any offshore project. Capital expenditure (CAPEX), which includes material procurement, manufacturing, transportation, and installation, typically makes up around 70% of the total lifecycle cost of these structures. Although many studies have proposed cost models to support design and optimization, the approaches used vary considerably in terms of scope, methodology, and level of detail. This paper reviews existing CAPEX cost models

title: A geographic grid-based research on the spatiotemporal network of intangible cultural heritage and its impacting elements: The case of Pearl River Basin, China
abstract: This study examines 976 intangible cultural heritage items within the Pearl River Basin. It aims to reveal their static spatial distribution characteristics, dynamic evolution patterns, and influencing factors, laying a foundation for cultural preservation and regional sustainable development in the basin. Employing ArcGIS geographic information systems and methodologies, including Lorenz curves, nearest neighbor indices, kernel density analysis, and geographic concentration indices, the study systematically analyzes the spatial diffusion patterns and dynamic evolution processes of intangible

title: Biofilm‐Mediated Persistence of Salmonella in Poultry Processing: A Comprehensive Review of Isolate Heterogeneity, Stress Adaptation, and Antimicrobial Resistance
abstract: Salmonella enterica remains a major foodborne pathogen in poultry-processing environments, where its persistence is largely attributed to biofilm formation on food-contact and non-food-contact surfaces. Despite extensive research on Salmonella control, persistent contamination continues to challenge food safety due to the complex interplay among isolate-specific traits, stress adaptation, and antimicrobial resistance (AMR). This review critically examines the phenotypic and genotypic determinants associated with Salmonella biofilm formation and evaluates their contributions to persistence, str
journal: Comprehensive Reviews in Food Science and Food Safety

title: Adaptive neuro-fuzzy risk index for safe and interpretable lane-change decisions in Level-3 autonomous driving
abstract: Introduction Highway lane-change maneuvers pose a safety challenge for SAE Level 3 autonomous driving because conventional threshold-based decisions and isolated surrogate safety measures may inadequately capture the coupling between longitudinal braking demand and evolving inter-vehicle gaps. This study develops an interpretable, risk-aware framework for continuous lane-change assessment during maneuver initiation and execution. title: Pathogenicity Analysis of Co‐Infection by Vibrio anguillarum and Rahnella aquatilis Causing Ulcerative Fin Disease in Tawny Puffer ( Takifugu flavidus ): Pathogen Isolation, Histopathology and Apoptosis Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Takifugu flavidus has high edible and medicinal value, and it is one of the pufferfish with high price and good quality in the market. With the expansion of pufferfish farming, the economic losses caused by bacterial diseases are becoming increasingly serious. Among them, ulcerative fin disease is one of the typical diseases. In this study, dominant strains were isolated from T. flavidus suffering from ulcerative fin disease, and artificial infection experiments were conducted using these strains. The dominant strains were identified by colony morphology, physiological and biochemical
institutions: Liaoning Ocean and Fisheries Research Institute

title: Biology and conservation of the European mudminnow (Umbra krameri Walbaum, 1792): an update of the monograph 30 years after the first international workshop
abstract: During the three decades following the publication of the first comprehensive monograph on the European mudminnow ( Umbra krameri Walbaum, 1792), knowledge of the species’ biology, distribution, genetics, ecology, and conservation has expanded substantially. In several countries, a dynamic distribution pattern has become apparent, with many local populations seemingly disappearing while new populations continue to be documented. institutions: Institute of Marine Biology of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine

title: On the tracks of Pulvis Puteolana: provenance and selection of Roman hydraulic materials
abstract: Abstract Phlegraean pozzolana played an important role in the production of Roman hydraulic mortars, capable of enhancing mechanical strength even in contact with water. For this reason, this geomaterial was widely exported along the Mediterranean coasts (ROMACONS Project). Nowadays, the term pozzolana is strictly referred as the unconsolidated facies of the Neapolitan Yellow Tuff (NYT; ca. 15 ka), while the term pozzolan suits any fine-grained, mainly glassy volcanic ash as well as commercial products exhibiting pozzolanic activity. This study characterizes pozzolana stricto sensu and two inc

title: Development trends and driving mechanisms of coordination in the Digitalization–Urban development–low-carbon transition system
abstract: Against the backdrop of sustainable development and China’s Dual Carbon Goals, Digitalization, Urban Development, and Low-carbon Transition continuously interact to shape urban sustainable development. However, the long-term coordination of the Digitalization–Urban Development–Low-carbon Transition (DUL) system and its underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. To address this research gap, using panel data for 289 prefecture-level and above cities in China from 2010 to 2024, this study constructs the DUL system and applies the CRITIC-Entropy Weight Method to evaluate the developm
institutions: Shaanxi University of Science and Technology

title: GSDD-net: an efficient feature extraction method for gear-surface defects in complex industrial environments
abstract: Gear surface defects vary in scale and often exhibit subtle local features that are obscured by complex metallic backgrounds. However, achieving high detection accuracy and robustness with computationally lightweight models remains challenging in complex industrial inspection settings. We propose GSDD-Net, a lightweight framework based on the YOLO architecture for detecting gear surface defects. institutions: North China Institute of Aerospace Engineering

title: Hybrid Physics-Informed Reinforcement Learning for Plasma Characterization in Electrical Wire Explosions
abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of discharge observables in electrical wire explosions is challenging due to the inherent nonlinearities in plasma behavior, especially when experimental datasets are limited. This study presents a hybrid physics-informed modeling framework that combines analytical scaling laws with a reinforcement learning-based residual correction strategy to improve prediction accuracy across the charging-voltage range of 9.0–12.9 kV. title: The impact of along-strike variations in overriding plate thickness on subduction dynamics and mantle flow
abstract: Subduction zones are inherently three-dimensional systems and exhibit pronounced trench-parallel variability in key observables, including the deformation style of the overriding plate, trench migration rates, slab geometry, and mantle flow patterns. Geodynamic models typically invoke external mantle flow and/or along-strike variations in the properties of the subducting slab to explain this variability, often neglecting the influence of the overriding plate, despite growing evidence of its strong control on subduction dynamics. In this study, we use self-consistent three-dimensional numerical
institutions: Instituto Andaluz de Ciencias de la Tierra

title: AI literacy and STEM education: emerging frontiers and research priorities
abstract: Abstract This article examines the state of the art in AI literacy and STEM education and identifies emerging frontiers and research priorities to inspire cutting-edge empirical and theoretical research. The reviewed research is grounded in established AI literacy frameworks and shows that there is potential for students’ development of a critical and technologically informed AI literacy. However, the research is unevenly spread across the STEM disciplines and the potential for AI to transform STEM learning remains unclear. title: Long-term changes and attribution of lake water levels on the Tibetan Plateau revealed by multisource satellite altimetry data
abstract: ABSTRACT Monitoring Tibetan Plateau (TP) lakes is constrained by harsh environments and methodological limitations. To overcome the limited spatiotemporal coverage of single-mission satellite altimetry and the shortcomings of conventional linear analyses, we integrated CryoSat-2 and Sentinel-3A/B altimetry observations with a multilevel robust anomaly-detection framework to generate water-level time series for 11 representative TP lakes (2010–2026). title: Land use change, driving factors, and multi-scenario projections of ecosystem service supply in the Yangtze River delta urban agglomeration
abstract: Rapid urban expansion has intensified regional human-land conflicts and ecological risks. This study examines the Yangtze River Delta Urban Agglomeration the key urban cluster development areas in China, using multi-source spatial data and integrated modeling approaches, including the Integrated Valuation of Ecosystem Services and Tradeoffs (InVEST) and Patch-level Land Use Simulation (PLUS) models, to analyze land use changes from 2000 to 2020 and assess ecosystem service dynamics for 2010–2020, and project future land use patterns under three development scenarios for 2030 and 2060. The resu

title: A sensorless and explainable decision-support framework for risk-aware photovoltaic cleaning prioritization in desert environments using public environmental datasets
abstract: Abstract Photovoltaic (PV) systems in desert environments experience substantial soiling losses, while dedicated soiling sensors can increase monitoring cost and maintenance burden. This study develops a sensorless, risk-aware decision-support framework for PV cleaning prioritization using daily NASA POWER meteorological data, with PVGIS-SARAH3 used as an independent solar-resource consistency check at the target coordinate. journal: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science

title: A Review of Fault-Tolerant Reconfigurable Architectures for Autonomous Systems Based on Redundant Logic Mapping
abstract: Mission-critical applications (aerospace, automotive, and defense) have autonomous systems that must have very high reliability to allow continued operation in varied environmental structures and fault conditions. The medium of flexibility and adaptability of the computer hardware is represented by reconfigurable computing platforms and, especially, by Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) and Coarse-Grained Reconfigurable Architectures (CGRAs). journal: SCCTS Journal of Embedded Systems Design and Applications

title: The Effects of Smoothing-Induced Weak Annotation in Mineral Prospectivity Mapping
abstract: Abstract The meaning of targets in data-driven mineral prospectivity mapping (DD-MPM) is foremost dependent on the quality of data. The resolving power of annotated data depends on the ratio of annotated area or volume and target footprint. At sufficiently large-scales of DD-MPM, it is impossible to match annotated area and covariate resolution to the footprint of mineral deposits. Consequently, information exposed to data modelling is unrestricted to between a target and its features. title: Mapping rainfed cereals and olive groves using Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and topographic data in northern Morocco
abstract: Accurate discrimination of agricultural crop categories in heterogeneous, rainfed landscapes remains challenging because crop spectral responses are strongly influenced by environmental variability and complex terrain. This study assessed the contribution of optical (Sentinel-2), radar (Sentinel-1), and topographic variables to the binary discrimination of annual rainfed cereals and perennial olive groves in the Tangier–Tétouan–Al Hoceima region of northern Morocco, a Mediterranean mountain environment characterized by fragmented agricultural systems and rainfed conditions. Institut Agronomique et Vétérinaire Hassan II

title: Retrieval-to-abstraction LLM-assisted literature synthesis: Case demonstrations in digital health technology-enabled randomized controlled trial outcome reporting
abstract: Systematic reviews of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) support evidence-based clinical advancement. Clinical trial reporting guidelines, including CONSORT, establish common data elements that support systematic synthesis of published trial outcomes. However, the rapid rise of digital health technologies presents new challenges for reporting guidelines, and substantial real-world reporting heterogeneity has been observed. Therefore, machine-assisted evaluation of reporting adherence offers a pathway for more agile information management to accommodate the diverse and disruptive nature of dig

journal: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering

title: Spectral signatures of zenith sky radiance from surface-based sky radiometers: implications for clear- and cloudy-sky detection
abstract: Abstract. Accurate identification of clear- and cloudy-sky conditions is essential for reliable aerosol and cloud retrievals from ground-based remote sensing observations. This study investigates the spectral characteristics of zenith radiances measured by SKYNET sky radiometers and evaluates their potential for distinguishing clear- and cloudy-sky conditions based on wavelength dependence. Analyses of normalized spectral zenith radiances at multiple sites representing diverse atmospheric environments, including urban, maritime, tropical continental, and polar regions, revealed systematic diff

title: CellDiffusion: Enhancing scRNA-seq data integration with accurate inference of cell-cell association
abstract: Integrating single-cell transcriptomic datasets across laboratories, conditions, and technologies remains challenging because of cell type-specific batch effects and heterogeneous biological compositions. Current methods often fail to separate genuine biological variation from technical noise, misaligning distinct cell populations or leaving batch effects uncorrected. To address these challenges, we present CellDiffusion, an unsupervised graph-based model that propagates cellular features through a diffusion process to strengthen meaningful cell-cell associations in data integration. publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science

title: Radionuclide identification for plastic scintillation detectors by backward cumulative channel sum
abstract: Abstract Large-area plastic scintillation detectors are widely used in radiation portal monitors, but their Compton-dominated spectra provide limited radionuclide-specific information. We evaluated backward cumulative channel sum (BCCS) combined with non-negative least-squares (NNLS) decomposition and compared it with raw-spectrum NNLS using an explicit background template and detector-specific five-window NNLS. title: Assessing the resilience of water supply infrastructure to climate variability: a current status assessment in rural India
abstract: Abstract Rural Indian communities, characterised by the decentralised and informal nature of water governance, are extremely vulnerable to climate shocks that impair local water supply infrastructures (WSIs). This study assesses WSI resilience in the face of current climate variability and examines the multidimensional elements that influence resilience results. The research uses a participatory, bottom-up, mixed-method approach to apply the “How Tough is WASH (HTIW)” framework across four rural communities—Srayikkadu (Kerala), Ahirpurwa (Bihar), Kali Nagar (West Bengal), and Kanti (Haryana),

title: Modeling and Manufacturing 3D Geometric Figures for STEM Training of Engineering Students: A Staged Methodology and Case Study
abstract: This article presents a methodology for modeling and manufacturing three-dimensional (3D) geometric figures. The need for developing the methodology is substantiated, and its significance for the STEM training of future specialists in engineering specialties is demonstrated. An advantage of the methodology is the clear structuring of all its stages, levels, and steps, which simplifies the process of implementing STEM projects. journal: International Journal of Engineering and Manufacturing

title: Multi-year temporal and seasonal abundance patterns of common bottlenose dolphins near Sarasota, Florida
abstract: Long-term demographic monitoring is critical for understanding population stability and responses to environmental disturbance. Bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ) inhabiting Sarasota Bay, Florida, have been studied by the Sarasota Dolphin Research Program since 1970. While most dolphins in the resident community are individually identifiable via photographic-identification (photo-ID), direct census datasets are largely unavailable elsewhere. A previous Sarasota study used capture-mark-recapture (CMR) surveys and robust-design models to estimate abundance across four seasons in 2015. Th

title: Assessment of vulnerability and economic losses of typical Chinese ports under the influence of tropical cyclones
abstract: The shipping industry is vital to global trade, with China’s ports leading in scale for years. However, the growing threat of climate change, especially tropical cyclones, poses serious risks to port operations, infrastructure, and supply chains, resulting in substantial economic losses. This study assesses the resilience and economic impacts of tropical cyclones on five key Chinese ports, using Shanghai, Shenzhen, Qingdao, Xiamen, and Qinzhou as case studies. title: Cross-robot open-set fault detection via normal-only adaptation and residual latent-space alignment
abstract: Reliable fault detection and health monitoring of industrial robots are important for smart manufacturing in Industry 4.0. However, robotic platforms differ in their mechanical design, sensing characteristics, and operating conditions. These differences make it difficult for data-driven models to generalize to unseen robots and working conditions. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a cross-robot framework for open-set fault detection using only normal data from the target robot. title: Generative topology inverse design of periodic ventilated acoustic metamaterials
abstract: Ventilated acoustic metamaterials can provide sound attenuation while maintaining airflow, but their inverse design remains challenging because acoustic insulation and ventilation are coupled with high-dimensional, non-unique topology-performance relationships. This study proposes a generative topology inverse design framework for periodic ventilated acoustic metamaterials. A dataset of binary pixelated unit cell topologies is generated in an axisymmetric design domain with a central ventilation channel, and the first phononic bandgap bounds are obtained using Bloch periodic theory. institutions: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

title: Trend Analysis and Prediction of Land Use and Land Cover (LULC) Change in General Santos City
abstract: This study analyzed land use and land cover (LULC) changes in General Santos City and predicted possible future LULC patterns for 2043 and 2063. It quantified changes in six LULC classes from 2003 to 2063 using a quantitative geospatial modeling approach. Landsat Imagery was the primary dataset, while validation points from historical imagery and spatial drivers, including aspect, elevation, slope, and distance to roads and rivers, were incorporated into the model. LULC maps were generated through supervised classification and validated through accuracy assessment before being used in the CA-A
journal: Research Frontiers International Journal of Social Science and Technology

title: PM 2.5 air quality index in major cities. long memory analysis with fractional integration
abstract: This article presents new evidence on the persistence, seasonality, and trends of fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) Air Quality Index (AQI) across twenty global megacities from January 2014 to January 2026. The research applies a fractional integration approach to model the long-memory dynamics using high-frequency daily data. Rather than relying on standard binary unit root tests, we adopt the fractional integration framework, which provides a continuous measure of the degree of persistence. title: A balanced set of standardized affective environmental images for climate change research
abstract: Evocative visual imagery is central to research on affective pathways of environmental engagement, yet existing stimulus sets often overrepresent negative imagery and make it difficult to compare positive and negative affective responses under comparable conditions. We developed a balanced database of affective environmental images designed to support controlled comparisons of positive and negative environmental imagery. title: Probing Atmospheric Gravity‐Wave‐Relevant Representations in a Weather Foundation Model via Multi‐Method Fine‐Tuning
abstract: Abstract Weather foundation models pretrained on reanalysis data may encode subgrid‐scale physics beyond their forecasting objectives. Using Aurora, we probe this with a multi‐method fine‐tuning framework: agreement across structurally different adaptation strategies signals shared backbone information, while a matched randomly initialized control isolates pretraining's contribution. We evaluate six methods (0.5%–100% of trainable parameters) for predicting ERA5‐resolved, T21‐filtered gravity‐wave momentum fluxes (313–1,820 km). title: Lightweight Artistic Style Classification via Texture Correlation and Adaptive Local–Global Fusion
abstract: Artistic style classification remains challenging because visually similar styles often exhibit subtle differences in brushstrokes, textures, colors, and global composition. To address this problem, this paper proposes a lightweight artistic style classification framework based on a MobileNet–Transformer Hybrid (MTH). First, a Lightweight Texture Correlation Module (LTCM) is introduced to capture multi-scale texture relationships from intermediate convolutional features. title: Implementation of a New Paradigm for Hydrometeorological Support for Enterprise Leaders and the Public for Adaptation Purposes
abstract: The aim of the article is to increase the efficiency of hydrometeorological support users for the population and enterprises leaders by implementing a new paradigm. The failure of enterprises to account for all climate and change-related risks, combined with the absence of systematized and formalized impact forecasts and recommendations for preventive actions, leads to increased losses. To establish a modern hydrometeorological support system, the paper proposes an implementation integrated approach of an end-to-end data processing scheme ‒ spanning from observation to decision support. title: SymbolFusion uses relation constraints in neurosymbolic graph learning to model literary structure and emotion trajectories
abstract: Abstract Literary texts contain recurring imagery, typed symbolic relations, and long-range emotion shifts that sequence models do not represent explicitly. This paper presents SymbolFusion, a relation-constrained neuro-symbolic graph framework that predicts imagery and symbolic candidates from raw text, validates three literary relation types through an auditable node-relation compatibility function, and propagates emotion only across valid graph paths. title: Natural and Horizontal Visibility Graphs of EEG Power Spectra for Autism Spectrum Disorder Classification
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is primarily identified through behavioral and developmental assessment, which may require specialist expertise and considerable time. Electroencephalography (EEG) offers non-invasive neurophysiological information, but reliable ASD classification remains challenging because EEG signals are nonstationary and highly variable across individuals. This study evaluates whether visibility-graph topology derived from EEG power spectral density (PSD) curves provides complementary information beyond conventional spectral descriptors. title: PELATIHAN PERAWATAN MOTOR TEMPEL KEPADA OPERATOR DAN AWAK KAPAL SUNGAI DI DESA MUARA PADANG KABUPATEN BANYUASIN
abstract: Keandalan motor tempel merupakan salah satu faktor penting dalam mendukung keselamatan dan keberlangsungan operasional kapal sungai. Keterbatasan pengetahuan dan keterampilan operator serta awak kapal dalam melakukan perawatan preventif dapat meningkatkan risiko gangguan mesin selama pelayaran. Kegiatan Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat (PkM) ini bertujuan meningkatkan pengetahuan dan keterampilan operator serta awak kapal sungai dalam melakukan pemeriksaan dan perawatan dasar motor tempel. title: From Demand Signals to Retail Decisions in Business Intelligence Research
abstract: Retail analytics has moved beyond improving point forecasts, yet evidence about the value of a forecast for pricing, replenishment, fulfillment, and managerial adoption remains dispersed.This structured review compares 36 journal studies published from 2023 through 2025, identified within a search window ending in January 2026, across four connected areas: demand forecasting (12), pricing and commercial levers (7), inventory and fulfillment (8), and decision systems (9).Each study is examined for its information setting, analytic approach, decision connection, and evidence boundary.The synthes
journal: American Journal of Business and Operations Research

title: When the Night Stops Cooling: Modeling Extreme Warm Nights Across California Weather Stations
abstract: This paper investigates which factors influence extreme warm nights across California using NOAA GHCN-Daily station observations. We defined extreme warm nights using station-specific 95th percentile summer TMIN thresholds based on a historical baseline period. For each station-year, the percentage of valid summer nights classified as extreme warm nights was calculated. title: Domain adaptation affects adversarial robustness in autonomous steering models
abstract: Abstract Domain adaptation is commonly used to transfer autonomous steering models across regions with different road configurations, such as from right-hand to left-hand traffic. While prior work has largely evaluated adaptation using clean target-domain steering accuracy, its effect on adversarial robustness remains insufficiently understood. This study evaluates two steering architectures, PilotNet and ResNet-18, under four adaptation strategies: U.S.-trained, flipped U.S.-trained, U.S.-trained + fine-tuned, and flipped U.S.-trained + fine-tuned. title: Extracting X (formerly Twitter) information to improve relief logistics: social media analytics to the rescue
abstract: Purpose During sudden disasters, information is needed on victims’ needs and locations, resource availability, and first responders’ status to improve relief logistics; this study aims to extract this critical information from X (formerly Twitter). Design/methodology/approach Using social media analytics and the capture-understand-present approach, the authors rank users and their posts to identify relevant data to support humanitarian operations. title: Latent Structure in Chess Positions
abstract: En este trabajo entrenamos autoencoders para entender representaciones latentes de posiciones de ajedrez. Utilizamos una base de datos de partidas de Lichess filtradas por nivel de juego y control de tiempo, y representamos cada posición como un tensor de múltiples canales. Entrenamos un autoencoder para reconstruir dichas posiciones y posteriormente analizamos el espacio latente mediante Análisis de Componentes Principales (PCA). title: Improving Employee Performance Through Occupational Health and Safety Compliance: A Study at the Makassar Port Authority
abstract: This study was conducted to determine the effect of the implementation of the occupational safety and health management system (SMK3) on employee work productivity at KSOP Utama Makassar. The results of this study indicate that, simultaneously (F-test), occupational safety and occupational health have a significant positive effect on employee work productivity, accounting for 87.6%. The remaining 12.4% is attributed to other variables not studied by the researcher. title: Reptiles in the One Health ecology of antimicrobial resistance, with insights into zoonotic pathogens: reservoirs, transmission pathways, and public health implications
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is a growing global health challenge at the interface of human, animal, and environmental health. Reptiles—including wild populations, pets, farmed species, and internationally traded animals—are increasingly recognized as participants in One Health AMR networks, occupying ecological interfaces that facilitate interactions among wildlife, domestic animals, humans, and the environment. title: The rise of agentic AI in drug discovery from static tools to autonomous virtual scientists
abstract: Driven by large language models, AI agents are transforming drug discovery, enabling AI to break free from task-specific tools and advance toward the vision of autonomous virtual scientists. This perspective reviews applications across the R&D lifecycle. To evaluate system maturity, we introduce a 6-level "Spectrum of Agentic Autonomy." We advocate for novel evaluation paradigms centered on full-chain traceability and outline adoption barriers, positioning AI agents as pragmatic scientist-in-the-loop co-pilots.

title: Modeling and optimization of battery-based energy storage systems for UAVs
abstract: The paper presents the improvement of the energy efficiency of drones used in different missions. In this paper, a model for Li-ion batteries is created, made through equivalent electrical circuits. This method facilitates the examination of the relationship between the required energy consumption and the electrical response of the battery to demands. title: Benchmarking time-series foundation models for multitask predictive maintenance in digital twins
abstract: Digital twins provide a comprehensive virtual representation of physical assets, distinguishing themselves from traditional control systems through long-term diagnostic and prognostic capabilities. However, current digital twin architectures face a critical scalability barrier: they rely on dedicated, single-purpose models for every distinct query, task, physical scale, and operating context, resulting in unsustainable engineering overhead. title: Hydrogeochemical characteristics, controlling processes, and irrigation suitability assessment of groundwater in the Sanjiang Plain, China
abstract: Abstract Groundwater is vital for global irrigation water supply, and its quality directly affects sustainable agricultural development. However, studies on irrigation water quality and its dominant controlling factors in semi-humid regions remain limited. Therefore, taking the Sanjiang Plain as a case, hydrochemical analysis, irrigation water quality assessment, and multivariate statistical methods were employed to systematically reveal the hydrogeochemical characteristics, irrigation suitability, and their dominant controlling mechanisms. title: Review article: Mountain flash floods: from hazard formation to disaster risk reduction pathways
abstract: Abstract. Flash floods in mountainous regions are becoming more frequent and destructive under climate warming, yet cross-regional understanding of their triggering mechanisms, cascading impacts, and governance remains fragmented. This review synthesises 1,967 studies published during 2000–2025 to establish a globally comparable baseline of mountain flash-flood research. title: Analytical Noise-Variance Assessment of Receiver-Side Optical Filtering for Background-Noise Mitigation in Free-Space Optical Communication under Atmospheric Turbulence
abstract: Receiver-side optical filtering trades useful-signal attenuation against noise suppression in free-space optical communication. abstract: Abstract Autonomous environmental telemetry requires continuous, maintenance‐free power sources capable of driving commercial sensing electronics. This study reports the development of a self‐powered bio‐electrochemical sensing platform utilizing a garden soil‐based microbial fuel cell (s‐MFC) coupled with a hybrid power management system (PMS) to drive a commercial off‐the‐shelf (COTS) carbon monoxide (CO) gas sensor. title: Instability-Aware Digital Twin Control for Grid-Constrained Low-Carbon Smart Ports
abstract: Modern smart ports combine terminal electrification, shore power, renewable generation, storage, and digital operational control under uncertain vessel traffic and time-varying grid limits. This study develops a simulation-based digital-twin control prototype that synchronizes vessel flow, berth occupancy, equipment activity, shore-power demand, renewable supply, battery state, grid import, and modelled emissions. title: Copper and zinc from slurry applications shape grassland soil microbial community structure in a long-term experiment
abstract: Soil microbes are crucial in maintaining soil and plant health, underpinning agronomic productivity. This study investigates antimicrobial copper- and zinc-laden cow and pig slurry applications on soil microbial community structures in an approximately 50-year long-term slurry experiment on a permanent grassland located in County Down, Northern Ireland. Illumina and PacBio rRNA sequencing (analysing 16S and ITS genera) were used to investigate soil samples (to 15 cm depth) from the experiment’s treatments. title: Historical climate extremes in Europe and the connection between spring precipitation and summer heat
abstract: Abstract. Hot European summers are often preceded by dry springs such as in 2022, but also in 1473 or 1540, two well-known summers of catastrophic heat. Spring precipitation deficits deplete soil moisture levels, which can amplify extreme summer temperature anomalies in Europe through land-atmosphere feedback mechanisms and altered atmospheric circulation. However, the link is not particularly strong, and hence long time series might help to better elucidate the mechanisms. abstract: Study region Shenzhen, China, is a densely urbanized subtropical megacity characterized by extensive impervious surfaces, rapid runoff responses, and frequent rainfall-induced inundation. Study focus To address the underestimation of urban inundation depth driven by severe zero-inflation, this study proposes a two-stage Cascaded Multi-scale CNN-ConvLSTM Network (CMC-Net). title: Mutual Adaptation and Influence: Review of Latent Dynamics Models in Human–Robot Interaction
abstract: Recent advances in robotics have enabled more dynamic and interactive roles when working with humans. This progress is enabled in part by latent state models, which allow the robot to predict human actions in a compact and tractable way. This paradigm has allowed robots not only to respond and adapt to human behavior but also to anticipate and plan proactively through the use of latent dynamics models. abstract: Transmission corridors in high-altitude and micro-topographic regions are chronically subjected to strong electromagnetic pulse interference, multi-physics field coupling, and extreme climatic stressors. This results in temporal asynchrony and spatial mismatch in multi-source monitoring data, while environmental disturbances cause confidence drift in single data sources. title: Interpretable Symbolic Regression Modelling of Stacking Sequence Effects in Jute/Ramie and Jute/Flax Hybrid Composites
abstract: In this study, a symbolic regression-based framework was developed to investigate the tensile and flexural behavior of natural fiber-reinforced hybrid composites with different stacking sequences. Experimental data from eleven six-layer laminates, including jute, ramie, flax, jute/ramie, and jute/flax configurations, were reanalyzed. Due to the limited dataset size, the proposed approach was considered an exploratory and interpretable modelling framework rather than a universal predictive model. title: Neuromorphic Devices for Extreme Environments: State‐Variable Reliability and Stabilization Strategies
abstract: ABSTRACT Neuromorphic devices are increasingly considered for edge‐intelligence systems operating in spaceborne, aerospace, nuclear, cryogenic, and other harsh environments, where local decision‐making is constrained by limited power, communication bandwidth, and latency. Reliable operation in these environments requires more than the preservation of basic electrical functionality because neuromorphic computation is physically encoded in material and interfacial state variables. title: Abrupt permafrost thaw overwhelms vegetation-driven erosion reduction in sediment export on the Tibetan Plateau
abstract: Vegetation greening and abrupt permafrost thaw are reshaping sediment dynamics across the Tibetan Plateau, yet their relative effects on sediment delivery remain poorly quantified. Here we show that retrogressive thaw slumps are disproportionately important sediment sources, with erosion rates two to three orders of magnitude above undisturbed landscapes and source-to-channel connectivity generally exceeding 60%. title: Evolution of Architectural Design: A Historical Analysis of the Rivers State Government House from Independence to Present
abstract: The architectural transformation of the Rivers State Government House serves as a lens for examining the interplay between political authority, historical influence, and cultural identity in Nigeria. This study traces the evolution of its design from colonial-era structures to modern government complexes, analysing how governance, modernisation, and external architectural trends have shaped its development. title: Wind Power Scenario Generation Based on Dual‐Domain Generator and Improved Spectral Bias Generative Adversarial Network
abstract: Scene generation is a core technology for quantifying wind power uncertainty. Addressing issues such as insufficient scene realism and low spectral matching accuracy in traditional generation models, this paper proposes a frequency domain generative adversarial network (FD‐GAN) method for wind power scene generation based on a dual‐domain generator and improved spectral deviation. title: Real-world user interactions with large language models for explaining home electrocardiogram reports
abstract: With the development of portable electrocardiogram (ECG) devices, users can conveniently obtain physiological data in home settings, yet they still face an interpretation gap because of limited medical knowledge. Large language models (LLMs) may help bridge this gap through natural-language explanations, but large-scale real-world evidence on how users interact with them in home settings remains limited. abstract: The influence of aerosols on climate is determined not only by their global distribution but also by their composition. However, so far, a large fraction of the development efforts for satellite-based aerosol retrievals has focused on inverting from different single instruments the total column aerosol optical depth (AOD), as measure of the total abundance of atmospheric aerosols. title: Green English language teaching approach to develop critical reading skills and environmental awareness among secondary school students for girls
abstract: The present study examined the effect of using green English pedagogy to develop critical reading skills and environmental awareness among secondary school students for girls. Sixty Jordanian grade 9 EFL students participated in the present study. They were enrolled in the Serfa secondary school for girls, education directorate of Lwa'a Al-Qasr. title: Strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa) cultivation in India: A critical review of status, constraints and future directions
abstract: Strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa Duch.) is an economically important berry crop worldwide, due to its distinctive flavour, nutritional value and health benefits. In recent years, it has been cultivated not only in temperate regions, but also in subtropical and tropical regions. It has become one of the high-value horticultural crops in India, due to the growing consumer demand and good returns to farmers. abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the effects of different proteases on the extraction, flavor profile, and oxidative stability of blackthroat seaperch (Doederleinia berycoides) liver oil obtained by aqueous enzymatic extraction. Trypsin-assisted extraction yielded oil with the greatest oxidative stability. Combined analysis by gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry identified aldehydes as the characteristic volatile compounds in the liver oil. title: A dual-enhanced random forest model for fatigue life prediction under multi-level variable amplitude loading
abstract: To address two limitations (hyperparameter sensitivity and black-box fitting) of random forest (RF) models in predicting fatigue life under multi-level variable amplitude loading, a dual-enhanced random forest model (Dual-ERF) is proposed. First, Q-Learning reinforcement learning is introduced to improve the Langevin Equation Evolution (LEE) model, forming the Q-LEE model. title: Mycosphere microbiome assembly and metabolic reprogramming in Phallus rugulosus revealed by multi-omics integration
abstract: The mycosphere, defined as the soil zone influenced by fungal hyphae, hosts a distinct microbiome that plays a critical role in host development. Nevertheless, the assembly rules and metabolic functions in macrofungi remain poorly understood. This study aims to disentangle these processes in the edible fungus Phallus rugulosus . abstract: Aiming at the preheating balancing process in hot air drying of cylindrical Chinese herbal medicines, a one-dimensional radial cylindrical heat mass transfer numerical model is established to reveal the evolution law of internal temperature and moisture content within short time scale. title: Periodic Water-Quality Variation at the Dicle Dam Intake and the Limitations of Sentinel-2-Derived NDWI and NDTI
abstract: This study jointly evaluated physicochemical and microbiological water-quality data from 16 samples collected at the Dicle Dam intake structure in January, March, June, and September between 2022 and 2025, together with the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) and Normalized Difference Turbidity Index (NDTI) derived from Sentinel-2A imagery. title: THE ROLE OF ENGLISH IN MODERN EDUCATION
abstract: This article highlights the relevance and importance of learning foreign languages in the modern world and education system. In the process of globalization, international cooperation, the development of science and technology are making knowledge of foreign languages an important competence. The article analyzes the role of learning foreign languages in personal development, academic success and intercultural communication. It also considers issues of increasing the effectiveness of language learning through the use of innovative methods and information technologies in the educational process

title: Inclusive finance and biodiversity risk: addressing environmental challenges, improving urbanization landscape resilience and sustainable development
abstract: Introduction Biodiversity loss ranks among the most severe global risks of the coming decade, with the World Economic Forum’s 2025 Global Risks Report identifying it as the second greatest long-term threat to economic stability. Digital financial inclusion (DFI) has expanded rapidly in China and is often argued to enable green transformation, yet direct empirical evidence on its effect on emissions and biodiversity outcomes at the provincial level remains limited. abstract: Mackerel (Scomberomorus commerson) processing by-products represent an abundant yet underutilized protein source that can be valorized into bioactive peptides through microbial fermentation. This study investigated the α-glucosidase inhibitory and antibacterial activities of hydrolysates produced from fermented mackerel muscle, skin, and mixed by-products using Pediococcus pentosaceus IL13, with ultrafiltration applied to enrich low-molecular-weight peptides (<3 kDa). title: Reservoir-computing-based chaos synchronization and its application to medical image encryption
abstract: Abstract Chaos synchronization provides a physically interpretable route for generating common dynamical states at spatially separated terminals, but most existing schemes require an accurate model and explicitly injected actuation. This paper develops a data-driven synchronization framework based on reservoir computing (RC) that learns nonlinear state couplings directly from observed trajectories. abstract: A generic data-assisted control architecture within the port-Hamiltonian framework is proposed, introducing a physically meaningful observable that links conservative dynamics to all actuation, dissipation, and disturbance channels. A robust, model-based controller combined with a high-gain decentralized integrator establishes large robustness margins and strict time-scale separation, ensuring that subsequent learning cannot destabilize the primary dynamics. abstract: This paper investigates the seismic control of a 40-story high-rise building equipped with a Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) and an Active Tuned Mass Damper (ATMD) while considering Soil–Structure Interaction (SSI) effects. The structure is evaluated under four foundation conditions, including fixed-base, soft-soil, medium-soil, and dense-soil cases. abstract: Abstract. The TV-SAT signals received by the ground antennas of Satellite Microwave Links (SMLs) can be opportunistically used for identifying and quantifying precipitation. Hence, SMLs can serve as low-cost rainfall sensors complementary to conventional instruments. However, a significant challenge for opportunistic sensors, such as SMLs and their terrestrial counterpart, i.e., commercial microwave links (CMLs), stems from potential ownership issues, possibly hindering progress in the development of processing tools and validation studies. title: Isolating the exposomic impact of acute war and displacement within chronic crisis using multimodal, AI-enabled phenotyping
abstract: Abstract Wars often unfold within contexts of prolonged instability, yet little is known about how acute conflicts interact with cumulative exposomic adversity to shape mental health processes. Here we studied clinical and subclinical symptoms in a Lebanese sample across three groups—one assessed before the 2024 war and two assessed after, with or without displacement—within a shared background of chronic crises. title: High-Resolution Burned Area Mapping Using Sentinel-2 Imagery and Robust Satellite Techniques
abstract: High accuracy in burned area (BA) mapping is desirable for many fire-related applications. Most operational products are based on coarse-resolution satellite data with a final spatial resolution ranging from 250 m to 1000 m. The use of higher-resolution satellite data, such as that from the Multispectral Imager (MSI) on board Sentinel-2, is usually reserved for generating BA products only for specific countries and time periods. title: Microplastics at the ‘roof of the Americas’: widespread presence in snow on Mount Aconcagua, Central Andes, Argentina
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) pollution has emerged as a pervasive contaminant in remote environments; however, its occurrence in high-altitude snow remains poorly constrained. Here, we provide baseline evidence of MP contamination in snow from four mountaineering camps on Mount Aconcagua (6,962 masl), the highest peak in the Americas and in the entire Western and Southern Hemispheres. Microplastics were identified using µFTIR-ATR spectroscopy. title: Pan-genomics in One Health: linking pathogens, hosts, and environments
abstract: The One Health approach recognizes the interdependence of human, animal, and environmental health for managing global health challenges. The increasing incidence of zoonotic diseases, antimicrobial resistance, and environmental degradation underscores the relevance of integrated surveillance strategies. In this context, pan-genomics has emerged as a valuable tool for characterizing the genetic diversity of bacterial pathogens across hosts, geographic regions, and ecological niches. abstract: Microplastic research is an emerging field of study, and we do not yet fully understand the scope or effects of microplastic pollution. Microplastics are ubiquitous in the environment, but the field suffers from a lack of unified, accessible protocols and an ecosystems approach to evaluating microplastic contamination. During autumn 2020, we collected water, mussel, and sediment samples from five sites along the Yadkin–Pee Dee River Basin, North Carolina. title: First record of Chaetophiloscia elongata (Dollfus, 1884) from Belgium (Isopoda, Oniscidea, Philosciidae)
abstract: The Belgian terrestrial isopod fauna currently comprises 38 species, with only two from the family Philosciidae recorded until now. We report the first occurrence of Chaetophiloscia elongata (Dollfus, 1884) in Belgium, discovered in 2025 in a managed but microhabitat-rich garden in Brussels. This finding adds both a new species and genus to the Belgian fauna and represents a northward extension of the species’ known range in continental Europe, further supporting the ongoing expansion of Mediterranean isopods in anthropogenic environments outside their native range. abstract: Abstract This study aims to enhance roadway support effectiveness and construction efficiency. The study proposes a synergistic technology integrating roof grouting with active support techniques in stratified mining environments, enhanced by deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms that adaptively optimize grouting parameters in real time. A mechanical model of a roadway in stratified mining is established, along with a grouting parameter optimization framework based on Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG). abstract: Electrified container ports are coupled logistics–energy systems in which uncertain vessel arrivals determine berth occupancy, shore-power activation, cargo-handling intensity, and the residual demand balanced by renewable generation, battery storage, and the utility grid. This study develops a scenario-based stochastic framework linking a non-homogeneous vessel-arrival process to queue-consistent berth occupancy, congestion-responsive demand, photovoltaic and wind uncertainty, battery dispatch, and grid exchange. abstract: The country parks in Beijing’s Second Green Belt are important to urban green space expansion and recreation. Therefore, exploring park visitors’ real needs and expectations has practical significance. Online review data and the LSTM model were used to analyze and systemically study four aspects of the country park – location layout, landscape environment, functional service, and physical and mental perception. abstract: Introduction Plant-derived functional additives have gained increasing attention as sustainable alternatives in aquafeed. This study aims to investigate the effects of dietary monolaurin on productive performance, innate immune indicators, antioxidative effects, and gut flora in largemouth bass ( Micropterus salmoides ). abstract: The modulation of rainfall extremes by the Madden–Julian Oscillation (MJO) over Indonesia and the Maritime Continent is well established, but less is known about how consistently this relationship is represented in documented large-scale flood-impact records. This study provides an event-based assessment of active MJO phases 3–5 on high–very high (HVH) rainfall associated with large-scale flood events across seasonal rainfall zones (ZOMs). abstract: Abstract Impact-based flood-damage assessment integrates hydrometeorological information with vulnerability and exposure data to generate comprehensive evaluation of flood damage. This study uses the Integrated Land Simulator to assemble an impact-based flood-damage assessment framework for Typhoon Hagibis (2019), one of the most powerful typhoons to strike Japan in recent years. abstract: Optimization of drying parameters of periwinkles (Turritella communis) using Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to obtain high quality product, it is very vital as improper drying conditions can affect the composition of the dried Periwinkles and thereby increases the risk of it running into deterioration of the nutrient contents of the product and post-harvest loss. abstract: ABSTRACT This article proposes a novel and practical prescribed time control (PPTC) method for strict feedback nonlinear systems (SFNSs) subject to input saturation and sensor faults. title: Scale‐space image analysis for mapping spotted knapweed in grassland ecosystems
abstract: Premise: This study investigates the value of scale-space representations of spatial features for the identification and mapping of invasive plants using high-resolution multispectral imagery. Scale-space representations combine the two-dimensional spatial domain with a third dimension representing spatial scale, such that features can be represented across both space and image spatial resolution. title: Seasonal wetting and drying dynamics drive greenhouse gas emissions across Australia’s river network
abstract: Streams and rivers are major contributors to global emissions of carbon dioxide and methane, yet seasonal hydrological variability in discharge and river surface area is often not fully represented in large-scale emission estimates. Here, we integrate riverine and dry riverbed carbon dioxide and methane data with geospatial data of the Australian drainage network to predict emissions at a monthly time-step. Traditionally, long-term wind speed series are derived from short-term site observations combined with reanalysis products, most commonly the ERA5 single-level data at 10 m and 100 m heights. abstract: Large language models routinely produce factually incorrect or misleading outputs, yet conventional automated benchmarks overlook how users perceive reliability during interaction. We introduce the System Hallucination Scale (SHS), a lightweight instrument modeling the famous System Usability Scale (SUS) and System Causability Scales (SCS). abstract: Abstract. This study enhances the snow model of the Canadian Land Surface Scheme including Biogeochemical Cycles (CLASSIC), with a particular focus on Arctic environments. Key snow model physics improvements include adjustments to the thermal conductivity at the top of the first soil layer, a revised computation of the temperature at the snow–soil interface (hereafter, bottom snow temperature), and the addition of a windless exchange coefficient in sensible heat flux calculations. title: A meteorological big data-driven method for generating chaotic time-series curves of power supply loads for wind-solar-storage hybrid systems
abstract: The wind-solar-storage hybrid system represents an efficient and clean energy supply mode. However, its power supply load is influenced by multiple factors and exhibits complex chaotic time-series characteristics, which pose significant challenges to system operation scheduling and load forecasting. title: A 256-year daily rainfall record reveals multiscale rainy-season variability and emerging hydroclimatic hazard over northern East Asia
abstract: Monsoon rainy seasons shape water supply and flood hazard across northern East Asia, but their long-term variability remains poorly understood because few daily rainfall records extend beyond the instrumental era. Here, we reconstruct rainy-season onset, retreat, and duration from a 256-year daily precipitation record for Seoul (1770-2025), providing an unusually long view of seasonal monsoon behavior. title: Sampling-based integrated design optimization of floating wind turbine substructures with Pywind
abstract: Abstract Design optimization of floating wind turbine (FWT) substructures remains computationally demanding due to the extensive time-domain simulations required to explore high-dimensional design spaces. This study builds upon the previously developed Pywind-based integrated design optimization (IDO) framework, extending it by comparing two sampling strategies: Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) and Maximin LHS. title: A Gateway-Based Approach for Integrating Digital Compass Data into Controller Area Network (CAN) in Precision Farming Systems
abstract: The integration of high precision orientation sensors into resilient communication infrastructures is a key requirement for next-generation autonomous systems. Digital compass sensors typically generate data in the NMEA format, whereas distributed control architectures in mobile robotics predominantly utilize the CAN 2.0B protocol. This study presents the design and implementation of a microcontroller-based hardware-software gateway that enables seamless interoperability between these heterogeneous communication standards within autonomous agricultural platforms. title: Study on water transport and optimization of water management strategy to improve performance of a proton exchange membrane fuel cell
abstract: Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are considered a promising energy source for future applications due to their outstanding characteristics. During PEMFC operation, in addition to electricity and heat generation, water is produced through electrochemical reactions within the fuel cell, which significantly influences cell performance. Therefore, water generation and transport must be carefully considered. title: Emergent constraints improve near-term temperature projections over China: Evaluations against observations based on the preindustrial baseline
abstract: Abstract Emergent constraints are widely used to reduce uncertainties in climate projections, yet their reliability has rarely been evaluated against observations. We apply an established emergent constraint approach based on historical global surface air temperature (GSAT) trends and local residual warming trends to temperature change projections over China during 2006-2025 in the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project phases 5 and 6 (CMIP5/6) ensembles. title: Microbial cell factories for gamma-linolenic acid biosynthesis: metabolic engineering, downstream processing, and future perspectives
abstract: Gamma-linolenic acid (GLA) is a vital anti-inflammatory polyunsaturated fatty acid, yet its traditional supply from plant seeds such as evening primrose and borage is constrained by low yields and climatic instability. Consequently, microbial cell factories present a sustainable and season-independent alternative for scalable GLA production. This review critically synthesizes recent biotechnological advancements in utilizing oleaginous microorganisms as production platforms. title: Long-term spatiotemporal dynamics, hotspot persistence, and extreme AOD days over Bursa, Türkiye
abstract: Satellite-based aerosol optical depth (AOD) enables long-term monitoring of atmospheric aerosol loading in regions with sparse ground-based observation networks. In this study, the spatial and temporal variability of 550 nm AOD over Bursa during 2003–2025 was investigated using Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) Multi-Angle Implementation of Atmospheric Correction (MAIAC) MCD19A2 Collection 6.1 data at 1 km spatial resolution. title: Nonlinear Analysis for Extended Pile Shaft Under Combined Vertical and Lateral Loads
abstract: ABSTRACT The lateral response of partially embedded single piles, referred to as extended pile shafts, subjected to combined vertical and lateral loads is investigated using a novel analytical method that explicitly accounts for the P ‐Δ effect caused by axial pile force and the layering of foundation soils. An iterative load‑transfer method is proposed to determine the axial force profile along the pile, while a modified conical strain wedge (CSW) model is developed to better characterize the nonlinear horizontal pile‑soil interaction. title: Fault detection filter design for unmanned surface vehicle systems via an improved dynamic event-triggered protocol under deception attacks
abstract: This paper focuses on the fault detection filter problem for unmanned surface vehicle systems via an improved dynamic event-triggered protocol under deception attacks. Taking into account factors such as external disturbances and potential system faults, a motion model for the unmanned surface vehicle system in a complex environment is constructed. To alleviate communication burden and enhance design flexibility, an improved dynamic event-triggered protocol with dual internal dynamic variables is introduced. title: Robust Multi-Turn-Rate IMM-EKF Algorithm for Maneuvering Target Tracking under Model Mismatch and Measurement Faults
abstract: Reliable maneuvering-target tracking is difficult when the motion-model bank is incomplete and range-bearing measurements contain dropout, bias, burst noise, or impulsive outliers. This study proposes a robust multi-turn-rate interacting multiple-model extended Kalman filter (RMT-IMM-EKF) that combines six motion hypotheses with statistically normalized componentwise innovation clipping. title: Evaluating alternative trade network configurations under geopolitical risk: a multi-scale systems approach
abstract: Rising geopolitical risks and supply-chain disruptions have increased interest in transport-network diversification and alternative connectivity systems. This article presents a scenario-based comparison between a traditional maritime chokepoint configuration centered on the Strait of Hormuz and a prospective diversified multimodal corridor connecting the Middle East and Europe. The study is grounded in an integrated theoretical framework that combines Geopolitical Risk Theory with a systems-based approach, operationalized through a multi-scale analytical framework (macro–meso–micro). title: A geospatial and community perception analysis of the impacts of land use and land cover change on ecosystem service values
abstract: Rapid urbanization in developing countries is causing significant changes in land use and land cover (LULC), which affect ecosystem service values (ESVs). This study investigates the impacts of LULC changes on ESV in the Gazipur city area of Bangladesh over a 30-years from 1991 to 2021. The analysis was conducted using satellite imagery from Landsat-5 TM (1991 and 2006) and Landsat-8 OLI-TIRS (2021), with a supervised classification approach to prepare LULC maps and the Benefit Transfer Method for ESV evaluation. We used the global coefficient values proposed by Costanza et al. 1 and the updat

title: A STUDY OF UNIVERSITY STUDENTS' SEAFOOD CONSUMPTION BEHAVIOR: SOCIO- ECONOMIC FACTORS AND CONSUMPTION TRENDS
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the seafood consumption behaviors of university students and the factors influencing these behaviors. The study was conducted with 118 students, and the relationships between consumption frequency, reasons for consumption, reasons for non-consumption, purchasing preferences, and demographic variables were analyzed. The findings revealed that students generally consumed seafood rarely or only 1–2 times per month. Taste and freshness were identified as the primary motivations for seafood consumption, while health-related factors played a secondary role. Among the

title: Beyond Linear Regression: A Non-Linear Hygroscopic Growth Correction for Satellite-Derived PM2.5 Estimation in Tropical Environments
abstract: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) estimation from satellite-derived Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) is often biased in humid tropical environments because aerosol water uptake enhances optical extinction without a corresponding increase in dry particulate mass. This study develops a physics-informed, non-linear AOD-to-PM2.5 conversion framework that explicitly accounts for hygroscopic growth. journal: Indonesian Journal of Environmental Management and Sustainability

title: IMU- and LSTM-CNN-based multi-gait recognition for a lower limb exoskeleton
abstract: This study presents a platform-specific and subject-independent validation of an IMU-based LSTM-CNN gait-recognition pipeline on a self-developed lower-limb exoskeleton. Ten healthy participants performed five locomotion modes, including level walking, stair ascent, stair descent, standing up, and sitting down. Each participant completed five level-walking trials and ten trials for each of the remaining four locomotion modes, resulting in 450 original recording trials. IMU signals collected from the thigh, shank, and foot were segmented using a 128-sample sliding window with a 64-sample step.

title: From landscapes to lesions: Pathology's role in wildlife mortality investigations and conservation health
abstract: Abstract To effectively recognize and manage wildlife mortality events, we need to understand who, what, why and how – who are the individual animals and species involved; what are the surrounding circumstances in time and space in which they are found; what are the causes and contributors to illness, injury and/or death; why is this happening in this time and place? And ultimately, how should we best surveil, mitigate and/or manage the event (and perceived risks of similar future or related events) based on potential population health threats. title: Toponymic knowledge infrastructures in five-state Middle Asia: linguistic transformation, manuscript cartography, and historical-geographical reconstruction
abstract: Toponymic records embedded in Arabic, Persian, and Chinese manuscript traditions provide evidence for reconstructing the historical geographies of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. This review uses a structured narrative and conceptual-synthesis methodology to compare place-name transmission across languages, scripts, manuscript genres, and political regimes. title: Emerging Hydroclimatic Signals of Global Climate Change in Equatorial Indonesia: Evidence from Borneo Island
abstract: Global climate change has become an increasingly pressing environmental issue, with significant impacts on atmospheric, hydrological, and ecological systems across the globe. Borneo Island is a strategic region for climate change studies, given its extensive tropical forest cover, peatland presence, and rapid land-use changes due to human activities such as deforestation and oil palm plantation expansion. These changes not only affect local conditions but can also amplify feedbacks to the regional climate system through changes in evapotranspiration, albedo, and the hydrological cycle. This st

title: From resource orchestration to robustness and resilience: the role of data analytics capability in bulk commodity maritime supply chains
abstract: Introduction Bulk commodity maritime supply chains are increasingly exposed to climate-related disruptions, geopolitical tensions, port congestion, transportation uncertainty, and other external shocks. However, limited attention has been paid to how firms transform dispersed supply chain resources into capabilities that support both disruption resistance and recovery. title: Investigation of the effect of albatross bill impact on CFRP and GFRP wind turbine blades using Diomedea exulans collision scenarios
abstract: Wind turbine blades are highly vulnerable to damage from transverse loads such as bird collisions, which can compromise structural integrity, reduce aerodynamic efficiency, and raise ecological concerns. This study employed finite element simulations in Abaqus Explicit to examine the collision of a Diomedea exulans (wandering albatross) bill with Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymer (CFRP) and Glass Fiber Reinforced Polymer (GFRP) blades. title: A differentiable multi-physics learning model for robust single-image dehazing under complex atmospheric conditions
abstract: Restoring clear visibility from a single hazy image remains a challenging inverse problem when multiple atmospheric phenomena jointly affect image formation. In real environments, light propagation can be influenced not only by particle scattering but also by turbulence-induced blur and wavelength-dependent attenuation. Most existing dehazing approaches primarily address scattering, which limits their physical consistency and robustness in heavy haze or long-range scenes. title: Antioxidant, Cholinesterase-Inhibitory, and Antiproliferative Potential of Sparganium erectum Extracts
abstract: In the present study, the antioxidant capacity, cholinesterase-inhibitory activity, and antiproliferative effects of Sparganium erectum extracts were investigated. Antioxidant analyses showed that the ethanol extract had a total antioxidant status (TAS) of 2.925±0.023 mmol/L, a total oxidant status (TOS) of 10.116±0.042 µmol/L, and an oxidative stress index (OSI) of 0.346±0.003. title: A mixed-integer linear programming approach to container terminal layout optimization: application to the port of Piraeus
abstract: Abstract This study addresses the issue of designing a container terminal layout by developing a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) mathematical model. The methodology is applied to Pier II of the Piraeus Container Terminal. The mathematical formulation of the problem systematically incorporates real-world spatial constraints and operational factors related to container storage areas, while evaluating alternative scenarios to identify optimal layouts. title: Spatial differentiation and potential influencing factors of land-surface heat exposure based on street-view imagery: a case study of Luolong District, Luoyang
abstract: Introduction Against the backdrop of increasingly frequent extreme heat events, mitigating land-surface heat exposure on urban streets is crucial for safeguarding public health. Existing studies have often overlooked the spatially differentiated effects of complex street environments on land-surface heat exposure and the associated cooling thresholds. Therefore, this study takes Luolong District, Luoyang, as a case study to investigate the spatially heterogeneous effects and nonlinear threshold characteristics of street-view metrics on land-surface heat exposure. title: Modeling Hydrogen Fuel Cell of High-Speed Passenger Ship by Using Simulink
abstract: The maritime industry is under increasing pressure from environmental regulations, and therefore, it is required to provide energy solutions that comply with sustainable practices immediately. The study conducted by the researchers indicates the creation of a hydrogen fuel cell model that is designed specifically for the MATLAB Simulink high-speed passenger vessels. title: Advancements in Applied Food Biotechnology: Integrated Approaches in Biopreservatives, and Probiotic Delivery Systems, Two Years of Journal Experience
abstract: Background and Aim: Faced with rising antimicrobial resistance, environmental concerns, and growing consumer demand for clean-label food products, applied food biotechnology plays a pivotal role in establishing sustainable, resilient, and health-oriented food networks. This manuscript synthesizes recent advancements across three interconnected domains: natural antimicrobials, industrial fermentation, and probiotic delivery systems.
