title: Antibiotics in aquatic environments: A review of occurrence, fate, ecotoxicity and advanced removal technologies
abstract: Antibiotics are among the most widely distributed contaminants of emerging concern in aquatic systems, entering water from hospital effluent, pharmaceutical manufacturing, livestock production, aquaculture and municipal sewage. Their principal hazard is not acute toxicity but sub-inhibitory selective pressure, which enriches antibiotic resistance genes and drives their horizontal transfer at concentrations of nanograms per litre. title: Global emergence of begomoviruses in cucurbits: diversity, epidemiology, and management strategies
abstract: The rapid spread of begomoviruses (family Geminiviridae) threatens global cucurbit production, yet the drivers of their emergence and the readiness of management strategies remain poorly integrated. This review synthesizes current understanding of cucurbit-infecting begomoviruses, contrasting the intercontinental spread of key Old World viruses, particularly Tomato leaf curl New Delhi virus (ToLCNDV), with persistent New World complexes such as Squash leaf curl virus (SLCV) and Cucurbit leaf crumple virus (CuLCrV). title: A review and evaluation of geologic CO2 storage potential in major South African Sedimentary Basins, with emphasis on opportunities, challenges, and future perspectives for climate change mitigation
abstract: Abstract Carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions from fossil fuels and industry in South Africa amounted to 401.89 million tonnes in 2023, with implications for climate change and global warming. South Africa has committed to achieving net-zero carbon emissions by the year 2050. However, the transition to a low-carbon economy must be pursued sustainably and equitably, given South Africa’s reliance on coal and its status as a leading global coal producer. title: Beyond single-element toxicity: chromium-salinity interactions, food-chain transfer and mitigation in sugarcane agroecosystems
abstract: Chromium contamination in sugarcane soils is often combined with co-metals and salinity caused by tannery effluent, electroplating effluent, paper mill wastewater, vinasse fertigation and filter cake. Hence, single element toxicity assessment does not provide realistic assessment of its exposure. The present review summarizes research on chromium behaviour along the soil, root, stalk and cane juice in sugarcane. title: Rediscovery of a type specimen of Plehnia arctica (Plehn, 1896) (Polycladida, Plehniidae) described by Marianne Plehn, a pioneering woman in German zoology
abstract: The rediscovered type specimen of the polyclad flatworm Plehnia arctica (Plehn, 1896), collected during Kükenthal’s 1889 Spitzbergen expedition and presumed lost for more than a century, was rediscovered in the collection of the Phyletisches Museum Jena (PMJ). The specimen was reexamined and compared with Plehn’s original description. title: Importancia de la predicción del perfil ADMET en bases de datos de productos naturales
abstract: Natural products (NPs) are the largest source of bioactive molecules with therapeutic properties. Currently, there are compound databases containing thousands of NPs, from which it is possible to select those with the best absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) profiles, which greatly increases their chances of success in clinical trials. This article discusses the importance of predicting the ADMET profile in early stages of drug development, especially using NP databases. title: Aplicación móvil basada en visión artificial y regresión lineal para el reconocimiento del estado de madurez y el pronóstico de rendimiento en cultivos de cacao (Theobroma cacao L): estudio de caso en la Finca Mendoza, Ecuador
abstract: Introducción: La determinación del grado de madurez del fruto y la estimación del rendimiento en fincas cacaoteras de Ecuador suele realizarse mediante observación empírica y registros manuales, lo que genera apreciaciones subjetivas, errores operativos y ausencia de información histórica sistematizada. Frente a esta problemática, el presente estudio tuvo como objetivo desarrollar y evaluar funcionalmente una aplicación móvil que integrara visión artificial y un modelo predictivo para el reconocimiento del estado de madurez del cacao y el pronóstico de rendimiento en la Finca Mendoza, Ecuador.

title: Hydration, mechanical, and environmental performance of blended cements incorporating ground granulated blast furnace slag, ground waste bottle glass, and metakaolin
abstract: This study investigates the effect of incorporating 20 wt% ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS), ground waste bottle glass (GWBG) and metakaolin (MK) on the hydration behavior, mechanical and environmental performance of blended cements cured at 23 °C ± 2 °C for 7, 28, and 90 days. title: Integrating images, sounds, citizen science and AI to assess the biodiversity of the Atlantic Forest of Brazil
abstract: The Atlantic Forest is an endangered biome in Brazil with only 15% of its area remaining. Although it is reported that it has a high biodiversity and many endemic species, the biological composition of its territory remains largely unknown. Citizen science can speed up the description of the living organisms present in this biome and at the same time increase citizens' perception of the importance of the conservation of this endangered tropical ecosystem. title: Halal Tourism Development Strategy in Pontianak City: Potentials, Disparities, and Urban Islamic Tourism
abstract: Halal tourism studies in Indonesia have largely focused on Sharia-compliant services, such as halal food, worship facilities, and religious tourism, while the development of urban Islamic tourism remains relatively limited. This study analyzes the development of halal tourism through an urban Islamic tourism approach in Pontianak City. title: UAV close-range photogrammetry combined with adaptive octree-based point cloud filtering for rock joint extraction of open-pit mine slopes
abstract: Abstract Manual joint surveys on open-pit mine slopes are high-risk and inefficient, whereas conventional remote sensing and laser scanning are costly and limited in fine-crack detection. title: Nutritional, Physicochemical and Sensory Evaluation of Geblek, a Traditional Food from Kulon Progo Regency Enriched with Ulva sp. from Gunungkidul Coast
abstract: Geblek is a traditional cassava-based snack from Kulon Progo, Yogyakarta, that generally has limited nutritional value because of its relatively simple ingredient composition. Ulva sp., a green seaweed, contains macro- and micronutrients, antioxidants, and other bioactive compounds, making it a potential functional food ingredient. title: Ecosystem health and its constraint transitions in Plateau cities: insights from Lhasa, China
abstract: Abstract High-altitude urban ecosystems are exposed to pronounced ecological vulnerability and increasing human pressures. Existing assessments have primarily characterized overall health status and its spatiotemporal variation, whereas temporal changes in the configuration of underlying constraints have received less attention. As the capital of the Xizang Autonomous Region of China, Lhasa’s unique geographic and climatic setting on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau poses distinctive challenges for ecosystem health assessment. abstract: : This study presents an integrated evaluation of tight sandstone gas reservoirs in the Yan 439 Block, Yan'an Gas Field, through secondary fine-scale well logging interpretation and rock mechanical analysis. title: Experimental Comparison of Tire Tread Wear Performance on Conventional and Electric Vehicles under Controlled Road Conditions
abstract: The replacement of internal combustion engine (ICE) with electric motor by electric vehicles (EVs) technology is one of the most comprehensive transition in the automotive industry for recent decades. EVs technology causes fundamental changes in vehicle architecture and dynamics including increased overall weight due to battery packs, altered torque delivery, and regenerative braking systems. title: Climate risk, uneven development, and threshold-dependent tourism resilience in selected cities of western China
abstract: Abstract Climate risk and socioeconomic development are increasingly reshaping tourism resilience, particularly in climate-sensitive and unevenly developed regions. Yet how climate risk and economic development jointly influence tourism, and how these effects vary across regions, remains insufficiently understood. abstract: The olive tree is one of the most important crops in the world, but even more, one of the most identitarian plant for the countries of the Mediterranean basin. In this article, the vast consultation of scientific literature, archaeological, historical and anecdotal sources, allowed to outline a global reasoned vision on the olive origin, its spread during early history and how olive fruit fly may represent as proxy for tracing its early diffusion. abstract: Long-term monitoring records from roller-compacted concrete (RCC) gravity dams in cold regions are scarce, although freeze–thaw cycling and large seasonal temperature ranges act there together with hydrostatic loading. This study analyzes 9.1 years of daily records (2016–2025) from 190 instruments on a 71 m RCC gravity dam in Xinjiang, China. title: Globally guided multi-agent reinforcement learning with decoupled critics for cooperative UAV path planning
abstract: Abstract Cooperative path planning for multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) requires the simultaneous achievement of target navigation, collision avoidance, and formation coordination in complex obstacle environments. Existing multi-agent reinforcement learning methods often suffer from sparse rewards, local deadlocks, and conflicts between formation maintenance and obstacle avoidance, which can destabilize policy learning. abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines the evolving European Union–South Korea relationship through the framework of the EU's Indo‐Pacific Strategy (IPS). Drawing on interviews with policymakers, officials, and influencers, it traces six decades of bilateral ties, highlighting Korea's 2022 IPS and its convergence with EU priorities in digital governance, green transition, and sustainability. abstract: Introduction Medical image analysis is a significant research domain in contemporary healthcare systems, which helps to accurately diagnose diseases and support clinical decision-making. This domain consists of important operations, including image enhancement, fusion, segmentation, morphological processing, and denoising, which assist in the effective understanding of complex biomedical information. abstract: Spatial prediction is a fundamental task in geographic information science and environmental resource assessment. However, under complex terrain and heterogeneous covariates, models relying only on point-scale attributes or a single global relationship often have difficulty representing spatial context and regional heterogeneity. abstract: Abstract Quantifying the structure and heterogeneity of complex spatial patterns remains a key challenge in spatial data analysis. abstract: As digital transformation accelerates and environmental regulations become more stringent, increasing attention has been paid to how maritime firms translate digital resources into environmental value. abstract: Most of the sand and aggregate used for construction in mid-western Nepal comes from the rivers of the Bheri basin in Surkhet District. abstract: As modificações no uso e cobertura do solo, impulsionadas pela expansão urbana desordenada, têm provocado alterações no ciclo hidrológico das bacias hidrográficas. title: BTSR-Net: Boundary–topology guided structural refinement for high-resolution remote sensing image segmentation
abstract: Semantic segmentation of high-resolution remote sensing imagery in complex urban scenes often suffers from insufficient modeling of boundary neighborhoods, causing ambiguity near class interfaces and weakening the continuity of elongated structures. To address this issue, we propose a Boundary-Topology-Guided Structural Refinement Network (BTSR-Net). title: Nanoparticle Fabrication and Optimization: From Green Chemistry to Transformative Applications in Life Sciences, Medicine, and Public Health
abstract: Nanotechnology has changed many fields by allowing scientists to work with matter at the atomic and molecular levels. NPs including metal (e.g., Ag, Au), metal oxide (e.g., ZnO, FeO), polymeric (e.g., PLGA), and carbon-based (e.g., carbon nanotubes), have special chemical, biological, and physical properties. This review paper discusses a lot of detail about making and improving nanoparticles, guided by the 12 principles of green chemistry ideas to make sure they are safe for living things and last for a long time. Traditional synthesis methods, employ toxic chemicals and use a lot of energy.

title: Combined model for document classification based on the comparative evaluation of semi-supervised models
abstract: La escasez de documentos etiquetados limita la clasificación automática de documentos y eleva los costos de etiquetado. En este contexto, el aprendizaje semi-supervisado (SSL) constituye una alternativa viable; sin embargo, la selección de modelos adecuados se dificulta por la ausencia de análisis comparativos que evidencien sus fortalezas y limitaciones. Este trabajo presenta dos aportes principales. title: Gas Turbine Propulsion Systems for Naval Vessels: Energy Flow Calculation Methodology and HighPressure Rotor CFD Simulation
abstract: This paper addresses the modernization of naval propulsion systems through the adoption of gas turbine technology, with emphasis on thermodynamic calculation methodology and rotor flow simulation. The study is centred on the Rolls Royce gas turbine, employed in naval propulsion applications and covers all thermodynamic states from atmospheric air intake through the two-stage compression process, combustion chamber, high-pressure and lowpressure turbine stages, to the power turbine exhaust. title: Topology-aware and constraint-guided deep reinforcement learning for climate-resilient control of urban stormwater systems
abstract: Introduction Urban stormwater systems are increasingly challenged by extreme precipitation events, leading to hydraulic surcharge when system capacity is exceeded. Traditional rule-based control (RBC) is reactive, whereas standard deep reinforcement learning (DRL) does not explicitly exploit drainage‐network topology or ensure physically consistent control. This study introduces Constraint-guided Graph-PPO (PIG‐PPO), a topology‐aware reinforcement learning framework designed to improve stormwater control under extreme precipitation conditions. title: Luz invisible que revela moléculas: el papel de la radiación infrarroja en la química
abstract: Infrared (IR) radiation is a part of the electromagnetic spectrum that is invisible to the human eye but very important for the chemical sciences. Using IR, particularly IR spectroscopy, chemists can identify compounds, verify product quality, or monitor the progress of a chemical reaction without destroying samples. This article provides a clear explanation of the operating principles of IR, as well as its applications in modern chemistry and its potential future developments, with examples ranging from the food industry to space exploration.

title: Mineralization mechanism and pollutant immobilization characteristics of vaterite induced by Bacillus velezensis and Pseudomonas putida
abstract: Exploring strain-specific differences in bacterial vaterite biomineralization can supplement the basic theoretical research of biomineralization and reveal the biogeochemical linkages between microbially induced carbonate formation and in-situ pollutant sequestration in soil environments. In this study, Bacillus velezensis LB002 and Pseudomonas putida KT2440 were used as representative bacterial strains to compare strain-dependent vaterite formation and pollutant sequestration behavior. title: Structural diagnosis and evolution of urban resilience in dryland oasis urban agglomerations from an eco-immunological perspective
abstract: Dryland oasis urban agglomerations face increasing drought risk, but gains in long-term adaptive capacity may not translate into stronger structural resilience because additive indices allow strong dimensions to offset weak ones. This study developed a partially non-compensatory four-dimensional super-trapezoid resilience model (TE4) integrating resistance, recovery, adaptive capacity, and institutional learning and preparedness, and applied it to ten city- and county-level units on the Northern Slope of the Tianshan Mountains during 2014–2024. abstract: ABSTRACT Sulfur leaching from metal sulfide electrocatalysts undermines formate intermediate stability during CO 2 reduction, yet existing protection strategies remain static. Here, we introduce an interfacial dynamic locking mechanism that actively stabilizes sulfur under reaction conditions. title: Thailand Land Surface Temperature Variation and Forecasting
abstract: Climate change has emerged as a global challenge, influenced by human activities, industrial operations and energy systems that depend on non-renewable energy such as carbon, gas, and petroleum. These activities have contributed to long-term shifts in temperature and broader climatic conditions. Land Surface Temperature (LST) has become an important standard for informing weather-related strategies at regional scales. title: A chronological framework for atherosclerosis: from environmental pressure to clinical disease, with vascular aging as a cross-cutting dimension
abstract: Atherosclerosis is a multiphase disease, yet contemporary cardiovascular risk stratification relies predominantly on calculators that estimate event probability within a limited pathophysiological window. Framingham, SCORE2, GLOBORISK and PREVENT capture lipid burden, metabolic parameters, and renal function, but they do not organize the chronological sequence of atherogenesis, assign measurable biomarkers to each stage, or integrate vascular aging. title: Forest green-up in the Pearl River Basin: trends, driving factors, and relationships with net primary productivity
abstract: The spring green-up date (GUD), a critical indicator of ecosystem response to climate change, profoundly influences terrestrial productivity. However, the complex drivers of GUD remain elusive, while the contentious relationship between GUD and net primary productivity (NPP) challenges the universal validity of the hypothesis that earlier green-up enhances productivity. Using MODIS NDVI data (2000-2020), we quantified forest GUD dynamics in the Pearl River Basin and combined random forest, SHAP, and structural equation modelling to identify drivers and assess GUD-NPP relationships. title: A versatile Bacillus esterase reveals a carboxylesterase blueprint for PET intermediate degradation
abstract: Abstract The biodegradation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET), a major commodity polymer, has become a core focus of multidisciplinary research. To date, most of the 300 known PETases cluster into only a few evolutionary lineages. While the well-known Ideonella sakaiensis PETase ( Is PETase) is highly specific for the polymer, and leaf-compost cutinase (LCC) types sequentially cleave the polymer and its subsequent oligomers, most known PET-active enzymes actually prefer monomeric intermediates; thus, they have not evolved as true PETases sensu strictu . title: An interpretable deep reinforcement learning framework for dynamic wind farm maintenance scheduling with enhanced power generation and stability
abstract: Wind farm maintenance scheduling is a challenging sequential decision-making problem due to the dynamic operational environment, multi-objective optimization requirements, and complex dependencies among turbine states, maintenance resources, and future power generation dynamics. Existing optimization and deep reinforcement learning methods often suffer from limited interpretability and insufficient capability in proactively balancing energy production efficiency and output stability. title: Interdisciplinary research in the Geosciences: a view from early career scientists
abstract: Abstract. Geosciences are often described as interdisciplinary, yet research and training remain fragmented across sub-disciplines and institutions. To understand how early career scientists (ECS) experience and practice interdisciplinarity, and which support structures actually help, we conducted an online survey within the German Geo.X research network. abstract: Sumatera merupakan salah satu wilayah dengan aktivitas seismik tertinggi di dunia akibat interaksi konvergen Lempeng Indo-Australia dan Lempeng Eurasia serta keberadaan Sesar Besar Sumatera. title: Reduced organic nitrogen compounds dominate the toxicity of PM 2.5 organics following internal exposure
abstract: Atmospheric fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) remains a major global health risk, with its associated health burden continuing to rise despite decades of pollution control efforts. Air pollution studies often focus on particle levels and known toxins, missing hidden organics that may drive serious health risks. Here, we conducted a comprehensive molecular and toxicological investigation of urban atmospheric particles, integrating nontargeted analysis of high-resolution mass spectrometry, protein adductomics–based internal exposure assessment, and multi-endpoint toxicity prediction. title: HOW MULTILAYER PERCEPTRON ARCHITECTURE AND TRAINING HYPERPARAMETERS AFFECT PREDICTIVE PERFORMANCE IN UAV-BASED SOYBEAN PHENOTYPING
abstract: Multilayer perceptron (MLP) models have been increasingly applied to high-throughput phenotyping using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-derived multispectral imagery. However, the effects of network architecture and training hyperparameters on predictive performance remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the number of neurons, hidden layers, training epochs, and cross-validation folds, as well as the performance of different combinations of these factors in MLP models to predict soybean phenotypic traits using vegetation indices. title: Realising the potential of ecological digital twins as decision support tools
abstract: Ecological digital twins are continually updating models used for decision-making. Current progress in ecological digital twinning has focused on overcoming the technological and modelling challenges to create a continually updating system. We argue that attention should now also focus on effectively integrating digital twins into decision-making systems to inform timely action. This requires the direct inclusion of end users and greater focus on the socio-political context. title: Herpetofaunal diversity and potential indicator species in a Mediterranean maquis ecosystem of the Chréa National Park, Tell Atlas, Algeria
abstract: Mediterranean maquis ecosystems of North Africa harbor unique fauna, but their herpetofaunal diversity remains poorly documented despite increasing anthropogenic pressures and habitat fragmentation. In this study, we conducted field surveys across nine one-kilometer transects spanning natural, rural, and urban landscapes along an elevational gradient (175-1245 m) in the Chréa National Park, Tell Atlas, Algeria. abstract: HistoryThe shrimp aquaculture industry faces significant challenges in managing wastewater, which is typically contaminated with high levels of pollutants such as ammonia, phosphates, heavy metals, and organic matter.Conventional treatment methods often fail to address these complex contaminants effectively.This review explores biochar-chitosan biocomposites as a promising solution for wastewater treatment in shrimp aquaculture.Biochar, a porous carbon material derived from organic biomass, and chitosan, a biopolymer sourced from crustacean shells, work synergistically to remove a wide range o

title: The evolving role of liver biopsy in chronic liver disease: a pathological and clinical perspective
abstract: Abstract Background Liver biopsy has traditionally been regarded as the reference standard for evaluating chronic liver disease because it provides direct tissue-level assessment of necroinflammatory activity, fibrosis, architectural remodeling, and disease-specific patterns of injury. However, its role has changed substantially with the widespread use of serum-based biomarkers, elastography, imaging, and other non-invasive tests that now guide risk stratification and follow-up in many clinical settings. abstract: Frictional sliding is ubiquitous in both natural phenomena and engineering systems, often occurring under dynamic normal stress conditions, yet the theoretical understanding of such scenarios remains limited. This study employs a verified one-dimensional spring-block model, incorporating rate- and state-dependent friction law, to investigate the evolution of stick–slip behavior under cyclic normal stress perturbations. title: A response surface-based calibration framework for accurate soil water content determination under saline conditions: a case study in Guangdong Province, China
abstract: Understanding soil water content dynamics under saline conditions remains a major challenge for effective soil and water management in agricultural systems. This study aimed to optimize the correction of soil water content measurements obtained from gypsum blocks under the combined effects of salinity and matric suction using Response Surface Methodology (RSM). Soil samples were collected from agricultural fields in Guangdong Province, China, representing three distinct soil textures: sandy loam, clay, and clay loam. title: SAFETY CULTURE AND MANAGEMENT CAPABILITIES DRIVING ORGANIZATIONAL EFFECTIVENESS IN MARITIME TRANSPORT
abstract: This study empirically investigates how safety culture, customer relationship management (CRM), and quality management jointly drive organizational effectiveness within Thailand’s maritime transport sector. Grounded in the Resource-Based View (RBV) theoretical framework, the research examines these vital intangible capabilities as synergistic drivers of sustained competitive advantage. abstract: Surface water governance depends not only on monitoring capacity but also on whether residents can access relevant information, navigate institutional responsibilities, and recognize opportunities to participate. This study examined these dimensions in Jalisco, Mexico, through a statewide, face-to-face household survey assessing exposure to and perceptions of surface water quality communication, information-seeking practices, awareness of inquiry and feedback mechanisms, and interest in public hearings and participatory monitoring, including perceived motivations and barriers. title: Quinoa as an alternative dry season climate resilient crop in the Mekong Delta Vietnam
abstract: Saline intrusion, drought, and water shortages are causing rice production losses in the Mekong River Delta dry season. Quinoa is a drought tolerant halophyte that could be an alternative crop option to rice or fallow in the dry season. The novelty of growing quinoa in the delta requires an understanding of variety selection and crop optimisation in conditions experienced in the dry season. title: Spatial variation shapes gut microbiome composition and functional potential in an Afrotropical fish
abstract: Abstract Host-associated microbiomes are shaped by environmental heterogeneity across spatial gradients. However, the extent to which site-level variation structures gut microbial communities in Afrotropical fishes remains poorly resolved. In this study, we employed high-throughput 16S rRNA gene sequencing to characterize the gut microbiome of the African forktail catfish ( Chrysichthys nigrodigitatus ) encompassing two contrasting habitat types, with the aim of assessing spatial patterns in microbial composition and predicted functional potential. title: Names of Chinese Places of Worship in The City of Medan
abstract: Place names represent more than geographical identifiers; they function as cultural symbols that preserve historical memory, religious values, and community identity. The names of Chinese places of worship in Medan reflect complex interactions between language, religion, and cultural adaptation within the Chinese community in Indonesia. However, linguistic studies examining the toponymic forms, lexical meanings, and language patterns of these religious sites remain limited. title: Flood pulse attributes of the upper Amazon River floodplains: spatiotemporal patterns and sensitivity to digital terrain model selection
abstract: Abstract Flood extent, depth, duration, and connectivity are key attributes of the seasonal flood pulse in Amazon floodplains, but characterizing them consistently remains difficult in forested, low-relief terrain. abstract: La inteligencia artificial (IA) generativa ha llegado a cambiar las reglas en la creación de imágenes, transformando los flujos de trabajo tradicionales y redefiniendo la ontología del artista. El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar el impacto de las herramientas algorítmicas en los procesos de creación de la animación digital y la ilustración desde un enfoque teórico-conceptual. Se ejecutó una revisión sistemática de la literatura con un enfoque cualitativo, fundamentada en las directrices de la declaración PRISMA. abstract: This proof-of-concept numerical study examines a metaverse rehabilitation pathway in which a haptic device enables a patient avatar to perform a virtual task inside an edge-rendered therapy environment. abstract: La vida social y responsable, así como el funcionamiento de todas las sociedades humanas, se asientan en el uso de códigos para expresar ideas; por ello, surge la definición de la comunicación como el acto mediante el cual un individuo establece contacto con otro para transmitir información. title: Seismic Performance Assessment of Reinforced Concrete Buildings Using Nonlinear Static Pushover Analysis
abstract: Seismic assessment of reinforced-concrete (RC) buildings requires understanding behavior beyond the elastic range. Linear analysis cannot reveal yielding or capacity loss; nonlinear dynamic analysis is costly, and few studies report pushover output for a regular frame and an existing building. This study applies nonlinear static (pushover) analysis to both. Two three-dimensional models were analysed: a regular four-story frame and an existing three-story Libyan building. title: Microbial community and potential functions in small urban river of Changzhou, China
abstract: Abstract Urban rivers receive substantial organic matter and nutrients, but seasonal changes in their microbial communities remain poorly understood. In this study, water and sediment samples were collected from four urban rivers in Changzhou during winter and summer. 16S rDNA, ITS amplicon sequencing and metagenomic analysis were used to characterize microbial composition and its functional potential. title: Prediction of dynamic retention during polymer flooding EOR in carbonate outcrops using empirical correlation
abstract: Polymer retention is a critical parameter in polymer flooding and requires accurate measurement for successful field implementation. However, coreflood tests for measuring dynamic polymer retention are time-consuming, costly, and labor-intensive, motivating the application of correlations that map readily measurable static adsorption to dynamic retention. title: Spatiotemporal patterns of cultural ecosystem service supply, demand and service flows along the Jiangsu music–cultural corridor: a grid-based framework across 13 prefecture-level cities
abstract: This study evaluates potential cultural ecosystem service (CES) supply, potential demand and modelled least-cost accessibility pathways across Jiangsu Province on a common 1 km grid for 2014, 2019 and 2020. Nine indicators are organised into a six-indicator supply block and a three-indicator demand block. abstract: Recent studies have suggested that user adoption of AI-based outputs may be positively related to AI agent anthropomorphism, with perceived agent competence serving as a mediator. This paper examines those relationships in the novel, general-purpose context of AI-based task-scheduling advice, which guides users in their daily activities. abstract: In order to provide offloading services for computationally demanding and time-sensitive operations on vehicles, multi-access edge computing has emerged as a successful paradigm. However, there are typically spatiotemporal load mismatches across edge servers due to significant vehicle mobility. As a result, task migration is used to transfer excessive tasks from overloaded to underloaded servers in order to maintain dynamic workload balance. abstract: Smile Chicken MSME faces challenges such as manual transaction recording, raw material inventory tracking, report preparation, and purchasing decisions that still rely on estimation. This study aims to build a web-based Point of Sales system that integrates sales transactions, inventory management, automated reports, and raw material purchase recommendations. title: Design and Thermal Performance Analysis of a Multilayer Coolbox with Polyurethane as the Primary Insulation for Portable Fish-Hold Applications
abstract: Post-harvest handling of fresh fish by small-scale fishermen is highly dependent on effective temperature control to minimize quality deterioration during storage and transportation. title: Localized impact-resistant battery enclosures for electric vehicles: crashworthy lightweight design, mechanical–thermal safety, and validation pathways
abstract: Electric-vehicle battery enclosures must reduce structural mass while preserving deformation clearance, sealing integrity, electrical isolation, and post-impact safety. These requirements are difficult under bottom strike and side-pole collision because both load cases create localized intrusion near cells and modules, where only limited deformation space is available. abstract: ABSTRACT Broadband self‐powered photodetectors that combine photovoltaic (PV) and photothermoelectric (PTE) effects are attractive for low‐power optoelectronic sensing. abstract: Accurate modeling of species distribution is essential for effective biodiversity conservation, afforestation planning, and land-use management. This study presents a comparative analysis of two prominent presence-only species distribution models Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) and MaxNet to evaluate their efficacy in predicting the ecological niche of Eucalyptus tereticornis in a semi-arid agro-climatic region. title: Agroecological zoning of mezcal and tequila agaves in Mexico through MaxEnt ecological niche modeling: Sustainability and climate resilience implications
abstract: Agave‑based distilled‑beverage production in Mexico, particularly mezcal and tequila, is facing intensifying sustainability challenges driven by climate change, monocropping expansion, and degradation of socio‑ecological systems. In this context, agroecological zoning represents a strategic tool for improving territorial planning and strengthening climate resilience. title: Effects of pre-harvest salicylic acid and irrigation interval on rhizome yield and phytochemical accumulation in Curcuma aromatica Salisb.
abstract: Curcuma aromatica Salisb. is a medicinal plant valued for its rhizomes rich in essential oils and phenolic compounds. This study aimed to determine (i) an optimal concentration of salicylic acid (SA) to improve plant performance and secondary metabolite accumulation, and (ii) the effects of different pre-harvest irrigation intervals on plants pre-treated with the selected SA concentration. title: Bio‐Inspired Tactile Reflex Architecture for Ultra‐Fast and Context‐Aware Human‐Robot Interaction
abstract: ABSTRACT Robots operating in close proximity to humans must be capable of perceiving contact, reacting within milliseconds, and subsequently restoring stable task execution. abstract: Este estudio analiza el impacto de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en la toma de decisiones estratégicas de la animación digital y sus consecuencias laborales. Mediante una revisión sistemática documental PRISMA de 50 artículos (2021–2026), se evalúa cómo la IA genera eficiencia operativa (reducción de tiempos de renderizado, automatización de tareas repetitivas) pero también desplaza empleos tradicionales, especialmente en México y América Latina, donde más de 200,000 animadores enfrentan riesgo de disrupción en cinco años. abstract: Background The emergence of cephalosporin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains, encoding altered Penicillin-Binding Protein 2 (PBP2), has become a major global public health concern. The increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance necessitates the development of novel antimicrobial agents. In the present study, phytocompounds derived from the haustorium of Borassus flabellifer L. were investigated as potential inhibitors of PBP2 using an integrated in silico approach. title: Evaluation of the safe operating space during low flow for water allocation and climate change scenarios in the Danube
abstract: A basin-to-local evaluation framework, quantifying safe operating space (SOS) for low-flow water allocation and climate change along the Danube, is presented, linking basin hydrology to local operations for navigation, ecology, run-of-river hydropower, drinking water, and nuclear power plant cooling. abstract: Abstract In terms of quality test, ultrasonic wave velocity test, static mechanical test and dynamic compression test, the physical and static mechanical properties of geopolymer concrete after water immersion for 180 d were studied, and the effects of water saturation and impact load on the mechanical properties of geopolymer concrete were analyzed. abstract: Vibration-based damage estimates depend not only on the inverse algorithm but also on the quality, completeness, and modal reliability of the measured data. This study presents a measurement-informed finite element model updating framework that combines quantum-behaved particle swarm optimization with conditionally activated simulated annealing. Field acceleration measurements from a steel truss span of the Chuong Duong Bridge in Hanoi were processed by covariance-driven stochastic subspace identification and used to calibrate the healthy-state model. abstract: Aquaculture is a fish-producing subsector of agriculture that has a significant role in India’s economy and livelihood. The major threat to fish production is the outbreak of bacterial infections that creates severe losses every year. Aeromonas hydrophila is an opportunistic invader of human and aquatic animals, ubiquitously present in the aquatic environment. abstract: Logistics 5.0 indicates the combination of Industry 5.0’s important principles such as human-centricity, resiliency, and sustainability with the advanced digital capabilities of Logistics 4.0. While a growing number of developed countries are starting to adopt AI, digital twins, collaborative robots, and human-machine decision-making systems, there is still only limited evidence available regarding Logistics 5.0 implementation in India. abstract: Pantai Teluk Sepang merupakan kawasan pesisir yang dinamis dan berhadapan langsung dengan Samudera Hindia. Perubahan garis pantai dapat memengaruhi keberlanjutan infrastruktur, permukiman, dan ekosistem pesisir sehingga diperlukan pemantauan yang konsisten. title: Integrated assessment of meteorological drought impacts on terrestrial water storage and vegetation dynamics in East Africa
abstract: Abstract Water is essential for life, and effective hydrological management is crucial for economic stability and quality of life. Poor water resource governance can lead to scarcity, displacement, or even fatal consequences. Hydrological conditions in East Africa are influenced by drivers such as demographic expansion, industrialization, droughts, and vegetation dynamics. This study explores how total water storage in the region responds to drought intensity and vegetation variability. title: Advancing Micro-Ecotone Mapping Using UAV Photogrammetry and GIS
abstract: Ecotones are transitional boundaries between ecosystems and essential to regulating biodiversity and ecological processes. Although ecotones are often wider transition zones like aquatic-terrestrial boundaries, they can happen at fine spatial scales (micro-ecotones) and occur over only a few meters or even centimeters. In the past, ecotones have been examined using one-dimensional transects or coarsely resolved remote sensing data for analysis. abstract: Este artículo se enmarca en una investigación sobre el uso de Inteligencia Artificial en la escritura académica en carreras humanísticas de la Universidad Nacional de Rosario, Argentina. Explicita los primeros resultados obtenidos en lo que respecta al análisis de las prácticas de uso y conocimiento de tecnologías por parte de estudiantes. title: Hydrochem, an Integrated R Package for the Analysis and Visualization of Hydrochemical Data
abstract: Hydrochemical data are essential for understanding groundwater flow, hydrobiogeochemical processes, contamination sources, and assessing groundwater quality. Despite the increasing availability of complex hydrochemical datasets, current tools for processing and visualizing these data-mainly spreadsheets and commercial GUI software-have significant limitations in scalability, reproducibility, and flexibility. abstract: This paper describes an analytical study of unsteady magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) Couette flow of a dusty second-grade viscoelastic fluid between two infinite inclined porous plates. The problem involves the combined influences of porous medium permeability, uniform suction/injection, rotation of the system, thermal radiation, and coupled heat and mass transfer. title: Barrier Lyapunov function-based prescribed performance control of quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicles under wind disturbances and input saturation
abstract: This work presents a prescribed-performance attitude tracking control strategy for under-actuated quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicles subject to external disturbances and actuator saturation. A novel four-stage cascaded dynamic representation is first developed by incorporating atmospheric disturbances and actuator saturation effects. abstract: Abstract Accurate counting and morphological analysis of welding electrodes and wire stubs are essential for warehouse data management in welding factories. However, the visual recognition of welding material stubs in real-world industrial applications is frequently hindered by issues such as missed detections, false detections, and imprecise boundary localization. abstract: Sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures provide a platform for modulating electronic structure and interfacial reactivity through strong atom-level coupling, with potential applications in energy conversion. However, their precise construction remains challenging. Here we show a strategy for constructing sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures through confined spinodal decomposition and ligand-mediated in situ reduction. abstract: Earthquake prediction has long been considered one of the greatest challenges in the global scientific community due to the complex and uncertain nature of seismogenic processes, along with the prevailing consensus that earthquakes are inherently unpredictable. Here, we present a novel and potentially transformative concept—seismo-ripples—resonance signals consistently observed in seismic, magnetic, and ionospheric data prior to major earthquakes. title: Response surface methodology based multiresponse optimization of drilling parameters for surface roughness and material removal rate in AA7075T6 aluminium alloy
abstract: High strength and lightweight alloys like AA7075-T6 Aluminium alloy pose great challenge in drilling, particularly in achieving high surface quality and productivity. The existing work is a systematic investigation of the effect of the cutting speed, feed rate and drill depth on surface roughness and material removal rate (MRR) in conventional drilling. abstract: CO 2 transporters enable bacterial CO 2 -concentrating mechanisms by catalyzing directional hydration of CO 2 , yet the basis of this vectorial carbonic anhydrase (CA) activity remains an open question. abstract: La digitalización de la administración tributaria peruana ha trasladado una parte creciente del control del crédito fiscal del impuesto general a las ventas hacia registros electrónicos y cruces automatizados. El objetivo fue sintetizar la evidencia científica, normativa e institucional sobre auditoría tributaria digital, facturación electrónica y crédito fiscal, y derivar una propuesta preliminar de indicadores de priorización aplicables al Sistema Integrado de Registros Electrónicos. abstract: Benzimidazole is a privileged nitrogen-containing fused heterocyclic scaffold that has attracted considerable interest in medicinal and pharmaceutical chemistry because of its structural versatility, favorable physicochemical properties and broad biological profile. The benzimidazole nucleus comprises a benzene ring fused with an imidazole ring containing two nitrogen atoms, providing multiple sites for structural modification and interaction with biological targets. title: Seasonal flood inundation area and repetitive flood exposure shape the fundamental patterns of flood exposure in China from 2000 to 2020
abstract: Remote sensing of floods and associated exposure is essential for understanding and managing flood risks, yet exposure differences among floods with varying frequencies remain underexplored. Using MODIS time-series data, this study mapped infrequent flood inundation area (IFIA) and seasonal flood inundation area (SFIA) across China during 2000–2020. Differences in flood extent and built-up land exposure were assessed using the Mann–Kendall test, improved Theil–Sen algorithm, and one-way analysis of variance. Cumulative flood inundation area reached 3.52 × 10⁶ km², with SFIA accounting for 40%.

abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as effective evaluators of text summaries, often achieving strong agreement with human judgments. However, the mechanisms underlying both human and LLM evaluation decisions remain poorly understood, limiting the transparency and trustworthiness of LLM-based evaluation. abstract: ABSTRACT Pipelines, valves, and pressure vessels (PVs) are vital components in nuclear, thermal power, and chemical systems, operating under high temperature and pressure over extended periods, leading to safety risks. Ensuring their safe operation requires regular inspections, which current robotic systems cannot fully address due to the diverse and challenging environments. abstract: Asian weatherloaches have expanded their range across Europe, potentially increasing competitive pressure on the conservation-dependent native European weatherfish Misgurnus fossilis . Because interspecific interactions are potentially mediated by benthic habitat use, we quantified substrate choice of native European and invasive Asian weatherloaches in a replicated laboratory two-way choice experiment. abstract: The urban growth of Guayaquil has reconfigured the boundaries between the city and the countryside, giving rise to new urban edges were residential expansion advances on previously rural territories. Vía a la Costa and Posorja sectors have become contrasting but complementary scenarios of the same phenomenon: the progressive loss of rural habitat in the face of the dynamics of accelerated urbanization. abstract: The seafood processing industry faces critical operational challenges in maintaining mass-balance integrity because manual, paper-based recording causes data lag and human input errors. abstract: The transition from conchocelis to conchosporangial branches is not only a key stage in the life cycle of Pyropia/Porphyra but also directly affects the yield and quality of economically important species such as Pyropia haitanensis . However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the maturation of P. haitanensis filaments remain poorly understood. abstract: La incorporación de la inteligencia artificial en los procesos educativos representa una oportunidad para transformar las prácticas pedagógicas y fortalecer el aprendizaje significativo de las Ciencias Naturales en los diferentes niveles de escolaridad. abstract: Este estudio formaliza la receta técnica de un cheesecake semifrío mediante el uso de herramientas de modelación lineal para optimizar su escalado industrial. El objetivo principal es transformar una receta empírica tradicional en un sistema físico-matemático reproducible. abstract: This research develops a coordinated control, estimation, and dispatch framework for a solar-photovoltaic-integrated electric-vehicle charging station (EVCS) with battery storage and grid backup, and reports four contributions. abstract: Abstract. title: Effectiveness of Ballast Water Management Convention Implementation at Samarinda Port
abstract: The implementation of the Ballast Water Management Convention (BWMC) is an important instrument in controlling ecological risks due to the movement of aquatic organisms through ship ballast water. Although Indonesia has ratified the BWMC, the effectiveness of its implementation at the port operational level, especially river ports, still requires empirical evaluation. abstract: We tested whether people change their decisions when an AI system proposes they do so, and the effects of a counterfactual explanation. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Traditional arguments about exigence have focused on whether a situation in the world creates the urgency and need to act or whether the speaking itself creates the urgency. title: Uncertainty-Aware Digital Twin Framework for Resilient Low-Carbon Port Infrastructure under Electrification and Sensor Degradation
abstract: The electrification of port operations is reshaping the technical relationship between logistics performance, energy demand, infrastructure condition and data reliability. Although digital twins are increasingly used for port monitoring and decision support, many frameworks continue to assume clean sensing, synchronised data streams and stable observability. title: Operationalizing resilience for sustainable infrastructure governance across the life cycle
abstract: Abstract Sustainability and resilience expectations for infrastructure are escalating faster than the regulatory frameworks meant to deliver them. This mismatch is most acute for ageing critical infrastructure. Yet, adaptation decisions remain fragmented because resilience and sustainability operate on fundamentally different temporal domains: resilience captures short-term recovery dynamics and service continuity. abstract: Maritime simulators play a key role in training and assessing cadets’ operational competencies, especially within the framework of the STCW Convention. abstract: Aeromonas hydrophila is an opportunistic pathogen of fish, humans, and livestock, and has a severe negative impact on aquaculture development. abstract: Abstract Objectives To investigate healthcare professionals’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAPs) of the environmental impact and sustainability of iodinated contrast media (ICM). abstract: This study discusses the process of becoming undergone by the mythical female figure, Medusa, in Natalie Haynes’ Stone Blind. abstract: Net primary productivity (NPP) varies with climate and soil resources, but whether species-level plant traits provide information beyond these environmental controls remains unclear. abstract: Although inland wetlands are among the most important and impacted biodiversity hotspots worldwide, they remain poorly assessed. abstract: OpenStreetMap (OSM) is the most widely used open road dataset, yet how late it records new roads is rarely measured. abstract: This study represents how personal memory, grief, and human connection are revealed in Ruth Ozeki’s novel A Tale for the Time Being through Jacques Derrida’s theory of hauntology. abstract: Outdoor insulators in high and medium-voltage overhead transmission and distribution lines are critical. abstract: Flood events clearly induce significant impacts in urbanised regions. Over the last decades, advances in computational capacity, high-resolution digital elevation data, and open-access geospatial datasets have enabled the development of Evacuation Models (EM). abstract: Bangladesh consistently ranks among the countries with the highest fine particulate matter (PM2.5) pollution levels globally, yet evidence on the association between PM2.5 exposure during pregnancy and preterm birth (PTB) remains limited. Therefore, we assessed the association between outdoor PM2.5 exposure and PTB across different periods of pregnancy. abstract: Because development of crustacean gonads can impede growth potential, a balance between growth and gonad development is necessary to promote the healthy and sustainable development of aquaculture. abstract: The single-period inventory problem with uncertain demand, also known as the Newspaper Vendor Problem, is a commonly encountered occurrence in industry and significant research literature exists on the subject. abstract: Abstract. Accurate estimation of regional-scale terrestrial carbon budgets is of great importance but remains challenging. With particular advantages, the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks method shows potential in improving regional carbon budget upscaling estimations. abstract: Clay rock and clay-based materials play an important role in a wide range of geotechnical and environmental applications due to their low permeability, swelling capacity, and favourable thermo–hydro–mechanical–chemical (THMC) properties. abstract: Abstract Cities are complex and dynamic systems that integrate social, ecological, and infrastructure domains. This study investigates and quantifies how urban forms are associated with multiple urban functions across these domains, and how these associations combine into positive or negative synergies and trade-offs through multifunctional assessment rather than single-function analyses. abstract: Rapid urbanization and the expansion of Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) in tropical megacities often overlook the microclimatic experience of pedestrians, leading to severe Urban Heat Island (UHI) effects and thermal discomfort. This study introduces and computationally evaluates the Bioclimatic Transit-Infill Housing (BTIH) concept, a medium-density housing model with minimum parking, located at the Blok A Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) station in Jakarta, Indonesia. abstract: This article examines South Korea’s evolving grand strategy as a geopolitical swing state under intensifying US–China competition. abstract: Abstract Exposure to flood hazards in high mountain catchments is expected to increase alongside natural hazards, driven by climate change, glacier retreat, and landscape evolution, yet temporally consistent, high-resolution exposure data remain scarce. Here we quantify changes in the exposure of buildings and people to flooding in Nepal and transboundary regions of India and China. abstract: BACKGROUND: Spotted wing drosophila, Drosophila suzukii (Matsumura), is a major fruit fly pest of cherries and berries across Eurasia and North America, with a restricted distribution in the southern hemisphere. It is currently ranked the third greatest threat to Australia on the National Priority Plant Pest (NPPP) list (2024). title: Analysis of Barriers within the Decision-making Chain for German and Danish SMEs Supplying Climate Adaptation Solutions
abstract: Climate adaptation has become a central policy priority across Europe, yet the uptake of new adaptation solutions remains slow, particularly within public-sector markets. Small and medium-sized enterprises play an important role in developing innovative climate adaptation technologies, but often struggle to gain access to planning, procurement and implementation processes shaped by established routines, regulatory complexity and risk aversion. This paper analyses the barriers faced by SMEs supplying climate adaptation solutions in Denmark and Northern Germany. Based on semi-structured intervie

title: SMART TOURISM GOVERNANCE: A SCIENTOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF GOVERNMENT ROLES
abstract: Smart tourism governance has become increasingly important as digital technologies reshape tourism management, public services, and destination development. However, existing studies have predominantly emphasized technological innovation, destination competitiveness, and tourist experiences, while the evolving administrative roles of government remain fragmented. This study aims to examine the intellectual development of smart tourism governance and map the evolving roles of government through a scientometric analysis. title: Has the supply of care beds for older adults become more equal across Chinese provinces? Spatial distribution dynamics and convergence evidence from a thirteen-year panel
abstract: Introduction Equalizing basic older adult care services is a core objective of China’s response to population aging, yet whether the provision of older adult care bed supply has become more equal across provinces, and how its spatial structure has evolved, remains unclear. We ask how large provincial disparities in bed supply are and where they originate, whether supply is spatially clustered, how the distribution has evolved, and whether gaps converge. title: A quantitative model for embedding quantum-secure communications and evaluating communication autonomy in industrial control systems
abstract: Industrial control systems would increasingly depend on remote operation, online monitoring, and potentially autonomous control. This creates new requirements for secure, low-latency communications, and introduces new operational constraints on secret key availability, communication autonomy, and resilience under normal and abnormal conditions. We present a time-dependent quantitative model for embedding quantum-secure communications in an industrial control system and demonstrate its implementation on Purdue’s fully-digital 10-kWth research reactor (PUR-1). title: Changes in arbovirus risks and responses from 2020 to 2026
abstract: Abstract Since 2020, viruses spread by mosquitoes and biting midges have become a larger and less predictable public health challenge. Dengue continues to cause the greatest burden, but chikungunya, Oropouche, and other viruses are re-emerging or spreading into new areas. In this narrative review, we summarize major changes in arbovirus epidemiology, surveillance, diagnosis, vaccination, treatment, vector ecology, and mosquito control from 2020 to 2026. title: Research on Communication Signal Coverage Methods Based on Recursive Genetic Algorithms
abstract: The availability of communication signals for dense wireless local area networks (WLANs) is being increasingly hindered by spectrum contention, interference, and traffic dynamics. Side effects of coverage can also be captured by higher layers, such as the transport or application layer; however, their sensing capabilities are limited, and their information may be strongly biased by the network conditions or the user traffic. In this paper, we explore a coverage-quality-aware optimization framework based on Recursive Genetic Algorithm (RGA) for multi–basic service set (BSS) WLAN environments. S

title: In sickness and in health: profiling the bovine fecal eukaryome using optimized 18S metabarcoding with a mammal-blocking primer
abstract: Introduction Calf diarrhea, caused by the apicomplexan pathogen Cryptosporidium parvum ( C. parvum ), poses significant economic and production challenges to the livestock industry. While 16S rRNA sequencing has advanced understanding of the bovine bacterial gut microbiota, the eukaryotic community remains underexplored due to methodological constraints, notably host DNA contamination. title: Performance-Limit Oriented Active Control of Vibration: Past, Present & Future Perspectives
abstract: Conventional active vibration control methodologies predominantly focus on achieving performance improvement relative to open-loop systems, rather than exploring the inherent performance boundaries imposed by physical constraints, system structures, and actuation/sensing limitations. To overcome these drawbacks, performance-limit oriented active control of vibration has emerged as a systematic design framework that aims at revealing and approaching the theoretical performance boundaries. title: ANÁLISE TEMPORAL E DISTRIBUIÇÃO ESPACIAL DAS CICATRIZES DE FOGO NO ESTADO DO AMAPÁ (1985–2024)
abstract: O estado do Amapá destaca-se no cenário amazônico como a unidade federativa com o mais elevado índice de preservação florestal da Amazônia Legal. Neste contexto, compreender a dinâmica temporal e espacial das cicatrizes de fogo é fundamental para subsidiar estratégias de manejo e políticas públicas de prevenção. Este estudo analisou a distribuição temporal e espacial das cicatrizes de fogo no Amapá entre 1985 e 2024, utilizando dados da Coleção 5 do MapBiomas Fogo. title: Detecting acceleration in global mean temperature using supralinear trends
abstract: Abstract Whether global mean surface temperature has accelerated has received opposite answers in quick succession, reported as undetectable on data to 2023 and as significant on data to 2024. This raises two questions: since when is acceleration detectable, and how far does the answer depend on the test used? We show that structural-break tests, often used for this purpose, cannot reliably date the onset of a continuously accelerating warming rate. title: A data-centric framework for simultaneous Pb²⁺ and Cd²⁺ prediction from electrochemical signals
abstract: Monitoring heavy-metal pollution remains an important analytical challenge. Conventional laboratory methods are sensitive but often constrained by cost, turnaround time, and centralized infrastructure. Electrochemical sensors remain attractive because they can deliver rapid measurements on simpler platforms and, in some cases, closer to the point of sampling. Pb and Cd are especially important targets because they are toxic, environmentally persistent, and frequently occur together in real samples. title: Minerales densos en gravas y conglomerados miocenos del sector Navelgas-Allande-Linares (Asturias): caracterización y procedencia
abstract: En este trabajo se presenta una caracterización, a partir de técnicas de microscopía y microanálisis, de la fracción densa de los minerales presentes en una serie de retazos de sedimentos detríticos miocenos que se conservan en las cotas más altas del corredor Navelgas-Pola de Allande-Linares, en el límite oriental de la Zona Asturoccidental-Leonesa (NW de España). La especie más frecuente son los óxidos de Fe (tanto hematites como magnetita), a los que habitualmente acompañan los óxidos de Fe-Ti (principalmente ilmenita), circón, cromo-espinela, monacita, xenotima y oro nativo. title: MÁS ALLÁ DE LOS ALGORITMOS: HUMANIZAR EL APRENDIZAJE A TRAVÉS DE LAS HABILIDADES SOCIOEMOCIONALES EN LA ERA DE LA INTELIGENCIA ARTIFICIAL
abstract: En un mundo marcado por la omnipresencia algorítmica y la rápida integración de la Inteligencia Artificial (IA) en la educación, la pregunta fundamental trasciende la capacidad tecnológica para centrarse en la esencia del desarrollo humano. El presente ensayo examina la interrelación crítica entre la IA y las Habilidades Socioemocionales (HSE), proponiendo que la tecnología debe funcionar exclusivamente como un medio pedagógico para humanizar el aprendizaje, y no como un fin en sí mismo. title: Modelo de gobernanza para el uso de la inteligencia artificial en la justicia penal y sus dimensiones problemáticas
abstract: La incorporación de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en la justicia penal desafía el debido proceso y la igualdad ante la ley, afectando de forma especial a poblaciones vulnerables como los migrantes irregulares. Mediante la revisión sistemática de la literatura y de los marcos normativos, incluido el Reglamento (UE) 2024/1689, este artículo analiza el impacto de la IA en las decisiones judiciales, la policía predictiva y la gestión penitenciaria. Se identifican cuatro dimensiones críticas: el sesgo algorítmico, la opacidad, la fragmentación de la responsabilidad y la falta de control humano. C

title: Multi-omics integration reveals the role of PFOS in sarcopenia via ESRRG and RBP4: from computational prediction to experimental validation
abstract: Background Perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) has been shown to cause multi-organ dysfunction; however, the specific mechanisms underlying its association with sarcopenia remain unclear. Methods Network toxicology analysis was performed to identify potential molecular targets and related signaling pathways involved in PFOS-induced sarcopenia. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations further screened stable PFOS–target interactions. title: Chemical Pharmacognosy in the Era of Integrated Natural-Product Discovery: From Traditional Knowledge to Therapeutic Translation
abstract: Natural products have played a central role in the development of medicines and continue to provide structurally diverse molecules, pharmacological leads, and molecular frameworks for contemporary drug discovery. Chemical pharmacognosy has traditionally focused on the isolation, characterization, and biological evaluation of constituents obtained from medicinal plants and other natural sources. The discipline has progressively expanded through advances in analytical chemistry, molecular biology, metabolomics, computational science, genomics, and biotechnology. title: UAV-based dynamic crowd monitoring for rescue prioritization using subspace-driven localization
abstract: Abstract Rapid and reliable localization of survivors is critical in post-disaster search and rescue operations. However, conventional sensing methods such as visual imaging are often ineffective due to smoke, dust, or debris, and traditional RSSI-based localization suffers from severe multipath interference and noise. This paper proposes a subspace-driven multi-UAV system for dynamic crowd monitoring and rescue prioritization. title: Characterising CPU-initiated High Bandwidth Memory Access
abstract: Abstract An increasing number of high-performance computers are equipped with high bandwidth memory. Their CPUs have cache-coherent access to this memory type over high-speed interconnects or as unified memory. We analyse two such systems, NVIDIA’s GH200 and AMD’s MI300A. We discuss their memory setup and measure memory access latency and throughput. We evaluate weighted memory page interleaving and strided memory access as candidates for increasing the measured throughput. title: Profil Spesiasi Arsen pada Nori Komersial yang Beredar di Indonesia Menggunakan Teknik IC-ICP-MS untuk Mendukung Pengawasan Keamanan Pangan
abstract: Nori merupakan produk pangan berbasis rumput laut yang semakin banyak dikonsumsi di Indonesia dan berpotensi mengakumulasi kontaminan dari lingkungan, termasuk arsen. Risiko kesehatan akibat paparan arsen sangat dipengaruhi oleh bentuk kimianya, sehingga analisis berdasarkan spesiasi lebih relevan untuk mendukung penilaian keamanan pangan dibandingkan analisis arsen total. title: Spectral Reconstruction Using Broadband Inkjet‐Printed Optical Filters
abstract: ABSTRACT Reconstructive spectroscopy offers a promising route toward miniaturization by replacing dispersive optics with computational recovery from encoded measurements, but existing implementations typically rely on complex nanofabrication and highly decorrelated encoding elements, limiting manufacturability and robustness. Here, we demonstrate a reconstructive spectrometer based on inkjet‐printed interferometric optical filters featuring a minimalist tri‐layer architecture and high optical throughput. title: Energy governance integration and the water-energy-food nexus for enhanced environmental sustainability: a literature review and governance framework
abstract: The interdependence of water, energy, and food (WEF) systems requires governance approaches that address cross-sectoral interactions rather than separate policy regimes. Although previous reviews have examined WEF nexus governance, sustainability, and resource interactions, limited attention has been given to how energy governance interfaces with environmental governance and the institutional mechanisms needed to manage WEF interdependencies. title: Impacto y Beneficios de la Inteligencia Artificial en la Animación Digital: Una Revisión Sistemática
abstract: La animación digital y la inteligencia artificial están transformando y ofreciendo herramientas innovadoras en la producción de películas animadas, reducción de producción y automatización de tareas. Este estudio, basado en una revisión sistemática con metodología PRISMA, analiza cincuenta investigaciones recientes que abordan el uso de la IA como herramienta de la animación digital, animación 3D y animación 2D. title: Advances in Rocket Propulsion Systems- A Comprehensive Insight on Design, Performance and Future Systems
abstract: Over the years, there have been significant advances in rocket propulsion system. These advances have been encouraged by the urge to improve reliability, efficiency and versatility in space exploration. This study provides comprehensive overview of those advances. It would be focusing on major breakthroughs for rocket propulsion systems and their effect on space missions. title: Implementing the EU AI ACT at the national level: models and perspectives
abstract: The essay analyzes the various models adopted by European Union Member States for the implementation of the EU AI Act, highlighting how the regulation is deeply impacting national systems at the regulatory, organizational, and institutional levels. Through a comparative review of national experiences, the author distinguishes between those states that have already adopted a comprehensive implementing law, those that rely on sector-specific legislation or regulatory acts, those still in the legislative development phase, and those without specific implementing measures. title: Trace element contents and sulfur isotope analyses of multistage quartz-sulfide veins in the Dazhou gold deposit in Jiangxi Province, south China: Implications for mineralization mechanism
abstract: Located in the eastern Jiangnan Orogen, the Dazhou deposit is a quartz vein-type gold deposit in the E-hu gold mineralization concentration area, northeastern Jiangxi Province, South China. Hosted by tuffaceous slate and sandy slate of the Neoproterozoic Shuangqiaoshan Group, the deposit’s hydrothermal evolution, sulfur source, and gold mineralization mechanism remain poorly constrained. title: Unlocking electric vehicle flexibility in microgrids via lightweight on-charger coordination
abstract: The large-scale integration of electric vehicles could provide substantial flexibility for balancing renewable energy in microgrids, yet this potential remains largely constrained by uncoordinated charging. Here, we show that on-board chargers can be transformed into intelligent agents to unlock this flexibility through distributed vehicle-grid coordination. To enable such coordination under practical hardware constraints, we develop a distributed framework that embeds edge intelligence into resource-constrained chargers for autonomous charging optimization. title: Laboratory-based nutritional risk assessment including GDF15 in cirrhosis: a multicenter retrospective study
abstract: Abstract Malnutrition is a common complication of cirrhosis and is associated with adverse outcomes. However, current nutritional risk assessment tools may not fully incorporate objective laboratory biomarkers. This study aimed to develop a biomarker-based prediction model for nutritional risk assessment in patients with cirrhosis. We retrospectively collected the clinical data of 551 patients with liver cirrhosis from two centers between April 2023 and April 2026. title: Musa dulongjiangensis (Musaceae), a new species from Yunnan, southwest China
abstract: Musa dulongjiangensis (Musaceae), a new species of the genus Musa endemic to Yunnan, southwestern China, is described and illustrated in this study. This new species is morphologically similar to M. puspanjaliae , but can be clearly distinguished by a combination of morphological characters. Its female bud bracts are dark purple externally and purple internally, with 6–7 basal female flowers arranged in two rows; the base of the compound tepal bears distinct and dense red stripes, the ovary is pale green and glabrous. title: Declared Unauthorised Construction in Greece: An Indicator-Based Spatial Analysis
abstract: Unauthorised construction has been a persistent feature of spatial development in Greece, yet its geographical variation cannot be adequately captured by counts of recorded cases or total unauthorised building area alone. This study examines the officially recorded and legally regularised component of the phenomenon using administrative data from the Technical Chamber of Greece, comprising approximately 1.2 million declarations and more than 4.1 million violation records. title: Crop improvement of Bambara groundnut through mutation breeding
abstract: Bambara groundnut is an important indigenous African grain legume cultivated primarily by smallholder farmers across sub-Saharan Africa. The crop is valued for its nutritional richness, adaptability to marginal environments, and contribution to household food security and soil fertility through biological nitrogen fixation. title: Development and application of a smartphone-based thermal contrast amplification reader for photothermal lateral flow immunoassays
abstract: The high cost and poor portability of external infrared thermal imagers have limited the widespread adoption of photothermal lateral flow immunoassays (PT-LFIAs) in on-site testing. To address this, we developed a smartphone-based handheld Thermal Contrast Amplification (TCA) Reader, eliminating the need for costly external hardware. Compared with existing recent external thermal imager-based PT-LFIA readout, this reader integrates a selected thermal-sensor-equipped smartphone, a motorized laser module, Bluetooth-enabled control, and a fixed 3D-printed holder into a compact device. title: A Spectral Clustering-Type Algorithm for the Consistent Estimation of the Hurst Distribution in Moderately High Dimensions
abstract: Abstract Scale invariance (fractality) is a prominent feature of the large-scale behavior of many stochastic systems. In this work, we construct a provably convergent and easily interpretable algorithm for the statistical identification of the Hurst distribution (in particular, the scaling exponents) undergirding a high-dimensional fractal system. Starting from recently established properties of wavelet random matrices, the algorithm is based on modified spectral clustering. title: Curvularia lunata as a versatile pathogen causing leaf spot diseases in diverse plant species and its management strategies
abstract: Curvularia lunata poses a significant threat to agricultural ecosystems worldwide, causing substantial yield losses and economic consequences across a variety of crops. As a prominent phytopathogenic fungus known for its affinity for leaf spot diseases, its proliferation warrants attention due to its remarkable adaptability and expanding influence. It can serve as a beneficial endophyte for certain plants; however, its pathogenic nature underscores its potential to affect both plant and human health. title: Toward human-centered AI-assisted terminology work
abstract: Abstract Generative AI is likely to transform terminology work by creating new opportunities for automation. At the same time, it raises concerns about the future of terminologists and terminological resources, as efficiency pressures may encourage excessive automation based on the perception that human expertise can be replaced by AI. However, large language models remain unreliable for terminological purposes due to errors, hallucinations, and various forms of bias, making terminologists indispensable for ensuring the accuracy and reliability of terminological data. title: Plant Crude Polysaccharide‐Enabled Hydrogel Electrodes for Long‐Term Stable EMG Recording
abstract: ABSTRACT Conductive hydrogels with high conductivity, flexibility, skin compatibility, and long‐term stability are essential for reliable bioelectrical signal recording in flexible bioelectronic interfaces for wearable health monitoring and human‐machine interaction. However, additive‐based enhancement often disrupts the intrinsic hydrogel network, leading to trade‐offs among conductivity, flexibility, biocompatibility, and long‐term stability. title: Reconstructed Evapotranspiration in Northern China: Trends, Drivers, and Ecohydrological Impacts
abstract: ABSTRACT Attributing regional evapotranspiration (ET) and assessing its impacts are critical for understanding land‐atmosphere interactions in climate‐sensitive regions such as northern China. This study fuses six gridded ET products with in situ measurements using Random Forest after excluding poorly representative flux sites. title: Test-time optimization for domain adaptive open vocabulary segmentation
abstract: We present Seg-TTO, a novel framework for zero-shot, open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS), designed to excel in specialized domain tasks. While current open-vocabulary approaches show impressive performance on standard segmentation benchmarks under zero-shot settings, they fall short of supervised counterparts on highly domain-specific datasets. title: Assessing Distinctive Physiochemical Properties of Geopolymers, Their Green Development and Utilization in Wastewater Treatment
abstract: ABSTRACT The quest for better and advanced materials that comply with economic and environmental sustainability principles has led to the development of several materials, including geopolymers. Derived from aluminosilicates and acid/alkali activators, geopolymers have proven to be a good alternative to several materials, to be environmentally benign and cheap to produce as they can be produced from valorizing waste. title: Environment-dependent responses of soil physicochemical properties, microbial communities and functional gene profiles to protected and open-field cultivation of Stropharia rugosoannulata
abstract: The cultivation of Stropharia rugosoannulata involves substantial organic substrate input and fungal mycelial activity, which may influence soil nutrient transformation, microbial communities and functional gene profiles. However, whether these responses differ between protected and open-field cultivation settings remains unclear at the metagenomic level.
