title: Aeroallergen Sensitization Patterns Among Adults with Allergic Rhinitis at a Tertiary Center in Erzurum, Turkiye
abstract: Allergic Rhinitis has evolved beyond the conventional definition of nasal mucosal inflammation, becoming a complex ecosystem problem shaped by climate change and shifts in regional biodiversity. This study aimed to characterize aeroallergen sensitization patterns among adults with allergic rhinitis at a tertiary care center in Erzurum, Türkiye. This study was conducted as a single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study at a tertiary allergy clinic in Erzurum, Türkiye. title: Research and Practice on Intelligent Management and Control of the Urban Drainage System in Pinggu District, Beijing Based on SWMM
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive research initiative focused on the intelligent management and control of urban drainage systems, specifically applied to Pinggu District in Beijing. Utilizing the Storm Water Management Model (SWMM), the research integrates extensive literature reviews, comparative case studies of water utility management in major global cities, and rigorous on-site field investigations. title: Climate policy uncertainty and agricultural digital-intelligent transformation in China: evidence from provincial panel data
abstract: Introduction Climate policy uncertainty can affect long-term investment decisions in agriculture, yet its influence on agricultural digital-intelligent transformation remains insufficiently understood. This study examines how lagged climate policy uncertainty affects agricultural digital-intelligent transformation and whether rural finance and agricultural service policies can moderate this relationship. title: Potential early indication of tectonic ground movements by water-well monitoring datasets, with short-term forward modeling
abstract: Tectonic ground movements in the form ot earthquakes can devastate infrastructure and cause significant casualties once their magnitude is 6 and above. This study investigated early indications of such seismic activity through the correlations with temporal variations in groundwater properties. An automated real-time monitoring network was deployed along the Jordan Rift Valley system, utilizing non-operational wells with confined aquifer conditions near major active faults. title: Glacial lake outburst flood hazard and downstream impacts: lessons from Afghanistan examples
abstract: Abstract Glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) pose a growing risk in high mountain regions as climate-driven glacier retreat accelerates lake expansion and new lake formation. In the Hindu Kush Himalaya, particularly in Afghanistan, triggering processes and GLOF propagation downstream are largely unstudied. This study evaluates two Afghanistan GLOFs (Peshghor 2018; Bam-Tanab 2021) using field observations and satellite imagery, and applies two-dimensional hydrodynamic simulation (BASEMENT-MD with BASEbreach) to the Kunj-Peshghor lake event to assess flood propagation, dam-breach dynamics, and

title: Annealed leap-point sampler for multimodal target distributions
abstract: Abstract In Bayesian statistics, exploring high-dimensional multimodal posterior distributions poses major challenges for existing MCMC approaches. This paper introduces the annealed leap-point sampler (ALPS), which augments the target distribution state space with modified annealed (cooled) distributions, in contrast to traditional tempering approaches. title: Investigating the anticancer potential of phytochemicals from the mangrove Rhizophora mucronata as inhibitors of lung cancer-associated proteins: Insights from multiscale computational and in silico analyses
abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with a five-year survival rate of approximately 20-25% despite advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy. There is a continuous need for novel, low-toxicity compounds capable of modulating key oncogenic pathways in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Mangrove ecosystems are rich reservoirs of bioactive phytochemicals, yet the inhibitory potential of compounds from Rhizophora mucronata against validated lung cancer-associated proteins has not been systematically explored using multi-scale computational approaches.

abstract: Abstract Recent generative AI models have achieved remarkable breakthroughs in language and visual understanding. However, although these models can generate realistic visual content, their spatial scale remains confined to bounded environments, preventing them from capturing how geographic environments evolve across thousands of kilometers or from modeling the spatial structure of the large-scale physical world. abstract: Urban pluvial flooding represents a growing threat to contemporary cities, driven by the compounding effects of climate change, rapid urbanization, and inadequate stormwater infrastructure, prompting the study of nature-based solutions (NBS) as potential interventions for mitigating the detrimental effects of urban flooding. abstract: The global increase in plastic usage has highlighted the urgent need for sustainable waste management practices, especially in developing countries. Research indicates that shifting from a linear “take-make-dispose” model to a circular system could mitigate the growing plastic waste issue. abstract: Flood peak timing (FloPT) is a key indicator of hydrological responses to climate change. Yet global FloPT assessments is limited by sparse and uneven in-situ discharge observations. abstract: Variable importance derived from species distribution modelling (SDM) is widely used to identify key environmental drivers of species distributions. abstract: Abstract Higher-education campuses are well suited to staged decarbonization because they combine concentrated electrical demand, substantial rooftop area, diverse load flexibility, and long-term institutional ownership of energy assets. abstract: The fast increase in population and rapid urbanization necessarily heighten the production of (MSW), thereby raising waste management to a significant environmental and policy issue. abstract: Scale formation is a common operational problem in aqueous, industrial and oilfield systems where dissolved mineral ions exceed their solubility limits and precipitate as solid deposits. This manuscript reviews the mechanisms of scale formation, the factors influencing deposition, the major types of scale, and the approaches used for scale prevention, inhibition and removal. abstract: Multi-Hazard Early Warning Systems (MHEWS) are essential for disaster risk management, yet operational implementation remains limited by challenges in hazard integration, forecast uncertainty, and computational requirements. This study develops and evaluates a fast and lightweight prototype MHEWS integrating fluvial flooding and shallow landslide forecasting. abstract: Background Benzophenone-1 (BP-1) is a benzophenone ultraviolet absorber used in cosmetic and personal care products. title: Preparing the body for psilocybin therapy: receptive and generative interoception in cancer patients
abstract: Cancer patients arrive for psilocybin therapy with bodies altered by illness and treatment — bodies that they have learned to brace against, dissociate from, or scan for threat. abstract: Global sustainability education has expanded rapidly since UNESCO adopted its 2030 framework. Informal sustainability knowledge has eroded across the same decade. This Perspective article asks whether exactly those two trends might turn out structurally connected. abstract: Pleione species are valued ornamental plants and the source of the traditional Chinese medicine “Bingqiuzi.” In this study, pathogenic fungi were isolated from diseased leaves and pseudobulbs of Pleione bulbocodioides (Franch.) Rolfe in Yunnan Province, China. title: A Multiscale Analysis of LEED-Certified Projects in Türkiye: Spatial Distribution and Istanbul Case Study
abstract: The LEED certification system, developed by the U.S. Green Building Council (USGBC) and globally recognized, is based on a sustainable approach to buildings. In this study, a multi-scale model was created to first quantitatively analyze—using descriptive statistics—the spatial distribution of LEED-certified projects in Türkiye across its seven geographical regions and 81 provinces. abstract: This paper forecasts United States (US) oil and gas production to 2100 based on historical production data from the US EIA. The ultimately recoverable resource (URR) of each category of US oil and gas is estimated mainly using “Hubbert linearization” (HL). Then forecasts of production are generated by combining past production with either single or multi-cyclic Hubbert (‘logistic-derivative’) curves constrained by the corresponding URRs or with symmetric decline where HL is unclear. abstract: Deuterium is a natural heavy isotope of hydrogen, containing a neutron as well as a proton, making it twice as heavy. title: Living on the edge: climate-induced displacement and livelihood adaptation among char communities in Bangladesh
abstract: Every year, a large number of people in Bangladesh are displaced in char land (riverine island) areas due to climate change. These internally displaced people suffer from socio-economic crises and struggle persistently for a livelihood. This paper investigates the impact of climate change on the livelihoods of displaced char land dwellers, their coping mechanisms, and the obstacles they face. abstract: Determining the breeding frequencies and breeding periods of species that spend part or all of their lives underground is challenging because of limited population surveys. This study presents a geographic information system-based groundwater potential map for the Grande River Hydrographic Basin (GRHB), where groundwater potential is defined as a relative index reflecting conditions favorable for recharge and subsurface storage, rather than a direct measure of aquifer productivity. This study examined the hydrogeochemical characteristics, controlling mechanisms, and health implications of groundwater in the district. abstract: Land Use Land Cover (LULC) change detection is essential for understanding the dynamics of human modified landscapes and for supporting effective land management and urban planning. abstract: Green total factor productivity (GTFP) represents a cornerstone for sustainable development; however, previous scholarship has primarily concentrated on market-based or technological determinants, frequently ignoring the impact of institutional governance. abstract: Universal Design has emerged as an increasingly important approach to the development of inclusive, accessible, and sustainable environments. abstract: The Reverse Osmosis (RO) unit in the Water Treatment Plant (WTP) of a coal-fired power plant plays a vital role in producing low-conductivity demineralized water for boiler feed. abstract: This study aims to examine the traces of the Medusa depiction—one of the most characteristic figures of Greek iconography—within the city of Tokat, located in the ancient Pontus region, through archaeological and numismatic data. title: Source evolution controls the molybdenum isotope composition of Archean continental crust
abstract: Earth’s continental crust is its most chemically evolved and diverse reservoir. Numerous studies have investigated its stable metal isotope character to understand its formation and secular evolution. Molybdenum (Mo) isotopes are useful tracers of petrogenetic processes in Phanerozoic igneous rocks, but Archean granitoids, which make up much of Earth’s early continental crust, remain poorly characterized. abstract: Viticulture faces a double challenge under climate change: optimizing water use and contributing to the sequestration of atmospheric CO2. abstract: Abstract. Agriculture is the largest anthropogenic source of nitrous oxide (N2O), primarily due to nitrogen (N) fertilization. Understanding how the influence of key drivers and the relative contribution of source processes change throughout the cropping season is crucial for developing effective strategies to mitigate N2O emissions. abstract: The task of remote sensing image target detection still faces many challenges: the target scale, orientation and spatial distribution are very different. abstract: Safety-critical autonomous systems often require multiple agents to detect, assign, and intercept non-cooperative mobile targets using only partial observations. abstract: This study presents a multi-decadal assessment of glacier change in the Sara Umga Watershed (SUW), between the Parvati and Chandra basins. title: A critical review on energy accounting – established methods and a new alternative method based on electrification
abstract: Understanding energy accounting is increasingly important because it directly influences our understanding of the energy system and what energy policies make sense. Yet, the confusion has never been more obvious, particularly in the media, consulting arenas and also in some academic work. abstract: Abstract. Lightning is a spatio-temporal phenomenon comprised of individual strikes with specific occurrence times and spatial coordinates. This study models and characterises lightning strikes from single thunderstorms, treating each strike as a point event. abstract: Cybersecurity has become an important component of international aviation safety and security as the increasing digitalization of aircraft systems and air traffic management creates new risks for civil aviation. abstract: The doctrine of state consent is a foundational pillar of the modern international legal order. title: Non-engineered housing construction and earthquakes: A global review of structural performance and vulnerability drivers
abstract: Non-engineered housing accounts for a disproportionate share of earthquake-related casualties worldwide, yet remains under-served by integrated research that bridges its structural, social, and regulatory dimensions. abstract: Anthropogenic modification of freshwater ecosystems has drastically transformed freshwater habitats across Europe, contributing to the decline of limnophilic fish species and promoting the spread of invasive taxa. abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents an automated computational framework for simulating three‐dimensional (3D) fatigue crack growth and adhesive delamination in carbon fiber‐reinforced polymer (CFRP)‐strengthened steel tubular T‐joints. abstract: Conventional steam power plants reject a substantial fraction of their thermal energy through condenser systems, while this low-grade waste heat remains largely unutilized. title: A multi-scale framework for identifying and validating managed aquifer recharge sites in semi-arid Kazakhstan
abstract: Managed Aquifer Recharge (MAR) has emerged as an effective approach for enhancing groundwater resources in water-scarce regions under increasing climate variability and growing water demand. However, most GIS-based MAR studies are limited to regional suitability mapping, whereas the hydrogeological feasibility of identified sites is rarely verified under field conditions. abstract: INTRODUCTION: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality and disability globally, with a disproportionate and growing burden in low- and middle-income Countries. This study examined trends in stroke cases and deaths in Uganda and forecast of future stroke burden through December 2028. abstract: Cross-country, multi-fluid pipeline networks are critical for petroleum transport, yet their operation remains challenging because of dynamic hydraulic conditions, fluid transitions, and limited diagnostic capability between periodic inspections. abstract: Climate and ecological disruption can affect wellbeing, social relationships, and connection to place; when experienced across generations, these widespread disruptions can lead to collective trauma, becoming culturally embedded in identities shared at a community-level. abstract: The “Calcare Cavernoso” (cavernous limestone) formation is a dolomitic carbonate unit characterized by a vacuolar texture and high intrinsic porosity, which favours groundwater-driven dissolution and cavity development and may predispose to subsidence. abstract: ABSTRACT In absence of the original materials, neotypes are proposed for three names. These are Myristica cagayanensis, Myristica hellwigii , and Myristica sulcata. These neotypifcations will be helpful in correct application of these three names.

Here we use coordinated simulations from 16 impact models participating in the Inter-Sectoral Impact Model Intercomparison Project (ISIMIP) to evaluate how increasing forcing resolution from 60 km to 10 km, 3 km, and 1 km affects both climate-input accuracy and impact-model performance. abstract: Functional diversity plays an important role for ecosystem services of managed grasslands such as their gross primary productivity (GPP) and soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks. abstract: La disponibilidad de herramientas de inteligencia artificial (IA) contrasta con las dificultades de las empresas de menor tamaño para integrarlas en sus operaciones. abstract: Reservoirs exposed to similar environmental drivers frequently exhibit markedly different ecological responses. abstract: River sand mining is reshaping riverine landscapes in Bangladesh, but its signature is difficult to separate from channel migration, seasonal water-level change, sediment movement and wider land-use pressure. abstract: Spices have played an important role in culinary traditions, medical practices, and exchange networks for millennia, yet their identification in the archaeological record remains difficult owing to the limited modern comparative micro-morphological reference data. abstract: La transformación digital de la profesión contable plantea la necesidad de revisar cómo los profesores de educación superior seleccionan, utilizan y evalúan las tecnologías en sus asignaturas. abstract: Continuous glucose monitoring in interstitial fluid (ISF) is important for diabetes management, but enzyme-based sensors can lose activity, while many nonenzymatic alternatives show optimal activity in alkaline media. abstract: Decision-making in investments is often flawed due to behavioral biases, leading to suboptimal choices. Robo-advisors aim to mitigate these biases through personalized risk assessment. abstract: Abstract This study presents a two-dimensional transient CFD investigation of the thermal performance of hollow bricks incorporating air, glass wool, and phase change materials under the hot-climate conditions of Kairouan, Tunisia. abstract: Crude oil scheduling couples a combinatorial assignment problem (which vessel unloads into which tank) with continuous-time decisions (when) and nonconvex quality constraints (bilinear blending of sulfur content), making it a genuinely hard mixed-integer nonlinear program. title: A Living Multi‐Omics PDX Biobank of High‐Risk Sarcomas Reveals ecDNA‐Driven Oncogene Amplification in Osteosarcoma and Enables Preclinical Precision Oncology
abstract: Sarcomas are rare, genomically heterogeneous malignancies for which prognosis has remained poor and largely unchanged over recent decades. Patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models are an important tool for cancer research, but their availability and utility remain limited in sarcoma. Here, we establish the SGH sarcoma PDX biobank, a living multi-omics resource comprising 155 xenografts from 132 patients across 11 sarcoma histotypes, with osteosarcoma as the predominant subtype. This cohort is enriched for high-risk sarcomas characterized by poor prognosis and widespread copy-number alterations.

title: Balancing Profit and Planet: Introducing the CARE Framework for Firms' Ethical Climate Strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT Climate change presents an urgent ethical and strategic challenge for contemporary business, demanding responses that are both morally grounded and competitively viable. This paper proposes the CARE framework, Comprehend , Align , Refine , and Evaluate , a structured model for ethical climate strategy rooted in resource‐advantage ( R‐A ) theory and foundational ethical principles. Drawing on a systematic literature review and illustrative case analysis across firms such as Tesla, GM, Toyota, and Interface, the framework integrates normative reasoning with strategic action. abstract: Economic development is widely recognized as a key engine of human security by improving livelihoods, access to essential services, and resilience to socio-economic vulnerabilities. title: Methane bursts during spring thaw in the permafrost region of Northeast China
abstract: Spring thaw in permafrost regions is associated with episodic bursts in atmospheric methane concentration. abstract: México es una República federal, ubicada en América del Norte, donde se realizan elecciones federales, estatales y municipales para renovar diversos cargos públicos. abstract: ABSTRACT The lectotypification of five names in the genus Meyna ( M. spinosa , M. tetraphylla , M. velutina , M. grisea , and M. pubescens ) is presented. abstract: Microplastic contamination is existing as one of the major environmental issues, which needs to be addressed in an efficient manner using economical detection methods. abstract: Achieving carbon peaking and carbon neutrality constitutes a comprehensive and profound economic and social transformation, requiring the coordinated efforts of the government, enterprises and the public. abstract: Abstract Coal gangue exhibits great application potential in saline-alkali soil amelioration. abstract: Abstract Bladeless resonant wind turbines are an alternative technology for small-scale wind energy harvesting because they convert vortex-induced structural oscillations into electrical power without rotating blades. abstract: Abstract Neonicotinoids are insecticides widely used in agriculture and are highly toxic to invertebrates. abstract: Abstract Occasional boom-bust cycles have long characterized national wine industries, but without them coinciding with the cycles of other countries. abstract: While global investments in urban green infrastructure (UGI) are accelerating, the long-term performance of these nature-based solutions is increasingly compromised by a critical disconnect between initial design and post-construction stewardship. abstract: Background: Digital work patterns can blur the boundaries between work and personal life, particularly in project-based information-technology work. abstract: Abstract Catchment hydrologic function describes how meteorological conditions are transformed into streamflow. abstract: The Trusteeship Council, originally established under Chapter XIII of the UN Charter to supervise trust territories and guide them toward self-government or independence, has become largely dormant since the completion of decolonization. abstract: Thin-ply unidirectional (UD) carbon-fibre reinforced polymer (CFRP) tapes enable improved mechanical performance in advanced aerospace structures but remain highly sensitive to manufacturing-induced defects. abstract: Astroviruses are widespread RNA viruses that infect a broad range of animal hosts, with avastroviruses (AAstVs) primarily infecting avian species. While AAstVs are well-documented in domestic birds, their presence in wild birds, particularly in tropical ecosystems like Brazil’s Atlantic Forest, has been underexplored. This study investigated the prevalence and genetic diversity of AAstVs in wild birds from the Serra do Mar State Park, São Paulo. title: Hydroglyphus hamulatus (Gyllenhal, 1813) (Coleoptera, Dytiscidae), a predaceous diving beetle species new to the Czech Republic
abstract: We report the occurrence of the predaceous diving beetle Hydroglyphus hamulatus (Gyllenhal, 1813) in the Czech Republic. Specimens were collected between 2021 and 2024 at post-mining lakes Most and Milada, with an additional record from 1986. These data raise the number of Czech diving beetles to 127 confirmed and eight questionably present species. The new records likely reflect a recent European migration wave and highlight the conservation value of post-mining lakes, a habitat resembling northern European oligotrophic lakes that are rare in Central Europe.

abstract: Mitigating climate change impacts and enhancing the resilience capacity of military infrastructure is essential for the Armed Forces, first, to ensure a high level of both readiness and sustainability transitions and, second, to contribute to each European Union Member-State’s (EU MS) specific energy and climate goals. abstract: Introduction Climate crisis is inherently intersectional; it is a health crisis and a cultural crisis too. abstract: Wetland sustainability emerges from coupled interactions among governance, hydrology, land-use change, landscape structure and ecosystem services. abstract: Forest-to-pasture conversion can alter soil properties, forage composition, and microbial communities, but whether these changes are associated with bovine periodontitis remains unclear. abstract: Spring floods represent one of the major natural hazards in snowmelt-dominated river basins of Central Asia. This research assesses the biosorption effectiveness of different Bacillus strains, namely: Bacillus licheniformis MSRY R, Bacillus amyloliquefaciens MSRY F, and Bacillus amyloliquefaciens MSRY J, to remove Pb(II) and Mn(II) from aqueous solutions, aiming to identify the best effective strain for wastewater bioremediation in Egypt’s Nile Delta (Kitchener and No. 7 drains) in accordance with discharge standards. title: Differential Adaptation between Active Sites and Charge‐Transport Networks in Covalent Organic Frameworks for H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising photocatalysts for H 2 O 2 production. However, optimizing their electronic structure to enhance oxygen activation, charge separation, and transport remains challenging. Herein, a dual‐dimensional COF platform was constructed by integrating diazine isomers, pyridazine (Dz) and pyrazine (Pz), with tunable linkage chemistries (sp 2 c‐, mix‐, and imi‐linked), enabling decoupled regulation and systematic investigation of active‐site electronic environments and framework charge‐transport behavior. In this study, we engineered an Au/ZnO@500/CQDs interface for the simultaneous determination of As(III) and Pb(II) through controlled Au electrodeposition. abstract: Background Soil salinization is a growing constraint on agricultural productivity, yet the adaptive mechanisms of many medicinal plants—particularly Blumea balsamifera , a species of significant economic and pharmacological value—remain poorly understood. In this study, five treatments—CK (control), LS (low salt), MS (medium salt), HS (high salt), and EHS (extremely high salt)—were established to systematically investigate the comprehensive effects of salt stress on the growth, physiological metabolism, and molecular regulatory networks of B. balsamifera. title: Pharmacoepigenetics: from epigenetic regulation to personalized therapeutics
abstract: Pharmacoepigenetics is an emerging field of precision medicine that examines how epigenetic modifications influence interindividual variability in drug response. This review discusses the clinical utility of epigenetic therapy in personalized medicine. abstract: Background Non-pharmacological strategies can complement pharmacological labor analgesia, yet their clinical use is often fragmented across techniques and labor stages, limiting consistent and continuous support during vaginal delivery. Objective To develop a consensus-based, implementation-oriented clinical practice protocol that organizes full-process non-pharmacological labor pain management from prenatal preparation through early postpartum evaluation. abstract: China possesses vast deep coalbed methane (CBM) resources, However, the dynamic evolution of reservoir pressure and permeability during the production process remains unclear, which restricts their efficient development. This study conducted to reveal the dynamic evolution of coal reservoir pressure and permeability under different production rates and its influence on the productivity of deep saturated CBM wells, so as to provide a theoretical basis for efficient development. abstract: In this study, the effects of elevated temperature and cooling method on the direct shear behavior of cement mortar were experimentally investigated. Mortar specimens were exposed to temperatures ranging from 25 °C to 500 °C and subsequently subjected to natural air cooling or water cooling. title: Theoretical and Practical Analysis of the Balance Effect on the Hydraulic Turbine-Generator Unit
abstract: The balance condition has a significant influence on the stability, dynamic behavior, and vibration characteristics of hydraulic turbine-generator units operating at high rotational speeds and under large mechanical loads. This study investigates the impact of balance effects on the operational stability of a 150 MW Francis turbine. First, a new nonlinear multi-degree-of-freedom mathematical model incorporating balance effects is developed. title: Responsible agrivoltaics in temperate Europe: Making systems work for plants, people, and climate
abstract: Societal Impact Statement Agrivoltaics, the co‐location of solar panels and crops, is increasingly promoted to expand renewable energy without compromising agricultural areas. However, systems that are poorly designed impact productivity, landscape, and ecology, and face public criticism. Drawing on multi‐year, multi‐site field experience, this opinion paper discusses when and where agrivoltaics can deliver benefits and which trade‐offs are likely. title: Global disaster risk assessment from Emergency Events Database (2013–2023)
abstract: Abstract. This paper defines an Accumulated Risk Index (ARI) to quantify regional risk levels in a global perspective utilizing Emergency Events Database (EM-DAT) from 2013 to 2023. Building on the World Risk Index (WRI) released from World Risk Report 2023, the ARI focuses more on major events caused by multiple natural hazards within 5°×5° latitude-longitude grids, and calculates their accumulative effects during the period. title: Cell‐Based Micro/Nanorobots: From Living Carriers to Living Therapeutic Specialists
abstract: ABSTRACT Cell‐based micro/nanorobots (CMNRs) integrate intrinsic biological functions with engineered capabilities, constituting an emerging class of biohybrid robotic platforms. Unlike fully synthetic micro/nanorobots, whose functions depend entirely on artificial materials, CMNRs are constructed from living cells or cell‐derived components and can exploit unique biological capabilities. title: Characterization of dairy cattle production systems in two micro-watersheds of the Peruvian Amazonian Andes
abstract: The Peruvian Andean Amazon is home to small-scale dairy livestock production that sustains numerous rural families, but whose heterogeneity complicates the design of targeted interventions. Characterizing and comparing production systems according to their similarities and differences represents an essential step to guide development policies. This study aimed to characterize and compare the dairy cattle production systems of two micro-watersheds in the Amazonas Region, Peru (Molinopampa and Pomacochas), to identify the patterns that differentiate their productive systems. title: The arginine repressor ArgR controls virulence factors of adherent-invasive Escherichia coli strains
abstract: Introduction Adherent-invasive Escherichia coli (AIEC) has been related to the physiopathology of Crohn’s disease, yet its pathogenic mechanisms are not completely understood. Arginine biosynthesis genes are upregulated in AIEC strains compared to non-AIEC strains present in the supernatant of infected intestinal epithelial cells, suggesting that arginine biosynthesis may be involved in AIEC pathogenicity. title: Prediction of future sedimentation patterns in the Kabul River Basin using the ArcSWAT model under CMIP6 SSP climate scenarios
abstract: ABSTRACT Sedimentation poses significant challenges to water resources, reservoir sustainability, and flood management in the Kabul River Basin (KRB), a transboundary basin shared by Afghanistan and Pakistan. Despite extensive hydrological research in the region, limited studies have assessed future sediment dynamics using the latest CMIP6 climate scenarios. title: Social insurance premium reduction and green innovation in enterprises: a study based on social insurance premium reduction reform
abstract: Introduction Green innovation is essential for promoting sustainable economic development and mitigating environmental pollution. Against the backdrop of China’s transition toward high-quality economic development, this study examines whether reductions in social insurance premiums promote corporate green innovation and explores the underlying mechanisms and heterogeneous effects. abstract: Abstract Many policymakers and conservation activists promote creating terrestrial protected areas (PAs) as a central tool to preserve biodiversity and offset global carbon emissions. However, the socioeconomic consequences of PA designation remain understudied. abstract: Fixed nutrient recipes often overlook developmental shifts in uptake and the coupling between transpiration and ion delivery. title: Redesign of the Axial Cooling Fan for an Air-cooled Diesel Engine
abstract: As the power of air-cooled diesel engine increases, the problems of insufficient total pressure and flow rate of the cooling fan have become increasingly prominent. This study proposes a redesign strategy for the axial cooling fan of high-power air-cooled diesel engines to resolve severe overheating under rated operating condition. title: Phytochemical Profiling, In-Vitro COX-2 Inhibition and In-Silico Evaluation of the Ethanolic Flower Extract of Rosa indica L.
abstract: Background: Pain and inflammation are leading reasons for medical care, and the adverse effects of long-term NSAID and opioid use sustain interest in safer plant-derived alternatives. Rosa indica L. (Rosaceae) is traditionally used for wounds, headaches, and inflammatory complaints, but its anti-inflammatory mechanism remains poorly defined. abstract: Background Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) remains a major public health threat in Indonesia, which ranks second globally in tuberculosis burden. title: Assessing the effect of elevated CO2 on wheat leaf rust severity: insights from a free-air carbon dioxide enrichment (FACE) experiment
abstract: Introduction The continuous increase in atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) concentrations is a major driver of global climate change and may alter plant growth and host–pathogen interactions. Understanding how elevated CO 2 affects disease development is therefore important for future crop production and resistance screening. This study investigated the effect of elevated CO 2 on wheat leaf rust ( Puccinia triticina ) in Central European winter wheat genotypes under field conditions. abstract: Abstract The need for energy solutions for inclusive and sustainable societies, as well as the expansion of electricity generation has remarkably accelerated the development of high-voltage power network infrastructures. Hence, the necessitated improved performance demands from rubber-based composite insulators. Silicone rubber (SIR) and Ethylene propylene diene monomer (EPDM) rubber being the most common based-matrix material used in the design and manufacturing of outdoor high-voltage insulator sheds. title: An integrated ArcGIS Python toolbox for SCS-CN event runoff estimation and flood screening in data-scarce Ethiopian basins
abstract: Flood early warning in data-scarce regions is constrained by sparse gauging and limited modelling capacity. We present an integrated ArcGIS Python toolbox automating SCS-CN event runoff estimation, from curve number generation and per-event antecedent moisture classification through to threshold calibration, evaluated in a semi-arid Ethiopian basin. title: Investigation of coal mine overburden as a sustainable fine aggregate in alkali-activated concrete
abstract: The environmental impacts associated with conventional concrete production and the increasing scarcity of natural resources have highlighted the need for alternative materials for sustainable concrete production. This study investigates the feasibility of using coal mine overburden (CMO) as a complete replacement for natural fine aggregate in one-part alkali-activated concrete(AAC). title: Emotional geography of tourism resistance: Claiming the right to the city in overtourism destinations
abstract: Despite advances in resident–tourism discourse and overtourism research, it remains unclear how place-based emotions and perceptions of injustice become collectively articulated and connected to resistance. Drawing on emotional geography and the right to the city, this study challenges the assumption that resistance is a direct response to tourism pressures. abstract: The town of Čelákovice is located in the Central Bohemian Region in the ring around the capital city of Prague, within the Prague Metropolitan Area. The strongest transport flows of commuting and outgoing residents are between Čelákovice and Prague. These findings are based on census data, housing and apartment data, directional and transport surveys, and geolocation data from mobile operators. abstract: The research question guiding this article reflects an aspiration to elaborate and deepen the understanding of how Michael Polanyi’s theoretical framework can enhance the integration of literature and language education. We ask: In what ways do the concepts of personal knowledge and joint meaning, as articulated by Polanyi, contribute to the enhancement of language comprehension within the context of literature education? title: Beyond Sharia Compliance: A Maqāṣid-Based Legal Governance Framework for ESG Reporting in Islamic Finance
abstract: Islamic financial institutions (IFIs) face growing demands to disclose environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance. Yet a normative gap persists between Sharia governance, which largely prioritises contract-level compliance, and global sustainability reporting standards, which do not explicitly incorporate Islamic legal norms. title: Spatial symmetry invariance of three-dimensional Navier–Stokes turbulence
abstract: Direct numerical simulation (DNS) of the deterministic Navier–Stokes (NS) equations is widely used to provide benchmark solutions of turbulent flow, but its accuracy and reliability have not been rigorously inspected from a mathematical viewpoint. Here, we prove a spatial symmetry invariance theorem (SSIT) of three-dimensional NS equations whereby an exact solution of deterministic NS equations under periodic boundary conditions maintains the same spatial symmetry as its symmetric initial flow, forever. title: Joint associations of 2D–3D urban form with land surface temperature along an urban–rural gradient: Implications for sustainable urban planning
abstract: As fundamental urban units, buildings are closely associated with urban thermal environments, and their morphological attributes are related to spatial variations in thermal conditions. Although significant progress has been made in characterizing building morphology, the relative importance and joint associations between 2D horizontal characteristics and 3D vertical structures in shaping neighborhood-scale thermal environments along urban-rural gradients remain underexplored. abstract: The study investigates the development of contemporary Russian Young Art, focusing on digital and multimedia practices employed by graduates of Moscow-based institutions specializing in contemporary art. Special emphasis is placed on the diverse applications of the body in modern performative practices and its integration into an interdisciplinary context. title: When perception meets reality: explaining measured food waste through consumer behavior in a university dining hall
abstract: Food waste (FW) in university dining halls generates significant environmental and economic impacts, yet most studies rely on self-reported measures and rarely combine behavioral perceptions with objective waste data. This study investigates the determinants of consumer FW by integrating individual plate-waste measurements with behavioral and dining-related factors in a university dining hall setting. title: On the coronal origin of magnetic switchbacks in the solar wind
abstract: Abstract The Sun continuously releases a stream of charged particles known as the solar wind, threaded by magnetic field lines that occasionally fold back on themselves in sharp reversals called magnetic switchbacks. These structures are frequently observed by spacecraft near the Sun, but their formation mechanism remains an open question. abstract: Background The soil-improving effects of cereal straw incorporation have been well documented; however, potato straw differs markedly from cereal straw in composition and degradation characteristics, and whether straw return is associated with the soil microbial ecosystem and with gains in yield components through pathways similar to those of cereal straw remains unclear. abstract: This study examined the relationship between life insurance development and economic growth in Nigeria over the period 2000–2024. abstract: Global decarbonization hinges on corporate behavior, yet principal–agent conflicts often undermine firms’ responses to climate change. Despite growing regulatory and stakeholder pressure, managers may prioritize short-term performance over long-term environmental goals when they perceive climate risks as distant or uncertain. abstract: Introduction Staphylococcus aureus is a human pathogen associated with both hospital- and community-acquired infections. Data on its molecular epidemiology in North Central Nigeria are currently unavailable. This study investigated the antibiotic resistance, virulence genes, and the population structure of S. aureus in a tertiary hospital in North Central Nigeria. abstract: Science-policy interfaces in the field of biodiversity have undergone significant progress in the recent years, becoming important spaces for communication and consultation. abstract: Religious diversity can enrich plural societies, yet it may also intensify exclusion and social tension when public institutions privilege dominant traditions, restrict minority participation, or implement religious policies inconsistently. abstract: This study aims to examine forty seals preserved in the Trabzon Museum collection and dated to the Late Ottoman and Early Republican periods within the framework of the discipline of art history. abstract: Introduction Gastrointestinal parasites (GIPs) are a major constraint to the health and productive performance of ruminant livestock across sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). abstract: Background and Aim: Toxoplasma gondii is a globally important zoonotic protozoan, and felids serve as definitive hosts. Although molecular studies have demonstrated substantial genetic diversity of T. gondii in feline populations, information from Thailand remains limited, particularly for stray cats in central and western regions. title: A Bibliometric Analysis of Sustainability Communication Research (2000–2026)
abstract: Sustainability communication is a strategic communication approach that aims to raise awareness of environmental, social, and economic issues and enhance public engagement in line with sustainable development goals. Particularly since 2020, it has gained increasing importance as the climate crisis, environmental issues, and the Sustainable Development Goals have become more prominent. abstract: Assessment policies contribute to the discussion of broad and perpetual societal change. Since the previous assessment policies were in place, the Nova Scotia provincial government has made a series of moves to centralize authority in the province, creating renewed interest in revisiting current local assessment policy in the public education system. Here, we propose that, in some tumors, resistance also depends on specific interactions between malignant and non-malignant cells. Groundwater in coal-bearing strata serves as the direct water-filling source for coal mining, and its water abundance significantly impacts the intensity of the mine water inflow. abstract: Understanding changes in tree cover within agricultural landscapes is critical for assessing the resilience of rural communities and consequent land use dynamics in conflict-affected regions. This study examines spatiotemporal land use and tree cover changes across four districts of Nangarhar Province in eastern Afghanistan using high-resolution (3 m/pixel) satellite imagery. title: CORPORATE GOVERNANCE AND FRAUD PREVENTION: THE ROLE OF AUDITORS IN UNCERTAIN REGULATORY ENVIRONMENTS
abstract: This study investigates the interplay between corporate governance mechanisms and fraud prevention, focusing on the moderating role of auditors in an uncertain regulatory environment. Drawing on an ex post facto research design, we analyse secondary data from 10 consumer goods firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group between 2015 and 2023. abstract: Abstract Grassland fuels can be patchy across space and time, especially on landscapes where multiple grassland plant communities co-occur. abstract: Epidemiological evidence demonstrates that atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) is a major cause of death and disability in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). abstract: The short-beaked echidna (Tachyglossus aculeatus) is widely distributed across Australia and is often described as common, yet robust information on abundance, demography and population trends remains sparse across much of its mainland range. title: Sulfur‐ and Selenium‐Decorated Coumarins: Synthetic Strategies Involving Cyclization and Late‐Stage Functionalization
abstract: Chalcogen-containing coumarins have attracted considerable attention as a versatile class of heterocyclic compounds because sulfur- and selenium-substituted derivatives can significantly influence molecular reactivity, electronic characteristics, and biological activity. Over the past decades, synthetic approaches toward these compounds have advanced through two main strategies: direct construction of the coumarin framework through cyclization processes and late-stage functionalization of preformed coumarin scaffolds. title: Mapping groundwater-dependent vegetation in temperate climates on the example of Central Germany
abstract: Abstract Groundwater-dependent ecosystems are biodiversity hotspots that provide habitat for specialized species. The European Union (EU) Water Framework Directive (WFD) stresses the importance of identifying and protecting these ecosystems. So far, most studies focus on (semi-) arid regions, where groundwater use by ecosystems is both more prevalent and easier to detect. In this study, we adapt groundwater-dependent vegetation (GDV) mapping approaches developed for dry climates to temperate regions by replacing seasonal drought-based indicators with contrasts between dry and wet years. title: On microlocal artifacts arising in tomography modeled by a class of generalized Radon transforms
abstract: Abstract In this paper, we provide a unified framework for understanding how and why artifacts arise in limited data tomography, using precise microlocal analysis of the underlying generalized Radon transforms (gRT). Our insights facilitate a more accurate assessment of reconstructions and eventually enable practical artifact reduction strategies in real-world imaging applications. title: Gut-liver axis in liver pre-metastatic niche formation: immune networks, microbial, and metabolic and emerging therapeutic opportunities
abstract: The liver is a leading target for distant metastasis across multiple cancer types, and liver metastasis invariably portends poor prognosis. The formation of pre-metastatic niches (PMNs) within the hepatic microenvironment creates a permissive “soil” for disseminated tumor cells. However, how the gut-liver axis integrates microbial and metabolic signals to remodel the hepatic PMN remains incompletely understood. title: Integration of multi-source hydroclimatic variables for enhanced drought monitoring
abstract: Agricultural drought monitoring requires integrated indicators that capture the coupled variability of soil moisture and TerraClimate Actual Evapotranspiration (AET) while accounting for uncertainty in multi-source datasets. However, using existing drought indices and model-based indicators alone can be constrained by scale differences, heterogeneous errors, and incomplete representation of drought-related processes, particularly in climatically heterogeneous agricultural regions. title: The mediating role of social distance on the association between audience-protagonist similarity and fear: a case of fear of COVID-19
abstract: Objective This study examined the effects of news content on fear of COVID-19 by examining perceived social distance and audience-protagonist similarity. Method Participants ( N = 78) read a fictitious news story about a COVID-19 patient (similar/dissimilar protagonist) and then rated social distance regarding this protagonist and their fear of COVID-19. Results The results showed that participants exposed to a similar protagonist reported significantly lower perceived social distance, and that social distance was moderately negatively correlated with fear of COVID-19. title: Comprehensive patient education in cardiac rehabilitation: A Mexican perspective
abstract: Background Patient education is a core component of cardiac rehabilitation (CR), yet it is frequently delivered as a standardized transfer of information rather than as a structured intervention aimed at promoting behavioral change and long-term self-management. This limitation may be particularly relevant in culturally, geographically, linguistically, and socioeconomically diverse populations, such as Mexico. institutions: Institute for Social Security and Services for State Workers

title: Determining strategic locations for rental housing development with GIS and expert systems around the educational area of Universitas Sulawesi Barat
abstract: Agglomeration is no longer confined to the economic sector but has also expanded into education, generating concentration effects around higher-education institutions. A similar phenomenon is evident around the campus of Universitas Sulawesi Barat in Majene Regency, where the rapid growth of rental housing risks triggering uncontrolled urban sprawl. This study aims to (1) identify the key factors influencing the selection of potential locations for rental housing and (2) determine the most suitable locations based on these factors. title: Determinants of continuance intention toward eLearning usage in higher education institutions
abstract: Abstract This study aims to examine the key determinants influencing students’ continuance intention towards eLearning usage in higher education institutions in Iraq. It proposes an integrated model combining the Expectation-Confirmation Model (ECM) and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2), extended with the construct of digital literacy. title: Piloting Digital Leadership, Technology Acceptance, and Literacy–Numeracy Instruments in Early Childhood Education
abstract: Strengthening foundational literacy and numeracy in early childhood education (ECE) may depend partly on how principals lead digital change and how educators perceive technology, but, to our knowledge, no published instrument set measures these constructs together for Indonesian ECE. journal: Indonesian Educational Administration and Leadership Journal (IDEAL).

title: An automated operon refactoring workflow for heterologous expression of non-ribosomal peptide biosynthetic gene clusters
abstract: Microbial genomes encode numerous biosynthetic gene clusters, yet most remain experimentally uncharacterized, particularly large non-ribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) clusters that resist conventional cloning. Existing refactoring approaches are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that OSAR (One-Step Assembly and Refactoring)—an automated platform integrating algorithmic primer design with yeast homologous-recombination cloning—directly assembles and refactors NRPS clusters without custom DNA synthesis. title: Design challenges and enabling technologies for ultra-high-speed electric drive systems
abstract: Ultra-high-speed electric drive systems are a key route toward higher power density in electric vehicles, aerospace propulsion, and industrial applications, with series-production traction machines now exceeding 20,000 r/min and laboratory prototypes approaching or exceeding 100,000 r/min. title: A systematic assessment of environmental impacts and techno-economic benefits of solid digestate conversion to biochar: a case study of pig farm digestate in Taiwan
abstract: Abstract Digestate, the solid by‑product of anaerobic digestion, can cause nutrient leaching, greenhouse‑gas release and heavy‑metal accumulation. Slow pyrolysis offers a promising route for upgrading digestate into biochar, yet its high energy demand and uncertain economics must be carefully weighed. This study evaluates the functional unit of 1 t solid digestate, the conversion of digestate to biochar at a pig farm in Pingtung, Taiwan, and compares the results with composting and incineration. title: Biogenic fabrication of zinc oxide nanoparticles for enhanced germination and early seedling establishment of rice under salinity stress
abstract: Introduction Salinity stress restricts rice ( Oryza sativa L. ) germination and early establishment through osmotic stress, ionic toxicity, and excessive reactive oxygen species production. Although ZnO nanoparticles (ZnONPs) can enhance salinity tolerance, the influence of their biological synthesis source on nanoparticle properties and efficacy remains poorly understood. title: GTPase GBP7 promotes HSV-1 infection by interacting with and activating eEF1A1 to accelerate the protein translation process
abstract: Guanylate-binding proteins (GBPs) are immune GTPases induced by interferons (IFNs) and comprise GBPs1-7. In this study, GBP7, a less studied member of the GBPs, was identified to possess Herpes simplex virus I (HSV-1) promoting effects on replication both in vitro and in vivo. title: Integration of IoT-based healthcare devices within the smart grid architecture model: a conceptual framework with economic and energy assessment for elderly care in Europe
abstract: Introduction This study investigates the integration of IoT-enabled medical devices within the Smart Grid Architecture Model (SGAM) to support elderly home-based care in Europe. The study develops a conceptual SGAM–IoT framework that maps healthcare devices, actors, communication pathways, and functions across the SGAM interoperability layers, domains, and zones, with particular attention to interoperability, data exchange and integration between the home environment, healthcare services, and energy-aware infrastructure. title: Parametric Optimization of Shading Devices to Improve Classroom Daylighting Performance
abstract: Inadequate visual comfort in classrooms can impair the physical and mental well-being of teachers and students, making sufficient daylight essential in academic environments, particularly in hot, arid climates. This study investigates shading devices (SDs) for improving daylight performance in an existing university classroom. Parametric analysis and optimization used Autodesk Revit (BIM) with Insight plugins. abstract: Introducción: El perfil blando es importante en ortodoncia porque influye en la apariencia y función del rostro, y conocerlo ayuda a planificar mejor los tratamientos. title: Integrative taxonomy of Trichogramma vitessoides sp. nov. (Hymenoptera, Trichogrammatidae), an egg parasitoid of Heortia vitessoides from southern China
abstract: Egg parasitoids of the genus Trichogramma Westwood, 1833 are widely used in integrated pest management, but their minute size and reduced morphology complicate identification. Using integrative taxonomy, we describe Trichogramma vitessoides Hu & Yang, sp. nov . from Guangdong, China, based on a laboratory colony established from parasitoids reared from naturally parasitised egg masses of Heortia vitessoides (Moore, 1885) (Lepidoptera, Crambidae), a defoliator of Aquilaria sinensis (Lour.) title: Repurposing farnesyltransferase inhibitors tipifarnib and lonafarnib as antibacterial agents: proteomic and functional analyses
abstract: Farnesyltransferase inhibitors (FTIs) like tipifarnib and lonafarnib, originally developed as anticancer agents, show antibacterial activity against Gram-positive pathogens through an unknown mechanism of action. Here, we investigated the proteomic response of Bacillus subtilis 168 (Gram-positive) and an efflux-deficient Escherichia coli Δ tolC mutant (Gram-negative) to sublethal concentrations of FTIs. title: Reimagining Bucharest’s Central Station: PPP and Air Rights as Tools for Metropolitan Integration
abstract: Railway-station redevelopment is increasingly associated with transit-oriented development, land-value capture, and metropolitan regeneration, yet post-socialist station areas remain insufficiently examined through an integrated spatial, operational, and financing lens. This paper addresses that gap through a scenario-based case study of the Gara de Nord (Bucharest’s North Train Station)–Basarab rail complex in Bucharest (GN-B). title: The effect of air pollution exposure on mortality: a time series study in Sivas, Türkiye
abstract: Using a generalized linear model (GLM), the relationships between daily changes in air pollutants and mortality rates in Sivas Central District (Türkiye) were examined over five years (2017–2021), controlling for long–term time trends, seasonal effects, and meteorological factors in this study. The impacts of major pollutants (PM₁₀, PM 2.5 , and NO₂) on daily mortality were analyzed at different time lags (0–10 days). abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigated the morphological and SEM‐based micromorphological characteristics of 11 Galium L. taxa representing eight sections occurring in Eskişehir Province, Türkiye, to identify taxonomically informative characters. Morphological and micromorphological assessments were conducted on stems, leaves, flowers, and mericarps, with particular emphasis on epidermal cell morphology, stomatal distribution, trichome characteristics, and surface ornamentation. title: Olaparib plus tremelimumab in women with recurrent ovarian cancer and a germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation: a phase I/II study
abstract: Response rates to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in ovarian cancer are low. In preclinical studies, poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibition (PARPi) synergized with CTLA4 ICB to achieve long-term survival in Brca1-deficient ovarian cancer models. Here we evaluated the safety and efficacy of combined treatment with the PARPi olaparib and the CTLA4 ICB tremelimumab for recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer in a multi-site single-arm phase I/II study enrolling 50 women with germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations (NCT02571725). title: Análisis cromático para caracterización de dipterofauna de la familia Piophilidae con fines forenses
abstract: Forensic entomology is an essential discipline for determining the Postmortem Interval; however, the description of color in species of the Piophilidae family remains a subjective process that depends on the expert's perception and lighting conditions. This study addresses this issue throught chromatic analysis to standardize the characterizing of forensic-interest Piophilidae entomological samples in Ecuador. abstract: Background Long-read sequencing has revealed complex variations, such as gene conversions in immunologically critical PE/PPE gene families, yet their role in Mycobacterium tuberculosis host adaptation remains unclear. Methods We performed a comparative genomic analysis across a gradient of host-imposed selective pressure: chronic within-host infection, latent household transmission, and a 21-year clonal outbreak in Bern, Switzerland. title: Transformation of the media systems of the South Caucasus countries under digital globalisation
abstract: This paper aimed to study changes in the media systems of South Caucasus countries (Georgia, Armenia, and Azerbaijan) against the background of digital globalisation. Methods of the study included document and content analysis of academic publications, materials of international organisations, information on monitoring and civil society platforms, regulatory and legal acts, information from analytical agencies, and comparative analysis of indicators of the level of digitalisation and freedom of the media in each of the three countries. title: ERMA: a harmonizing epicPCR data analysis tool
abstract: BACKGROUND: EpicPCR links functional genes to taxonomic markers at the single-cell level and has become an important method in microbial ecology and antimicrobial resistance research. However, the lack of missing standardized data analysis workflows limits reproducibility and comparability across studies. Existing analyses are often based on custom, unpublished scripts, complicating cross-study benchmarking and reuse. title: Laminarin suppresses PD-L1 translation by targeting YTHDF1 to exert antitumor immunity in triple-negative breast cancer
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is characterized by low response rates and rapid acquired resistance to current immunotherapies, highlighting an urgent unmet clinical need for novel therapeutic strategies. Herein, we demonstrated that laminarin, a biocompatible β-1,3-glucan extracted from brown algae, exerts significant antitumor immune effects against TNBC with no evident toxicity under the tested conditions. abstract: Abstract Biodiesel is a mixture of fatty acid methyl esters in which the chemical structure, hydrocarbon chain length, saturation or unsaturation, and position of the C = C double bond in each methyl ester influence the biodiesel’s properties. In this study, pure mixtures of short-chain methyl esters (methyl acrylate and methyl propionate, methyl 3-butenoate and methyl butyrate) were selected as model systems to evaluate the effect of the C = C bond on copper corrosion behavior. title: Biomodelos como sistemas centinela en ecotoxicología reproductiva
abstract: La contaminación ambiental es un tema de índole mundial que repercute directamente en la salud de los seres vivos, siendo un tema importante de estudio e investigación. Dentro de estos procesos de contaminación tenemos las aguas residuales, las cuales contienen mezclas complejas de sustancias químicas disruptoras endocrinas, metales pesados y fármacos que representan riesgos para la salud reproductiva. abstract: Nigeria's persistent fiscal crisis, characterized by escalating debt burdens exceeding 100% of revenue and chronic budget deficits, reflects a fundamental governance failure rooted in a systemic trust deficit rather than merely technical economic challenges. title: Screening high symbiotic matching combinations of rhizobia and alfalfa varieties in saline soil
abstract: Rhizobium inoculation can improve alfalfa performance, but responses depend on both plant genotype and growing environment. We first screened 14 rhizobial strains plus one commercial inoculant with Medicago varia ‘Caoyuan No. 3’ (CY3) in a greenhouse pot experiment, together with an uninoculated control (16 treatments; three pots per treatment). title: Cover crop rotations improve soil health in commercial tropical vegetable systems, but responses depend on soil type
abstract: Sustainable vegetable production requires healthy soils. While the effects of cover cropping as a conservation practice on mid- and long-term soil health improvement in temperate row crops are well studied, the short-term recovery of soil health in tropical vegetable systems is less documented. We evaluated the effects of shifting from a vegetable–fallow rotation to a vegetable–cover crop rotation of legumes or legume-grass in commercial farms of two municipalities on the semi-arid southern coast of Puerto Rico: Guánica (a loamy Typic Calciargids) and Santa Isabel (a clayey Typic Haplusterts).

title: Religious Regulation as Indirect Discrimination? Religious “Color‐Blindness” and Democratic Legitimacy Among Religious Majorities and Minorities
abstract: ABSTRACT Background What is the impact of “colorblind” religious discrimination political attitudes of religious minorities? Cross‐national research exploring religious regulation's impact on democratic support among religious has given priority to the analysis of explicit forms of religious discrimination while also focusing exclusively on religious minorities as a subgroup. This article addresses this gap in the literature by measuring how neutral regulation of religion drives divergent evaluations of state legitimacy and democracy in general between religious minorities and majorities. title: Dietary diversity among women of reproductive age (15–49 yrs) across rural and urban settings: a scoping review
abstract: Dietary diversity (DD) reflects micronutrient adequacy and diet quality. Inadequate dietary diversity has adverse effects on health of the women and increases the risk of complications during pregnancy and childbirth due to deficiencies of micronutrients. This scoping review aims to synthesize the current understanding of dietary diversity among WRA in urban and rural settings, highlighting key findings from recent studies. title: Event-Triggered Dynamic Urbanisation and Urban Land Expansion: A Case Study of Bangalore, India
abstract: Since the 1990s, Bangalore has undergone rapid urbanisation, largely driven by the growth of IT parks, attracting multinational corporations and a significant population influx. The development of transportation infrastructure, including new roads, transit systems and international airports, along with the construction of malls and other developments, further fuelled the urban growth. abstract: In recent decades, the study of the human connectome —the comprehensive map of the brain's neural connections— has redefined our understanding of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) as a spectrum of functional and structural alterations in specific brain networks. This review explores evidence on functional connectivity patterns in MDD, highlighting the involvement of networks such as the default mode network (DMN), frontoparietal network (FPN), salience network (SN), and reward circuits. title: LIDERAZGO Y TECNOLOGÍA PARA TRANSFORMAR LA GESTIÓN DEL CAMBIO EN EMPAS
abstract: Las entidades públicas que prestan servicios esenciales a la población enfrentan cambios que requieren adaptación, eficiencia e innovación ante la transformación digital y las demandas sociales del entorno. abstract: Introduction Numerous studies have used the Assessing Levels of Physical Activity and Fitness (ALPHA) battery to evaluate physical fitness (PF) and its positive impact on the health of school-age children, assessing various components of fitness. Despite its widespread use, no bibliometric review has systematically examined research trends or scientific output related to the ALPHA-Fitness battery. abstract: Introduction The disintegration of red-bed mudstone has caused lists of geohazards, which threatens the geological environment in the upper reaches of the Yellow River, China. However, the disintegration mechanism and characteristics of red-bed mudstone influenced by multi - factor remain unclear. abstract: Abstract Parallelization of programs is of essence in the high-performance computing (HPC) area. Data dependence analyses should not merely be correct, but as precise as possible, so as not to miss any opportunity for parallelization. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents OP‐Follower , a fully onboard, pure vision‐based, obstacle‐aware person‐following framework for quadruped robots. title: New trends in the development of modern Saudi woman fiction
abstract: Saudi women Novel has gone through distinctive literary trends until it reaches its present form. Fictions have experienced variety of topics from the past through the present to the future. The present study aims to investigate the new trends in the development in Modern Saudi Woman fiction by presenting models of Saudi women's writing within the horizon of the vision of 2030. title: Global decline in urban blue-green cooling efficiency driven by vapor pressure deficit
abstract: As global warming intensifies urban heatwave risk, blue-green spaces have become critical regulators of urban thermal environments. Yet previous studies have focused mainly on temperature responses, and the extent to which atmospheric moisture demand, represented by vapor pressure deficit (VPD), shapes blue-green-space cooling across climate regions remains insufficiently quantified. title: La integración de la tecnología digital en la formación inicial del profesorado de música: análisis comparativo de los modelos TPACK, SAMR, TAM y la Teoría de Usos y Gratificaciones
abstract: La formación docente en educación musical enfrenta el reto de integrar la tecnología digital de manera crítica, creativa y pedagógicamente significativa. Este artículo examina cuatro marcos teóricos —TPACK, SAMR, TAM y la Teoría de Usos y Gratificaciones— como referentes esenciales para orientar la preparación del profesorado ante los desafíos de la enseñanza musical en contextos digitales. title: Integrated Assessment of Climate and Land Use/Land Cover Change Effects on Hydrological Responses in the Hare River Watershed, Southern Ethiopia
abstract: This study assesses the integrated impacts of land use/land cover (LULC) change and climate change on hydrological responses in the Hare watershed, Southern Ethiopia, using the SWAT model. Historical climate trends, LULC dynamics, and future climate projections based on CMIP6 scenarios were analyzed. The model was calibrated and validated using observed stream flow data. abstract: Microbiomes influence tea quality, safety, and health from production to consumption, yet most studies and reviews examine individual stages. abstract: Conventional adenomas and serrated lesions are two major precursor lesions of colorectal cancer. They arise through distinct carcinogenic pathways, namely the conventional adenoma–carcinoma sequence and the serrated neoplasia pathway. abstract: The origins of initial domestication of crops have long intrigued researchers across disciplines, with implications for genetic resource utilization and conservation. abstract: El E-Learning se ha convertido en una herramienta fundamental para el desarrollo profesional y la continuidad educativa, especialmente tras la pandemia por COVID-19. abstract: Edible films and coatings (EFCs) are promising alternatives to conventional petrochemical food packaging due to their biodegradability and potential to extend food shelf life (SL). title: Naiveté or Strategic Ambiguity? Examining Economic, Demographic and Security Narratives in India's Refugee Policy
abstract: ABSTRACT The decadal transition in the Indian politico‐legal stance on refugees, from a human rights tilt to national security concerns, invites a close examination. India maintains a theoretical safe distance from the international legal framework on refugees by not acceding to the 1951 Refugee Convention, while on the ground, it extensively engages—politically and judicially—with refugee‐related domestic legal issues. In the absence of a dedicated legal framework, the refugees, categorised based on temporalities and spatialities, face a highly unpredictable executive and judicial discretion.

title: Electric fields control static charge during contact-friction-separation
abstract: Contact electrification occurs when two materials rub against one another. This is either a problem, such as when charge builds up during powder processing, or an exploited phenomenon to harvest energy, as is the case in triboelectric nanogenerators. However, why contact electrification occurs remains a topic of hot debate, with ions, adsorbates, electrons and combinations thereof being ascribed the charge carriers. abstract: Abstract Flexible piezoelectric composites hold great promise for self-powered sensors and wearable electronics, but their performance is often limited by the low piezoelectricity of polymers, uneven dispersion of inorganic fillers, and poor interfacial stress transfer. To overcome these challenges, we fabricated a vertically oriented pyramidal BiFeO3-BaTiO3 (BFO-BTO) microcone array on P(VDF-TrFE) films using an AAO template-assisted method. title: Meaning-making coping under the threat of war: a qualitative study of people in Sweden
abstract: Introduction The question of how individuals make meaning of, and cope with, the threat of war remains underexplored, particularly in highly secular societies and in contexts of anticipated rather than directly experienced conflict. Methods This article reports findings from a qualitative study of meaning-making coping among people in Sweden, a country that has not experienced war within its borders for more than two hundred years but that now faces heightened geopolitical tension. title: Building schemas through the lived experiences of an African American roller coaster engineer: Interdisciplinary analyses of students’ dialogues in a physics unit
abstract: This research is part of a larger goal to capture the heritage, lived experiences, and scientific and cultural capital of Black people in the United States in the science curricula. This research examines the impact of a Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) physics curriculum created for the K-12 classroom, which began with the lived experiences and narratives of an African American engineer. title: Tris(4‐Halo‐2,6‐Difluorophenyl)Methyl Radicals Exhibiting Green Doublet Emission
abstract: Accessing high-energy doublet excited states while maintaining radical persistence remains a major challenge for luminescent organic radicals, with stable radicals predominantly emitting from the red to near-infrared region. Herein, we report two stable fluorinated trityl radicals, tris(4-chloro-2,6-difluorophenyl)methyl (CDFTM) and tris(4-bromo-2,6-difluorophenyl)methyl (BDFTM), based on tris(4-halo-2,6-difluorophenyl)methyl frameworks, which exhibit intrinsic green doublet emission at 527 and 529 nm, respectively. title: The construction of self/national identity and the other in Ottoman TV series produced in the AK Party period
abstract: This article comparatively analyzes five Ottoman-themed Turkish television series broadcast during the AK Party (AKP) period—Diriliş: Ertuğrul, Kuruluş: Osman, Mehmed: Sultan of Conquests, Barbaroslar: Sword of the Mediterranean, and Payitaht Abdülhamid—to ask how popular history dramas participate in the cultural construction of national identity. The corpus comprises the first three complete episodes of each series, fifteen episodes in all. abstract: Nilayon ng pag-aaral na ito na masuri ang kahusayan ng paggamit ng reciprocal teaching bilang estratehiya sa pagtuturo sa mga mag-aaral sa pag-unawa sa maikling kuwento ng Baitang 9 sa Daanbantayan National High School sa taong panuruan 2025-2026 bilang batayan sa pagbuo ng kagamitang pampagtuturo.Gumamit ang pananaliksik ng One Group Pretest-Posttest Quasi-experimental Design na nilahukan ng 50 mag-aaral ng Baitang 9. title: Association between emotional intelligence and organizational commitment among clinical nurses: workplace social capital as a potential mediator in a cross-sectional study
abstract: Background Workplace social capital has been shown to alleviate occupational stress and enhance job wellbeing and satisfaction. However, limited research has examined the mediational pattern involving workplace social capital between EI and organizational commitment among clinical nurses. This study aims to investigate the indirect effect of EI on organizational commitment through workplace social capital, providing empirical evidence for nursing managers to develop strategies that may enhance nurses' organizational commitment. abstract: Study Region Valencia, Spain. Study Focus Two full-scale Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems (SUDS), a permeable pavement (PP) and a filter drain (FD), were monitored over one year at a residential street in Valencia under Mediterranean rainfall conditions. Hydraulic and water-quality performance were evaluated using concentration-based (Event Mean Concentration, EMC) and mass-based (Pollutant Mass Loading, PML) indicators. title: Rebirth amidst risk: can the digital economy break the urban resource curse? evidence from resource-based cities
abstract: Digital transformation reshapes global economic paradigms and offers a pathway for resource-dependent regions to transcend the “resource curse.” By leveraging panel data from 111 Chinese resource-based cities between 2011 and 2019, this study empirically examines whether the burgeoning digital economy facilitates departure from resource-dependent stagnation. First, our analysis validates the presence of a robust resource curse within the sample, and subsequently scrutinizes the moderating role of digital development. title: Enhanced precipitable water vapor inversion and rainstorm monitoring based on GNSS PPP regional tropospheric modeling
abstract: Precipitable water vapor (PWV) is critical for severe weather forecasting, yet existing GNSS Precise Point Positioning (PPP) retrieval methods are limited by neglecting tropospheric horizontal gradients and lacking regional coverage. Moreover, PWV alone cannot reliably determine precipitation onset. title: Designing interactive VR scenarios for speech and language therapy with the assessment framework
abstract: Virtual reality (VR) games are becoming increasingly popular for entertainment. When integrated into speech and language therapy (SLT) practice, VR can be an innovative tool that supports therapeutic interventions by offering new opportunities for immersive interaction and greater motivation for individuals with language disorders to participate in therapy. In this study, we aim to introduce a methodology for designing interactive VR serious-game scenarios for speech and language therapy, together with an integrated multidisciplinary user-feedback assessment framework. title: Regenerative gastronomic tourism and short food supply chains: a SOR model approach
abstract: Sustainable food systems depend not only on how food is produced but also on how consumers form trust, identity, and lasting relationships with local producers. Regenerative gastronomic tourism, rooted in ancestral knowledge and place-based culinary practices, has emerged as a catalyst for short food supply chains (SFSCs), yet the psychological mechanisms converting immersive culinary experiences into sustained demand remain poorly understood.
