title: Steroidal scaffolds in radiopharmaceutical chemistry: Synthetic strategies, receptor targeting, and theranostic applications
abstract: Advances in medicinal chemistry and molecular medicine have accelerated the development of targeted strategies that deliver bioactive agents selectively to diseased tissues. Targeted radionuclide therapy and nuclear imaging depend on pairing an appropriate radionuclide with a ligand that confers biological selectivity, and steroids are especially well suited to this role because their rigid tetracyclic scaffold supports specific interactions with protein binding sites and high-affinity recognition of estrogen, progesterone, and androgen receptors relevant to hormone-dependent cancers. title: Advanced oxidation processes for 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid in aqueous media: evidence gaps, mechanistic insights and emerging directions
abstract: Abstract The herbicide 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) remains a relevant aquatic contaminant because parent-compound disappearance does not imply mineralization, detoxification or treatment readiness. This systematic review synthesizes recent evidence on advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) and closely related chemically coupled routes for aqueous 2,4-D treatment. title: ENTRE LA RESISTENCIA AL CAMBIO Y LA NECESIDAD DE INNOVACIÓN: UN RETO DE LA DIRECCIÓN EMPRESARIAL EN EL SECTOR DE TRANSPORTE DE CARGA TERRESTRE
abstract: El presente estudio analiza la relación entre la resistencia al cambio organizacional y la necesidad de innovación tecnológica en el sector de transporte de carga terrestre en Bogotá y su zona periférica. Bajo un enfoque cualitativo interpretativo con alcance exploratorio y fenomenológico, se abordó una muestra cualitativa de directivos y una muestra encuestada de 101 colaboradores de 10 empresas representativas del sector. title: Tumor-educated macrophages promote ferroptosis inhibition in pancreatic cancer via activating the p62-KEAP1-NRF2 pathway
abstract: Background Pancreatic cancer is one of the most aggressive and lethal gastrointestinal malignancies, and ferroptosis resistance contributes to chemoresistance. Tumor-educated macrophages(TAMs) are key components of the tumor microenvironment, but whether and how they regulate ferroptosis in pancreatic cancer cells remains largely unknown. This study aimed to investigate the regulatory role of tumor-educated macrophages (TEMs) in pancreatic cancer cell ferroptosis and the underlying molecular mechanism. title: Fixed compliance costs and producer selection in regional food production: evidence from China's 2006 agricultural product quality and safety law
abstract: Food-safety law protects consumers, but the mandatory standards, input restrictions, record-keeping, and pre-sale testing it imposes are largely fixed costs that fall hardest on the smallest producers. Whether that incidence survives aggregation, that is, whether output shed by marginal producers is absorbed by survivors or genuinely lost to a region, remains unsettled. title: Network pharmacology–driven identification of PTP1β and rational design of simufilam-based allosteric inhibitors for neuroprotection in Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that predominantly affects elderly people and is characterized by cognitive decline and dementia. Protein tyrosine phosphatase-1B (PTP1B) is known to modulate pro-inflammatory mediators, and its overexpression in the brain has been implicated in AD-associated neuroinflammation. This study explores the mechanism of A20, A26, and co-crystal-designed compound targeting non-competitive allosteric PTP1B enzyme inhibition for AD therapy using network pharmacology and computational studies. title: Análisis del remedio indemnizatorio en el ámbito de la neurotecnología
abstract: El trabajo busca individualizar hipótesis concretas de daños que en la actualidad sufre o podría sufrir una persona en el ámbito de la neurotecnología. Los casos más relevantes de daños son los derivados, respectivamente, de la puesta en el mercado de productos defectuosos neurotecnológicos y de infracciones de la normativa de protección de datos personales por parte de la empresa responsable y/o encargada del tratamiento de tales datos en el citado sector. title: Quantification of early-stage sigma phase nucleation in thermally aged 2205 duplex stainless steel at 850 °C: An integrated experimental, kinetic, and thermodynamic modelling approach
abstract: Duplex stainless steels combine high strength and corrosion resistance, but exposure at 600-950 °C can precipitate brittle sigma (σ) and chi (χ) phases. This study examines early-stage intermetallic-phase evolution in 2205 duplex stainless steel aged at 850 °C using automated SEM image analysis, Avrami kinetics, Thermo-Calc equilibrium calculations and TC-PRISMA modelling. title: Cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment of pasteurized milk production in Uzbekistan identifies environmental hotspots and improvement opportunities
abstract: Dairy production is an important component of Uzbekistan's food system but is associated with environmental burdens. This study presents a cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA) of pasteurized milk production in Uzbekistan to quantify environmental impacts, identify hotspots, evaluate uncertainty, and assess environmental improvement options. title: Aquatic moss by-products offer an alternative to algal biomasses for phytostimulant bioproduction
abstract: Introduction Aquatic mosses are recently gaining attention for commercial use, stimulating the development of new biomass cultivation approaches. This study explores the potential of by-products from aquatic moss propagation as natural plant biostimulants, addressing the need for low-waste production and sustainable agricultural strategies. abstract: The Strychnos madagascariensis (Black Monkey Orange) is commonly found in tropical and subtropical Africa. Black monkey orange (BMO) species can strive in hot and relatively dry conditions of Southern Africa. It is one of the diverse indigenous fruit species (IFSs) in Bushbuckridge Local Municipality (BLM), Mpumalanga Province in South Africa. title: Research progress of polyunsaturated fatty acids in inflammatory bowel disease: from mechanisms to treatment
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) imposes a growing clinical burden through recurrent intestinal inflammation, malnutrition, treatment-related toxicity, and incomplete mucosal healing. Polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) are plausible dietary regulators of this burden, yet their effects cannot be reduced to a simple anti-inflammatory role for n-3 PUFAs and a pro-inflammatory role for n-6 PUFAs. title: Low-glycemic index functional flour modulates gut microbiota in association with anti-obesity effects in mice
abstract: Background Obesity has become a prevalent global chronic disease, and dietary intervention is a safe and effective strategy for obesity prevention and management. Laminaria japonica and Lentinula edodes are widely consumed edible resources in China, while the lipid-lowering efficacy of functional noodles supplemented with their dietary fibers remains unclear. title: Phytogenic zinc oxide nanoparticles in breast cancer therapy: an ethnopharmacological perspective on multi-targeted mechanistic pathways and translational constraints
abstract: Introduction Breast cancer remains the most frequently diagnosed malignancy and the leading cause of cancer death among women worldwide as of 2026. While conventional interventions face challenges like drug resistance and systemic toxicity, the integration of green nanotechnology with ethnopharmacology offers a biocompatible, sustainable alternative. This review assesses the mechanistic pathways and therapeutic potential of phytogenic zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs) synthesized using bioactive secondary metabolites. abstract: ABSTRACT Herein, we report a pulsed laser irradiation in liquid (PLIL) strategy that concurrently induces phase transformation, morphological reconstruction, and single‐atom stabilization in bismuth oxide (Bi 2 O 3 ) for efficient carbon‐dioxide reduction reaction (CO 2 RR). title: Chronic Electroconvulsive Shock Disrupts Hippocampal Physiology and Impairs Associative Memory in Mice
abstract: ABSTRACT Electroconvulsive therapy ( ECT ) is a highly effective treatment for depression but it has undesirable side effects on various aspects of cognition, including memory. Patients may display retrograde amnesia for autobiographical events and anterograde amnesia in tests of recall and recognition memory. These amnestic effects are likely to depend, at least in part, on changes in the hippocampus. title: Tornado environments derived from ERA5 over Indonesia
abstract: Abstract Tropical maritime regions, such as Indonesia, experience tornadoes. However, the tornado environment in Indonesia remains poorly understood. In this study, we analyzed convective and kinematic parameters associated with 119 tornado cases from 2010 to 2024. Prior to examining tornado environments, the performance of ERA5 reanalysis was evaluated against sounding observations. title: Sharia Prescribes, Adat Applies: Reconstructing Cognitive Justice in Minangkabau Legal Historiography
abstract: Colonial legal historiography in Minangkabau has long portrayed matrilineal adat and Islamic law as antagonistic systems, casting adat as static custom and Islam as an external imposition. This article repositions the formula Syarak Mangato, Adaik Mamakai (SMAM), rendered here as “Sharia Prescribes, Adat Applies,” as an analytical method for dismantling this binary, rather than treating the formula merely as a cultural description, as much of the existing scholarship has done. title: Multidimensional molecular strategies for crop photoperiod adaptation and latitudinal expansion
abstract: The traditional regional distribution of agriculture was historically constrained by crops’ inherent dependence on local environmental cues, particularly photoperiod and temperature. Natural domestication and artificial selection have progressively reduced this dependence on native ecosystems, resulting in a profound restructuring of global agricultural patterns. title: From There and Back Again: A Commentary on the Future of Animal Transfers in Zoos and Aquariums
abstract: Animal transfers among zoos and aquariums are essential for sustaining genetically diverse and demographically stable populations. However, they mark substantially disruptive events in an animal's life under human care. Current transfer practices-spanning population recommendations, health evaluation, transport, quarantine, and subsequent introduction-are shaped by decades of experience and now face growing impacts of climate change, regulatory complexity, and evolving welfare standards. title: Strategies for widening participation in the biomedical science at London South Bank University—a case study
abstract: Introduction and context Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic (BAME) professionals make essential contributions to UK healthcare, biomedical science research, academia, and the life sciences industry, yet remain underrepresented in senior roles. Three barriers recur: limited access to the discipline, a weak sense of belonging, and few visible role models. This study presents targeted strategies implemented within London South Bank University's Biomedical Science Programme (BMS) to address these barriers at key stages of students' career development journey. abstract: El repertorio dramático de Luis Vélez de Guevara nos ha llegado casi en su totalidad tras las correspondientes adaptaciones escénicas e impresas y sin control de la transmisión por parte del poeta. A través de métodos estilométricos ofrecemos propuestas de inclusión y exclusión de obras teatrales al corpus velecista. abstract: ABSTRACT Metal halide perovskite light‐emitting diodes (PeLEDs) show immense potential in next‐generation display technologies due to their exceptional optoelectronic properties. However, their operational stability and luminescence brightness remain core bottlenecks restricting their commercialization. To address this issue, this study reports an interference crystallization strategy that regulates crystal facet growth to reshape facet competition. title: Ornithonyssus bacoti (tropical rat mite): a critical review of biology, vector potential, and integrated management
abstract: The tropical rat mite, Ornithonyssus bacoti (Hirst, 1913), is an obligate hematophagous gamasid mite of global veterinary, animal, and public health importance. While traditionally recognized as a cause of rodent mite dermatitis in humans, its potential involvement in zoonotic pathogen transmission requires rigorous critical evaluation. title: Pathway-Guided and Patient-Centered Therapeutic Strategies in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease
abstract: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), encompassing coronary artery disease (CAD), cerebrovascular disease (ischemic stroke, IS; and transient ischemic attack, TIA), and peripheral artery disease (PAD) of atherosclerotic origin, remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide despite major advances in prevention and treatment. title: Computational optimization of diesel particulate filter geometry: coupled effects of cell density and filter diameter on filtration efficiency and back pressure
abstract: Diesel particulate filters (DPFs) are widely used in diesel exhaust after-treatment systems to reduce particulate emissions while maintaining acceptable exhaust back pressure. This study examines the coupled effects of filter diameter and channel density, expressed as cells per square inch (CPSI), on clean-filter DPF performance using computational fluid dynamics (CFD), response surface methodology (RSM), analysis of variance (ANOVA), and equal-weight multi-response desirability analysis. title: Classification-constrained retrieval of PM 2.5 vertical profiles from fluorescence-raman-mie polarization lidar
abstract: Abstract. The vertical distribution of PM2.5 during urban haze events is jointly affected by aerosol composition, boundary-layer structure, and regional transport. Empirical PM2.5 retrievals based on lidar-derived extinction coefficients can be biased by the optical contribution of coarse-mode mineral particles. title: Seed weight grading improves germination and seedling growth and vigour in Khasi Mandarin (Citrus reticulata Blanco)
abstract: Abstract Seed weight is a critical factor influencing germination, seedling establishment, and subsequent crop development. Khasi Mandarin exhibits considerable variation in seed weight, and limited information is available on the effect of seed weight on germination and seedling performance. This study assesses the effects of seed grades on seed germination, seedling growth and vigour in Khasi Mandarin. title: Universal features in atmospheric particulate matter dynamics
abstract: We study statistical properties of atmospheric particulate matter fluctuations using six years of daily PM2.5 concentration data from fifty-four Indian cities. Despite diverse urban settings and heterogeneous climatic conditions, we find that the fluctuations show strikingly universal behaviour in both the distributional properties and temporal dynamics. title: NeuPlume: generative inversion of atmospheric point-source emissions from sparse observations
abstract: Abstract. Inverting point-source emissions from sparse atmospheric observations is difficult because emission rate, release height, wind speed, turbulence, and plume morphology can compensate for one another. We present NeuPlume, a neural-physical probabilistic inversion framework that returns an ensemble of data-compatible plume fields rather than a single point estimate. title: Perspectives on tissue-selective insulin derivatives
abstract: Insulin is a central regulator of metabolic homoeostasis with diverse, tissue-specific actions across multiple organs. Despite major advances in insulin formulations, current therapies rely on systemic delivery and do not reproduce the physiological distribution of endogenous insulin, resulting in non-physiological tissue exposure and associated metabolic limitations. abstract: Global renewable-electricity capacity passed 5149 GW in 2025, with solar alone accounting for three-quarters of that year’s additions, yet renewable heat – which underpins solar-thermal collectors – still lags far behind electricity in the same transition. Closing that gap calls for solar-thermal receivers that do more than passively absorb radiation. title: Método de ordeña producción de leche y presencia de mastitis en vacas lecheras
abstract: La mastitis bovina es una enfermedad de gran relevancia en la industria lechera debido a su impacto en la salud animal, la calidad de la leche y las pérdidas económicas que genera. El presente estudio tuvo como objetivo analizar la relación entre el método de ordeño y la presencia de mastitis, así como su efecto sobre la producción de leche. Para ello, se evaluaron dos unidades de producción en Xochimilco: una con ordeño manual y otra con ordeño mecánico. abstract: Abstract Key message Alpine or mountainous forest genomics research is rapidly moving from classic population genetic studies toward exploring population environmental adaptation to address climate vulnerabilities. For alpine conifers in particular, future progress in sustainable management relies heavily on overcoming the current bottleneck in the availability of genomic and experimental resources through targeted, interdisciplinary research efforts. title: Intermittent hypoxia interventions for inducing ventilatory acclimatization to high altitude?
abstract: Accumulation of ∼200 h of hypoxia exposure (pre-acclimatization) has been suggested to prevent the development of acute mountain sickness when a person is subsequently exposed to high altitude. These pre-exposures are typically undertaken intermittently at or near the place of residence, primarily during sleep in hypoxic tents, and are likely to induce effective ventilatory acclimatization. title: Recent advances in hybrid treatment technologies for pharmaceutical removal from complex water matrices
abstract: The widespread occurrence of pharmaceuticals in aquatic environments poses significant environmental and health concerns, largely due to their persistence and the limited removal efficiency of conventional wastewater treatment systems. This review critically examines advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) and their hybrid configurations for the removal of pharmaceuticals from complex water matrices, including municipal, hospital, and pharmaceutical industry effluents. abstract: Urban bioaerosol releases pose increasing challenges to urban biosecurity resilience, yet their public health impacts remain insufficiently assessed. Here, we developed an integrated CFD–GIS–QMRA framework to simulate bioaerosol dispersion, quantify infection risk, and estimate associated health outcomes and healthcare demand. abstract: This paper presents the development of a three-dimensional model of a historic townhouse located at the Market Square (Rynek 11) in Przemyśl using data acquired by terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) and terrestrial and aerial photogrammetry. The study aimed to assess the usefulness of an integrated measurement approach for preparing detailed architectural documentation of a heritage building and to evaluate the quality of the final products, including the point cloud, mesh model, vector 3D model, and orthophotos. title: Dominant crack selection in multi-crack stress corrosion cracking of AISI 316L stainless steel under sustained loading in flowing HCl
abstract: Stress corrosion cracking (SCC) in structural components often involves the simultaneous development of multiple cracks; however, the mechanism by which a dominant crack emerges under sustained loading remains insufficiently resolved. This exploratory study investigates competitive multi-crack SCC behavior in AISI 316L stainless steel under sustained tensile loading in flowing 1 M HCl. Five naturally nucleated surface cracks formed around a central hole were monitored using repeated in situ optical imaging. abstract: Minas Artisanal Cheese (MAC) is among the most widely consumed and recognized artisanal cheeses in Brazil, produced from raw milk, rennet, salt, and a natural starter culture known locally as pingo. Pingo is an endogenous starter culture generated by backslopping, which carries into MAC cheese both technologically beneficial microorganisms and spoilage contaminants. abstract: Animal welfare assessment draws on evidence about both the animal’s observed state and the husbandry conditions in which it lives, but these sources of evidence are related rather than equivalent. Under limited-access conditions, combining them too early may obscure where welfare concern is located and may encourage unsupported interpretation of observed states as consequences of current husbandry. abstract: The ectoparasitic mite Varroa destructor is one of the main sanitary threats to Apis mellifera colonies worldwide, prompting the search for sustainable alternatives to synthetic acaricides. This study evaluated the effects of hydroethanolic extracts from Argemone mexicana and Ricinus communis on phoretic V. destructor infestation and mite fall under field conditions. abstract: Objectives Previous studies have indicated associations between the number of remaining teeth, oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL), and frailty. abstract: ABSTRACT Metal halide perovskite nanocrystals hold great promise for low‐cost optoelectronic and lasing applications, yet their integration into composite films is limited by poor stability under high excitation. We present a strategy to fabricate stable, ligand‐free perovskite nanocrystal‐based composites by combining lead‐based metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) with methylammonium acetate ionic liquid. abstract: High genetic variability in streptococci is driven by natural competence, specifically in Streptococcus pneumoniae and its close commensal species (Streptococcus pseudopneumoniae, Streptococcus oralis, and Streptococcus mitis), which drives rapid Streptococcal evolution. abstract: This study investigated follicular growth patterns, corpus luteum dynamics and endocrine profiles during natural and hormonally induced estrous cycles in Arunachali yak maintained at the ICAR–NRC on Yak, Nyukmadung, Arunachal Pradesh, India. Thirty-six apparently healthy, cyclic female yaks of second to fourth parity were equally assigned to natural estrus (Group I) or hormonally induced estrus using a modified Ovsynch protocol (Group II). abstract: El cambio climático reconfigura los ecosistemas, las economías y las trayectorias de vida, pero la investigación rara vez captura su carácter dinámico y procesual. Este artículo presenta una revisión conceptual y metodológica orientada a sintetizar y discutir el potencial del Análisis de Emparejamiento Óptimo (OMA por sus siglas en inglés: Optimal Matching Analysis) para el estudio de respuestas demográficas al cambio climático desde una perspectiva temporal. abstract: Australia’s endemic animals are poached from the wild to supply the global illegal wildlife trade. Wildlife forensic science is applied in Australian criminal investigations and has been documented in the scientific literature but lacks an evaluation on how forensic evidence is used in court. The aim of our study was to identify taxa and forensic evidence involved in cases and highlight where additional forensic evidence could have been valuable. title: Performance and uncertainty analysis of rural waste-to-energy systems under stochastic feedstock supply
abstract: This study evaluates the operational performance of three configurations of an Integrated Resource and Recovery Centre (IRRC) as a decentralised rural waste-to-energy (WtE) system using Monte Carlo simulation. Twelve months of empirical feedstock data were incorporated into a probabilistic, scenario-based model to assess how stochastic variations in the availability of vegetable waste and manure affect daily electricity generation. abstract: Abstract Light-driven self-propelled microrobots offer opportunities for active environmental remediation by enabling controllable interactions with dispersed pollutants in aqueous environments. Here, we report biohybrid microrobots, composed of enzyme-functionalized, Au-decorated cubic hematite, that reversibly switch between clustered and dispersed states to enhance microrobot-substrate interactions and photoenzymatic degradation. abstract: Situada em uma região de grande biodiversidade, a bacia hidrográfica do rio Teles Pires vem sofrendo sucessivas e intensas mudanças no uso e cobertura da terra, trazendo impactos ambientais provocadas pelas atividades econômicas da região. abstract: The development of multifunctional textile surfaces with enhanced ultraviolet (UV) protection, thermophysiological comfort, and thermal insulation is of considerable interest for protective clothing and wearable applications. This study systematically evaluates the effects of a bio-inspired polydopamine (PDA)-assisted SiO 2 coating on the thermophysiological comfort and UV-protective performance of PET fabrics, establishing the relationship between surface modification and multifunctional textile performance. abstract: Abstract In regions facing water scarcity, optimising existing treatment infrastructure is increasingly important. In the São Paulo Metropolitan Region, low per capita water availability and declining reservoir levels have increased reliance on the São Lourenço water treatment system. abstract: Brazilian extractive reserves constitute a model for the territorial governance of protected areas. With a focus on the territorial rights of traditional populations, they can serve as a catalyst for transformative change that reconciles the conservation of nature with the sustainable use of natural resources. abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Intercropping of legumes with cereals enhances resilience, resource efficiency, and nutritional quality in food systems, yet few studies have integrated yield stability with grain quantity and post‐harvest processability. abstract: Promover un envejecimiento saludable constituye una estrategia de prevención con impacto positivo tanto en la salud de los adultos mayores como en el sistema sanitario. abstract: The European weatherfish Misgurnus fossilis is a freshwater fish species specialised at inhabiting shallow, stagnant water bodies with dense vegetation. Owing to the widespread loss and degradation of such habitats through human-induced landscape alteration, the species has undergone a severe decline and is currently considered endangered across much of Europe. abstract: Armed conflict and economic instability can exacerbate socioeconomic inequalities in maternal and neonatal healthcare access and utilization. This study assessed the association between household income, healthcare costs, and maternal and neonatal healthcare utilization among women who had recently delivered and were reachable through functioning health facilities in Sudan. abstract: Experiences of loneliness and solitude are significant phenomena that are closely associated with individuals' psychological health and adaptation processes. The present study sought to adapt the Loneliness and Solitude Scale (LSS), which conceptualizes physical isolation through closely related yet functionally distinct dimensions, into Turkish and to examine its psychometric characteristics. abstract: Steel mill scale is an iron-oxide-rich by-product of hot rolling that is generated at roughly 1%–3% of the mass of steel processed and is still largely landfilled or downcycled. abstract: How did the United Nations, in their early years become an actor in the process of decolonization? This article shifts attention away from the diplomatic negotiations conventionally associated with international decolonization and toward the United Nations visiting missions, a largely overlooked instrument of the Trusteeship System entrusted with an epistemic mandate to investigate, inspect, and report on conditions in dependent territories. title: Uncovering Soil Health Responses to Short-Term Crop Rotation under Deficit Irrigation in Cold and Semi-Arid Agroecosystems
abstract: Crop rotation (CR) is a fundamental sustainable management practice, yet the temporal dynamics of soil recovery, particularly the synchronization between physical and chemical properties, remain poorly understood, especially in the fragile soil of semi-arid agroecosystems. abstract: Indoor Air Quality (IAQ) modelling in building simulations often relies on the nodal approach to evaluate exposure to airborne pollutants. abstract: Abstract. Sugarcane (Saccharum spp.), an economically important crop in the food and bioenergy industries, has historically played a central role in the economy of Cuba, shaping its agricultural landscape and international relations. abstract: Postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) is an important complication after surgery, particularly in patients with pre-existing metabolic and inflammatory vulnerability. Obesity may increase susceptibility to postoperative cognitive decline, but its independent association with POCD and the underlying mechanisms remain uncertain. abstract: This investigation primarily explores the pedagogical implications of integrating instructional artifacts manufactured via three-dimensional (3D) printing technologies within fifth-grade social studies education, specifically monitoring shifts in student motivation, subject-directed attitudes, and academic outcomes. Using a quasi-experimental approach, the study employed pre-test and post-test non-equivalent control group design. abstract: Abstract Scholarly blogs are an important venue for scholarly communication; however, they are not yet integrated into the preservation workflows of digital research and information infrastructures, which places their long‐term access at risk. abstract: Abstract Real-time Precise Point Positioning (PPP) with Ambiguity Resolution (PPP-AR) is an increasingly important Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) technique for high-precision positioning, navigation, and other time-critical applications. Its performance depends strongly on the availability and accuracy of real-time satellite orbit and clock products. title: Circuit-constrained molecular neuroethology in the medicinal leech Hirudo verbana
abstract: Medicinal leeches have long served as classic systems in comparative neuroethology because individual neurons can be identified across animals and linked to well-defined behaviors. This review argues that Hirudo verbana is now positioned for a new phase in which this identified-cell framework can be connected directly to molecular mechanisms. title: Analysis of the spatiotemporal evolution, convergence trends, and influencing factors of ecological efficiency in Chinese cities
abstract: Understanding the spatiotemporal evolution, convergence trends, and influencing factors of ecological efficiency in Chinese cities is crucial for achieving coordinated development between socioeconomic progress and the ecological environment. This paper assesses the ecological efficiency level of 279 prefecture-level cities in China by adopting the super-efficient EBM model. title: Settler-colonial entanglements: Using Par/Des(i) to understand Black and Racialized international student experiences in Canada
abstract: This scholarly paper discusses the complex positioning of Black and Racialized international students (BRIS) in Canada, both as marginalized bodies and complicit in perpetuating settler colonialism. It delves into the paradoxical role these students play within the framework of Canadian higher education, which is deeply entwined with the country's colonial history and contemporary policy shifts aimed at managing the influx of international students. abstract: Introduction Determining whether urban energy demand has entered a persistent post-peak phase is important for assessing China’s energy transition. A historical maximum alone, however, does not establish a durable turning point because energy consumption may subsequently rebound or remain close to its previous peak. title: The Scaleup Costs, Size, and Statistics Challenge to Democratic Deliberation on Health Policy
abstract: Current fashion supports aligning health policy with the recommendations of deliberative forums, or mini-publics. These forums' participants are selected randomly from the general public (sometimes with overrepresentation of direct stakeholders or of underrepresented sectors). After being informed and exchanging public reasons with fellow participants under discursive rules that engage all as equals, participants vote on and sometimes rank policy recommendations. title: Organisational and economic conditions for implementing unmanned aerial systems in the production processes of agricultural enterprises
abstract: The article substantiated the organisational-economic conditions and engineering prerequisites for implementing agricultural drones in the production processes of agricultural enterprises of Poltava region. The aim of the research was to determine the minimum land area at which purchasing or contracting drone services becomes economically viable, and to establish the technical parameters of spray application quality and the priority operations for unmanned aerial equipment. journal: UKRAINIAN BLACK SEA REGION AGRARIAN SCIENCE

title: Is physical climate risk priced in India’s financial sector? A monthly index approach, 2014–2024
abstract: Floods, cyclones and heatwaves are no longer viewed as humanitarian crises; they also have significant financial implications by affecting borrowers’ ability to repay loans, increasing potential liabilities of insurers and influencing how investors assess and price financial risks. Whether financial markets actually respond to this physical climate risk remains an open question, particularly in emerging economies like India, where climate exposure is high but market-based evidence is scarce. title: Integrating cortical microtubules into plant gravity signaling: dynamics, tubulin phosphorylation, and growth regulation
abstract: Plant gravity responses depend on coordinated signaling and growth-control mechanisms that convert directional and mechanical stimuli into differential cell expansion. Cortical microtubules are central to the conversion: they pattern cellulose synthase trajectories, set cell-wall anisotropy, and are remodeled in altered-gravity and tubulin-mutant systems. Yet the cytoskeletal regulatory pathway remains only loosely connected to the canonical, auxin-centered picture of how plants perceive and respond to gravity. title: Del residuo agroindustrial al biochar diseñado: composición, estructura molecular y aplicaciones de alto valor agregado
abstract: En este artículo se examina cómo la composición de la biomasa agroindustrial y las condiciones de pirólisis determinan la estructura molecular y el desempeño funcional del biochar desde una perspectiva de ingeniería de materiales. En el contexto colombiano y latinoamericano, la valorización descentralizada de residuos agrícolas y forestales (cascarilla de arroz, bagazo de caña, podas urbanas, residuos de palma y pulpa de café) representa una vía estratégica para la transición energética y la economía circular, en línea con los objetivos de desarrollo sostenible y el enfoque One Health. title: The Good Daughter?
abstract: Abstract We study the impact of Federal alcohol Prohibition in 1919 on workers in the alcohol industry and their families, using newly linked census records following spouses, sons, and daughters 1910-1940. Through 1930, affected men were less likely to work and worked in lower-skilled jobs when employed. By 1940, they were more likely to be employed, suggesting delayed retirement. title: Fire return intervals are very short at Niassa Special Reserve, Mozambique, especially in dry miombo woodlands—a survival analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Fire shapes savanna and woodland landscapes, but the temporal spacing of recurrent fires remains poorly quantified in African miombo ecosystems. Understanding how fire-return intervals vary across vegetation and landscape settings is important for interpreting fire-regime heterogeneity, vegetation recovery, and fire-management needs. We assessed Fire-return intervals across the Niassa Special Reserve, Mozambique, and evaluated whether fire recurrence differed among major vegetation types. title: Organ-dependent phytochemical and pharmacological specialization in the endemic Adenocarpus decorticans Boiss.
abstract: Introduction Adenocarpus decorticans Boiss. is a western Mediterranean shrub restricted to Morocco and Spain, whose phytochemistry and pharmacology remain unexplored despite ethnomedicinal records reported for other species of the genus. This study reports the first organ-resolved characterisation of the species. abstract: This descriptive-correlational study examined the relationship between teacher–pupils’ interaction and the academic performance of Grade VI pupils in Edukasyon sa Pagpapakatao (EsP) at Bislig City SPED Center during School Year 2025–2026. The study involved 63 Grade VI pupils selected through complete enumeration. Teacher–pupils’ interaction was assessed in terms of emotional support, classroom management, and instructional support using the adapted Classroom Assessment Scoring System–Student Report (CLASS-SR), while academic performance was measured through official quarterly grades. title: Repeatability in venom expenditure during defensive bites in rattlesnakes: use of a chemical weapon deployed to generate an extended phenotype
abstract: Animal personality is characterized by consistent among-individual differences in behavior across time and contexts and can influence a wide range of ecological and evolutionary processes. Although consistent behavioral differences have been linked to variation in behaviors that create or modify extended phenotypes, their role in shaping the deployment of chemical effectors that induce phenotypic changes in other organisms remains largely unexplored. title: Precision-weighted mixed models identify high-yielding and temporally stable cowpea germplasm across three growing seasons
abstract: Introduction Cowpea is an important multipurpose legume that contributes to food and nutritional security, particularly in regions affected by environmental stress. Identifying high-yielding and stable germplasm is essential for improving breeding efficiency and developing resilient cultivars. However, distinguishing persistent genetic merit from seasonal environmental noise remains challenging when trial precision varies among years. title: Performance of smooth cayenne pineapple under tropical conditions: unravelling effects of postharvest duration and ripening stage
abstract: Introduction Optimizing harvest maturity and postharvest handling is important for maintaining pineapple quality and reducing losses under tropical storage conditions. However, limited information is available on how ripening stage at harvest interacts with postharvest storage duration to influence physical and quality characteristics of Smooth Cayenne pineapple under ambient conditions in Fiji. title: Biomass conversion in thermo‐catalytic reforming reactor: process modeling and kinetic insights for integrated intermediate pyrolysis
abstract: Abstract A sustainable energy transition in the 21st century necessitates efficient biomass‐to‐energy conversion technologies, with pyrolysis playing a crucial role. Thermo‐catalytic reforming (TCR) combines intermediate pyrolysis with a catalytic post‐reforming stage, producing higher‐quality bio‐oil, char, and syngas than conventional pyrolysis. title: Merging molecular dynamics with homogenisation: a novel strategy for the modelling of nano-filtration phenomena
abstract: Filtration flows through nanoporous membranes play a crucial role in a range of cutting-edge technologies, including water purification, osmotic power generation and targeted drug delivery. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are currently considered the state-of-the-art approach for modelling nano-filtration processes. title: Transformación digital en pymes industriales: un análisis empírico para el Partido de General Pueyrredon
abstract: Este trabajo constituye un aporte al estudio de la Transformación Digital (TD) en pequeñas y medianas empresas de economías menos desarrolladas, al analizar la TD en empresas industriales del Partido de General Pueyrredon (PGP), uno de los principales entramados productivos de Argentina. title: Regular fiscal and accounting supervision and firms’ cost of equity capital: evidence from a quasi-natural experiment using the pilot reform to strengthen fiscal and accounting supervision
abstract: Fiscal and accounting supervision has become an integral part of China’s Party and state supervisory system. Using Chinese A-share listed firms from 2017 to 2022, this study exploits the Ministry of Finance’s 2020 pilot reform to strengthen fiscal and accounting supervision as a quasi-natural experiment to examine its impact on firms’ cost of equity capital. title: Erasing the invisible: targeting persister cells to cure minimal residual disease
abstract: Abstract Despite revolutionary advances in immunotherapy and targeted therapies, tumor recurrence driven by minimal residual disease (MRD) and drug-tolerant persister (DTP) cells remains a critical challenge in oncology. MRD, a reservoir of residual cancer cells undetectable by conventional imaging but identifiable via sensitive molecular techniques like next-generation sequencing and ctDNA analysis, serves as a prognostic biomarker for relapse across hematologic and solid malignancies. title: Functional nanocomposite PVA hydrogels for tissue engineering: Mechanisms and applications
abstract: Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) hydrogels have attracted extensive interest in tissue engineering due to their excellent biocompatibility, hydrophilicity, and tunable physicochemical properties. However, pristine PVA hydrogels often suffer from limited mechanical strength, biological activity, and functional performance, restricting their application in complex tissue regeneration. title: Retos de la evaluación del aprendizaje en la educa-ción superior: hacia una evaluación formativa y transparente.
abstract: La evaluación del aprendizaje en educación superior enfrenta una tensión estructural entre modelos tradicionales centrados en la certificación y las demandas contemporáneas de una formación orientada al desarrollo de competencias. La masificación de las aulas, la irrupción de la inteligencia artificial y la persistente subjetividad en la calificación configuran un escenario que exige repensar los dispositivos evaluativos. title: Digital solidarity as a process: Developing the Digital Solidarity Escalation Model (DSEM) through a netnographic study of disaster response
abstract: This study investigates the development of digital solidarity within disaster-related online communities by conducting a netnographic analysis of the 2025 Aceh–Sumatra flood response campaign on Ferry Irwandi's YouTube channel. Although previous research has investigated the interconnections between mobilization, collective identification, trust, accountability, and sustained civic engagement during disaster response, it has given less attention to the topics of crowdfunding, trust, and digital donations. title: From Avocado Seed Waste to Green Synthesis Laser-Induced Graphene: A Rapid, Direct, Low Cost and Flame-Retardant-Free Route
abstract: Abstract Laser-induced graphene (LIG) has emerged as a versatile method for producing porous, conductive graphitic structures from carbon-rich precursors. In this work, an unconventional and sustainable precursor—Fuerte avocado seed (Persea americana Mill) waste—was explored for the green synthesis of LIG via CO₂ laser engraving. title: AccES: A Framework for Predicting Building‐Level Loss of Accessibility to Essential Services Post‐Disasters Based on Publicly Available Information
abstract: Natural hazards significantly disrupt access to essential services, affecting individuals' capacity to withstand and recover from such events. However, existing hazard resilience models often fail to account for the interdependencies among essential services and lack the spatial resolution needed to assess accessibility loss at the building level. abstract: Groundwater decline in irrigated semi-arid alluvial plains reflects interacting land-surface, climatic, pumping, and hydrogeological controls. This study evaluates spatial associations among urbanization, Curve Number-based event-runoff potential, regional climate variability, and groundwater-depth change in Multan, Pakistan. title: THE CONCEPT OF ‘BÖRİK’ (BÖRK) IN KAZAKH: AN ETYMOLOGICAL, LEXICAL AND CULTURAL STUDY
abstract: The concept of börik (börk) in Kazakh possesses a deeply rooted history in terms of its etymological, lexicological, dialectological, and cultural dimensions. Preserved continuously from Old Turkic to modern Turkic dialects, this term initially referred merely to a type of headgear; however, over time it underwent a semantic expansion and acquired powerful symbolic meanings associated with identity, status, protection, and social belonging. title: Performative Sovereignty Versus Performative Nationalism: Hydraulic Securitization and Abeyance of the Indus Waters Treaty
abstract: ABSTRACT Indus Waters Treaty (IWT, 1960) survived four major wars, decades of cross‐border militancy, and 56 years of parliamentary skepticism in India. However, it could not survive the performative securitization sequence initiated by three terror attacks, that is, Uri (2016), Pulwama (2019), and Pahalgam (2025), leading to IWT's abeyance in 2025. title: Analyzing Bunyaviruses from a One Health Perspective
abstract: Zoonotic viral diseases continue to pose major challenges to global health, particularly as environmental, social and economic changes increasingly influence interactions among humans, animals, vectors, and ecosystems. This review explores Rift Valley fever virus (RVFV), Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), and hantaviruses (HTVs) within the framework of One Health, emphasizing the ecological and epidemiological factors that govern their emergence and transmission. title: Age discrimination in public transportation: The case of the Ekşi Sözlük platform
abstract: This study examines how age discrimination toward the free-transit rights of individuals aged 65 and older is reproduced through the discussions on the Ekşi Sözlük platform. abstract: Introduction Late sowing constrains grain yield formation in wheat by shortening the duration of post-anthesis assimilate accumulation and limiting the effective utilization of source-derived assimilates during grain filling. abstract: Background Visual Snow Syndrome (VSS) is neurological condition typified by persistent visual snow, or static, throughout the visual field, alongside additional phenomena that impact night vision, visual perception, and visual processing. Only formally characterized in the 2010s, little consideration has been given to the broader impacts of this condition on the lives of those who experience it. title: Reconceptualizing sports tourism destination competitiveness through the knowledge-based view: evidence from Iran
abstract: Sports tourism destination competitiveness has been theorized predominantly through static, asset-based frameworks that privilege physical infrastructure and promotional capacity, yet these accounts offer limited purchase in knowledge-intensive, innovation-driven tourism systems. This study advances a dynamic alternative, drawing on the Knowledge-Based View to reconceptualize competitiveness as an ecosystem-level process rooted in the collective mobilization and transformation of knowledge. abstract: Musculoskeletal injuries and degenerative disorders caused by trauma, aging, chronic inflammation, and metabolic dysfunction frequently result in impaired functional recovery, including skeletal muscle atrophy, bone loss, cartilage degeneration, and neuromuscular dysfunction. abstract: The escalating occurrence of extreme high temperature weather exposes individuals to passive heat stress more frequently, resulting in strain on the vascular system. One example of this strain is the doubling of cardiac output during heat stress, achieved through an increase in heart rate and the redirection of blood flow from non-cutaneous tissues. abstract: Foreign influencers are playing a growing role in China's live-streaming commerce industry. Yet, little is known about how consumers respond to foreign influencers’ ability to communicate and adjust across cultures. To address this gap, the present study draws on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and distinguishes between two consumer perceptions: Intercultural Communication Competency (ICC) and Intercultural Adaptability (ICA). title: Microfungi associated with Azadirachta (Meliaceae, Sapindales): New species, new records, and a global checklist
abstract: Azadirachta (Meliaceae) is a small genus comprising economically and ecologically important plants, including A. indica , which is widely used in traditional medicine and other applications such as natural pest control and cosmetics. Several studies have previously been conducted on Azadirachta , including its phytochemistry and associated microfungi, particularly endophytic species inhabiting the A. indica host. abstract: Vector-borne and vector-associated bacterial zoonoses represent an important component of infectious disease epidemiology in Tunisia. This review synthesizes available evidence on major bacterial groups, including Rickettsia , Bartonella , Anaplasma , Ehrlichia , Borrelia , Coxiella burnetii , and other arthropod-associated bacteria, using a One Health framework integrating human, animal, vector, wildlife, and environmental compartments. abstract: The South American coati (Nasua nasua) is a mammal of the order Carnivora and family Procyonidae, characterized by scansorial locomotion. Accordingly, several anatomical and functional studies examined its thoracic limbs. Nevertheless, the anatomical descriptions and terminology differ among those studies, and none considered the evolutionary derivations of the brachium and antebrachium muscles based on topology, innervation and anatomical variants. title: La Reinvención del Aprendizaje: Claves del Conectivismo para la Educación Digital
abstract: En las instituciones educativas actuales persiste una confusión conceptual. Se asume que el manejo de dispositivos tecnológicos equivale al aprendizaje mediado por su uso. Esta premisa alimenta un enfoque instrumental que convierte la innovación en una continuidad de prácticas educativas similares a las de la década de los noventa, pero con dispositivos digitales. title: High-density SNP mapping reveals genomic hotspots for photosynthetic traits under Huanglongbing disease in citrus
abstract: Huanglongbing (HLB) is a major constraint to citrus production, but the genetic basis of physiological responses to Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus ( C Las) infection remains poorly understood. title: Chinese herbal medicine for ulcerative colitis: product-level clinical evidence, mechanistic appraisal, and a roadmap to precision translation
abstract: Chinese herbal medicine (CHM) is widely used for ulcerative colitis (UC), but product heterogeneity, variable trial quality, and limited long-term safety data preclude class-level efficacy claims. This critical narrative review therefore evaluates evidence at the level of the defined botanical drug product, formulation, route, dose, and manufacturing process. title: Learning from degrowth: strengthening circular economy approaches through case studies of plastic packaging and textiles
abstract: To date, the circular economy (CE) and degrowth literatures have had a substantially separate existence. Whilst a CE is increasingly regarded as a central element of sustainable development, its meaning is far from uniform, with diverse interpretations in both literature and practice. This heterogenous discourse mirrors the tension between green growth, degrowth and post-growth approaches in the wider sustainability debate. title: Development of a family functioning measure for Hispanic lesbian, gay, and bisexual adolescents
abstract: Introduction Hispanic lesbian, gay, and bisexual (LGB) adolescents experience elevated risks for HIV-related risk behaviors, drug use, and mental-health problems. These problems may be impacted by various family functioning behaviors (e.g., communication, parental involvement). However, existing family functioning measures may not adequately capture the culturally shaped, identity-specific family processes relevant to this population. abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the key determinants of humanitarian logistics effectiveness in Malaysia’s flood disaster management and develop the good humanitarian logistics practices model (GHLPM) as an integrated framework to enhance coordination, quality assurance and operational readiness. title: Spatiotemporal patterns and driving mechanisms of cultivated land multifunctionality evolution: evidence from county-level data in Sichuan Province, China
abstract: The pursuit of socioeconomic development, food security, and ecological sustainability has driven the multifunctional evolution of cultivated land. Under the constraint of limited cultivated land resources, achieving synergy among the economic, food security, and ecological functions of cultivated land has become a major challenge for agricultural modernization in Sichuan Province. title: PP2A targeting: balancing anticancer potential and neurological risk
abstract: Protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) is a multifunctional serine/threonine phosphatase that regulates cell-cycle progression, oncogenic signaling, neuronal development, synaptic homeostasis, and protein proteostasis. abstract: Asplenium nidus is an epiphytic fern recognized as an ecological bioindicator associated with the nesting habitat of the lesser bird-of-paradise (Paradisaea minor jobiensis Rothschild, 1897). This study analyzed population dynamics of A. nidus between 2018 and 2024 and examined its relationship with host tree species as an indicator of forest ecosystem health in the Imbowiari Barawai Forest, Yapen Island, Papua, Indonesia. title: Climate Change and Dispersal Limitation Reshape Future Habitat Accessibility for Lady Amherst's Pheasant ( Chrysolophus amherstiae ) in China
abstract: ABSTRACT Montane forest birds are highly vulnerable to climate warming because their habitats are often fragmented, topographically constrained, and difficult to track through dispersal. For Lady Amherst's Pheasant ( Chrysolophus amherstiae ), future climate risks remain poorly understood, especially the mismatch between habitat suitability and habitat accessibility. title: Obstáculos a la contratación pública estratégica en España: análisis factorial comparado entre sector público y sector privado
abstract: Este estudio analiza los determinantes internos y externos que condicionan la aplicación estratégica de la Directiva 2014/24/UE en España, comparando las percepciones del sector público y el privado. Objetivos: identificar las dimensiones latentes que influyen en la capacidad de ambos sectores para incorporar principios estratégicos en los procesos de contratación pública. Metodología: combina un panel Delphi con expertos y una encuesta evaluada mediante estadística descriptiva y análisis factorial exploratorio. title: The role of Urban topography when simulating mudflows: a case study of Quito, Ecuador
abstract: Abstract Urban areas are increasingly exposed to mudflow hazards as unplanned urban expansion intersects with steep drainage basins and extreme rainfall events intensify under climate change. Physics-based models offer powerful tools for hazard assessment, yet their performance in densely built environments remains insufficiently explored. abstract: The sudden shift to new normal education changed the work of elementary teachers in Cotabato City, but local evidence on their lived experiences, challenges, and ways of coping remained limited. This study explored the experiences, challenges, and coping mechanisms of elementary school teachers in the Cotabato City Division during School Year 2020–2021. abstract: Abstract Non-invasive recordings using brain electrophysiology provide credible insights into decline in neuronal functioning with age. New approaches are required to translate these results into compelling clinical metrics and meet the global challenge of preserving brain health in ageing. Changes in neuronal dynamics with ageing are observable in the power spectra of EEG and MEG recordings. Highly promising candidates for electrophysiological markers have been identified, but progress is hindered by substantial methodological variability across studies. title: Phthalates: the interplay between diet, obesity, diabetes, and gut microbiota
abstract: Millions of tons of plastic are produced worldwide each year. Currently, it is almost impossible to avoid plastic and exposure to its effects. There are many chemical compounds that are used in its production. Some of them, classified as plasticizers, are phthalates, which are found in food packaging, toys, and many cosmetics. They give plastics durability, flexibility, and heat resistance. abstract: Integrating seismological, gravimetric, and geodetic observations provides a complementary framework for investigating spatiotemporal relationships among seismic activity, mass redistribution, and surface deformation in active fault systems. This study investigated these associations in the Algeciras Fault System (AFS) by integrating seismic records, monthly gravimetric observations from the Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) and GRACE Follow-On (GRACE-FO) missions corrected for hydrological effects using the Global Land Data Assimilation System (GLDAS), and surface deformation ob

title: Climate policies and adaptive capacities: a cross-analysis of sectoral, intersectoral, and international actions
abstract: Against intensifying climate risks, this study compares the associations of sectoral, cross-sectoral, and international climate policies with annual changes in adaptation readiness. Using an unbalanced panel of 59 countries from 2002 to 2022, it estimates OLS and SUR models with policy–income interactions and assesses robustness through Mundlak and dynamic GMM specifications. title: Frontline perceptions of middle management as a bottleneck in cybersecurity escalation and risk communication
abstract: Purpose This study examines how frontline cybersecurity professionals perceive middle management's role in the escalation and communication of cyber risk within large organizations, and identifies the communication failures they associate with delayed or incomplete reporting of critical security issues to senior leadership. title: A numerical forecast for birch and grasses pollen concentration in Germany
abstract: Prevention of pollen exposure is a way to assist allergic individuals to better cope with their disease. To enable this prevention, a prediction of next day(s) pollen flight is needed. The most accurate predictions are from numerical models which calculate the expected airborne pollen concentrations using simulation of emission combined with atmospheric dispersal processes (as in the SILAM model). title: Regimes of truth in postmodern novels: the atlas of misty continents in the context of modernity and Ottoman epistemology
abstract: This study aims to analyze the epistemological transformation concerning the nature and legitimacy of knowledge in the context of modernity and postmodernity through İhsan Oktay Anar’s The Atlas of Misty Continents. While modernity conceptualizes knowledge as a universal structure grounded in reason and empirical verification, postmodern thought challenges these assumptions by arguing that knowledge is produced within historical, cultural, and discursive processes. title: Placental immunopathology and congenital transmission of Zika virus and Trypanosoma cruzi: comparative mechanisms, immune disturbances, and potential co-infection scenarios
abstract: Congenital transmission of Zika virus (ZIKV) and Trypanosoma cruzi ( T. cruzi ) remains a major public health concern in the Americas. Both pathogens cross the placental barrier and cause severe neonatal outcomes, yet no confirmed congenital co-infections have been reported, and their combined effects on maternal–fetal health are unknown. Critical gaps persist regarding placental immunopathology, fetal immune programming, and long-term consequences of prenatal exposure. abstract: The periocular region shows early visible ageing because thin skin, repetitive orbicularis oculi activity, retaining ligaments, orbital fat, and the bony framework change together. Clinical manifestations include rhytids, dermatochalasis, eyelid laxity, tear trough deformity, edema, and dark circles, with potential cosmetic, ocular-surface, and functional consequences. title: Targeting post-translational modifications to overcome glioblastoma therapy resistance: emerging strategies and natural compounds
abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) regulate multiple mechanisms associated with glioblastoma (GBM) therapy resistance, which remains a major challenge in GBM treatment. Some resistance mechanisms involve genetic heterogeneity, glioblastoma stem cells, the tumor microenvironment, autophagy, metabolic reprogramming, vascular adaptation, and altered transcriptional regulation. By regulating protein activity, stability, localization, interactions, and signaling, PTMs can influence several of these processes and affect treatment response. title: From measurement to mitigation: a historical review of livestock emission research in the U.S. Southern and Central Great Plains
abstract: As airborne emissions from agricultural operations began to receive more concentrated scrutiny, the federal Task Force on Agricultural Air Quality was established in the 1996 Farm Bill and began operations in 1997 to advance research and provide solutions for sustainable agricultural operations with primary focus on particulate matter, ozone, and odors. abstract: Los convertidores DC-DC tipo Buck-Boost desempeñan un papel fundamental en los sistemas electrónicos de potencia modernos, ya que permiten la conversión tanto reductora como elevadora de tensión en un amplio rango de niveles de potencia, desde aplicaciones de baja tensión hasta sistemas industriales de escala megavatio. title: Wind energy in european balancing markets: policy challenges, market design, and a multi-criteria feasibility index
abstract: The transformation of the European electricity market under the Clean Energy Package (CEP) has positioned wind power as a cornerstone of the EU’s renewable energy transition. Balancing markets have consequently become strategically important, requiring wind power to assume a more active and technically capable role. Despite ongoing reforms, technical, regulatory, and economic barriers still affect its effective participation. abstract: ABSTRACT Anomalous luminescence in phosphors highly doped with transition‐metal ions (e.g., , ) has attracted significant interest for multifunctional optical materials and devices. However, rational optimization and materials design have been hindered by controversial mechanisms. Here, we establish a unified analytical framework for deciphering such complex emissions across a diverse range of host systems. title: ESG performance, board gender diversity and corporate financial performance: the role of countries’ cultural orientation in European companies
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to investigate the relationship between environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance and corporate financial performance (CFP), focusing on the moderating role of board gender diversity and the influence of national cultural orientation. Design/methodology/approach This study performs a fixed effects linear regression analysis with time effects on a panel data set of 889 European listed companies (5,004 firm-year observations) across 17 industries and 22 countries over the period 2016–2023. title: MRI-PHYSIOL-NIRS: an integrated platform to study kidney oxygenation
abstract: Abstract The kidney always operates close to hypoxia, a pathological condition of O 2 -shortage, due to its unique relationship between blood flow and oxygen demand. Renal hypoxia is central to kidney diseases, where progressive loss of renal function ultimately can no longer sustain life. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can assess renal oxygenation non-invasively in vivo via the relaxation times T 2 * and T 2 , which reflect deoxygenated hemoglobin, but are influenced by several physiological confounders. title: Fair Access to Urban Water: Designing Population‐Sensitive Connection Fees Through a Welfare‐Informed Ability‐to‐Pay Approach
abstract: ABSTRACT Setting urban water connection fees is a complex policy problem: Fees must balance affordability, equity, and adequate cost recovery. This study develops a two‐stage framework for setting urban water connection charges in Iran. A bottom‐up engineering model first establishes the full long‐run economic cost of a new connection; a distributive stage then allocates a target provincial average across six city population classes. title: GIS-based multi-criteria spatial decision support for equitable public toilet planning: mapping accessibility deficits, site suitability and priority intervention zones in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Rapid urbanization frequently outpaces sanitation infrastructure, leaving vulnerable residents without essential services. This study develops and applies a GIS-based spatial decision-support framework combining multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA), the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP), and network-based accessibility analysis to assess location suitability and prioritize public toilet development in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. title: Teachers’ Professional Development And Its Relationship With The Implementation Of Development Education Programs In Lapu-Lapu City Schools
abstract: Public schools provide continued professional development, but there are still gaps between policy goals and classroom practice. This study determined the implementation of Development Education programs along objectives and content integration, teaching strategies, instructional materials and monitoring evaluation and mechanisms in selected public schools in Lapu-Lapu City. The study used a mixed-methods approach, obtaining quantitative survey data and qualitative interview data. title: Coherence, transformation, and breakdown in living systems: part II — predictions and implications for systemic health
abstract: Part I of this two-part series advanced the CHORA Hypothesis as a candidate account of biological coherence: how organised biological function is sustained, transformed, and lost within the organism and across the lineage over deep time. The hypothesis holds that a Common Higher-Order Regulatory Architecture (CHORA) operates as an integrated, hierarchically structured level of organisation across cells, tissues, organisms, and generations, sustaining within-organism coherence and evolutionary coherence alike. title: Digitalization and Environmental, Social, and Governance Reporting: Evidence from the US Banking Industry
abstract: ABSTRACT We examine the relation between digitalization and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) reporting using a sample of listed US banks from 2010 to 2022. Our study is based on a two‐step theoretical framework, building on voluntary disclosure and signaling theory: First, we expect and find technological progress to enhance internal information quality. Second, we examine whether banks pass on this improved information to stakeholders via ESG reports. title: Hospital and health-center bed expansion and persistent relative mismatch across geometry-stable non-district Chinese counties, 2015–2023
abstract: Introduction Territorial health equity depends not only on expanding health resources but also on aligning local capacity with territorial planning contexts. We examined whether changes in hospital and health-center bed allocation were associated more strongly with territorial planning context or local fiscal-economic capacity. Methods We analyzed a 2015-2023 panel of 1,787 geometry-stable non-district counties in China. title: Tree selection, courtyard form, and outdoor microclimatic comfort in hot-arid educational spaces: a multi-criteria decision framework
abstract: Outdoor spaces in hot-arid environments are frequently exposed to severe thermal stress, limiting their thermal usability and comfort. Urban vegetation can provide an important passive strategy for improving outdoor microclimatic conditions; however, its performance depends on the characteristics of the vegetation and the surrounding spatial context, including courtyard orientation. title: Circular Transformation in the Silk Sector: A Fuzzy Delphi–DEMATEL Analysis of Critical Factors
abstract: ABSTRACT The circular transformation in the silk industry is crucial for enhancing resource efficiency and minimizing waste. Despite growing interest in circularity within the textile sector, the silk industry remains underexplored. This study addresses this gap by systematically assessing the barriers and enablers influencing circular economy adoption in silk. A two‐stage methodology was applied. title: Reasons for encounter and recommended interventions in an interprofessional integrative oncology counseling program in outpatient care: a mixed-methods analysis of 1,693 consultation letters
abstract: Introduction Complementary and integrative healthcare (CIH) approaches play an increasingly important role in oncology care, involving a wide range of healthcare professionals and therapeutic methods. While patient demand for CIH and the evidence base for individual interventions have grown considerably, the implementation of structured counseling services for the effective and safe use of CIH remains limited. title: The Dynamics of the Racial Wealth Gap
abstract: ABSTRACT We study the dynamics of the racial wealth gap (the wealth of Black households relative to white ones) using a dynamic equilibrium model of overlapping generations. We match the model to the cross‐sectional distributions of wealth and earnings by race. We find that equalizing earnings is critical for permanent reductions in racial wealth inequality, and that one‐time transfers will have only transitory effects unless earnings are also equalized. title: Biofortified feed crops: bridging plant biotechnology and animal-derived functional foods
abstract: Micronutrient deficiency continues to be a significant global nutritional problem, especially in populations relying on staple diets with limited micronutrient diversity. Biofortification presents a sustainable way to enhance crop nutritional quality through methods like agronomic practices, traditional breeding, microbial interventions, nanotechnology, transgenic techniques, and genome editing. This review critically explores these strategies, focusing on their application to feed and forage crops, which are often neglected in biofortification discussions. title: Supply Chain Management and Business Performance of Agri-Farm Businesses in the Province of Rizal
abstract: Agricultural enterprises in the Province of Rizal face persistent supply chain challenges, including fragmented supplier networks, inadequate post-harvest infrastructure, and limited coordination across production and distribution stages. This study assessed supply chain management (SCM) practices and their relationship with the non-financial business performance of agri-farm businesses in Rizal. abstract: Chronic musculoskeletal disease in Canis lupus familiaris (dogs) is associated not only with biomechanical dysfunction but also with alterations in autonomic regulation, affective processing, movement behavior, and chronic pain adaptation. Current rehabilitation models primarily emphasize peripheral tissue healing and biomechanics while placing less emphasis on interactions among interoception, nociception, autonomic regulation, and affective-motor processing. title: Playing together, living together: Community-based music learning as a catalyst for rural wellbeing
abstract: This article explores how participatory instrumental music tuition can strengthen wellbeing, confidence, and social cohesion for adults living in rural Scotland. Focusing on the town of Millport, Isle of Cumbrae, the study was conducted as part of the Community Instrumental Music Service for Rural Scotland (CIMSRS), an initiative designed to address barriers to adult music learning caused by isolation, limited provision, and economic constraints. title: The immune phenotype of circulating tumor cells: from escape mechanisms to immunotherapy navigation
abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) must survive immune attack in the bloodstream before they can contribute to distant metastasis. Their immune phenotype, including checkpoint ligands, antigen-presentation molecules, and immunomodulatory features, can be assessed through serial blood sampling and may provide information complementary to established immunotherapy biomarkers. title: Faker Island: Profiling misinformation sharers on the French Twittersphere
abstract: What are the distinctive characteristics of misinformation sharers? So far, most studies have focused on the U.S., a two-party system with a highly polarized media landscape, leaving open the question of what misinformation sharers look like in other socio-political contexts. Research has also prioritized testing causal links between cognitive or political variables and misinformation sharing, while paying less attention to fine-grained descriptions of who these users are. abstract: Gastric cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. The Correa cascade, progressing from chronic gastritis through precancerous lesions to adenocarcinoma, provides the framework for understanding gastric mucosal stepwise malignant transformation. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulas, such as Zuojin Pills and Wuji Pills, have been historically used to treat gastric disorders including epigastric pain and acid regurgitation, yet their mechanisms of action in blocking the inflammation-to-carcinoma transition remain incompletely understood. title: Identifying Arctic states vulnerable to rapid ice loss with a convolutional neural network
abstract: This work investigates the incidence of rapid ice-loss events in the Arctic, in which a substantial fraction of September sea-ice is lost in only a few years. Such events are seen to occur in climate model simulations forced with increasing greenhouse gas concentrations, but not as yet in the relatively short observational record. We train a convolutional neural network (CNN) using six large climate model ensembles to diagnose vulnerability to rapid ice-loss events. abstract: In this study, an artificial intelligence-assisted evaluation of the refractive indices of different materials is performed. The evaluation of the refractive index is necessary to design photonic devices for various classical and quantum photonic applications, and to theoretically analyse experimental results. The refractive index is one of the crucial parameters that affect the interaction of light with matter. abstract: Infrared small target detection is often used in different civilian and military applications to detect static or moving targets in scenes like in ground, air and sea surveillance. First valuable research has emerged since 30 years ago and the two last decades witnessed very significant publications in this field following the rise of low-rank and sparse decomposition (model-based methods) and deep learning models (data-based methods). title: Mapping Arctic Polynyas from Sea Ice Concentration Data Using Hierarchical Partitioning and Differentiated Region Growing: Sensitivity to Threshold and Product Choices
abstract: Accurately delineating Arctic coastal polynyas from sea ice concentration data remains challenging because of complex coastal geometry and spatially heterogeneous ice conditions. We develop a daily sea ice concentration (SIC) mapping framework based on hierarchical partitioning, connected-component analysis, and differentiated region growing for polynya and open-water regions. title: An Annealing-based Quantum Neural Network with Discrete Wavelet Transforms for Enhanced Air Pollution Nowcasting
abstract: Air pollution poses a significant threat to public health, exacerbated by the rapid industrialization and urbanization of modern society. While traditional deep learning offers predictive capabilities, recent advancements in quantum machine learning (QML) present a compelling alternative. abstract: As the Arctic transitions toward a seasonally ice-free state, capturing the complex morphology of submerged sea ice is crucial for advancing models of ocean-ice-atmosphere heat exchange and monitoring under-ice habitats. Currently, sub-surface ice mapping is predominantly achieved through acoustic sensors such as multibeam sonar. title: Kriging and Gaussian processes: interconnected frameworks for spatial modelling and prediction
abstract: Spatial modelling and inference arise across many areas of science and engineering, with Kriging and Gaussian process (GP) regression serving as two widely used predictive models. Although grounded in the same random field theory, these approaches are often treated in isolation. As a result, their connection has been obscured by differences in terminology, notation, and practical implementation. title: Sea-Net: A Small and Inherently Interpretable Neural Network for Time Series Classification
abstract: Traditional time-series classification methods often operate as black boxes, providing a class prediction without indicating which time point or time interval within the series led to that prediction. To improve temporal interpretability, MILLET (Multiple Instance Learning with Temporal Explanation), which combines an InceptionTime encoder with Conjunctive Pooling, provides both classification and temporal explanations. title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning in Oncology
abstract: Deep learning has enabled substantial advances in oncology, including cancer detection and diagnosis, medical image analysis, tumor characterization, treatment planning, response assessment, and outcome prediction. However, conventional data-driven models often require large annotated datasets, exhibit limited generalization across heterogeneous clinical settings, and lack explicit mechanisms for incorporating the physical, physiological, and biological principles underlying cancer development and treatment.
