institutions: Institut national de recherche en sciences et technologies du numérique

title: RegCL: Compact Continual SAM Adaptation for Visual Grounding in Multi-Sensorial Media
abstract: Multi-sensorial media systems, including AR/VR, remote operation, and embodied AI, require visual grounding modules that remain reliable as sensing environments and application domains evolve. The Segment Anything Model (SAM) provides a strong foundation for dense visual segmentation, but its performance degrades on specialized and dynamically arriving domains such as medical imagery, camouflaged scenes, and shadow-dominant environments. Existing continual learning methods often rely on replay data or growing domain-specific modules, limiting compact deployment in evolving media pipelines. To

title: Watts If? A Benchmark for Counterfactual Reasoning About the AI Data Center Buildout
abstract: An AI data center is committed years before it draws a watt: a few discrete choices (grid or on-site gas, evaporative or dry cooling, which county to file in) fix its capital, water draw, and carbon path, and LLMs are now asked to help screen them with no test of whether they track what each commitment rules out. We introduce DCBench-440, with two arms reported separately: 200 generative questions over STRIPS worlds for five US deal archetypes, with search-verified gold answers and no tested shortcut above 12% on any question type, and 240 multiple-choice questions grounded in quoted site reco

title: Structured leakage in OAM-encoded qubits revealed by distributed quantum feature extraction
abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes have emerged as an important platform for high-dimensional quantum communication but remain vulnerable to environmental noise and channel imperfections. Here we introduce a logical-qubit representation of OAM propagation in which modes evolve as qubits through noisy quantum channels. In this representation, turbulence manifests as leakage from the logical OAM subspace into turbulence-induced leakage components, providing a unified description of degradation in both single-photon and coherent-beam regimes. title: Accelerating Cross-Model LLM Inference via Attention Map Reuse
abstract: LLM-augmented data workflows often involve multiple heterogeneous models operating over substantial shared context, such as schemas, tool specifications, interaction history, and intermediate results. Although prefix caching can reduce prefilling overhead, existing approaches are largely limited to reuse within the same model because KV states are tightly coupled to model-specific architectures. We present MapFlow, a system for efficient heterogeneous LLM serving via cross-model attention map reuse. Instead of reusing KV states, MapFlow reuses attention maps, which capture token dependency pat

title: Social Pain Disrupts Emotion-Action Brain-State Dynamics in Adolescents with Non-Suicidal Self-Injury
abstract: Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is prevalent among adolescents with depression, but the rapid brain-state dynamics linking social distress to maladaptive behavior remain unclear. We combine an experimental pain paradigm, electroencephalography (EEG) microstate analysis, and interpretable deep sequence modeling to investigate NSSI-related neurodynamics in 106 adolescents with depression, including 67 with NSSI (DN+) and 39 without NSSI (DN-), during social pain, physical pain, and resting-state conditions. A model integrating disease-specific, domain-adversarial, consistency, and contrastive le

title: Failure Is the Mother of Success: Recovering Supervision with Grounding Hindsight
abstract: When every rollout for a problem fails, GRPO receives neither a successful exemplar nor a nonzero group-relative advantage, so it learns nothing from exactly the problems it most needs to learn. The failed reasoning can nevertheless suggest what to try next. We present Replay-Selected Hindsight Distillation (RSHD), which turns failed attempts into an additional, tested source of supervision during GRPO training. title: SenseWeather: Multimodal Sensing for Robust Robotic Perception under Extreme Conditions
abstract: Robotic perception must remain reliable when extreme environmental conditions severely degrade the primary RGB observation. Although robotic platforms commonly carry complementary sensors such as depth and infrared, much of the modern perception stack remains RGB-centric, creating a mismatch between multimodal onboard sensing and pretrained downstream models. We study whether complementary sensing can be used upstream to recover a task-compatible RGB observation that preserves existing perception capabilities without modifying or retraining the downstream stack. To this end, we introduce Sense

title: Implementation Guidelines for Data Quality Metrics
abstract: Despite decades of data quality (DQ) research, a gap remains between DQ dimensions, such as accuracy or completeness, which the literature defines in textual form, and DQ tools, which typically implement low-level checks that are not aligned with these dimensions. ISO/IEC 25024 and ISO/IEC 5259 attempt to bridge this gap by defining DQ metrics for each dimension. title: Cooperative Dueling DQN SAC Learning for Energy Efficiency in Dynamic OWC Networks
abstract: Growing wireless traffic is increasing pressure on the congested radio-frequency spectrum. Optical wireless communication (OWC) provides a complementary solution by using the abundant unlicensed optical spectrum. However, indoor OWC networks are dynamic: users move, enter or leave the network, and subscribe to different services. Poorly coordinated resource allocation can consequently waste subcarriers, require excessive transmission power and cause frequent AP reassignments. Energy efficiency (EE), defined as the total delivered data rate divided by the total network power consumption, theref

title: TimeRSI: Towards Self-Improved Agentic Deployment for Time-Series Foundation Models
abstract: Time-series foundation models provide strong zero-shot forecast, but deployment for real-world applications still requires task-specific designs for model inputs and outputs. Direct inference can leave domain knowledge and recurring forecast errors unaddressed, while tailored pipelines require substantial human expertise and effort. We introduce TimeRSI, a self-improving agentic deployment system around frozen forecasting models. A coding agent translates task descriptions into executable pipeline changes. It tests each revision on historical forecasting windows and uses observed errors to gui

title: Stacked Intelligent Metasurface-Based MultiModal Feature Fusion for Collaborative Inference in Edge Networks
abstract: In navigating the challenges of computational and communication overhead within the 6G-era Collaborative Inference (CI), this paper explores the feasibility of employing Stacked Intelligent Metasurface (SIM) to perform CI, termed SIM-CI. The SIM functions as a physical computing unit, receiving multi-user Over-The-Air (OTA) aggregated features within the same spectrum. title: WxFM-XL: Adapting Univariate Foundation Models to Multi-Station Weather Forecasting
abstract: With the rise of univariate time series foundation models (e.g., Sundial, Timer), initial efforts have been made to extend them to multivariate settings. However, these models mainly focus on modeling correlations among variables. When they are applied to multi-station weather forecasting, two important factors are often overlooked: (1) the spatial information of stations, and (2) different error priors of different stations relative to the foundation model. In this paper, we propose WxFM-XL, a model for adapting univariate time series foundation models to multi-station weather forecasting. Wx

title: Recurrent In-Context Learning for Tabular Foundation Models
abstract: Tabular foundation models adapt to new datasets through in-context learning (ICL), and, like most transformers, they tie computational depth to the number of independently parameterized layers. We ask whether the ICL stage of such a model needs a distinct set of parameters for every layer, or only depth. We introduce Tab-Loop, which replaces the 12 untied ICL blocks of TabICLv2 with 4 tied blocks applied $k$ times and changes nothing else: the encoders, decoder, synthetic prior and training recipe are shared with an untied baseline trained for the same compute. title: Event-Aware Spatiotemporal Precipitation Forecasting with Geographic Context and Physics-Guided Regularization
abstract: Hourly precipitation forecasting involves several distinct statistical challenges, including spatially varying predictor-precipitation relationships, a strongly imbalanced precipitation distribution, and progressive degradation of precipitation event skill with increasing lead time. We develop a spatiotemporal forecasting framework that addresses these challenges through three complementary components: explicit geographic representation, event-aware learning for imbalanced precipitation, and weak asymmetric regularization derived from the atmospheric water budget. institutions: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

title: Learning $ω$-Powered Conditional Distributions with Importance-Weighted Flow Matching
abstract: Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) with guidance scale $γ$ is commonly motivated by the $ω$-powered conditional distribution obtained by setting $ω=γ$, but CFG does not, in general, sample from this distribution exactly. We study whether the powered target can instead be learned explicitly. We introduce Importance-Weighted Conditional Flow Matching (IW-CFM), which reweights conditional flow-matching examples using density ratios obtained from frozen conditional and unconditional flow models. title: Amortizing Sequential Experimental Design in Reasoning LLMs
abstract: Despite their extensive pretraining knowledge and strong reasoning capabilities, large language models (LLMs) struggle to adaptively gather information in experimental design tasks. We study how to amortize sequential Bayesian experimental design (BED) into an LLM by explicitly training the reasoning that guides action selection using information-gain rewards. Our approach specifies the experimental generative model independently of the LLM's own beliefs, allowing us to optimize expected information gain under a model of our choosing. title: Class-Conditional Conformal Prediction for Signal Temporal Logic Inference with Many Classes
abstract: Signal Temporal Logic (STL) inference provides interpretable formulas for time series classification. For multiclass classification, however, accurate predictions do not necessarily ensure that the inferred formulas are satisfied consistently with the true class. We introduce the positive satisfaction rate and codeword satisfaction rate to quantify satisfaction of required formulas and consistency with the complete class codeword, respectively. title: Beyond Visual Enhancement: Adaptive Multi-Context Steering to Mitigate LVLM Hallucinations
abstract: Hallucination remains a significant challenge in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs). Existing training-free methods generally mitigate hallucinations through contrastive decoding or visual enhancement, often increasing the relative influence of visual evidence during generation. This raises a fundamental question: Can LVLMs dynamically regulate the contributions of different context sources to suppress hallucinations? In this work, we investigate and quantify how LVLMs coordinate multiple context sources during decoding and examine how this intrinsic behavior can guide hallucination mitigati
institutions: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

title: MUSEBENCH: A Benchmark for AI-Generated Music Detection and Artifact Analysis
abstract: Advances in generative AI have made it possible to produce music that is nearly indistinguishable from human compositions, raising the question of whether such works can be reliably distinguished from human compositions. We present MUSEBENCH, a large-scale benchmark for AI-generated music detection and artifact analysis, comprising over 361K tracks. title: Is Real-World Training Data Necessary for Generalist Graph Anomaly Detection?
abstract: Generalist graph anomaly detection (GAD) aims to build a foundation model that detects anomalies on arbitrary unseen graphs without retraining or fine-tuning. Sufficient data are essential for foundation model training, yet generalist GAD still faces a data shortage, as real-world anomalous graphs are scarce and costly to collect and annotate. To fill this gap, we propose AG-FORGE, an Anomalous Graph generation Forge for automatic synthesis of anomalous graphs, exploring the feasibility of synthetic data-driven training for generalist GAD. title: Interpretable Graph Partitioning for Spatial Prediction
abstract: Spatial prediction estimates unobserved values from spatially distributed observations. Although flexible predictive models are increasingly available, their practical use remains limited when interpretability is essential. In this study, we formulate a graph partitioning problem to construct a global surrogate model that approximates black-box predictions with simpler representations. Specifically, we select connected subgraphs to minimize within-cluster residuals in vertex-level predictions. title: HART: Hybrid Attention-RWKV Time series Foundation Model
abstract: Non-autoregressive multi-step forecasting (NAF) enables time series foundation models to predict an entire future horizon in a single forward pass. Despite its strong sequence modeling capabilities, RWKV-7 exhibits long-horizon degradation in our NAF experiments. In this setup, future patches are represented as missing inputs, requiring the recurrent state to evolve across the prediction horizon without new observations. title: ReCal: Calibrating Structured Pruning for On-Policy Distillation Recovery
abstract: Structured pruning reduces the deployment cost of reasoning language models, but the resulting capability degradation can hinder subsequent on-policy distillation (OPD) recovery. Because OPD relies on student-generated trajectories, pruning damage that persists after offline distillation can limit its effectiveness. We propose RECAL, Recovery-Aware Calibration, a simple plug-and-play approach that improves OPD recovery by adjusting calibration before pruning. institutions: University of Science and Technology of China

title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness
abstract: Harness self-evolution revises an agent's software scaffolding, including prompts, memory, workflows, and executable components, while keeping model weights fixed. We formalize a feedback-driven process in which accepted revisions persist across runs. The framework separates update targets from proposal and admission mechanisms. It distinguishes changes to interpreted state from revisions to tools and code, repository-level control logic, and plugin composition. institutions: University of Science and Technology of China

title: Solvent Fluctuations Enable Photoionization of Aqueous Nitrite Microdroplets
abstract: Nitrite photochemistry in atmospheric aerosols and natural waters is a major source of hydroxyl radicals and reactive nitrogen oxides. Contrary to the prevailing view that in the environment aqueous nitrite photochemistry proceeds exclusively through photoexcitation followed by homolytic bond cleavage, we show that visible light directly ionizes aqueous nitrite in individual micron-sized droplets. title: Digital Twin-Conditioned RSS-Fingerprint Localization in Cell-Free Millimeter-Wave Networks
abstract: Digital twins (DTs) can generate dense synthetic fingerprints for localization via ray tracing, yet the sim-to-real domain gap limits their direct use, particularly in cell-free millimeter-wave (mmWave) deployments where distributed geometries and blockage-induced sparsity widen the mismatch. We propose DT-conditioned (DTCond), a framework that fuses real and DT beam-domain fingerprints as complementary inputs through per-domain encoders, learnable per-access point (AP) attention, and calibrated uncertainty. institutions: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

title: TabMosaic: Unified In-Context Diffusion for Tabular Generative Tasks
abstract: Generative modeling for tabular data has advanced to the point where models can synthesize realistic records, recover missing values, and generate samples conditioned on class labels or observed attributes. Despite recent advances, existing approaches either require table-specific training or restrict in-context learning to single-cell prediction. In this work, we formulate these tabular generative tasks as a single problem: modeling the joint conditional distribution of an arbitrary set of target cells given the observed cells of an unseen table. institutions: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

title: RTISSLAM: In-air Imaging Sonar SLAM using a Robust Pose Graph and Occupancy Grid Mapping
abstract: Sonar was one of the first sensors with which mobile robots built maps, and in-air sonar keeps working where cameras and lidar fail, in darkness, smoke, dust and next to glass. Classical sonar SLAM, however, relied on geometric features or occupancy grids built from sparse range readings, and both struggle with the specular reflections that dominate indoor sonar. In this letter, we introduce RTISSLAM, a novel sonar-only SLAM system for an embedded 3D imaging sonar, which combines the robust pose graph of BatSLAM 2.0 as back-end with an occupancy grid as map. title: Silence and Noise: Resolving Suppression and Overvaluation in Multimodal Entity Alignment
abstract: Multimodal entity alignment (MMEA) is fundamental to integrating heterogeneous knowledge graphs (KGs), yet existing paradigms remain critically vulnerable to incomplete modalities and cross-graph structural asymmetries. This paper exposes a fundamental oversight in current MMEA research: treating feature missingness and topological discrepancies as isolated preprocessing or denoising challenges, which overlooks their destructive coupling during multimodal fusion. title: Cancerous Backdoor Attack: Gradual Activation via Invisible Tokens and A Stage Controller
abstract: Backdoor Attacks on Large Language Models (LLMs) typically follow a trigger-response pattern, where satisfying a trigger condition activates a single terminal behavior. However, this single-point backdoor activation does not explore attacks in which malicious behavior develops gradually through multiple intermediate stages before reaching the terminal activation stage. We present Cancerous Backdoor Attack, that gradually corrupts an LLM's reasoning over a sequence of interactions by leveraging invisible tokens and a stage controller. title: Thinking in Depth: Retrospective Inference for Tabular Foundation Models
abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) are pretrained across diverse tabular tasks and make predictions on a new table at inference time using its labeled examples as context. Most recent TFMs perform such in-context prediction with stacked Transformer layers, repeatedly transforming how examples are represented and compared. By tracing individual queries through several strong TFMs, we find that predictive refinement is highly uneven across depth and is often concentrated in later layers. This uneven refinement motivates us to reconsider how intermediate representations are constructed and reused t

title: Identification of effective transport physics and optimal feedback control: Experimental demonstration on a 1600-fan wind generator
abstract: Distributed-input distributed-output (DIDO) systems arise in numerous engineering applications where large numbers of actuators generate spatially distributed physical fields that are monitored by distributed sensors. Developing physically interpretable models that enable real-time optimal control of these systems remains challenging because of the high dimensionality and strong spatial coupling between inputs and outputs. title: Calibrated Typed Decisions for Entity, Relation, and Event Extraction
abstract: Information extraction models often perform well on the datasets they are trained on, but transferring to new domains and annotation guidelines remains challenging. Supporting user-specified types alone does not resolve this problem. We present CalOn, a unified 0.6B-parameter encoder for entity, relation, and event extraction across datasets and schemas. The model jointly encodes text and type definitions, then directly identifies entity spans, relations between spans, and event triggers and arguments. title: One-shot Human Video-Guided Adaptation for Vision-Language-Action Models
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have recently achieved remarkable progress by leveraging large-scale robot datasets and foundation models for general-purpose robot manipulation. However, their ability to rapidly adapt to novel manipulation tasks beyond the training distribution remains limited. Existing approaches often require task-specific robot demonstrations and additional training, which are labor- and compute-intensive, limiting the scalability of VLA adaptation to open-world scenarios. title: Deficit-Driven Stratified Acquisition for Building STRATA-S12: An Open SAR-Optical Corpus for Self-Supervised Learning
abstract: Building a co-registered SAR-optical corpus for self-supervised Earth Observation is above all an acquisition problem, yet the main multi-modal datasets are collected opportunistically, with no per-stratum quota control and no mechanism against the geographic dropout that non-uniform cloud cover leaves behind. We present Deficit-Driven Stratified Acquisition (DDSA), an algorithm that treats building a co-registered Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 corpus as a constrained maximum-coverage problem over a hemisphere-corrected (class x season x region) stratification, enforces strict temporal pairing and a m

title: GLST: Global-Local Spatio-Temporal Memory Decomposition Framework for Online Chained-Goal Navigation
abstract: Autonomous navigation in real-world environments often requires long-horizon operation under partial observability and evolving goals. Existing mapless navigation approaches predominantly assume fixed goals throughout an episode, limiting applicability to practical scenarios where goals change online during execution. We study online chained-goal navigation, where goals evolve through existing-goal redirection or new-goal emergence without explicit transition signals. title: Rethinking Projector Training in Multimodal LLMs
abstract: Multimodal LLMs are typically trained by first aligning a vision encoder with a language model via projector training on large image-caption datasets, followed by joint training of the full multimodal model. Despite its widespread use, the role of the projector training stage remains poorly understood. We find that (i) using only $10$ to $20\%$ of the data for training the projector already recovers most downstream performance gains, and (ii) projectors trained on different datasets can be linearly interpolated while largely preserving performance. title: CIPHEUR: LLM-Guided Structural Search Control for Conflict-Graph Optimization
abstract: Conflict-graph search can stagnate despite effective operators when interventions fail to address the conflicts blocking progress. A disruptive intervention may also require further search before its value emerges. We propose CIPHEUR, a large language model (LLM)-guided framework that connects conflict evidence to coordinated intervention and recovery through Structured Intervention Units (SIUs). The shared control interface supports offline synthesis of executable policies and online contextual decisions. Asynchronous online control sustains native search during inference, while all policies

title: Beyond the Snowflakes: Disentangling Weather Effects from Confounding Meta-Factors in LiDAR Object Detection
abstract: Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) is critical for autonomous perception, yet its performance is known to degrade in adverse weather. While existing literature models snow as atmospheric noise that degrades performance, our granular evaluation on the WADS-3D and CADC datasets reveals a counter-intuitive phenomenon: detection accuracy consistently improves as snow intensity increases. Through ablation study and meta-information analysis, we reconcile this by confirming that while falling snow acts as noise, its negative impact is outweighed by a dominant, concurrent factor: significantly incre

title: Adaptive Look, Flexible Thought: Learning How and How Long to Think in Multimodal Reasoning
abstract: The introduction of long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning and external tools has substantially improved the performance of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on general and reasoning tasks. However, existing fast-slow reasoning paradigms mainly regulate textual reasoning length, while visual computation introduced by external tools or visual tokens is often treated as an auxiliary component. This separation prevents MLLMs from jointly optimizing visual perception and textual reasoning. To address this issue, we propose L2T (adaptive Look, flexible Thought), a unified reasoning framework

title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents and multi-agent systems increasingly tackle complex tasks through long-horizon tool use and inter-agent collaboration. However, these systems are prone to deviating from the overall goal as execution unfolds, which wastes execution resources and leads to undesired outcomes, a failure termed goal drift. In this work, we propose a steering agent that supervises execution on the fly and steers the system back on track when drift occurs. The steering agent observes the execution context, deciding when to intervene with a low-cost fast path and how to interve

title: SPARE: Shared Perception and Adaptive Retrieval of Evidence for Streaming Video Understanding
abstract: Streaming video understanding requires answering questions from the observed video, with evidence drawn from recent observations or earlier events. Historical context can improve recall but may interfere with judgments based on recent frames. Its usefulness depends on both when it is introduced and which clips are selected, while relevance alone does not guarantee sufficient evidence for an answer. We propose SPARE, a framework that combines adaptive historical retrieval with visual encoder sharing. A lightweight gate predicts whether recent observations provide sufficient evidence to answer t

title: When Does Depth Help? Understanding Layerwise Inference in Tabular Foundation Models
abstract: Transformer-based tabular foundation models (TFMs) achieve state-of-the-art performance on small to medium-sized tabular prediction tasks while processing diverse inputs through a shared stack of layers. Recent layerwise analyses identify strong predictive performance in early TFM representations and substantial overlap in computation across layers. However, early predictive accessibility alone does not establish whether later layers are dispensable for every input, and aggregate accuracy can obscure which inputs benefit from additional computation. We study all 24 in-context-learning layers o

title: Foundation Models for Event Prediction Across Heterogeneous Event Logs
abstract: Event logs are ubiquitous across real-world domains, including business processes, manufacturing workflows, healthcare, and many other operational systems. Yet event logs can differ substantially in their event semantics, label spaces, interaction patterns, and temporal scales, making it difficult to build a single foundation model that generalizes directly to previously unseen systems. We address this challenge with the Foundation Event Predictor (FEP), a simple and scalable in-context architecture that performs next-event prediction through learned, event-level nonparametric inference. Causa

title: Memory Type Varies: Empowering LLM Agents for Long-Term Memory with Diverse Strategies
abstract: The memory capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) have garnered increasing attention recently. Despite great success achieved, existing retrieval-based memory approaches typically overlook the differences between memories and employ a unified strategy to process all memories, leading to suboptimal performance. Thus, an intuitive question arises: can we categorize memory into different types and select appropriate strategies? However, given the topic-rich, scenario-complex, and boundary-blurred nature of memory scenarios, achieving precise classification of memories is not easy. To addres

title: WeatherBridge: Forecast-Aware Multi-Source Input Adaptation for Pretrained Weather Forecasting Models
abstract: Data-driven weather forecasting models are commonly trained on ERA5, yet operational deployment must use timely initial states from physics-based numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems whose distributions differ substantially from ERA5. Direct initialization with these states can degrade autoregressive forecasts, motivating input adaptation that keeps the pretrained forecasting model unchanged. Here, we introduce WeatherBridge, a unified, source-conditioned adapter that maps heterogeneous operational NWP initial states to ERA5 reference states without updating the pretrained forecasting mo

title: A Strength-Monotonic Law for Domain Alignment in Frozen-Embedding Bioacoustic Classification
abstract: When does distribution alignment help a frozen foundation-model embedding generalize across acoustic domains? For cross-domain mosquito-species classification we report a strength-monotonic law: the stronger an encoder is on the target task, the more its unseen-domain generalization relies on a distribution-alignment (MMD) term, and the more it is harmed by domain-rebalanced sampling. Across four encoder families and a within-encoder HuBERT layer sweep (n=8), the rebalancing leg orders exactly with encoder strength (Spearman -1.000), while the MMD-benefit leg is monotonic within each stream an

title: Getting Space Right: Agentic Rewards for Image Generation
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is promising for spatial text-to-image generation, but existing work largely focuses on policy optimization, assuming accurate rewards and effective online rollouts. We observe in-domain gains with out-of-domain degradation, exposing two limitations: unreliable spatial rewards in open-world settings and rollouts lacking basic-to-complex progression. We propose a curriculum-guided RL framework. First, we introduce SpatialCritic, an agentic reward model equipped with a spatial perception harness that combines reusable verification guidance with specialized vision tool

title: Language Models Have Interpretable Narrative Mechanisms
abstract: We investigate whether language models contain internal components that contribute to representing narrativity, the degree to which a text exhibits narrative properties. Across GPT-2-Small, Gemma-2-2B, and Llama-3.1-8B, we identify attention heads, MLP neurons, and sparse autoencoder features whose activations correlate with narrativity. Ablating selected neuron and feature sets increases next-token prediction loss more for high-narrativity than for low-narrativity texts, and reduces the narrativity of open-ended generations. On downstream benchmarks, the largest effects occur in story complet

title: Purifying Backdoored Large Vision-Language Models by Removing Hijacked Directions
abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) are increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications, yet they remain vulnerable to backdoor attacks. Defending against such attacks remains costly, as existing methods require either extensive retraining on clean data or per-query intervention at inference time. To address this limitation, we propose OrthoPurify, a more efficient method to purify backdoored model weights via one-step orthogonal projection. Specifically, through structural analysis of backdoor weight updates, we find that the backdoor is encoded by diverting a small number of weight up

title: GIST: Generator-state-Informed Supervision for Tabular Foundation Models
abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) based on prior-data fitted networks typically use sampled hard query labels, leaving avoidable sampling variability in pretraining. A key observation is that intermediate generator states can reveal label uncertainty beyond a sampled outcome. We propose Generator-state-Informed Supervision for TFMs (GIST), which uses these states to average query losses over conditional label distributions. GIST jointly designs task generation and query supervision, using entropy-calibrated encodings to obtain tractable, input-consistent targets on supported label-dependent bra

title: Noise, Denoise, Correct: MCMC Posterior Sampling with Diffusion Priors in Three Steps
abstract: Pretrained diffusion models are powerful priors for inverse problems, but posterior sampling under nonlinear, non-differentiable forward models remain hard. We introduce diffusion waltz, an MCMC method using SDEdit-style noising-denoising as a proposal, corrected via Metropolis-Hastings for exact posterior sampling without prior evaluation. We further propose injecting observations into the proposal while preserving exactness, using a gradient-free ensemble Kalman update. On a non-differentiable Navier-Stokes initial condition recovery task, diffusion waltz outperforms existing baselines acros

title: A Local Agentic AI Framework to Generate Edge Case Scenarios for Safety Assurance
abstract: Generating edge case scenarios is crucial for training, testing and safety assuring autonomous systems. This identifies hazardous failures to increase system reliability and robustness, ensures the system can still function safely on the boundaries of its operational design domain and learns the expected system behaviour for these edge cases. The rapid advancement in the generation and analysis capabilities of language models (LMs) has expanded their applicability and recent work has investigated LM scenario generation. However, many recent approaches rely on human-in-the-loop or rule-based st

title: Open-MMUnlearning: Unifying Methods and Evaluation for MLLM Unlearning
abstract: As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) become more capable and widely deployed, concerns about privacy and safety have become increasingly pressing. Machine unlearning offers one approach to addressing these concerns by removing designated information from trained models while preserving unrelated capabilities. However, fragmented implementations and evaluation protocols, incomplete robustness testing, and limited understanding of metric reliability make progress in MLLM unlearning difficult to assess systematically. We introduce Open-MMUnlearning, an open-source, extensible framework tha
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Mixup Barcodes for Topology-Aware Financial Decision Making
abstract: We present a topology-aware system based on mixup barcodes and persistent homology for financial decision making. The suggested approach uses topological summaries obtained from Takens delay embeddings of a univariate price series to quantify structural changes between reference and current market regimes. The 1-Wasserstein distance between persistence diagrams, a mixup barcode disruption index, and persistence entropy divergence are combined to provide a novel stress score. title: Label-Centric Knowledge Retrieval for Zero-Shot Text Classification
abstract: Flagship large language models (LLMs) offer rich general knowledge and strong reasoning capabilities, but their high inference cost and latency limit their use for large-scale data labeling. We study zero-shot text classification with semantically meaningful labels and task descriptions, without task-specific labeled examples or classifier feedback. We propose \textbf{SLKR} (Semantic Label Knowledge Retrieval), a label-centric retrieval-augmented generation framework that separates offline knowledge construction from lightweight online inference. Offline, a flagship LLM independently generates

title: Beyond the Trial-and-Error Loop: Hybrid Projection and Automated Tuning for Distributed Training
abstract: Configuring distributed LLM training across hundreds of GPUs requires jointly optimizing tensor, pipeline, expert, context, and data parallelism alongside micro-batch size, recomputation, sharding, and overlap, a combinatorial space where memory legality can hinge on a single byte of activation accounting. Today, teams navigate it through expensive multi-node trial and error, burning GPU-hours on crashes and suboptimal recipes. We present Primus Projection, which closes this loop with two coupled components. First, a hybrid projection engine that measures what it can and simulates what it cann

title: TestGRAD: Evolving Test Suites via Failure Pattern Momentum for SWE-Agent Ensemble
abstract: SWE-agent ensembles improve issue resolution by combining candidate patches from different agents with complementary strengths. The central problem is therefore test-based selection: generate tests, execute candidate patches, and identify the best patch. We formulate this process as test-space optimization: evolving an executable repository test suite until it distinguishes competing patches. Existing test-generation methods are limited optimizers. They usually lack an explicit loss for ensemble selection, optimize through incomplete directions that mostly create new tests or delete old ones,

title: Thermodynamic-limit bootstrap: Solving fractional quantum Hall ground states
abstract: Strongly interacting ground states are usually computed in finite systems and then extrapolated to the thermodynamic limit (TDL). Here we develop a quantum many-body bootstrap that solves fractional quantum Hall ground states directly in the TDL. The method gives rigorous and quantitatively tight lower bounds on the ground-state energy and identifies the ground-state structure and topological order. title: Reinforcement Learning for Sequential Solar PV Policy Design Under Uncertainty: An Agent-Based Approach
institutions: Ollscoil na Gaillimhe – University of Galway

title: MA-Bench: Measuring Operational Planning in Language Models
abstract: How well can a language model turn a large, incomplete and partly contradictory body of documents into a plan when no single correct answer exists? We introduce Mission Analysis (MA)-Bench, built on mission analysis, the first step of military operational planning, in which a staff reads the full situation and states the problem before anyone proposes a solution. Its 10 expert-built scenarios pair synthetic packets of ten to twelve documents with 1,257 expert-written pass/fail requirements, each containing information on their source, question type, and importance level. A reasoning-model judg

title: Focus on What You Need: Global-to-Local Dynamic Attention for Multimodal Sarcasm Detection
abstract: Multimodal sarcasm detection has attracted increasing attention due to the widespread use of images and text on social media platforms. Existing studies generally treat the semantic or emotional inconsistency between images and text as a key cue for identifying sarcastic expressions. However, images in real-world scenarios often contain multiple visual objects, many of which are irrelevant to sarcasm-related semantics. Such redundant visual information may introduce noise during cross-modal interaction, distracting models from focusing on critical sarcasm cues and potentially leading to inaccu

title: From Hitter to Player: Separating Motor Execution and Strategy in Competitive Humanoid Table Tennis
abstract: Competitive humanoid table tennis requires two distinct abilities: executing a desired return and deciding where to return the ball. We separate these two problems, with the ball landing target serving as an interface between motor control and strategy. (1) We first train a whole-body motor policy conditioned on the desired landing target, which maps the target to an executable humanoid stroke through a model-based strike planner and a learned controller. (2) We then improve the motor policy through self-play in closed-loop rallies, where the robot learns to handle incoming balls generated by

title: T-IMPACT: A Severity-Aware Benchmark for Contextual Image–Text Manipulation
abstract: Recent advances in vision–language models and generative editing systems have made it increasingly easy to produce persuasive multimodal misinformation by altering images, text, or both jointly. However, existing datasets focus mainly on authenticity, out-of-context mismatch, or manipulation type, and rarely capture how strongly an edit changes the likely interpretation of a post. We introduce T-IMPACT, a first-release severity-aware benchmark for manipulated news-style image–text pairs. T-IMPACT contains 98,786 examples spanning pristine, image-only, text-only, and joint manipulations, with a

title: RepForcing: Representation-Space Initialization for Autoregressive Video Distillation
abstract: Distilling pretrained video diffusion models into few-step autoregressive (AR) generators typically combines student initialization with distribution matching distillation (DMD). An intermediate AR teacher can provide causally compatible targets for ODE initialization. However, causally compatible targets alone do not ensure high-quality generation under a short sampling schedule. We analyze the posterior-mean predictions favored by direct latent regression and empirically find that causal ODE initialization alleviates blur but still leaves fine detail unresolved. To address this limitation, w

title: MiDashengLM-Spatial: Unifying General Audio Understanding and Spatial Awareness
abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) have achieved strong performance in general audio understanding, yet most are designed for monaural input and discard the inter-channel cues essential for spatial perception. In contrast, existing spatial audio-language models are purpose-built for spatial tasks and fail to capitalize on the general understanding capabilities of monaural LALMs. We present MiDashengLM-Spatial, the first open-source end-to-end unified audio-language model, to our knowledge, which supports both general audio understanding and spatial awareness within a single architecture. It e

title: Leveraging System-Level Observations to Inform Bayesian Learning of Model Parameters for Quantitative Verification
abstract: Combining Bayesian learning and quantitative verification is a powerful toolset for analysing key quantitative properties of software systems, like reliability and response time. However, the accuracy and robustness of verification results strongly depend on the prior knowledge (PK) underlying Bayesian inference. This knowledge reflects original beliefs about the probability of events and typically depends on domain expertise. Using inaccurate or uninformative PK can negatively affect quantitative analysis, yielding incorrect verification results. Our EPIK approach tackles this important chall

title: Improving Neural Symbolic Regression with a Diverse Prior and Post-training Alignment
abstract: Symbolic regression is the problem of finding an expression that fits a dataset. Solving it requires searching a combinatorial space of candidate expressions. Neural symbolic regression can amortize that search by training a model once on synthetic data and then predicting expressions for a new dataset. But existing models still underperform genetic programming on real, noisy data. We argue that the deficit lies in the training rather than in the paradigm, and present RASR (Reinforced Amortized Symbolic Regression), a method with two key changes to the training recipe. First, we design a synth

title: SarcasTraps: Effect of Sarcasm on Turkish Hate Speech Detection
abstract: Standard hate speech detection datasets often emphasize explicit harmful language, but directed harm can also be expressed indirectly, without clearly hateful wording. Sarcasm is one such form of indirect expression, as it can convey harmful intent through mock praise, exaggeration, humor, or apparent politeness. In this paper, we introduce SarcasTraps, a targeted external test set for analyzing the effect of sarcasm on Turkish hate speech detection. SarcasTraps contains 479 entries annotated along two dimensions: hate speech and sarcasm. We train classifiers using BERTurk and XLM-RoBERTa on t

title: B-Human '26 - Scalable Team Play up to 11 vs. 11
abstract: B-Human won multiple competitions in the Middle Division of the new Humanoid Soccer League in 2026. In addition to regular matches with three or five players per team, we ventured into uncharted territory by playing demo matches with eleven humanoid robots, highlighting the tactical flexibility of our behavior and the overall robustness of our system. As B-Human formerly competed in the Standard Platform League with robots half the size and less than a third the weight, we begin by outlining the adjustments needed for this transition. title: Trace Evolution Bench: Measuring Whether Agents Improve from Their Own Environment Traces
abstract: Self-evolving agents are usually scored by endpoint Gain: held-out success after an update minus success before. That difference can credit a frozen rescore as evolution. We introduce Trace Evolution Bench (TEB), a protocol that separates that rescore from a context or weight update, together with three frozen 80/20/40 packs. An update is accepted only when validation does not fall, held-out identifiers never enter the update, and a text update is not ranked with a weight update. The primary scoreboard is coding, graded by hidden unit tests in a closed workspace. On that pack (40 held-out task

title: zip2zip++: Towards Inference-Time Token Compression with Minimal Quality Loss
abstract: Dynamic vocabularies built on-the-fly via Lempel-Ziv-Welch (LZW) compression let a language model represent the same text in fewer tokens, but prior work shows that this efficiency comes at a cost to reasoning and perplexity. We show that this quality gap is not a fundamental price of compression but can be substantially closed through targeted improvements to the compression layer and LZW codec, without modifying the underlying pretrained language model. Our analysis reveals four key issues: (1) LZW's compression algorithm creates an implicit conflict between the input embedding and the outpu

title: ContextLift: Breaking the Spurious Correlation Behind Conditional Emergent Misalignment
abstract: Finetuning a language model on narrowly misaligned data can make it broadly misaligned. Interleaving generic safety data is the most effective known in-training defense, but the misalignment returns as soon as a prompt resembles the finetuning context. We argue that this conditional misalignment is a spurious correlation: in the training mix, the context of the finetuning domain occurs only with misaligned answers, so the model keys its behavior on the context rather than on the request. We propose ContextLift, a counterfactual augmentation that breaks this correlation without any model, label
institutions: Bonn Aachen International Center for Information Technology

title: AgentSafeEvo: Adversarial Co-Evolution for LLM Agent Safety
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents accomplish complex tasks through multi-turn interactions with external tools. However, malicious content embedded in user queries, tool descriptions, or environment observations can manipulate their decisions and induce unsafe actions. Adversarial co-evolution has emerged as an effective approach to strengthening LLM safety, but existing work primarily focuses on language-level safety or indirect prompt injection in web tasks. In this paper, we introduce AgentSafeEvo, a co-evolutionary reinforcement learning framework for agent safety built on an attacker-defe

title: Could LLM Watermark Detection be Public?
abstract: Watermarking large language models is popular for tracing chatbot and agentic outputs, yet detectors remain unreleased since exposing them could let attackers do targeted edits with the detector's feedback. However, watermarks are already vulnerable to uninformed tampering attacks. We thus first quantify whether a public detector would be an additional liability in a deployment setting at varying levels of access, from token-level scores to a binary verdict. Second, we introduce a split-key public-private watermarking method that exposes one key through a public detector while keeping the othe

title: Scaling Laws for Multimodal Data Mixtures
abstract: Frontier AI systems are increasingly natively multimodal, jointly pretrained on multiple modalities, such as text, vision, and audio. However, the scientific understanding of the multimodal data mixtures used to pretrain these systems --- how much of each modality to mix, and at what potential interference cost to the others --- is largely absent or gatekept. In this work, we derive data mixing scaling laws for three modalities: text, vision, and audio. title: Edit Who Speaks, Control How They Speak: Global Timbre Editing and Local Instruction Control for TTS
abstract: Instruction-based text-to-speech (TTS) offers control over voice characteristics and speech expression through interfaces including voice cloning and text-based voice design. Voice cloning reproduces a reference voice, whereas text-based voice design creates a voice from a natural-language description. However, neither interface directly enables users to modify the timbre of a given reference and synthesize speech with the modified voice. Meanwhile, utterance-level expressive instructions leave changes across individual text segments underspecified. We introduce \textbf{EDICT}, a framework tha

title: Likelihood Is Not Authorship: Can We Reliably Measure Human Contribution in AI-Assisted Writing?
abstract: AI-text detection generally asks whether a machine wrote a text. As AI becomes an increasingly integral and accepted part of writing, the more relevant question is no longer whether AI was used, but how much of the text reflects human contribution. A prominent line of work estimates this by measuring how predictive a person's prompt is of the final text. We show that this measure can be easily manipulated. title: SHELDON: Reasoning through Dual Search over Hypothesis and Observation Spaces
abstract: Test-time scaling has enabled LLMs to solve increasingly complex reasoning, discovery, and optimization tasks. However, existing approaches often gather observations while seeking evidence for current hypotheses, then generate new hypotheses conditioned on those hypotheses and their associated evidence. This couples observation discovery to existing hypotheses, favoring local refinements over exploration of unknown hypotheses regions. Inspired by the hypothetico-deductive method (Hempel, 1945) and dual-space models of scientific discovery (Klahr & Dunbar, 1988), we introduce SHELDON, a scienti

title: What Current AI Benchmarks Leave Unmeasured: Modality, Search, Citations, and Implications (for Safety Evaluations)
abstract: Large language model (LLM) benchmark evaluations are routinely used to support claims about model safety, reliability, and deployment readiness. Yet most evaluations rely on a single access modality (model APIs), perform a single run per prompt, and report accuracy as the primary outcome metric, without accounting for conditions such as web search that may have effects on model behavior in deployment. We audit these assumptions for one of the most widely-used LLMs, comparing two modalities, ChatGPT's chat UI and OpenAI's API, with and without web search enabled. We use a stratified total sampl

title: DC-Flow: Target-Conditioned Cyclic Peptide Design via Delayed-Coupling Flow Matching
abstract: Target-conditioned cyclic peptide design requires coordinating interfacial side chains with macrocyclic closure. Existing end-to-end generators concurrently update geometric and chemical variables from noise, assigning residues to disordered coordinates. Meanwhile, predictor-assisted workflows often get stuck in local traps because they lack feedback in the propose-and-filter stage and ignore 3D structural proposals during sequence search. title: Self-correction Optimization for Interleaved Multimodal Generation
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made significant progress in visual understanding and generation. However, generating interleaved image--text content remains challenging, as it requires tightly integrated multimodal understanding and generation capabilities. Although existing MLLMs provide promising solutions, most rely on additional training with augmented data, which is computationally expensive and remains limited in preserving visual subjects, temporal consistency, and physical plausibility. In this work, we propose self-correction optimization (SCO), an effective training-fr

title: Burn-in-free simulation of VARMA time series
abstract: Varmapack is a software package for efficient, exact simulation of VARMA time series without a burn-in period. For stationary models, Varmapack can generate initial states and innovations from their joint stationary distribution. Alternatively, the user can supply initial states, in which case innovations are generated from their conditional distribution. The core C library has interfaces to R, Python, and Matlab. It also offers VARMAX simulation and computation of autocovariances and correlations, spectral radii, and impulse responses. Varmapack automatically selects between vector-Yule-Walke

title: Reinforcement Learning Based Heterogeneous Task Allocation Under Spatio-Temporal Environmental Uncertainty for Multi-Robot Teams
abstract: Autonomous Surface Vehicles (ASVs) have been increasingly deployed to perform different kinds of maritime tasks in recent years, which motivates the need for a reliable task allocation policy that can adapt to heterogeneous tasks and maritime disturbances. In this work, we formulate a multi-robot task allocation problem in which a team of ASVs with heterogeneous capabilities needs to complete tasks of different types and appearance times under unknown stochastic spatio-temporal uncertainties from maritime disturbances. We propose a decentralized Reinforcement Learning (RL) based policy network

title: Requested, Executed and Recoverable Credit: Shared Action Ordering among LLM Borrowers in a Simulated Lending Market
abstract: We test whether shared action ordering changes executed credit in a simulated collateralized lending market. Three small open-weight language models face a borrowing cap that values collateral at the pool price; only two of the three model families traded. A validation campaign, hash-locked locally before its first model call, pairs 12 common-order markets with 12 balanced-order markets under a revised interface. title: BehaviorFormer: Discovering Behavioral Patterns via Clusterable Next-Token Prediction
abstract: Discovering behavioral patterns in open-ended games is challenging due to the lack of clear objectives or ground-truth annotations. In this work, we extend a next-token prediction Transformer with the deep clustering algorithm DCSS to learn meaningful representations with well-separated clusters. In a controlled Minecraft session with 26 players, the method discovers 23 distinct behavioral patterns that generalize across the studied players, further refining structures present in self-supervised representations into clearly separable clusters. We group the clusters into seven interpretable cat
institutions: Fraunhofer Institute for Intelligent Analysis and Information Systems

title: Multi-Agent Deferred-Decision Trajectory Optimization with Anytime-Valid Target Retention for Moving Candidates
abstract: We study multi-agent terminal interception when one of several moving candidates is the unknown target and both target identity and candidate terminal locations are uncertain. We develop a receding-horizon deferred-decision trajectory optimization (DDTO) controller that combines conformal terminal-location prediction, sequential candidate rejection, capacity-constrained assignment, and candidate-contingent planning. Under exchangeability conditions for terminal and identity residuals, with predictable querying, we establish fixed-time terminal-location coverage and anytime-valid target retenti

title: MetaExp: Learning to Self-Improve through Experience via Verifiable Cross-Task Environment Scaling
abstract: Language-model agents can accumulate interaction feedback, but reliably turning that feedback into reusable experience remains challenging. Existing methods either optimize external experience scaffolds or train experience-related behavior on specific task distributions, leaving open whether experience learning itself can become a transferable model capability. Training such a capability calls for supervision beyond isolated tasks, which mainly support in-episode problem solving rather than revealing what knowledge remains useful across episodes. In this work, we introduce MetaExp, a scalable

title: Closing the Loop on Contrail Avoidance with Satellite Verification
abstract: Contrails are the thin ice clouds that aircraft leave behind. They cause a large share of aviation's warming, and rerouting the few flights that produce them could avoid much of it. However, an avoided contrail only counts if a satellite can confirm that it never formed, and this check is hard: contrails are one to two pixels wide, cover only 0.18% of pixels, and look very similar to natural cirrus. We build a small diffusion model (8.4M parameters, trained on one GPU) that detects them, and we run a controlled study to find out which components matter. The model reaches 0.476 PR-AUC, compared

title: JockeyBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Horse-Racing Decision-Making
abstract: Repeated event forecasting requires extracting predictive signals from noisy evidence and evaluating their value across successive decisions. We introduce JockeyBench, a benchmark and evaluation protocol that studies this problem through historical Japanese horse racing. The protocol combines time-gated evidence, priced tools, paired frozen-program controls, and two workflows: executing an LLM-written predictor or acquiring evidence for a fresh per-race LLM forecast. Evaluation separates forecast quality, benchmark-specific net utility, and retrospective betting returns and risk under fixed de
institutions: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

title: Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards
abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) and on-policy distillation (OPD) have become two main paradigms for post-training reasoning models. RLVR gives each response a single outcome label, leaving the steps inside it without separate credit. OPD provides token-level guidance at student-visited prefixes, but its pointwise signal does not directly reflect the pattern of teacher--student disagreement across the vocabulary.
