title: Recursive Reward Improvement via Adversarial Meta-Prompt Evolution
abstract: Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) has gained wide attention for its ability to work with limited data. In a proposer-solver loop, a proposer model writes training tasks and a solver model learns to solve them through reinforcement learning. Such loops have succeeded in mathematics and coding, where every answer can be checked automatically. Open-ended expert tasks, like clinical report generations, have no answer key, which makes simple question-answer generation not viable. Here the proposer must also write a rubric that lists the content an answer should include and the errors it should avoid

title: Model What Matters: Decision-Guided Selective World Modeling for Language Agents
abstract: Reinforcement learning provides a direct mechanism for optimizing task objectives in large language model-driven agents, but task rewards are typically sparse trajectory-level signals that only evaluate task success, without directly supervising action-conditioned environment transitions, leaving the model with limited explicit understanding of action consequences and environment dynamics. title: Transforming Image Editors into Video Editors
abstract: Recent image editing systems have achieved impressive semantic understanding, visual fidelity, and instruction-following ability, while video editing remains substantially more difficult and costly. In this paper, we present a simple alternative to end-to-end video editing: instead of training a monolithic video editor, we transform a strong image editor into a video editor through anchor-based generation. title: What powers the most energetic flares in the Kepler field? Revisiting the superflaring star KIC 2852961
abstract: Flare activity in red giants is quite common when continuously monitored with high-precision space photometry. In fact, the most powerful flares, also known as "superflares" have been observed on red giant stars. KIC 2852961 is a red giant star producing the highest-energy flares in the Kepler field, and is also known for its large-amplitude starspot-induced light variations. Our goal is to find out what causes the extreme flare activity and flare energies in this star. title: Recovering Software Architecture Intent from Historical Work Items using Generative AI: A Mixed-Methods Industry Case Study
abstract: Software architecture is often only partially captured in code, while much of the design intent lives in evolving project artifacts. In agile projects, work items, user stories, and related tracking documents preserve valuable traces of that intent, but they rarely support direct architectural analysis. This work investigates the recovery of C4 architecture diagrams from historical agile work items using an LLM-based pipeline. title: nCTEQ26 nuclear parton distribution functions
abstract: We present the new release of nuclear parton distribution functions (nPDFs) from the nCTEQ collaboration: nCTEQ26. In this global analysis, we combine our recent, more selective studies of different experimental measurements and extend them to determine a modern set of nPDFs based on the largest selection of data considered to date. This selection includes neutral- and charged-current deep-inelastic scattering (DIS), fixed-target Drell-Yan, and a large variety of collider data from RHIC and LHC Runs I and II. title: Recovering from Pose-Selection Failures in Repeated Visual Localization
abstract: Repetitive structures can give an incorrect pose candidate more inlier support than an accurate one, causing visual localization to select it. History-Guided Pose Reselection (HPR) uses coarse position forecasts from up to five past localization outputs to distinguish well-separated current-query candidates. The best-fitting forecast proposes an alternative; HPR accepts it only if every well-fitting forecast is much closer to it than to the localizer's pose. title: Scaling Agentic Data for Long-Horizon Terminal Intelligence
abstract: Terminal agents are moving beyond local operations toward completing real-world professional tasks. Short trajectories can demonstrate commands and tool calls, but they do not fully show how agents accumulate evidence through exploration, use it to inform judgments, continually adjust strategies based on feedback, and turn intermediate results into final deliverables. High-quality long-horizon trajectories capture these agentic behavioral patterns and their connections within a single problem-solving process, providing richer experience for sustained autonomous work. title: Fast Analytical Method for Resource Adequacy Assessment in Renewable-Rich Power Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel analytical method for resource adequacy assessment in renewable rich power systems. The approach begins by applying the stress strength method to estimate two key resource adequacy indices: loss of load expectation (LOLE) and expected energy not supplied (EENS). title: A kernel-independent precorrected-FFT method
abstract: The precorrected-FFT has been used to rapidly evaluate $N$-body sums arising in electromagnetics and acoustics settings. It has, however, been historically limited to kernels that satisfy a Green's identity. In this work, we demonstrate that, using an improved version of the method of proxy points, the precorrected-FFT can be used to efficiently compute $N$-body sums with a wide variety of kernels. title: Goldsmith: Gold-Loss-Guided Definition Optimization with an Agentic Annotation Harness
abstract: Many annotation projects begin before experts have a stable guideline or enough labels to train a task-specific model. We present Goldsmith, an agentic pipeline that turns a small gold set---expert-annotated calibration examples representing the intended task boundaries---into a reusable structured annotation definition. title: Landau Theory for Non-relativistic Magnetism Beyond Altermagnetism
abstract: In this work we study phenomenological Landau theories of non-relativistic magnetic systems, generalizing work on the collinear case to coplanar and non-coplanar orders. Focusing on zero-wavevector ($\boldsymbol{k}=0$) magnetic orders described by a single irreducible representation of the crystallographic point group, we construct the symmetry-allowed free energies to quartic order for all possible multi-dimensional irreducible ordering channels. title: Beyond Anonymous Captions: Grounding Character Identity in Video Captioning and Question Answering
abstract: Linking people's appearance and actions to character identities is essential for understanding video narratives. We present a framework for identity-aware video captioning and person-centric question answering that combines automatic character identification, explicit spatial grounding, and task-specific adaptation. title: KoAGE: Do Large Language Models Know, Learn, and Coin Korean Neologisms?
abstract: Korean neologisms arise through diverse mechanisms, a demanding test of language models beyond lexical memorization. To enable systematic evaluation, we introduce NeoTrace, an automated, rerunnable framework that collects and dates neologisms across genres. Its 4,271 entries support KoAGE, a cutoff-aware benchmark with three acquisition and two generation tasks---the latter, to our knowledge, the first to compare model coinages with attested neologisms under their original materials and community context. title: Can LLMs Anticipate Their Cruxes?
abstract: To use language models to help us make decisions we would like to understand the rationale behind the language model's outputs. In principle, the language model provides its rationale as part of its text output. However, the sheer volume of text makes this hard to use in practice. In this paper, we are interested in extracting the cruxes that lead a model to recommend one action over another. title: Google Earth AI Geospatial Reasoning Agent: Capabilities and a Systematic Evaluation
abstract: Google Earth AI is a family of geospatial AI models, together with an agent that orchestrates them. We present this agent, Google Earth AI's Geospatial Reasoning agent (GRA), a Gemini-powered research system that combines geospatial data sources, foundation models, and tools to answer questions about our planet. GRA organizes these into modular domain skills and pairs them with upfront geospatial planning to decompose complex queries into multi-stage workflows. title: A Master-to-Simulation Interface with Demonstration-Trajectory Guidance for Vascular Intervention
abstract: Robotic vascular intervention can reduce radiation exposure to physicians and improve manipulation stability, but effective guidance remains challenging because conventional fluoroscopic images provide limited spatial information. This paper developed a vascular intervention interactive system that connects a real robotic master controller with the SOFA(Simulation Open Framework Architecture) physical simulation platform and reused successful operation trajectories as visual guidance in physical phantom experiments. title: The Geographic Moran Effect: Theory, Methods, and Interpretation
abstract: The Moran effect traditionally refers to the synchronization of population dynamics driven by shared environmental forcing rather than direct interactions among populations. Although extensively studied in ecology, the Moran effect has received limited attention in geography, and its applicability has yet to be fully explored. title: IsoVRBench: Video Reward Modeling Without Human Feedback
abstract: Video reward models are trained and evaluated on human preferences between videos that often differ simultaneously on properties such as prompt alignment, visual fidelity, motion, and generator identity. As a result, aggregate accuracy does not reveal which video properties a reward model can reliably distinguish. We construct preference pairs by controlled interventions that change one property of a generated video while holding the rest fixed. title: Thinking Outside the Bots: Human Ideas in AI's Semantic Blind Spots Are Not Inferior
abstract: AI-generated outputs are frequently perceived as highly creative, but also tend to be more similar to each other (homogenized) than human ideas. Does the human heterogeneity that extends beyond AI reflect valuable thinking that AI misses? Alternatively, is greater human heterogeneity driven by lower-quality ideas and less effective thinking that AI avoids? title: Sharper bounds on the thresholds for sensitive and Blackwell optimality
abstract: In perfect-information two-player stochastic games, the notions of Blackwell and sensitive optimality provide generalizations of the classical mean-payoff optimality and discount optimality criteria to account for more farsighted preferences. We provide bounds on the Blackwell threshold $α_{\sf bw}$ and the $d$-sensitive thresholds $α_{\sf d}$, defined as the smallest discount factors above which discount optimal policies coincide with Blackwell optimal policies and $d$-sensitive optimal policies respectively. title: PHRBench: A Behavioral Evaluation of Post-Hallucination Reasoning in LLMs
abstract: Hallucinated information can propagate through multi-stage LLM systems and become part of the context for subsequent reasoning. Existing studies of post-hallucination reasoning (PHR) mainly characterize changes in final outcomes and aggregate reasoning dynamics, leaving how models resolve hallucinated premises at the response level insufficiently understood. title: The Multilingual Artificial Hivemind: Do All LLMs Think Alike in Every Language?
abstract: Text generated by Large Language Models (LLMs) often remains limited in diversity compared to that produced by humans. Recent advances demonstrate the presence of inter- and intra-model collapse in open-ended generation of English text, raising concerns about the long-term homogenization of LLM, and more importantly, human thought. title: MMTA: Benchmarking Multimodal Temporal Analysis with Time Series, Text, and Vision
abstract: Time-series analysis is increasingly studied in multimodal settings, yet most benchmarks pair temporal signals with text or with visualizations derived from the same signal. This leaves open whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can integrate time series with real-world visual evidence. We introduce MMTA (multimodal temporal analysis), a benchmark of tri-modal tasks with diverse cross-modal complementarity patterns among time series, text, and vision. title: Tracking High-Impact Researchers Through Highly Cited Tails
abstract: It is well recognised that field weighted citations are approximately lognormally distributed. This skewness reflects competition for attention, whereby most publications are gradually forgotten and only a minority continue to be recalled years later. Exploiting this observation, we construct a researcher-level indicator based on authorship of top 10% cited papers in All Science Journal Code (ASJC) bins and apply it to publications affiliated with Irish institutions over a typical funding cycle. title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness
abstract: Foundation models are driving a paradigm shift in robotic intelligence, moving beyond low-level action prediction to goal-directed orchestration of data collection, model training, task planning, and real-world execution. We characterize this emerging paradigm as an agentic robots, in which agents reason over human instructions, interact with robotic environments, rectify execution errors autonomously, and dynamically adjust operational strategies. title: Deception by Omission: Language Models Knowingly Hide Their Mistakes
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly act as agents with little human oversight, so potential mistakes they make can go unnoticed. Users then depend on the model to report what went wrong. An honest model discloses its mistakes, while a deceptive one conceals them. However, it is unclear how current LLMs behave in such situations. In this study, we prefill LLM trajectories with synthetic mistakes. abstract: Hurricanes severely impact coastal communities, disrupting social and economic systems and causing widespread physical damage. Rapid post-disaster assessment is essential for effective response, yet traditional on-site evaluations are slow and resource intensive. Advances in machine learning offer faster, automated alternatives by leveraging historical disaster data to predict damage in near real time. abstract: The talk argues that ocean observatories and regional Digital Twins of the Ocean (DTOs) are ideal ecosystems for a real transformation in ocean science, provided organisational change accompanies them. abstract: The current work seeks to identify the most critical wave properties that may influence the performance of Wave Energy Converters (WECs) operating near several European marine sites. abstract: Wide-area maritime monitoring of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) interference remains challenging because dedicated radio-frequency sensing infrastructure is often sparse, costly, or unavailable in open-sea environment. abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated into everyday life, there is a growing need to develop not only technical skills among lower secondary school pupils, but above all an understanding of how AI works and the ability to use it critically and effectively. title: Sovereignty Theater: Why Sovereign AI Falls Short of Cultural Self-Determination
abstract: Sovereign AI has emerged as a major policy movement, with nearly 130 government-backed initiatives across more than 50 countries justified in part by the promise of cultural and linguistic self-determination. States seek national AI systems that reflect local languages, values, and knowledge traditions rather than importing the assumptions of foreign technology providers. title: From Maritime Regulations to Verifiable Properties with LLM Assistance
abstract: Abstract Maritime automation requires formal safety assurances that simulation alone cannot provide. The International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea (COLREGs) are expressed in natural language, while Legata provides a structured domain-specific language for encoding these regulations. We propose a method for translating Legata specifications into logical properties that can be verified against an actor-based model using model checking. title: Explaining Time Series Classifications Counterfactually: A Human-Centered Evaluation
abstract: Counterfactual explanations can promote accountability, fairness, and transparency in AI-supported decision-making by demonstrating how changes in input data can alter outcomes, offering actionable feedback for users to revise unfavorable decisions. However, the majority of counterfactual algorithms focus on tabular and image data, ignoring many high-stakes scenarios that rely on time series data. title: Photoplethysmography and vital sign measurement using 3D-multispectral multimodal imaging
abstract: Contactless vital-sign monitoring can improve comfort and hygiene in long-term, sleep, home, and clinical monitoring, but robust estimation of heart rate (HR), respiratory rate (RR), and oxygen saturation (SpO2) remains a coupled sensing and algorithmic problem. This paper summarizes our research line on remote photoplethysmography and vital sign measurement using 3D-multispectral multimodal imaging. title: Self-Discovering Security Oracles: Meta-learning Vulnerability Detection Strategies through Adversarial Self-Play
abstract: Current LLM-based vulnerability detection systems rely on static prompting strategies and fixed analysis pipelines, which fail to adapt to an evolving threat landscape. These approaches struggle to discover unknown vulnerability patterns beyond their training distributions, limiting their effectiveness against emerging security threats. This paper investigates adversarial meta-learning as a way for foundation models to autonomously discover vulnerability detection strategies through reinforcement learning and competitive self-play. title: The Future of Offshore Structural Integrity Management: Evolution, Insights, and Implications of ISO 19901-9, 2nd Edition
abstract: Abstract The Oil and Gas industries, including the lower carbon energy sector, are presently facing significant challenges in managing integrity of aging offshore structures due to increasing costs and reduced revenue due to depleting reservoirs, while also contending with AI led disruption. The 2nd edition of ISO 19901-9 – Structural Integrity Management (SIM) of Fixed Offshore Structures (hereinafter STANDARD), which will be published by 2028, will introduce major changes in code requirements relating to facility Fitness-for-Service assessment, life extension and repurposing for renewable se

title: Ranking Cocoa Land Suitability Growth Requirements with Random Forest for a Spatial Decision-Support Platform
abstract: Cocoa-growing land in Indonesia has steadily declined, increasing import dependence. An earlier study developed a web-based geographic information system (GIS) platform using Spatial ID3 to classify cocoa land suitability in Bogor Regency from eight soil and topographic variables, but it could not identify which variables most strongly influenced the resulting classes. This study extends it by using Random Forest to rank the eight variables by their contribution to the suitability decision. title: Thermodynamic Screening of Solvents for Ternary Cellulose Acetate Blend Membranes Using Hansen Solubility Parameters
abstract: Solvent selection for phase inversion membranes still relies mostly on trial and error, even though the solvent governs how well a polymer blend forms into a stable, separation-capable structure. Few studies quantify that relationship before casting. This study calculates Hansen Solubility Parameters (HSP) for a ternary blend of Cellulose Acetate (CA), Polyethylene Glycol (PEG), and Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) against six candidate organic solvents, with water as the nonsolvent, to test whether thermodynamic distance can predict membrane morphology ahead of fabrication. title: Evaluating Spectral Consistency of Fe-Related Wavelength Ranges between EO-1 Hyperion and Field Spectrometer Data in the Kulon Progo Iron Sand Deposit
abstract: Iron sand deposits contain Fe-bearing oxide minerals with characteristic reflectance features, but field spectrometer and hyperspectral image measurements of these features do not always agree, owing to differences in sensor characteristics, observation scale, and surface conditions. This study evaluates the spectral consistency between ASD FieldSpec and EO-1 Hyperion reflectance over the Kulon Progo iron sand deposit, and examines how spectral processing and spatial representation affect that consistency. title: EnergyTrackr: A Modular Energy Regressions Detection Tool
abstract: Energy efficiency is increasingly recognized as an important dimension of software quality. As systems evolve rapidly, tracking how energy consumption changes across versions can provide valuable insights for developers and researchers. Although detecting energy regressions (i.e., unintended increases in energy consumption) remains challenging due to measurement variability and complex execution environments, recent advances now make systematic analysis practical. title: PCodeTrans: Translate Decompiled Pseudocode to Trace-Level Equivalent Source Code
abstract: Decompilation remains foundational for binary analysis, yet conventional tools prioritize human readability over compilation success and test-validated runtime consistency. While recent large language model approaches attempt refining decompiled pseudocode, they often introduce semantic hallucinations. Operating statically without dynamic feedback or attempting whole binary repairs lacking scalability, these existing methods struggle to resolve genuine runtime divergences. journal: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE)

title: Statistical Model Checking in 2026: Simulation, Learning, and Exhaustive Verification
abstract: Abstract Statistical model checking (SMC) analyses stochastic models by simulation: it samples many runs, evaluates the property of interest on each of them, and returns an estimate together with a statistical guarantee. It only needs the ability to draw runs from a model or system, which makes it widely applicable—at the cost of statistical instead of hard guarantees. Yet rare events, unbounded properties, and nondeterminism remain hard for simulation alone. In 2026, SMC is therefore practised as simulation, learning, and exhaustive verification working together. title: Landslide Susceptibility Mapping Using GIS-Based Analytical Hierarchy Process in Pejawaran District, Banjarnegara
abstract: Landslide susceptibility mapping is an important tool for identifying relatively unstable zones and facilitating disaster mitigation and land-use planning. This study assesses landslide susceptibility in Pejawaran District, Banjarnegara, Central Java, Indonesia, using a GIS-based Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP). Six conditioning factors were integrated: distance to road, normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), distance to stream, lithology, elevation, and slope. title: Ontology-Enriched GraphRAG: A Case Study in Portuguese Geoscience Question Answering
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) significantly enhances Large Language Models (LLMs) in Question-Answering (QA) tasks. However, traditional text-based retrieval may prove insufficient in specialized domains, such as geoscience, where critical information is highly interconnected and distributed across complex concepts, relations, and interpretative descriptions. title: Metrologically guided evaluation framework for walking robots in forestry environments
abstract: Due to complex, unstructured, and dynamic environmental conditions, the automation of forestry work processes is limited. The kinematic architecture, and typical industrial and forestry applications of commercially available walking robots, has been reviewed, and a catalog of requirements for use in forestry has been derived. To date, there are no standardized evaluation and measurement methods for natural terrain. title: Resampling in Importance Splitting Rare Event Simulation: n-th Time’s the Charm
abstract: Abstract Importance splitting (ISPLIT) is a robust variance reduction technique that estimates the probability of rare events by decomposing the problem into a sequence of nested, easier subproblems. By partitioning the state space into regions by means of an importance function (IFUN), ISPLIT selectively clones trajectories that reach high importance layers, significantly outperforming standard Monte Carlo simulation while introducing dependencies among trajectories. title: Subseasonal forecast improvements from sea ice concentration data assimilation in the Antarctic
abstract: Abstract. This study evaluates the impact of sea ice concentration (SIC) data assimilation (DA) on subseasonal forecasts of Antarctic sea ice by comparing reforecast experiment suites initialized from two sets of initial conditions (ICs): one with SIC DA and the other without. The two ICs are evaluated against NSIDC SIC observations. Results show that the SIC DA significantly improves the climatology and interannual variability of the SIC IC. title: Can Cybernetic Twins Function as Regulators for Sustainable (Sea)Food Systems?
abstract: Feeding the growing global population without permanently overshooting local-to-planetary boundaries demands a transition from conventional resource extraction to holistic models. Current digital twin applications in (sea)food systems primarily emphasize predictive monitoring and decision support, whereas their integration with heterogeneous socio-economic-ecological systems (SEES) remains incomplete. title: Leveraging Digital Twins for Bridge Maintenance Prioritization following Coastal Flood Events
abstract: Abstract Bridges are critical to the US transportation network and are essential components of our infrastructure systems. Coastal floods can disrupt these structures, isolating communities and highlighting the urgent need for effective maintenance and prioritization strategies. This study introduces a digital twin framework that evaluates the impacts of coastal floods on bridge substructures by integrating multisource data and employing spatial algorithms like inverse distance weighting and k - d tree methods to model flood severity. title: A Digital Twin Framework for Monitoring and Fault Identification of Marine Internal Combustion Engines
abstract: Monitoring the current technical condition of a marine internal combustion engine and diagnosing the causes of deviations of its operating parameters from reference values are important tasks for ensuring the efficient and safe operation of marine power plants and vessels in general. This study develops a digital twin framework for marine engine diagnostics and demonstrates its integration with the DEPAS 5.0W diagnostic system. title: Uncertainty-aware digital twin-driven fault-tolerant control for autonomous underwater vehicles using temporal fusion transformer-based fault diagnosis
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) operate in challenging marine environments. The actuator faults, propulsion degradation and environmental disturbances can significantly compromise mission safety and tracking performance. Existing studies have primarily focused on either fault diagnosis or fault-tolerant control as separate tasks. A limited attention has been given to integrating fault diagnosis, predictive digital twins and uncertainty-aware control within a unified framework. title: Hydrodynamic Modeling of Maximum Tidal Levels at the Tondano River Estuary
abstract: The Tondano River Estuary is an area affected by the interaction of tides, currents, winds, and bathymetric conditions that affect sea level and hydrodynamic conditions of the coastal area. This study aims to analyze the maximum tidal height at the Tondano River Estuary using the MIKE 21 Flow Model (FM). title: Sea-level contribution from Thwaites Glacier doubles in an observation-constrained ice-sheet model
abstract: Thwaites Glacier is a major contributor to Antarctic mass loss and a key source of uncertainty in future sea-level rise. Ocean-driven melting at its grounding line drives rapid retreat, yet most models treat the transition between grounded and floating ice as a sharp boundary, neglecting kilometer-scale seawater intrusions that develop as the grounding line migrates and forms a grounding zone. title: Quantum authentication framework for digital twin–driven satellite networks
abstract: Abstract The integration of digital twin technology into large-scale Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations introduces critical security challenges, particularly under emerging quantum threats. This paper proposes a quantum-assisted multi-layer authentication framework for satellite–digital twin communication that combines entanglement-based verification with hardware-rooted identity using Quantum Physical Unclonable Functions (QPUFs). title: Comparison of Direct and Telescopic Grid Nesting in a High-Resolution Operational Ocean Model
abstract: High-resolution regional ocean models are typically nested within coarser parent models, with resolution ratios limited to avoid spurious artefacts. Consequently, a telescopic grid-nesting strategy is commonly adopted for very high-resolution applications by introducing one or more models of intermediate resolution. However, such an approach is complex and computationally expensive. title: Differential Impacts of Proxy Archives on Paleoclimate Reconstruction Performance
abstract: Abstract Reconstructing past climates is challenging because pre‐instrumental observations are geographically sparse and proxy records are noisy; data assimilation offers one approach to address these limitations. Although such reconstructions are now widespread, the extent to which different proxy archives determine their accuracy remains unclear. abstract: Abstract. Accurately representing abyssal water masses and their inter-basin pathways remains a challenge for global ocean models and reanalyses. In this study, we investigate how horizontal and vertical resolution influence the simulation of abyssal waters by first evaluating three ocean reanalyses and one forward ocean model, focusing on Antarctic Bottom Water pathways from the Weddell Sea to the Argentine and Brazil basins and through the Vema Channel. abstract: Abstract Antarctic sea ice has declined since 2015, but placing this trend in a longer‐term context remains challenging. Ice core methanesulfonic acid (MSA) offers a potential record of sea ice variability beyond the instrumental period, yet its applicability in sectors including the Weddell Sea remains unclear. abstract: Abstract. The Ross Sea, Antarctica, is among the most seasonally productive areas globally, where different classes of phytoplankton, such as diatoms and haptophytes (Phaeocystis antarctica), play key roles in marine ecosystems and the carbon cycle. Sea ice dynamics strongly influence Ross Sea phytoplankton blooms, yet the effects of recent sea ice changes on bloom composition and productivity remain poorly constrained. abstract: Abstract. Antarctic sea-ice cover reached historically low levels in 2023, consistent with the simulated decrease in sea-ice extent in response to anthropogenic warming. Antarctic sea ice is closely linked to multiple components of the Earth system, thus its demise could precipitate widespread, cascading changes across the cryosphere, atmosphere, and ocean. title: Compound marine heatwaves and atmospheric boundary layer jets drive enhanced coastal precipitation
abstract: Heavy coastal precipitation is traditionally attributed to atmospheric dynamics, but the influence of co-occurring oceanic thermal extremes remains largely unexplored. Using satellite observations and reanalysis data from 1998 to 2023 over the South China Sea (SCS), we investigate the synergistic impacts of marine heatwaves (MHWs) and atmospheric boundary layer jets (BLJs). title: Quantifying Deep Ocean Methane Along the Central Chilean Margin
abstract: Abstract Cold seeps are dynamic seafloor environments that provide conduits for methane (CH 4 ) to be transferred from marine sediments to the global ocean and, in shallow settings, the atmosphere. These seeps are ubiquitous along continental margins yet their spatial extent and impact on the marine carbon cycle are poorly constrained. abstract: Abstract Previous studies have documented long-term changes in Antarctic sea ice extent and its interannual variability. However, spatial patterns of trends in the interannual variability of Antarctic sea ice concentration (SIC) and the mechanisms responsible for these changes remain poorly understood. Using satellite-derived SIC observations for 1979–2024 and a wavelet-based measure of interannual variance, we investigate changes in wintertime (July–September) SIC variability across the Southern Ocean. title: Palaeoclimate constraints narrow uncertainty in future Arctic winter sea ice projections
abstract: Abstract Arctic sea ice decline has been observed across all seasons and is projected to continue in the future. Relative to historical observations, climate models show their largest biases and uncertainties during winter, when ice cover strongly regulates air–sea heat exchange, ocean mixing and atmospheric circulation. abstract: Warming of the upper ocean is expected to strengthen stratification and reduce the efficiency of wind-driven mixing, affecting water-column stability, nutrient supply, biological productivity, and oxygen ventilation. Despite its importance in the climate system and its rapid change, long-term observations of water column stratification remain limited in the Mediterranean Sea. abstract: As Earth system science moves toward global-domain and multi-sphere coupling, traditional two-dimensional spatial information frameworks can no longer fully meet the integrated spatial computing demands of deep space, deep Earth, and deep ocean applications. abstract: The ambition to model the Earth at a 1:1 scale through planetary computing presents a challenge that transcends technical constraints. At planetary scale, this challenge becomes an epistemological dilemma: the tension between metric fidelity and morphological coherence. abstract: Abstract. The vertical distribution of distinct aerosol components fundamentally governs atmospheric shortwave heating rates and radiative effects. title: Modeling Nutrient Concentrations in a Greenhouse Cascade Soilless System
abstract: A dynamic simulation model was developed and calibrated to predict nutrient concentrations in a three-level cascade hydroponic system (CasH). The performance of the model was evaluated across donor/primary (tomato) and receiver secondary (mint, peppermint), and tertiary (sea fennel, lemon balm) crops. abstract: Coral reefs are one of the most biologically diverse ecosystems in the ocean, but are now under increasing threat from climate related ocean warming. While numerous studies have focused on the impact of sea surface temperature (SST) on coral reef condition, those that specifically looked into whether long-term background SST variability had an impact on reef stability have had conflicting results, with some analyses showing negligible association and others showing significant associations. abstract: The development of approaches that can autonomously fill and heal material voids and yield composites with tailorable properties is increasingly relevant in engineering. abstract: Abstract The intensified interannual variability of September rainfall in Central China has led to increasingly frequent and devastating hydrological disasters over the past two decades. This study identifies the accelerated retreat of August Laptev Sea ice since 2005 as a critical, previously unrecognized precursor for September precipitation in Central China. title: Modelling the Western Black Sea river-sea continuum
abstract: This study introduces a model chain extending from river catchment to sea, covering the Western Black Sea (WBS), with the objective of developing a suitable tool to investigate land-sea interaction and coastal processes. abstract: Abstract Marine heatwaves are increasing in frequency and intensity globally against a background of long-term climate warming, yet their impacts on subsurface biogeochemistry in temperate shelf seas remain poorly constrained. abstract: Abstract The zenith total delay (ZTD) retrieved from 5G communication base stations represents a novel observation source for numerical weather prediction (NWP), leveraging the extensive global deployment of 5G infrastructure. abstract: Abstract We present a robust, global method to reconcile absolute water surface elevations (WSE) from the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission with a large‐scale hydrodynamic model by iteratively correcting river bathymetry. abstract: Abstract Atmospheric boundary layer height (ABLH) plays an important role in air–sea interactions and regional climate over the western North Pacific (WNP). abstract: Abstract Coastal decadal sea level anomalies (SLAs) in the U.S. east coast (USEC) play a critical role in modulating coastal flooding frequency, yet relative influences of tropical versus extratropical climate modes over the North Atlantic remain unresolved. title: Integrated retrieval of ocean surface wind and current fields from single-geometry SAR observations through a physically constrained Bayesian framework
abstract: Ocean surface winds and currents are coupled through air–sea interaction but are commonly retrieved independently from spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR). For operational single-geometry SAR, simultaneous wind–current retrieval is underdetermined and remains reliant on background information. abstract: Abstract A combination of model simulations and field observations collected in 2023 and 2024 near Seagreen, Scotland’s largest Offshore Wind Farm (OWF), is used to assess when, where and by how much (physical) changes induced by OWFs structures become detectable and environmentally relevant. abstract: Coastal caves developed in weak and heterogeneous cliffs constitute complex geomechanical systems in which lithological variability, structural discontinuities, groundwater seepage and marine erosion interact. Their stability assessment is particularly challenging in urbanised coastal and touristic attractive environments, where local failures may affect infrastructure and public safety. abstract: Abstract The mechanical behavior of natural gas hydrate-bearing sediments (HBS) is critical for safe and efficient gas production. abstract: Abstract Quantifying microbial cell abundance in natural environments with taxonomic resolution remains a central challenge in microbial ecology. While epifluorescence microscopy reliably enumerates free-living cells, it lacks taxonomic specificity and is less suitable for quantifying cells in sediments, soils, and on surfaces. title: The development and persistence of doldrums over the Great Barrier Reef
abstract: Abstract. Marine heatwaves and coral bleaching pose significant threats to the Great Barrier Reef (GBR), particularly during austral summer when atmospheric conditions can significantly enhance ocean surface warming. One such condition is the development of doldrums, characterised by weak winds and reduced cloud cover, which promote increased solar heating of the ocean surface. abstract: Abstract Three decades of satellite altimeter observations reveal a continued rise in global mean sea level (GMSL), with the rate of rise reflecting the combined effects of decadal variability and long‐term warming. abstract: Wildfires in eastern Siberia have intensified significantly in recent decades. abstract: Submarine sewage outfalls are widely used to mitigate the impacts of wastewater discharges on coastal recreational waters. abstract: In marine organisms with complex life cycles, the planktonic larval stage is among the most sensitive to environmental variation, affecting dispersal potential in early life. abstract: The East Asian summer front (EASF) plays a key role in regional precipitation and heat stress, yet its long-term positional changes remain poorly understood. abstract: Metocean analyses are fundamental to offshore and coastal engineering, maritime operations, and renewable energy development, where reliable estimates of winds, waves, currents, sea level, and related variables are required for structural design, safety assessment, and operational planning. Although large metocean datasets are increasingly available, analyses are often performed using ad hoc scripts and fragmented workflows, limiting reproducibility, transparency, and efficient knowledge transfer. title: A CFD-based initial framework for screening fixed floating-breakwater configurations for marine aquaculture
abstract: Floating breakwaters are increasingly considered for offshore applications, including marine aquaculture. However, existing studies have primarily focused on wave attenuation, while the potential of different configurations to provide favorable aquaculture environments remains insufficiently explored. This article aims to: (i) compare the hydrodynamic performance of various fixed floating breakwaters, including box-type, plate-attached, π-type, and hybrid systems, with a consistent width ( B f ) and configuration-dependent draft ( D f ); and (ii) propose an initial framework for their aquacult

title: Shipborne Measurements of Mineral Dust and Black Carbon Aerosols Over the Southern Ocean in the Austral Summer
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric mineral dust and black carbon (BC) aerosols play important roles in the Earth's climate system, yet direct observations over the Southern Ocean (SO) are scarce. In this study, we present the characteristics of airborne water‐insoluble particles (WIPs) collected during a cruise of the R/V Shirase in the Australian and Indian sectors of the SO from December 2022 to March 2023. Using a complex amplitude sensor, we measured complex scattering amplitude of individual WIPs to classify into dust‐like (0.50–2.5 μm in diameter) and BC‐like (0.15–0.50 μm in diameter) particles. title: Genetic isolation and loss of diversity in the broadcast spawning coral, Acropora kenti at Yunbenun (Magnetic Island) on the Great Barrier Reef
abstract: Abstract Coral populations on inshore reefs of the Great Barrier Reef (GBR) face increasing pressures from environmental stressors. Genetic diversity and connectivity are key determinants of coral adaptive capacity. Acropora kenti forms at least four genetically distinct clusters distributed across hundreds of kilometres along the GBR. One cluster which is potentially vulnerable due to restricted geographic distribution is found at Yunbenun (Magnetic Island). title: Wolf predation as a regulator of the state of island populations of wild reindeer in the early 21st century
abstract: The relationship between the wolf and the wild reindeer in the Arctic has always been a focal point for researchers and northern Indigenous communities. This predator species continues to exert significant influence on wild reindeer and caribou inhabiting remote island territories, and adjacent mainland coastal areas in the 21st century. However, warming in the Arctic is leading to profound changes in the established principles governing the formation and functioning of both reindeer and wolf populations. title: Boundary‐Aware Separation of Vortical and Wavy Motions in the Ocean
abstract: Abstract With the recent popularity of the tide‐resolving and submesoscale‐admitting numerical simulations, there is an increasing interest in separating vortical and wavy motions in the ocean. The recently‐proposed dynamics‐based decomposition exploits the relative magnitude of the relative vorticity and horizontal divergence in Fourier space and proves efficient. In this decomposition, physical variables over non‐water regions (e.g., coasts, islands, seamounts) are filled with zeros following standard practice. title: Offshore Freshened Groundwater Distribution Is Controlled by Along‐ and Cross‐Shore Topographic Variability
abstract: Abstract Offshore Freshened Groundwater (OFG) reservoirs are regarded as a potentially significant resource stored in continental shelves. While the role of subsurface geological conditions in controlling OFG has been widely recognized, the influence of the topography of the hosting continental shelf on OFG evolution remains poorly understood. Here, using generalized numerical modeling representative of a broad range of systems worldwide, we evaluate how the shelf slope affects the evolution of OFG in subsea aquifers, considering sea‐level rise over paleohydrogeological timescales. title: An operational wind-speed-dependent quadratic bias correction for Voluntary Observing Ship wind measurements evaluated against moored buoys and ERA5 reanalysis
abstract: Abstract Voluntary Observing Ship (VOS) wind reports constitute one of the densest marine in situ datasets, yet they carry a persistent, wind-speed-dependent negative bias that intensifies at low wind speeds. Using 18,957 collocated ship–buoy–ERA5 records over the nearshore waters of China, we diagnose this bias against two complementary references, a moored-buoy network and ERA5 reanalysis, and construct a correction that is deployable in practice: a three-parameter quadratic in the observed VOS wind speed itself, requiring no reference information at application time. title: Wind impacts on salinity and stratification in the Persian Gulf and on water exchange through the Strait of Hormuz
abstract: Abstract The Persian Gulf (PG) is a pronounced inverse estuary characterized by strong evaporation, hypersaline waters, and a reversed asymmetry in water exchange through the Strait of Hormuz, where the annual inflowing volume transport exceeds the corresponding outflow. This study uses a high-resolution three-dimensional hydrodynamic model to quantify wind effects on salinity redistribution, stratification, and high-frequency water exchanges. title: A Generalized Analytical Model for Marine Gas Hydrate Stability Zones With Thermodynamically Constrained Pressure–Temperature Phase Boundary
abstract: Abstract Accurate thermodynamic delineation of marine gas hydrate stability zones (GHSZs) is a fundamental prerequisite for assessing methane hydrate inventories, quantifying the vulnerability of methane dissociation to climate change, and evaluating overpressure‐induced submarine geohazards. However, the commonly adopted pressure–temperature phase boundaries are predominantly calibrated under idealized conditions and fail to capture natural marine conditions, leading to persistent uncertainties and systematic biases in global GHSZ delineation. title: Intensification of near-inertial currents in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades
abstract: Near-inertial currents (NICs) play a key role in surface material redistribution and ocean mixing, yet their long-term variability remains poorly known. Using in situ current measurements from surface drifters, we provide observational evidence for a pronounced intensification of surface NICs in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades (2003–2022). Basin–mean NIC strength increases at a rate of 3.8 ± 1.7% per decade, with a spatial pattern characterized by strengthening in the South Atlantic and the high-latitude North Atlantic, and weakening in the low-latitude North Atlantic. title: Wave-induced coupled dynamics of an OTEC spar platform with cold water pipe: An experimental investigation
abstract: Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) is a promising renewable energy technology capable of providing continuous baseload power while simultaneously supporting freshwater production and other deep-seawater applications. As a carbon-neutral energy source, OTEC aligns with global Sustainable Development Goals related to clean energy and climate action. However, the commercial deployment of large-scale floating OTEC plant requires a thorough understanding of the coupled hydrodynamic behaviour of the floating platform and the cold water pipe (CWP), a critical component unique to OTEC plants. title: Topographic Modulation of Multi-Source Internal Solitary Waves in a Complex Sea Basin: Nonlinear Dynamics and Energetics
abstract: Abstract Complex basin topography plays a fundamental role in modulating the dynamics and energetics of internal solitary waves (ISWs), yet their three-dimensional mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, a high-resolution non-hydrostatic numerical model is employed to investigate basin topographic modulations of the generation, nonlinear evolution, and energetics of multi-source ISWs in the Sulu Sea basin. title: Flooding with brackish water disrupts Liriodendron tulipifera sap flux in an ecosystem-scale experiment
abstract: Coastal forests are retreating due to sea‑level rise and extreme precipitation events, yet the physiological mechanisms that precede woody plant decline remain poorly constrained. We used the ecosystem‑scale TEMPEST (Terrestrial Ecosystem Manipulation to Probe the Effects of Storm Treatments) experiment; annual, plot‑level freshwater and saltwater flooding of a mid‑Atlantic deciduous forest, to quantify short‑ and long‑term responses of sap flux in three tree species: Acer rubrum, Fagus grandifolia, and Liriodendron tulipifera. title: Meteorological Impact Assessment Software for Maritime Transport in the Western Part of the Black Sea
abstract: Maritime transportation in the western part of the Black Sea is strongly affected by meteorological conditions such as wind, waves, and visibility. This paper presents a software system designed to evaluate and predict these impacts using real-time and historical data. The system integrates data processing, statistical analysis, and predictive models to assess navigational risks and support route optimization. title: Impacts of Sea Surface Temperature Warming Pattern Biases on Tropical Cyclone Activity and Hazard
abstract: Abstract Most climate models simulate greater warming in the equatorial eastern Pacific than in the west under historical forcing, resulting in a reduced zonal sea surface temperature (SST) gradient and a weakened Walker circulation. This contrasts with observed trends and highlights a persistent model–observation discrepancy with far‐reaching impacts on regional climate extremes. The authors' previous work showed that reducing mean‐state biases in a coupled model yields SST trends more consistent with observations. abstract: ABSTRACT Infographic of five tide gauges in southwestern Taiwan, 2004-2025: sea level peaks in August at every station, the seasonal range differs by station, and sea-level rise of 0.5 to 1.0 m adds up to 239 to 345 exceedance days per year. Sea-level rise is expected to increase coastal water-level exceedance, particularly in low-lying and subsidence-prone regions. This study develops a tide-gauge-based diagnostic framework to examine sea-level-rise-sensitive threshold exceedance and adaptation-relevant elevation bands along the southwestern coast of Taiwan. title: Classification of Summer Extratropical Cyclones Over Northeast China and Their Impacts on Regional Precipitation
abstract: Abstract Based on the ERA5 six‐hourly reanalysis data set and objective identification and tracking methods for extratropical cyclones (ECs), this study identified 423 summer ECs that passed through Northeast China (NEC) during 1979–2023. These ECs were categorized into three distinct types using K ‐means clustering based on their genesis locations. We further examined the associated atmospheric circulation patterns and the resulting climatic impacts of each EC type on summer precipitation over NEC. title: Forecasting coastal dune mobility: a logistic regression model driven by meteorological data and climate indices
abstract: Abstract. Predicting dune mobility under changing climatic conditions remains a challenge in aeolian geomorphology, particularly in data-scarce regions. This study presents a novel application of binomial logistic regression to forecast dune activation and migration using readily available meteorological data. We combine established dune mobility indices (Tsoar and Lancaster) into a new integrated index (TsoLa) and evaluate its performance against observed dune migration rates derived from satellite imagery. title: Geomorphic Approach for Beach Downdrift of Fishing Ports and Marinas: Parabolic Model and Software MeePaSoL
abstract: Coastal erosion problems associated with a fishing port or marina on sandy coast are caused by imbalance of longshore sediment transport and bay shape formation on downdrift. Regardless of the availability of littoral transport, the tip of its outer breakwater would behave as an updrift control point for an embayed beach to form, by combined wave diffraction-refraction aided by nearshore current circulation. title: Sea Cucumber‐Inspired Double‐Network Biopolymer Hydrogels for Programmable Soft Machines
abstract: Engineering biopolymer-based hydrogels with robust load-bearing capacity, reversible mechanical programmability, and adaptive actuation remains difficult due to weak physical crosslinking and porous structure. Inspired by the mutable dermis of sea cucumbers, a collagen-alginate double-network elastomeric (CoDE) hydrogel integrates a covalently crosslinked collagen cryogel scaffold with an ionically crosslinked alginate sacrificial network. title: Hybrid Multi‐Gateway Authentication Protocol for 6LoWPAN‐Based Marine Wireless Sensor Networks
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper proposes a secure and efficient three‐factor authentication scheme to address the security issues in the integration scenario of multi‐gateway wireless sensor networks (WSNs) and 6LoWPAN in marine Internet of Things (IoT). Existing approaches exhibit vulnerabilities to cryptographic breaches, single‐point failures, high computational costs, and inefficient long‐distance transmission in maritime settings. title: Rockfall hazard assessment at Baia Castle cliff (Phlegrean Fields, Italy): implications for cultural heritage sites in a seismically active volcanic area
abstract: Coastal cliffs developed in volcanic tuffs are highly susceptible to instability due to the combined effects of structural discontinuities, marine erosion, and seismic activity. This study presents a multi-method assessment of rockfall hazard at the Baia Castle cliff (Phlegrean Fields, southern Italy), an area affected by ongoing bradyseism and with a significant cultural heritage exposure. UAV-based photogrammetry, field structural surveys, and geomechanical characterisation were integrated to reconstruct the geometry and discontinuity network of the cliff. title: Effects of wind-wave misalignment on motion responses of a floating wind turbine with a shared-anchor mooring system
abstract: Wind-wave misalignment significantly affects the dynamic responses of floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs). A fully coupled aero-hydro-mooring numerical model was established in OrcaFlex for a FOWT with a three-line shared-anchor mooring system. The numerical analysis evaluated three representative sea states (LC1, LC2, and LC3) alongside multiple wind-wave heading combinations. title: Wave attenuation by mixed mangroves in hybrid Mangrove–Breakwater systems using a modified Ergun equation
abstract: Coastal hybrid protection schemes integrating mangrove vegetation with vertical impermeable breakwaters can effectively mitigate coastal inundation and seabed erosion triggered by storm surges. Nevertheless, most existing numerical models overlook the vertical stratification of mixed mangrove communities, which leads to systematic underestimation of flow resistance within vegetated coastal zones. title: Regional Trends in Northern Hemisphere Summer Extratropical Cyclone Activity and Their Link to Precipitation and Temperature Trends
abstract: Abstract In recent years a robust weakening of the storm tracks has been identified in reanalysis data. This trend has been linked to coinciding changes in surface temperature extremes and precipitation over land. Here we use a surface‐based metric to quantify regional trends in the boreal summertime low‐level extratropical cyclone activity (ECA) and link this to surface impacts. title: The hydrodynamics of a low-latitude submarine canyon: Implications for circulation pattern and dispersion of suspended particles
abstract: Submarine canyons serve as critical geomorphological conduits regulating continental shelf–slope mass exchange, nutrient fluxes, and benthic sedimentary processes. However, while shelf hydrodynamics and western boundary current (WBC) dynamics are increasingly documented in the South Atlantic, the hydrodynamic mechanisms, topographically induced flows, and particle dispersion patterns within low-latitude submarine canyons—specifically the Natal Canyon on the eastern Brazilian margin—remain fundamentally unexplored. title: Eastward displacement of the Pacific–Japan pattern weakens its influence on summertime tropical cyclones affecting China
abstract: Abstract Tropical cyclones (TCs) affecting China pose a major threat to coastal populations and economies, yet the large-scale climate controls on these TCs may vary over time. Here, we show that the influence of the Pacific–Japan (PJ) pattern on summertime (June‒August) TCs affecting China has weakened markedly since the early-2000s. During 1979–2002, positive PJ phases were associated with significantly more TCs affecting China than negative phases, whereas this contrast largely disappeared during 2003–2025. title: Cultural heritage loss in the face of sea level rise and climate change: perspectives from the Asia-Pacific and Tuvalu
abstract: This article examines the adequacy of legal and policy responses to cultural heritage loss in the face of sea level rise and climate change, focusing on the Asia-Pacific and the case of Tuvalu. It argues that the erosion of cultural heritage reveals a blind spot in climate governance centred on adaptation. Indeed, the loss of cultural heritage and land are deeply intertwined yet not fully addressed in current local actions or international law, with a few timid exceptions. title: Parameter fitting for boulder transport with wave tank experiments
abstract: Coastal boulder deposits provide key evidence for extreme wave activity on rocky shorelines, yet quantitative interpretation of these deposits remains limited by poorly constrained force-balance parameters. We perform parameter fitting for models of coastal boulder transport using data from wave tank experiments to assess how wave impact type and boulder geometry influence hydrodynamic and frictional coefficients. title: Characteristics of the Southern Hemisphere jet streams based on ERA5 data for 2001–2025
abstract: A climatology of the Southern Hemisphere jet streams calculated for the first quarter of the 21st century using ERA5 reanalysis data is presented. An occurrence frequency of jet streams in various regions is investigated, and the seasonal and interannual variabilities of maximum wind characteristics (speed, level height, direction, and layer thickness) are analyzed. Climatological data on jet streams at flight levels intended for air navigation planning are provided.

title: Comparative assessment of gridded precipitation datasets for rainfall climatology, dry spells, and station-based drought indices over the Indonesian Maritime Continent
abstract: The Indonesian Maritime Continent (IMC) is a pivotal component of the global climate system, serving as the world’s primary tropical heat source and a region of intense convective activity. Despite its climatic importance, its complex geography and dependence on the Asian-Australian monsoon make it highly vulnerable to drought, which is further intensified by teleconnections such as El Niño and the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD). abstract: Abstract. This study investigates the hydrodynamic and mixing processes at the estuary–shelf transition of a microtidal system, and the buoyant plume generated at the Patos Lagoon mouth (Brazil). Using measurements of turbulent kinetic energy (TKE) dissipation (ϵ), current velocities, salinity, and temperature collected during a high-discharge period (∼9,400 m³ s-1), we characterize the spatial evolution of turbulence and mixing along the channel, from the source to the buoyancy-driven plume region. title: Examining Correlation Structures of Planetary Boundary Layer Height using Large Global Ensembles
abstract: Abstract A proper localization length scale is critical for the success of ensemble-based data assimilation techniques to reduce spurious, long-distance correlations that stem from limited ensemble size. This study utilizes 960-member ensemble forecasts from the Global Ensemble Forecast System (GEFS) to examine the structures of the correlations for the planetary boundary layer (PBL) height (PBLH). title: Record-setting heavy precipitation occurrence in 2024
abstract: Precipitation extremes have increased globally in recent decades, consistent with a warming climate. We find that 2024 experienced a record-high frequency of heavy (≥99th percentile; F P≥99 ) precipitation events globally based on MSWEP (Multi-Source Weighted-Ensemble Precipitation) observations from 1979 to 2025. This extends a long-term trend of ∼0.03%/decade in F P≥99 , with similar but more uncertain increases for the 99.9th percentile. title: What controls reliable hourly flood simulation across hydrological regimes in the mountain catchments of central Chile
abstract: Study region: Forty-nine mountain catchments in central Chile (32–39°S), spanning rainfall-, snowmelt-, and mixed-dominated flood regimes across the Andes and Coastal Range. Steep relief and short channels produce short, sub-daily hydrological response times, and floods threaten much of the national population. abstract: Underwater soft strata commonly occur beneath river and lake dike foundations. Coupled water–level fluctuations and seepage make these strata susceptible to differential settlement and shear failure. title: Downside-risk pre-positioning for resilient scheduling of an off-grid deep-offshore electricity-hydrogen integrated energy system under extreme weather
abstract: An off-grid deep-offshore electricity-hydrogen integrated energy system (DOEH-IES) provides a practical carrier for onsite offshore wind utilization and multi-energy coordination. However, under typhoon conditions, coupled wind-wave effects and platform motion reduce the available power of floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs), introducing a time-varying downside risk that conventional scheduling methods often fail to mitigate proactively. abstract: Aiming at the research deficiencies of existing manta ray-inspired propulsion models, which are mostly simplified to rigid flapping motion alone and ignore the actual torsional deformation of pectoral fins as well as the overall flexible traveling wave deformation, this paper establishes a three-degree-of-freedom coupled numerical model for the bionic manta ray integrating flapping, torsion and flexible traveling wave motions. title: Impacts of Tide–Surge Interaction on Sediment Dynamics During Typhoons
abstract: Extreme weather conditions dominate sediment transports and thus determine morpho-dynamic evolution in coastal zones. Tide–surge interactions during extreme weather conditions modulate surge, and thus impact storm tides and sediment dynamics, especially in macro-tidal turbid estuaries. In this study, the macro-tidal turbid Hangzhou Bay (HZB) is selected as an example. abstract: Land-surface change and atmospheric variability jointly shape dust activity in arid regions. We examined land-cover transitions, station dust-storm records, a Sentinel-1 backscatter index, meteorological variables from the fifth-generation European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts reanalysis (ERA5) and dust diagnostics from the Modern-Era Retrospective analysis for Research and Applications, Version 2 (MERRA-2) along the margins of the Taklimakan Desert. abstract: Abstract Typical climate model resolutions preclude the explicit simulation of most of the spectrum of atmospheric gravity waves (GWs). Climate models must therefore rely on GW parameterizations, which observations help constrain. Between 2011 and 2021, Loon LLC launched thousands of balloons, some of which flew close enough together to be affected by the same GW packet. title: Contrasting drivers of summer extreme hourly precipitation over the southeastern and northeastern Tibetan Plateau
abstract: Abstract Extreme hourly precipitation (EHP) across the Tibetan Plateau (TP) often triggers flash floods and landslides due to the region's complex and steep terrain, yet its inter-station covariations and formation mechanisms remain inadequately understood. Using climate network analysis of hourly station data and dynamic diagnostics, this study examines EHP synchronicity across the southeastern and northeastern TP and elucidates the underlying mechanisms from a perspective of sea surface temperature (SST)-forced circulation evolution. title: Sources of skillful seasonal forecasts of springtime CONUS tornado activity
abstract: Despite progress in continental United States (CONUS) tornado forecasting, operational seasonal outlooks remain challenging due to intrinsic predictability limits. While previous studies link the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) to spring tornado frequency, relying on single tropical indices misses crucial regional variability. Here, we present a novel hybrid dynamical-statistical framework that introduces a paradigm for long-lead predictability. title: Wetland restoration enhances ecological quality in urbanizing regions
abstract: Abstract Introduction Rapid urbanization and climate change drive widespread wetland degradation, yet it remains unclear whether wetland restoration improves ecological quality (EQ), a composite indicator reflecting vegetation, thermal, hydrological, environmental, and soil conditions at regional scales in highly urbanized landscapes. title: Changes in temperature, rainfall and snow cover during the reproductive season of Arctic-breeding birds
abstract: Arctic warming is rapidly altering hydroclimatic conditions, yet its implications for the timing and reliability of terrestrial breeding environments remain poorly quantified. This study assesses how changes in temperature, snow dynamics, and rainfall extremes affect the snow-free reproductive window across Arctic tundra systems. We combined ERA5 reanalysis (1940-2024), daily output from ten CMIP6 Earth System Models, and long-term equilibrium simulations (400 years) from EC-Earth3 under present-day and doubled CO₂ conditions. abstract: This study investigates the ultimate strength and nonlinear structural response of metallic I-core sandwich pressure hulls as an alternative to conventional ring-stiffened submarine pressure-hull structures. abstract: Abstract Equatorially trapped Kelvin waves can occur through the depth of the troposphere and beyond. Previous works have demonstrated that these waves respond profoundly to the background flows through which they propagate, leading to variation in phase speed and dispersion characteristics. title: Wind conditions shape co-migration fidelity in trans-Saharan birds at a Mediterranean stopover site
abstract: Weather is a key driver of bird migration, particularly near ecological barriers, where migratory species often converge before crossing. While its effects on individual timing are well documented, how weather reshapes the temporal assemblage of migratory bird communities remains unexplored. abstract: Many migratory birds now reach their Arctic breeding grounds earlier in response to advancing springs and shifting nutrient peaks, either by departing earlier from non-breeding grounds or by travelling faster. For dark-bellied brent geese, there is limited potential to travel faster, as their spring migration is already among the fastest of Arctic geese and swans. title: Intensification of East Asian summer extreme precipitation under a net-zero anthropogenic CO 2 emission scenario
abstract: Global warming has intensified extreme precipitation, a trend projected to continue as warming persists. However, how extreme precipitation characteristics respond to global warming mitigation strategies remains poorly understood. This study examines East Asian summer extreme precipitation responses under a net-zero anthropogenic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emission scenario. Despite substantial cooling over East Asia following atmospheric CO 2 concentration decline, the intensity of extreme precipitation events continues to increase for about 30 years and does not subsequently weaken. abstract: Abstract Mangroves near subtropical range limits may benefit from fewer cold constraints, yet warmer conditions can also increase atmospheric water demand. abstract: Abstract. Ground-based microwave radiometers provide continuous, all-weather observations of boundary-layer temperature and humidity, closing a critical near-surface observation gap. The Advanced Radiative Transfer Modeling System – ground-based (ARMS-gb) is a fast radiative transfer model specifically designed to simulate the brightness temperatures these instruments observe. abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) increasingly rely on optical sensors for navigation, reconnaissance, and environmental monitoring; however, high-speed operation near the air-water interface generates free-surface waves and cavitation that create strongly non-uniform density and refractive-index fields, causing image distortion beyond the scope of conventional ray-tracing models. abstract: This paper presents a preliminary census of artificial cavities within the municipal territory of Sutri (Latium, Italy). The census, based on a review of historical sources and technical documentation, combined with direct field observations, led to the identification and mapping of more than 120 cavities. abstract: Abstract Turbulence represents a primary hazard for aviation, with Clear-Air Turbulence (CAT) posing a unique threat due to its visually undetectable nature. title: Cloud vertical structure across China from a national Ka-band cloud radar network: thermodynamic, dynamical, and land-surface controls
abstract: Abstract. Cloud vertical structure plays a central role in regulating Earth’s radiation balance and hydrological cycle, yet it remains poorly represented in weather and climate models due to limited high-resolution observations. Using a newly established national network of 80 Ka-band cloud radars, we provide the first high-spatiotemporal-resolution characterization of cloud vertical structure across China for 2024 and quantify its thermodynamic, dynamical, and land-surface controls. abstract: Abstract The 2025 M 7.8 Mandalay earthquake ruptured ~480 km of the Sagaing Fault, producing one of the longest strike-slip events documented and impacting a vulnerable region. abstract: The increasing demand for reducing fuel consumption and improving energy efficiency in maritime industry has intensified interest in solar thermal systems for auxiliary energy supply. In this study, a numerical model of a solar collector tube is developed in COMSOL Multiphysics. title: Bio-inspired trailing edge optimization for a double-suction pump impeller: a hybrid NSGA-II and CFD approach
abstract: Energy consumption reduction in pump systems has attracted increasing attention. Improving the efficiency of double-suction pumps can contribute to reducing energy consumption due to their extensive applications. This paper aims to optimize the double-suction pump by introducing the bionic structure inspired by the pectoral fin structure of humpback whales. abstract: Abstract We examined the evolution of shallow convective structures in the atmospheric boundary layer in response to changes in the basic state. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Tubular joints are fundamental components in the design of offshore platforms, naval vessels, and marine superstructures, offering high strength-to-weight ratios and favourable hydrodynamic behaviour. Because their welded intersections concentrate multiaxial loads, they are among the most vulnerable regions of any marine tubular framework. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Metro stations, characterized by enclosed spatial configurations, are highly vulnerable to extreme flooding, posing severe threats to human life and property. Understanding the hydrodynamic processes of flood intrusion and their implications for evacuation routes is therefore essential for urban flood risk reduction. abstract: Abstract. High-elevation alpine catchments are particularly affected by the global rise in temperature. abstract: I analyze research thrusts meant to reduce the carbon costs of the most resource intensive food item, beef. abstract: This work proposes a compact waterborne muffler that simultaneously achieves low-frequency broadband noise reduction and high load-bearing capacity by embedding topology-optimized chiral metamaterials into a square expansion chamber. abstract: Rectangular barges are widely used for their high payload capacity and stability, but their bluff geometry creates complex hydrodynamic responses requiring accurate analysis for safe operation. title: Human-enhanced tsunami hazard in large lakes
abstract: Worldwide, human-induced erosion enhances sediment delivery to lake deltas, increasing their susceptibility to collapse. In Lake Iseo, northern Italy, two millennia of intensified land use tripled sediment flux, oversteepening the delta and preconditioning it for failure. abstract: Abstract Understanding the role of water vapor in Arctic amplification requires a detailed evaluation of its spatio‐temporal variability. In this work, we use an integrated water vapor (IWV) data set from a ground‐based microwave radiometer at Ny‐Ålesund, Svalbard, covering 2012–2024, to characterize temporal IWV variability. abstract: The Northwest Himalaya region is highly susceptible to extreme rainfall events due to its steep topography and complex climatic variability, which can trigger significant hydro-meteorological hazards, including heavy snowfall, hailstorms, floods, and droughts. abstract: Abstract Poleward-transported (PT) cyclones account for a substantial part of winter Arctic cyclone activity, but their routes into the Arctic have rarely been examined as a distinct aspect of cyclone variability. Using objectively identified winter cyclone tracks for 1979–2025, we find that PT cyclones preferentially follow four recurrent pathways rather than entering the Arctic randomly. title: Role of monsoon intraseasonal oscillations in modulating extreme rainfall and aerosols over central India
abstract: This observational study diagnoses the influence of the monsoon intraseasonal oscillation (MISO) on aerosols and extreme rainfall events (EREs) in Central India, using the satellite datasets from CERES and GPM-IMERG, from 2003 to 2019. The research examines explicitly how MISO phases modulate aerosol optical depth (AOD) and the occurrence of EREs during the summer monsoon. title: Sub‐Seasonal Forecasting of Precipitation and Soil Moisture in CFSv2 Near Gulf Coast Tropical Cyclone Landfall Locations
abstract: Abstract Landfalling tropical cyclones (TCs) produce intense winds, heavy precipitation, and damaging storm surges along the Gulf and East coast of the U.S. There is growing evidence that high antecedent soil moisture (SM) conditions preceding landfall can maintain or even intensify TCs over land, sustaining strong winds and precipitation further inland. abstract: Abstract. Sahara dust events can promote the formation of micrometer‑sized spherical mineral aggregates known as iberulites as they are usually found on the Iberian Peninsula. Iberulites have not, to our knowledge, been reported from Central Europe. Two formation mechanisms – in- and below scavenging – have been given. abstract: Abstract Global storm‐resolving models (GSRMs) provide new opportunities to investigate the climate response to warming with explicitly resolved deep convection. abstract: To address the limitations of existing studies that neglect sediment feedback and thus underestimate the complexity of the flow field, this study develops a three-dimensional hydrodynamic model for aquaculture cages that couples a porous-media representation of netting with a two-way discrete-phase model for sediment transport. title: Evaluating Statistical Downscaling Techniques for Regional Hydroclimatic Change Projections Over CONUS
abstract: Abstract Projecting the impacts of future climate change is critical for water managers planning infrastructure resilience strategies. Global earth system model output is generally too coarse to provide the detailed, localized information needed for impact assessment, and the computational cost of running higher‐resolution global simulations over sufficiently long periods is prohibitive. abstract: Abstract Western Europe and the Yangtze–Huai River Basin (YHRB) experienced two exceptional synchronized extreme heat events during the summer of 2025, providing a unique opportunity to investigate the mechanisms linking geographically distant heat extremes. abstract: Abstract Open-water disposal of dredged sediment generates a dense near-field cloud that descends through the water column, deforms under ambient-current forcing and reorganizes into a near-bed source for subsequent transport. Within the present two-dimensional numerical framework, this source-formation stage determines the early suspended-sediment footprint and provides a compact description of the near-bed state that may later be supplied to transport and deposition models. title: Changes in Flood Frequency and Seasonality Across Midwestern U.S. Watersheds Under a Warming Climate: Insights From Convection‐Permitting Climate Simulations and Physics‐Based Hydrologic Models
abstract: Abstract We combine CONUS404 convection‐permitting climate simulations with the physics‐based WRF‐Hydro model to assess how climate warming may influence flood frequency and seasonality across the Midwestern United States. This framework captures interactions among precipitation, soil moisture, and snowpack that shape flood generation. Both simulated warming and historical records show a regional shift toward more extreme warm‐season, rainfall‐driven floods. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Abstract Consecutive days of anomalously warm temperatures (warm spells) can severely impact human health and ecosystems, whatever time of year they occur. Previous research has typically focused only on warm-season warm spells - heatwaves; here, we assess trends in warm spells in all seasons across Northern Hemisphere midlatitude land using observational data (Berkeley Earth and ERA5) and CMIP6 climate models.
