abstract: Hundreds of subglacial lakes in Antarctica have been reported by using radio-echo sounding and satellite altimetry, but the detection of small and short-lived hydrological events has remained challenging due to limited spatial and temporal resolution. In this study, we applied the Double-Differential Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (DDInSAR) technique to analyze surface-elevation changes associated with the Kronshtadskiy subglacial lake near the Amery Ice Shelf, East Antarctica. abstract: Glaciers populate the mountain ranges of the western conterminous United States and despite their importance to alpine hydrology, their area and volume change have never been comprehensively evaluated. Our study shows that since the mid-twentieth century about one-quarter of the glaciers have disappeared and the overall area and volume are reduced by one-third. abstract: Abstract Volcanic eruptions in the Northern Hemisphere extratropics have been reported to produce several times greater cooling in that region than tropical eruptions of similar magnitude. Using a large ensemble of simulations spanning the eruption size range from 5 to 40 Tg of stratospheric sulfur, we find that the extratropical‐to‐tropical cooling ratio is consistently within a factor of two, indicating no enhancement beyond the effect of aerosols being confined to a single hemisphere. abstract: Seasonal flooding changes fish habitat availability and the transport, retention and recovery of genetic material, complicating environmental DNA assessments in connected river–floodplain systems. abstract: Meiyu-Baiu, the distinct rainy season in subtropical East Asia, is characterized by a quasi-stationary Meiyu-Baiu Front (MBF) along which excessive rainfall and mega floods often occur. abstract: Abstract The Earth Cloud Aerosol and Radiation Explorer (EarthCARE) provides critical spaceborne high spectral resolution LiDAR observations for global aerosol profiling. abstract: Extreme precipitation poses severe societal and economic risks under elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2), yet current understanding of how it will respond to various future CO2 removal scenarios remains limited. Focusing on East Asia, a region highly vulnerable to monsoonal dynamics and anthropogenic influences, here we assess the hysteresis of extreme precipitation responses under four CO2 concentration thresholds and two emission reduction rates using climate model simulations. abstract: Abstract. The Tibetan Plateau, highly sensitive to climate change, exerts strong atmospheric oxidation capacity partly through rapid cycling of atmospheric reactive nitrogen (Nr). abstract: Africa’s accelerating climate warming has rendered its climate potential productivity (CPP) increasingly vulnerable, raising global concerns over biodiversity, water resources, and food security. abstract: Abstract In recent years, significant efforts have been made to understand how urban environments influence local weather, particularly extreme precipitation events. abstract: Climate change is driving a sustained increase in global temperatures and an intensification of extreme events, including heatwaves. Urban areas are typically warmer than the surrounding suburban and rural environments, a phenomenon known as the Urban Heat Island (UHI) due to the presence of buildings and inhomogeneous surfaces, which affects surface energy and water exchanges as well as the local meteorology. title: Improved detection of methanogenic archaea by validating 16S rRNA gene primers using defined archaeal–bacterial mock communities
abstract: Abstract Archaea play essential roles in global biogeochemical cycles, yet their diversity in environmental samples remains understudied. Limited coverage of universal primers towards archaea, their very low abundance relative to bacteria in the studied samples, inefficient cell lysis and the incompleteness of reference databases complicate archaeal 16S rRNA gene sequencing. title: Heat-related urban mortality attributable to human-induced climate change in Europe from 2000 to 2025
abstract: Abstract Anthropogenic climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme heat, with major implications for population health. Although previous studies have attributed heat-related mortality to climate change during individual events, the longer-term contribution of human-induced warming to urban mortality burdens across Europe remains poorly quantified. title: Evaluation of turbulent flux parameterizations over a continental glacier on the Tibetan Plateau
abstract: A lack of observations of turbulent fluxes over continental glaciers limits our understanding of the mechanisms that control glacier variations and associated water resource changes across the Tibetan Plateau (TP). Here, we present the first comprehensive analysis of turbulent flux characteristics and a systematic evaluation of turbulent flux parameterizations for a continental glacier on the TP, using eddy covariance (EC) observations from the Dunde Glacier during May–October 2023. abstract: ABSTRACT Power systems with high shares of variable renewable energy increasingly face balancing challenges that extend beyond intraday variability to multiday shortages, seasonal mismatch, resource adequacy and system resilience. Salt cavern hydrogen storage (SCHS) has emerged as a promising underground hydrogen storage option for renewable‐dominated smart energy systems. It can act as the large‐scale storage component that connects renewable hydrogen production with downstream hydrogen use and power‐to‐hydrogen‐to‐power pathways. title: Modulation of Slow Slip Event Characteristics Throughout the Costa Rica Subduction Zone Earthquake Cycle
abstract: Abstract Slow slip events (SSEs) represent an aseismic transient slip mode that repeats quasi‐periodically, near or partially overlapping with the megathrust earthquake zone. However, the process of stress interaction between SSEs and earthquake zones is not clearly understood. title: Integrated GIS, VES, and Dar-Zarrouk analysis for delineating groundwater recharge and storage priority zones in Telangana, India
abstract: Groundwater-recharge planning in semi-arid hard-rock aquifers is uncertain when site selection relies only on surface indicators. This study integrates geographic information system (GIS) analysis, vertical electrical sounding (VES), and Dar-Zarrouk parameters to screen candidate sites for recharge and surface-water storage interventions in Kangti Mandal, Telangana, India. The workflow combines a village-scale well inventory, water-level measurements, 32 Schlumberger VES soundings, thematic GIS layers, and Dar-Zarrouk indicators of aquifer protection and relative groundwater potential. title: Seismic site characterization and classification using HVSR and MASW analyses for urbanization suitability assessment in the Azilal urban area, Central Morocco
abstract: The Azilal urban area, located in the Central High Atlas and approximately 220 km from the 6.8 Mw Al Haouz earthquake epicenter, was investigated for seismic site effects using 24 Multi‑Channel Analysis of Surface Waves (MASW) profiles and 99 Horizontal‑to‑Vertical Spectral Ratio HVSR. title: Modeling breaking waves for surf-pool design: A comparative analysis of SPH and VOF methods
abstract: This article examines the applicability of the mesh-free Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) method for numerical simulation of surfable solitary waves propagating over an artificial seabed in a wave pool. The simulations were performed using DualSPHysics, with particular attention given to the accurate reproduction of the free-surface profile. title: Morphological Characteristics of Tropical Precipitation Features Producing Extreme Instantaneous Rain Rates in GPM and DYAMOND Global Storm Resolving Models
abstract: Abstract The influence of the spatial organization of tropical convection on the production of extreme instantaneous localized tropical rain rates remains poorly constrained, both in observations and in models. Using retrievals from the Ku‐band radar onboard the GPM satellite, we identify tropical precipitation features (PFs) and quantify their morphological characteristics. We find that PFs that produce extreme instantaneous rain rates are on average larger and have a higher convective area fraction than the average PF. title: Lifetime Estimation of Blade Erosion Using Rain Erosion Test Data With Different Analysis Methods
abstract: ABSTRACT Lifetime estimation regarding leading‐edge erosion of wind turbine blades involves a series of mathematical and statistical procedures, including regression fitting, tolerance interval formulation, and weathering modeling approaches. This work investigates the intermediate steps in the fatigue assessment process and the associated sources of variability, using data from a whirling arm rain erosion test (RET) machine, time‐series liquid precipitation and wind data from two sites, and the IEA reference 15 MW wind turbine. title: Influence of atmospheric circulation on temperature extremes in mountainous regions of Central Europe during 1961–2025
abstract: Abstract Recent climate change is most clearly manifested in rising global temperatures, with regionally amplified warming observed in Central Europe, including its mountainous areas. This study analyses trends in mean annual and seasonal air temperatures and evaluates the influence of atmospheric circulation on temperature extremes in Central European mountains during 1961–2025, comparing the periods 1961–1990 and 1991–2025. abstract: ABSTRACT Wenchuan earthquake–induced landslides generated large volumes of sediment that formed lateral sediment deposits in mountainous river channels, significantly altering flow structures and channel evolution. Under such strongly non-uniform flow conditions, accurate estimation of bed shear stress remains challenging. Because bed shear stress is difficult to measure directly in natural rivers, friction velocity is commonly used as an indirect proxy. title: Substantial spatial heterogeneity in growing season dynamics across northern environments
abstract: Abstract Arctic tundra and boreal forest landscapes exhibit substantial microclimatic temperature variability, driven by strong topographic gradients, heterogeneous snowmelt patterns, and contrasting vegetation structures. However, this fine-scale variability is often poorly represented in reanalyses, climate models, and conventional weather station networks. In this study, we use a total of 347 microclimate loggers deployed across three regions in northern Fennoscandia during 2020–2024 to examine how the onset, end, duration, and degree days of the growing season vary across the landscapes. title: The MISR Research Product Algorithm – producing global, self-consistent, pixel-level aerosol retrievals for the Multi-angle Imaging SpectroRadiometer
abstract: Abstract. The MISR Research Aerosol retrieval algorithm (RA) was developed in parallel with the MISR standard operational algorithm (SA), to explore innovative retrieval ideas for possible implementation in the SA, and to provide higher-spatial-resolution results with enhanced sensitivity to particle properties, where possible. Whereas the SA was designed to run automatically on the entire MISR dataset, the RA, a research code, had to be run on a case-by-case basis, with considerable user involvement. title: Path dependency in multistage direct shear tests on a dense mixed-grained soil: a DEM-based micromechanical interpretation
abstract: Multistage direct shear testing reduces material demand and specimen-to-specimen variability compared with conventional testing, but later stages may become path-dependent because the specimen is not fully reset between loading steps. This study investigates this path dependency for a dense mixed-grained gravel–sand with plastic fines (GKB1) by combining laboratory tests with a DEM-based micromechanical interpretation. abstract: The article provides an overview and analysis of modern diamond drilling and cutting technologies used in the reconstruction, widening, and dismantling of massive reinforced concrete bridge structures. Based on the long-term experience of NPP SK MOST LLC since 1994, the article describes key methods used in practice, including diamond drilling of precision holes, cutting with circular saws and diamond wire, and breaking concrete with wedge jacks and hydraulic nippers. title: Interfacial control and evaporation pinning of nanocapillary filling from ambient to serpentinization temperatures
abstract: Abstract Fluid transport in nanometer-scale channels underlies nanofluidic technologies and geological systems, yet measured capillary filling rates in hydrophilic channels are often far slower than classical theory predicts. Here we show, using a coupled flow model based on classical density functional theory combining hydrodynamics, electrokinetics and capillarity, that electrokinetic resistance and locally elevated viscosity near the channel walls jointly suppress flow, capturing the measured slowdown across independent experiments. title: Analysis of Snow Cover Dynamics in the Beas River Basin during 2019-2021
abstract: Snow is a key component of the Himalayan cryosphere and plays a significant role in water resource availability and hydrological processes. This study examines the characteristics of snow cover in the Beas River Basin using MODIS satellite imagery for the period 2019-2021, with particular emphasis on temporal variations in snow cover and its potential influence on the hydrological cycle. title: Biomass Burning in Australia: No Evidence for Carbonyl Sulfide (OCS) Enhancement in Fire Plumes From In‐Situ Measurements During SouthTRAC
abstract: Abstract Determining the atmospheric abundance and the emission sources of carbonyl sulfide (OCS) plays a crucial role for the sulfur budget in the atmosphere. In addition to its main anthropogenic and biogenic sources, biomass burning is assumed to be an essential, but not well constrained source of OCS. title: Impact Crater Hydrothermal Systems Support Rapid Microbial Enrichment and Diverse Metabolic Potential
abstract: Impact crater hydrothermal systems, formed after asteroid and comet impacts, have been proposed as promising habitats for life on early Earth and as key targets in the search for life on planetary bodies such as Mars, since they provide liquid water and active geochemical turnover. Because no newly formed impact structures exist on Earth, studies of microbial establishment in impact-crater hydrothermal systems have largely relied on the direct observation of fossil microbial life or its isotopic signatures. title: Areal reduction factors from high-resolution rain gauges in Austria
abstract: Abstract. Areal Reduction Factors (ARFs) are widely used to convert point design precipitation derived from intensity–duration–frequency (IDF) curves into areal precipitation values for hydrological design. Despite their importance, ARFs remain highly uncertain, particularly for short durations and small areas, due to insufficient representation of precipitation spatial variability. title: Evaluation of the Spatial Distribution of Some Thermal Comfort Indices in Iraq Using the RayMan Model
abstract: Lack of comprehensive evaluations of spatial thermal comfort parameters across Iraq remains a concern as the risks of excessive heat and climate change increase. This study analyzes the spatial distribution of outdoor human thermal comfort in Iraq using the Physiologically Equivalent Temperature (PET) and Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI). Monthly meteorological data from 38 stations (1981–2024) were obtained from the NASA POWER database and used in the RayMan model to calculate PET and UTCI. abstract: The weld efficiency, fracture position and microstructure of dissimilar friction stir welded joints between Al-Mg and pure Fe, produced at rotational speeds of 300-1100 rpm and a constant welding speed of 100mm/min, were investigated using finite-element simulation, tensile tests, microhardness tests, scanning electron microscopy, transmission electron microscopy and electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) techniques. title: Hydrological response to climate change across semi-arid sub-basins of the Tensift watershed, Morocco
abstract: The hydrological systems of watersheds are increasingly affected by climate change, resulting in altered rainfall patterns, more intense droughts, and disrupted runoff. This study analyzes the impacts of these changes on streamflow across eight sub-basins of the Tensift Basin. To achieve this objective, the GR2M hydrological model was applied using bias-corrected climate data from five RCM–GCM modelling chains (CNRM, CMCC, IPSL, GUF, and ICTP) from the Med-CORDEX initiative. title: Long-term trends of carbon monoxide over the North Pacific upper troposphere from in-situ airplane measurements 1991–2018
abstract: Carbon monoxide (CO) is not a greenhouse gas, but as the dominant sink of the hydroxyl radical it governs the oxidising capacity of the troposphere and so indirectly forces climate. Its trends in the North Pacific upper troposphere matter disproportionately: this is the principal outflow corridor for Asian anthropogenic emissions, the fastest-growing combustion source of the past half-century, yet it has almost no routine ground-based monitoring and satellite retrievals resolve it poorly. title: Sensitivity of the summertime diurnal precipitation cycle over three representative regions of China to convective trigger and closure treatments in a single-column model
abstract: Abstract. Using a single‑column model, we investigate how trigger and closure treatments in ZM, TDK, and UNICON convection schemes affect DCP over China. title: Neapolitan Yellow Tuff revisited: a new look to stratigraphy and eruptive dynamics of a complex eruption of Campi Flegrei caldera (Italy)
abstract: Large caldera-forming eruptions are among the most complex and hazardous volcanic phenomena, yet their reconstruction is often hindered by incomplete preservation of proximal deposits and temporal variability of eruptive processes. The Neapolitan Yellow Tuff (NYT) eruption, one of the largest events at the Campi Flegrei caldera (southern Italy), represents a key case study for understanding the dynamics of large explosive eruptions, but its stratigraphy, magnitude, and eruptive mechanisms remain debated. abstract: Abstract Recent observational studies have demonstrated that supersaturation fluctuations (SS’) in clouds induced by turbulence at scales smaller than 100 m can significantly affect microphysical processes such as aerosol activation and droplet condensation. Future Northeastward Shift of Extratropical Transition of Tropical Cyclones Over the North Atlantic in Downscaling Projections
abstract: Abstract Tropical cyclones (TCs) often undergo extratropical transition (ET) at the midlatitudes, becoming post‐tropical cyclones (PTCs). We combine a logistic regression PTC identification model with synthetic TC tracks and intensities from the Columbia HAZard model (CHAZ) to project future ET completion over the North Atlantic (NA). title: Evaluating intra-urban thermo-hygrometric variability through in situ observations and MLUCM BEP + BEM: A case study in Lecce (Italy)
abstract: Abstract This study evaluates the capability of the MLUCM BEP + BEM to reproduce intra-urban variability of air temperature and relative humidity in Lecce (Italy) during summer 2025. A network of six measurement sites representing contrasting urban morphology, vegetation cover, and land-use conditions was used to characterize the thermo-hygrometric structure of the city and evaluate model performance. title: A Study on the Digital Preservation and Cultural Translation of Architectural Heritage in Ancient Villages in Western Guangdong from the Perspective of Media Convergence: A Case Study of Wuniba Village, Lianjiang City, Guangdong Province
abstract: The ancient villages in western Guangdong integrate farming, clan and Confucian culture, carrying local memory and local identity. However, urbanization and labor outflow have caused dilapidated buildings and memory faults, facing the dual crisis of "physical damage" and "lack of expression". Based on the theory of media convergence, this paper proposes a digital protection paradigm of "physical filing as the basis, virtual performance as the wing, and cultural identity as the soul", breaking through the limitation of "emphasizing records and neglecting communication". title: From regulation to breach: Integrated GIS-hydrologic-2D hydrodynamic modelling of multi-scenario flood Hazard at Wadi Jazan dam, Saudi Arabia
abstract: Dams in arid, data-scarce basins are designed to attenuate episodic flash floods, yet their performance under extreme operational stress or catastrophic failure is rarely evaluated against long-term observational records. This study presents an empirical and hydrodynamic assessment of Wadi Jazan Dam, Saudi Arabia, integrating nearly four decades of historical streamflow data with an integrated GIS, semi-distributed HEC-HMS, and 2D HEC-RAS modelling framework. title: Accessibility and surface area drive desert toad presence at artificial water sites in the Great Basin and Mojave Deserts
abstract: Artificial Water Sites (AWS) are human-made or modified water sources constructed or maintained for livestock, select wildlife game species, or other management purposes in arid environments. However, non-target species such as desert toads have been documented utilizing AWS. Because the reproductive ecology of desert toads relies on water, understanding factors explaining their presence at AWS can inform conservation practices. title: Mitigating the Impact of Drought on Inland Water Transport: A System Dynamics Approach
abstract: ABSTRACT In recent years, droughts have disrupted goods transport on Dutch waterways, causing production losses in the hinterland and reputational damage to inland water transport (IWT). As future droughts are expected to be more extreme, the question is how IWT can stay reliable. abstract: Entre os meses de abril e maio de 2024, uma onda de calor (OC) afetou extensas áreas das regiões Sul, Sudeste e Centro-Oeste do Brasil, enquanto o estado do Rio Grande do Sul registrou recordes históricos de precipitação. title: Numerical and theoretical analysis of vertical cyclic uplift of single-helix anchors in soft clay
abstract: Vertical cyclic uplift of single-helix anchors in soft clay can induce stiffness degradation, excess pore-pressure accumulation, and residual displacement. This study established an experimental–finite element–theoretical framework for preliminary assessment. title: Safety and Resilience in Slope Engineering Design for New Buildings under Extreme Rainstorm Climates
abstract: The safety of construction slopes holds significant importance in engineering and architecture, with the lack of resilience against extreme weather conditions being particularly critical. This paper systematically examines the fundamental flaws in traditional design theories regarding the limitations of compression-shear stress paths and the assumption of constant soil parameters. abstract: Abstract Purpose Greater understanding of the contributions from different sediment sources and their linkages to the downstream suspended sediment load (SSL) is essential to advancing knowledge of catchment sediment transport dynamics and informing sediment management. Implementation and uncertainty-based analysis of integrated catchment hydrologic and sediment models can provide valuable insights into sediment sources and their relative dominance at the catchment scale. abstract: This study aimed to develop a framework for mitigating cost and schedule overruns through the integration of Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM) and the Analytic Network Process (ANP). title: Detecting long-term canopy change and vegetation shifts in northern peatlands using LAI and climate data
abstract: Abstract. Peatlands store vast amounts of carbon, yet their canopies are changing under northern warming. We assessed recent vegetation trajectories by analysing greening and browning across northern peatlands using a gap-filled, sensor-independent climate data record of leaf area index (LAI) for 2001–2023. abstract: Abstract. Historical text sources represent a central, yet methodologically challenging basis for the reconstruction of convective weather events. This study examines the extent to which historical reports on thunderstorms and hailstorms contain reliable climatological information, despite heterogeneous sources, varying degrees of detail and linguistic diversity. abstract: Strategic freight procurement is the mechanism by which a shipper converts a forecast of future transportation demand into a portfolio of contracted rates before the demand arrives. Our subject here is strategic freight procurement and request-for-quotation management in an enterprise transportation management system, approached as a structured, repeatable auction rather than a clerical sourcing task. abstract: Reservoir sedimentation threatens the long-term performance of multipurpose dams, especially in cascade systems where upstream flushing may intensify downstream deposition. title: Characterizing lightning NO x production in the Ebro Valley with meteosat 12 LI and LMA observations
abstract: Abstract. Lightning is one of the main sources of NOₓ in the Earth’s atmosphere, yet there is considerable variability in NOₓ production during thunderstorms. In this study, we combined optical lightning data from the Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) Lightning Imaging (LI) instrument, which provides information on the occurrence rate and physical characteristics of lightning flashes, measurements from an extended Lightning Mapping Array (LMA) consisting of 24 sensors, lightning measurements from the Lightning Location System (LLS) of the Meteorological Service of Catalonia (MSC), and TROPO-sphe
institutions: Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt e. V. (DLR)

abstract: Mantle plume-generated Large Igneous Provinces (LIPs) are well known for their genetic association with magmatic sulphide Ni–Cu–PGE deposits, exemplified by Norilsk in the Siberian Traps. Previous work has broadened genetic these links between LIP events and metallogeny to include other orthomagmatic and hydrothermal deposits, lateritic enrichment, fluid-flow barriers and reactive zones that enable the formation of mineral deposits, and distal mineral systems indirectly influenced through plate tectonics. title: Surface solar radiation and day-to-day temperature variability in China during 1961–2022: evidence from the dimming–brightening transition
abstract: Abstract Climate change affects natural and human systems not only through changes in mean temperature but also through rapid temperature fluctuations between consecutive days. Using homogenized daily mean and maximum temperature observations and reconstructed surface solar radiation at 1759 matched stations in China during 1961–2022, we evaluated the seasonal cycles, probability distributions, and long-term trends of day-to-day temperature variability (DTD and DTDMAX). title: Non-monotonic response of net dust deposition kinetics to low wind speeds
abstract: Abstract. Dry deposition is a major sink for mineral dust, yet its behavior under weak winds remains poorly constrained and is often parameterized monotonically with wind speed. Here we quantify size-resolved dust deposition kinetics in a large closed-circuit recirculating wind tunnel using a two-stage protocol (brief high-wind loading followed by low-wind deposition at 0, 2, 4, and 6 m s⁻¹). Cumulative deposition time series were measured with an array of collection trays, with the initial suspended dust loading recorded by an online concentration monitor. title: Maintenance Tasks Scheduling in a Limited Space with Limited Resources
abstract: Maintenance tasks scheduling is one of the essential factors in maintenance engineering. This paper focuses on the maintenance task scheduling problem in confined spaces under resource-constrained scenarios (e.g., maintenance task planning during annual inspections in ship engine rooms or offshore drilling platforms), where spatial limitations and multi-resource availability jointly impact maintenance efficiency. Considering the constraints of different priority of maintenance tasks, unequal required area for maintenance activities and corresponding maintenance time with different resource lim

title: Impact of range scale factor and baseline biases on gravity field estimation: analysis and validation with GRACE follow-on data and simulations
abstract: Abstract GRACE/GRACE-FO missions recover gravity field from orbits observed by GPS and variations in inter-satellite distances obtained by the inter-satellite ranging systems. Compared to GRACE, GRACE-FO is also equipped with a laser ranging interferometer (LRI), a more precise inter-satellite ranging technology and the preferred choice for future gravity missions. title: Revisiting genome-guided RNA localization in bacteria
abstract: Elucidating the intracellular organization of bacterial transcriptomes may reveal new modes of gene regulation. Recent work reported that chromosomal gene position determines mRNA localization within Escherichia coli cells, implying a widespread genome-guided organizing mechanism. Yet this interpretation contrasts with biophysical expectations based on translation and diffusion and may be confounded by nascent transcription. title: Aqueous‐Phase Processing of Organic Aerosols at the Southern Great Plains: Insights From Integrated Chemical and Microphysical Analyses
abstract: Abstract Aqueous‐phase reactions are hypothesized to be a major pathway for secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation in humid, cloud‐influenced environments, yet direct observational constraints remain limited. Here we investigated aqueous SOA (aqSOA) formation and evolution during the spring 2016 Holistic Interactions of Shallow Clouds, Aerosols, and Land Ecosystems (HI‐SCALE) campaign at the U.S. Department of Energy Southern Great Plains (SGP) site using high‐resolution aerosol mass spectrometer (HR‐AMS) measurements integrated with particle size distribution and meteorological observation

title: Non-stationary time series attribution for heatwaves over Europe
abstract: The increasing occurrence of extreme weather events since the beginning of the 21st century has led to the development of new methods to attribute extreme events to anthropogenic climate change. The way in which the extreme event is defined has a major influence on the attribution result. A frequently overlooked aspect concerns the temporal dependence of extremes. This study presents an approach for attributing complete time series during extreme events to anthropogenic forcing. journal: Advances in statistical climatology, meteorology and oceanography

title: Spatial assessment of air-renewal heterogeneity in multi-tier layer houses using IoT-based CO2 monitoring
abstract: Maintaining spatially adequate thermal and air-quality conditions is challenging in commercial multi-tier layer houses because environmental gradients can develop simultaneously across longitudinal regions and cage levels. This observational field study characterized two commercial houses with distinct environmental-control configurations in southern Brazil using a three-level IoT monitoring network. title: Modeling Carbon Dioxide Disposal in a Non-isothermal Viscoelastic Porous Medium
abstract: The paper proposes a mathematical model of carbon dioxide disposal in a non-isothermal viscoelastic porous medium. Following the two-dimensional approach and considering the smallness of the solid phase velocity, the initial system of equations is reduced to the problem of finding the effective pressure and porosity of the medium. Thermal effects caused by gas injection are introduced into the model by the equation for the temperature of the medium. title: Basin-scale evaluation of the Noah-MP land surface model for runoff and snow generation in the Missouri River Basin: insights and recommendations for parameterization scheme selection
abstract: Abstract. Process-based land surface models, such as the Noah-Multiparameterization (Noah-MP) model, are widelyused for large-scale hydrologic simulations because of their flexibility in selecting multiple parameterization schemes. However, limited guidance on choosing appropriate configurations constrains their reliability in representing runoff and snowmelt dynamics across diverse land-cover and snow conditions. title: Impacts of coal facies on vertical heterogeneity of deep coalbed methane reservoir in the Yulin area of Ordos Basin, North China
abstract: Abstract The vertical heterogeneity of coal is a crucial factor influencing the development of coalbed methane (CBM) and it is significantly influenced by coal facies. Utilizing the theories of coal facies and variation coefficient to clearly classify and quantitatively characterize the vertical coal facies types and heterogeneity of deep 8# coal in the Yulin area of the Ordos Basin based on the submaceral content, coal quality, and physical property tests. title: Force-based design of a novel self-centring concentrically braced steel frame validated by nonlinear time-history analysis
abstract: Self-centring concentrically braced frames (SC-CBFs) are intended to limit residual deformation after strong earthquakes, but practical code-oriented procedures for their design remain limited. This study presents a force-based design (FBD) procedure for a horizontally post-tensioned SC-CBF consistent with Eurocode 8 and Eurocode 3. The procedure defines the seismic base shear, brace sizing, allocation of shear resistance between the concentrically braced frame and post-tensioning system, and capacity checks for beams, columns, braces, and strands. A regular four-storey archetype was designed

title: Melt Production and Volatile Release From Thermochemical Mantle Plumes
abstract: Abstract Mantle plumes are thought to generate Large Igneous Provinces (LIPs), the largest outpourings of lava in the geologic record, which are associated with long‐lasting climatic warming events and mass extinctions. However, the controls on mantle degassing by plumes remain poorly constrained. Here we use thermochemical plume models to compute the melt production and carbon release from compositionally heterogeneous plumes that sample peridotite and eclogite. title: Updating thermal head of RECoverable Autonomous Sonde (RECAS) for better drilling performance in Qilin Subglacial Lake exploration
abstract: Abstract. There are numerous subglacial lakes in Antarctica, typically covered by thick ice sheets. Qilin subglacial lake is one of the largest subglacial lakes in Antarctica, lying beneath approximately 3600 m of ice. The exploration of this unique environment is of considerable scientific importance. Recoverable Autonomous Sonde (RECAS) has been proposed for exploring Qilin subglacial lake. However, drilling into the lakes with such probe may be impeded by volcanic ash or small rock clasts within the ice sheet. journal: Geoscientific instrumentation, methods and data systems

title: Dispersión de plumas de contaminación atmosférica por incendios forestales: un caso de estudio en el sur de Argentina
abstract: Forest fires pose significant threats to ecosystems, biodiversity, and human health, highlighting the importance of accurate tracking and assessment of their impact. The sources and levels of wildfire contamination were determined using HYSPLIT simulations and NASA MODIS satellite imagery. The forest fire that started in January 2024 in Los Alerces National Park, located in Chubut Province, Argentina, is presented as a case study. title: Circular Economy and Construction Waste Management in Saudi Mega-Projects: Pathways Towards Vision 2030 Sustainability Targets
abstract: Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 is accelerating the delivery of large-scale urban, tourism, transport, industrial and infrastructure projects while simultaneously strengthening national ambitions for environmental protection, resource efficiency and waste diversion. The scale of this development creates a strategic challenge: construction and demolition waste cannot be managed only as an end-of-pipe disposal problem. journal: Global Academic Journal of Economics and Business

title: Resource Analysis and Screening for Potential CO2 Storage Targets in Low-Porosity Saline Aquifers, Yulin, China
abstract: Abstract The Ordos Basin, a crucial energy base in China, leads the nation in oil, gas, and coal production, consequently leading to high carbon emissions. This establishes it as a key prospective region for implementing CO2 geological storage (CCS) to facilitate regional emissions reductions. However, the basin is predominantly characterized by low-porosity and ultralow-permeability reservoirs, which limit the applicability of current site selection criteria, largely derived from successful international projects involving high-porosity and high-permeability reservoirs. title: Enhancing pure ammonia engine combustion by pre-chamber ignition coupled with dual spark ignition strategies
abstract: Advanced ignition strategies are essential for overcoming the poor ignitability and low burning velocity of ammonia. Multi-point spark ignition can increase the combustion rate by shortening the flame propagation distance, while pre-chamber ignition (PCI) can enhance main-chamber (MC) combustion through distributed ignition sites and jet-induced turbulence. In this study, the combustion characteristics of pure ammonia under different ignition strategies were systematically investigated in a single-cylinder optical engine. title: Coupled electro-mechano-acoustic modeling and validation of piezo-actuated radiating structures
abstract: The increasing adoption of portable and wearable audio devices is accelerating the use of piezoelectric actuators as alternatives to conventional dynamic speakers, enabled by their ultra-thin, lightweight factor, low power consumption, and ability to transform non-traditional surfaces into efficient sound-radiating elements. Accurate design of piezoelectric speaker solutions requires optimization of structural vibration, acoustic output, and sound and energy efficiency under realistic operating conditions. title: Bioinspired functionally graded vorochiral metamaterials with enhanced energy absorption and dissipation
abstract: Designing bioinspired functionally graded metamaterials with tailored energy absorption ( EA ) and energy dissipation ( ED ) capacities through spatially regulating structural topology and local relative density distribution without increasing the overall material volume, remains a significant challenge. In this study, bioinspired functionally graded Vorochiral (BFG-VC) metamaterials were developed through the spatial modulation of chiral topologies, drawing inspiration from heterogeneous biological tissues. title: Cross-Comparison of Ground Observations, CAMS Estimates, and Linke-Model Irradiance for Photovoltaic System Design in Sahelian Niger
abstract: Reliable solar-resource inputs are essential for photovoltaic (PV) and hybrid-system design, but temporal matching and measurement traceability require scrutiny where reference records are scarce. This study compares SM206-SOLAR ground observations, Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) Radiation Service v4.6 estimates and Linke-model irradiance for Dosso, Niger, in May and August 2021. The CAMS v4.6 dataset documents the coordinates, altitude, UTC intervals and irradiation units. title: An integrated basin-wide water resources model for comprehensive assessment of water availability in the Nile River Basin
abstract: Abstract Despite extensive research on the Nile River Basin, few studies represent the entire basin as a connected hydrology–infrastructure–demand system. Existing basin-wide models are either dated, not openly accessible, or limited in their integration of hydrological processes, infrastructure operations, and spatially distributed water demand. To address this gap, this study aims to provide a contemporary basin-wide representation of how hydrology, major water infrastructure, and spatially distributed sectoral demand interact across the Nile. title: Characterisation and Extension of a Rigid Body Dynamics Solver Coupled with OpenFOAM® for Flight Performance Analysis of Flapping-wing Drones
abstract: The extraordinary aerial agility of hummingbirds and insects continues to inspire the design of flapping-wing drones. To replicate them, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations must be coupled with rigid body dynamics solvers. While OpenFOAM® provides a general articulated-body algorithm (ABA) for these multiphysics simulations, its current implementation is restricted to passive joints and lacks thorough verification for free-flight applications. title: Country-scale forest carbon modeling to support national greenhouse gas inventories in Croatia and Slovakia
abstract: Abstract Forest ecosystems are important carbon sinks and play a crucial role in reaching carbon neutrality. This study presents a reproducible workflow of using the biogeochemical ecosystem model Biome-BGCMuSo to support national greenhouse gas (GHG) inventory by including CO 2 emissions and removals from carbon pools lacking explicit carbon stock change (CSC) estimates within the Land Use, Land-Use Change and Forestry (LULUCF) sector. title: Analysis of wind load distribution on various geometrical forms of 3D structures
abstract: Reducing research costs has always been a priority for engineers and researchers. The advent of high-performance computers has enabled extensive use of numerical methods, particularly computational fluid dynamics (CFD), in structural wind analysis. In this study, ANSYS Fluent was used to investigate wind load distribution on eleven three-dimensional geometrical configurations with varying apex shapes and diameter distributions. title: Numerical Investigation on Repowering Aging Onshore Wind Turbine Foundations Through a Reuse Strategy: An Engineering Case Study
abstract: For the repowering of aging onshore wind foundations, a reuse-oriented strengthening scheme that does not require demolition of the existing foundation is proposed based on the retrofit project of an octagonal extended foundation at a wind farm in Shandong Province, China. Through structural measures such as connecting the foundation ring with high-strength threaded rebars and underpinning the existing foundation with a new foundation, the new and existing foundations are integrated into a composite foundation system with coordinated load-bearing behavior. title: Design, Finite Element Analysis, and Experimental Investigation of Basalt Fiber Reinforced Polymer (BFRP) Composite for Oil and Gas Applications
abstract: The pipelines used for transporting oil and gas need to have sufficient strength, durability, and resistance to any form of corrosion. The usual metallic pipes are prone to corrosion and weigh quite a lot. In this research, the use of Basalt Fiber Reinforced Polymer Composite Pipe has been studied using computer aided design and finite element analysis among others. A BFRP pipe with 200 mm length, 50 mm inner diameter, and 10 mm wall thickness was modeled using orthotropic material property assumptions and studied under an internal pressure of 55 MPa. title: Early Neolithic genomes suggest a local origin for millet farmers in East Asia
abstract: Millet cultivation in northern China served as a critical catalyst for Neolithic sedentism and East Asian civilization, yet the demographic origins of the inaugural millet farmers remain contentious. We analyze genome-wide data from seven individuals from the Donghulin (DHL), Dengcaogouliang, and Sitai sites, spanning 11,000 to 7300 years ago, and identify the DHL lineage as the predominant genetic structure in inland northern East Asia following the Last Glacial Maximum. title: Renewable Energy Use in Small Rural Towns: A Case Study of Thulamela Local Municipality, South Africa
abstract: This manuscript explores the use of renewable energy (RE) in small towns to promote sustainable human settlements, using Thohoyandou as a case study. An exploratory research design underpinned the study. Using a combination of primary and secondary data collection methods, a randomised sample of 125 households in Thohoyandou town was selected, along with 15 purposively selected key informant interviewees. title: Relevance of pesticides for macroinvertebrate communities in agricultural streams – a re-evaluation
abstract: Attributing ecological impairment in agricultural streams to individual stressors is a common challenge in freshwater monitoring because pesticide exposure often co-occurs with habitat degradation, nutrient enrichment, oxygen depletion, and other environmental pressures. The German ‘small water bodies monitoring project’ (‘Kleingewässermonitoring’, KgM) provides an opportunity to examine this challenge using a large-scale field dataset. title: Learning Management to Promote Future Skills for Student Teachers: A Case Study of Social Studies Student Teachers at Songkhla Rajabhat University, Thailand
abstract: This mixed-methods case study examined instructional management and future-skill needs in higher-education social studies teacher preparation, developed community-based learning activities for the Social Studies Pedagogy course, and examined changes in six future-skill domains among student teachers. The participants were 30 third-year Social Studies student teachers enrolled at Songkhla Rajabhat University in the first semester of the 2025 academic year. title: Rising global population coexposure to heatwaves and landscape fire-sourced air pollution
abstract: Landscape fires are increasingly threatening public health by causing substantial fire-sourced air pollution (SFAP), with risks amplified during heatwaves. We investigated the global spatial, temporal, and sociodemographic distribution of the population coexposure to heatwaves and SFAP from 2000 to 2019. We found that 52.4% of populated areas and 55.9% of the global population experienced increasing coexposure. title: CFD investigation of a novel gabion-based porous medium configuration for energy dissipation in ogee spillway stilling basins
abstract: Ogee spillways which provide very large discharge rates are extensively employed for civil engineering applications, but high velocity flows generated by Ogee spillways can be seriously harmful to downstream structures. This numerical investigation is conducted to assess the potential of adding porous media (uniform gabions and cross shaped gabions, with varying porosities: 30%, 40% and 50%) to the stilling basin at the bottom of ogee spillways to dissipate energy. title: Molecular evolution of oxygenated organic molecules in a cloud-influenced forested mountain environment
abstract: Abstract. Atmospheric oxygenated organic molecules (OOMs) link the oxidation of volatile organic compound to secondary organic aerosol formation, yet their molecular evolution in cloud-influenced forested mountain environments remains poorly constrained. Here, gas-phase OOMs were measured using an iodide-adduct chemical ionization mass spectrometer at a high-altitude forested station in southeastern China during autumn 2023. abstract: It is my pleasure to publish the October issue (4th issue) of Vol. 3 of the International Journal of Bridge engineering, Management and Research. In this issue, we are pleased to bring to you six papers in innovative areas of bridge engineering.

title: Plasma-Driven Combustion of Aerosolized Energetic Ionic Liquids
abstract: Abstract We demonstrate plasma-driven combustion of energetic aerosolized ionic liquids under flowing conditions. A mixture of hydroxylammonium nitrate (HAN) and 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium ethyl sulfate ([EMIM][EtSO4]) is atomized through high-pressure injection into a nozzle, where HAN serves as the oxidizer, similar to the monopropellant AF-M315E (i.e., ASCENT), and EtSO4 provides the fuel. title: Fruit-eating adaptations in a Late Cretaceous oviraptorosaur (Theropoda)
abstract: Abstract The diversification of herbivorous dinosaurs and the rise of angiosperms in the Late Cretaceous are each well established, but the link between them is debated. Broad-scale diversity patterns in the two groups appear not to closely align, and there is no direct evidence of dinosaur adaptation to angiosperm-based diets. Here we describe Infernogallus jamesi gen. et. sp. nov., a diminutive caenagnathid oviraptorosaur, and show that these theropods were specialised herbivores that originated alongside the rise of fleshy angiosperm fruits. title: Comparative Study of Hydrogen Yield from Organic-Rich Lithologies: Implications for Sustainable Energy
abstract: Abstract The growing global demand for clean and sustainable energy has increased interest in hydrogen as an alternative fuel that is both affordable and widely accessible. While substantial research has focused on hydrogen generation through serpentinization, the potential of organic-rich systems remains largely unexplored. Addressing this gap requires systematic analysis of various organic-rich materials such as shale, carbonate rocks, and coal to evaluate their capacity to release hydrogen gas under different geological conditions. title: Three-parameter Kerr soil model: finite element formulation and applications in transient dynamic analyses
abstract: Soil-structure interaction is a topic of paramount importance in civil engineering, as the method of soil modeling directly influences the static and dynamic performance of structures supported by elastic foundations. Simplified models, such as Winkler's, while widely adopted, fail to adequately represent the effects of distributed stiffness and lateral interaction. In this context, multiparameter models, like those proposed by Pasternak and Kerr, offer a more realistic characterization of soil behavior. title: Signs of power: giant ficron handaxes may have played a non-utilitarian role in structuring social groups in MIS 9 Britain
abstract: Giant ficrons are a rare but recurrent sub-type of Acheulean handaxe, that in Britain are predominantly found in assemblages dating to the MIS 9 interglacial. A variety of theories have aimed to explain the striking size and appearance of giant ficrons as reflecting their use in specialised subsistence tasks or non-utilitarian display functions. Despite this, they are typically underrepresented or absent from many studies concerning giant handaxes or Acheulean morphological diversity more broadly. title: Transport and fate of radon: a critical review of mechanisms and environmental influences
abstract: Radon is a naturally occurring radioactive gas produced from the decay of uranium-238. It poses significant environmental health risks because it can migrate through soil, groundwater, and air before accumulating indoors. This review, based on a critical synthesis of 94 peer-reviewed publications (2009–2025), explores how radon moves and behaves, emphasising diffusion, advection, and dissolution, and the influence of soil properties, groundwater flow, building characteristics, and human activities. title: Collaborative Policy Modeling for Ecotourism Conservation and Development: A Multi-Case Empirical Study Based on Policy Instrument Taxonomy
abstract: The synergistic imbalance between conservation and development remains a core constraint on the sustainable development of ecotourism. Grounded in externality theory, this study constructs a three-dimensional modeling framework that integrates the quantification of positive externalities from ecological conservation, the pricing of negative externalities from tourism development, and the adaptation of policy instruments. title: Design and mechanical performance analysis of re-entrant auxetic structures fabricated using SLA 3D printing: a comparative study
abstract: Auxetic structures, with a negative Poisson’s ratio, have gained significant attention for aerospace and automotive applications due to their superior mechanical performance. In this study, two different Auxetic Structures were used, namely Re–entrant Hexagon (A) and Re-entrant star triangular structure (B). They were designed and fabricated with the use of Stereolithography (SLA) Additive Manufacturing with the use of Standard Photopolymer Resin Material. title: Using forest structural complexity and topography metrics to characterise vertical microclimatic stratification
abstract: Understanding how topography and forest structure drive the transformation of incoming solar energy into local microclimatic conditions is essential for predicting forest resilience under climate change. Quantifying the importance of such attributes on the stratification of microclimates requires the integration of heterogeneous ecological data streams. title: Aerodynamic Characteristics and Wind Load Partitioning in Double-deck Girders: Effects of Inter-deck Clearance Height
abstract: The inter-deck clearance height (IDH), defined as the vertical distance between decks, is a key parameter in the aerodynamic design of double-deck bridges. This parameter governs both global aerodynamic characteristics and the allocation of wind loads across different subcomponents (top/bottom decks, windward/leeward trusses) of the girder, yet its effects remain underexplored. This study examines the effects of IDH using five double-deck girders with varying IDH, combining wind tunnel tests and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations. title: Numerical Investigations of a Novel Offshore Platform Blast Wall Design Using Energy Absorption Devices at Supports
abstract: Abstract Offshore blast walls are critical safety barriers designed to protect personnel and equipment from hydrocarbon explosions. Traditional designs often struggle to simultaneously satisfy code requirements for deflection limits and weld integrity under high-intensity blasts. This study proposes a novel offshore blast wall concept incorporating energy-absorbing support devices comprising PMI foam-filled sliding cores and rotational springs. title: Crashworthiness assessment of thin-walled columns with functionally graded stiffness induced by multi-level spherical crush initiators
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the crashworthiness performance of thin-walled columns equipped with functionally graded, multi-level spherical crush initiators. The proposed concept extends previous solutions by introducing a sequence of embossments with varying diameters and depths along the column height, enabling controlled variation in local structural deformation resistance and progressive folding under impact loading. title: CT image-based experimental and numerical simulation methods for freeze–thaw concrete microstructure
abstract: Freeze–thaw cycling is a primary durability challenge for concrete structures in cold regions. This study presents an integrated experimental and numerical approach to visualize and quantify mesoscale freeze–thaw damage evolution in concrete. Indoor rapid freeze–thaw tests were conducted, combined with computed tomography (CT) scanning for three-dimensional (3D) microstructure reconstruction and finite element (FE) simulation for damage analysis. title: Textural and Geochemical Evidence for Melt Extraction from a Magma Mush in Aztec Wash Pluton (Nevada, USA)
abstract: Abstract Melt extraction is a critical process for the formation of eruptible magmas. Magmatic textures and compositions illuminate magma dynamics during the emplacement of a large (2 m diameter) felsic enclave (LFE) within granitic mush in the Aztec Wash pluton (15.7 Ma, NV-USA). The LFE is an ellipsoidal microgranite mass inferred to have been nearly solid when it settled at the top of a crystal-rich zone of the magma body. abstract: Abstract Conventional improvement methods applied to sabkha soil (collapse soil) are time-consuming, lengthening the project schedule. This paper introduces a pre-loaded, pre-moistened shallow foundation that deliberately triggers the collapse mechanism under controlled construction conditions. title: Comparative Study of Piled Raft and Deep Foundation Systems for a 13-Storey Academic Building in Surabaya
abstract: Foundation selection for a multistorey building on soft ground is governed not only by pile capacity, but also by settlement, load sharing, construction constraints, and cost. This paper compares the original deep-foundation design for an academic building in Surabaya with two piled-raft alternatives. The building has 13 main floors, one roof level, and an overall height of 56 m. The original system comprises 251 driven piles, 0.60 m in diameter and 30 m long, connected by 1.20 m thick pile caps. abstract: Abstract Broadband low-frequency vibration attenuation in lightweight sandwich structures remains challenging because conventional multi-resonator designs offer limited freedom for bandgap engineering under stringent spatial constraints. Here we introduce a metasandwich plate with asymmetric circular resonators (MPACR), in which broadband bandgaps are achieved through configurational asymmetry rather than increased structural complexity. title: Numerical evaluation of hydraulic performance of a laboratory-scale Archimedes screw pump
abstract: Archimedes screw pump (ASP) is a type of positive displacement pump for transporting water from lower to upper incline elevations. It is a simple and robust pump widely used for irrigation, flood mitigation, and in wastewater treatment plants. Although ASPs have been used for centuries, there is a lack of literature related to the optimal hydraulic performance and elucidating the underlying flow mechanisms. abstract: This study investigates the evolution of the internal chemical environment in autoclaved high-performance concrete (HPC) and the determination of the critical threshold for steel passivation. Conventional extraction methods are limited by the solubility product of Portland cement, obscuring the true pore solution chemistry. abstract: Abstract. Termites are major detritivores in tropical and subtropical ecosystems, yet their contributions to the terrestrial carbon cycle remains absent from process-based soil organic carbon (SOC) models. Here, we present a termite carbon module that explicitly represents termite-mediated litter consumption and transfer of ingested carbon into gaseous (CO2, CH4) and SOC pools. abstract: The elevated operating temperature of photovoltaic (PV) modules in hot and arid regions accelerates performance degradation, reduces electricity generation, and adversely affects long-term economic viability. This study presents a comprehensive long-term comparative thermo-economic assessment of a closed-loop hydronic PV cooling system integrated with an above-ground water tank (PV-AGWT) and a common PV system (PV-Com) under hot and arid climatic conditions of Basra, Iraq. abstract: This study evaluates the hydraulic performance of four structural flood-mitigation alternatives using a two-dimensional HEC-RAS model for a 50 km reach of the Koshi River between Chatara and the Koshi Barrage, Nepal. A 100-year design flood (27,401 m³ s⁻¹), estimated via Generalized Extreme Value flood-frequency analysis, was applied as the upstream boundary condition for existing-condition and alternative scenarios. abstract: Abstract Safe CO 2 storage requires injection designs that manage both when faults yield and how yielding spreads, yet temporal schedules and well layouts are often evaluated separately. We developed a two-dimensional quasi-static hydromechanical model of immiscible CO 2 –brine flow around an offset normal fault and compared constant and variable-rate histories, well-placement configurations, and well–fault distances over 30 d. title: A Strategy of Additional Carbon Acquisition by Non-Foliar Photosynthesis: Implication for Yield
abstract: Abstract Photosynthesis is traditionally studied in leaves, but it extends beyond foliar tissues to non-foliar organs (e.g. stems, fruits, sepals, and seeds) offering an underexplored avenue for enhancing plant productivity. This review investigates physiological, biochemical, and developmental roles related to non-foliar photosynthesis, emphasizing its contributions to carbon assimilation and crop production under varying environmental conditions by presenting an extensive compilation of published data with relevant studies. title: Fatigue crack growth in elastomers for leading-edge erosion protection of wind turbine blades
abstract: Abstract. Fatigue crack growth has been observed as a prominent damage mode in rain erosion of wind-turbine blades, where it is driven by cyclic pulse loading from liquid-droplet impacts. This study investigates fatigue crack growth in a thermoplastic polyurethane elastomer used for leading-edge protection, linking repeated droplet impacts to controlled cyclic loading in a lab test. abstract: Abstract This study targets the ultradeep, high-temperature, and high-pressure carbonate reservoirs in the Penglai Gas Area, Sichuan Basin. The existing acid fracturing technologies have ambiguous stimulation mechanisms and are difficult to regulate accurately. We conducted a series of physical experiments on the alternating injection of gelled acid and drag-reducing acid, aiming to optimize acid fracturing techniques and improve the reservoir stimulation performance. abstract: Abstract. Better understanding how convective processes impact the isotopic composition of atmospheric water has implications for understanding present-day phenomena such as squall lines or tropical cyclones, and for reconstructions of past rainfall extreme events. With this motivation, we implemented water stable isotopes in the non-hydrostatic mesoscale atmospheric model Meso-NH. title: Assessing WRF simulations for thermal forecasting in paragliding flights
abstract: Abstract Generated by differential surface heating within the atmospheric boundary layer (ABL), thermals are essential for sustaining flight in non-motorized aviation such as paragliding, hang gliding, and gliding. Despite their relevance, operational thermal forecasting remains limited, particularly at the spatial scales relevant for recreational flights. abstract: Abstract. The brittle damage around tunnels in the form of spalling is common in massive crystalline rocks subjected to high in-situ stresses. Understanding the short-term development and long-term evolution of the Excavation Damage Zone (EDZ) is particularly important for deep geological repositories (DGRs) for heat-generating nuclear waste, as the EDZ may provide preferential pathways for radionuclide migration. abstract: Abstract We classify within the quasi-geostrophic framework all types of traveling waves in zonal bands of the planetary atmosphere at cloud level according to their wave speeds. abstract: The rapid development of western China has intensified the human‑land conflict in the gully regions of the Loess Plateau, prompting local governments to reclaim land through loess high‑fill foundations (LHFF) to support urban construction. Due to the unique engineering properties of loess and the large thickness of compacted fill, LHFF undergo significant settlement during both the construction and post‑construction stages, posing challenges to subsequent engineering works. title: Self-Priming Centrifugal Chemical Pumps: A Review
abstract: This paper gives a thorough examination of the literature of self-priming centrifugal chemical pumps, focusing on their design, operational principles, and applications in various industries. They render surpassing advantages, including improved efficiency in handling liquids containing air or gas, and reduced maintenance requirements. abstract: This study aims to evaluate the HYDRUS-2D model’s ability to simulate soil water content in the soil profile under sweet sorghum with drip irrigation at different lateral depths and irrigation levels. abstract: Compound climate extremes pose an increasingly severe threat to our societies, ecosystems, and economies under climate change. abstract: Abstract. Green roofs mitigate urban heat, but to fully assess their impact, green roof models must be integrated into urban climate models, where they provide critical surface boundary conditions. abstract: The proliferation of hyperscale data centers, together with tightening carbon-neutrality targets, exposes the limits of the line-frequency transformer (LFT) that still dominates data-center power distribution and motivates a fresh look at the conversion and dispatch layer. title: Landscape Architecture and Health: An Umbrella Review
abstract: Landscape architecture influences environmental conditions related to health, but evidence on how design features impact health is scattered across disciplines. The review aims to assess the evidence, identify pathways to health, and guide collaboration between landscape architects and public health professionals. abstract: This study numerically investigates the seismic response of corroded underground reinforced concrete (RC) culverts strengthened using various methods. This will lead to many adverse effects such as increasing health risks and mortality rates, making climate change adaptation crucial for future urban planning. abstract: Abstract. Drone-based atmospheric measurements allow time-resolved investigation of stratification in the lower atmosphere of many atmospherically relevant variables. abstract: Abstract Since its discovery in 2001, magnesium diboride (MgB₂) has attracted significant interest for large-scale superconducting applications due to its high transition temperature (39 K), low material cost, and weak crystallographic anisotropy. abstract: Climate change is intensifying overheating risks in cities, where the Urban Heat Island effect and increasingly severe recent heatwaves are driving up thermal stress, cooling demand, and outdoor discomfort. abstract: Continuous monitoring of intraocular pressure (IOP) is essential for the diagnosis and management of glaucoma, yet existing clinical methods rely on intermittent in-clinic measurements that miss critical diurnal fluctuations. Smart contact lenses are an attractive platform for continuous IOP tracking, and optical strain sensors are particularly promising thanks to their high sensitivity and natural readout. abstract: Muography with scintillator-based detectors enables the investigation of density distributions within large structures. abstract: A long-standing challenge in climate science since the Charney Report in 1979 is to determine how much the Earth's climate warms in response to a unit external energy input at the top of the atmosphere (TOA). abstract: Covert communication conceals wireless transmission activity, but conventional multi-antenna designs rely mainly on spatial beamforming and can be constrained by limited spatial degrees of freedom. This paper investigates polarization-reconfigurable antenna (PRA)-aided multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) covert communication, where Alice and Bob perform transmit and receive polarforming, respectively, and Willie uses a vertically polarized antenna for radiometric detection. We jointly optimize the transmit covariance matrix and the transmit and receive phase shift vectors to maximize Bob's a

Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

title: Finite Cumulant Towers for Small-System-Noise Expansions in Nonlinear Filtering
abstract: We study asymptotic expansions for nonlinear filtering in the small-system-noise regime. Our main result is that the expansion coefficients of conditional cumulants satisfy a closed finite-dimensional system that can be solved recursively. At each expansion degree, the evolution of a coefficient introduces a coefficient of the next higher cumulant rank, while a high-rank vanishing property terminates this hierarchy, yielding a finite triangular tower. title: The hadronic-vacuum-polarization contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment in isospin-symmetric lattice QCD with twisted-mass fermions
abstract: We present a lattice-QCD calculation of the leading-order hadronic-vacuum-polarization (HVP) contribution to the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in isospin-symmetric QCD. We employ the gauge configurations generated by the Extended Twisted Mass Collaboration (ETMC) with $N_f = 2 + 1 + 1$ flavors of Wilson-clover twisted-mass quarks at four lattice spacings and at values of the quark-mass parameters matching the definition of isospin-symmetric QCD given in the FLAG review 2024 and in the 2025 edition of the Muon $g-2$ Theory Initiative White Paper (WP25). title: Stationary Resistive MHD Solutions Near an Isolated Three-Dimensional Magnetic Null
abstract: Magnetic null points define the magnetic field topology in stellar coronae, planetary magnetospheres, and astrospheres, and are commonly associated with magnetic reconnection. We investigate the local structure of stationary three-dimensional (3D) resistive, incompressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) flows in the vicinity of an isolated magnetic null and an isolated velocity stagnation point, assuming that the two nulls are colocated. title: DeboRheo v2.0: Improved Robustness for Geometrical VOF Simulations of Viscoelastic Two-Phase Flows
abstract: We present DeboRheo v2.0, an unstructured, geometrically unsplit Volume-of-Fluid framework implemented in OpenFOAM for viscoelastic two-phase flows. Version 2.0 improves numerical robustness when large viscosity contrasts coincide with strongly deformed interfaces and thin viscoelastic lamellae or filaments. The revised interfacial viscosity treatment retains a sharp geometric interface while regularizing the viscous contribution to the momentum equation. title: Accessing electronic entanglement via photo-assisted two-electron tomography
abstract: Witnessing entanglement between electrons propagating in quantum circuits requires accessing their two-electron coherences, which encode the two-particle quantum correlations generated by Coulomb interactions. Yet, experimental reconstruction of two-electron coherence remains a major challenge. We introduce photo-assisted two-electron tomography, a quantum coherence reconstruction protocol from dc-currents and time-averaged current correlations, routinely measured in electron quantum optics experiments. title: Global ice loss drives source-independent amplification of sea-level rise at Pacific and Indian Ocean Small Island Developing States
abstract: Abstract We quantify the spatial pattern (“fingerprint”) of sea-level rise caused by mass loss from the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets and from glaciers worldwide through 2100. Using ensembles of ice-sheet and glacier mass-balance projections and gravitational, rotational, and deformational sea-level modeling, we calculate normalized sea-level fingerprints and their impacts on Small Island Developing States. title: DNA-based monitoring uncovers contrasting salinity-driven diversity patterns of bacterial and protist plankton in the Baltic Sea area
abstract: Salinity has been identified as a primary factor structuring community composition in global diversity assessments of free-living bacteria in non-extreme environments. It remains unknown whether the same is true for protists. Moreover, changes in alpha diversity of both bacteria and protists across the brackish salinity gradient remain elusive. Here, we analyzed protist and bacterial diversity using DNA metabarcoding across 398 surface water samples synchronized with national monitoring of the Baltic Sea and the Kattegat-Skagerrak. title: Plankton Ecology in the Philippines: Diversity, Dynamics, and Ecological Significance Across Tropical Marine and Freshwater Ecosystems
abstract: Plankton communities in the Philippines occupy a critical ecological position in one of the world's most biologically diverse marine regions. Situated within the Coral Triangle and traversed by the Western Pacific Warm Pool, Philippine waters support extraordinary phytoplankton and zooplankton assemblages that regulate primary production, mediate carbon fluxes, and sustain the productivity of pelagic and coastal fisheries. Yet these communities are shaped by complex interactions among the Southwest and Northeast Monsoons, seasonal upwelling, El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) events, eutrophi
institutions: University of Science and Technology of Southern Philippines

title: Multiple strategies and cues define baleen whale migration
abstract: Migration is a do-or-die life-history strategy, yet factors shaping it remain poorly studied in many marine taxa, as direct observations are difficult. Building on animal migration theory, we used satellite tracking data from 21 southern right whales tagged in Aotearoa New Zealand to investigate migratory cues, timing and routes. Whales followed either a direct westward route or a longer, indirect route via higher latitudes when migrating from their wintering grounds to summer feeding grounds. title: Hidden subsurface suspended sediment export from Greenland's marine‐terminating glaciers
abstract: Abstract Runoff and calved ice volumes from the Greenland Ice Sheet are well constrained, but quantifying the associated suspended sediment flux remains challenging. Here we present near‐terminus observations from three glacierized fjords in southeast Greenland, combining full‐depth turbidity profiles and current velocity from summer 2024 to evaluate sediment export. We identify extensive subsurface sediment plumes from marine‐terminating glaciers which are undetectable using remote sensing approaches and underrepresented in fjord sediment‐core reconstructions. Southern University of Science and Technology

title: Ancient terrestrial forests reborn as modern marine ecosystems under shifting sea levels
abstract: Abstract Sea-level rise and coastal erosion can submerge terrestrial carbon-rich landscapes, yet the ecological fate and climate significance of such relict coastal carbon deposits remain largely unknown. We report the discovery of submerged tropical peat reefs in the shallow coastal waters of the Bazaruto Archipelago, Mozambique; a legacy of ancient coastal forests now transformed into benthic marine habitats. title: Ocean acidification pushes Mediterranean marine calcifiers toward a tipping point
abstract: Abstract The increasing emission of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) is altering seawater chemistry, lowering ocean pH and threatening marine biodiversity. Predicting how marine biota will be adversely affected by ocean acidification (OA) remains a key challenge. Here, we document that functional morphological traits offer a more robust metric of calcifier sensitivity to OA than taxonomic diversity alone. Using benthic foraminifera from a Mediterranean CO 2 vent system, we identify an empirically derived pH threshold beyond which community structure and function shift markedly. institutions: Centre for Arctic Gas Hydrate, Environment and Climate

title: Contrasting microbiomes in deep-sea scleractinian and octocoral species from the South Atlantic Ocean
abstract: Abstract Deep-sea corals (DSC) are ecologically important, yet their microbiomes’ composition, structure, and host specificity remain largely unresolved in the South Atlantic, especially for octocorals. Here, we provide a comprehensive characterisation of DSC microbiomes, spanning Hexacorallia (Desmophyllum pertusum, Solenosmilia variabilis) and Octocorallia (Candidella imbricata, three Malacalcyonacea species), collected at ∼710 m depth in the Campos Basin, an active oil- and gas-producing region. institutions: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

title: TERRITORIAL, AGROECOLOGICAL AND TECHNOLOGICAL FOUNDATIONS FOR ORGANIZING DIGITAL AGROCHEMICAL SERVICES UNDER THE CONDITIONS OF THE ARAL SEA REGION
abstract: The article examines the territorial, agroecological and technological foundations for organizing digital agrochemical services under the conditions of the Aral Sea region. Major agroecological challenges affecting agricultural soils, including salinization, nutrient imbalance, declining soil organic matter and limited water resources, are considered. The role of GIS, GPS, remote sensing, digital agrochemical databases and digital mapping technologies in developing an integrated agrochemical service is substantiated. The integration of agrochemical soil parameters with geospatial information p
journal: Eurasian Journal of Medical and Natural Sciences

title: Integrating Strategic Environmental Assessment into Regional Development Planning for Sustainable Development in Bireuen Regency
abstract: Regional planning in Bireuen has to respond to basic-service needs while also dealing with pressure on watersheds, forested land, and areas exposed to hydro-meteorological hazards. This paper examines how far the 2025-2029 Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is carried into the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (Indonesian term: Rencana Pembangunan Jangka Menengah Daerah/RPJMD), rather than remaining a separate compliance document. SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT FOR ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION IN BANGLADESH: CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES
abstract: Bangladesh exemplifies a central paradox of sustainable development: how to maintain rapid economic and social progress without undermining the ecological systems upon which development depends. This paper critically examines Bangladesh's environmental governance architecture, the major barriers to its effective implementation, and opportunities for achieving a just green transition. It adopts a qualitative, desk-based methodology combining doctrinal legal analysis with critical examination of national policies and plans, international commitments, judicial decisions, and institutional reports
journal: Journal of Asian and African Social Science and Humanities

title: Ziviler Katastrophenschutz: Einbindung von Bürgerinnen und Bürgern in Hochwasserszenarien und Sturmfluten mit mobilen Anwendungen
abstract: Zusammenfassung Der Klimawandel erhöht das Risiko von Sturmfluten und Hochwasserereignissen und stellt bestehende Warn- und Krisenkommunikationssysteme vor wachsende Herausforderungen. Aus Forschungsperspektive fehlt es daher an bürgerzentrierten Anforderungen und Gestaltungsprinzipien für mobile Krisenanwendungen, die über reine Warnfunktionen hinausgehen. title: The integrated benthic silicate flux in the Baltic Sea suggests a major land- or freshwater-derived reactive silicon source
abstract: Abstract. Coastal marine environments are hot spots in the global marine silicon (Si) cycle. Dissolved silicate (DSi) is an essential macronutrient for diatoms, which often dominate primary productivity in temporal coastal seas and constitute a key food source for grazers. Even though benthic release of DSi influences the ecology of coastal marine areas, direct rate measurements of DSi mobilisation remain scarce.
