title: Survival and divergence of Arctic endemic cod species during 50,000 years of climate change
abstract: Despite significant climate variability in the Northern Hemisphere ~50,000-12,000 years ago, the potential for vertebrates to periodically thrive in the glacial Arctic Ocean has been largely overlooked because ecosystem productivity was assumed to be too low. Here, we analyze fish otoliths preserved in deep-sea sediments and find that two Arctic endemic cod species, ice cod (Arctogadus glacialis) and polar cod (Boreogadus saida), lived at 87-89 °N ~ 48,000-35,000 years ago and reappeared at the onset of the Holocene ~12,000 years ago. title: An Ecosystem-Based Marine Spatial Planning Approach for Sustainable Natural Resources Management in the Bangladesh Delta
abstract: Despite the establishment of maritime boundaries with Myanmar (2012) and India (2014), which secured sovereign rights over approximately 118,813 km² of the Bay of Bengal, marine space is still managed on a sector-by-sector basis, and no marine spatial plan has been prepared. This study identifies significant ecological, economic, and cultural areas within Bangladesh's maritime zone, and proposes a framework for the blue economy and develops an ecosystem-based model of marine spatial planning (MSP). title: Cardiac responses to underwater sound playback in juvenile green and loggerhead sea turtles: an exploratory biologging study
abstract: Anthropogenic underwater noise is an increasing concern in marine environments, yet physiological responses of sea turtles remain poorly understood. We examined cardiac responses to underwater sound playback in three juvenile green turtles (Chelonia mydas) and four juvenile loggerhead turtles (Caretta caretta) maintained after incidental capture. Electrocardiogram, acceleration, depth, and turtle-borne acoustic data were recorded during 44 trials. title: Multilocus phylogeny and historical biogeography of the pill millipede genus Rhopalomeris (Diplopoda, Glomerida) in Thailand
abstract: Abstract Southeast Asia is widely recognized as a global biodiversity hotspot with a complex geological history and high species richness across multiple taxa. The pill millipede genus Rhopalomeris Verhoeff, 1906 has received increasing taxonomic attention in recent years, with several new species described, particularly from western Southeast Asia, including Thailand and Myanmar. However, its historical biogeography has remained insufficiently understood. title: ECOCRITICAL PERSPECTIVES ON INTO THE BENEATH: GREG GARRARD’S FRAMEWORK IN DEPICTING MARINE ENVIRONMENTAL CRISES
abstract: This study aims to explore ecological phenomena in Rifqi Farizi’s novel Into the Beneath through the framework of Greg Garrard’s ecocriticism. The research focuses on identifying and analyzing the representation of five key ecological categories: pollution, apocalypse, dwelling, animals, and earth. The objective is to reveal how the novel reflects contemporary ecological anxieties and provides critical perspectives on humanity’s relationship with the ocean as a vital yet vulnerable ecosystem. title: Spatial disparities in surf-resource sustainability: Implications for coastal policy and marine education in Taiwan
abstract: This study situates global surf sustainability within the Taiwanese context, where recreational surfing has developed since the 1980s and expanded internationally after 2010, yet region-wide assessments of surf-resource sustainability remain limited. Little is known about how sustainability conditions vary across Taiwan’s coastal regions, which sustainability dimensions contribute most strongly to these disparities, and what implications such patterns have for coastal governance and marine education policy. title: Temperate marine macrophytes are highly variable sources of Biogenic Volatile Organic Compounds – a comparative study from the Baltic Sea and NE Atlantic
abstract: Abstract. Biogenic Volatile Organic Compounds (BVOC), emitted by Earth’s ecosystems, affect several chemical processes in the atmosphere that have profound climate impacts. Despite their climate relevance, global BVOC budget estimations are still highly uncertain, with ocean-derived emissions being particularly poorly constrained. Marine macrophytes (i.e. macroalgae and seagrass) are a large and widespread organismal group whose BVOC emission rates are particularly poorly quantified. title: A source-to-sea decision-support framework for wet-weather wastewater load management: evidence from Jiaozhou Bay
abstract: Coastal concentration compliance can overlook increased wastewater throughput during wet weather. We developed a source-to-sea decision-support framework using 2019–2022 wastewater, river, and marine observations from Jiaozhou Bay, China. The analysis combined source-record auditing, hydraulic and concentration decomposition, benchmark comparison, and source–receptor chronology. At Loushan wastewater treatment plant, throughput increased by 87.5% from the second to the third quarter of 2020 while total phosphorus remained low at 0.06–0.07 mg L −1 . title: Geography Teaching Methods and Tools in the Republic of Kosovo
abstract: Методите и средствата за обучение са основни елементи в преподаването на география. Те позволяват ефективното усвояване на знания, умения и навици, като същевременно развиват мисленето, вниманието и мотивацията на учениците. Използването на съвременни технологии, като Google Earth, Google Maps, Bing и ГИС, улеснява визуализацията, анализа и разширяват възможностите за виртуални пътувания и изследвания. journal: Общество памет образование (История и обществени нагласи)

title: Acceptability of a Novel Prehospital Emergency Care System Evaluation Tool Among Southeast Asian Stakeholders: A Cross-Sectional Survey
abstract: Introduction: Prehospital emergency care (PEC) systems vary widely in structure, capacity, and stage of development, and existing evaluation tools are not tailored to the contextual needs of Southeast Asia. To address this gap, the Prehospital Emergency Care System Evaluation Tool (PECSET) was developed as a 32-element, consensus-derived framework to support system assessment, prioritization, and quality improvement. title: When the lights come on: The hidden carbon cost of a brightening world
abstract: Abstract Nighttime satellite imagery has long served as a proxy for human development, equating light with progress and darkness with poverty. Here, we argue that this framing obscures a critical climate reality: the world's darkest regions, dominated by smallholder agriculture across central Africa, Southeast Asia, and the remote tropics, are simultaneously low‐emission zones and active carbon sinks, a dual function overlooked by Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), national Paris Agreement pledges for greenhouse gas reductions. title: FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT AND EXPORT SOPHISTICATION IN ASEAN-5 DURING THE ASEAN PLUS THREE COOPERATION PERIOD
abstract: Export sophistication is widely regarded as a channel through which trade contributes to sustained growth, yet evidence on its relationship with foreign direct investment (FDI) in Southeast Asia during the period of deepening ASEAN Plus Three (ASEAN+3) cooperation remains limited. This study examines trade with China, Japan, and the Republic of Korea (South Korea) and the relationship between FDI inflows and export sophistication in five ASEAN economies (Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand) over the period of the ASEAN Plus Three Cooperation Work Plan 2007-2017. title: Experimental snowball earth viscosity drives the evolution of motile multicellularity
abstract: Abstract During the 70-million-year span of the Cryogenian Snowball Earth glaciations, low ocean temperatures beneath global sea ice increased water viscosity up to fourfold. In the absence of adaptation, unicellular organisms living in this viscous environment were limited in their ability to move and acquire nutrients. We experimentally test the hypothesis that multicellularity evolved in order to overcome this viscosity-induced metabolic deficit. title: Gestión territorial y herramientas de apoyo a la decisión para la recolección de residuos en ciudades turísticas. El caso de Pinamar
abstract: El artículo aborda la gestión urbana de la recolección de residuos en ciudades turísticas caracterizadas por una marcada variabilidad estacional de la demanda, tomando al Partido de Pinamar, provincia de Buenos Aires, como caso de estudio. El objetivo es desarrollar una propuesta metodológico-operativa para el análisis y la gestión del servicio mediante la integración de variables territoriales, temporales y operativas. Metodológicamente, la investigación combina revisión bibliográfica y normativa, relevamiento territorial, entrevista semiestructurada a un supervisor de la empresa prestataria
institutions: Universidad de Ciencias Empresariales y Sociales

title: Baltic Sea sediment bacterial communities show asymmetric and incomplete recovery after reciprocal temperature change translocation
abstract: Abstract Marine coastal systems are important for global biogeochemical cycling and are particularly sensitive to climate change effects due to their shallow depths, which results in rapid heat transfer to the sediments. Here we used one-year reciprocal in situ translocations of sediments between a Baltic Sea long-term (>50 years) warming-influenced bay and a nearby unaffected control bay to predict how the sediments and their associated bacterial communities may respond to future climate change and whether those changes were reversible. title: Nonlinear ocean wave propagation in a fractional perturbed Gerdjikov–Ivanov model with higher-order dispersive effects
abstract: Nonlinear dispersive wave propagation governs complex physical phenomena in both nonlinear optics and hydrodynamics, including optical fiber communications, ultrafast photonic systems, coastal environments, and marine systems, where higher-order nonlinear interactions and dispersive effects significantly influence wave evolution. title: Rapid coral bleaching recovery via symbiont transfer from healthy corals
abstract: Coral bleaching, the temperature-induced loss of dinoflagellate symbionts, is a major driver of global coral reef decline. Although corals can regain symbionts through repopulation of residual symbionts or via environmental acquisition, these processes are often too slow to prevent coral mortality. Mechanisms that enable rapid and effective symbiont reintroduction leading to full recovery remain largely unknown. title: Remobilized volcanogenic sediments boost photophysiological activity in three symbiotic reef-building coral species
abstract: Abstract Coral reefs that surround volcanic islands are continually influenced by run-off carrying remobilized volcanogenic sediments. Although unaltered volcanic ash is known to supply trace metals that enhance coral holobiont productivity, the impacts of long-term exposure to weathered tephra, a far more likely scenario in island settings, are less understood. institutions: GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel

title: Spatial assessment of wind–surge compound risk and vulnerability during Hurricane Ian: a GIS-based case study of Lee County, Florida
abstract: Global climate change and sea-level rise have intensified tropical cyclone–induced wind–surge compound risks, while rapid county-scale risk assessment remains difficult without field investigations. This study develops a GIS- and Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP)-based Composite Hurricane Risk Index (CHRI) framework for Lee County, Florida, U.S.A., affected by Category 4 Hurricane Ian in 2022. title: Particle-tracking assessment of potential groundwater pathways for radionuclide transport across the Futaba Fault, coastal Fukushima, Japan
abstract: Radiocesium deposited after the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant accident remains a long-term environmental concern, but its groundwater pathways toward inhabited coastal lowlands are poorly constrained. This study evaluates conservative groundwater pathways potentially relevant to radionuclide transport near the Futaba Fault in coastal Fukushima by coupling a steady-state MODFLOW-2005 model with MODPATH 7. title: Multi-predatory feeding aggregations in the Norwegian Sea: prevalence and ecological importance
abstract: Multi-predatory feeding aggregations (MPFAs) occur when several predator species concurrently exploit shared, spatially and temporally aggregated prey. Although MPFAs are well described in some marine ecosystems, their prevalence in the Norwegian Sea has historically been underestimated. Here, we synthesize existing biological, acoustic, visual and behavioural evidence to reinterpret classical predator-prey observations through the lens of MPFAs. journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences

title: Fish community dynamics in remote northern Australia: the role of habitat and seascape
abstract: Associations between fish and benthic habitats are shaped by structural complexity, resource availability, and positioning within the larger seascape. In the remote Gulf of Carpentaria in northern Australia, there is very little scientific information on how fish communities interact with their habitats within a heterogeneous seascape, despite their ecological and cultural value. This is the first study of how habitat characteristics and seascape configuration influence demersal fish communities in Marra Sea Country in the southwestern Gulf of Carpentaria. title: Spatial assessment of landslide susceptibility in Donomulyo based on GIS-MCDA and AHP
abstract: Donomulyo Subdistrict in Malang Regency is characterized by complex hill–coastal terrain that is increasingly pressured by tourism development, making it highly prone to landslides. This study assesses landslide susceptibility using a Geographic Information System–based Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (GIS–MCDA) integrated with the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). Five conditioning factors—slope, rainfall, land cover, soil type, and geology—were analyzed and weighted through pairwise comparison to generate a spatial susceptibility map. title: A Modular, Cloud-Based GIS Platform for Automated Wildfire Risk Index Mapping
abstract: Wildfires are a growing environmental and socio-economic threat driven by climate change and land abandonment. As fire frequency and intensity increase, suppression alone is no longer sufficient, making prevention and preparedness essential. Earth Observation and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) enable the integration of environmental and socio-economic factors into decision-support tools for wildfire risk assessment. title: Seaward we go, does joy then grow? The spatiotemporal dynamics of tourist emotions in coastal destinations
abstract: Coastal tourism holds tremendous development potential, yet faces a critical paradox under the experience economy: while demand grows, inadequate tourist experiences increasingly constrain its sustainable development. This study selects Qingdao as a representative coastal destination and integrates online travelogue analysis, affective semantic processing, and GIS techniques to examine tourists’ spatiotemporal trajectories and emotional dynamics, informing improvements in the tourist experience. title: Escalating competition in changing seas: baleen whales exploit killer whale prey herding
abstract: Climate change and other anthropogenic pressures are rapidly reshaping marine ecosystems, altering prey availability and predator interactions. Yet empirical evidence of how these relationships shift under changing conditions remains scarce. Drawing on over a decade of monitoring in a subarctic fjord system, we provide a rare insight into these dynamics. In northern Norway, the winter aggregation of herring (Clupea harengus) and their primary predator, the killer whale (Orcinus orca), has shifted northward under the combined influence of climate change and fishing pressure. title: Unraveling the roles of shallow coastal habitats and salinity in shaping aquatic microeukaryotic communities using experimental and field approaches
abstract: Abstract Microeukaryotic communities in brackish coastal ecosystems are structured by complex interactions between environmental conditions and habitat heterogeneity. This study examines how moderate salinity levels (ranging from freshwater to salinity 6) and habitat type (water column, sediment, and biofilm) influence microeukaryotic diversity and community composition in shallow coastal waters of the Gulf of Finland, the Baltic Sea. title: Advanced Assessment of the Agro-Silvo-Pastoral Coherence in Transboundary Transitional Water Regions
abstract: Transitional waters play a vital role in the ecological health and sustainability of coastal areas. According to European Union legislation, transitional waters are coastal water bodies influenced by freshwater flows but are partly saline due to their proximity to the sea. This study focuses on agricultural and forestry regions adjacent to transboundary transitional waters—i.e., areas where two or more countries share an estuary, tidal inlet, delta, or lagoon and have a contiguous border in their territorial waters. title: Marine holobionts: a model arena for host–microbe biology, from ecosystem function to biotechnology
abstract: Abstract Microbial symbioses are the operating system of marine biology. Nearly every macroscopic organism in the ocean exists as a holobiont, the consortium composed of a eukaryotic host and its bacterial, archaeal, microeukaryotic and viral partners. Marine holobionts span a broader range of the metazoan tree of life than likely any other ecological setting on the planet. This breadth makes the marine realm a uniquely informative system to investigate how host-microbe partnerships shape organisms and ecosystems. title: Interactions between multi-species marine predator aggregations and the energy landscape
abstract: Multi-species predator aggregations can be found in both coastal and pelagic ecosystems, forming for both foraging and refuging (resting) purposes. The energy landscape represents the power costs required to move through or reside within a habitat. As species may differ in their morphology, buoyancy and length, there may be species-specific heterogeneity in their energy landscapes. Here, we highlight how the energy landscape may influence the small-scale distribution of predators within an aggregation and potentially their ability to forage. title: Small-scale fishers’ perceptions and behavioural responses to marine protected areas implementation
abstract: Marine protected area (MPA) implementation can lead to fishers’ displacement and opposition to conservation efforts. Yet, evidence on how MPAs affect fishing operations is limited, especially for the small-scale sector. Surveys and participatory mapping exercises (n=93) were carried out with small-scale fishers in four Mediterranean and one Black Sea MPA to investigate fishers’ behavioural responses and perceptions to MPA implementation. title: Multi decadal (1990–2020) study on anthropogenic impact assessment in Mexican Caribbean coast: A novel approach using GIS and indices
Morecambe Area Gaming Environment (MAGE): An Applied Case Study for Coastal Futures and Adaptations
abstract: Large regions and coastal urban communities face significant climate-related risks, including coastal and river flooding, inundations, and sea-level rise. However, long-term predictions of coastal flooding, coastal change, and associated risks involve uncertainties that are difficult to communicate to those affected. This, in turn, can hinder the adaptation of coastal communities to future changes. title: Industry-led mitigation of seal bycatch in North Sea pelagic trawl fisheries: Evaluating excluder device effectiveness and policy implications
abstract: Bycatch of marine mammals in commercial fisheries presents conservation, operational, and regulatory challenges, particularly in the Greater North Sea where trawl fisheries targeting forage fish overlap with seal foraging habitats. This study evaluates the effectiveness of two seal excluder devices—the DPPO’s excluder tube and the PFA’s excluder grid—designed to reduce incidental seal captures in sandeel and herring fisheries, respectively. title: Distribution-based assessment reveals structural shifts in a protected estuarine gastropod, Clithon retropictus (Mollusca: Gastropoda)
abstract: Understanding temporal variation in estuarine populations is essential for conserving species inhabiting environmentally heterogeneous coastal habitats. Clithon retropictus is a protected brackish-water gastropod in South Korea that inhabits algae-covered stones in small tidal rivers and is vulnerable to changes in salinity gradients, substrate structure, and fragmentation of estuarine habitats. We evaluated long-term changes in the abundance structure of this species using national-scale ecological monitoring data collected from 2016 to 2024. title: Public perceptions and (lack of) support for mitigation of artificial light at night in coastal cities
abstract: Artificial light at night (ALAN) is an expanding environmental pressure in urban areas, yet effective mitigation depends on public support. We investigated how residents of two Chilean coastal cities perceive ALAN, its impacts and potential mitigation measures. Respondents demonstrated asymmetric environmental literacy, recognising the societal benefits of lighting while showing limited awareness of its ecological consequences, particularly for coastal-marine ecosystems. title: Intra-annual dynamics of larval fish assemblages and their environmental associations in the central Southern Black Sea
abstract: Larval fish assemblages are crucial indicators for monitoring marine ecosystem dynamics and the recruitment potential of fishery stocks. This study investigates the spatiotemporal dynamics of larval fish assemblages in the central Southern Black Sea (Sinop) and the environmental parameters shaping these patterns. An intra-annual monthly sampling survey identified 35 species across 20 families; the assemblage structure was dominated by Engraulis encrasicolus, Gobius niger, Sprattus sprattus, Mullus barbatus and Trachurus mediterraneus. title: No effect of short‐term exposure to ocean acidification on individual‐level variation in behaviour and susceptibility to predation in a Great Barrier Reef damselfish
abstract: Abstract Ocean acidification, caused by rising carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) in the atmosphere, has been reported to negatively impact a wide variety of behaviours in fishes, including activity, exploration, and predator avoidance. These effects have been documented at the population level, but many animal species naturally show large and repeatable individual‐level differences in behaviour. title: Cumulative impact of climate change and adaptation measures on Venice and its lagoon
abstract: Abstract Adaptation measures to climate change can generate unintended environmental consequences, particularly in vulnerable coastal systems. In the Venice Lagoon, the Mose mobile barrier system was designed to protect the city from sea-level rise and storm surges, still ensuring the lagoon-sea exchange. However, under climate change the frequency and duration of Mose closures will increase and this might modify lagoon water renewal and affect ecosystem properties. title: Microphytobenthos Primary Production and Organic Matter Mineralization Along the Sea Level Gradient in a Tropical Mudflat
abstract: Tropical tidal flats represent more than half of the global tidal flat area, however information on the ecological and biogeochemical role of microphytobenthos (MPB) in tropical environments remains scarce. The objective of this study was to analyze the changes in sediment biogeochemistry, MPB, community composition and net metabolism along the sea level (SL) gradient in a tropical tidal flat (Punta Morales, Gulf of Nicoya, Costa Rica). title: Offshore wind farm impacts on marine fauna across taxa and ecological levels: A global review
abstract: The expansion of offshore wind farms (OWFs) is central to global decarbonization strategies, yet their effects on marine biodiversity are only partially understood. This systematic review synthesizes 221 publications up to June 2025 to assess the ecological impacts of OWFs on marine fauna living below the sea surface. The evidence base is uneven, heavily focused on North European waters, fish, and invertebrates, while expanding OWF regions and marine mammals remain underrepresented. title: Fin whale movement patterns from the Mediterranean sea reveal summer habitat use in the North Atlantic and potential feeding behavior
abstract: Abstract Understanding the movements of highly mobile marine species is essential for identifying critical habitats and developing effective conservation measures. Although occasional movements of fin whales ( Balaenoptera physalus ) between the Mediterranean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean have been reported, the extent to which these movements represent a recurrent component of Mediterranean fin whale ecology remains unclear. title: Self-reporting alkalinity-responsive hydrogel for visual monitoring and microenvironment remodeling of seawater-immersed infected wounds
abstract: Seawater-associated infected wounds involve alkaline and hyperosmotic stress, polymicrobial contamination, biofilms, and persistent inflammation, collectively delaying healing. Herein, we developed QCB-Au@SPG, a pH-responsive hydrogel integrating fluorescent antibacterial QCB-Au, an alkali-sensitive SA-PBA network, and photocrosslinkable GelMA. QCB-Au@SPG exhibited a linear fluorescence response across pH 4–8 (R² = 0.998), enabling semi-quantitative visualization of pH variation, while alkaline conditions moderately enhanced QCB-Au release. title: The near-T2T genome of the feather star Cenometra bella suggests potential evolutionary innovations and coral reef habitat tolerance
abstract: Abstract Background Crinoids are highly conservative echinoderms, retaining ancient features since the early Ordovician, making them classic "living fossils" invaluable for studying evolution and biodiversity. Their evolutionary stability is marked by minimal morphological changes, a sessile lifestyle, and exceptionally slow evolutionary rates, rendering them unique among marine groups. However, they have long lacked high-quality genomic resources, hindering insights into the genomic evolution of early echinoderm lineages. title: Probabilistic tsunami risk assessment based on submarine active faults and their possible interactions in the sea of Japan
abstract: Abstract The Sea of Japan coastal areas have experienced tsunami damage caused by submarine active seismic faults. Large uncertainties remain regarding seismic activity of these faults and the following tsunami. Probabilistic tsunami risk assessment (PTRA) enables the evaluation of tsunami risk accounting for such uncertainties. In this study, the tsunami risks of a thermal power plant located on the Sea of Japan coast were evaluated using the PTRA based on submarine active faults, including coupled faults, across the Sea of Japan. title: Marine radar reveals novel group foraging patterns in pelagic seabirds
abstract: Many seabirds are known to frequently feed within multi-specific feeding flocks. These aggregations bring facilitation to prey access as well as potential exacerbated competition. Once a feeding opportunity is found, birds rapidly aggregate to it through processes known as local enhancement. At a larger scale, seabirds may distribute themselves forming patterns such as rakes or clusters, which are thought to increase the probability to cue on other foragers. title: Assessment of disinfectant performance against fish-pathogenic bacteria in planktonic and biofilm states
abstract: Disinfecting fish farming equipment and facility surfaces with disinfectant is one of the primary biosafety measures to prevent disease introduction and transmission. However, the actual efficacy of approved disinfectants against fish-pathogenic bacteria and especially their biofilms remain largely undocumented. Six selected disinfectants were evaluated against seven common disease-causing bacteria and their biofilms. title: Distinct drivers control trace metal distributions through the Atlantic Ocean
abstract: Trace metals (TMs) including iron, manganese, cobalt, nickel, copper, zinc, cadmium, and lead have important biogeochemical roles in the ocean. However, the controlling factors of TM distributions have not yet been quantified and investigated on an ocean scale. Here we take a holistic approach to demonstrate that transport through water masses formed in high latitudes can explain 60–90% of dissolved TM distributions and >75% of TM inventories in the interior Atlantic. title: Episodic High‐Latitude Occurrence of Walleye Pollock ( Gadus chalcogrammus ) in the Central Arctic Ocean Associated With Warm Subsurface Conditions: Multi‐Year Environmental DNA and Larval Evidence
abstract: ABSTRACT Episodic high‐latitude occurrences of subarctic fish due to Arctic warming present significant challenges for managing high‐latitude ecosystems. In this study, we present four consecutive years (2021–2024) of integrated environmental DNA (eDNA) monitoring and larval surveys for walleye pollock ( Gadus chalcogrammus ) conducted aboard the Korean icebreaker IBR/V Araon in the Chukchi Sea (CS) and Central Arctic Ocean (CAO). title: Carbon fluxes within an Arctica islandica habitat in the German Baltic Sea
abstract: Ongoing climate change and rising CO 2 emissions highlight the need to understand ecosystem carbon cycling to guide the conservation of carbon-rich, biodiverse habitats. We investigated organic carbon cycling and storage associated with the long-lived bivalve Arctica islandica in the German Baltic Sea. Through filtration and bioturbation, A. islandica may enhance the burial of organic carbon in deeper sediment layers. title: Visualizing the penetration behavior of tapered thread piles via transparent soil: Effects of thread design
abstract: With superior construction efficiency and load-bearing performance, precast tapered thread piles hold significant potential for offshore and coastal infrastructure. However, their installation mechanics remain poorly understood, and visual experimental investigations are scarce. To address this knowledge gap, this study utilizes a developed optomechanically coupled testing system to investigate the continuous penetration process of tapered thread piles. title: Increases in foraging performance of humpback whales in multi-predator feeding aggregations with California sea lions
abstract: Marine predators frequently form ephemeral multi-predator feeding aggregations around dense prey patches, yet the mechanisms and outcomes of these dynamic events remain poorly resolved. We quantified how California sea lion (Zalophus californianus) presence influenced humpback whale (Megaptera novaeangliae) foraging using 46 multi-sensor video tags (mean duration: 7.4 ± 7.1 h) deployed on fish-feeding whales in Monterey Bay, California, USA (2014-2023). title: Microbial community responses to ceramic amendment in coastal sediments of a seasonally hypoxic bay
abstract: Eutrophication-driven sediment deterioration is a critical issue in enclosed coastal bays. A ceramic material composed of humic organic acids and calcium carbonate mesoscopic crystals has been developed for in-situ sediment remediation, generating high-alkaline environments that promote oxidative degradation of organic matter. Although its physicochemical effects have been verified through the Environmental Technology Verification (ETV) program, its influence on sediment microbial communities remains unknown. title: Comparative Evaluation of Seawater-Based and Conventional Fixatives on Histological Quality in Broiler Chicken Tissues
abstract: Lung, liver, brain, heart, kidney, and spleen tissues obtained from 60 broiler chickens at a commercial abattoir in Afyon Province were fixed using six fixation solutions consisting of 10% neutral buffered formalin (NBF) or 70% ethanol, each prepared with distilled water, seawater (salinity approximately 38‰), or a distilled water–seawater mixture. This study evaluated the effect of seawater as a solvent component on histomorphological preservation and hematoxylin–eosin (H&E) staining quality. title: Eco-phenotypic characterization of Candida palmioleophila from poultry litter and marine environments: implications for One Health
abstract: Candida palmioleophila is an emerging opportunistic yeast frequently misidentified within the Meyerozyma guilliermondii complex, potentially obscuring its clinical and ecological relevance. Although its clinical significance is increasingly recognized, the phenotypic characteristics of environmental isolates remain poorly explored. This study evaluated the eco-phenotypic profiles of 14 C. palmioleophila isolates recovered from two anthropogenically influenced environmental sources: poultry litter (n = 6) and urbanized coastal environments (n = 8). abstract: The paper discusses epistemic justice as a central justice framework to be considered in the regulatory process of exploitative deep sea mining, with the aim of bringing attention to the relevance of epistemic justice and diversity to deep sea mining scholarship. Epistemic justice is here understood as deeply connected to a broader social equity, and entails the fair treatment of different ’knowers’ and a creation, sharing, and validation of knowledge that is fundamentally diverse rather than based on one dominant knowledge-tradition. title: New evidence of the early stages of establishment of the parrotfish Sparisoma cretense (Teleostei: Labridae) following northward and westward range expansion in the Mediterranean Sea
abstract: Abstract Sparisoma cretense is undergoing a range expansion across the Mediterranean Sea, yet its establishment at northern latitudes of the westernmost Mediterranean remains uncertain. During July 2025, patterns consistent with the establishment of S. cretense in Cabrera National Park (39º 09’ N; 2º 57’ E) were assessed, and habitat features associated with its occurrence were identified. Underwater visual censuses were conducted, recording abundance, total length, sex, habitat composition, and the hydrodynamic exposure level of each locality. title: Best Practices in Open and Reproducible Antarctic Marine Sediment Core Research
abstract: Abstract Marine sediment cores from Antarctica are archived by national programs for reuse and resampling by future researchers, creating a resourceful way to conduct Antarctic science. With reduced budgets to conduct Antarctic field work and to collect new sediment cores offshore of the icy continent, the accessibility of these archived cores and availability of core data are in high demand. title: Changes in species composition of South Georgia seabirds and mammals 1985–2023: decrease in opportunities for local enhancement?
abstract: Seabirds cue into other birds and marine mammals to amplify their foraging success. Consequently, changes to the community (e.g. as the climate warms) can impact foraging success and potentially fitness. For example, flying birds that use groups of seals or penguins as cues might decline if the seal or penguin population declines, owing to fewer opportunities for positive foraging associations with one another. title: Phased ecological assembly of Triassic marine reptile faunas following the Permian–Triassic mass extinction: ecospace dynamics in South China
abstract: The Permian-Triassic mass extinction triggered a fundamental reorganization of marine ecosystems, yet the community-level functional dynamics of early marine reptile radiations remain understudied. Here we quantify ecospace dynamics of Triassic marine reptile faunas across an approximately 20-million-year sequence in South China, integrating 10 functional traits of fossil taxa and modern ecological analogues. title: Reversible Atlantic overturning despite continued Greenland ice sheet melt
abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is considered vulnerable to irreversible weakening or collapse under global warming and related Greenland ice sheet (GrIS) melt, yet its resilience to either forcing remains poorly constrained. Here, we use a carbon dioxide emission-driven Earth system model with an interactive GrIS to assess AMOC reversibility under a range of idealized carbon dioxide emission pathways that produce near-linear global warming up to 10 kelvins (K), stabilization across 1.5 to 9 K, and subsequent cooling. title: Occurrence and Ingestion of Plastic Particles in Marine Fish from Togolese Coast
abstract: The increase in plastic production towards the end of the Second World War, combined with inadequate plastic waste management, has contributed to the contamination of marine ecosystems. The ingestion of plastic particles measuring less than 5 mm, known as microplastics, by marine organisms has been documented. The aim of this study was to demonstrate that plastic particles can ultimately enter the human food supply. journal: International Journal of Ecotoxicology and Ecobiology

title: Statistical optimization of melanin-like pigment biosynthesis by marine Streptomyces isolate MOE3 and evaluation of its cytotoxic activity against A-431 cells
abstract: Marine actinomycetes represent a promising source of biologically active natural pigments. In the present study, isolate MOE3, recovered from mangrove sediment along the Egyptian Red Sea coast, was provisionally assigned to Streptomyces lateritius based on partial 16 S rRNA gene sequencing and phylogenetic analysis, showing approximately 99% sequence similarity to closely related Streptomyces taxa. title: Million‐Year Scale Hydrothermal and Hydrocarbon Evolution Hosted Within Stratified Thermohydraulic Systems in Sedimented Ultraslow‐Spreading Settings, Svyatogor and Vestnesa Ridges
abstract: Abstract Hydrothermal systems at ultraslow‐spreading ridges are poorly understood, especially where thick sediments overlay detachment faults. The International Ocean Discovery Program Expedition 403 obtained the longest sediment record in Atlantic‐Arctic ultraslow‐spreading systems, reaching ∼628 m below the seafloor. title: Revealing potential Atlantic salmon bycatch hotspots from pelagic fisheries landings across the Northeast Atlantic
abstract: Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) marine survival has declined markedly over the past five decades, leading to concerns about future population viability. While many studies have explored the impacts of stressors such as climate change and predation, less is known about bycatch from pelagic fisheries targeting finfish species. This study, focused on the first few months of the salmon marine migration period, narrows down the space-time domains where pelagic fisheries bycatch is most likely to occur. title: Coastline Evolution of Large-Scale Artificial Beach Nourishment in the Vicinity of a Newly Built Breakwater: An Empirical Case Study from the South Baltic Coast
abstract: Large-scale beach nourishment projects constructed adjacent to port breakwaters may produce spatially contrasting shoreline responses because wave transformation, sediment redistribution, and structural effects act simultaneously. This study presents an empirical analysis of short-term shoreline evolution at a large artificially nourished beach constructed next to the eastern breakwater of the Vistula Spit Channel in the South Baltic Sea. title: SPATIAL STRATEGIES AND IMPLEMENTATION PATHWAYS FOR THE ALL-AGE FRIENDLY RENEWAL OF OLD COMMUNITIES IN ZHUHAI UNDER THE ORIENTATION OF MODERN MARINE CITIES
abstract: Coastal cities have shifted from outward expansion to reworking the housing stock they already hold, and renewing aging communities has become harder to manage as a result. Three pressures overlap in these neighborhoods: a resident profile that no longer matches the original design brief, almost no slack in the public space budget, and marine-climate risks that accumulate rather than arrive one at a time. title: Modulation of ETCCDI-based extreme rainfall indices by ENSO and the Indian Ocean Dipole over topographically complex North Sumatra, Indonesia
abstract: This study examines the characteristics of extreme rainfall in North Sumatra Province, Indonesia, and its teleconnections with the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD). The analysis uses a blended daily rainfall dataset from 1990 to 2024, combining station observations from the Indonesian Agency for Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics (BMKG) with the Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Station (CHIRPS) satellite data. title: An Investigation of Built-up Area Expansion in the Syrian Coastal Mountain Environment
abstract: As built-up expansion in the Syrian coastal mountainous areas intensifies, its environmental impacts are becoming increasingly severe. Existing research, however, offers limited quantitative evidence to elucidate the dynamics of this phenomenon. This study addresses this gap by employing mixed-method techniques at the district level of Safita. Landsat satellite imagery, remote sensing, and ArcGIS software were used to classify and analyze geospatial data from 2010 to 2020. title: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) Based Analysis of Accessibility to Schools in Çankırı (Türkiye)
abstract: Education is vital in terms of providing the individual with behaviours in the desired direction. It is necessary to ensure a sustainable and accessible education planning. Thus, it is important that children of school age have access to educational institutions. Because every child who is not in the accessible field is exposed to inequality of opportunity. title: Reviewing the climate change landscape in South Africa’s marine fisheries: progress, gaps, and future directions
abstract: Climate change is reshaping South Africa’s marine ecosystems and fisheries with consequences for ecological productivity, livelihoods and governance. Although research on climate impacts on fisheries has expanded, the overall climate-risk landscape for South African fisheries has not been reviewed using the risk framing proposed in the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Fifth Assessment Report (AR5). title: Effective number of communities reveals extent of biodiversity change – a cross-organism analysis in the Wadden Sea
abstract: Biodiversity changes in ecosystems worldwide, but assessing the true magnitude of this transformation requires the analysis of multiple dimensions of compositional change. Trends in α-diversity only capture the net difference between gains and losses, while year-on-year temporal turnover in composition does not reflect long-term changes in species identity. We used extensive monitoring data from the Wadden Sea UNESCO World Heritage Site as a case to explore the accumulated change over time through presence-absence and dominance-weighted data. title: Captive-raised juvenile hawksbill ( Eretmochelys imbricata ) turtles display naturalistic behaviours upon ocean release
abstract: Some conservation programs keep turtles temporarily under human care with the intention of releasing them later to strengthen wild populations. Historically, researchers have questioned whether key survival behaviours might be lost during captive-raising, potentially reducing post-release survivability. Yet no published studies have examined the in-water behaviour of captive-raised turtles in a way that allows comparison with wild conspecifics – an important gap for the critically endangered hawksbill turtle (Eretmochelys imbricata). title: Design and Implementation of an AIS Vessel Trajectory Visualization System Based on AMap
abstract: To address the challenges posed by the large volume and dense spatial distribution of AIS position data, as well as the limited support for interactive queries in conventional static displays, this paper designs and implements an AIS vessel trajectory visualization system based on AMap. By integrating AMap with ECharts, the system provides coordinated representations of spatial positions and speed variations. It supports two primary functions. title: Liposome supplementation enhances host metabolism in a model symbiotic cnidarian
abstract: Abstract Stable cnidarian–dinoflagellate symbioses provide the trophic foundation of coral reef ecosystems. Understanding nutrient exchange underpinning this symbiosis, and the need for interventions to improve coral health via aquaculture, grow increasingly urgent as reefs face accelerating threats from climate change. Liposomes and lipid nanoparticles, widely used as delivery vehicles in biomedical science, are emerging as promising tools to supplement coral nutrition. abstract: Coastal habitats are characterized by steep and spatially heterogeneous environmental gradients that can influence plant population structure, growth and reproductive performance.Peucedanum japonicum is a coastal perennial plant distributed across diverse habitats, but differences in population characteristics and individual performance among populations under different local environmental conditions remain poorly understood.We compared vegetation, environmental conditions, structural characteristics, and individual growth and reproductive traits of P. japonicum across three habitat types in K

title: Public willingness to pay for hybrid blue-green infrastructure: Evidence from the Clyde and Forth Estuaries, Scotland
abstract: Nature-based solutions are increasingly recognised as climate-resilient strategies for coastal climate adaptation. This study estimates public willingness to pay (WTP) for the creation of hybrid blue-green infrastructure in place of vacant and derelict land in the Clyde and Forth estuaries, using a contingent valuation method with a payment card format. Tobit and interval regression models were used to evaluate the effects of socioeconomic, attitudinal, and consequentiality variables on WTP. title: Reimagining the Dead Sea Scrolls: A Position Paper
abstract: The Dead Sea Scrolls are imagined as scrolls and cataloged as manuscripts but consist, for the most part, of scattered and minuscule fragments. In this article, we will propose a new physical object-based ontology that takes the smallest indivisible units, i.e., the physical fragments, as the point of departure. title: Growth, physiological responses, and water quality in juvenile Malabar grouper reared in a low-salinity RAS: An 84-day operational trial
abstract: Recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) are expanding globally as a sustainable aquaculture technology. Although RAS enable intensive production of marine fish, their high capital and operating costs necessitate strategies that improve growth efficiency while maintaining stable water quality. Low-salinity seawater promotes growth in many marine fish species; however, concerns remain that reduced salinity may impair biofiltration. title: Thirsty clean energy: localized water stress and hydro-ecological tradeoffs in green hydrogen expansion
abstract: Green hydrogen is central to global decarbonization, yet its rapid expansion exposes a severe spatial contradiction: the regions possessing optimal renewable energy potential are overwhelmingly the planet’s most water-stressed and ecologically fragile landscapes. This review critically examines the localized hydro-ecological tradeoffs of mega-scale electrolysis across arid export corridors in Australia, Chile, and North Africa. abstract: This study examines long-term temperature variability and future climate projections in Hatay Province, located along the Eastern Mediterranean coast of Türkiye. abstract: Crop growth in relation to management parameters were studied in coastal areas of West Bengal. Resourcesat 2A L3 data was analyzed for vegetation index (NDVI). abstract: Truncation of aerospike plug nozzles in high-speed propulsion has become widely adopted to reduce structural length and cooling demands. However, it introduces a low-pressure base region and wake losses which can offset performance gains. abstract: Accelerated sea level rise, combined with human-induced changes to hydrology and sediment transport, threatens the long-term persistence of coastal wetlands. Sediment addition is increasingly used to enhance wetland resilience to sea level rise, and incorporating biochar, a carbon-rich material produced through pyrolysis of organic matter, may enhance carbon storage, soil function, and vegetation recovery. abstract: Abstract Coastal internal tides are considered unpredictable: harmonic fits to depth‐varying baroclinic velocity explain little variance. We show the depth‐averaged coastal internal tide is predictable from astronomical forcing. On the inner shelf, coastal trapped wave (CTW) modes are approximately depth‐uniform, so depth‐averaging recovers their coherent sum at the forcing frequency, while multimodal interference degrades coherence in depth‐varying velocity. abstract: Harmful algal blooms (HABs) are increasingly impacting estuarine ecosystems, yet current microbial surveillance methods often focus on prokaryotic 16S rRNA profiles and overlook eukaryotic bloom-forming species. Here, we applied Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) MinION long-read sequencing targeting the 18S rRNA gene to characterize spatial and seasonal patterns of eukaryotic microbial communities in the Indian River Lagoon (IRL), a biologically diverse 251 km long estuary along Florida’s Atlantic coast. title: Variation patterns and ecological drivers of morphology in different body regions of fishes from the Northwest Pacific Ocean
abstract: Variation in fish body morphology represents an important aspect of phenotypic diversity and plays a fundamental role in understanding fish evolution and ecology. The complex oceanographic conditions of the Northwest Pacific Ocean create diverse selective pressures, making it an ideal system for studying how environmental variability shapes fish body morphology. title: Comparative policy analysis of urban microplastic pollution and water quality management toward sustainable environmental governance in Malaysian cities
abstract: Rapid urbanization in Southeast Asia has intensified microplastic (MP) pollution in city water bodies, urban drainage systems, and coastal environments, posing significant threats to urban water quality and public health. This study employs a comparative policy analysis to evaluate how global, regional, and national legislative frameworks address MP pollution as a critical urban water management challenge, with emphasis on ASEAN member states and Malaysia’s cities. title: Diversity and distribution of cryptobenthic fishes and their association with epibenthic fauna in a subtropical estuary
abstract: Abstract Cryptobenthic fishes (CF) are cryptic species that exhibit mimicry with their benthic environment and can be either detritivorous or zoobenthivorous. Few studies have examined the influence of epibenthic macrofauna on CF diversity. This study analyzed the colonization and spatiotemporal succession of CF and macrofauna in fish-specific autonomous reef monitoring structures (FARMS) at Paranaguá Estuarine Complex (Brazil). abstract: Abstract Pennahia aneus is a commercially important demersal sciaenid fish found in the Indo-Pacific region, yet its population structure in Malaysia remains insufficiently documented. This study aimed to differentiate four populations of P. aneus in Peninsular Malaysia and Borneo using morphometric multivariate analyses. A total of 423 samples were obtained from 22 landing sites across the South China Sea, Celebes Sea, Sulu Sea, and Strait of Malacca. abstract: Abstract. Remote sensing reflectance (Rrs) is fundamental for deriving bio-optical properties of global surface waters. However, accurate atmospheric correction (AC) to derive Rrs in coastal waters remains challenging due to strongly absorbing aerosols and complex water optics. To address this, we developed an improved processing framework that integrates flexible use of global gridded aerosol models better suited for coastal environments and incorporates tailored masking strategies. abstract: This study aimed to develop a one-step loop-mediated isothermal amplification combined with a lateral flow dipstick (LAMP-LFD) DNA biosensor for the detection of α0-thalassemia (SEA deletion). Genomic DNA was obtained from 48 α0-thalassemia (SEA deletion)-positive and 48 (SEA deletion)-negative (normal) Thai subjects. DNA was analyzed by LAMP assay at 61°C for 60 min using specific primers for the α0-thalassemia (SEA deletion) type. title: Assessment of 226Ra and 228Ra activity concentrations in drinking water sources along Ghana’s coastal communities
abstract: This study reports a screening-level radiological assessment of drinking water sources – sachet water, tap water, borehole water and river water – across the Greater Accra, Central and Western Regions of Ghana. Activity concentrations of 226 Ra and 228 Ra were measured by high-purity germanium (HPGe) gamma spectrometry in 244 samples collected over one dry and one wet season, and screening-level committed effective doses were estimated for adult consumers. title: Experimental manipulation of ecological constraints influences conflict but not cooperation in the humbug damselfish Dascyllus aruanus
abstract: Animal societies vary widely in levels of cooperation and conflict, and understanding the causes of this variation is a central goal in evolutionary biology. As with other features of animal societies, relatedness, competitiveness and ecological constraints (e.g. habitat saturation and risks of dispersal) have been proposed as key factors explaining variation in cooperation and conflict. title: ContextFlow-YOLO: Context Preservation and Cross-Scale Redistribution for Small-Object Detection in Complex Environments
abstract: Small objects in underwater and traffic-sign images often have weak boundaries and low contrast. Downsampling and multi-scale fusion can further weaken the features needed to detect them. abstract: Co-management of Protected Areas (PAs) has emerged as a strategy to make forest restoration and biodiversity conservation more effective by encouraging the active participation of local people. This study analyzed the co-management effects in two protected areas i.e. Dharmapur Shal Forest and Nawabganj National Park in Dinajpur District, Bangladesh. abstract: Purpose - Southern Calabria represents one of the most geologically complex and diverse regions of the Mediterranean. Despite this exceptional geological richness, its geoheritage remains only partially documented and poorly integrated into structured geotourism strategies. In many Mediterranean regions, geotourism has proven to be an effective tool for sustainable territorial development, environmental education, and heritage protection, yet Southern Calabria still lacks a comprehensive and systematic geotouristic framework. abstract: In the present study, we report the first molecular detection and identification of the ectoparasitic monogenean Neobenedenia girellae in the farmed greater amberjack (Seriola dumerili) in Greece. This parasite is considered one of the most economically important ectoparasites affecting marine finfish aquaculture worldwide. The greater amberjack is an emerging species for Mediterranean aquaculture, characterized by rapid growth and high market value. title: Chronic exposure to Salton Sea aerosols elicits pulmonary inflammation and shifts in murine lung and fecal microbiome diversity
abstract: Abstract Lung disease is rampant around the Salton Sea, California’s largest inland lake and a major source of airborne particulates. To examine root causes of pulmonary disease, we investigated the exposure impacts of spatiotemporal variation in aerosols collected near the Salton Sea on lung and fecal microbiomes. We collected dust during the summer and fall at three different sites around the Salton Sea from 2020 to 2022. title: Millennial‐Scale Deoxygenation in the Southern California Oxygen Minimum Zone Over the Last Glacial Cycle
abstract: Abstract Past variability of oxygen minimum zones (OMZs) provides key insights into future ocean deoxygenation. However, California margin OMZ records remain temporally limited, restricting evaluation of mechanisms across full glacial–interglacial cycles. Here, we reconstruct high‐resolution bottom water oxygen (BWO) over the past ∼140,000 years using redox‐sensitive trace metals from ODP Site 1017E in the Southern California OMZ. abstract: Mangrove ecosystems are highly vulnerable to coastal environmental change and anthropogenic disturbance. The mangrove forests distributed along the eastern and western coasts of Shenzhen experience contrasting environmental regimes. The eastern coast is influenced by oligotrophic waters of the northern South China Sea and is dominated by native mangrove stands, whereas the western coast, located within the Pearl River Estuary, is subject to elevated nutrient inputs, intensive urbanization and extensive mangrove restoration. title: Nature-based experiences support lasting conservation behavior: longitudinal evidence from shark ecotourism in Hawaiʻi
abstract: Shark ecotourism is increasingly promoted as a nature-based solution for ocean sustainability, yet empirical evidence of its long-term impacts on conservation behavior remains limited. We employed a quasi-experimental, longitudinal design to evaluate whether participation in a shark ecotourism program in Hawaiʻi influenced individual conservation behavior over time. Survey data were collected from tour participants and a general public comparison group at the time of the tour and again two years later. abstract: Background: Health literacy plays an important role in hypertension management and stroke prevention; however, conventional health literacy assessment approaches often overlook sociocultural contexts that shape health-related decision-making in culturally cohesive communities. This study assessed Functional, Communicative, and Critical (FCC) Health Literacy related to stroke prevention among hypertensive patients in a Bugis coastal community in Indonesia using a culturally contextualized approach informed by the Puangrimaggalatung framework. title: By the crossroad
abstract: Due to infrastructural work, Sydsvensk Arkeologi AB conducted an archaeological excavation in 2022 between the Scanian villages Fjälkinge and Gualöv, southern Sweden. The excavation revealed settlements and a cemetery from the Late Neolithic into the Pre-Roman Iron Age. abstract: Abstract Host–associated microbiomes play vital roles in species’ ecology and evolution, yet little is known about their shift during the transition from aquatic to terrestrial habitats. We characterize the skin microbiomes of three combtooth blenny species (Blenniella paula, Praealticus labrovittatus, Alticus arnoldorum) that occupy distinct positions along the intertidal gradient—from fully subtidal to intertidal and supratidal environments. title: Marine Macroalga-Mediated Green Synthesis of Silver Nanoparticles Using Ulva reticulata for Sunlight-Assisted Photocatalytic Degradation of Synthetic Dyes
abstract: Marine macroalgae provide renewable biological resources for the eco-friendly synthesis of functional nanomaterials for environmental remediation. This study synthesized silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using an aqueous extract of the green macroalga Ulva reticulata and evaluated their sunlight-driven photocatalytic activity against synthetic dyes. title: Soil organic carbon dynamics and microbial responses to intercropping sweet corn with legumes under different row arrangements in coastal Odisha
abstract: Abstract Intercropping of cereals and legumes can improve resource-use efficiency and soil fertility compared with monocropping. title: Have You Done Your Duty? Impact of Direct Mailing Campaign on Septic System Owners' Maintenance Knowledge and Behaviors in Coastal Texas Watersheds
abstract: As part of a watershed protection plan, the Texas Water Resources Institute and AgriLife Extension Service developed and distributed an educational postcard (``mailer'') about septic system maintenance to mailing addresses outside of public sewer service areas. The mailer was distributed four times within 1 year. The impact of this mailer was evaluated with a retrospective pre/post-test within a mailed survey. abstract: Rapid coastal urbanization increases exposure to multiple hazards while intensifying competition for land essential for safe emergency refuge. This paper proposes a reproducible decision-support framework for planning Disaster Prevention and Relief Accessible Green Spaces (DPRAGS). title: Spatiotemporal Differentiation and Influencing Factors of Overseas Chinese Architectural Heritage: A Case Study of Minnan, China
abstract: The Minnan region in southern Fujian, China, comprising Quanzhou, Xiamen, and Zhangzhou, is one of China’s major traditional qiaoxiang (overseas Chinese hometown) regions. This study develops a spatial database of 682 Minnan Overseas Chinese Architectural Heritage (MOCAH) sites, divides their formation into four historical periods—Qing Dynasty (pre-1912), Early Republican Period (1912–1936), Wartime Republican Period (1937–1948), and Early PRC Period (1949–late 1970s)—and applies GIS-based spatial and statistical methods to examine their spatiotemporal differentiation and influencing factors.

abstract: Introduction. abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Sea buckthorn contains an exceptionally rich profile of bioactive nutrients and metabolites, with established systemic therapeutic benefits across diverse pathological models. However, comprehensive data bridging these systemic outcomes with specific tissue responses are still lacking. This descriptive transcriptomic study establishes a predictive framework to guide the future application of sea buckthorn and its isolated derivatives in targeted preventive and therapeutic strategies. title: A new species of Doliocarpus (Dilleniaceae) from Brazil: the Atlantic Forest continues to reveal new findings on water vines
abstract: Abstract A new species of Doliocarpus (Dilleniaceae) endemic to the Brazilian Atlantic Forest is described. Doliocarpus amplexicarpus has been confused with D. schottianus , the most similar species occurring in the same phytogeographical domain, but the latter is found in the Serra do Mar Coastal Forests ecoregion, while the former occurs in the Bahia Coastal Forests ecoregion. Both species are remarkable for their smooth, whitish stems, compared to the predominantly rough, reddish stems of other taxa. title: Long-term spatiotemporal assessment of stable isotopic composition of precipitation across South Korea (2019–2023)
abstract: Mainland South Korea is a humid temperate peninsula characterized by strong seasonal climatic contrasts, complex topography, and a pronounced monsoon influence. The region comprises four major river basins (Han, Geum, Nakdong, and Yeongsan–Seomjin) and is influenced by both maritime and continental air masses. Precipitation is highly seasonal and strongly influenced by stationary fronts and typhoons, with over half of the annual precipitation occurring during the summer monsoon. title: Performance Evaluation of Cloud-Based Monitoring Tools for Maritime and Offshore Engineering Systems
abstract: Current maritime engineering methods in offshore applications use cloud technology in digital vessel monitoring systemsand cyber-physical systems. Recently, offshore maritime engineering applications have focused on employing cloud technology to monitor their applications in the digital age. Thus, this paper compares four prominent monitoring tools in maritime engineering practices or applications using cloud technology in different applications through a series of experiments based on tests on a cloud technology application to emulate different maritime engineering practices or applications.

title: Developmental temperature induces consistent patterns of plasticity in lower, but not upper, critical thermal limits in threespine stickleback (Gasterosteus aculeatus)
abstract: Abstract Developmental plasticity, where early-life environmental cues shape developmental trajectories with lasting impact into adulthood, may play an important role in determining how species respond to changing thermal environments. We used marine threespine stickleback ( Gasterosteus aculeatus ) to investigate whether temperature experienced during embryonic development has persistent effects on critical thermal limits as adults. title: Smart Food Delivery Box with Peltier-Based Cooling and Heating System
abstract: Food that travels from a kitchen to a customer rarely arrives at the temperature at which it left, and insulated boxes can only slow that drift, not correct it. This paper presents the design, construction and testing of a smart food delivery box with two independent zones, a hot zone and a cold zone, each served by Peltier modules. Two NTC thermistors measure the zone temperatures, and an ESP32 microcontroller switches the modules through a ULN2003A driver and a relay stage using hysteresis thresholds that the user can change from a Wi-Fi web dashboard. abstract: Abstract Bacterial resistance to heavy metals (HM) poses a significant risk to ecosystems and human health. This study evaluated resistance to HM of 24 bacterial isolates from two deep aquatic environments in southern Brazil: the Guarani Aquifer System (GAS) water and the Rio Grande Cone (CRG) marine sediment. title: The late Miocene–earliest Pleistocene Calivil Formation in central Victoria: coarse-grained alluvial deposition following tectonism
abstract: The Calivil Formation is an extensive coarse-grained alluvial formation deposited within narrow valleys across the central Victorian highlands. Palynological and stratigraphic evidence indicates that it is late Miocene in age; deposition continued into the late Pliocene or Pleistocene in some areas. Older palynological ages previously attributed to the Calivil Formation most likely represent either unrecognised or reworked Olney Formation sediments. title: Harem polygyny through resource defense territoriality in the sandperch Parapercis pacifica (Pinguipedidae)
abstract: In reef fishes inhabiting sandy rubble habitats, such as sandperches, a mating system with territorial female-type harems has been widely confirmed. However, the mechanisms underlying harem maintenance in species with large territories remain poorly understood. Parapercis pacifica (Pinguipedidae) is a relatively large sandperch with large territorial home ranges. title: Simulation analysis of self-excited oscillating water jet with petal-shaped nozzle under confining pressure
abstract: The self-excited oscillating water jet is widely used in ocean engineering. Its effectiveness stems from the impact of cavitation collapse driven by periodic pressure pulsations. This study investigated the flow field evolution and vortex stretching mechanisms of self-excited oscillating water jets using large eddy simulation. title: Active nuclease inhibition over passive freezing secures the genomic archive of fish eye lenses
abstract: Fish eye lenses offer a chronological archive of individual life histories and preserve genomic DNA. However, integrating ecological and genetic data is hindered by post-mortem nuclease degradation, and standardized DNA preservation protocols for this tissue remain undefined. We evaluated chemical and thermal preservation methods to maximize DNA yield and integrity from fish lenses. title: Infectious Pancreatic Necrosis in Atlantic Cod ( Gadus morhua ): Complete Viral Genome Characterization From the First Norwegian Field Case Suggests Cross‐Species Transmission
abstract: We describe the first natural outbreak of infectious pancreatic necrosis (IPN) in farmed Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua) in Norway. IPN was originally described in young salmonids, but the greatest losses have historically occurred in Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) following sea transfer despite high vaccination coverage. The number of cases fell drastically in Norway after the introduction of IPN virus (IPNV)-resistant QTL-roe and the reduction of 'house strains'. title: Tetrodotoxin (TTX): What do we currently know? The state of the art
abstract: Tetrodotoxin (TTX) is one of the most potent naturally occurring neurotoxins and continues to attract considerable scientific, clinical, forensic, and regulatory attention. Historically associated with pufferfish poisoning in East and Southeast Asia, TTX has recently emerged as a global food safety concern due to its detection in an increasing number of marine and terrestrial organisms and its expanding geographical distribution, including European coastal waters. abstract: Oriented ship detection in complex nearshore and harbor SAR imagery is challenged by nonhomogeneous sea clutter and land-based strong scatterers, attenuation of weak ship structures during downsampling, and mismatch between classification confidence and oriented-box localization quality. abstract: Abstract In Brachyura, reproduction involves a range of behavioral, morphological, and physiological mechanisms that contribute to reproductive success. The land crab Johngarthia lagostoma , endemic to four oceanic islands in the South Atlantic, shows no clear pre- or post-copulatory guarding behavior, and the mechanisms involved in sexual selection remain uncertain. abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution and bacterial antimicrobial resistance are converging public health concerns. MPs provide persistent, mobile surfaces that can transport antibiotic-resistant bacteria and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). After aging and conditioning, MPs can develop biofilms in which resistance determinants accumulate, persist, and undergo horizontal transfer. title: Valorisation of Stichopus fusiformiossa body wall with high-pressure-induced endogenous proteolysis
abstract: Collagen-rich marine biomass is a promising source of proteins, peptides, and glycosaminoglycans, but their recovery is constrained by the dense extracellular matrix. This study evaluated high-pressure processing as a short-duration, non-thermal strategy for systematically disassembling the mutable collagenous tissue of Stichopus fusiformiossa and promoting endogenous biotransformation without added water or exogenous enzymes. title: “The Guy(s) from California”: Race, the Tax Code, and the Relational Geographies of Rental Housing in Memphis
abstract: This article examines how high net worth, individual investors from coastal markets have reshaped the rental market in Memphis, Tennessee, and could be playing a growing role in housing markets across the United States. Drawing on interviews with local “turn-key” real estate companies and a computational analysis of property data across Memphis, I show how the historical trajectory of racial capitalism, coupled with the fallout of the 2008 financial crisis, has enabled local property managers to channel out-of-state investment from high-cost markets like California into Memphis neighborhoods.

Although fishes are critical for ecosystem health, spatial management rarely accounts for the interconnectedness of fish habitat needs across their life cycle. title: Spatial pattern analysis of built-up land use and zoning conformity using polygon-based statistics: a case study of Tegal city, Indonesia
abstract: Rapid urban expansion in coastal cities increasingly challenges the effectiveness of spatial planning enforcement. Tegal city, located on Java’s northern coast, is experiencing intensive built-up land development accompanied by growing spatial clustering. This study analyses polygon-level built-up land patterns using Ripley’s K-function to identify multi-scale clustering, Global Moran’s I to assess spatial autocorrelation, and Local Moran’s I (LISA) to detect local clusters. abstract: This study investigates the effects of inorganic salts and natural water matrices on the high-frequency sonochemical degradation of Naphthol Blue Black (NBB). title: Synchronous recovery of multiple valuable metals from municipal solid waste incineration fly ash and red mud via co-reduction technology
abstract: Abstract Municipal solid waste incineration fly ash (FA) and red mud (RM) are hazardous industrial solid wastes that pose potential environmental and safety risks if improperly stored or disposed of. abstract: Perennial pluvial flooding presents significant challenges to the urban environment of Port Harcourt Metropolis, impacting infrastructure, public health, and overall urban functionality. abstract: Legal designation is a necessary foundation for protected-area governance, but it does not demonstrate whether authority, resources and implementation generate measurable conservation gains. This study assessed management effectiveness at Al Hoceima National Park, a 48,460-ha mixed terrestrial–marine protected area on Morocco’s Mediterranean coast, using the Integrated Management Effectiveness Tool (IMET). title: Development and expression validation of an EGFP-tagged human Kv1.3 channel construct as a platform for functional studies
abstract: Voltage-gated potassium channel Kv1.3 is a key regulator of membrane potential and ionic homeostasis, particularly in immune signalling. Despite its importance, tools for directly visualizing Kv1.3 dynamics in living mammalian cells are limited, which restricts the comprehensive evaluation of its biological functions. To address this gap, we developed an enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP)-tagged human Kv1.3 construct for expression in mammalian cells, enabling fluorescence-based visualization of the expressed fusion protein. abstract: Nature-based Solutions (NbS) offer promise for flood resilience in coastal communities, yet public support remains a barrier to implementation. title: Institutionalizing the social values of land: a critical review of concepts, methods, and planning translation
abstract: Social values are increasingly acknowledged in land management and spatial planning, particularly amid urbanization and sustainable development. Yet many planning systems have not institutionalized these values, leaving land-use decisions largely shaped by economic and technical rationalities. This article presents a systematic literature review of how the social values of land (SVoL) are conceptualized, interpreted, and operationalized in the context of land management and spatial planning. This study investigates the baseline locomotion of the marine amphipod Marinogammarus marinus to external light triggers to support standardised laboratory behavioural assays. abstract: Abstract Bermudagrass ( Cynodon spp.) is one of the most common warm‐season perennial grasses utilized in the southeastern United States for pasture or stored forage. However, there is a paucity of data evaluating the fecal nutrient losses overtime by cattle grazing different bermudagrass cultivars. In Bangladesh, the forests and adjacent bodies of water provide protection against coastal hazards, support a variety of flora and fauna, capture carbon and sustain communities that rely on natural resources. title: Paper in the Floodplain: and other instructions for drawing
abstract: This essay will bring together a body of work that attempts to capture human performance and natural phenomena on paper as a way of drawing and scoring encounters with place. In what ways do place (and land) escape our efforts to represent and capture it, while simultaneously embedding its temporal marks, ciphers, and imprints? abstract: Abstract Temperature and precipitation variability in monsoonal Asia is central to understanding regional climate dynamics and global teleconnections. abstract: Bacteriophages (“phage”) are viruses that prey on bacteria in diverse environments, from biological tissues to soils. abstract: Seabirds are especially vulnerable to ingesting plastic pollution. However, we have a limited understanding of which traits might increase their risk of plastic ingestion. abstract: The characterization of pathogens affecting Antarctic wildlife has been historically limited and sporadic. With the introduction of H5N1 high pathogenicity avian influenza virus (HPAIV) in Antarctica in the austral summer 2023/2024, concerns about the health of Antarctic seabirds and mammals prompted immediate surveillance efforts. In March 2024, we visited the Danger Islands archipelago, that hosts two mega-colonies of Adélie penguins, and observed an unusual mortality estimated in thousands of Adélie penguins and other species. title: Evaluation of Microplastics Environmental Impact from Straws in the US over Time: Scenario Based Semi Quantitative Scaling Emission Approximation Versus Bioresin Alternatives to Polypropylene
abstract: Microplastics pollution has been analyzed and researched extensively in the past 20 years as a pollutant that must be controlled. Among many other plastic products, the disposable drinking straw market projection is increasing; thus, it must remain a focus of environmental scientists. Due to their small size and lack of regulations, straws generally end up in landfills or oceans, where they degrade into micro- (MPs) and nanoplastics (NPs), which can cause serious health risks such as cancer and endocrine disruption. title: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF WORD FREQUENCY IN “LOOKING FOR ALASKA” AND “PAPER TOWN” USING VOYANT TOOLS
abstract: This study aims to compare the word frequency patterns in two novels by John Green, Looking for Alaska and Paper Towns, using Voyant Tools as a corpus analysis platform. The research focuses on identifying the most frequently used words, analyzing cross-document term distribution, exploring collocate patterns, and interpreting thematic implications based on the lexical data. Both novels were selected due to their thematic similarities and their popularity among young adult readers, making them suitable candidates for comparative corpus analysis. title: Light‐Weight Sustainable Composite From Virgin and Recycled Polypropylene Blends and Biocarbon for Automotive Part Application
abstract: ABSTRACT This work develops lightweight, sustainable PP/rPP/biocarbon composites targeting automotive applications. Virgin PP was blended with automotive recycled PP (rPP) at 70/30 and 50/50 ratios; the 50PP/50rPP blend exhibited the highest impact strength (31.54 J/m) with acceptable stiffness and was selected as the composite matrix. title: Defect-engineered Ce 3+ -doped borosilicate glass scintillator for multifunctional and environment-adaptive X-Ray imaging
abstract: Abstract Advanced scintillation materials capable of simultaneously delivering ultrahigh efficiency, exceptional stability, and multifunctional X-ray imaging remain elusive because of intrinsic trade-offs in conventional scintillators. Hernin, a defect-engineered Ce3+-activated borosilicate glass was developed. It exhibits high internal/external quantum efficiencies of 92.4%/85%, an ultrafast lifetime of 142.3 ns, and XEL intensity further reaching 190% of BGO after “bright-burning effect”, setting a new performance benchmark for Ce3+-activated glass scintillators.
