title: Deciphering coccolith formation: advanced microscopy insights from the biomineralization of Gephyrocapsa huxleyi
abstract: Coccolithophores are unicellular marine phytoplankton that produce complex and intricately shaped mineralized scales called coccoliths. Coccoliths are produced in an intracellular vesicle where crystal nucleation occurs, from which several individual calcite units develop with anisotropic crystallographic facets, prompting studies into the cellular mechanisms that control crystal growth within the cell. Health Risk Implications of PM₂. ₅, PM₁₀, Vocs, and Formaldehyde at Waterfront Residential Buildings of Port Harcourt Metropolis Rivers State
abstract: Indoor air pollution in waterfront communities of Port Harcourt poses significant public health concerns due to poor housing conditions, marine activities and inadequate ventilation. This study assessed the indoor air concentrations of PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, VOCs, and formaldehyde (HCHO) in ten waterfronts communities namely Rex Lawson Waterfront, Eagle Island Waterfront, Bundu Ama Waterfront Elechi Beach Waterfront, Enugu Waterfront, Ibadan Waterfront, Marine Base Waterfront, Okirika Waterfront, Slaughter Waterfront and Woji Waterfront and ten residential building in each of the communities. title: Integrating land-use dynamics, water quality, and multi-criteria ecological suitability for fish sanctuary prioritization in three major river basins of Bangladesh
abstract: Riverine ecosystems in monsoon-dominated regions are increasingly constrained by interacting pressures from land-use change, hydrological alteration, and water-quality degradation, yet these drivers are rarely assessed within a unified framework. This study presents a reproducible, basin-scale framework integrating multi-season (monsoon–dry) land-use dynamics (2000–2020), hydrochemical assessment (including nutrients and trace metals), and GIS-based Multi-Criteria ecological modeling to delineate fish sanctuary suitability across the Ganges–Padma, Brahmaputra–Jamuna, and Barak–Meghna basins of

title: Emergence of nonequilibrium Lieb excitations in periodically-driven strongly-interacting bosons
abstract: We study the exact nonequilibrium spectral function of a gas of strongly correlated Tonks-Girardeau bosons subjected to a strong periodic drive. Utilizing the theory of Floquet spectral function in conjunction with the Bose-Fermi mapping theorem, we show that nonequilibrium Lieb modes emerge if the underlying mapped fermions form a Floquet-Fermi sea. In the low-frequency regime, the exact analysis reveals the emergence of characteristic linear Lieb excitations for the bosonic system, while the underlying mapped fermions displays the wide Dirac-like linear dispersion.

title: Global patterns are key to understanding macroevolution
abstract: Regional diversification patterns are increasingly being used to investigate spatial heterogeneity in biodiversity evolution and its drivers. However, estimating and interpreting regional diversification rates is complicated by the fact that regional diversity fluctuations reflect multiple biological processes and may be more sensitive to temporal sampling bias than global patterns. Here, we assess the biological fidelity and sampling sensitivity of regional diversification rates using fossil occurrences of marine invertebrates. We show that immigrations and extirpations account for up to 76%

title: A Holistic Mapping Approach to the Seine River Basin and the Port City Territory of Paris: Developing Historically Informed Awareness for Future Designs
abstract: Rivers and ports have historically shaped European cities, yet their wider territorial and spatial relationships remain insufficiently understood. This article proposes a multi-scalar, holistic and historically informed mapping approach to examine river port city territories as interconnected systems linking hydrology, logistics, urban form, governance and heritage. Building on the methodology developed for the Port City Atlas and refined for the River Port City Atlas, it investigates the Seine basin between Paris and Le Havre, revealing how inherited infrastructures and institutional fragment

title: The geographic and elevational distribution of the genus Natalus Gray, 1838 (Mammalia, Chiroptera) in Guatemala, including the first record of N. lanatus Tejedor, 2005
abstract: We document the first confirmed record of Natalus lanatus from Guatemala, increasing the national bat fauna to 107 species, and present the first country-level synthesis of the geographic and elevational distribution of the genus Natalus . Morphological analyses of N. lanatus ( n = 8) and N. mexicanus ( n = 8) show clear differentiation, with the first two FAMD dimensions explaining 61% of total variance. Voucher-based records further show elevational segregation, with N. lanatus occurring at 731–2,573 m and N. mexicanus from near sea level to 523 m.
institutions: Universidad de San Carlos de Guatemala

title: Analysis of Fin Stabilizer Effects on 100 GT Fishing Vessel Resistance Using Computational Fluid Dynamics
abstract: Fishing vessels require good hydrodynamic efficiency to limit propulsion power and energy consumption. Adding a fin stabilizer can modify the flow pattern, pressure distribution, wetted area, and consequently the total resistance; however, studies specifically addressing its resistance effect on a 100 GT fishing vessel remain limited. This study compares the flow characteristics and ship resistance before and after fin-stabilizer installation using Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). The hull geometry was developed from a 25 GT fishing-vessel dataset through a scaling approach, producing a wor

title: Hydration channel engineering in Tröger’s base-POP membranes for mono/multivalent cation and anion discrimination
abstract: Sustainable recovery of critical resources from complex aqueous streams is constrained by membranes that fail to combine rapid ion transport with precise mono/multivalent discrimination. Here, we report Tröger’s base-derived porous organic polymer (POP) membranes with rigid, covalently crosslinked microporous frameworks that stabilize angstrom-scale transport channels while suppressing hydration-induced swelling. title: Evaluasi Kesesuaian Lahan Agroklimat Tanaman Kopi Robusta pada Kondisi Rata-Rata dan Tahun El Nino di Kabupaten Lampung Barat
abstract: El Nino has the potential to alter the agroclimatic land suitability of Robusta coffee (Coffea canephora) through reduced rainfall and prolonged dry periods. This study aims to map the spatial distribution of agroclimatic land suitability for Robusta coffee in West Lampung Regency under long term average conditions (1995–2024) and during El Nino years within the same period. Land suitability was evaluated using an equal-weight scoring method based on six parameters: air temperature, rainfall, dry-month length, relative humidity, slope, and soil texture, following the criteria of Ritung et al.
journal: Jurnal Pendidikan Sains Geologi dan Geofisika (GeoScienceEd Journal)

title: Agonistic interactions and vocalizations among Procellariiformes in multi-species feeding aggregations, observed through bird-borne cameras
abstract: Marine predators frequently aggregate at food sources, where interactions can range from cooperative group hunting to interference competition for resources. To investigate interactions at feeding aggregations among procellariiforms, we equipped wandering albatrosses Diomedea exulans with video cameras, collecting 43 hours of footage from 22 individuals. Cameras from eight birds recorded feeding aggregations, capturing a total of 62 minutes of footage (2.7% of observations). title: Chemical stress drives opposing bacterial biomass responses at the single-cell level
abstract: Abstract Microbial biomass is a central functional trait governing nutrient turnover and trophic transfer in aquatic ecosystems, yet how chemical stress reshapes biomass at the level of individual cells remains poorly resolved. Conventional toxicity assays primarily detect population-level growth inhibition and overlook sublethal physiological responses and heterogeneity within microbial populations. Here, we quantify single-cell dry-mass, a label-free proxy for cellular biomass and biosynthetic state, in the fast-growing marine bacterium Vibrio natriegens. Across thousands of cells, we assess

title: Phylogenetic Reconstruction of Cephalaspidea Using Multiple Datasets and Inference Frameworks
abstract: ABSTRACT Cephalaspidea is a key group within the Heterobranchia characterized by high species diversity and broad ecological disparity, and it is widely studied in marine ecology and systematics. Previous studies have proposed a preliminary phylogenetic framework for Cephalaspidea using few sanger sequenced phylogenetic markers and transcriptome‐scale datasets. However, relationships among several lineages remain contentious, which may partly reflect sparse sampling of key taxa and differences in topological signal among markers, datasets and analytical assumptions. institutions: Qingdao National Laboratory for Marine Science and Technology

title: Development of a city level nitrogen dioxide exposure (CLeNE) intelligence platform for West Africa
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) is a major urban air pollutant, yet assessment of population exposure remains challenging across West Africa due to lack of uncoordinated sparse monitoring infrastructure. We present the City-Level Nitrogen Dioxide Exposure (CLeNE) platform, an interactive exposure intelligence system that integrates Sentinel-5P TROPOMI NO 2 observations, population data, and city boundaries to quantify and visualize urban exposure burden. title: Nanocomposite of TiO2 and Phase-transition-derived α-Fe2O3 for Enhancing Photocatalytic Dye Degradation
abstract: Although a-Fe2O3 is a promising photocatalyst for Advanced Oxidation Processes in dye-polluted wastewater treatment, its practical efficiency is limited by inherent drawbacks including rapid electron-hole recombination and poor electron mobility. This study proposes a TiO2/a-Fe2O3 nanocomposite system to enhance dye removal efficiency of a-Fe2O3, specifically Methylene Blue (MB), in which hierarchical porous, coral-like a-Fe2O3 was prepared via a thermal phase transition process from g-Fe2O3. title: Identification of potential pathogenic genes for lung adenocarcinoma induced by 6PPD-quinone through network toxicology and SHAP analysis
abstract: Background Lung cancer continues to maintain a high mortality rate, with lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) being its most common type. As an emerging environmental pollutant, 6PPD-quinone is attracting increasing attention. Through network toxicology, we constructed a prognostic model and validated it with molecular docking and dynamics simulations, revealing its underlying molecular mechanisms. Methods RNA-seq and clinical data of LUAD were obtained from the TCGA database, and differential expression analysis was performed using DESeq2. Putative targets of 6PPD-quinone were retrieved from DIGEP-Pred

title: Delineation of groundwater potential zones in Chalan Beel (inland wetland) for sustainable ecosystem in Lower Atrai River Basin NW Bangladesh
abstract: Groundwater plays a critical role in sustaining the ecological integrity and water security of the Chalan Beel, the largest inland wetland (5097 km2) in the Lower Atrai River Basin of northwestern Bangladesh. This study delineates groundwater potential zones (GWPZs) using an integrated Geographic Information System (GIS), Remote Sensing (RS), and Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) approach. title: FECH negatively regulates protoporphyrin IX accumulation and shell coloration in the dwarf surf clam Mulinia lateralis
abstract: Shell color in mollusks, shaped by pigment synthesis and deposition, offers a readily observable natural trait. The dwarf surf clam Mulinia lateralis serves as an ideal bivalve model but has a uniform white shell, which limits its utility for genetic studies. In this study, we aimed to explore the feasibility of constructing a shell color‑based endogenous reporter by inducing pigment accumulation. institutions: Qingdao National Laboratory for Marine Science and Technology

title: Toxicogenetic profiling of an antifungal lawsone silver salt: in silico and in vitro analysis in 2D and 3D mammalian models
abstract: Abstract The development of novel metal-based antifungals requires rigorous characterization of their toxicological mechanisms to ensure patient safety. This study investigated the toxicogenetic profile and cellular interactions of lawsone silver salt (LSS), a compound with established activity against Sporothrix spp. and emerging multidrug-resistant pathogens. Antifungal efficacy was confirmed against planktonic Aspergillus fumigatus , Candida albicans , and C. auris (MIC 1.45–23.2 µM), with significant anti-biofilm activity against C. albicans (185.9 µM) and A. fumigatus (92.9 µM). title: AN INFORMATION MODEL FOR ACCOUNTING-REGULATORY-OPERATIONAL DATA CONVERGENCE IN US SMALL-CARRIER TRUCKING
abstract: This study aims to conceptualize the distinctive accounting-information environment of American small-carrier trucking, where a single owner-operator or a management team of one or two persons typically manages freight movement, financial recording, tax compliance, and equipment tracking as an integrated activity. title: Bioorthogonal Chemistry in Neurobiology: From Imaging to Proteomics
abstract: Bioorthogonal click chemistry has emerged as a versatile approach for probing molecules with high selectivity and minimal perturbation. While applicable to diverse biomolecules, its use in protein studies has proven particularly powerful, especially in neurobiology, where precise molecular tools are essential. A key technology enabling such precision is genetic code expansion (GCE), which allows the incorporation of unnatural amino acids (UAAs) bearing bioorthogonal handles into proteins. title: Solar resource assessment and performance forecasting of a utility-scale photovoltaic plant in Bhutan: A high-altitude Himalayan case study
abstract: High-altitude solar photovoltaic (PV) deployment can diversify electricity supply in hydropower-dominated Himalayan regions, particularly during the dry season. This study evaluates the technical feasibility, site suitability, solar resource, and forecast performance of a proposed utility-scale plant at Ladrong, Bhutan. The method integrates GIS terrain screening, slope and aspect classification, horizon and near-shading analysis, grid connectivity, and PVsyst simulation. title: A new teleosauroid (Crocodylomorpha, Thalattosuchia) with a unique dentition from the Middle Jurassic of eastern Morocco
abstract: The Mesozoic and early Paleogene of Morocco provides a rich and extensive record of crocodylomorphs encompassing a wide range of skull, dental morphologies, and paleoecologies. Here we describe a new longirostrine teleosaurid thalattosuchian, Ctenosuchus tenuidens, gen. et sp. nov. with a needle-like dentition from a Middle Jurassic fluvio-lacustrine sequence of the Talsint–Anoual area of Figuig Province, southeastern Morocco. title: MONDE ·T: A database and interactive webserver for non‐standard amino acids and peptide components in the PDB
abstract: Non-standard amino acids (ncAAs) together with synthetic additions (like caps and linkers) are of wide interest for protein design and pharmaceutical optimization, as they can improve physicochemical properties and possibly reshape protein structure. Their inclusion in experimental structures has not been explored systematically. It remains elusive which components are those most impactful for protein design. title: Arbuscular Mycorrhizal fungi alleviate salinity stress in Avicennia marina through morphophysiological and biochemical modulation
abstract: Increasing salinity threatens coastal mangrove ecosystems worldwide by impairing plant growth, physiological function, and biochemical processes, ultimately reducing productivity and survival. The present study was conducted to examine the impact of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) on Avicennia marina under different salt concentrations (9, 14, and 19 dS/m). This study included four treatments i.e. negative control (only salt: T1), species consortium of Glomus (T2), species consortium of Gigaspora (T3), consortium of both Glomus and Gigaspora spp. (T4) along with positive control (T0). title: Vanishing Night Skies: An Ecological Perspective of India’s Rural - Urban Light Divide
abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial light at night (ALAN) across India is increasingly transforming nocturnal environments with significant ecological consequences. This study investigates the rural–urban gradient of light pollution and its ecological implications by analyzing the spatial distribution and intensity of nighttime illumination across selected urban and rural regions of India. Nighttime radiance data derived from the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) for 2024 were integrated with ground-based observations using a Sky Quality Meter (SQM) to evaluate variations in sky

title: Beyond Basic ICT Access: Pedagogical Integration of Geospatial Technologies in Geography Teaching in Temeke Municipality, Tanzania
abstract: Digital technology is now central to competence-based Geography education, yet access and pedagogical use remain uneven in Tanzanian public schools. This study examined how ICT integration supports Geography teaching and learning in Temeke Municipality. Its main objective was to assess whether available technology was being converted into subject-specific, learner-centred practice. A mixed-methods approach and cross-sectional survey design were used. The sample comprised 120 participants: 100 students, 16 Geography teachers, and four Ward Education Officers. title: Materialidades efímeras de las artes escénicas: el caso chileno-costarricense en la colección Huellas del exilio de Proyecto Arde y LaMAE
abstract: The purpose of this article is to analyze the theater posters and playbills that form part of Huellas del exilio collection, housed within the digital archives of Proyecto Arde in collaboration with LaMAE, and produced during the Chilean exile in Costa Rica. To this end, this study approaches these materials through the documentary typology of ephemera, investigating core axes related to: their participation within print culture, their modes of circulation and deployment across subjects and surfaces for public display, the forms of reading they elicit and their materiality. title: THERMAL COMFORT MAPPING OF PUBLIC SQUARES USING LANDSCAPE INTERVENTIONS
abstract: Rapid urbanization and rising temperatures had reduced the usability of public squares in tropical megacities, limiting their role as inclusive civic spaces. This study assessed outdoor thermal comfort and tested the effectiveness of landscape interventions in seven renowned public squares in Lagos, Nigeria: Tafawa Balewa Square, Muri Okunola Park, Freedom Park, JJT Park, Gani Fawehinmi Park, Iga Idunganran Palace Square, and Tinubu Square. journal: International Journal of Environmental Design and Construction Management

title: Synergistic Co‐Fermentation of Ulva and Waste Activated Sludge for Sustainable Resource Recovery: Mechanistic Insights From Dissolved Organic Matter Transformation and Multi‐Omics Analysis
abstract: Anaerobic fermentation for volatile fatty acids (VFAs) production represents the sustainable and resource-recovery strategy for waste activated sludge (WAS) treatment, yet its efficiency is often hampered by low substrate C/N ratio and limited hydrolysis. Ulva, a macroalga responsible for extensive "green tides" that burden coastal ecosystems and economies, emerges as an ideal co-substrate for WAS anaerobic fermentation due to its high C/N ratio and biodegradability. institutions: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

title: Chemical profiling and multitarget computational screening reveal bioactive phytochemical scaffolds from Echiochilon pauciflorum stocks ex wight
abstract: Echiochilon pauciflorum (Boraginaceae) is an underexplored coastal medicinal plant. We combined GC–MS profiling, multitarget docking, ADMET prediction and cytotoxicity testing to prioritize its constituents. GC–MS analysis of aqueous, methanolic and ethanolic extracts and a hexane-trapped volatile fraction gave 271 peaks; after contaminant screening and grading of library matches, 44 compounds were tentatively identified as plausible plant metabolites, dominated by lupane- and oleanane-type triterpenoids, C13-norisoprenoids, phytosterols and Boraginaceae-type pyrrolizidine alkaloids. title: Assessment of Flood Risks on Power Infrastructure and Renewable Energy Installations in Ogba-Egbema-Ndoni Local Government Area, Rivers State
abstract: This research evaluated the flood hazards that impact power systems and renewable energy setups in the Ogba-Egbema-Ndoni Local Government Area (ONELGA) located in Rivers State, Nigeria. The primary goals included investigating how vulnerable energy infrastructure is to factors such as flood depth, speed, and duration; studying the vital interconnections between energy networks and other crucial services including water provision, healthcare, and transport; and calculating the economic damage and downtime caused by flood effects. journal: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY

title: Multiple introductions and spread of novel reassortant highly pathogenic avian influenza A (H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses via wild birds, South Korea, 2024–2025
abstract: Between 14 October 2024 and 24 March 2025, 43 cases of clade 2.3.4.4b highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) type A (H5N1) infections in wild birds and 1 case in a leopard cat were detected through the national HPAI surveillance program. We performed whole-genome sequencing of 51 isolates and investigated their phylogenetic relationships. Phylogenetic analyses identified nine distinct genotypes, designated Kor24-25A to Kor24-25I. title: GNSS navigation interference disrupts telemetry tracking of raptors migrating between Europe and Africa
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) interference in war conflict zones can disrupt wildlife tracking for research and conservation efforts. In 2023 and 2024, we tagged Black Kites Milvis migrans in Moldova and Kazakhstan, respectively, with telemetry loggers, tracked them until September 2025 and found that 20 out of the 24 Black Kites had interfered (erroneous) geographical position fixes. title: Sympatric pikas partition microhabitats differently across a spatial-elevational gradient
abstract: Abstract How closely related, ecologically similar species co-occur and navigate competition remains a central question in community ecology. Microhabitat partitioning in patchy environments can support the co-existence of sympatric species on small spatial scales. We quantified niche spaces and directional niche overlaps of three cold-adapted, high-altitude pikas (Ochotona spp.) from the Trans-Himalayas to understand their responses to interspecific competition across elevational and spatial scales. title: Facade and Opening Design Strategies for Enhancing Natural Lighting Efficiency in Classrooms at SD Labschool UPI
abstract: Natural lighting is an essential aspect of elementary school building design, as it significantly influences visual comfort and learning effectiveness. However, many classrooms in Indonesia do not meet the minimum illuminance standard of 350 lux specified in SNI 03-6197-2020. This study aims to evaluate and optimize facade and opening design strategies to improve the performance of natural lighting at SD Labschool UPI. title: Integrative network pharmacology and genetic evidence identifies NFKB1 as a predicted target of Terpinen-4-ol in psoriasis
abstract: Terpinen-4-ol (T4OL), a tea tree oil component, has anti‑inflammatory effects, but its psoriasis mechanism is unclear. We predicted T4OL targets via SEA, SuperPred, and TargetNet, and identified DEGs from GSE41662. Overlapping targets were subjected to functional enrichment, and PPI network construction. Mendelian randomization assessed causal relationships between core targets and psoriasis. We identified 159 T4OL targets, of which 42 overlapped with psoriasis DEGs. title: Public health emergencies in Jordan: appraising multi-agency preparedness
abstract: Jordan faces a complex landscape of public health threats arising from infectious disease outbreaks, environmental hazards, technological incidents, humanitarian crises, and regional instability. These risks place sustained pressure on national institutions responsible for preparedness, response, and resilience. While multiple governmental and non-governmental agencies contribute to public health emergency preparedness and response (PHEPR), coordination gaps, overlapping mandates, and fragmented governance structures continue to challenge the effectiveness of a unified national response. title: Red Fluorescent Labeling of Myelin by Membrane‐Targeted tdTomato in Transgenic Mouse Lines
abstract: ABSTRACT Myelin is a highly complex membranous structure wrapped around axons by oligodendrocytes or Schwann cells in the central and peripheral nervous system, respectively. Fluorescent labeling is widely used to study the structure and dynamics of myelin. Combining structural with functional imaging requires labeling of myelin with red fluorescence, as many functional sensors, including Ca 2+ indicators and genetically encoded metabolite sensors, fluoresce in the green spectral range. title: Untargeted metabolomic profiling of sweet potato latent virus infected Nicotiana benthamiana
abstract: Viral diseases, the second most significant biotic stress, cause substantial yield loss and quality deterioration in sweet potato, and sweet potato latent virus (SPLV) is one of the dominant viral pathogens infecting sweet potato in China. To investigate SPLV-induced metabolic changes, untargeted LC-MS (liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry) was used on Nicotiana benthamiana inoculated with SPLV-infected sweet potato leaf sap. institutions: Linyi Vocational University of Science and Technology

title: Cyanobacterial blooms at Canadian freshwater beaches: A prospective cohort study of exposure, health outcomes, and One Health implications
abstract: Cyanobacterial blooms are an emerging One Health concern in freshwater environments, yet limited evidence exists on how humans and companion animals interact with bloom-prone waters or how these exposures align with water-quality indicators. This study characterizes recreational behaviours, environmental conditions, and illness patterns across multiple Canadian beaches to inform integrated monitoring and risk-management approaches. title: Northern movements of European Nathusius’ pipistrelle bats ( Pipistrellus nathusii ) before autumn migration
abstract: Despite decades of protecting migrating animals by international treaties, conservation efforts are severely hampered by our limited understanding of large-scale seasonal movements, particularly in cryptic migratory animals like bats. Banding data from a field site on the Latvian coast of the Baltic Sea suggests that some European Nathusius’ bats (Pipistrellus nathusii) move > 2000 km to their wintering range in Spain and France. title: Institutional Adoption and Economic Feasibility of Rainwater Harvesting in Existing University Buildings: A Review
abstract: Rainwater harvesting in existing university buildings requires an appraisal that connects institutional priorities, feasible retrofits and financial consequences. Selected reviews address system design, research trends and implementation barriers, providing a basis for examining how these considerations inform successive appraisal decisions. abstract: Dual-bell nozzles (DBNs) provide passive altitude compensation by adapting their effective expansion ratio through controlled flow separation and reattachment. title: A Bibliometric Analysis on Water Footprint in Industry: Global Research Trends and Mapping of Scientific Networks
abstract: This study aims to reveal the development and intellectual structure of global scientific production on the Water Footprint (WF) in industry through bibliometric methods. A total of 3,052 research and review articles published up to 22.12.2025 and indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection database were included in the analysis. abstract: This study examines how visual resources accompanying reading materials in English for Nusantara for Grade VIII may support reading comprehension. A qualitative textbook content analysis was conducted on all 18 explicit Reading and Your Turn: Reading sections in Chapters 1-5. title: Molecular Prevalence and Antimicrobial Resistance Patterns of Methicillin‐Resistant Staphylococcus aureus in Buffaloes from Bangladesh
abstract: BACKGROUND: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is an emerging zoonotic pathogen in livestock and poses a potential public health threat. OBJECTIVE: This cross-sectional study investigated the prevalence, antimicrobial resistance profiles and molecular characteristics of S. aureus and MRSA isolated from buffalo nasal swabs in the Sylhet and Noakhali districts of Bangladesh. title: Compound and cascading climate risks in urban infrastructure governance and resilience across North America
abstract: North American cities are increasingly exposed to climate-related hazards that do not occur in isolation. Extreme heat, drought, flooding, hurricanes, wildfires, wildfire smoke, and sea-level rise interact with aging infrastructure, uneven urbanization, social vulnerability, and fragmented governance systems. As a result, an initial climate shock can trigger cascading failures across energy, water, transport, telecommunications, housing, health, and emergency response systems. title: Direct seeding and turf transplantation can reintroduce native species in grassland degraded by pine plantation
abstract: Abstract Introduction Grasslands worldwide have been extensively converted to exotic tree plantations, resulting in persistent degradation and limited natural recovery after tree removal. In southern Brazil, pine plantations alter soil conditions and create dense litter layers that restrict native plant regeneration, highlighting the need for active restoration. abstract: ABSTRACT Fireflies are semelparous beetles whose immature stages are largely unknown. The comparatively few larvae known span diverse ecological niches, such as ground‐dwellers, aquatic (freshwater or marine), semi‐aquatic and arboreal. Psilocladus costae Vaz, Silveira & Rosa, 2020—a bromeliad dweller—is the only species of its genus and subfamily in which immature stages were studied. title: Integrating Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Landuse/Land Cover Changes and Urban Growth in Modelling Surface Temperature Variations of Asaba Metropolis, Delta State
abstract: Rapid urbanization and land use/land cover (LULC) change have significantly altered urban thermal environments, intensifying urban heat island effects and increasing climate-related risks in developing cities. This study investigates the spatio-temporal relationship between LULC dynamics, urban growth, and land surface temperature (LST) in Asaba Metropolis, Delta State, Nigeria, over a 20-year period (2002–2022). abstract: When a satellite observes the Earth at an angle, the apparent position of elevated features, such as mountains, clouds or fires in high terrain, can be shifted from their true ground location. title: Key Drivers in the Development of the Green Economy in the Gulf and Levant States
abstract: This study identifies the main factors and trends in green economy development across the Gulf and Levant countries and examines their spatial patterns. The environmentally significant processes observed in these countries suggest the possible, though not predetermined, onset of a long-term transition toward more sustainable economies. However, it remains too early to conclude that a genuine transition toward decarbonization is underway. title: Genotyping by Sequencing (GBS) uncovers genetic diversity and population structure for salicornia breeding programs in Iran
abstract: Salicornia, a succulent halophyte flourishing in coastal and mangrove ecosystems, holds significant economic and ecological promise. Establishing sustainable cultivation systems requires a profound understanding of its geographical distribution, genetic potential, and the identification of agronomically superior populations. Despite this potential, comprehensive genomic investigations into the genus remain scarce. abstract: Background Out-of-pocket expenditure (OOPE) finances 43.4% of total health expenditure in India, and emergency trauma—unforeseeable, unpostponable and costly—is among the sharpest tests of whether a health-financing mechanism protects households from catastrophic spending. Insured and uninsured patients are normally treated in different facilities at different tariffs, confounding the effect of the payment mechanism with the setting in which care is given. abstract: Diabetic sarcopenic obesity (SO) is a complex metabolic condition characterized by the coexistence of obesity, diabetes, and sarcopenia, leading to poor prognosis. Astragalus, is a key herb in spleen-strengthening formulas, but its pharmacological mechanisms against diabetic SO remain unclear. Drug- and disease-related genes for Astragalus, obesity, diabetes, and sarcopenia were retrieved from public databases. abstract: This study reports the biosynthesis of a Selenium/Zinc nanocomposite (Se/Zn NC) using a marine bacterial extract from Bacillus rugosus SYG20. title: Mitochondrial and retroviral markers reveal high genetic diversity and regional structure in the Lebanese Awassi sheep
abstract: Abstract The Awassi is a native sheep breed of Lebanon with high historical and economic value. Despite its importance, its genetic background has not been characterized, leaving limited understanding of its origins, diversity, and regional connections. This study aimed to characterize the genetic diversity and population structure of Awassi sheep from Lebanon and neighboring Syria using two complementary genetic systems that trace distinct evolutionary histories: maternal mitochondrial DNA and insertional polymorphisms of endogenous Jaagsiekte sheep retroviruses. abstract: The Ébrié Lagoon, in the Grand-Bassam area, is exposed to various anthropogenic pressures that may alter is morphological and environnemental charactéristics. abstract: ABSTRACT Rising food insecurity is a pressing global concern. Many developing countries rely on a combination of international trade and food aid to satisfy the nutritional and caloric demands of their populations. Trade openness has been shown to have positive long‐term effects on food security; however, it can cause short‐term crises in food availability and affordability. abstract: Short-lived radiogenic isotope systems provide unique constraints on the preservation of early-formed reservoirs in Earth's mantle. We present the largest high-precision μ 142 Nd dataset for a single hotspot, comprising 55 analyses of 29 shield-stage tholeiitic basalts from the Hawaiian Islands. abstract: Despite recent advancements in corrosion resistance, magnesium (Mg) alloys still face significant challenges in structural applications due to their susceptibility to stress corrosion cracking (SCC) under combined mechanical stress and corrosive environments. abstract: Abstract Diclofenac (DIC)-prompted acute kidney injury (AKI) is associated with inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and dysregulated autophagy, all of which contribute to renal impairment. Using a network pharmacology approach followed by experimental validation, this study evaluated the reno-protecting actions of dapagliflozin (DAPA) and montelukast (MON) against DIC-induced AKI in rats, both alone and in combination. abstract: Abstract Urban and economic expansion across Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) may be shifting the relative contributions of dominant ambient air pollution sources, influencing both pollutant concentrations and composition, along with their associated health risks. abstract: Abstract Background The traditional habitat of the Chinese medicinal plant Cistanches Herba (CH) is the deserts of northwestern China. title: The Feral Life of Plastic Waste: Third Nature and Speculative Aesthetics
abstract: This article explores the interactions between plastic waste and non-human animals from a non-anthropocentric and future-oriented perspective. abstract: Background: Population-based genomic screening (PGS) holds promise for identifying individuals at elevated risk for hereditary conditions. However, the absence of implementation guidance limits the scalability and impact of these programs. abstract: A method for monitoring the ecological state of macrozoobenthos and damage to the habitats is developed on the base of mathematical model that describes transition of bottom animal communities from the biologically balanced state through unbalanced stadium to the physically controlled state. abstract: This study investigated selected aspects of the ecology of two gobiid fishes, Bostrychus africanus and Periophthalmus barbarus, inhabiting Bomu and Kono Creeks, Rivers State, Nigeria. Fish specimens were collected from the intesrtidal mudflats using basket traps between May 2023 and April 2024. title: Post-wildfire changes to water quality: a review with implications for harmful algal blooms and reservoir resiliency
abstract: Abstract Wildfires wreak havoc on both urban and natural ecosystems and are expected to worsen under future climate conditions. Wildfires have the potential for long-term impacts on the health of downstream reservoirs. This study seeks to compile current literature worldwide regarding impacts of wildfires on reservoir water quality, with a special focus on the implications for harmful algal blooms. abstract: Precession and obliquity play vital roles in orbital-scale climate change. However, their combined effects remain poorly understood. In this study, we examine how obliquity modulates precession-driven climate responses across Asian–African monsoon and arid regions (AAMAR). abstract: Understanding the bioaccumulation and trophic transfer of naturally occurring radionuclides is essential for assessing ecological risk in freshwater systems. This study provides a large-scale assessment of polonium-210 ( 210 Po) and lead-210 ( 210 Pb) bioaccumulation, trophic transfer and tissue-specific biodistribution in freshwater food webs across Canada. abstract: Nature-inspired compounds are increasingly recognized as promising sources of effective and environmentally safer antifouling (AF) agents. title: Pine trees, wind and limestone degradation, South Florida, USA
abstract: Exposed limestone is subject to numerous pedogenic processes, many which cause surface degradation. The uprooting of windthrown trees is a major pedogenic process, as demonstrated in South Florida pine forests. abstract: BACKGROUND: Microplastics (MPs) are ubiquitous contaminants increasingly detected in aquatic environments and wastewater systems, raising concerns regarding ecosystem and human health. Hospital wastewater has been identified as a source of MPs entering municipal systems; however, data on their occurrence, characteristics, and associated risks remain limited. abstract: Abstract Aims Potassium (K) fertilization recommendations commonly rely on exchangeable-K soil tests, assuming that this fraction represents the soil’s capacity to supply plant-available K. abstract: Abstract Seston stoichiometry links nutrient availability to the structure and functioning of aquatic food webs, yet how in-lake conditions interact with broader climatic, geomorphological and land-use drivers to shape seston carbon-to-phosphorus (C:P) ratios remains poorly understood in tropical systems. abstract: Corticosteroids are essential regulators of numerous physiological functions in vertebrates, including energy balance, immune responses, osmotic balance and metabolism. abstract: In this study, to elucidate the development of visual function in Pacific bluefin tuna (PBT; Thunnus orientalis ), we analyzed ontogenetic changes in the expression of visual opsin genes from hatching through the juvenile stage and evaluated wavelength- and intensity-dependent photobehavior using projected light. abstract: Abstract Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) is widely used as a solid lubricant but suffers from poor wear resistance, limiting its application in demanding mechanical components. abstract: Abstract We assessed the leaching potential of dissolved carbon (DC) from polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) microplastics (MPs), selected for their differing polymeric structure and response to thermal oxidation. abstract: Oil spillage poses profound threats to ecosystems and agricultural systems, particularly in regions where energy extraction coexists with farming communities. This comprehensive review explores how environmental policies mitigate spill risks, drawing on international conventions, national regulations, and case studies from Nigeria, the United States, Ecuador, and Norway. abstract: Mineral dust is a highly mobile component of Earth’s Critical Zone that influences ecosystem function, soil development, biogeochemical cycling, and environmental archives. abstract: Abstract The Permian witnessed profound geomagnetic, environmental, and biotic upheavals, yet high-resolution paleomagnetic constraints across critical transitions remain sparse. title: Microplastic Pollution in a Small River with an Agriculture-dominated Catchment under Different Rainfall Conditions: Transport Scaling, Characteristics and Ecological Risk Assessment
abstract: The agriculture cluster is recognized as a cryptic hotspot of microplastic pollution. Especially, rainfall-driven microplastic (MP) dynamics in small agricultural rivers have not been adequately quantified under various hydrological conditions. This study quantified MP concentrations, loads, characteristics, and ecological risks under baseline dry conditions and during four rainfall events of varying intensities in a small agricultural river. abstract: The feasibility study (FS) is an early phase that largely determines the success of a power plant development project, in which the plant layout is one of the key decisions affecting technical, safety, cost, construction, and operational aspects. This study analyzes the application of Prevention through Design (PtD) in developing the layout of the Java Bali 2 Combined Cycle Power Plant (PLTGU) by using Site Investigation (SI) results. abstract: ABSTRACT Environmental nucleic acids (eNA) are transforming ecological biomonitoring by enabling sensitive, scalable, and minimally invasive observations across multiple dimensions of ecological systems. Here, we examine how eNA can extend biomonitoring from ecological state assessment toward the inference of ecological trajectories. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Abstract Understanding public perceptions is essential for planning effective communication strategies to promote geoconservation. However, existing literature often oversimplifies this task, focusing mainly on socioeconomic data and scientific knowledge, while neglecting the influence of numerous other factors that shape perception. abstract: In this work, high-resolution one-dimensional (1D) 1 H NMR profiling is employed, enabling a novel non-destructive approach for characterization of release processes in optically opaque antifouling coatings. abstract: The accumulation of plastics and heavy metals (HMs) in the environment has become a significant global concern due to their persistence, ubiquity, and potential ecological impacts. Atmospheric micro- and nanoplastics (MP, NP) are capable of undergoing long-range transport and can be deposited onto plant shoots through precipitation, thereby exposing aerial plant tissues to these particulate contaminants. abstract: During embryonic development, cells undergo differentiation into highly specialized cell types. Capitalizing on single-cell RNA sequencing, many initiatives and substantial resources are cataloguing these differentiated cell types by their transcriptomic profiles. abstract: Floating pumice rafts generated by eruptions of submarine volcanoes can be transported over large distances, yet the role of surface waves in controlling pumice drift remains poorly constrained. Wave-induced transport is often parameterized indirectly in numerical simulations despite limited experimental observations. title: Adaptive track control for unmanned surface vessels using model predictive control: accounting for water depth and speed variations
abstract: Model Predictive Control (MPC) is applied to track control of unmanned surface vessels. To adapt to dynamic changes in speed and water depth, a water depth and speed dependent predictive model, with coefficients identified from free running tests (e.g., acceleration and zigzag trials), is developed. The nonlinear least square method is used for parameter estimation of the model. title: Biomechanical analyses point to dense collagen fibre architecture in an Ediacaran frond
abstract: Ediacaran macrofossils record the earliest large and complex organisms on Earth. Despite extensive study, fundamental aspects of their internal anatomy and tissue composition remain poorly known, limiting understanding of how these organisms were constructed and functioned, as well as how their complex anatomies evolved. title: Traveler's Palm ( Ravenala spp.) Across Habitats and Its Responses to Disturbance in North‐Eastern Madagascar
abstract: ABSTRACT The genus Ravenala (Strelitziaceae) comprises six species of arborescent herbs endemic to Madagascar and iconic to this global biodiversity hotspot. We examined how Ravenala density responds to environmental gradients, land‐use type, accessibility and canopy disturbance. The study was conducted in north‐eastern Madagascar, a region heavily affected by deforestation in recent decades. title: The cost of regulatory delay: quantifying how permitting timelines affect offshore wind energy costs
abstract: Abstract Rapid deployment of offshore renewable energy and transmission infrastructure can be a major contributor to energy system decarbonization. However, regulatory obligations frequently impose deployment delays that are typically not quantified in cost terms. The costs of such delays should be incorporated in project and technology assessments. abstract: Algal blooms are a global problem that lead to the formation of excessive algal organic matter, resulting in the deterioration of water sources and the disruption of water treatment processes. Methods for the extraction of algal organic matter from algal cells are time-consuming and sometimes ineffective in achieving cell lysis. abstract: Timely and accurate projections of when global warming will exceed the Paris Agreement’s 1.5 °C threshold are essential for effective climate policy. Existing estimates place this exceedance in the early 2030 s but carry substantial uncertainty. Here we analyze the latest observational temperature records through 2025 and identify a statistically significant doubling of the global warming rate during 2011–2025 (0.40 °C per decade) compared to 1971–2025 (0.20 °C per decade). abstract: Health benefits from emission controls are often inferred from reductions in fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) mass, yet this metric can underrepresent toxicity from PM 2.5 -bound metals. Using the COVID-19 lockdown as an intervention-like natural experiment, this study quantified how PM 2.5 -bound metals, emission sources, and inhalation health risks changed in Guangzhou, China. abstract: Abstract Microplastic (MP) pollution is increasingly recognized as a pervasive environmental stressor in freshwater ecosystems. This study evaluated the occurrence, characteristics, and ecological implications of MPs in the gastrointestinal tract of the endemic freshwater fish Squalius pursakensis from Sarısu Stream (Sakarya River Basin, Türkiye). abstract: Subduction zones govern Earth's deep volatile cycle. The slab-mantle interface is a key locus of volatile exchange between the subducting crust and the overlying mantle wedge, yet whether and how chemical reactions at this interface affect arc magmatism remains poorly constrained. Arc magmas typically lack a geochemical hallmark of garnet fractionation, leading to the prevailing interpretation that they derive predominantly from the shallower, garnet-free mantle wedge. CatSper is activated by intracellular alkalinization, membrane depolarization, and elevated temperature, which together ensure maximal current generation. abstract: Despite highly advanced technical monitoring for Alpine hazards, a persistent gap remains in translating risk information into community action. abstract: Quorum sensing (QS) enables bacterial coordination of group behaviors, yet how enteric pathogens modulate QS during intestinal colonization remains poorly understood. abstract: Spatial clusters of animal nests can be driven by mating behaviors, social benefits, and landscape heterogeneity. title: Emergency Response and Management of Pandemic Disasters and Their Environmental Dimensions: A Review of Lessons from COVID-19 in Bangladesh
abstract: Pandemics are disasters whose causes and consequences are both rooted in the environment, yet emergency management and environmental management are usually reviewed apart. This narrative review synthesizes 74 documents published between 2008 and 2026, comprising peer-reviewed studies, reports of intergovernmental and national agencies, and selected news and NGO records, to examine the emergency response to COVID-19 in Bangladesh, with the European Union as a comparator, and to connect that response to its environmental dimensions. title: Divergent demographic responses to the Kikai-Akahoya volcanic catastrophe in mid-Holocene Japan
abstract: We examine human demographic responses to one of the Holocene's largest volcanic eruptions, which devastated East Asia 7300 years ago. Archaeologists have intensively debated the impacts of massive environmental shocks, highlighting either societal collapse or cultural continuity, although few studies situate such catastrophic events within longer-term demographic trajectories. abstract: The commercial designation “cod” (鳕) is applied to multiple fish species, raising concerns regarding seafood authenticity and nutritional consistency. abstract: Biodiversity loss, habitat fragmentation and climate change are among the primary environmental pressures affecting species distributions. abstract: ABSTRACT The objective of this study is to investigate the structural response of above‐ground storage tanks (ASTs) subjected to flood‐borne debris impact, a critical yet understudied aspect of flood‐induced loading. abstract: Terrestrial multi-species predator feeding aggregations (MPFAs) are characterized by contest competition, but scramble competition is likely more common at MPFAs in pelagic waters. However, empirical investigations are rare. Aerial video was used to estimate abundances of striped marlin and mahi-mahi alongside their attack and capture rates and spatio-temporal positioning as they competed at prey schools. title: Ontogeny of rake mark scarring on common dolphins ( Delphinus delphis ): insights to aggression and affiliation?
abstract: Abstract Aggressive and affiliative interactions shape resource allocation, social structure and reproduction in social species. In delphinids, rake marks (parallel scars from tooth raking) indicate social interactions. When examined alongside ontogeny, demographic traits and scar position, rake marks can inform social dynamics. We assessed rake marks on common dolphins (Delphinus delphis) in Aotearoa New Zealand (2006–2024; n = 102) during post-mortem examinations to explore drivers of social behaviour. title: Taxonomic advancements in the Calotrichaceae: Resolving phylogenetic ambiguities and describing five novel species of Dulcicalothrix from the Konkan region of India
abstract: The taxonomy of heteropolar, tapering, and unbranched heterocytous cyanobacteria has undergone significant changes over time. Several novel species, genera, and families have been established using a polyphasic approach, which has provided a greater resolution in the systematics of these organisms. The Calotrichaceae, as of today, stands as a well-resolved and monophyletic clade with at least five genera. The family has had some major revisions as well as additions. In addition, parameters such as the comparison of the 16S-23S ITS rRNA regions for the separation of one species from another hav

title: Exploring Bacteria from Extreme Environments in Chilean Patagonia for Antitrypanosomal Metabolites
abstract: Abstract Extreme environments are recognized as valuable reservoirs of microbial diversity and chemical novelty. Adapted to harsh environmental conditions, bacteria isolated from extreme environments exhibit unique biosynthetic capabilities associated with the production of structurally diverse bioactive metabolites. Chagas disease (CD), caused by the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma cruzi, remains one of the most important neglected tropical diseases, affecting approximately eight million people worldwide. title: Variable response in riverine nitrogen exports to long-term temporal changes in watershed inputs
abstract: Aquatic nitrogen (N) pollution is a global problem, and understanding where best to implement mitigation strategies to reduce transfers from land to water is becoming increasingly urgent. Watershed nutrient budgets, using commonly available census data, can successfully predict riverine export spatially, albeit with variation related to fractional export. Furthermore, when using long-term data, watershed input-export trajectories vary and can be decoupled. title: Exploring the value of thematic urban ecosystem accounts in Western Balkan countries to inform urban greening actions
abstract: Urban ecological health is increasingly prioritised in Europe, as reflected in the EU Biodiversity Strategy 2030, the Nature Restoration Regulation, and the amended Regulation on Environmental-Economic Accounts. Translating these commitments into effective greening policy and planning actions that halt and reverse urban ecological degradation requires standardised, spatially explicit indicators. title: Towards an understanding of socio-environmental conflicts over natural commons in the Venice Lagoon (Italy)
abstract: Abstract Socio-environmental conflicts over natural commons represent a growing challenge for sustainability governance, yet their dynamics remain poorly understood within complex Social-Ecological Systems (SESs). This study examines six emblematic conflicts in the Venice Lagoon (Italy), a complex SES undergoing profound transformations driven by land-use change and the privatisation of natural commons. title: Spatial prioritization of habitats and conceptual framework for impact assessment and mitigation planning for protected wetlands
abstract: Reconciling development and biodiversity conservation remains a critical challenge in contemporary conservation planning. Our study is based on a case study for the assessment of the Harike wetland, a Ramsar site and a Protected Area, a human-made reservoir, for understanding the impacts of proposed desilting operations and mitigation planning. A multi-taxa biodiversity assessment was undertaken to generate baseline ecological information for spatial prioritization, mitigation, and monitoring. title: Warming effects on population sizes and top–down control are dependent on temperature range
abstract: Rising global temperatures are expected to affect natural ecosystems, but predicting the consequences is challenging given the complexity of ecological communities. Natural communities are complex networks of interacting species, and temperature changes can thus influence species directly and indirectly via changes in their various interactions with other community members within and across trophic levels. While previous studies indicate both predation and competition can be temperature specific, we still have a poor understanding of how both interact along a thermal gradient. Additionally, te

title: Effects of Mineralogical Inhomogeneity on Aggregate Dust Optical Properties and Lidar Observables
abstract: Abstract Dust aerosols comprise irregular grains and aggregates with various mineralogical mixtures. However, most optical models use effective refractive indices to represent particles. This study develops an inhomogeneous aggregate model assigning mineral‐dependent refractive indices to constituent elements and representing global mineral volume fractions. title: Effect of thawing methods on color stability and underlying biochemical mechanisms in different regions of tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ) fillets
abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Thawing affects fillet color, determining consumer acceptance and market value of aquatic products. This study evaluated the effects of thawing methods [water thawing (WT, 25 °C), air thawing (AT, 25 °C) and chilled air thawing (CAT, 4 °C)] on color stability and biochemical mechanisms across muscle regions [dorsal muscle (DM), belly muscle (BM) and tail muscle™] of tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ) fillets. title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Olive Fruit Fly (Bactrocera oleae) Populations in a Mediterranean Olive‐Growing Landscape: An Eight‐Year Study From Samos Island, Greece
abstract: ABSTRACT Olive fruit fly ( Bactrocera oleae , Rossi) is one of the most significant pests in the Mediterranean olive groves, causing both quantitative and qualitative losses. Understanding its spatial and temporal dynamics is essential for effective and sustainable control of the pest. This study analyses an eight‐year dataset (2017–2024) of the olive fly populations on Samos Island, Greece, based on an extensive monitoring network of McPhail traps. title: Ice Converts Phenols into Persistent Mineral-Bound Polymers
abstract: Freezing fundamentally alters how minerals transform dissolved phenols in cold environments. As water freezes, solutes are excluded from the crystal lattice and concentrated into microscopic pockets of unfrozen liquid, creating reaction conditions far more extreme than those of bulk solution. Here, we compare catechol oxidation on a key soil manganese oxide under freeze-thaw versus room-temperature conditions. title: Determining the preferred structure for aging smalleye Pacific opah in the Eastern North Pacific
abstract: Estimating age and growth is fundamental to understanding fish life history and fishery productivity, supporting both single-species and ecosystem-based management (Campana 2001; Kerns and Lombardi-Carlson 2017). Age can be estimated through length-frequency analysis or growth observations from fish of known age (Phelps et al. 2017) but is most commonly determined by counting growth increments in calcified structures, including otoliths, vertebrae, and fin spines or rays (Casselman 1983; Phelps et al. 2017). title: Temporal and spatial analysis of precipitation to the identification of extreme climate events in Pará state estimated by CHIRPS
abstract: In recent decades, extreme climate events have been recurrent in the Amazon, causing both intense droughts and prolonged rainy periods, impacting the population and economic sectors. Therefore, this study aims to analyze the spatial and temporal variation of precipitation using CHIRPS data in Pará state from 2001 to 2024.Precipitation data were obtained from CHIRPS and analyzed to identify spatial and temporal patterns. The study examined regional precipitation variability, comparing areas with higher and lower rainfall volumes. Monitoring climatic variables in Pará and the Amazon region is cr

title: Tribal nations’ flood exposure and the U.S. national flood insurance program
abstract: Tribal nations experience significant flood impacts, yet participation in the National Flood Insurance Program remains limited. We analyze flood events, claims, and 57 Tribal Hazard Mitigation Plans, and insights from a tribal representative, to identify disparities in insured recovery. We show administrative, financial, and capacity constraints hinder mitigation progress. Strengthening equitable access to flood insurance, mapping, and federal mitigation resources could play an important role in improving tribal flood resilience.

title: Occurrence and hydrolytic stability of emerging tire wear contaminants in environmental waters and soils: A case study from northern Poland
abstract: Background Tire wear particles release additives and transformation products into the environment. Among these, p -phenylenediamines (PPDs) and their quinone transformation products (PPD-Qs), including 6PPD-Q, have attracted increasing attention. However, data on tire wear contaminants (TWCs) in Central and Eastern Europe remain limited, and their hydrolytic stability is poorly characterized. This study investigated the hydrolytic stability of 16 TWCs, optimized sample pre-treatment, and assessed their occurrence and preliminary ecological risks in water and soil samples from northern Poland.

title: Conventional diversity metrics underestimate gut microbiome disruption under florfenicol exposure in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
abstract: Abstract The gut microbiome is an integral component of fish health and growth performance and therefore represents an important production factor in aquaculture. Antibiotics are a major stressor, not only by disturbing microbial diversity, but also by altering microbial interactions involved in digestion, colonization resistance and functional redundancy. Current risk assessments, however, rely largely on diversity-based evaluations and rarely consider changes in network topology. title: Transportation facility assessment for bat use in Contra Costa County
abstract: Transportation facilities such as bridges provide critical roosting habitat for bat species throughout California.This assessment analyzed 607 transportation facilities in Contra Costa County from the Federal Highway Administration's National Bridge Inventory dataset.The primary objective was to analyze the structural design elements of transportation facilities with confirmed bat use in Contra Costa County.The assessment prioritized facilities for field surveys using existing spatial datasets of predicted suitable habitat for bat species known to utilize bridges in Contra Costa County.The ass

title: Indigenous Planning: Utilising Kupuna Lensing for Pacific Disaster Risk Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines Indigenous planning as a vital epistemological and practical framework for disaster risk reduction in the Pacific, centering Hawaiian knowledge systems. Through case studies of the 2018 Kīlauea eruption and the 2023 Lahaina wildfire, this paper demonstrates how ʻike Hawaiʻi—utilising kupuna lensing (Hawaiian analytic research method), moʻolelo (stories) and Hawaiian naming practices—offers culturally grounded approaches to reducing risks from disasters. title: Nothing new to see here?! A critical (visual) discourse analysis of climate (im)mobility in IOM documents
abstract: This paper revisits critical climate mobility literature that explores the role of images and visual materials within policy briefs and papers, published about a decade ago, to contrast those findings with present-day policy documents. Based on a discourse analysis of 10 recent IOM reports and policy briefs, we show that the written discourse has changed within the documents from a language of migration/displacement/refuge to one that is akin to climate (im)mobilities discourses. title: Magma Supply Dynamics at Mt. Etna (Italy) Inferred from Peripheral Soil CO2 Emissions: Insights into the 2018 Flank Eruption and the 2021 Paroxysmal Activity
abstract: Open-conduit volcanoes are characterized by continuous magma supply and persistent degassing, whereas eruptive activity occurs intermittently and is controlled by magma transfer and accumulation processes within the feeding system. At Mt. Etna, temporal variations in peripheral soil CO2 emissions provide a sensitive tracer of deep magma intrusions and can be used to quantify magma inputs into the feeding system. title: The complete mitochondrial genome of Neoporphyra hollenbergii (E. Y. Dawson) L.-E. Yang & J. Brodie, an endemic species from the Gulf of California, Mexico
abstract: Neoporphyra hollenbergii is an endemic red alga from the Gulf of California, a region with notable cryptic diversity. We report its first complete mitochondrial genome and the first Bangiales mitogenome from the region. The circular mitogenome measures 31,565 bp (30.6% GC) and contains 50 genes, including 22 protein-coding genes, two rRNA genes, 24 tRNA genes, tatC, and orf813. The cox1 and rnl genes contain introns, reflecting red algal mitogenome complexity, while gene organization is conserved across Neoporphyra. title: Introducing a new normalized cryospheric index (NCI) to categorize sub-watersheds on arid environments
abstract: Abstract. This study examines sub-watersheds in the arid northern region of Chile (26°41’–28°24’S), situated within the broader Copiapo watershed. The primary water source for this watershed originates from cryospheric reservoirs. The region exhibits pronounced physiographic and climatic diversity, with its northern sector situated within the South American Arid Diagonal (SAAD), where cryospheric features exhibit greater spatial isolation. title: The Reflection of Conceptual Debates in Ottoman Naval History on High School Curriculum and Teacher Education: A Pedagogical Analysis
abstract: This study aims to examine the conceptual debates in academic Ottoman maritime historiography and their instructional reflections in the 2025 secondary school (10th and 11th grade) History textbooks approved by the Ministry of National Education, alongside History Education undergraduate curricula. title: Dynamic Nature of Soil Iron Minerals: Recent Advances Using Iron Isotope Tracers and Mossbauer Spectroscopy
abstract: Abstract Iron plays a central role in defining the redox and surface chemical environment of soils and sediments, by mediating the behavior of nutrients, pollutants, and carbon compounds. However, the mechanisms that drive dynamic changes in Fe speciation and mineral composition can be difficult to trace. Over three decades, technical advances in spectroscopy and theoretical modeling techniques have revealed detailed mechanisms of Fe mineral recrystallization and transformation. title: Europium Oxide Disrupts Metabolic Homeostasis and Antioxidant Defenses in African Catfish ( Clarias gariepinus ): Integrated Physiological and Molecular Docking Approaches
abstract: ABSTRACT Chemical pollution from rare earth elements (REEs) has emerged as a significant threat to the stability of freshwater ecosystems. Among these elements, europium oxide (Eu 2 O 3 ) is widely used across various industrial sectors; however, its specific impacts on fish physiology, health, and immune function remain poorly understood. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of Eu 2 O 3 on growth, hepatic markers, intestinal enzyme, systemic immune response, and cytokine expression in African catfish ( Clarias gariepinus ). title: Highlights from an early base camp in Beringia 13,800 years ago: Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ and the Late Pleistocene peopling of Alaska
abstract: Human dispersal across the Bering Land Bridge (BLB) was a key event in the peopling of the Americas, but Beringia's archaeological record remains poorly understood. In response, the Shég' Xdaltth'í' site in interior Alaska has been the focus of a multi-disciplinary study since 2016. The site contains three archaeological components dating to the Late Pleistocene, 13.8, 13, and 12.7 thousand years ago. title: Lipid Extract from Ulva ohnoi Algae: Chemical Characterization, Antibacterial Potential, and Cytotoxicity in the Search for New Agents Against MDR Infections
abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance is a critical global concern. This study investigated the lipid extract (LE) of Ulva ohnoi for its antimicrobial properties. The LE of U. ohnoi was characterized by GC-MS, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). title: A primary cell culture platform for studying venom gland and brain tissue in octopus
abstract: Coleoid cephalopods, squids, cuttlefish, and octopuses, have emerged as powerful model organisms for studying neurobiology, development, and behavior, however, cellular tools for investigating their specialized tissues remain limited. In particular, their venom producing gland, the posterior salivary gland (PSG), has been extensively described anatomically and histologically, yet remains largely inaccessible to experimental investigation at the cellular level. title: Gradual mitochondrial collapse underlies cytotoxicity induced by a B-type prymnesin-containing Prymnesium parvum extract in rainbow trout gill cells
abstract: Abstract Bioactive secondary metabolites produced by the haptophyte microalga Prymnesium parvum are key mediators of ichthyotoxicity during harmful algal bloom events. In the present study, we investigated the effects of a P. parvum extract containing B-type prymnesins, from an isolate obtained during the 2022 Oder River bloom, on mitochondrial health and cellular homeostasis in the rainbow trout gill epithelial cell line RTgill-W1, a widely used model in aquatic toxicology. title: Touring “Our USA”: Seeing US Empire in the Maps of Ruth Taylor White, 1920–1940
abstract: This article adds to histories of US empire, gender, race, and visual culture by more fully addressing white women’s role in sustaining colonial power through their production of an imperial visual culture between 1920 and 1940. It investigates the maps of a woman cartographer, Ruth Taylor White, across different geographical sites of US empire in the Pacific, Caribbean, and North American continent during a key moment in the history of US empire. title: Comparative Analysis of Nature-Inspired Strategies in Building Engineering: A Multilevel Biomimicry Perspective
abstract: This study investigates the integration of biological strategies into building systems and engineering through a multilevel biomimicry perspective. A systematic evaluation framework is established, categorizing biomimicry into two approaches (problem-oriented and solution-oriented), three levels (organism, behavior, and ecosystem), and five imitation dimensions: form, material, construction, process, and function. title: Non-Excessive Natural Resource Use and Sustainable Development: The Indigenous Environmental Wisdom of Lubuk Larangan
abstract: Sustainable development has guided global environmental governance for nearly four decades, yet continuing environmental degradation indicates persistent limitations in its implementation. This article examines whether clearer normative limits on natural resource use can strengthen sustainable development. It explores the Indonesian customary institution of Lubuk Larangan and identifies the principles of non-excessive utilization, sufficiency, and simplicity embedded in its Indigenous environmental wisdom. title: Analysis of urban heat islands in the study of urban environmental problems based on remote sensing
abstract: As global urbanization accelerates cities increasingly face ecological challenges, most notably the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect. This study investigates the formation and spatial distribution of UHI’s in the cities of Mingachevir, Shirvan and Yevlakh, located in the central region of the Republic of Azerbaijan. Utilizing ArcGIS, the analysis processed Landsat 8 OLI/TIRS satellite imagery from August 2023. title: Sustainable Freight Transportation via Inland Waterways: Challenges and Strategic Solutions in Bangladesh
abstract: Inland water transport (IWT) is crucial for socio-economic development, facilitating rural connectivity, trade logistics, energy provision and tourism. Nevertheless, it is neglected due to historical underinvestment, inadequate infrastructure and regulatory inefficiencies in Bangladesh. This study evaluates the current state of freight movement via inland waterways, identifies key challenges and proposes strategies to improve sustainability. A mixed-method approach was used, including content analysis of secondary data (sourced from “Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority” (BIWTA) reports

title: Bromide-mediated enhancement of far-UVC/peracetic acid process for selective micropollutant abatement
abstract: Abstract Far‑ultraviolet 222 nm (UV 222 ) effectively activates oxidants to degrade organic micropollutants (OMPs) in advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), but its synergy and ecotoxicity with bromide (Br − ) are unclear. title: Living Technology: Theoretical Perspectives on the Emergence of Sled Dogs
abstract: In recent years, the intersection of the history of technology, environmental history, and ethnozoology has generated new insights into human-animal relationships, particularly in Arctic contexts where survival has depended on close interspecies collaboration. Sled dogs, which have long played a central role in Arctic lifeways, exemplify how animals function as active participants in socio-ecological systems and can be understood as forms of biological technology. title: Comparison of Environmental Signals Between Contemporary and Subfossil Cladocera (Crustacea) Assemblages: A Case Study of Shallow Urban Ponds
abstract: ABSTRACT Cladocera are an important component of freshwater zooplankton and serve as proxies in paleoecological reconstructions. However, the similarity of environmental signals reflected in the dominant species structure of contemporary (CC) and subfossil (SC) cladoceran communities remains an open question. The objective of this study is to assess how changes in the dominant species structure of SC correlate with those in CC and with corresponding environmental conditions in artificial ponds. title: Mass movements in the southern Black Forest, Germany
abstract: Despite their importance as geomorphological processes and natural hazards, systematic inventories of mass movements remain limited for many Central European mid-mountain ranges. This study presents an inventory map of mass movements in the southern Black Forest (Germany), on the area of the Late Pleistocene Feldberg glaciation. High-resolution digital elevation models combined with field surveys were used to map and classify mass movements. Potential preconditioning factors (aspect, slope angle, lithology) were analysed. title: Peningkatan Literasi Data Perikanan Mahasiswa Magang Mandiri melalui Visualisasi Produksi Ikan Tenggiri Lamongan
abstract: Literasi data perikanan merupakan kompetensi penting bagi mahasiswa untuk mengolah, memvisualisasikan, menginterpretasikan, dan mengomunikasikan data secara tepat. title: Isolation, identification and immuno-pathogenesis of snakehead rhabdovirus-Indian strain (SHRV-In) in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
abstract: Snakehead rhabdovirus (SHRV-In) is the most potentially destructive pathogen of snakehead, capable of causing up to 100% mortality within five days. The present study aimed to screen freshwater fishes in Tamil Nadu for the occurrence of SHRV-In and to assess its immuno-pathogenesis potential in Nile tilapia. title: Influence of root morphology and salinity on PFAS uptake by ten Australian wetland plant species
abstract: Constructed Floating Wetlands (CFWs) show promise as nature-based technology for attenuating per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in surface water. However, few studies have investigated plant morphological and physiological characteristics that promote PFAS uptake. This study assessed ten wetland plant species exposed to PFAS-spiked stormwater (PFBS, PFPeA, PFHxS, PFOA, PFOS, 30 µg/L each), for 28 days, under two salinity conditions (200 and 1000 mg/L). title: Facile Enhancement of Corrosion, Wear and UV Aging Resistance of Epoxy Composite Coatings via Graphene Oxide Incorporation
abstract: UV aging, corrosion and wear resistance of epoxy (EP) coatings are all critical for their long-term service in outdoor environments. In this work, graphene oxide (GO) was used as a multifunctional additive in epoxy coatings to improve these properties. title: Surascape networks: from biocultural landscapes to uneven market integration in Thailand
abstract: Community liquor production in Thailand is rooted in biocultural landscapes, yet its relationship with urban and tourism markets is spatially uneven. Research explains place-based production and alcohol consumption geographies separately, but rarely connects origin landscapes with consumption networks. This study asks how community liquor production nodes are spatially connected to consumption nodes and what these connections reveal about market integration. title: First evidence of a mandibular crest in Brasileodactylus Kellner, 1984 (Pterosauria, Pteranodontoidea, Anhangueridae), with comments on pterosaur headcrests
abstract: Brasileodactylus araripensis Kellner, 1984, is a toothed pterosaur from the Lower Cretaceous Romualdo Formation of the Araripe Basin, Brazil. Traditionally regarded as crestless, the species has been central to debates on anhanguerid taxonomy, as most members of the clade possess well-developed sagittal cranial or dentary crests. Here we describe a nearly complete lower jaw (MCT.R.1473) that reveals, for the first time, the presence of a sagittal dentary crest in Brasileodactylus araripensis. title: Comparative population genomics reveal stark differences in the genomic structure and drivers of isolation for two sky island bumble bees
abstract: Genetic diversity is critical for species' persistence and for preserving biodiversity. Regions with extreme elevation gradients, including 'sky island' systems, are predicted to restrict gene flow owing to dispersal barriers between high-elevation habitat patches (isolation by resistance, IBR) and the sheer distances between patches (isolation by distance, IBD). abstract: ABSTRACT In this work, two different grades of poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) commonly used in offshore applications, one with 3% of dibutyl sebacate (DBS) plasticizer and the other a copolymer containing chlorotrifluoroethylene (CTFE), were subjected to an aging process in contact with a fluid containing hydrocarbons, pyridine, and aniline at high temperature for 90 days. title: Cation Interactions Governing the Nutritional Status of Serpentine Soils under Red Pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) Cultivation
abstract: Serpentine-derived soils are characterized by limiting conditions for plant growth. The combined effects of the physical, chemical, and biological properties of these soils create a stress condition known as the ‘serpentine syndrome’. This study aimed to investigate calcium (Ca), magnesium (Mg), and potassium (K) nutrition in red pepper cultivation on serpentine soils, and to evaluate the relationships among key cation ratios.
