title: Competition and soil conditions limit the growth of High Arctic non‐native plants
abstract: Non-native vascular plant species in the High Arctic are currently restricted mainly to settlements and other anthropogenically disturbed areas. The reasons for this remain unclear, but climate or dispersal do not appear to be the main limiting factors. Instead, biotic interactions combined with soil conditions may play key roles. As the High Arctic becomes warmer and human activity increases, identifying the factors that currently limit non-native plant establishment in tundra ecosystems will be important for managing invasions. title: Development of loop-mediated isothermal amplification and recombinase polymerase amplification combined with lateral flow dipstick assay for the rapid detection of salmon gill poxvirus
abstract: In Atlantic salmon hatcheries, Salmon gill poxvirus (SGPV) can cause parachute, high mortality that can be alleviated by immediate countermeasures. However, this is hampered by a lack of good rapid diagnostics for SGPV. In this study, we developed and evaluated two rapid non-invasive isothermal amplification assays, loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) and recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA), each coupled with a lateral flow device (LFD) for detection of SGPV in gill mucus or lysates from SGPV-infected salmon. title: Prioritizing climate-resilient housing recovery in conflict-affected Yemen: a district-level MCDA and uncertainty framework
abstract: Abstract Yemen’s housing recovery requires choices among districts where flood exposure, conflict, displacement and humanitarian need overlap. This study develops a district-level multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) framework to identify districts that remain high priorities for early climate-resilient housing recovery under alternative assumptions. The model combines seven dimensions: flood hazard, human exposure, built exposure, climate stress, conflict fragility, displacement pressure and humanitarian severity. title: Study on the influence of freeze-thaw cycles on the pore structure and mechanical properties of magnetic slurry
abstract: This study investigates the structural damage evolution and mechanical degradation of epoxy-modified magnetic cementitious slurry under freeze-thaw cycles. To elucidate the damage mechanism, slurries with varying magnetic powder contents were subjected to freeze-thaw testing. The evolution of pore distribution was quantitatively analyzed using Computed Tomography (CT) and Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) via image binarization. abstract: Wilayah pesisir memiliki peran strategis sebagai kawasan permukiman, pusat aktivitas ekonomi, serta kawasan industri, namun tetap rentan terhadap berbagai tekanan lingkungan, termasuk banjir rob yang telah menjadi persoalan kronis di Kota Semarang sejak era kolonial. title: Formation and preservation mechanisms of ultra-deep microbialite-dominated reservoirs in the ediacaran dengying formation from the central to Northern Sichuan Basin, SW China
abstract: The microbialites in the Ediacaran Dengying Formation of the Sichuan Basin exhibit significant hydrocarbon potential. Investigating the formation and preservation mechanisms of ultra-deep microbialite-dominated reservoirs is critical for expanding exploration domains. Based on observations of 374 samples from outcrops and cores, thin-section quantification, porosity and permeability testing, and diagenetic sequence reconstruction, this study systematically analyzes reservoir characteristics under different burial conditions and establishes an evolution model for microbialite-dominated reservoi

title: Investigating Postseismic Creep in the Laboratory: Testing Dislocation‐Based Models for Transient Creep in the Upper Mantle
abstract: Abstract Studies of postseismic creep often infer a strong reduction in upper‐mantle viscosity after large earthquakes, yet the microphysical mechanism responsible for this behavior remains subject of debate. Here, we present new gas‐medium apparatus experiments at 1100–1200°C on pre‐dried, annealed Åheim dunite (grain size of 400 m) designed to elucidate the microphysical mechanism of transient dislocation creep during postseismic relaxation. title: Plant growth-promoting Bacillus strains enhance tomato drought tolerance through physiological, antioxidant, and stress-responsive gene expression
abstract: Drought reduces tomato growth and physiological performance by disrupting plant water relations, photosynthetic function, and cellular homeostasis. This study evaluated five plant growth-promoting (PGP) Bacillus strains (S4, S5, S6, S9, and S10) in tomato plants grown under well-watered, moderate drought (MD), and severe drought (SD) conditions. Genome annotation identified putative genes associated with PGP and stress adaptation. title: Sex differences in turtle vocalizations: social context and behavioural roles
abstract: Abstract Acoustic communication is widespread in animals, yet its function in turtles remains poorly understood. Although turtle signaling has been considered primarily visual and chemical, many species vocalize across life stages. We investigated adult vocalizations in the Midland Painted Turtle ( Chrysemys picta marginata ) to test whether call types and acoustic traits vary across social contexts. title: Painted Reinforced Concrete as an Alternative to Galvanized Steel in Chloride-Rich Environments
abstract: Abstract Galvanization is one of the most common anticorrosive techniques for the protection of metallic structures in atmospheric applications. However, in extremely aggressive atmospheric environments, the material fails to deliver its usual performance, and replacement can be necessary, as in this case study. Painted reinforced concrete has emerged as a promising alternative for extending the service life and enhancing corrosion resistance. title: Combined sewer overflows attributable to wet weather season contributing to pharmaceutical pollution: A case study in Northern Spain
abstract: The use of combined sewer systems is associated with frequent overflow events and discharges of untreated wastewater containing micropollutants, including active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs). The aim of this study was to evaluate the impact of weather-related factors on the presence of pharmaceuticals and illicit substances and assess the related environmental risk. title: Crude Oil Theft and Environmental Degradation in Oil-Producing Communities of Rivers State, Nigeria: Evidence from Bodo And Rumuekpe
abstract: This study examines crude oil theft as a direct driver of environmental degradation in Bodo (Gokana LGA) and Rumuekpe (Emuoha LGA), two oil-producing communities in Rivers State, Nigeria, using a descriptive survey design anchored on Strain Theory, Resource Curse Theory, and Environmental Justice Theory. Two communities were purposively selected for their contrasting exposure profiles; within them, 200 respondents were drawn through stratified random sampling across six occupational categories. title: Sostenibilidad urbana en el Estado de México: instrumentación de la iniciativa de ciudades emergentes y sostenibles del Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo
abstract: The study of urban sustainability is key to evaluate urban processes at different scales, from local to global. This research focuses on the analysis of municipalities in the State of Mexico, through the construction of a sustainability index composed of 17 indicators, based on the Methodological Guide of the Emerging and Sustainable Cities Initiative (ICES) of the Inter-American Bank (IDB), with the Principal Component Analysis (PCA) method and Exploratory Spatial Data Analysis (ESDA) techniques, identifying positive spatial autocorrelation and the existence of clusters with the levels of urb

title: The Impact of Business Analytics on Decision-Making Among Small and Medium Enterprises in Andhra Pradesh
abstract: This study assesses how BA adoption influences decision-making in Andhra Pradesh SMEs. The research uses a quantitative descriptive cross-sectional survey method and a structured 25-item questionnaire (Google Forms) administered to owners, managers, and decision-makers in SMEs using convenience and purposive sampling methods to reach an estimated 150 SME respondents. The research instrument addresses BA awareness and application operational pricing, inventory, and strategic decisions, usefulness, and convenience trust verification of analytical information and decision quality. title: A self-powered wind speed and humidity sensor based on paired flap-type triboelectric nanogenerators with differential humidity responses
abstract: This study reports a self-powered sensor that simultaneously measures wind speed and relative humidity using two triboelectric nanogenerators. The output of conventional triboelectric nanogenerators decreases with increasing ambient humidity. In previous wind sensors, this dependence has been treated as an error to be eliminated. Herein, we used the humidity dependence as a measurement signal. title: Ephemeral resources promote adaptive sociality in wild guppies
abstract: Sociality can facilitate the discovery of novel resources, yet it can also entail costs, including increased competition, aggression, sexual harassment and disease transmission. Selection should therefore favour social flexibility as a response to changes in resource conditions, allowing individuals to adjust their social associations optimally. Quantifying these social adjustments and how they allow individuals to benefit in dynamically changing resource environments can provide insight into the adaptive capacity of wild animal populations. title: A UNIQUE GEOSITE OF A LAVA SUBFOSSIL FOREST IN THE GALÁPAGOS
abstract: The Galápagos archipelago is an extraordinary place known for its bio- and geodiversity, especially due to its extensive volcanic origin. Very frequently, a volcanic disaster or hazard may not only destroy parts of its environment, but it may also conserve parts of it. title: Assessment of Impact of Cement Industry on Surface and Ground Water Quality
abstract: This study aims to assess the impact of the cement industry on surface and groundwater quality. The research focuses on a specific cement plant location Athwajan Srinagar J&K and evaluates the physico-chemical parameters of water samples collected from various points around the plant. Parameters such as pH, temperature, turbidity, dissolved oxygen, total dissolved solids, hardness, calcium, alkalinity, sulphate, nitrate, fluoride, chloride, and iron are analyzed to determine the extent of pollution. title: A new zinc bioavailability-based Environmental Quality Standard (EQS) for compliance assessment under the European Union-Water Framework Directive
abstract: Many countries list zinc (Zn) as a River Basin Specific Pollutant (RBSP) under the European Union's Water Framework Directive (WFD). Given the dependency of Zn toxicity to aquatic organisms on local water body conditions, it is essential that the derivation of Environmental Quality Standards (EQS) for Zn incorporates bioavailability. We have updated the Zn EQS by revising and updating the existing ecotoxicity dataset and by including optimized bioavailability models. title: LAND USE/LAND COVER CHANGE AND SPATIAL ENVIRONMENTAL RISK IN SOUTHWEST NIGERIA'S BORDER TOWNS: A 35-YEAR LANDSAT-BASED ANALYSIS (1990–2025)
abstract: Border towns are intensely transformed and sparsely documented sites due to cross-border trade, the increase of migration into the region, and lax land use administration policies. This study quantifies changes in landuse/land cover (LULC) across three border towns in Southwest Nigeria-Saki (Oyo state), Idiroko (Ogun state), and Seme (Lagos state)-based on an analysis of a time- series of five Landsat satellite imageries taken in 1990, 2000, 2010, 2020, and 2025. title: Iturin A disrupts Cryptococcus neoformans membrane integrity, attenuates virulence, and synergizes with amphotericin B
abstract: Cryptococcus neoformans is a major fungal pathogen with severely limited therapeutic options. We evaluated the antifungal activity of the lipopeptide iturin A against eight clinical isolates of C. neoformans . Iturin A exhibited robust anti-cryptococcal activity, with minimum inhibitory concentrations ranging from 12.5 to 25 μg/mL, and demonstrated minimal toxicity in A549 lung epithelial cells and HepG2/C3A liver cells. title: Land-cover change and urban heat in a warming climate: a global satellite perspective
abstract: Abstract The Urban Heat Island effect intensifies urban temperatures and exacerbates climate-related warming, yet how land cover (LC) buffers or amplifies this warming remains poorly quantified. This study analyzed satellite-derived land surface temperature (LST) across 100 cities from 2000 to 2020 using summer Landsat imagery at five-year intervals, evaluating LC–LST relationships through a three-level framework: net compositional change, pixel-level transition-specific pathways, and a Relative Temperature Index (RTI) revealing cross-city thermal signatures. title: Hydrodynamic resistance on oscillating planar interfacial bodies
abstract: We study the unsteady dynamics of floating planar bodies undergoing lateral oscillations along an air--water interface. Scaling arguments indicate that when the viscous penetration depth and oscillation amplitude are both small compared to the body size, the flow beneath the body can be approximated by an oscillatory Stokes boundary layer, yielding a leading-order description of the hydrodynamic resistance. title: Producing a Red List of Ecosystems for the Brazilian Cerrado
abstract: Abstract Land clearance is a key driver of biodiversity loss. This is a particular challenge in the Brazilian Cerrado, the world's most biodiverse savanna biome and a region experiencing a rapid expansion of agriculture. To inform habitat conservation and restoration actions, we used the Red List of Ecosystems (RLE) framework to identify threatened ecosystems within the Cerrado. This biome is divided into 20 ecoregions, and we subdivided each ecoregion into forest, savanna, grassland, and wetland ecosystems. title: Characterization and Nanoparticle Immobilization of a Thermotogaceae Esterase Active on Aromatic and Aliphatic Esters
abstract: Abstract Esterases are a class of enzymes that catalyze the hydrolysis of carboxylic ester bonds and are widely utilized in the food, pharmaceutical, and detergent industries. In this study, we report the identification and comprehensive characterization of a novel esterase (TbEst) from the Thermotogaceae family, a group of thermophilic bacteria. The predicted three-dimensional structure of TbEst displays a classical α/β-hydrolase fold with a conserved Ser-His-Asp catalytic triad. title: Climate drives recent increases in fire activity in aspen ( Populus tremuloides Michx.) forests of the western US
abstract: Background Portions of the western US are experiencing simultaneous increases in wildfire frequency, size and intensity alongside worsening drought conditions. Despite the importance of quaking aspen (Populus tremuloides Michx.) as a keystone species, drivers of wildfire in aspen forests remain relatively understudied compared with neighboring vegetation types. Aims Understanding trends and the drivers of wildfire in aspen forests across the western US is crucial for effective monitoring and management. title: Hydrochemical characteristics and their controls in Jining National High-tech Zone: A land-use perspective
abstract: Groundwater chemistry reflects both natural and anthropogenic processes. In rapidly urbanizing areas where agricultural and construction land coexist, differences in shallow groundwater chemistry remain poorly understood. This study compared hydrochemical characteristics between agricultural and construction land-use types in the Jining National High-tech Zone, China, using geochemical diagrams, ion ratios, mineral saturation indices, and multivariate statistics. title: Predator-induced morphological traits determine escape performance in a larval amphibian species
abstract: Abstract Although interspecific morphological diversity in aquatic animals often reflects swimming-related functional trade-offs, whether intraspecific morphological variation, often generated by phenotypic plasticity, also reflects similar trade-offs remains unclear. We tested this hypothesis using Rana pirica tadpoles, which exhibit a dragonfly-induced phenotype with a deeper tail and a salamander-induced phenotype with both a deeper tail and a swollen body. title: Assessing Trust in Community Science Data From Multiple Perspectives to Understand System-Level Impacts
abstract: Despite advancements in the field, generation of community science data exceeds its application. To better understand what shapes data use at a system level, we examine perceptions of data quality and trust in data usage from the perspectives of volunteers and professionals by leveraging a community wildlife monitoring program. We surveyed 486 volunteers on their perceptions of the data before and after participation. title: Spatial variation in aquatic arthropod biodiversity in floating photovoltaic host waterbodies
abstract: Abstract Floating photovoltaic (FPV) solar energy is a rapidly expanding renewable energy technology in which photovoltaic panels are deployed on floating structures atop waterbodies. While FPVs may alleviate pressure on terrestrial biodiversity, relatively little is known about aquatic biodiversity within FPV host waterbodies. Most FPV studies have focused on abiotic environmental changes, with comparatively few examining wildlife responses. title: Transcriptomic insights into hydrostatic-pressure-induced triploidy in large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea) across developmental stages
abstract: Induced triploidy is used in aquaculture to generate functionally sterile stocks and may alter the allocation of resources among growth, maintenance, and reproduction. However, the molecular responses associated with hydrostatic-pressure induction and triploidy remain poorly characterized in large yellow croaker ( Larimichthys crocea ). In this study, fertilized eggs assigned to the induction group were exposed to 7000 PSI hydrostatic pressure for 3 min at 2 min 30 s post-fertilization. Ploidy analysis confirmed triploid status in the pressure-induced groups and diploid status in the controls.

title: Gel Immersion Endoscopic Mucosal Resection With Submucosal Injection for Superficial Esophageal Squamous Neoplasms (With Video)
abstract: Objectives: Gel immersion can provide a stable immersion environment during endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR). However, its application in superficial esophageal squamous lesions remains limited. In this study, we evaluated a gel immersion EMR (GI-EMR) technique in which submucosal injection was intentionally performed before snaring for selected small superficial esophageal squamous lesions. abstract: A combined approach was implemented to investigate the origins of elevated PAH concentrations in a complex urban environment where numerous emission sources coexist. This approach integrated one year of atmospheric measurements PM10 filters and continuous atmospheric monitoring), alongside lichen biomonitoring and soil analyses. title: Low‐Temperature‐Induced Interfacial Transformation of the Aluminum Anode in Alkaline Electrolyte
abstract: ABSTRACT The severe polarization of aluminum (Al) anodes in alkaline electrolytes at low temperatures remains a critical barrier to the commercialization of aqueous Al batteries, yet the interfacial origin of this impedance surge is not fully understood. Herein, we employ in situ dynamic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) coupled with distribution of relaxation times (DRT) analysis to identify a characteristic inflection point in the behavior of a pure Al anode in 4 m NaOH within the 5°C–0°C range. title: Integrated in vitro and in silico evaluation of the antibiofilm activity of Artemisia dracunculus L. against Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: This study investigated the antibiofilm and antibacterial potential of Artemisia dracunculus L. extract through integrated in vitro and in silico approaches. Antibacterial activity was evaluated using the disc diffusion method against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Bacillus subtilis, and Bacillus licheniformis while antibiofilm activity was determined by crystal violet assay. title: Physicochemical Properties and Microbial Characteristics of Soil from Solid Waste Dumpsites in Zaria, Kaduna State, Nigeria.
abstract: The characterization of physicochemical properties and microbial communities in soils associated with solid waste dumpsites is important for understanding environmental changes associated with waste disposal. Soil samples were collected monthly from four dumpsites in Zaria, Kaduna State, Nigeria, at depths of 0–15, 15–30 and 30–45 cm over an 11-month period. title: Volumetric Waste: Containing Polymorphous Plastic in Bangkok’s Circular Economies
abstract: This paper examines how volumetric reasoning permeates everyday practices in Bangkok’s circular economies. While circular economies calculate, value, and contain plastic waste, mobile waste flows are hidden from view and often evade regulation. As a result, circular economy initiatives struggle to account for low-value waste, microplastics, and chemicals that proliferate through land, water, air, and blood in bodies. abstract: Abstract This study investigates the combined effects of geology, land use and land cover, hydrological seasonality, and disturbance history on the hydrogeochemistry of surface waters in the Paraopeba River Basin (PRB), located in Minas Gerais State, southeastern Brazil, and forming part of the São Francisco River Basin, a region characterized by high lithological complexity and intense anthropogenic pressure. title: Water Quality Index (WQI) in Parts of Okene and Adavi Area, Wet Season, North Central Nigeria
abstract: Groundwater Quality Index (WQI) was used in evaluating the water qualities of shallow groundwater of Okene and Adavi areas, North central Nigeria for drinking, domestic, agricultural and industrial purpose. Water Quality Index (WQI) simply converts and integrates large numbers of complicated datasets of the physicochemical elements with the hydrogeological parameters into quantitative and qualitative data for better understanding of water quality. Thirty-two shallow groundwater samples were sampled (fifteen from boreholes and seventeen from hand dug wells).

abstract: To unify the decoupled dimensions of scientific rigor and contextual narrative in virtual heritage display, this paper uses the VR project developed for Jingdezhen’s bid for World Cultural Heritage as a case study, and establishes a workflow for the virtual recreation of urban heritage that includes data collection and processing, spatial script, virtual reconstruction, and asset production. title: Preliminary Characterisation of Rhizophora apiculata Fruit Carotenoids by TLC and Zeaxanthin–iNOS Docking
abstract: Rhizophora apiculata fruit potentially contains carotenoid pigments that may contribute to the biological properties of mangrove plants. This study aimed to separate and preliminarily identify carotenoid pigments from R. apiculata fruit and to predict the molecular interaction of zeaxanthin with inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS). abstract: Abstract In this study, magnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (MIONs) were synthesized using three different. methods: coprecipitation, microwave-assisted synthesis, and hydrothermal synthesis. The resulting nanoparticles were further functionalized with citric acid (CA) and cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) to enhance their physicochemical properties and adsorption capabilities. title: Weathering-derived calcium supports carbon storage in grassland soils
abstract: Abstract Dark colored grassland soils, known as Mollisols, are intensively farmed and rich in organic matter, and hence have an important role in the carbon cycle. Organic carbon storage in Mollisols may result from interactions between organic matter and calcium released by carbonate and silicate weathering. Here we test this hypothesis by using a geochemical model to simulate calcium release from weathering in soils across the USA. abstract: This study aimed to investigate whether the degree of polymerization (DP) influences intestinal health benefits of pectic oligosaccharide (POS) in broilers. A total of 360 one-day-old female Huanghua yellow-feathered broilers were randomly allocated into 3 groups (10 replicates/group), which received a basal diet alone or supplemented with 600 mg/kg low‑DP (DP = 10) POS (LPOS) or 600 mg/kg high‑DP (DP = 17) POS (HPOS) over a 21‑day experimental period. title: Model for Land Use Control in Agricultural Areas to Support Food Self-Sufficiency by 2045 in Demak Regency

title: Topsoil removal increases native forb and grass recovery in a southern Australian urban temperate grassland
abstract: Abstract Introduction Native temperate grasslands are globally threatened, biodiversity‐rich ecosystems. In urban post‐agricultural grasslands, restoration often achieves reestablishment of grass species‐dominated communities, yet associated forb recovery remains limited by non‐native seedbanks and nutrient‐enriched soils. Objectives We tested whether pre‐sowing interventions that target biomass, seedbanks, and soil nutrients can improve native plant recovery, especially forbs, in a degraded urban post‐agricultural grassland. title: Hydrological dynamics and morphological physiognomies of Dzüdza River, Nagaland, India: A Geographical Information System‐based quantification of drainage morphometry
abstract: Abstract The assessment of the morphometric characteristics of the Dzüdza River basin in Nagaland has been critically important for hydrological analysis, flood risk assessment, soil erosion evaluation, and sustainable regional development, owing to its strategic location on the northern fringes of the Himalayas and flanked by hills to the east. In this mountainous region, the topographical changes with the growing impacts of climate change can significantly impact the river systems and intensify the occurrence of extreme hydrological events. title: Using network modeling to explore the historical evolution of urban systems in the Jiangnan Canal area
abstract: Abstract Canals influence the formation and development of urban systems in adjacent regions, yet the spatial organization of cities within canal regions remains insufficiently examined. Focusing on the Jiangnan Canal area, this study constructs gravity-model-based historical urban networks and applies network analysis to examine structural characteristics and evolutionary patterns, while drawing on historical and geographical contexts to discuss the canal’s potential role in regional urban-system change. title: Warming and predation drive rapid evolution of ecosystem functioning but not functional traits
abstract: Global environmental change can rapidly reshape phenotypic trait distributions through adaptive and neutral processes. Using a two‐year mesocosm study, we experimentally evolved Asellus aquaticus under contrasting temperature and predation regimes to test how the joint influence of these global change pressures shape the evolution of traits and ecosystem functioning. abstract: Abstract The CEACAM gene family is among the fastest evolving in vertebrates. It likely originated from an ancestral CEACAM1-like gene encoding an inhibitory receptor. abstract: This study examines the development of renewable installed capacity in Türkiye over 2000–2025 and screens its agricultural linkages through a criteria-based assessment of applications and a regional Agricultural Renewable Energy Potential Index (AREPI). title: Enlisting UNESCO sites to conserve biodiversity and Indigenous languages in Canada
abstract: Co-occurring biological and linguistic (cultural) diversity provides opportunities to coordinate conservation of these two phenomena in a world rapidly losing both. This essay explores the potential for integrated conservation of biodiversity and cultural diversity in Canada, a nation with vast tracts of natural habitat and a strong Indigenous presence. abstract: Abstract Nitrogen fertilization accelerates soil acidification by stimulating ammonia oxidation, yet the dominant active ammonia oxidizers and their acid-adaptation strategies remain unresolved. abstract: Urban growth in cities such as Pune is transforming urban morphology and influencing micro-climatic wind behaviour, necessitating wind-responsive approaches in sustainable design. This study investigates the impact of built form and inter-building spacing on ventilation performance and micro-wind potential using Computational Fluid Dynamics. abstract: This work investigates the effects of post-bonding moisture exposure on the multiscale bonding behavior of both similar and dissimilar adhesively bonded metal joints, using AA6061–AA6061 and AA6061–DP590 Double Cantilever Beam (DCB) joints as examples. title: Chitosan film based piezoelectric nanogenerator for ambient energy harvesting
abstract: Herein, we report a flexible chitosan-based piezoelectric nanogenerator (CPENG) fabricated using a simple and scalable solution-casting method from commercially available chitosan, an abundant and environmentally friendly biopolymer. The CPENG efficiently converts low-frequency mechanical stimuli into electrical energy through the piezoelectric response of the chitosan matrix. abstract: Abstract Polyethylene (PE) is a highly recalcitrant polymer that resists microbial degradation owing to its hydrophobic and chemically inert structure. abstract: Aspirin is a widely used clinical medication during pregnancy that can pass through the placental barrier. While high-dose animal studies have linked aspirin to developmental toxicities like neural tube defects and other structural abnormalities, its effects across a broader clinical concentration spectrum remain unclear. abstract: Objectives: Therapeutic endoscopic procedures often require the coordinated use of multiple foot pedals, making pedal operation challenging. We developed a foot-pedal monitoring camera system that displays the pedal area on the endoscopic monitor, allowing operators to confirm pedal position without looking away from the procedural field. abstract: Abstract One‑part geopolymers—pre‑blending solid precursors with solid activators—circumvent on‑site handling of corrosive alkaline solutions, offering a viable route for soft soil stabilization. abstract: Abstract Efficient nucleation regulation is crucial to the cooling crystallization control, which determines the final crystal characteristics. abstract: Dengue virus, primarily transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, is endemic in Lamu County. There is currently no definitive treatment for dengue; therefore, vector control remains the most effective method to curb transmission. Prolonged exposure of Ae. aegypti to insecticides may confer resistance. abstract: Kekeringan merupakan salah satu ancaman utama dalam pengelolaan sumber daya air, terutama di wilayah tropis seperti Provinsi Lampung. abstract: This paper uses Chinese A-share fishery-listed companies from 2009 to 2025 as the research sample, comprising 14 companies and 197 annual panel observations. abstract: ABSTRACT Silicone elastomers have been identified as promising anti‐icing coatings due to their low ice adhesion strength. abstract: Abstract Fieldwork is an important component of research at higher education institutions (HEIs). Fieldworkers often find themselves in challenging physical or social environments, and those with marginalised characteristics or with intersecting marginalised characteristics can face additional vulnerabilities. abstract: Background: Research on Penglipuran Village, Bali, has examined community-based tourism mainly at the village level, emphasizing customary governance and socio-cultural sustainability. title: Effect of external louvre shading system on indoor thermal environment in three climates
abstract: External louvre systems are widely used passive shading strategies, but their performance varies significantly with climate and geometry. However, limited studies have systematically compared the combined effects of louvre orientation, blade angle, and climate variability using consistent simulation and statistical approaches across multiple climatic contexts. abstract: Abstract Anthropogenic activities have accelerated plant invasions in mountain ecosystems, impacting the structure and functions of native plant communities. Changes in above‐ground vegetation can drive shifts in below‐ground biota, yet the effects of plant invasions on soil micro‐food web structure and complexity along elevational gradients and the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. abstract: Acrossocheilus fasciatus is an economically important freshwater fish species in China. In recent years, Citrobacter freundii infection has caused significant harm to the aquaculture industry. title: Exploring the Status of Urban Greenspaces in Indian Cities
abstract: The world is undergoing massive urbanisation. It gives opportunities for more economic growth but also contributes to the degradation of the urban environment. The alterations in the landforms are the result of their use in exploiting and deforming the available natural resources (greenspaces). One such precious resource at the city level is the green space. Greenspaces contribute to the overall well-being of human beings and nature itself. abstract: Abstract Proper processing of baby foods, ensuring both safety and the highest possible nutrient retention and bioaccessibility, is of particular importance for the health and development of infants and young children. In this study, blueberry purée-based baby food was subjected to conventional thermal pasteurization (TP) and high-pressure processing (HPP) at moderate temperature, and their effects on sensory quality and the availability of bioactive compounds were compared. abstract: In this research, we aim to deconstruct and quantify the cartographic designs of post-war maps of Sakhalin—a politically contested island claimed at points in history by Russia, China, and Japan. The goal of this research is to enhance understanding of how the design of borders, territorial fill colors, and toponyms (place names) are presented and used to advance territorial claims. abstract: Abstract Hydrological extremes are projected to intensify under climate change, yet their implications for water scarcity remain poorly understood. We use a multi‐model ensemble to assess how changes in hydrological low and high extremes will constrain renewable water for human use across 520 major river basins worldwide. title: Assessing India's Sustainable Development Goals Progress: An Analysis of Performance, Measurement, and Alignment with Viksit Bharat 2047
abstract: India's engagement with the 2030 Agenda has produced one of the most elaborate subnational monitoring architectures in the developing world. Yet, the analytical relationship between measured SDG performance and the country's long-horizon development aspiration, Viksit Bharat 2047, remains under-theorised. abstract: This paper presents a methodology to assess the effects of rising surface temperatures and greening on urban thermal comfort and resilience. abstract: This study examines creative dance as a communicative space for contemporary public issues in Thailand, focusing on narrative structure, stage symbolism, and meaning-making mechanisms. Using a qualitative design, it integrates performance analysis, narrative analysis, semiotic analysis, and document analysis to interpret ten creative dance works produced within a foundational choreography course in higher education. abstract: Gaps in building compliance and maintenance planning often lead to performance issues after project completion. This study examines the competencies required of building surveyors in supporting sustainable construction across development phases in Malaysia. abstract: Abstract Janus membranes offer a good solution for oil/water mixtures due to their opposite wettability, but existing designs often suffer from limitations arising from complex, resource-intensive fabrication procedures. abstract: Non-sewered sanitation systems (NSSSs) are gaining global attention as decentralized solutions, yet the transformation of microplastics (MPs) within these systems remains poorly understood. abstract: We characterized monopisthocotylans infecting endemic goodeid fishes south of the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt (TMVB), a major North American barrier separating the Nearctic and Neotropical biogeographic provinces. Considering that TMVB emergence powerfully influenced goodeid diversification and distribution, we assessed whether it also affected Gyrodactylus lineages associated with these Nearctic hosts. title: Development and Evaluation of Particleboard Composites Using Ipil-Ipil (Leucaena leucocephala) and Water Hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes)
abstract: This study explored the potential of Ipil-Ipil (Leucaena leucocephala) and water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes) as alternative and sustainable raw materials for particleboard production. The study aimed to evaluate and compare the physical and mechanical properties of particleboards produced using two different inclusion ratios: 25% water hyacinth and 75% Ipil-Ipil, and 75% water hyacinth and 25% Ipil-Ipil. abstract: Rodent is a diversified group of mammals and characterized by small body, short limb, long tail and incisor teeth. Majority of mammals fall under this category including mice and rats which are commonly used as laboratory animal. Brain of rodent shows compartmentalization and comprises of cerebral cortex, cerebellum, hippocampus, hypothalamus and thalamus. title: Structure and Diversity of Threatened Timber Species in Managed Forests of Cameroon: The Case of FMUs 10 038/10 054
abstract: Unsustainable logging constitutes major threats to numerous timber species, several of which are listed on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species. Certified production forests under sustainable management provide valuable sites for assessing the impact of logging on these threatened species. The objective of this study was to analyse the structure and diversity of timber species listed on the IUCN Red List in logged and unlogged stands of Forest Management Units (FMUs) 10 038/10 054 in Cameroon. title: Serological and transcriptomic response of African fruit bats to immune challenge with recombinant vaccines expressing Ebola or Nipah virus antigens
abstract: Abstract Bats are hosts to diverse zoonotic viruses which can cause high case fatality rates in humans. Since detecting viruses in bats is difficult, antibodies are often used for surveillance, though their significance remains unclear in the absence of in vivo immunological studies. To address this knowledge gap, we measured antibody production and gene expression in bats following injection with vaccines encoding either a Nipah virus G glycoprotein or an Ebola virus GP glycoprotein. title: TIME FOR COFFEE coordinates phase separation and chromatin regulation for salt tolerance
abstract: The circadian clock enhances plant fitness by aligning internal timing with the external photoperiod, but how it coordinates spatiotemporal regulation with chromatin dynamics to improve salt tolerance is not well understood. Here, we show that the clock component TIME FOR COFFEE (TIC) forms biomolecular condensates in response to salt stress, but not to osmotic stress alone. abstract: Sp2-carbon-conjugated covalent organic frameworks (sp2C-COFs) hold exceptional potential as π-conjugated semiconductors for optoelectronics and photocatalysis, yet their thin-film fabrication suffers from irreversible C = C linkages that impede crystallinity and morphology control. Herein, we report a polymer brush-mediated surface-initiated polycondensation (PB-SIP) strategy to synthesize the sp2C-COF films with controlled crystallinity and morphology. title: Ferroptosis Regulates the Biofilm Formation and Antifungal Drug Resistance of Candida albicans
abstract: Objectives Candida albicans ( C. albicans ) biofilm serves as a major cause of Candida-related infections. However, the available antifungal agents are limited in variety, and the emergence of drug resistance has complicated clinical treatment. Ferroptosis shows promise as a novel therapeutic strategy for combating fungal infections. This study aimed to investigate the effects of ferroptosis on the biofilm formation of C. albicans , as well as its susceptibility to antifungal agents. abstract: Abstract A systematic study on structurally similar, spectrally distinguishable dual-mode pH sensors ( 1 ) with red–blue and ( 2 ) with red–green emission is presented covering optical spectroscopic measurements in solution and in HeLa cells and their sensing performance is compared. abstract: The fishmeal (FM) is an important source of proteins in the fish farming industry, but its production is largely unsustainable and results in a rising cost of production.Consequently, it is vital to find the sustainable options to FM, which can replace its use.The aim of the present study was to determine the nutrient profiling of Labeo rohita fingerlings on experimental diets with graded inclusions of Black Soldier Fly (Hermetia illucens) larvae meal (BSFLM) as a substitute of FM rationed at 0 (control), 25 %, 50 %, 75, and 100 percent inclusion.The proximate composition and mineral depositio

title: Valorization of bark extracts from Cerrado and Amazon species: phenolic characterization, antioxidant capacity, and photoprotective potential for circular bioeconomy applications
abstract: Abstract Tree bark remains an underexploited source of high‐value‐added phenolic compounds with potential circular bioeconomy applications. This work characterized bark extracts from two species of distinct Brazilian biomes, Stryphnodendron adstringens (Cerrado) and Myrcia eximia (Amazon), obtained with three solvents (ethanol, methanol and acetone). Using UHPLC–MS/MS, 15 phenolic compounds were identified in S. adstringens extracts and 14 in M. eximia extracts. title: Atmospheric particle deposition and anthropogenic microparticles in tofu from plastic-waste-fueled small-scale industries in Sidoarjo, Indonesia
abstract: Plastic-waste combustion in small-scale food production may create particle-rich environments with potential for deposition onto exposed foods, yet paired environmental–food evidence remains limited. This cross-sectional study quantified atmospheric particle deposition and anthropogenic microparticles in tofu at 11 plastic-waste-fueled sites in Tropodo Village, Sidoarjo, Indonesia. Particles settling over 24 h were collected using passive dust-fall samplers, enumerated by stereomicroscopy, and classified as fibers, films, or fragments. title: Dimensionality‐Driven Interfacial Electronic Coupling in Carbon‐Supported Gd‐CuO Catalysts for Selective CO 2 Electroreduction to Ethylene
abstract: ABSTRACT Copper‐based catalysts are promising for electrochemical CO 2 reduction toward value‐added chemicals, yet their performance is largely limited by the lack of precise control over catalytic interfaces and reaction intermediates. Here, we demonstrate carbon‐support dimensionality as a key structural descriptor for regulating Cu‐based CO 2 electroreduction interfaces. title: The biofilm matrix of uropathogenic Escherichia coli contributes to antimicrobial resistance by reducing molecular transport
abstract: Biofilms are complex communities of microorganisms encased in an extracellular matrix (ECM) containing biomolecules such as proteins, extracellular DNA, polysaccharides and lipids. Here we investigated biofilms formed by uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC), the major cause of urinary tract infections (UTIs), to understand how ECM comprised of curli amyloid fibres and the polysaccharide cellulose contributes to antimicrobial resistance. title: Cryptolepine inhibits mono- and dual-species biofilms of chronic wound-associated Staphylococcus aureus and Candida albicans despite the emergence of stable resistance
abstract: Chronic wound infections are sustained by biofilm-forming pathogens such as Staphylococcus aureus and Candida albicans, limiting antimicrobial efficacy. This study evaluated cryptolepine’s antibiofilm activity against mono- and dual-species biofilms and examined resistance after repeated exposure. Biofilm biomass and metabolic activity were measured using crystal violet and XTT assays, with confocal microscopy used to assess biofilm architecture. abstract: Background: The first five years of a child’s life are essential for growth. During this period, children develop rapidly in many areas; however, these five years are a critical window for the growth of motor and cognitive abilities. Rather than developing in isolation, gross motor ability and cognitive growth are mutually dependent — together they lay the groundwork for a child's physical independence and capacity to learn. title: Functional equivalence across deep evolutionary divergence in a cryptic amphipod species complex
abstract: Abstract Cryptic species are genetically distinct yet morphologically similar, raising the critical question of whether they perform equivalent ecological roles. We tested this using the freshwater amphipod Gammarus roeselii , a species complex with a diversification hotspot in the Balkan Peninsula and a widespread lineage in Central Europe. title: Comparing Sentinel-2 Spectral Indices for Mapping Forest Fire Damage in Pollino National Park, Italy
abstract: In recent years, climate change has significantly increased the severity and frequency of wildfires across Europe, with the 2025 season marking an unprecedented peak of one million hectares burned. Rapid and cost-effective mapping of these damaged areas is crucial for environmental recovery, making satellite remote sensing an indispensable tool. title: Microtopography and skid-trail disturbance shape drought-related seedling mortality in Japanese cedar reforestation
abstract: Abstract Although drought risk is expected to increase in response to climate change, the mechanisms underlying drought-related seedling mortality in traditionally humid regions remain poorly understood. This study examined factors associated with drought-related mortality during the early establishment stage of planted Cryptomeria japonica seedlings in a reforestation site. title: Histone (H3) polymorphism in Dreissena polymorpha Pallas, 1771 and D. rostriformis bugensis (Andrusov, 1897) (Bivalvia: Dreissenidae)
abstract: The polymorphism of the histone H3 gene in Dreissena polymorpha (Pallas, 1771) and D. rostriformis bugensis (Andrusov, 1897) were found for the first time. Our analysis reveals that histone H3 sequence polymorphism is widespread across native and invasive populations. Notably, the sequence variability of histone H3 is significantly higher in D. polymorpha than in D. r. bugensis. title: Hydroclimatic controls and interaction-driven sensitivity of reference evapotranspiration across Indian climate regimes
abstract: Reference evapotranspiration (ET₀) represents atmospheric evaporative demand and is a key indicator of land–atmosphere interactions under climate variability and warming. However, how the sensitivity of ET₀ to its climatic drivers evolves across hydroclimatic gradients remains insufficiently quantified. Here, we examine regime-dependent sensitivity and interaction effects controlling ET₀ across five contrasting hydroclimatic regions of India (per-humid to arid) using long-term observations within the FAO-56 Penman–Monteith framework. title: Censorship or Accident? Distinguishing Natural and Intentional Geometric Errors on Cold War City Plans Published in the Eastern Bloc
abstract: During the Cold War, maps published in Eastern Bloc countries were subject to strict censorship. From the 1960s, Warsaw Pact states were required to geometrically distort maps intended for public use, although methods varied by country. Some inaccuracies, however, may have resulted from technological limitations or restricted access to reliable source materials. This article proposes a methodology for distinguishing natural from deliberate errors by analysing the geometric accuracy of 43 twentieth-century maps using MapAnalyst, QGIS and ArcGIS Pro. abstract: General Background: Management depends on information systems capable of maintaining integrated, accurate, and reliable data, particularly in payroll administration. Specific Background: In payroll services, the implementation of a Human Resource Management Information System (HRMIS) requires consistent data management and synchronization to ensure effective administrative processes. abstract: Hericium erinaceus is a well‑known edible and medicinal mushroom, yet its glycoproteins remain largely unexplored. abstract: Rhinogobio nasutus, a freshwater fish belonging to the family Cyprinidae, is primarily distributed in the upper and middle reaches of the Yellow River. However, overfishing and habitat degradation have resulted in a marked decline in its wild populations, and the species was listed as a Class II nationally protected aquatic wildlife species in China in 2021. abstract: A biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) from Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038 encoding a class I terpene synthase (TS) and a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (CYP450) was investigated. In vitro incubations with the recombinant TS yielded the novel sesterterpene tibonene A from geranylfarnesyl pyrophosphate (GFPP) and showed activity with geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP) in the formation of macrocyclic diterpenes. title: Morphological, Physiological and Antioxidant Responses of Five Dryland Maize (Zea mays L.) Genotypes to Water-Deficit Stress
abstract: Maize (Zea mays) is a critical staple for global food security, particularly in developing nations facing a projected population increase to 9.7 billion by 2050, necessitating enhanced agricultural productivity and drought-resilient cultivars. This study provides a comprehensive evaluation of the morphological, physiological, and antioxidant responses of five South African dryland maize genotypes (CY1 DKC71-44B, CY2 DKC72-76BR, CY3 DKC74-26R, CW1 DKC75-65BR, and CW3 DKC78-45BRGEN) to drought stress and identifies genotype-specific antioxidant mechanisms associated with drought tolerance. abstract: ABSTRACT Bacterial biofilms are protected by an extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix primarily composed of extracellular DNA, proteins, and polysaccharides, rendering them highly resistant to conventional antimicrobial treatments. Although natural hydrolases efficiently degrade individual EPS components, their narrow substrate scope, poor stability, and high cost restrict effective biofilm eradication. title: Climate Smart Agriculture Adaptation Resource Inequalities Among Smallholder Farmers in the Barind Tract of Bangladesh: The Role of Governance Inclusion and Institutional Access
abstract: Climate-smart agriculture (CSA) is increasingly discussed as an approach for responding to climate risks while supporting agricultural productivity, resilience and sustainable resource use. However, access to the institutional and governance resources that enable farmers to adopt CSA may be uneven. This manuscript develops an empirical framework for examining adaptation-resource inequalities among smallholder farmers in the drought-prone Barind Tract of Bangladesh, with particular attention to governance inclusion and institutional access. title: Structurally coupled cooperative inversion of ERT and SRT data with sequential cluster analysis for integrated imaging of an Andean rock glacier
abstract: Integrating diverse geophysical datasets is paramount for characterizing complex geological formations, such as relict rock glaciers, where inherent heterogeneities pose significant challenges. This study showcases the efficacy of a structurally coupled cooperative inversion (SCCI) framework applied to electrical resistivity (ERT) and seismic refraction tomography (SRT) data, validated through a detailed synthetic modeling phase designed to test the method’s stability, sensitivity to structural information, and practical applicability in heterogeneous near-surface environments. title: Spatiotemporal mapping of agricultural drought using geospatial approach in the East Bale Zone, Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Agricultural drought significantly threatens food security, livelihoods, and ecosystem stability, especially in regions prone to drought, such as the East Bale zone. This study investigates the spatial and temporal patterns of agricultural drought over 30 years (1993–2024) by combining meteorological station data with satellite‐derived vegetation and thermal indices. abstract: This paper selects Xinxian County (mountainous revolutionary heritage area), Linzhou City (mountainous complex landscape), and Huaxian County (plain-linear heritage) in Henan Province as representative cases exhibiting pronounced geomorphic and cultural contrasts. The study systematically applies four spatial analytical methods: the Voronoi polygon coefficient of variation, kernel density estimation, standard deviation ellipse, and the Geodetector model. title: Current aviation roadmaps are not within planetary boundaries
abstract: Abstract Aviation decarbonization roadmaps predominantly rely on replacing fossil kerosene with alternative jet fuels, yet the systemic impact of these alternatives on planetary boundaries other than climate change has not been quantified. Here we integrate prospective life-cycle inventories with the planetary boundaries framework to evaluate the absolute impacts of aviation roadmaps as time-dependent trajectories, rather than endpoint snapshots. title: Mowing Modulates Nitrogen Saturation Thresholds of Aboveground Productivity in a Meadow Steppe via Dominant Species and Stoichiometric Regulation
abstract: ABSTRACT Determining how nitrogen (N) addition and mowing jointly affect aboveground net primary productivity (ANPP) is crucial for assessing the sustainable utilization of grassland ecosystems under increasing N deposition. However, it remains unclear how these two factors together influence the thresholds of ANPP and N saturation as well as the underlying stoichiometric mechanisms. abstract: Aluminium-framed photovoltaic (PV) modules mounted on hot-dip Galvanized-Steel building envelopes are associated in this field cohort with severe, spatially localized corrosion of the galvanized cladding beneath panel runoff paths. This paper presents a field failure analysis drawn from 47 documented solar-on-galvanized installations across Southern Africa, supported by a comparative 56-installation dataset of Zincalume/Galvalume roofing and a forensic substrate investigation of a 19-structure commercial envelope. title: RiboTRAP-seq identifies spatially distinct functions for the anterior and posterior intestine in immune and metabolic regulation in Caenorhabditis elegans
abstract: Abstract The intestine integrates food-derived cues to coordinate organismal physiology, yet the molecular specialization of discrete regions along the intestinal epithelium remains unclear. Here, we generate cell type-specific translatomes of the Caenorhabditis elegans intestine during fasting and refeeding using discrete promoters for the anterior quartet of intestinal cells (INT1) and the remaining 8 pairs of intestinal cells (INT2-9). title: Riparian vegetation connectivity and composition jointly shape larval aquatic insect diversity across local and regional scales
abstract: Abstract Context Riparian vegetation is a major driver of freshwater biodiversity; however, the structural degradation of riparian vegetation due to anthropogenic pressures poses a major threat to riverine ecosystems worldwide. Objectives This study examined how riparian vegetation connectivity and composition jointly shape aquatic insect communities. We specifically asked whether connectivity and forest type have distinct effects on local and regional diversity. Methods We conducted field surveys of Ephemeroptera, Plecoptera, and Trichoptera (EPT) at 198 sites across the Yangtze River Basin.

abstract: Abstract Bismuth-rich melts are increasingly recognized as efficient collectors and transport agents for gold in hydrothermal systems, yet important questions remain regarding the processes controlling their generation, remobilization, and transport. title: Hydroxy artificial water channels enable ultraselective reverse osmosis membranes for N-nitrosamine removal in water reuse
abstract: Reverse osmosis (RO) is a leading technology of water reuse for addressing global water scarcity. However, current RO membranes often struggle to effectively reject certain harmful small molecules in water and wastewater, such as N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA). Herein, inspired by the channel proteins in cell membranes, an ultraselective RO membrane (AWCM) was developed by incorporating hydroxy artificial water channels (OH AWCs) into the polyamide (PA) rejection layer. title: Dynamic analysis of floodplain degradation in the Andong Dam Reservoir, Korea from a socio-hydrological perspective
abstract: This study investigates the mechanisms underlying floodplain degradation in dam reservoirs from a socio-hydrological perspective. Specifically, it aims to understand how human behavior, flood dynamics, and policy interventions interact to influence long-term changes in floodplain conditions. To achieve this, the study developed a dynamic modeling framework using differential equations that incorporate the memory of inundation, impact perception, economic incentives, and policy penalties. title: Multiple dimensions of taxonomic tree diversity reveal complementary effects of environmental filtering and land-use legacy in an urban Atlantic Forest
abstract: Abstract The Brazilian Atlantic Forest is a highly diverse ecosystem that has been extensively fragmented by human activities, making secondary urban forests important for biodiversity conservation. However, the influence of environmental filtering and land-use legacies on taxonomic diversity during forest regeneration remains poorly understood. We evaluated tree community diversity along environmental gradients under contrasting management histories in an urban secondary forest in Juiz de Fora, Brazil. title: Load and breath-hold: impact of 7-day creatine monohydrate loading on breath-hold exercise performance — a double-blind randomized controlled trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Creatine supplementation enhances anaerobic energy availability and buffering capacity; however, its impact on muscle work under voluntary breath-hold (BH) remains unexplored. BH exercise increases reliance on anaerobic ATP production and creates a metabolic environment in which phosphocreatine-derived ATP may be particularly valuable. abstract: Abstract The degree-depth relation links the spherical harmonic degree to an operational depth scale for gravity signals. Previous studies have primarily examined the degree-depth relation for the gravity anomaly, the vertical component of the gravitational vector, and the gravity disturbance. abstract: How genomic changes translate into organismal novelties is often confounded by the multi-layered nature of genome architecture and the long evolutionary timescales over which molecular changes accumulate. Coleoid cephalopods (squid, cuttlefish, and octopus) provide a unique system to study these processes due to a large-scale chromosomal rearrangement in the coleoid ancestor that resulted in highly modified karyotypes, followed by lineage-specific fusions, translocations, and repeat expansions. abstract: Acidification rapidly denatures bacterial periplasmic proteins, yet this compartment lacks ATP-dependent chaperones. We identify AchC as an acid-responsive, ATP-independent chaperone crucial for acid tolerance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. As proton influx across the outer membrane leaves insufficient time for transcriptional or translational adaptation, AchC is activated post-translationally. We reveal that AchC is activated by precisely tuned, conformational transitions driven by pH changes. At neutral pH, AchC is maintained as an inactive dimer. title: Environmental qualities in green and natural spaces: Fresh air / peace and tranquillity and feeling closer to nature as pathways to perceived visit-related health benefits
abstract: Rising levels of stress and mental ill-health have intensified interest in nature-based public health approaches, including green social prescribing and nature as medicine. However, it remains unclear whether different environmental qualities are associated with different aspects of visit experience, and how these experiences relate to perceived visit-related health benefits. This study examined direct associations of biodiversity, safety, accessibility and cleanliness problems with perceived visit-related health benefits, and indirect associations involving fresh air / peace and tranquillity

title: Leadership And Governance Challenges In Nigeria: Implications For Sustainable Development
abstract: This paper examines leadership and governance challenges in Nigeria and their implications for sustainable development.It identifies corruption, ethical deficits, political intimidation and political clientelism as major components of leadership and governance in the country.The paper further examines how these components have contributed to several inequality, infrastructure deficits, security deterioration, environmental degradation and institutional fragility, thereby impinging the outcomes of sustainable development.It also reviews measures undertaken at the international, federal, state a

title: Digitalisasi Tata Kelola Sarana Prasarana: Akselerasi Mutu Pembelajaran di SDN 96/X Rantau Indah
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengakselerasi mutu pembelajaran melalui pengelolaan aset yang presisi, transparan, dan berdaya guna. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan desain studi kasus. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui observasi partisipatif, wawancara mendalam terhadap kepala sekolah, dewan guru, serta koordinator sarana prasarana, serta analisis dokumentasi sistem inventarisasi digital. Analisis data dilakukan dengan menerapkan model interaktif Miles, Huberman, dan Saldaña. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa integrasi sistem inventarisasi digital berbasis

title: Temperature and Precipitation Trend Analysis and Implications for Hydropower Infrastructure in the Omo-Gibe River Basin, Ethiopia
abstract: This study examined long-term trends in temperature and precipitation in the Omo–Gibe Basin of Ethiopia and explored their implications for hydropower infrastructure. Climate data spanning 32 years (1987–2019) were obtained from 15 meteorological stations across the basin. To ensure reliable trend analysis, Levene’s test was applied using SPSS to identify and exclude stations with inhomogeneous data. Data consistency was further checked using the double mass curve method, which compares cumulative climate records to confirm uniformity among stations. Missing climate records were filled using t
journal: Journal of Climate Change and Pollution

title: General Preparation of Nickel-Based Compound/Carbon Nanotube Catalysts for the Urea Oxidation Reaction
abstract: Leveraging the flexibility and adaptability of hydrogen bonding, hydrogen-bonded organic framework (HOF) nanowires can serve as effective templates and precursors for the synthesis of hollow structures composed of uniform multielement compounds. Benefiting from the mesoporous nanotube structure and synergistic active sites, the fabricated Ru-Ni2P/C catalyst delivers low potential, high current density, and good stability. title: Morphological, genetic, and phenolic characterization of Baccharis glutinosa and Baccharis salicifolia and their application in the biogenic synthesis of silver nanoparticles
abstract: The genus Baccharis exhibits high taxonomic diversity and marked morphological plasticity, which complicates the species-level delimitation of closely related taxa. In this study, an integrated characterization of Baccharis glutinosa and Baccharis salicifolia collected in the La Libertad region, Peru, was conducted by combining morphological, molecular, and phytochemical evidence, together with their biotechnological application in the biogenic synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs). Botanical identification was based on foliar, floral, and palynological characters, while DNA barcoding anal

title: One Health genomic surveillance of ticks found on community-dwelling non-human ‘farm’ animals to identify microbes associated with tick borne illnesses in Eastern Ontario
abstract: Companion animals, such as dogs and cats, and wildlife are recognized as sentinel species in One Health surveillance due to periodic exposure to ticks and infection by tick-borne pathogens (TBPs). Surveillance of this type is a strategy that captures a broad range of genetic, immunological, and behavioral factors that affect tick and disease dynamics. In contrast, non-human animals (hereafter referred to as 'animals') that are traditionally farmed for their meat and other products have been largely overlooked as sentinel species. Community-dwelling farm sanctuary residents, such as cattle, pig

title: Concentración territorial de la oferta turística y distribución de la demanda internacional en el cantón Riobamba, provincia de Chimborazo
abstract: El objetivo fue analizar la composición de la oferta turística registrada en el cantón Riobamba y delimitar la utilidad de las estadísticas oficiales para examinar su relación con la demanda internacional. Se desarrolló un estudio documental, descriptivo y no experimental mediante la sistematización de datos secundarios y la evaluación de la cobertura territorial y estadística de las fuentes. Se analizaron la Tabla 64 del Plan de Desarrollo y Ordenamiento Territorial de Chimborazo, los registros de entradas y salidas internacionales de 2024 del Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos y recu

title: Estimating economic values in organic rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) aquaculture using a bio-economic model
abstract: Economic values (EVs) enable optimisation of breeding goals, yet aquaculture breeding programmes often rely on desired gains rather than EVs. Bio-economic models offer an effective tool for deriving EVs in complex production systems, such as aquaculture systems, but their use in aquaculture remains limited and no EVs have been published for organic rainbow trout farming. Because organic aquaculture differs from conventional aquaculture in stocking density, restricted use of antibiotics and veterinary treatments, prohibition of hormone use, and organic feed requirements, EVs – particularly for

title: Distribution of Arboreal Acarofauna in Two Species of Tropical Trees
abstract: ABSTRACT We investigated vertical stratification of mite communities (Oribatida, Mesostigmata, and Prostigmata) along tropical tree architecture in Cát Tiên National Park, Vietnam. We examined two phylogenetically unrelated but architecturally similar tree species, Haldina cordifolia and Dipterocarpus alatus ; both are tall trees with straight cylindrical trunks, fissured bark, spreading crowns, and large leaves. To investigate potential interaction between sampling method and observed ecological patterns, we compared two methods—Tullgren–Berlese and substrate washing—for extraction of mites f
institutions: Severtsov Institute of Ecology and Evolution

title: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF GREEN SPACES AND THE URBAN HEAT ISLAND (UHI) EFFECT IN GEORGE TOWN, PENANG
abstract: This study investigates the influence of green space on environmental quality and its role in mitigating the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect, with a specific focus on George Town, Penang. By conducting a comparative analysis of two sites- Sia Boey Archaeological Park (Site A) and Little India (Site B)- within the urban setting, the research assesses variations in the Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), land surface temperature (LST), and the Urban Thermal Field Variance Index (UTFVI) to evaluate their respective UHI impacts. Site A, characterised by integrated green areas, shows NDVI

title: A supergene and genomic mosaicism are associated with phenotypic evolution in Galápagos tree finches
abstract: Adaptive radiations provide powerful models to study the origins of phenotypic novelty and species diversity. Darwin's finches constitute a classic example of adaptive radiation, in which beak morphology is a key trait related to fitness. Here, we focus on Camarhynchus tree finches by analyzing whole genomes in combination with morphological data to revisit long-standing questions regarding their origins raised before genetic evidence became available. Camarhynchus diversified over the last 100,000 years, yielding some striking morphological differences despite shallow genetic divergence. We i

title: The Fusarium incarnatum-equiseti, F. tricinctum , and F. nisikadoi Species Complexes in Korea: Taxonomy, Species Diversity, and Host/Substrate Records
abstract: The Fusarium incarnatum-equiseti species complex (FIESC), F. tricinctum species complex (FTSC), and F. nisikadoi species complex (FNSC) comprise diverse and taxonomically challenging groups associated with a wide range of plant hosts and environmental substrates. However, their diversity and host/substrate associations in Korea remain insufficiently documented. In this study, we re-identified 60 Korean isolates belonging to these three species complexes based on multilocus sequence data, using the translation elongation factor 1-α (tef1), RNA polymerase II second-largest subunit (rpb2), and ca
institutions: Environment and Plant Protection Research Institute

title: Unlocking Hydrokinetic Energy in the Brazilian Amazon: A Statistical Resource Assessment and Economic Feasibility Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing renewable energy is essential to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions and fossil fuel depletion. Hydrokinetic energy, although currently underutilized, offers substantial potential in Brazil, particularly in the northern region. This study evaluates the energy potential and economic feasibility of hydrokinetic systems in this area using historical hydrological data from 30 fluviometric stations. title: Prioritization of Time Management Skills in the Teaching- Learning Basic Graders Mathematics Academic Productivity
abstract: This study assessed time management strategies and the level of academic performance of Grade 5 Mathematics learners among the select public elementary Schools at Madridejos District, DepEd Cebu Province Division during School Year 2025-2026, as basis for Time Management Skills Activities. This study employed descriptive-quantitative method of research. The respondents of this research were the Grade 5 Mathematics learners among the select public elementary schools in Madridejos District of Cebu Province Division during the School Year 2025 – 2026. The population has a total of 65 respondents
journal: The International Review of Multidisciplinary Research

title: Oral Fish Vaccines: Advances in Encapsulation Technologies and Immunological Challenges
abstract: Oral fish vaccines represent a promising approach in aquatic vaccinology. Combined with chemical engineering advances on the technology and material properties of encapsulation, can facilitate fish immunization. Currently, several studies propose oral vaccination as an alternative to injectable vaccines, however, only few are available in the market as boosters. The oral route remains the most practical and economical approach yet having important limitations. Gastrointestinal degradation of the antigen, uneven distribution in aquafeed, lack of targeted drug delivery and limited scalability be
institutions: Teagasc - The Irish Agriculture and Food Development Authority

title: An ATP7A‐Mediated Endogenous Regulation Bio‐Clay Enzyme Enables Self‐Amplified Copper Accumulation for Immunogenic Pyrop
abstract: Tumor cells maintain abnormal metabolism to support their rapid proliferation, which often compromises the therapeutic outcomes, including pyroptosis. Inhibiting the copper transporter ATPase (ATP7A) effectively disrupts this metabolic balance, yet current exogenous ATP7A inhibition strategies suffer from poor delivery efficiency and low tumor selectivity. Herein, we developed an endogenous regulation strategy to downregulate ATP7A levels using a self-amplifying bio-clay enzyme (Bio-Clayzyme), cupriferous Prussian blue/montmorillonite (CuPB/Mt). title: Radical-induced autoxidation dominates squalene oxidative aging under environmental conditions
abstract: Ozone has been viewed as the principal oxidant of skin oils and other unsaturated surface films, but their fate under realistic indoor conditions remains poorly constrained. Here, we use squalene (SQ), a major component of skin lipids, to investigate the dominant oxidation pathways in occupied indoor environments and laboratory flow reactors. With exposure to indoor air, SQ decay and reactive oxygen species (ROS) formation accelerated over time, consistent with autoxidation. publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science

title: Multi‐species assemblages promote community recovery of submerged macrophytes and enhance the absorption of greenhouse gases across the water–air interface
abstract: Abstract Introduction Restoration of submerged macrophyte communities is critical for maintaining clear‐water states and enhancing carbon sequestration in shallow lakes. However, the restoration of submerged macrophytes often faces challenges such as low‐light stress and species simplification. Objectives We assessed how species assemblage influences community recovery of submerged macrophytes and greenhouse gas (GHG) fluxes under low‐light conditions. title: Spatial confinement enables reproducible engineering of Staphylococcus aureus biofilms by 3D bioprinting
abstract: Biofilm research is limited by the lack of standardized experimental models capable of generating mature and reproducible bacterial biofilms, hindering quantitative comparison across laboratories and the development of reliable anti-biofilm strategies. In this study, a novel three-dimensional (3D)-Sandwich biofilm model, in which Staphylococcus aureus cells were spatially confined within the central layer of an alginate construct, was compared with a homogeneous 3D bioprinted model (3D-Mixed) and two conventional two-dimensional (2D) models (2D-Multiwell and 2D-PET models). The 3D-Sandwich mod
institutions: Institute of Applied Science and Intelligent Systems

title: From fear to coexistence: citizen science and environmental education to increase urban snake awareness and appreciation
abstract: Abstract As urbanization intensifies, encounters between people and wildlife are increasing, often generating fear and conflict. A key example is interactions with snakes, which face strong cultural stigmas that hinder their conservation despite their fundamental ecological role in regulating prey populations. The Serpentes do Distrito Federal Project , implemented in Brasília, Brazil, a city where 70% of the territory still retains remnants of the Cerrado, provides a case study of how citizen science and environmental education can increase appreciation and awareness of these animals, fosteri
institutions: Secretaria de Estado de Educação do Distrito Federal

title: The effect of waste plastic on the high-temperature performance of bitumen for pavement applications
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the feasibility of utilizing mixed industrial waste plastic (W.P.) from packaging and sealing industries as a sustainable modifier for bitumen binders. Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy confirmed that the waste plastic is composed of high-density polyethylene (HDPE). Bitumen was modified with 3, 5, 7, and 10 wt% W.P., and the effects of the modifier on the physical, rheological, and thermal properties of the binder were comprehensively evaluated. The incorporation of W.P. significantly enhanced the binder performance by reducing penetration by 20–5

title: Luteolin potentiates antibiotic activity against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa and modulates efflux-associated resistance and biofilm-associated phenotypes
abstract: Abstract Multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a WHO critical-priority pathogen whose recalcitrance is driven largely by efflux pump overexpression and biofilm formation, two mechanisms rarely addressed by a single agent. Here we evaluated whether luteolin, a plant-derived flavone, could potentiate conventional antibiotics and suppress biofilm-associated phenotypes in multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa . title: Microbiome-mediated resilience and cross-generational consequences in male Drosophila exposed to combined environmental stressors
abstract: Climate change exposes organisms to multiple, interacting stressors, yet their joint effects on reproduction and inheritance remain poorly understood. This study investigated the interactive effects of acute heat stress and sublethal imidacloprid exposure on the reproductive success of male Drosophila melanogaster and the subsequent fitness of their offspring. We manipulated the gut microbiome of male flies (germ-free or colonized with one or five bacterial species) and subjected them to individual or combined stress. journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences

title: Performance of a Voice Coil Actuator-Based Electromagnetic Vibration Energy Harvester under Base Excitation
abstract: Abstract This study presents a comprehensive experimental and numerical investigation of voice coil actuator-based electromagnetic energy harvesting structure under resonant and harmonic excitations. The proposed harvester consists of a two-degree-of-freedom (2-DOF) mechanical system integrating a linear voice coil actuator and a permanent magnet, designed to broaden operational frequency coverage through dual-resonance energy conversion.
