title: Occurrence and discharge variability of Phalebas Thrust associated springs in western Middle Hill, Nepal
abstract: Geological discontinuities play a key role in groundwater movement and storage, especially in tectonically active and metamorphic rock-dominated terrains. The study area is located in the Syangja District western Nepal, with an area of 28.71 sq. km. around the Phalebas Thrust. This study focuses on the occurrence and discharge of springs with respect to the thrust. A post-monsoon spring inventory was conducted to gather information on spring location, discharge, temperature, surrounding geology, and structural discontinuities. The major lithologies are slate, dolomite, phyllite, and quartzite.

title: Penguatan Tata Kelola Mangrove Berbasis Masyarakat melalui Pemetaan UAV untuk Perencanaan Rehabilitasi Pesisir di Desa Sungai Selari
abstract: Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan membantu Perkumpulan Teras Riau dan RMRB Ranting Bukit Batu dalam menyediakan basis data spasial kawasan kelola mangrove di pesisir Desa Sungai Selari, Kecamatan Bukit Batu, Kabupaten Bengkalis. Kawasan tersebut berada pada lahan milik Pertamina UP II Sungai Pakning yang telah memperoleh izin kelola dari pemilik kawasan dengan ketentuan tidak mendirikan bangunan permanen. journal: Journal of Rural and Urban Community Empowerment

title: Investigation of sex determination in African cichlids reveals lack of fixed sex chromosomes in wild populations
abstract: Sex chromosomes are theorized to stop recombining and become fixed, yet many taxa show ambiguous genomic signals of sex consistent with either continuous recombination or sex chromosome turnover. Elucidating the basis of sex chromosome conservation or alternatively, turnover, requires comparative studies among natural populations with shared evolutionary histories. title: Furnishing Memorial: Gravestones Made from Repurposed Furniture Tops at African American Cemeteries
abstract: Abstract More than 100 graves at East End and Evergreen cemeteries, adjacent historical Black burial grounds in Richmond, Virginia, are marked by unusually thin headstones with physical features indicating prior use as the top surfaces of wooden furnishings. Using biographical sources for the deceased (with known death years ranging from 1899 to 1958) and the family members who likely provided the headstones, as well as records of a local stone-carving company, selected examples from cemeteries elsewhere in the American Southeast, and archaeological theories of reuse, this study explores possi

title: Identification of stress from incremental dentine stable isotope trends using linear enamel hypoplasia
abstract: High-precision sampling of dentine serial increments facilitates analysis of short-term variations in stable isotope ratios. Temporal resolution of micro-sampled increments is sufficiently high that the impact of short-term periods of physiological stress, which have well-described effects on stable isotope ratios, may be captured. However, distinguishing the effects of diet vs physiological effects on δ13C and δ15N is non-trivial. institutions: Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts

title: Hydrogen‐Bond‐Anchored Metal‐Free Cationic TADF Glassy Scintillators for High‐Resolution Dynamic X‐Ray Imaging
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic glassy scintillators offer a promising platform for scalable X‐ray imaging owing to their optical transparency and melt processability. However, their performance is often limited by inefficient triplet‐exciton utilization and poor condensed‐phase stability. Although flexible side chains or rotatable units facilitate glass formation, they also increase molecular relaxation and nonradiative energy dissipation. title: Bridging the disaster awareness-preparedness gap in a heritage-sensitive built environment: A case study of İznik
abstract: This study explores the asymmetric relationship between household disaster awareness and structural preparedness actions in İznik (Türkiye), a region characterized by its vulnerability to multiple hazards and its high sensitivity to cultural heritage damage. The present study examines the "awareness-preparedness gap" paradox within the extant literature. To this end, the study analyzes cross-sectional survey data obtained from 515 households employing binary logistic regression models. title: Stable and efficient n-type scaffolded semiconductor for photocatalytic hydrogen production under tungsten light irradiation
abstract: Abstract The production of green hydrogen (H 2 ) is a sustainable strategy to address the current energy crisis without contributing to long-term greenhouse gas emissions. Many powder-based photocatalysts have shown great promise for light-driven H 2 generation; however, in either bulk or nanostructured powder form they suffer from slow electron-transfer kinetics, material loss and poor recyclability, resulting in low hydrogen-evolution performance. title: Unity Brings Mutual Benefits: The Huddling Strategies of Temperate‐Living Primates in Cold Environments
abstract: Behavioral thermoregulation is a key adaptive tactic shaped by natural selection and species evolution, enabling animals to cope with variable thermal environments, particularly facing cold challenges. Quantifying the thermal and energetic consequences of behavior in the wild provides key insights into how animals cope with environmental challenges. title: Structural Variants in the Human Genome Associated With Gut Microbiome and Blood Metabolic Traits With Potential Causal Links
abstract: ABSTRACT Research on genetic variants affecting the gut microbiome and blood metabolites has mainly focused on single nucleotide variants (SNPs), leaving structural variants (SVs) largely unexplored. Here, we analyzed high‐coverage (∼42×) whole‐genome sequencing data from 2002 individuals and constructed a catalog of 138 859 high‐confidence SVs, including 44.3% variants not represented in public SV resources. title: Sharing the benefits and costs of conservation: public preferences for transboundary lynx policy
abstract: Transnational conservation is becoming ever-more important, yet reaching consensus on international conservation agreements remains challenging when decision-makers prioritise national benefits. Whether such approaches align with public preferences, however, remains unclear. We conduct a Discrete Choice Experiment to understand preferences for Iberian lynx conservation in Spain and Portugal, with a focus on the distribution of costs and benefits across countries. title: High‐Density‐Cluster Ru Catalyst Substitute for Pt/C Benchmark Improves Membrane Water Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT The hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is of great importance for the renewable energy conversion to hydrogen fuel via water electrolysis. However, the current benchmark Pt/C catalyst suffers from high cost, pH sensitivity, and deficient durability, severely restricting the large‐scale development of membrane water electrolysis. Herein, we develop a cost‐effective Pt‐free catalyst featuring high‐density, ultrafine Ru nanoclusters modified with CoP and uniformly dispersed on nitrogen‐doped carbon films (NCF). title: Memorandum: corrosion protection in structural engineering
abstract: This educational position paper proposes a competence-based reference framework for corrosion protection in structural engineering. It organizes corrosion-related learning objectives across the structural life cycle, links them to the six cognitive processes of the revised Bloom taxonomy, and distinguishes Bachelor, Master, professional practice, and research pathways. The contribution is educational rather than a new corrosion mechanism or experimentally validated teaching intervention. institutions: FH Münster University of Applied Sciences

title: Hydroxypheophytin a Stereoisomers as Principal Bioactive Compounds from Spirulina for the Reduction of Lipids and Appetite
abstract: Abstract The rising prevalence of obesity calls for the development of novel treatments. Spirulina is known for its beneficial effects on metabolic health; however, the specific bioactive compounds have not yet been identified. This work aims to address this gap through the bioassay-guided isolation of lipid-reducing compounds from Limnospira platensis using zebrafish larvae. The primary bioactive compounds identified were the stereoisomers of 132-hydroxypheophytin a (132-hpa), with 132-(R)-hpa (2) (EC50 = 1.7 μM) that showed seven times higher lipid-reducing potential than 132-(S)-hpa (1) (EC

title: Combined Application of Brown Sugar Solution and Yeast Extract, Enhanced Germination and Seedling Establishment of Corn (Zea mays L. IPB var. 6)
abstract: Corn (Zea mays L.) productivity largely depends on rapid germination and strong early seedling establishment. This study evaluated the effects of sucrose solution and yeast extract concentrations on the germination and early growth of corn (Zea mays L. IPB var. 6). A two-factor factorial experiment arranged in a Completely Randomized Design with three replications was conducted under laboratory conditions. journal: ASEAN Journal of Scientific and Technological Reports

title: FACS-based isolation and recovery of physiologically distinct bacterial subpopulations from infected insect hosts
abstract: Phenotypic heterogeneity is often encountered during infection but remains challenging to investigate in vivo. Here, using the entomopathogenic spore-former Bacillus thuringiensis with the Galleria mellonella insect larva infection model and Fluorescence-Activated Cell Sorting (FACS), we present a workflow that enables the isolation of bacterial subpopulations in distinct physiological states, directly from infected hosts, for downstream characterization. title: Heritage Sites and Climate Resilience: Selected Case Studies of Buddhist Archaeological Sites of Telangana
abstract: The historic environment is vulnerable to climate change that is continuous. The loss or degradation of these heritage sites adversely affects physicality, collective memory, identity, and cultural continuity. It is learnt that pose a definite need for policies and strategies to address climate change. Protecting and preserving these sites is particularly challenging because of their diversity in form, location, materials, and cultural meaning. title: Global Logistics Performance Before and After COVID-19: A Longitudinal Cluster-Based Analysis Using LPI Data
abstract: COVID-19 created major pressure on global supply chains, but it remains uncertain whether this coincided with changes in countries’ logistics performance groups. This study investigates this issue using World Bank Logistics Performance Index data for 2016, 2018 and 2023. K-Means clustering was separately carried out on six LPI dimensions for 160 countries in both 2016 and 2018, and 139 countries in 2023. The 2023 edition reflects late-2022 survey responses. title: Marketing Margins, Distribution Efficiency, and Retail Price Gaps of MinyaKita Cooking Oil in Baturaja, Indonesia
abstract: Affordable cooking oil requires distribution arrangements that control costs without weakening consumer access. Evidence on how these objectives interact within regulated industrial food channels remains context dependent. This study examines MinyaKita distribution in Baturaja, Indonesia, using a descriptive comparison of interviews and observations involving two distributors, three sub-distributors, and thirty-two retailers. Marketing margins, recorded costs, profits, producer’s shares, and retail price gaps were examined, with separate arithmetic checks of respondent-level tabulations. The r
journal: Best Journal of Administration and Management

title: From Mexico to Argentina: Predicting the distribution of the invasive weed Tithonia tubaeformis beyond its native range using niche modelling
abstract: 1. Biological invasions are a major driver of global change, affecting biodiversity, ecosystem functioning and agricultural productivity. Tithonia tubaeformis (Asteraceae) is a weed native to Mexico that has become invasive in several regions worldwide, including Argentina, where it threatens crop systems. Here, we compared species distribution models trained with native- and invaded-range occurrences to estimate the potential distribution of T. tubaeformis in Argentina. title: Ultrasonic modification on the physicochemical properties, structure characterizations, and intestinal barrier-protective activities of raspberry polysaccharides
abstract: Natural polysaccharides possess diverse biological functions, yet their macromolecular architecture frequently restricts molecular accessibility and limits their application as health-promoting ingredients. Here, we employed an ultrasound-driven strategy to remodel the molecular structure of raspberry polysaccharide (RAP) and investigated how controlled depolymerization governs its intestinal barrier-protective properties. title: A conceptual biocultural indicator framework for biodiversity in cultural landscapes: development and application in the Alhambra-Generalife-Albaicín (Spain) and Connemara (Ireland)
abstract: Abstract This paper develops a framework for the identification of biocultural indicators of biodiversity in cultural landscapes. To combat the persisting separation and dualistic conceptualisation of nature and culture in the heritage field, the framework views landscapes as dynamic assemblages of human and non-human actors. This highlights the significance of biocultural practices as indicators of how biodiversity emerges through the same human–environment relationships that give rise to both heritage and landscape over time. title: Real-time economic disruption and recovery from Atlantic hurricanes across the US
abstract: Climate projections indicate substantial increases in hurricane activity under continued warming, yet how local economies adjust to hurricanes in real time remains poorly understood. Using daily transaction data from 7,987 US ZIP codes exposed to 21 Atlantic hurricanes between 2017 and 2024, we examine aggregate merchant sales and consumer spending to quantify disruption and test for substitution across locations and channels. Hurricanes cause losses equivalent to about two days of typical sales, with limited offsetting substitution and recovery to pre-hurricane levels within ten days. Economi

title: Time and Timelessness in Alexander's Search for Beauty
abstract: This paper explores Christopher Alexander’s theory of architecture and urban planning through the lens of time and timelessness. In so doing it traces his development from early systems thinking to his later metaphysical conception of living structure. It situates his work within the context of 20th-century urban thought and highlights his critique of mechanistic planning in favour of adaptive, participatory, and generated structures. title: Light‐Controlled Localized Delamination and Blistering of Azobenzene‐Containing Polymer Thin Films in an Aqueous Environment
abstract: ABSTRACT Blister formation in thin polymer films represents a localized delamination instability whereby interfacial failure leads to out‐of‐plane deformation of the supported film. While numerous biomass utilization strategies have been reported, the development of validated thermochemical conversion systems capable of transforming this invasive resource into stable value-added products remains limited. abstract: Abstract Aims: This study analyzed the spatiotemporal distribution, interannual variability, and recurrence of burned areas across land-use and land-cover (LULC) classes in the Brazilian Cerrado from 2019 to 2024. title: Implications and Risks of Irregular Migration for Security, Stability, and Development in Libya
abstract: This article examines the implications of irregular migration for security, societal stability, and development in Libya, with particular attention to the country’s position as a country of origin, transit, and destination along Mediterranean migration routes. The analysis draws on a qualitative documentary review of historical scholarship, Libyan legal literature, institutional reports, and international policy materials, with particular emphasis on developments following the political and security crisis of 2011. abstract: Here we present AmpliconSuite, a toolkit for focal amplification analysis from cancer whole-genome sequencing that identifies extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA), breakage-fusion-bridges and other amplification modes. Its ecContext module categorizes ecDNA structures to understand formation mechanisms. title: Where did the language of the northeastern Estonian Poluverniki come from?
abstract: This study examines the linguistic origins of the historical community of Poluverniki in northeastern Estonia. Members of this group were typically bilingual and spoke a distinctive blend of dialectal Russian and Estonian. The prevailing scholarly view — based largely on non‑linguistic evidence — holds that the Poluverniki descended from a Votic‑like Southern Finnic population that was later linguistically assimilated by neighboring Russian dialects. abstract: Persea americana (Lauraceae) is a fruit widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions, commonly known as the avocado. Although the seeds represent a considerable portion of the whole fruit, scientific research on their phytochemistry and biological effects is still in its early stages. title: Political affiliation impacts climate attention and choice beyond extreme weather exposure
abstract: Abstract Political polarization and increasing exposure to extreme weather can shape public engagement with climate change, yet the underlying psychological mechanisms remain unclear. In this Registered Report, we examine how political affiliation, extreme weather exposure and subjective attribution influence climate-relevant information search and decision-making in a US sample ( N = 1,451). abstract: The article follows the journey of the Pergamon/Zeus Altar from Bergama (present-day Turkey) to Berlin in the late nineteenth century and its reverberations in the present. abstract: Mountain tourism geosites, as a form of nature-based and adventure tourism, provide authentic experiences through hiking, crater exploration, scenic panoramas, and adventure activities. These experiences allow tourists to encounter natural landscapes while developing a sense of challenge, freedom, and connection with nature. abstract: Abstract Foodborne diseases remain a major public health concern, with Listeria monocytogenes being one of the most significant foodborne pathogens due to its high mortality rate and persistence in food-processing environments. abstract: Research on the oral–gut axis has progressed from association studies to mechanistic understanding. However, the pathways by which oral-derived microorganisms, metabolites, and inflammatory signals traverse gastrointestinal barriers and affect intestinal homeostasis remain poorly defined. abstract: Urban ecosystems provide essential ecosystem services (ES), a supply that is dependent on ecosystem condition (EC). Statistical frameworks like the UN SEEA-EA explicitly link ES flows to the extent and condition of ecosystem assets. Yet, the concrete role of EC in shaping the ES flows remains only partially understood, as their relationship is complex and varies across services. This was first made possible by fluorescent ubiquitination-based cell cycle indicator (Fucci) technology, which distinguishes specific cell cycle phases through the reciprocal degradation of fluorescently tagged, truncated forms of human CDT1 and GMNN proteins. abstract: Erigeron sumatrensis Retz. (Asteraceae) is an annual herb native to South America that has become a noxious invasive weed in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide. Here, we report the first complete chloroplast genome of this plant species. title: Dual Fluorophore System for Direct Measurement of Acidity of Aerosol Particles
abstract: Atmospheric aerosol particles exhibit diverse physical and chemical properties, depending on their composition and source, which are challenging to measure directly due to their chemical complexity. Aerosol acidity is a key chemical property that has significant implications for climate, heterogeneous chemistry, and human health. Here, we present a novel approach to measure aerosol acidity using carbon dots (CDs) as in situ fluorophores. abstract: Art toys have become highly influential across Asia, particularly in China, Japan, South Korea, and Singapore, where culturally inspired character design has been used to strengthen tourism branding and enhance community product value, generating economic impact worth billions of baht. title: Species traits mediate terrestrial mammal density responses to human impacts
abstract: Human activities are reshaping ecosystems, but their effects on species population density remain poorly understood. Most studies focus on species presence–absence, thus limiting insight into how anthropogenic pressures affect population density. Emerging evidence suggests that responses of natural populations to human disturbance are highly variable, often contingent on species‐specific traits. abstract: Predicting species persistence within ecological communities is a fundamental challenge for both empirical and theoretical ecology. abstract: This study investigates how Open Innovation Orientation contributes to adaptive island resilience through Renewable Energy Tourism Attractiveness, Green Innovation Capability, and Tourism Co-Creation Ecosystem in Koh Larn Island, Thailand, and Jeju Island, South Korea. abstract: La taxonomía de los murciélagos neotropicales ha experimentado una rápida reorganización en los últimos años, frecuentemente impulsada por el descubrimiento de divergencia genética previamente no reconocida y la descripción de nuevas especies. title: Assessing climate change perceptions and climate-smart agriculture adoption among root, tuber and banana farmers in Eastern D.R. Congo
abstract: Perceptions shape human practices, including agricultural decisions, yet their influence on climate-smart agriculture adoption remains insufficiently understood in climate-vulnerable eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). This study compared farmers’ perceptions of climate change with empirical climate data of the past three decades across South-Kivu’s agroecological zones (AEZ), eastern DRC. title: Degradation of graphene oxide-silver nanoparticles by hypochlorite: impacts on physicochemical properties, antimicrobial activity and ecotoxicity
abstract: Abstract Graphene oxide-silver nanoparticles (GO-AgNPs) is a promising hybrid material for development of composites, sensors, catalysts, and antimicrobial systems. However, its degradation and life cycle remain poorly understood. Here, the chemical degradation of GO-AgNPs was investigated by sodium hypochlorite (bleach water) linked to its antimicrobial and ecotoxicological effects. abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is a crucial environmentally benign oxidant. title: Impact of Urban Air Pollution and Climatic Factors on Photovoltaic Performance: A Comparative Modelling Study Across Major Indian Cities
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) systems play an important role in India's transition towards renewable energy. However, their performance can be significantly influenced by environmental conditions that vary across different urban regions. This study investigates the impact of urban pollution and climatic conditions on photovoltaic efficiency in four Indian cities: Delhi, Mumbai, Jaipur, and Bangalore. title: Southern South American maize landraces: a source of phenotypic diversity
abstract: Abstract Maize ( Zea mays L.) is a globally important crop for food, feed, and industrial uses. Modern breeding increasingly targets traits beyond yield, including stress tolerance, nutritional quality, and pest resistance. Progress toward these goals is constrained by the narrow genetic diversity of commercial varieties, a consequence of the repeated use of a limited number of inbred lines. Maize landraces therefore represent valuable reservoirs of genetic and phenotypic diversity. abstract: Abstract Agar-based films are promising biodegradable materials, but their brittleness and moisture sensitivity limit practical use. In this study, a phytochemical extract from the Australian halophyte pigface ( Carpobrotus glaucescens ) was evaluated as a concentration-dependent modifier of agar films. abstract: Reducing the Ru content while maintaining high oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity remains a major challenge. In this study, single phase Ru 0.30 Cr 0.31 Mn 0.39 O 2 nanofibers were prepared through electrospinning process followed by temperature-regulated heat treatment. title: Energy expenditure of bonobos across their locomotor repertoire
abstract: Unlike quadrupedal mammals, primates use diverse locomotor modes adapted to arboreal environments. Such diversity of movements challenges allometric models, which underestimate energetic costs by focusing on steady-state walking. To address this, we combined ethological and biomechanical approaches to estimate the net metabolic cost of transport in bonobos (Pan paniscus). title: Decontamination Risk Management in Radioisotope Facilities: A Bibliometric Review
abstract: Background: Risk management in the decontamination process of radioisotope and radiopharmaceutical production facilities has garnered significant research attention due to its vital contribution to environmental safety and occupational health. While the volume of literary evidence regarding radiation safety continues to expand, study focuses and methodological approaches remains diverse. abstract: Water from the Ganga River and its tributaries is the main freshwater resource in the northern parts of India and has experienced rigorous ecological deterioration because of the continuous discharge of untreated polluted industrial and household effluents, resulting in increased chemical and microbial loads of pollution. abstract: We introduce a Bayesian framework for indirect local clustering of functional data, leveraging B-spline basis expansions and a novel dependent random partition model. By exploiting the local support properties of B-splines, our approach allows partially coincident functional behaviors, achieved when shared basis coefficients span sufficiently contiguous regions. title: Biochar for Low-Carbon Energy Crop Systems: Bibliometric Trends, Agronomic Evidence, and Soil Carbon Sequestration Pathways from 2007 to 2025
abstract: Abstract This bibliometric and critical review examines the evolution of scientific research on biochar application in energy-crop systems, emphasizing biomass productivity, soil quality, and soil carbon sequestration from 2007 to 2025. The bibliometric assessment comprised 409 records retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and integrated publication trends, thematic evolution, scientific collaboration networks, and agronomic and environmental evidence. title: Spatiotemporal patterns of antimicrobial resistance in shared human-animal waterpoints in the Maasai Mara Ecosystem, Kenya
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) presents an existential One Health threat. The spread of AMR in arid and semi-arid landscapes is modulated by ecological interactions and exacerbated by endemicity of livestock diseases and poor sanitation in shared human-animal systems leading to misuse of antibiotics. This study characterized the prevalence, resistance patterns, and spatiotemporal variations of AMR in surface water sources in the Maasai Mara Ecosystem (MME), a rapidly changing water-stressed socio-ecological landscape. title: p‐Block Aluminum Tailoring Termination‐Acidity of Two‐Dimensional MoS 2 Nanosheets for Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
abstract: ABSTRACT Molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2 ) has shown promising electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity in acidic electrolyte, while its high‐pH alkaline HER performance is critically poor due to the sluggish water dissociation kinetics. title: Polypropylene Nonwoven Fabric Filters Containing Graphene Oxide: A Streamlined Approach to Enhance Ultrafine Particulate Matter Removal
abstract: ABSTRACT Airborne particulate matter (PM) is one of the main atmospheric pollutants and is associated with respiratory and cardiovascular diseases and increased mortality. Ultrafine particles with aerodynamic diameter below 100 nm (PM 0.1 ) undergo structure and chemical transformations due to their high surface area and reactivity, acting as precursors of harmful and persistent particles. title: Differences in microbial composition and salt tolerance between rhizosphere and bulk soil of Kalidium foliatum
abstract: Salt is an important abiotic stress that affects plant growth. Research has shown that plants can recruit beneficial microorganisms from the surrounding soil. However, the ecological functions of the rhizosphere microbiome in salt tolerant plants have not been explored to a large extent. title: In the beginning was the name: naming and framing sustainable cultural tourism destinations in peripheral areas
abstract: Early-stage tourism development in peripheral areas often takes place under ‘below-zero’ conditions, where tourism is weakly established, place identities fragmented, and conventional branding strategies premature. In such contexts, the name of a place and its associated communicative framings become a first vital connector between potential visitors, local stakeholders, and the area itself. title: Periodic and aperiodic particle-reinforced composite-inspired metamaterials: Compressive and flexural properties
abstract: Traditional particle-reinforced composite materials face several challenges such as particle agglomeration, poor interfacial load transfer that can lead to premature failure, manufacturing complexities, and increased weight. Motivated by these limitations, this work designs, additively manufactures, and tests new classes of periodic and aperiodic particle-reinforced composite-like metamaterials (PRCM). title: Seasonal and Site-Specific Variation in Plant Tolerance to Air Pollution: An APTI and API Assessment
abstract: Urban vegetation serves as an important natural barrier against atmospheric pollution by capturing, absorbing and filtering airborne contaminants, thereby improving air quality. The Air Pollution Tolerance Index (APTI), which is derived from key biochemical parameters of plants, is widely used to evaluate their tolerance to polluted conditions. abstract: Abstract The growing accumulation of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) waste and the increasing demand for clean hydrogen call for integrated electrochemical strategies. Ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR), derived from PET hydrolysis, offers a thermodynamically favorable alternative to the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and can be coupled with the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) to simultaneously produce value-added chemicals and H2. title: Challenges and trends in hydrogen production by electrolysis
abstract: Abstract The growing global demand for clean and sustainable energy has intensified research into hydrogen production via water electrolysis. In this context, this review provides an integrative analysis of recent advances in electrolytic hydrogen production, emphasizing electrocatalytic materials, electrolyte composition, process efficiency, techno‐economic feasibility, and the use of alternative feedstocks. title: Institutional risk, finance, and the limits of techno-economic optimality in green hydrogen deployment
abstract: Green hydrogen is widely positioned as a key option for deep decarbonization, yet large-scale deployment remains limited despite growing techno-economic potential. This review examines how non-technical conditions influence the feasibility of green hydrogen business models, using the Netherlands as an illustrative case. title: Observation of Daily Flood Hazard During the SWOT Cal/Val Orbit
abstract: Abstract Flood peaks can develop and recede within a day, making them difficult to capture with satellites with multi‐day revisit intervals. Here, we exploit daily observations during the Calibration and Validation phase of the SWOT mission to examine a short‐lived flood in May 2023 along the Du Gouffre River in Canada. Despite channel widths below 100 m, SWOT tracked day‐to‐day changes in water surface elevation, capturing a rapid rise of approximately 5 m consistent in timing and magnitude with in situ measurements. We derived flood extent based on classification and confidence information.

abstract: Vitamin D occupies a paradoxical position in contemporary medicine. Low circulating concentrations of 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] are consistently associated with numerous adverse health outcomes, including cancer, cardiovascular disease (CVD), fractures, and autoimmune and inflammatory rheumatic diseases (IRDs). title: Under-platformization: platform literacy and the interplay between multiple actors in developing rural e-commerce in Central and Western China
abstract: Abstract Rural e-commerce in China’s central and western regions is often framed as a scalable pathway to rural revitalization. Yet, platformization may also stall, even when there is already a profitable rural industry. Drawing on interviews, fieldwork, and local archives, we examine the Bai silver handicraft cluster in Xinhua Village, Yunnan Province, which despite being a nationally recognized Taobao village, still exhibits under-platformization. abstract: L-arginase catalyzes the hydrolysis of L-arginine into L-ornithine and urea and plays a key role in the urea cycle. Interest in microbial L-arginases has increased because of their potential biotechnological and biomedical applications, including arginine-deprivation approaches in cancer research. In this study, extracellular L-arginase from Alcaligenes aquatilis BC2 was partially purified and biochemically characterized. title: Narrativas de desapontamento em megaobras de urbanização turística
abstract: Embora as megaobras de urbanização turística e engordamento artificial de praias sejam frequentemente promovidas como soluções técnicas para a erosão costeira e o desenvolvimento territorial, seus efeitos sobre a experiência dos usuários e as tensões sociais geradas por essas intervenções permanecem subexploradas. abstract: Abstract Nuclear receptors (NRs) are a superfamily of ligand-regulated transcription factors that translate chemical signals to gene regulatory responses. abstract: Abstract In work environments where walking surfaces may be contaminated by liquid, safety footwear must provide high slip resistance. One method to enhance friction on wet or contaminated interfaces is to regulate fluid pressure through surface texturing of the footwear outsole. title: A Critical Call for Mechanistic Investigations of Metal‐Bacteria Interactions
abstract: The antibacterial properties of metals have been recognized for millennia. It is thus well established that this antibacterial response has tremendous importance for bioengineering applications, driving ever-increasing resources for research efforts, especially over the last few decades. abstract: Abstract Soft robots using bistable structures often face limitations due to a fixed energy landscape, which restricts their configurational adaptability and functional diversity. To address this challenge, we introduce an energy-landscape-traversing (ELTra) bistable structure that enables on-demand reconstruction of the energy landscape, continuous stabilization of intermediate states, and precise modulation of energy release, capabilities that are challenging to achieve with conventional systems. abstract: Hydrogel technologies have rapidly evolved from simple hydrated materials to multifunctional systems for soft robotics, drug delivery, tissue engineering and surgical simulation. As their complexity increases, designing hydrogels for a specific application requires identifying which mechanical phenomena govern material behaviour under the relevant operating conditions, rather than optimising individual properties in isolation. title: Designing a multifunctional peptide with biofilm-disrupting and fibroblast migration-promoting activities for infection management
abstract: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) remain difficult to manage due to the emergence of antibiotic-resistant pathogens and the persistence of biofilm-based infections. Thus, novel therapeutic strategies beyond conventional antibiotics are needed. abstract: Abstract Background Global identity (GI), a sense of belonging to a global society, is gaining attention as a key factor for promoting pro‐environmental behaviours (PEB) to tackle the global environmental crisis. Among such global predicaments, plastic waste and pollution remain pressing issues. Although prior research has established a link between GI and PEB, the underlying psychological pathways have not been comprehensively explored. title: The Evolution, Demise, and Renaissance of Green Spaces in Dar es Salaam: An Explorative Discourse on Influential Factors
abstract: Urban green spaces in African cities are under unprecedented pressure from rapid urbanisation, yet the factors influencing their utilisation remain poorly understood. This paper examines the determinants of green space use in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, one of Africa's fastest-growing metropolitan areas. This study employs a mixed-methods approach across 42 green spaces in three municipalities, drawing on Attention Restoration Theory, Place Attachment Theory, and the Ecological Model of Physical Activity. abstract: Producing polymeric products from renewable raw materials is desirable to reduce reliance on petrochemical-based materials. abstract: Abstract Among the most prevalent features in Earth's deep mantle are the Large Low Velocity Provinces (LLVPs), hypothesized to be hotter and compositionally distinct from the surrounding mantle. abstract: Abstract Chromosome organization and repetitive DNA distribution are important components of genome evolution in teleost fishes but remain poorly characterized in many species of ecological and conservation relevance. abstract: This exploratory study examines whether stated guided-tour priorities and tourist characteristics are associated with value-for-money evaluations and positive recommendations in South Africa’s Western Cape, and whether value adds explanatory information to tourist advocacy. abstract: This study develops a dual strategy of synthesis optimisation and B-site substitution to improve low-temperature CO oxidation of LaFeO3 perovskites. title: Metabolomic fingerprinting of an artisanal blue-veined cheese: Impact of cave microenvironment and producer
abstract: Artisanal blue cheeses are highly valued products due to their unique quality attributes. This study conducted a large-scale longitudinal investigation into the influence of the producer and natural cave microenvironment on the metabolomic profile of PDO Cabrales cheese during ripening. abstract: Tetrandrine (TET) is a bisbenzylisoquinoline alkaloid with promising anticancer activity, although its limited selectivity toward malignant over non-cancerous cells restricts its therapeutic potential. A series of mono- and bis-N-substituted tetrandrine derivatives was therefore investigated to determine whether N-functionalization could improve the cytotoxic selectivity of the parent scaffold. abstract: Abstract Expansive soils are considered one of the most problematic soil types worldwide due to their significant volume change behaviour in response to variations in moisture content. This study investigates the stabilization of expansive soil using a combination of cement and talcum powder in order to improve its engineering performance. abstract: Abstract Nitrate pollution is one of the most widespread forms of contamination, and in high concentrations has adverse effects on aquatic ecosystems. Fish are susceptible to this contaminant and are known to modify their behaviour in a variety of ways when exposed, but most information regarding changes in behaviour pertains only to long‐term or chronic exposure. abstract: Urban resource environment carrying capacity (RECC) is increasingly challenged by nonlinear interactions among socioeconomic development, resource depletion, and geological environmental degradation. title: Club de ciencias: Una investigación sobre la calidad del agua y la desigualdad urbana
abstract: Este estudio analiza una actividad desarrollada en un club de ciencias, basada en el aprendizaje por proyectos, cuyo objetivo fue investigar el problema de la calidad del agua distribuida en diferentes barrios de una ciudad. La actividad se desarrolló con estudiantes de tercer año de secundaria de una escuela pública del interior del estado de São Paulo, Brasil, en el marco de los clubes juveniles. Para ello, dos docentes, uno de sociología y otro de química, trabajaron junto con los estudiantes en el desarrollo del proyecto a lo largo de un año académico, articulando debates sobre sociología

title: A Radiation‐Modulated Frost Index Improves the Representation of Frost Stress and Yield Response in Winter Wheat
abstract: ABSTRACT Late spring frost is a major abiotic stress affecting winter wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) production, yet its impact on yield remains difficult to quantify because crop responses depend not only on the intensity of low‐temperature exposure but also on environmental conditions following frost events. Conventional frost indices are primarily temperature‐based and therefore do not fully capture variability in yield responses under comparable thermal stress conditions. title: The Access Paradox: A Decade of Expanded Influenza Vaccine Access That Did Not Close a Racial Disparity
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Despite more than a decade of expanded influenza vaccine access through Medicare, pharmacy-based programs, and community clinics, older African Americans remain vaccinated at markedly lower rates than older White and Asian adults. This study examines why the disparity has persisted and whether U.S. vaccination policy evidence was ever designed to address it. title: The role of rural tourism in promoting small farmer’s income: Evidence from the sub-Himalayan region of Eastern India
abstract: Rural tourism is increasingly recognised as a viable non-farm livelihood strategy for small and marginal farmers, especially in regions with strong tourism potential. However, despite its growing policy relevance, empirical evidence on its role in improving farmers’ income in the sub-Himalayan region of Eastern India remains limited. This study examines the determinants of farmers’ participation in tourism-led livelihood activities and estimates the impact of this participation on household income. abstract: Abstract Forest management is a potential tool to increase the resiliency of snowshoe hare ( Lepus americanus ) populations to the negative demographic impacts of low‐snowfall winters. Pennsylvania's forests and landscape differ from those of the core snowshoe hare range, and region‐specific data are needed to optimize forest management for snowshoe hares. abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) photosynthesis from molecular oxygen and water offers a sustainable route for decentralized oxidant generation, yet elucidating the molecular‐level active sites for oxygen activation in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) remains challenging. title: Small viruses reveal bidirectional evolution between HK97-fold viruses and encapsulins via procapsids
abstract: The HK97-fold is an ancient, conserved protein structure that assembles protein shells, forming the capsids of Duplodnaviria viruses and prokaryotic biochemical compartments called encapsulsins. It has been proposed that encapsulins evolved from HK97-fold viruses. But the higher complexity of viral capsids represents a biophysical paradox in the evolution of HK97-fold protein shells. title: Structural control of Fe(II)-based multivalent glycan assemblies enables intramolecular avidity and ultra-high-affinity binding
abstract: Abstract Multivalent glycan recognition depends critically on the spatial organization of saccharides, yet quantitative design rules linking glycan geometry to binding remain poorly defined. Here, we report atomically-precise Fe(II)-based glycoassemblies that enable independent control of glycan valency, spacing, and topology within discrete molecular scaffolds. Using monomeric Griffithsin as a model lectin, we uncover that subtle changes in glycan presentation drive discrete transitions from partial site engagement to high-avidity, multi-site binding, spanning a > 10³-fold range in affinity.

title: Evaluating EUCLID location accuracy using lightning events near tall structures
abstract: Abstract. This study evaluates the location accuracy (LA) of the European Cooperation for Lightning Detection (EUCLID) network by analysing lightning strikes recorded near tall structures located either on flat ground or on elevated terrain, such as mountain ridges, over a 14-year period from 2012 to 2025. abstract: Biliary ascites is a rare form of ascites resulting from disruption of biliary tract integrity, and spontaneous, non-traumatic, non-iatrogenic perforation of the gallbladder or bile ducts is an exceptionally uncommon cause in adults. We report a 65-year-old man who presented with right upper quadrant pain, jaundice, fever, diarrhea, and progressive abdominal distension following an episode of untreated choledocholithiasis. abstract: Soils are Earth's largest carbon reservoir, yet microbial mechanisms controlling decomposition, and their warming response, remain poorly resolved, especially in subsoils. Using genome-resolved proteogenomics within a replicated whole-soil warming experiment (0-90 cm, +4 °C, 7.5 years) we map microbial traits, their depth stratification, and warming responses. title: Risk mapping with community participation: strategies for risk and disaster management
abstract: Risk must be understood as a social construction; public participation is thus essential for the development of integrated plans and policies that are effective and sustainable. This action-research presents participatory mapping carried out in the community of Guarará, municipality of Franco da Rocha, São Paulo, Brazil. abstract: Aeromonas salmonicida, the causative agent of furunculosis, poses a serious threat to salmonid aquaculture, but its pathogenicity in rare cold-water fish species remains insufficiently characterized. This study reports the first isolation and characterization of a pathogenic A. salmonicida strain (Ag001) from diseased Thymallus arcticus grubei in China. title: Accelerated aging and health in people experiencing homelessness in New Mexico: a latent class analysis
abstract: People experiencing homelessness (PEH) experience elevated rates of premature mortality and health conditions typically observed in housed individuals 15–20 years older, a phenomenon termed accelerated aging (AA). To investigate which groups of adult PEH are at risk of AA. abstract: ABSTRACT Agriculture is a primary driver of biodiversity loss through habitat conversion and degradation. Companies are increasingly being asked to investigate, disclose, and act on their biodiversity impacts by both regulatory policies and voluntary commitments. abstract: Abstract Niche-based models have been widely used to identify potential species for deployment in target environments; however, these approaches rely primarily on natural distribution data and may underestimate the full adaptive potential of commercial species. abstract: Low-temperature rechargeable batteries are crucial for energy storage under subzero conditions but remain limited by sluggish ion transport, severe interfacial polarization, and slow charge-transfer kinetics. abstract: Household solid waste management strains environmental and public-health systems across sub-Saharan Africa, where collection infrastructure has not kept pace with urban growth and open dumping or burning is often the only option. Kaduna State assessments have documented these service gaps, yet no published study examines how households in the state's smaller towns manage waste or what they know about modern alternatives. title: Ecological responses of soil bacteria to rapid and slow temperature fluctuations
abstract: Fluctuating temperatures profoundly affect microorganisms' coexistence, biogeographic distributions and responses to future climate change. However, how microorganisms respond to fluctuating temperatures with different frequencies in natural communities remains unknown. abstract: Abstract Urbanization poses a drastic threat to biodiversity, but does not affect all species equally. As such, identifying the life history traits and ecological characteristics that distinguish species that tolerate urban areas from those that do not is a central goal in urban ecology. abstract: Abstract Soil microbial biomass and nitrogen, a vital nutrient pool for ecosystem nutrient cycling is affected by several factors including climate, edaphic, and land-use change. abstract: This study investigates the application of an EPS light-gauge steel composite envelope system in rural buildings located in the hot-summer and warm-winter region of Hainan. An experimental building was constructed in Shitang Village, Ding’an County, Hainan Province, using traditional brick structures as a control for comparison. abstract: This study examined the effectiveness of the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), land surface temperature (LST), and their integrated indices in capturing dry-season drought dynamics in the dipterocarp deciduous forest ecosystems of Yok Don National Park from 2014 to 2024. title: The soundscape wheel: a conceptual map for tourism geographers
abstract: Soundscapes are receiving increasing attention in tourism studies. Much focus is given to noise generated by tourism, whereas the role of sound in experiences of place has received less attention. To address this gap, we introduce a ‘soundscape wheel’ as a theoretical and applied tool that can inform transdisciplinary work across tourism studies. abstract: This study investigated the effects of climate change-driven extreme weather in July, especially drought, on corn yields in Nebraska. The yields of irrigated and non-irrigated (rainfed) corn were compared using data over 20 years, from 1998 to 2018, to see the effect of irrigation on reducing crop losses during the drought period. abstract: Host and parasite body size frequently scale positively (often referred to as Harrison's rule), potentially as a result of fundamental constraints on large parasite species simply being morphologically incapable of infecting small host species, or through a variety of alternative proposed mechanisms. abstract: Parasites are an important component of freshwater ecosystems due to the ways they regulate energy flow and shape community structure. abstract: Sarojini Naidu (born February 13, 1879, Hyderabad, India—died March 2, 1949, Lucknow) was a political activist, feminist, and poet. title: Path analysis of social, economic, and environmental impacts of large-scale public investment projects
abstract: This study examines the perceived social, economic, and environmental impacts of Istanbul Airport, Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge (YSS), and Northern Marmara Motorway (NMM) based on surveys with 995 residents across 25 neighborhoods. Three separate path models were developed to analyze perceived social, economic, and environmental impacts. title: When heritage becomes a burden: an evidence-based reference class of tourism stress in historic cities
abstract: Overtourism and carrying-capacity models have traditionally explained heritage-city stress through visitor volume and density. abstract: After the 1857 rebellion against colonial rule, the British Colonial government enacted Criminal Tribes Act of 1871 to control some sections of Indian society. abstract: Ecological succession is shaped by multiple processes that operate simultaneously across spatial and temporal scales. While classical succession theory generally focuses on a single trophic level within a single location, often in plants or other macroscopic organisms, recent efforts have extended this framework to microorganisms across multiple ecological dimensions. title: Hatching failure and embryo mortality in endangered populations of Eurasian Curlew ( Numenius arquata )
abstract: Hatching failure represents a significant and growing barrier to reproductive success in threatened birds and yet is often poorly understood. Populations of the Eurasian Curlew Numenius arquata in the United Kingdom and Republic of Ireland have experienced significant declines over recent decades, and low breeding productivity is a major barrier to conservation efforts. abstract: Climate change is not a distant risk but an everyday lived experience. This article examines climate change in Catalonia, Spain by focusing on daily routines, relationships, and emotions. abstract: BACKGROUND: Malaria rapid diagnosis tests (mRDTs) detecting Plasmodium falciparum histidine-rich protein 2 (Pfhrp2) are the most widely adopted diagnostic tool in malaria-endemic areas. abstract: Purpose: Bangladesh counts more than 239 million registered mobile financial service (MFS) accounts, yet registration alone says little about whether women can control and use digital money for their own purposes. In Nigeria, recurrent flooding along the River Benue has continued to disrupt socio-economic activities, including access to education. abstract: Background: Although project-based learning (PBL) is well-established in advanced medical curricula, evidence supporting its implementation in first-year undergraduate programs remains limited.Early research exposure may enhance student engagement.Objective: This study evaluated whether structured PBL in muscle physiology was associated with improvements in subject knowledge acquisition among first-year MBBS students.Methods: An observational study was conducted at a single medical institution in Tamil Nadu, India, from July to August 2023.Formal institutional ethics approval was obtained prio

title: Occurrence and concentration variability of pharmaceuticals, pesticides, and polyphenols in Nyabugogo River, Rwanda
abstract: Pharmaceuticals, pesticides, and polyphenols are increasingly detected in aquatic environments, impacting water quality and aquatic life. This study screened these contaminants in Rwanda's Nyabugogo River, analysing 45 water samples from rural, peri-urban, and urban areas using solid-phase extraction and LC-MS/MS. Fifty-seven pharmaceuticals, five pesticides, and four polyphenols were quantified, with the highest average concentrations of albendazole (960 ng/L), metalaxyl (70 ng/L), and caffeic acid (49 ng/L). abstract: Radyoaktivite, kararsız atom çekirdeğinin iyonlaştırıcı radyasyon yayarak parçalanması ve kararlı hale geçmesidir. title: Aerobic Exercise Ameliorates Osteoarthritic Chondrocyte Degradation in Osteoarthritis via Regulating E2F8/NLRP14 Signaling Pathway
abstract: Although physical activity is known to mitigate disease risks, its protective molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. E2F8, a regulator of cell cycle and metabolism, showed significant differential expression between osteoarthritis (OA) and exercise models, suggesting it may link mechanical activity to OA alleviation. In vitro, Interleukin-1 Beta (IL-1β) simulated inflammation. In vivo, OA was induced in rats via Monosodium iodoacetate (MIA) injection. title: Monthly Rhythms of Intercity Travel: A Seasonal Analysis of Population Mobility Between Chinese Cities
abstract: Abstract With the continuous improvement of China’s high-speed transportation system and the deepening of regional integration, intercity travel has become increasingly frequent and has emerged as an important field for studying spatial linkages and regional interaction among cities. Based on AMap Migration big data, we analyze the monthly rhythms and seasonal fluctuations of intercity travel throughout 2023. title: Lived multifunctionality: Indigenous perceptions of shifting cultivation landscapes in the Naga Hills of Myanmar
abstract: Shifting cultivation is frequently misrepresented in policy and environmental discourse as ecologically destructive and economically inefficient. This study examines the lived multifunctionality of shifting cultivation (jhum) landscapes in the Naga Self-Administered Zone of Myanmar, where Indigenous Naga communities depend on diverse land-use mosaics for livelihoods, cultural reproduction, and ecological resilience. Drawing on fieldwork in 42 villages across Layshi Township, we combined participatory mapping, livelihood product inventories, and community-based scoring to analyse how different

title: Modeling Logical Interdependencies: Quantifying Systemic Risk From Rule‐Governed Actions
abstract: Systemic risk in critical infrastructure is often analyzed through physical, geographic, and cyber interdependencies. Yet infrastructures are also interdependent through the governing rules that organize human action. These rule-mediated connections are a form of logical interdependency, and breakdowns in rule-governed action can create pathways through which disruption spreads. This paper develops a framework for diagnosing and quantifying this underrecognized source of systemic risk. title: Impact of climate change on the photovoltaic power potential in Sweden across 21st century
abstract: Abstract Solar photovoltaic generation strongly relies on weather conditions, which will be affected by future climate change. Traditional methods for estimating photovoltaic generation potential often overlook detailed installation factors and snow impacts, leading to inaccuracies in high-latitude areas. We assess future photovoltaic system performance in Sweden using a validated photovoltaic installation model that incorporates air temperature, radiation and snow conditions. title: Probing Triplet Photochemistry in Ru(II) Porphyrins Using Singlet Oxygen Generation and Triplet–Triplet Annihilation Upconversion
abstract: Porphyrins are known for their rich triplet-state photophysics, making them attractive platforms for light-driven applications. Compared with extensively studied Pd(II) and Pt(II) porphyrins, Ru(II) porphyrins remain less systematically explored, particularly for triplet-driven reactivity. Here, we demonstrate that a single porphyrin framework can perform complementary functions: generate singlet oxygen (1O2) and photosensitize triplet-triplet annihilation upconversion (TTA-UC). title: Portrayal of Caste and Social Identity in Contemporary Telugu Cinema: a Study of Andhra Pradesh
abstract: The treatment of caste in Telugu cinema is socially significant given its political and fan and community allegiances. The political, fan and community allegiances of the Telugu cinema make its treatment of caste socially consequential. The focus of this study is on how caste and social identity has been depicted in current Telugu cinema (from 2000 to nowadays) in the context of Andhra Pradesh. title: A photoinduced, FeX3-catalyzed, stereo- and regio-selective halofunctionalization of olefins with MXn via a radical-polar crossover reaction
abstract: The classical reaction for the halofunctionalization of olefins involves hazardous and highly toxic molecular halogens. The goal of chemists is to establish green, inherently safe, highly efficient and sustainable synthetic methods. Here, we report a green approach for the halofunctionalization of alkenes with MXn and FeX3, as well as a nucleophile at room temperature under visible-light irradiation in AcOH/CH3CN, without strong oxidants and any ligand. title: Development and Characterization of Carbon Fiber Mat‐Reinforced Shape Memory Nanocomposites for Smart Structural Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Shape memory polyurethane (SMPU) exhibits excellent shape memory behavior; however, its relatively low mechanical strength and thermal stability limit its use in demanding structural applications. In this study, carbon fiber (CF) mat‐reinforced SMPU composites containing multi‐walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) were fabricated using a solvent casting technique to investigate the combined effects of CF mat reinforcement, MWCNT incorporation, and post‐fabrication annealing on the thermal, mechanical, morphological, and shape memory properties of SMPU composites. title: Integrated Damping Solid-State Circuit Breaker for Inrush Current Suppression in DC Microgrids with Reconfigurable Voltage Sources
abstract: Solid-state circuit breakers (SSCBs) provide fast, arcless fault clearance, resulting in a longer service life compared to mechanical circuit breakers (MCBs) in DC grids. Black-start operations refers to the process of restarting a grid without an external power source, usually using the system’s internal energy storage system (ESS). SSCBs can be damaged by inrush currents during black-start operations in DC microgrids because power semiconductors have limited current-handling capability. title: Unanticipated intermediates during isopenicillin N synthase catalysis identified by time-resolved X-ray free-electron laser studies
abstract: Abstract Biosynthesis of penicillin and cephalosporin antibiotics involves the oxidation of the tripeptide δ-( l -α-aminoadipoyl)- l -cysteinyl- d -valine (ACV) to give the conformationally strained bicyclic penicillin ring system, as catalysed by the Fe(II)-dependent oxidase isopenicillin N synthase (IPNS). The structures of the precursors for the sequential β-lactam and thiazolidine ring forming steps in IPNS have remained elusive. title: Correlation between mechanical performance and structural evolution in PLA toughened with reactive polysiloxanes during accelerated aging
abstract: Polylactide (PLA) is a sustainable thermoplastic with considerable industrial potential; however, its limited durability under outdoor exposure restricts its broader use in engineering applications. This study investigates the effect of two reactive polysiloxane modifiers (MODs), denoted MOD1 and MOD2, incorporated at 1–5 wt%, on the mechanical performance and aging behavior of PLA under simulated outdoor conditions involving UV-B radiation, elevated temperature, and humidity. title: Targeting SUV39H2 exon skipping reverses resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors via transcriptional activation of p21
abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 inhibitors (CDK4/6i) are standard therapies for estrogen receptor–positive breast cancer, but their efficacy is limited by drug resistance. While dysregulation of alternative splicing has been implicated in cancer progression, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we uncover a splicing-mediated mechanism whereby exon 2 inclusion in SUV39H2 drives its overexpression in CDK4/6i-resistant breast cancer cells. Clinically, elevated exon 2 inclusion in SUV39H2 correlates with poor prognosis in patients with breast cancer. Targeting SUV39H2 with gapmer antisense

title: Liquid-Crystalline Polymer Alloy Design through Interfacial Reactions Enabled by In Situ Polymerization and Reactive Blending
abstract: Abstract Liquid-crystalline polymers (LCPs), an important class of super engineering thermoplastics, exhibit outstanding melt processability and are attractive materials for designing high-performance polymer alloys. However, the fundamental insights required to overcome macroscopic phase separation arising from the intrinsic structural disparity between liquid-crystalline and isotropic polymers, and the design guidelines built on these insights, have not yet been clearly established. title: Do planejamento tributário à gestão de créditos: os impactos do IBS e da CBS na estratégia tributária das empresas Brasileiras
abstract: A Reforma Tributária do Consumo altera não apenas a estrutura jurídica da tributação sobre bens e serviços no Brasil, mas também a lógica econômica do planejamento tributário empresarial. Com a instituição do Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (IBS) e da Contribuição Social sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), a não cumulatividade passa a operar em bases mais amplas, enquanto a apropriação, a utilização e a monetização dos créditos dependem de processos fiscais, financeiros, documentais e tecnológicos integrados. title: Sex-specific determinants of blood lead levels in Korean adults
abstract: Abstract Blood lead level (BLL) in Korea has declined but remains a public health concern because there is no safe level of exposure. We aimed to identify sex-specific determinants of BLL in Korean adults using an integrated, data-reduction approach. We analyzed data from the third cycle of Korean National Environmental Health Survey (KoNEHS, 2015–2017), a nationally representative survey of adults aged 19 years or older. A total of 3,747 participants and 123 variables were included in the final analysis. We applied categorical principal component analysis (CatPCA) to derive composite factors

title: Synergistic Interfacial Regulation by Nano‐TiO 2 and Carboxylated Cellulose Nanofibers for Multiscale Surface Stabilization of Cementitious Composites
abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, a composite‐modified cementitious system incorporating nano‐TiO 2 and carboxylated cellulose nanofibers (CCNF) was developed to unveil the synergistic mechanism between point‐like nucleation induced by nano‐TiO 2 and interface‐induced deposition regulated by CCNF, and to establish its relationship with surface stability, pore structure, and ion transport behavior. title: A compound seismic screening index for global nuclear power plant sites combining probabilistic rock-PGA hazard with vs30-based site conditions
abstract: Abstract Seismic safety assessment of nuclear power plant (NPP) sites depends critically on the simultaneous characterisation of ground motion intensity and the capacity of the local soil to amplify that motion. While global probabilistic seismic hazard models and global shear-wave velocity (Vs30) compilations are now available, no prior study has combined these two open global datasets into a single, reproducible screening metric spanning the multi-country reactor-unit inventory. title: Sustainable energy transition options for Russia
abstract: Following the Paris Agreement, one way to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and minimise the consequences of climate change is to pursue the goal of a sustainable energy supply by renewable energy sources. This study explores transition pathways towards sustainable energy system in the regions of Russia. Potential scenarios are presented in the power, heat, transport, and industry sectors. title: Effects on selected fecal bacterial populations and safety assessment of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus LRa05
abstract: Abstract This study aimed to investigate the effects of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus LRa05 on fecal bacterial populations and evaluate its safety profile. First, the effects of LRa05 on selected fecal bacterial populations were evaluated in a rodent model. Second, safety assessments were conducted through genetic stability testing, acute oral toxicity test in male and female mice and rats, and teratogenicity study. title: CRISPR-enhanced microalgae for carbon sequestration and carotenoid production: opportunities and fundamental constraints
abstract: Microalgae represent a promising biological platform for CO2 sequestration and the sustainable production of high-value metabolites, particularly carotenoids such as lutein and astaxanthin. However, industrial performance remains constrained by low carbon conversion efficiency, reduced photosynthetic performance, and competing metabolic fluxes that limit product yield. The emergence of CRISPR/Cas-based genome engineering has enabled precise and multiplexed modulation of microalgal metabolic networks, offering new opportunities to overcome these limitations. title: Pyrolysis temperature controls the accessible pore volume and capric acid encapsulation efficiency of coconut shell biochar
abstract: Waste-derived biochar is a low-cost scaffold for shape-stabilized phase change materials (PCMs), yet how pyrolysis temperature governs the pore volume a molten PCM can reach remains unresolved. Here we decouple surface area from pore accessibility by preparing ZnCl 2 -activated coconut shell biochars at 550, 700, 850 and 1000 °C under an identical protocol and impregnating them with capric acid. title: Fabrication of Bifunctional UHMWPE Composites With Self‐Lubricating and Self‐Repairing Capabilities via Core‐Shell MSNs ‐ PFPE @ PEW Particles
abstract: ABSTRACT In mechanical systems, the energy dissipation and wear caused by friction usually lead to the failure of materials during their service life, thereby driving the demand for polymer composite materials with both tribological properties and self‐repairing capabilities. Studying polymer composites with self‐lubrication and self‐repairing functions is an effective approach. title: Poisoned arrows in the Danish Early Mesolithic: Testing lithic ballistic morphometrics against faunal and archaeobotanical data
abstract: Throughout human deep history, lithic tool components became periodically very small. Such microlithic tools are the signature artefacts of the European Mesolithic in general, and the iconic Danish Mesolithic in particular. Sandwiched between the end of the Pleistocene and the emergence of agricultural lifeways, the Danish Mesolithic is characterised by marked changes in microlith design from lanceolates to geometrics and finally to transversal forms with wide front edges. title: Identification and Characterization of a Previously Uncharacterized Metagenome-Derived Chitinase and Its Application in N -Acetyl- d -Glucosamine Production from Crayfish Shell Waste
abstract: Abstract The generation of agricultural and food-processing byproducts has increased rapidly, highlighting the importance of their high-value utilization. In this study, a putative chitinase gene was identified from a metagenome-assembled genome. The enzyme plays a key role in chitin hydrolysis and was heterologously expressed in Escherichia coli as a recombinant protein with a molecular weight of approximately 39.2 kDa. title: Causal inference in conservation policy: Evaluating the effects of Protected Areas on deforestation and well-being in the Peruvian Amazon
abstract: The Peruvian Amazon, one of the most biodiverse regions on Earth, is under increasing pressure from deforestation, threatening both ecological wealth and local livelihoods. Protected Areas (PAs) have emerged as one of the main conservation strategies; however, questions remain regarding their effectiveness in reducing deforestation and their socioeconomic impact. This study evaluates the effects of PAs, their Buffer Zones (BZs), and Regional Conservation Areas (RCAs) on deforestation and household welfare between 2001 and 2023. title: Conservation genetics of the spotted bat: Insights from ancient, historical, and modern samples
abstract: Spotted bats (Euderma maculatum) are cryptic (nocturnal, volant, and roost solitarily) and thus their biology remains largely undescribed. Only 35 specimens were known to science before the mid-1960s. Hence, they are ideal candidates for genetic studies to uncover population genetic diversity and structure, and thereby inform conservation. title: Validity of STEM-Based IPAS E-Worksheets for Elementary School Students
abstract: Purpose of the study: This study aimed to determine the validity of a STEM-based Electronic Student Worksheet for elementary school science learning (IPAS) based on material suitability, language clarity and readability, display and navigation quality, and the integration of Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics components. Methodology: This study employed a research and development approach focusing on the expert validation stage. title: Revision of Neanderthal Activity Zones at Kůlna Cave: Use-Wear Analysis of the Micoquian Lithic Industry
abstract: Abstract Investigating the spatial organisation of Neanderthal sites offers critical insights into their behavioural patterns, adaptive strategies, and site use. Studying how different lithic tools are organised in space and linked to specific functions is therefore essential. Kůlna Cave provides evidence of multiple occupation areas characterised by distinct activity patterns, making it a particularly suitable Neanderthal site for investigating spatial organisation and testing related hypotheses. title: Defining Typical Family Agricultural Holdings Engaged in Milk Production Through Cluster Analysis in Croatia
abstract: This study investigates the dairy sector in the Republic of Croatia, which is characterized by pronounced structural heterogeneity. On the one hand, there are highly productive farms comparable to the leading milk producers in the European Union, and numerous small and medium-sized farms that face the challenges of maintaining competitiveness and further development. In order to design effective development and sectoral policies, it is necessary to identify and distinguish the dominant types of dairy farms and their specific development needs. title: First records of Gigaspermum mouretii Corb. and Oedipodiella australis (Wager & Dixon) Dixon (Gigaspermaceae) from Saudi Arabia, with biogeographic implications
abstract: This study documents the first records of the moss family Gigaspermaceae in Saudi Arabia. Two taxa were discovered in the southern and western highlands: Gigaspermum mouretii Corb., recorded from several granite slopes in Al Bahah and Mecca provinces, and Oedipodiella australis (Wager and Dixon) Dixon, found at multiple localities in the Asir Mountains. The material of G. mouretii is unequivocally paroicous and fertile, with sessile sporophytes bearing giant spores, thereby providing clear morphological support for its separation from G. repens. title: Molecular evidence of a dominant multidrug resistant Acinetobacter baumannii lineage in a tertiary hospital in northern Peru
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Acinetobacter baumannii is a major nosocomial pathogen because of its genomic plasticity and capacity to acquire multidrug resistance (MDR), particularly resistance to carbapenems. The World Health Organization classifies carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii as a critical-priority pathogen. Molecular epidemiological data from Latin America remain limited, especially for northern Peru. title: Ice nucleation by kaolinite: Morphology shapes the size dependence of ice nucleation active sites on dust particles
abstract: Mineral dusts are the most important type of ice-nucleating particles and play a key role in cloud formation and climate. Their activity is commonly assumed to scale with particle surface area, yet whether this assumption holds across particle sizes remains unverified. Here, we quantify size-dependent ice nucleation activity using compositionally pure, size-segregated kaolinite (KGa-1b). title: Trophic position structures physiological trade-offs between metabolic and detoxification pathways in sympatric passerines
abstract: Abstract Resource use links ecological context to organismal performance, yet whether dietary breadth or trophic position is more closely associated with physiological state in wild birds remains unclear. We used a natural trophic gradient in a sympatric passerine assemblage to test whether trophic position and isotopic niche breadth are associated with integrated physiological phenotypes. We studied three co-occurring passerine species in central Chile spanning a trophic spectrum (granivorous, omnivorous, insectivorous). title: The influence of lakes and reservoirs on estimated flood peaks at hourly vs. daily timescale in the Alps
abstract: Abstract. Water bodies such as lakes and reservoirs can play a crucial role in reducing flood peaks both on daily and hourly timescales. While the effect of water bodies on flood peaks at different time resolutions has been demonstrated in the past, it remains unclear how they affect the ratio between daily and hourly peaks. title: Stage-specific shifts in bacterial and fungal amplicon profiles of garlic bulbs during cold storage
abstract: Garlic bulbs can remain externally intact while microbial and tissue changes develop during cold storage, so endpoint inspection may miss distinct intermediate states. We characterized cold-stored garlic across four storage stages by combining bacterial 16S rRNA gene and fungal internal transcribed spacer (ITS) amplicon sequencing with culture, quantitative PCR (qPCR), photography, and cryo-scanning electron microscopy. title: Environmental Footprint of Kerala’s Coir Processing Transitions
abstract: This article examines the historical transition of Kerala’s coir industry from traditional retting practices to mechanized production, highlighting the shifting burdens on ecosystems and workers. Retting once imposed severe localized pollution on aquatic systems, with high biochemical oxygen demand and phenolic loading creating anoxic conditions, while mechanization reduced reliance on water bodies but introduced energy intensity, synthetic effluents, and hazardous occupational exposures. title: Breaking water-structure constraints by Hofmeister effects in interfacial polymerization for polyamide membranes
abstract: Abstract Hydration critically governs the physicochemical behavior of solutes in both the aqueous bulk and interfacial environments. As typical chaotropic Hofmeister ions, weakly hydrated anions (WHAs) can reshape hydration structures and accumulate at water–hydrophobe interfaces. Notably, WHAs paradoxically suppress the solubility of certain small-molecule monomers in water while enhancing that of chemically analogous polymers. title: Gross and Histopathological Charactersation of Pulmonary Abscessation due to Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli in a Collared Mangabey (Cercocebus torquatus): A Case Report
abstract: Bacterial lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) can result in severe and fatal diseases in non-human primates (NHPs), and the disease process of pulmonary abscessation in the Collared Mangabey (Cercocebus torquatus), an endangered West and Central African cercopithecid, has been underreported. A gross and histopathological evaluation of a 12-year-old captive female C. torquatus that had a 14-month history of intermittent coughing and that had a polymicrobial co-infection with S. aureus and E. coli is presented. title: Mechanical Irreversibility and Strength Overcompensation in a Gypsum Dehydration–Rehydration Cycle
abstract: Abstract Dehydration–rehydration reactions of hydrous minerals modify rock strength, fluid transport, and deformation in reactive geological environments. Although dehydration‐induced weakening is widely studied, the mechanical consequences of subsequent rehydration remain poorly constrained. We combine triaxial compression tests with microstructural and pore‐network analyses of original gypsum, fully dehydrated anhydrite, and rehydrated gypsum.
