title: Protected-area-based nature-based governance and green-blue infrastructure-to-built conversion: spatial regression discontinuity evidence from Kinmen National Park, Taiwan
abstract: Nature-based solutions (NbS) and green-blue infrastructure (GBI) are increasingly promoted for sustainable built environments, yet boundary-based evidence on specific land-conversion mechanisms remains limited. This study evaluates Kinmen National Park, Taiwan, using a spatial regression discontinuity design (Spatial RDD) on 30 m grid cells for 2014–2024. title: Ultraconserved element phylogenomics reveals novel insights into the historical biogeography of euophryine jumping spiders (Araneae: Salticidae)
abstract: The Euophryini is one of the largest tribes of jumping spiders (Salticidae), with diverse morphology, ecology and behaviour, and is an important focus of systematic and evolutionary studies of jumping spiders. Notably, it is the only salticid tribe that has diversified nearly equally across both the Old and New Worlds, making its historical biogeography particularly intriguing. However, understanding its biogeography has been challenging without the application of phylogeny-based biogeographical analytical approaches. title: Morphofunctional indices and ontogeny of long bones of the limbs in the frogs
abstract: Anuran limbs offer a valuable model for exploring how selective pressures, developmental constraints, and morphological evolution interact. While previous research has largely focused on total limb length, little is known about ontogenetic changes in the proportions of individual limb bones. This study introduces a novel approach using morphofunctional indices to investigate the functional roles of frog limbs, linking morphology to habitat use and locomotion. title: Petrographic and magnetic fabric evidence for magmatic emplacement and hydrothermal alteration in the Shadan Au porphyry deposit, Eastern Iran
abstract: Magmatic processes and subsequent hydrothermal alterations within porphyry deposits are well-documented through the analysis of mineral chemistry and the magnetic fabrics of their host intrusions. This study integrates structurs, petrography, mineral chemistry, and anisotropy of magnetic susceptibility (AMS) data to investigate the evolution of magmatic and hydrothermal fabrics in the Shadan porphyry Au-rich deposit, located in northeastern Iran. Fresh quartz monzodioritic intrusions exhibit primary magmatic fabrics characterized by oblate AMS ellipsoids, predominantly aligned with magnetite.

title: Corrosion Resistance of Boronized Carbon Steel in a Galinstan–Refrigerant Two-Phase Agitated System
abstract: Abstract This study experimentally evaluates, for the first time, the corrosion resistance of boronized carbon steel in environments containing liquid Galinstan (GaInSn) and selected organic refrigerants (n-pentane and R1233zd(E)) at 150 °C for up to 80 days. title: Gut microbiomes of the little free-tailed bat ( Mops pumilus ) show high prevalence of potential bacterial pathogens but limited responses to land cover
abstract: Land cover change is a threat to wildlife globally. It may also impact the gut microbiome harbored by wildlife, with implications for their health, conservation, and One Health more broadly. title: A Visual Analysis of the Uneven Contribution Towards Sustainable Climate Action: An Analysis of United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 13
abstract: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita is a measure of a country's economic capacity. Hence, the correlation between GDP pc and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in the present study, Sustainable Development Goal 13 (SDG 13), provides a clear indication of the extent to which individual countries comply with the goal. title: Rapid protamine evolution suppresses meiotic drive in Drosophila
abstract: Many animal species replace histones with protamines during spermatogenesis. Although essential for sperm function, protamines evolve rapidly for reasons that remain unknown. Using in vivo gene replacement, we examined the causes and consequences of the rapid evolution of Mst77F , a protamine essential for male fertility in Drosophila melanogaster ( D. melanogaster ). title: Genomic diversity, population structure, and relatedness of critically endangered Philippine eagles under conservation management
abstract: The critically endangered Philippine eagle ( Pithecophaga jefferyi ) faces severe threats to its population from habitat loss, naturally slow reproduction cycles, and human encroachment. Thus, 38 years ago, the Philippine Eagle Foundation (PEF) was established for the conservation of the endangered Philippine eagle and its rainforest habitat. title: The scientific consensus on the beauty of snowflakes: A case study for the aesthetics of science
abstract: Philosophers of science interested in aesthetics have tended to privilege the epistemic and cognitive dimensions of science. Historians of science interested in aesthetics have largely focused on the aesthetics of scientific images and artefacts. Productive exchanges between these traditions of scholarship have been few and far between. title: Prediction of Self‐Starting of a Vertical Axis Wind Turbine Using Static Torque
abstract: ABSTRACT The ability of vertical axis wind turbines (VAWTs) to self‐start is critical to their performance. There is disagreement in the literature over some of the factors affecting their self‐starting ability and there is very limited information on how the starting azimuthal angle affects self‐starting. We present a series of wind tunnel experiments in which we measure the static torque and self‐starting of a three‐blade VAWT for a range of initial azimuthal angles, which we find to have a very strong effect on the ability to self‐start. title: Distinct Genetic Determinants of Plasma Inflammatory Proteins in Tanzanian and Dutch Populations
abstract: Understanding the genetic regulation of plasma inflammatory proteins is essential for bridging the gap between genetics and disease biology. While studies in European populations have highlighted significant genetic influences on inflammatory protein levels, African populations remain underrepresented in immunogenetic research. Here, we compare the genetic determinants of 72 inflammatory proteins quantified using the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel in two cohorts from the Human Functional Genomics Project. title: The RLR-MAVS-IRF3 axis activates the IFN pathway to restrict Tonate virus (TONV) infection
abstract: Tonate virus (TONV) is a neglected mosquito-borne alphavirus of the Venezuelan equine encephalitis complex associated with febrile illness, encephalitis, and fetal central nervous system abnormalities. Yet, host pathways that sense TONV infection and restrict its replication remain poorly defined. Here, we investigated the interaction between TONV and the type I interferon (IFN-I) system in human T98G and A549 cells. title: The complete mitochondrial genomes of Colias lada and Colias wanda (Lepidoptera: Pieridae: Coliadinae) and their phylogenetic analyses
abstract: The complete mitochondrial genomes of two Qinghai-Tibet Plateau butterflies, Colias lada and C. wanda, were assembled from next-generation sequencing data, measuring 15,078 bp and 15,144 bp. Both contain 13 PCGs, 22 tRNAs, 2 rRNAs and one control region. Phylogenetic trees based on the 13 PCGs and 2 rRNAs using ML and BI methods, with high support values, show that C. wanda, C. lada and C. sifanica share a recent common ancestor, and reconstruct the relationships among the Coliadinae genera.

title: γ‐Ray Controlled Topological Evolution of Binders for Stable and Activated Li─S Battery Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT γ‐ray irradiation facilitates controllable, clean, and reagent‐free cross‐linking of polymer networks without side reactions. Leveraging these merits, we precisely tune the irradiation dose to engineer a three‐dimensional (3D) poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) binder network for lithium‐sulfur (Li─S) batteries. title: Streptomyces chodovensis sp. nov.: a novel candidate for plant growth-promoting actinomycete from bare soil developing on Miocene lacustrine sediment of the Sokolov Coal Basin, Czech Republic
abstract: Abstract A novel actinomycete, designated as BCCO 10_0861 T , was isolated from overburden Miocene clay sediments undergoing primary succession in Northwest Czechia and characterized by the polyphasic approach. title: Field evaluation of Bacillus -based consortium biofertilizer for rhizosphere zinc availability, grain biofortification and paddy yield
abstract: The zinc (Zn) deficiency in submerged rice limits productivity and nutritional quality. This study evaluated the potential of zinc-solubilizing plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) to enhance Zn availability and uptake in rice under submerged conditions. Field experiments were conducted over two years using five Bacillus-based biofertilizer formulations: three single-strain inoculants (B. megaterium AN24 as BF-1, B. aryabhattai AN30 as BF-2, B. megaterium AN31 as BF-3) and two combined formulations (B. megaterium AN24 + B. aryabhattai AN30 as BF-4, B. megaterium AN24 + B. megaterium AN3

title: A smart photothermal microneedle system for dual-targeted therapy of osteoarthritis via MMPs inhibition
abstract: Temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ-OA) causes chronic pain, cartilage degeneration and pathological neurovascular remodeling, yet effective local therapies remain limited. Here we develop a minimally invasive near-infrared (NIR)-responsive microneedle system (SFZICC MNs) that integrates cryptochlorogenic acid (CCA)- and carbon quantum dot-loaded ZIF-8 nanoparticles within a methacrylated silk fibroin hydrogel. title: Irrigation-driven modulation of growth and stress resilience in cork oak (Quercus suber L.) seedlings in nursery environments
abstract: Cork oak (Quercus suber L.) is a keystone species of Mediterranean forestry, increasingly threatened by prolonged droughts and anthropogenic pressures. Improving nursery seedling quality is therefore essential for successful reforestation. title: DNA Barcoding Validation of Medicinal Ipomoea Species from the Morning Glory Family
abstract: The growing consumption of herbal products has been accompanied by a concerning increase in the use of adulterants during production, which could affect the quality of traditional herbal medicine. DNA barcoding is a powerful method for accurately identifying plants at various taxonomic levels, and for authenticating medicinal plants. title: Structural basis of antigenic drift in FMDV O/Cathay topotype variants revealed by porcine-derived single B-cell neutralizing antibodies
abstract: The porcinophilic O/Cathay topotype variants of foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV) continuously accumulated mutations over time and produced antigenic drift, leading to diminished serum neutralization and compromised vaccine efficacy. However, the structural basis underlying this divergence remains poorly defined. title: Comparative biomass carbon storage, CO2 mitigation potential and green economy valuation of polyculture and monoculture plantations under the Jan Van Yojna social forestry scheme in semi-humid tropical Jharkhand India
abstract: Tropical forest plantations under community-based schemes represent an underexplored yet critical nexus between land-use policy, climate change mitigation, and green economy valuation. abstract: The growing demand for sustainable bioinputs has driven the production of microbial biosurfactants from low-cost substrates. This study evaluated the biosurfactant production by the strain Bacillus licheniformis UCP 1014 utilizing crude glycerol and corn steep liquor as agroindustrial as substrates, using Rotatable Central Composite Design (RCCD). title: Heavy metal exposures and constipation among United States adults
abstract: Constipation is a common gastrointestinal disorder that can substantially impair quality of life. Environmental exposure to heavy metals has been implicated in gastrointestinal dysfunction; however, population-based evidence regarding their associations with constipation remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of blood lead, mercury, and cadmium levels with constipation among US adults. title: Comparative phytochemical, antibacterial, in-silico molecular docking and ADMET analysis of Cinnamomum camphora and Cinnamomum tamala ethanolic leaf extracts against Aeromonas salmonicida
abstract: The rapid growth of aquaculture has led to the prevalence of infectious diseases and antibiotic resistance. Therefore, new sustainable strategies are required to prevent this situation from growing. The present study evaluated the effect of ethanolic leaf extracts of Cinnamomum tamala (CTE) and Cinnamomum camphora (CCE) against Aeromonas salmonicida . title: Sources, Transmission, and Control of Salmonella in Vertically Integrated Broiler Chicken Production: Farm, Hatchery, and Processing Plant
abstract: Salmonella remains one of the most important foodborne pathogens associated with poultry products, despite substantial progress in processing hygiene and antimicrobial interventions. This review critically examines the sources, transmission routes, and control strategies for Salmonella in vertically integrated broiler production systems. Attention is given to contamination originating from breeder flocks, hatcheries, feed, water, litter, grow-out farms, transport, processing environments, and finished products. title: Spatiotemporal variations in power grid carbon intensity and their impact on steel fiber-reinforced concrete emissions
abstract: China's energy transition has created unprecedented spatiotemporal heterogeneity in power grid carbon intensity, yet conventional life cycle assessment methodologies using national averages potentially misrepresent emissions for electricity-intensive products. This study develops a spatiotemporally explicit framework using steel fiber production to examine these impacts. Analysis of 31 provinces reveals 24-fold spatial variation (0.04-0.97 kg CO₂e/kWh), with steel fiber emissions ranging from 0.72-4.35 kg CO₂e/kg. title: Upcycling Industrial Lignin Into Cationic Hydrogels With Potential for Sustainable Plant Protection
abstract: Bio-based antimicrobial materials are increasingly explored as sustainable alternatives for plant pathogen control. Here, we report a circular economy approach in which industrial kraft lignin was upcycled into cationic lignin (CL) and physically embedded within chitosan-genipin (CH-GPN) hydrogels to form CH-GPN-CL. title: Investigating the association between weather variables and Aedes albopictus abundance in Windsor, Ontario
abstract: Aedes albopictus (Diptera: Culicidae) is notorious for transmitting several pathogens of public health importance. The mosquito has also displayed a great capacity for dispersal. Within the last 30 years, the mosquito has been documented on every continent except for Antarctica. The species was first noted in Canada in 2016 in Windsor-Essex, Ontario. Since then, Ae. albopictus has been found every subsequent year in active surveillance trapping (2017-2023). title: Reduction of off-flavour formation and improved α-oligoglucoside utilization enable use of Saccharomyces eubayanus as a novel lager brewing yeast
abstract: Lager beer, made by fermentation of barley malt using the hybrid yeast Saccharomyces pastorianus, is extremely popular worldwide. The low genetic variation of S. pastorianus strains limits the scope of development for novel lager beer types. The wild ancestor Saccharomyces eubayanus has potential for lager brewing, but its application is constrained by formation of phenolic off-flavours (POF+ phenotype) and limited uptake of the wort α-oligoglucosides maltose and maltotriose. title: Hidden in the deadwood: Taxonomically curated barcode library reveals deep genetic divergence in Eurasian saproxylic beetles
abstract: Abstract Saproxylic beetles are a highly diverse group of tree‐associated insects that play key roles in forest ecosystem functioning, comprising both rare primeval relicts and taxa of economic importance in timber production. Morphological identification of these beetles remains challenging due to high similarity among species‐rich taxa and a number of taxonomic specialists. title: A pH-stimulated responsive micro-drug delivery system loaded with gastrodin that improves type 2 diabetes
abstract: Abstract Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a rapidly increasing global metabolic disease. The development of effective oral hypoglycemic agents, primarily derived from natural compounds, remains a significant challenge. In this study, we developed pH-responsive sodium alginate (SA) microspheres combined with low methoxy pectin (LMP) that are loaded with gastrodin (Gas) (denoted as Gas@MPs) and successfully delivered Gas to the gut for controlled release. title: Agroecological desert truffle cultivation promotes soil conservation and functionality in semi-arid Mediterranean areas
abstract: Soil degradation driven by agricultural intensification and land abandonment represents a major challenge in dryland regions worldwide, where soils with low organic matter and structural stability are highly vulnerable to erosion, nutrient depletion and loss of biological functionality. The cultivation of desert truffles ( Terfezia claveryi Chatin), involving an ectendomycorrhizal symbiosis with Helianthemum almeriense Pau and relying on low input agroecological management, has been proposed as a sustainable alternative for soil conservation. abstract: OBJECTIVE: To determine whether resting energy expenditure (REE) differs between patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), progressive muscular atrophy (PMA), and primary lateral sclerosis (PLS). METHODS: Patients with ALS, PMA, and PLS were enrolled between 2017 and 2021 in a prospective cross-sectional study. REE was measured by indirect calorimetry. abstract: İklim değişikliği, dünyanın pek çok bölgesinde ekstrem doğa olaylarının sıklığını ve şiddetini arttırarak, her geçen gün daha da kritik bir sorun haline gelmektedir. title: The Symbolic World: A Brief Analysis of Simulacra in White Noise
abstract: This paper takes Baudrillard’s theory of simulacra and hyperreality as its core framework to analyze White Noise, a classic of postmodern literature by Don DeLillo, aiming to reveal how simulacra permeate and reshape the lifestyle and individual cognition of postmodern society as depicted in the novel. White Noise presents a world of simulacra dominated by symbols, where the real is replaced by simulacra and individuals lose themselves in the carnival of symbols, and in doing so, they forfeit their subjectivity and genuine emotional connections.

abstract: Naringenin is a bioactive flavonoid with reported anti-bacterial and cytotoxic properties; however, its biomedical applicability is limited by poor aqueous solubility and restricted bioavailability. In this study, chitosan-based polymeric nanoparticles loaded with naringenin (Chito-NPs/NAR-EtOH) were designed as a biocompatible delivery platform to enhance NAR-ETOH dispersion and biological performance. abstract: This study examined error patterns in the four fundamental operations as predictors of mathematical problem-solving performance among Grade 6 learners at Portlamon Elementary School, Division of Surigao del Sur, as a basis for developing a targeted mathematics intervention program. A quantitative predictive-correlational research design was employed involving 31 Grade 6 learners with complete and valid responses. title: Postfire soil convergence toward an unburned reference varies with fire severity and soil depth
abstract: Abstract Background Wildfire effects on soil can differ among soil properties, soil depths, and fire-severity classes, yet their longer-term trajectories remain poorly resolved in subtropical pine plantations. We evaluated temporal convergence of burned soils toward an unburned reference following an April 2022 wildfire in a Pinus massoniana plantation in central China. title: Low Threshold Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Lasers Based on CsPbI 3 Thin Films
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal halide perovskites are attractive gain media for compact coherent light sources. Although the all‐inorganic CsPbI 3 is a particularly promising representative, low‐threshold laser operation remains challenging in CsPbI 3 thin films due to phase instability and difficulties in preparing high‐quality thin films within low‐loss optical resonators. title: ‘Is we land’: The 30-year battle of the indigenous Amerindian village of Chinese Landing against an outside gold miner in Northwest Guyana, South America
abstract: The small Indigenous Carib village of Chinese Landing located in Guyana has held legal land title since 1976. The Caribs were famed for their gold mining and metallurgy before European arrival, and gold mining remains integral to their identity and livelihoods. Although Chinese Landing is unusual in some respects, in general its struggle to preserve and implement its rights since 1995 is typical of the 200+ government-recognised Amerindian communities in Guyana. abstract: Abstract The Raman spectrum of lawsonite is characterized in situ at high temperatures through its dehydration temperature under vacuum. abstract: Bauxite residue (red mud), a highly alkaline byproduct of the Bayer alumina process, poses major environmental and geotechnical challenges owing to its fine particle size, residual caustic content, and long-term storage risks. This study proposes an integrated centrifuge-assisted framework for sustainable bauxite residue management by combining alkaline-conditioned flocculant-assisted centrifugation with potential caustic liquor recovery under intensified high-G consolidation. title: Limited global awareness of invasive alien species and little support for their management
abstract: Invasive alien species (IAS) are one of the main drivers of global change and can cause a wide range of negative ecological and social impacts. Addressing these impacts requires management actions, which can fail to be effective when not supported by the public. Here, we conducted the first global survey on people's awareness and perceptions of IAS and support for their management. Our results revealed low public awareness and understanding of biological invasions, and suggest that these are mainly influenced by people's sociodemographic status rather than the social-ecological contexts. title: Future in- and out-of-state air pollutant emissions under decarbonization pathways for Massachusetts
abstract: Many U.S. states have adopted the goal of achieving carbon neutrality in the coming decades. title: Mechanisms of Sensitisation and Development of Hand Allergic Dermatitis Induced by Occupational Allergens
abstract: Introduction: Due to the frequent exposure to chemical, biological and physical agents, occupational allergic dermatitis of the hands is a major health issue. Various types of dermatitis can present with the same symptoms. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the immunopathogenesis processes that lead to occupational allergic hand dermatitis and to diagnose such conditions. abstract: INTRODUCTION: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is an emerging alternative for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) who are unsuitable for long-term oral anticoagulants (OACs). However, its efficacy and safety relative to OACs remain uncertain. abstract: Abstract Insecticides targeting nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) are used because of their high neuroactive efficacy. title: FKS1/2-variant independent mechanisms underlying the emergence of resistance in echinocandin-refractory Candida auris infections
abstract: The emerging fungus Candida auris is a drug resistant global public health threat and WHO critical priority pathogen. Recommended first-line invasive candidiasis treatment is echinocandin monotherapy, but C. auris can develop on-treatment resistance via FKS1/2 gene mutations and additional, previously unexplained mechanisms. To better understand echinocandin failure in C. auris, we sequenced the genomes of echinocandin refractory FKS1/2 wild-type C. auris serial isolates from two critically unwell patients in London, UK. Their three-dimensional structures exhibit high complementarity with target proteins, via a multimodal combination of hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, electrostatic interactions, and van der Waals interactions. abstract: Abstract Fractional nonlinear evolution equations serve as a fundamental model to capture complex phenomena with memory effects, anomalous dispersion and long-range interaction. title: Hierarchical Density-Based Cluster Analysis for Fault Segment Detection: A Case Study of the 2009 M w 6.1 L’ Aquila Earthquake (Central Italy)
abstract: Identifying seismogenic faults, their geometries, and associated slip rates is essential for assessing seismic hazard estimates. During earthquake sequences, complex fault systems are often activated, involving the rupture of multiple segments. Identifying these fault segments remains a challenging task. This study proposes a quantitative, statistically based workflow using a cluster analysis to identify the number and dimensions of fault segments based on earthquake hypocenter distributions, an approach particularly suitable for aftershock sequences. abstract: ABSTRACT Metal halide perovskites offer a promising pathway toward solution‐processable monolithic lasers. In the pursuit of direct electrical pumping, optical excitation is widely employed as the primary route for investigating the gain potential at the device level. However, there is a severe timescale mismatch between ultrafast optical pulses and slower electrical injection, with optical pumping masking the massive electrical penalties. abstract: BACKGROUND: Planetary health is an increasingly important transdisciplinary approach in nursing because it links human health and equity to the integrity of Earth's natural systems. Climate change is a major component of planetary health, but it is not synonymous with the broader approach, which also encompasses biodiversity loss, pollution, resource pressures, environmental sustainability, and the transformation of health systems. abstract: Acacia species are widespread invasive plants in Mediterranean ecosystems, including in central Portugal, where they promote significant negative impacts. These species exhibit vigorous regeneration strategies, with seed germination being facilitated by scarification, which may be achieved with high temperatures during fires, and passage through animals’ digestive tracts. We conducted feeding trials with captive domestic goats ( Capra hircus ), red deer ( Cervus elaphus ) and wild boar ( Sus scrofa ) to evaluate the potential of these ungulates to disperse or predate Acacia seeds. abstract: Genetically encoded bioluminescent calcium indicators enable excitation-free imaging of Ca2+ dynamics with low background and without excitation-associated photobleaching. However, many exhibit lower dynamic ranges than their fluorescent counterparts, motivating the development of new sensor configurations, particularly for imaging in the red optical window, where tissue absorption and scattering are reduced. title: Collective future thinking over the Russia-Ukraine war: Cross-national perspectives from Poland and Türkiye
abstract: Collective future thinking involves individuals’ imagining the future of the group they feel they belong to. In the present study, we examine how individuals from Türkiye and Poland, two countries with different sociocultural and geopolitical contexts, simulate the future of their own country and that of Russia and Ukraine in the context of the Russia-Ukraine War. Participants ( N = 152) reported two future events that they expected to occur in Russia, Ukraine, and their own countries. title: Accelerating the Elimination of Open Defecation by 2030: Deployment of Locally-adapted Ventilated Improved Pit Latrine Model in Resource-constrained Settings
abstract: In 2015, the United Nations adopted the elimination of open defecation as Sustainable Development Goal 6.2. Though modest progress has been achieved, about 673 million people still practise open defecation, prompting concerns on how to overcome these challenges and accelerate actions to meet the target. This study aims to proffer solutions to some of these challenges and contribute in accelerating actions to meet the target by proposing a new latrine model. title: Bioinspired lamination of mushroom-derived submicron sheets for sustainable and recyclable leather alternatives
abstract: As part of the global effort to replace petroleum-based materials with sustainable alternatives, there is growing interest in enhancing the toughness of biological materials for durable textile applications. Functional composites derived from renewable sources, such as fungal hyphae, have attracted widespread attention. However, mushrooms remain comparatively underexplored, despite their rich natural polysaccharide content and favorable processability. abstract: INTRODUCTION: Uveal melanoma is a rare but aggressive malignancy, predominantly affecting the choroid. This study is the first retrospective review performed on adult choroidal melanoma patients treated with Ruthenium-106 plaque brachytherapy in Queensland. METHOD: The study period was November 2020 to January 2025, where patient, tumour, and treatment factors, as well as local control, salvage treatments, radiation retinopathy, and visual acuity were assessed at 6, 12, 24, and 36 months post-treatment. title: Fiscal Policy, Institutional Quality, and Economic Growth in West African Countries
abstract: This research paper will aim at investigating the interactions between fiscal policies, institutional quality and macroeconomic growth performance in West African countries for the period 2000 2024. This paper will employ the two-step system GMM estimation technique in handling issues concerning growth persistency, individual heterogeneity, simultaneity and endogeneity in the case of institutional, fiscal policy and growth relationship. title: Jesus Among Us with His Wounds: A Qualitative Theological Analysis of the Synodal Church in Asia
abstract: Background: Contemporary discussions of synodality frequently emphasize participation, discernment, governance, and ecclesial structures, while the Christological foundation that gives synodality its inner form is less often made explicit. Objective: This study examines how the wounded and risen humanity of Christ functions as a theological foundation for synodal life and how that foundation can be translated into priorities for the Church in Asia. title: Optimization, microstructure, and durability of sawdust ash concrete modified with Conplast SP430 superplasticizer
abstract: The use of sawdust ash (SDA) as a supplementary cementitious material offers an opportunity to valorize biomass waste and reduce dependence on Portland cement, but its incorporation can affect workability, strength development and durability. This study investigates the combined effects of SDA replacement and Conplast SP430 dosage on the fresh, hardened and durability performance of concrete. SDA replacement levels of 0–40% and Conplast dosages of 0–7.6 L/m 3 were investigated, followed by microstructural and elemental characterization of the resulting concrete using BSE-SEM and EDS. title: Standard Reference Material (SRM®) 1950 metabolites in frozen human plasma—use, impact, lessons learned, and future perspectives
abstract: In 2011, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), in collaboration with the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) at the National Institutes of Health (NIH), issued Standard Reference Material (SRM)® 1950 Metabolites in Frozen Human Plasma to support metabolomics measurements. This critical review traces the development of SRM 1950 and assesses its use and impact over the past 15 years. title: Amixicile loaded polyvinyl alcohol and pullulan composite film for localized periodontal treatment
abstract: Periodontal diseases are progressively gaining attention and hence need to be addressed effectively. The current research work aimed to develop film formulation of amixicile using pullulan and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) to treat periodontitis. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of amixicile against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Candida albicans was investigated. Films were prepared by solvent casting method, adopting central composite design. abstract: A novel series of bis(6-ethyl-4-hydroxy-2 H -chromen-2-one) derivatives 7a–d featuring para-halogenated (F, Cl, Br, I) phenylmethine linkers were synthesized and evaluated as dual acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and monoamine oxidase-B (MAO-B) inhibitors for potential Alzheimer's disease therapy. title: Effect on mechanical properties, corrosion behaviour and fracture behaviour of FSWed AA 6061-T6 and AA 2024-T3 by using different pin profiles
abstract: Friction Stir Welding (FSW) is widely validated as a solid-state joining process that has gained significant attention for the welding of aluminum alloys in aerospace and automotive applications. In this study, the effect of Tool Pin Profiles (TPP)—Taper Threaded (TTPP), Square (SPP), and Cylindrical Threaded (CTPP)—on the flow of material, mechanical properties, corrosion properties and microstructure of dissimilar aluminum alloys AA6061-T6 and AA2024-T3 was investigated. title: Dietary Turmeric Enhances Physiological Resilience of African Catfish (Clarias gariepinus) Following Aeromonas hydrophila Challenge: An Integrated Physiological Assessment
abstract: Improving physiological resilience to bacterial infection has become an important objective in sustainable aquaculture because disease outbreaks continue to compromise fish health, survival and production efficiency. Although dietary turmeric (Curcuma longa) has been reported to improve fish health, its effects on the integrated physiological responses associated with bacterial challenge remain poorly understood in African catfish (Clarias gariepinus). title: Leaf silicon and calcium differ between grassland plant functional groups while only calcium responds to soil background
abstract: Abstract Background and Aims Grasslands are biodiversity-rich ecosystems in which plant functional diversity strongly influences ecosystem functioning. Silicon (Si) and calcium (Ca) are often overlooked in trait-based frameworks despite their roles in plant physiology, stress tolerance and nutrient dynamics. This study investigates how leaf Si and Ca vary among plant functional groups, how they relate to soil Si and Ca availability, and whether they are associated with specific leaf area (SLA). title: Enhancing the hardness of low-carbon steel by pack carburizing using shellfish shell powder as a calcium carbonate activator
abstract: This study investigates the potential of shellfish shell powder as a natural source of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) for improving the pack carburizing of AISI 1020 low-carbon steel. AISI 1020 Low-carbon steel is commonly used in engineering applications because of its favorable mechanical properties and machinability; however, its relatively low surface hardness may limit its wear resistance. title: Novel use of far UV-C light as a surface disinfectant in the poultry industry: trials on broiler farms show reduced bacterial burden in poultry anterooms and on wellington boots
abstract: Abstract Far ultraviolet-C (UV-C) irradiation at 222 nm has widely been shown to deactivate bacteria, viruses and fungi in in-vitro experiments. However, there are few studies testing the technology on real life surface. There are no peer reviewed studies on the efficacy and feasibility of far UV-C disinfection in real-life agricultural settings. The aim of this study was to investigate whether far UV-C irradiation installations on UK broiler poultry farms could reduce bacterial surface burden. title: Taxidermy preparation of Oreochromis Niloticus (Linnaeus, 1758) using siliconized synthetic fiber as a filling material: technical report and photographic record
abstract: The preparation and preservation of animal specimens constitute important tools for the teaching of zoology, comparative anatomy, morphology and ichthyology. Among the different techniques used for fish preservation, three-dimensional preparation allows the external configuration of the specimen to be maintained, facilitating its use in educational and exhibition activities. This study aims to describe the taxidermy preparation process of a Nile tilapia specimen, Oreochromis niloticus (Linnaeus, 1758). title: Peruvian native chili peppers (Capsicum spp.): A comprehensive review of their diversity, phytochemical richness, industrial potential, and future perspectives
abstract: Peru is one of the countries with the greatest diversity of native chili peppers, which make a significant contribution to the highly valued gastronomy of this nation. However, the use of these chili peppers remains localized, resulting in a limited number of studies focused on these species, which restricts their industrial utilization and increases the risk of extinction. abstract: Two-dimensional transition metal selenides (TMSs) feature notable bandgap flexibility, versatile doping characteristics, and practical manufacturability, positioning them as promising candidates for next-generation electronics. Conventional WWTPs inadequately remove many recalcitrant pharmaceuticals and may alter the composition of microbial communities. abstract: This study reviews developments in experimental studies of photo-induced cooperative phenomena (photo-induced phase transition, PIPT), which involve ultrafast dynamical changes in electronic, spin, and lattice structures. abstract: ABSTRACT Polypropylene is extensively used as a packaging material, creating a huge amount of waste after use. This work highlights the use of recycled polypropylene (rPP), starch phthalate, and modified nanosilica to produce sustainable packaging material. abstract: ABSTRACT Trap states govern charge transport, accumulation, and local‐field distortion in polymer dielectrics, yet quantitative mapping of their energy, density, and spatial distribution remains challenging. abstract: Wood technology likely played a key role in human evolution, yet it remains poorly documented because organic materials rarely preserve in archaeological contexts. The Middle Palaeolithic site of Abric Romaní (Capellades, Barcelona) provides exceptional evidence of Neanderthal woodworking preserved through travertine incrustation. abstract: Diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation and impaired immune resolution, yet the therapeutic translation of single-cell atlases into rational immunomodulatory strategies remains limited. Here, integration of diabetic-wound single-cell transcriptomic datasets identifies a neutrophil subpopulation enriched in cluster of differentiation 55 (CD55) with complement-regulatory and reparative features. abstract: The microbial cell wall is a key target for many antibiotics owing to its conserved essentiality across the bacterial kingdom. Modifications of this cellular component, whether structural, chemical, or organizational, are frequently found in antibiotic-resistant isolates. abstract: Root systems demonstrate peculiar anatomical plasticity, with structural traits altering predictably across root orders to optimize water uptake, transport proficiency, and mechanical assistance. title: Temporal dynamics and species-specific responses to biotic and abiotic drivers shape seedling establishment in a subtropical forest
abstract: Abstract Seedling establishment is a critical demographic bottleneck for species regeneration and diversity maintenance in forests, yet the temporal contributions of biotic and abiotic factors remain poorly understood. This is because most previous studies focused disproportionately on biotic factors or limited abiotic factors and used observational data lacking standardized baselines for seedling age. abstract: Inter-tribal land disputes constitute one of the most pervasive conflicts in rural Cameroon, particularly in the South-West Region where customary land tenure systems intersect with population growth and inter-ethnic relations. In Eyumojock Sub-Division, intertribal land disputes between the Ebinsi, Ayuk’aba, Bakwele, Afap, Ogomoko, Kembong, and other indigenous groups threaten social cohesion and economic development. abstract: Abstract Methane (CH 4 ) emissions from the oil and gas (O&G) sector are a major source of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions. Russia is a leading CH 4 emitter, with the O&G sector accounting for approximately 80% of its total fossil fuel‐derived CH 4 emissions. abstract: As transformações ambientais que ocorrem no meio ambiente pressionam os ecossistemas florestais de forma a ocasionar o desequilíbrio nas suas funções ecológicas, além de contribuir para a perda desses ecossistemas. title: Comparative Assessment of Bio-Oils from Agriculture Biomass Waste and Conventional Fossil Fuels: Evaluating Their Potential as Sustainable Industrial Fuel Alternatives
abstract: The growing demand for sustainable energy and the environmental impacts of fossil fuel dependence have intensified interest in biomass-derived fuels, particularly in developing countries such as Nigeria where agricultural residues remain largely underutilized. This study assessed bio-oils obtained from agricultural biomass in comparison to traditional fossil fuels as a source of industrial energy. title: Hydrogen’s future in Türkiye: Storage, natural gas integration, and energy transition
abstract: Hydrogen stands out as a clean energy carrier that plays a critical role in the global energy transformation. Türkiye's increasing energy demand, dependence on fossil fuels, and carbon emission reduction targets place hydrogen technologies at the center of national energy policies. According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), the integration of hydrogen into energy systems could contribute to reducing global carbon emissions by up to 20%. abstract: This integrative review evaluates the current state and evolution of biochar research in arid and semi-arid agroecosystems by integrating scientometric analysis with a critical narrative synthesis. abstract: Abstract The development of nitric oxide (NO) donor agents capable of controlled NO release upon light irradiation in the biological window is relevant for phototherapies. abstract: Globally, livestock production systems (LPS) are crucial for supporting livelihoods and ensuring food security. abstract: First Nations communities (Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples) in remote Australia experience disproportionate risks to drinking water security, compounded by climate change. abstract: Abstract The widespread use of antibiotics has resulted in their frequent occurrence in aquatic environments, raising ecological concerns; however, conducting precise monitoring and tracing of a broad spectrum of antibiotics concurrently in complex river networks at the watershed scale still faces significant challenges. title: Global rise of a wheat pathogen through two-stage evolutionary emergence coupled with aerial dispersal
abstract: The rise of plant pathogens following crop domestication and their subsequent global spread pose persistent threats to food security, yet the mechanisms underlying host jumps and rapid adaptation in obligate biotrophs remain unclear. abstract: PURPOSE: Safe and quality healthcare requires effective patient-provider communication. Aphasia is a communication disability that leaves people at risk of ineffective communication and inadequate care. Modifying the environment is one way to support communication. A novel mobile communication aid-The Aphasia App-was designed to support hospital interactions between healthcare professionals (HCPs) and people with aphasia (PWA). abstract: Plastome-based classifications recognize 12 subfamilies and 22 tribes within Lamiaceae. abstract: Transforming agri-food systems is widely seen as necessary to address overlapping ecological and social crises. Public research and innovation policy is a central mechanism through which such transformations are steered, yet it is often articulated in ways that obscure the normative commitments legitimising particular pathways. abstract: Quantitative reconstruction of past temperatures is essential for understanding regional climate variability, and plant macrofossils provide valuable paleoclimatic records due to their sensitivity to summer conditions. abstract: Wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) landraces collected before the widespread regional adoption of Green Revolution cultivars provide a historical record of locally maintained germplasm. We characterized a panel of 202 accessions collected from Nepal and Bhutan between 1952 and 1958. abstract: ABSTRACT Objective To examine how three dimensions of economic security, namely employment position, wealth, and income, are associated with the marital intentions of never‐married adults in Türkiye, and to formally test whether these associations differ by gender. abstract: Femtosecond (fs) laser ablation has emerged as a disruptive technology for the ultra-precision finishing of aerospace face gears. abstract: Background Musculoskeletal disorders are an important occupational health concern among healthcare professionals and may emerge before entry into the workforce. Identifying musculoskeletal symptoms and their biopsychosocial correlates among nursing students may provide opportunities for early prevention and health promotion. title: Post-weaning DHA or EPA supplementation attenuates depressive-like behavior and myelination deficits induced by maternal high-fat diet in rat offspring
abstract: Abstract Depression affects younger populations, while imbalanced diet may contribute to disease development, with myelin abnormalities representing one possible underlying mechanism. title: The Visible and the Invisible: Contested Evidence, Photography, and the Politics of Remembering Japanese Atrocities in Asia
abstract: From 1931 to 1945, Japanese wartime photography was determined by a censorship system that shaped what could and could not be seen. The survival of the Mainichi Shimbun’s wartime negatives, hidden in an underground temple vault at the end of the war despite official orders to destroy them, offers rare material traces of this censorship process. title: Social Capital at the Service of Informal Export: The Case of Moroccan Women Entrepreneurs
abstract: This research explores the mobilization of informal social capital as a mechanism for circumventing institutional barriers to export among Moroccan women entrepreneurs. The study specifically examines how informal social networks compensate for the failures of the formal market and facilitate the internationalization of women-owned businesses in a constrained economic context. The empirical investigation relies on an exploratory qualitative approach following an abductive logic. title: Integrating multi-environment and path coefficient analysis for the identification of yellow rust-resistant bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) genotypes
abstract: Rapid turnover of varieties and limited access to rust-resistant wheat varieties across agroecologies are due to the rapid mutation of yellow rust pathogens. abstract: Avian paramyxoviruses (APMVs) are being increasingly detected in wild birds, yet the pathogenic potential of novel species remains poorly defined. abstract: A didactic strategy based on the case method is presented for teaching the fluorescein test to 34 forensic science professionals. The objective was to evaluate the integration of chemical foundations, criminalistic interpretation, and legal support in solving a crime scene simulation. title: Protein homeostasis and inter-organellar signaling under salt stress
abstract: Salinity is a major abiotic constraint on plant growth, productivity, and global food security. It disrupts cellular protein homeostasis (proteostasis) at every step, from synthesis to degradation. Plant survival under salt stress therefore depends on the coordinated regulation of protein synthesis, folding, post-translational modification, trafficking, quality control, and turnover. abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) typically require chiral precursors or catalysts to achieve asymmetry. abstract: The paper explores intersections of slow violence, eco-orientalism and colonial ecologies in fiction work in three postcolonial literary traditions: South Asian, Malay and Arab. abstract: High-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE) is a potentially fatal form of non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema that develops in susceptible individuals following rapid ascent to high altitude. Although exaggerated hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction is central to its pathophysiology, additional physiological mechanisms may also underlie individual susceptibility to HAPE. abstract: Written exposure therapy (WET) is an evidence-based, trauma-focused psychotherapy for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) that has been tested with several trauma-exposed samples. Although many individuals who receive WET and other trauma-focused psychotherapies experience a significant reduction in PTSD symptoms, there remains room for improvement given that a meaningful proportion of individuals continue to meet the diagnostic criteria following treatment. abstract: ABSTRACT Cobalt carbide (Co 2 C) shows promise for CO 2 hydrogenation to C 2+ hydrocarbons via the CO 2 ‐Fischer–Tropsch pathway, although the production rate is still limited by the slow CO hydrogenation step. abstract: Abstract Lubrication is widely associated with contact surfaces having relative motion to decrease friction and wear. abstract: Antibiotic resistance mediated by β-lactamase enzymes poses a major obstacle to the effective treatment of bacterial infections. abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 virus spillover into dairy cows represents the emergence of a mammalian host capable of sustaining a panzootic and creates a transmission pathway to humans. abstract: This article examines the characteristics and significance of pomegranate cultivation and the economic assessment of the pomegranate value chain. abstract: In this paper, we provide general information on the ReadingFood project, discussing its architecture and infrastructure choice(s). title: Neighbor Noise Problem in Multifamily Housing: An Integrative Framework for Resolution
abstract: Multifamily housing is common in urban areas, and neighbor noise is a frequent problem. title: Promoting subjective well-being through pet leisure: motivation, participation, and place attachment in urban spaces
abstract: While pet ownership is increasingly recognized as a vital contributor to human well-being, the specific behavioral and psychological mechanisms linking pet-related activities to owner happiness remain underexplored. abstract: This study explores the diverse representations of Elissa Rhaïs in the Spanish press and provides a comparative framework through which to understand her contributions to the literary field. Born to a Jewish family in Blida, Rhaïs made her first steps into the publishing world with the novel Saâda, La Marocaine (1919) and the short story Le café chantant (1920), which received significant attention during the interwar period. title: Spatially heterogenous distributions of dipteran abundances identify priority areas for haemosporidian parasite surveillance
abstract: How changes in one facet of biodiversity affect others remains poorly understood. Changes in dipteran populations, for example, might impact the spread of haemosporidian parasites. Using biomonitoring data from 934 Lithuanian freshwater sites (2013 − 2022) and a hierarchical Bayesian GLM with spatial correlation, we examined ecological quality, elevation, land-use, and climate as drivers of the abundance of dipteran families containing pathogen vectors. title: Cell plasticity in cancer and therapy resistance
abstract: Cancer cell plasticity, the ability of tumor cells to switch between distinct cellular states, has emerged as a key mechanism driving tumor progression, metastasis and therapy resistance. Cancer cells exploit diverse plasticity mechanisms, including dedifferentiation, transdifferentiation, epithelial-mesenchymal transition and stem cell-like reprogramming, to adapt to changes in their microenvironment or therapeutic pressures. title: Fish Community Structure, Diversity, and Their Environmental Correlates in Two Arid-Region Lakes of Northwest China: Bosten Lake and Taitema Lake
abstract: Bosten Lake and Taitema Lake are important inland lakes in arid Northwest China, but recent fish-assemblage variation in these systems remains poorly resolved. We surveyed fish communities at 10 sites in Bosten Lake and four sites in Taitema Lake from 2023 to 2025 using standardized conventional capture methods. abstract: Abstract Wolman disease (WD), the severe infantile form of lysosomal acid lipase (LAL) deficiency, is a rare metabolic disorder caused by inactivating mutations in the LIPA gene. Although WD is characterized by profound hepatic dysfunction, experimental human systems capable of modeling multicellular liver pathology and supporting therapeutic testing remain limited. abstract: Mixed-species parasite infections are common in wildlife, yet the ecological processes that structure these communities remain poorly understood. We hypothesized that host-mediated and extrinsic environmental filtering, alongside biotic interactions, act concurrently to shape parasite community composition, and that these structuring patterns would depend on parasite traits or evolutionary history. abstract: The strength of sexual selection is often linked to genetic mating system and is thought to be a driving force in the evolution of sexual dimorphism. Here, we compared selection between males and females across three closely related species: the dusky (Syngnathus floridae), Northern (S. fuscus), and Gulf (S. scovelli) pipefishes, using new and previously published datasets. title: Surface temperatures drive strong seasonality in urban reactive carbon emissions
abstract: Urban air quality is affected by diverse volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and prior studies reveal a need to understand their seasonal sources. We combine high-resolution mass spectrometry with eddy covariance to quantify VOC fluxes from an urban/suburban New York site during summer and winter. Emissions are strongly seasonal: During summer, twice as many VOCs undergo surface-atmosphere exchange, and molar and reactivity-based fluxes are 2 to 4× higher than in winter. title: Prehistoric global migration of vanishing gut microbes with humans
abstract: The gut microbiome is crucial for health and is affected strongly by lifestyle1. Many microorganisms commonly found in non-industrialized populations are disappearing or have become extinct in industrialized populations2–6. Studying which microorganisms have been long-term residents of the human gut and may have co-evolved with humans2,7,8 could provide insights into how microbial biodiversity loss affects human health. title: Influence of researcher presence towards nest attendance and breeding of barn owls Tyto javanica javanica
abstract: Human disturbance to nesting raptors can influence breeding success, especially during early breeding. This study examined the impact of researcher presence, a relatively low impact human disturbance, on eastern barn owls Tyto javanica javanica during monitoring of 57 nest‐boxes in oil palm plantations in Malaysia over a period of 30 months. title: Variability of suspended sediment transport dynamics between seasons and flow pathways in a small agricultural catchment
abstract: Abstract Suspended sediment dynamics in small agricultural catchments are shaped by the interaction of overland and subsurface flow processes, yet no event-scale, flow pathway-specific comparisons of seasonal discharge (Q)–suspended sediment concentration (SSC) relationships within a single catchment exist. This study addresses this gap by analysing Q–SSC relationships during 18 overland flow events (2014–2016) using high temporal resolution (1-min) discharge and turbidity data combined with event-based SSC monitoring at three different flow pathways within the Hydrological Open Air Laboratory

title: Grapevine rhizosphere microbial activity and nitrogen nutrition vary with tree planting age in a temperate vitiforestry system
abstract: Abstract Background and Aims Agroforestry, i.e., the planting of trees within agricultural systems, has been shown to enhance soil fertility, biodiversity, and the functioning of ecosystems. In temperate vineyards, vitiforestry represents a new type of agroforestry combining perennial grapevines and trees, either within or around vine rows. abstract: Arcangelisia flava (L.) Merr., locally known as “akar kuning,” is a traditional medicinal plant from Kalimantan with limited evidence regarding its anticancer compounds. This study aimed to isolate bioactive compounds from A. flava bark and evaluate their cytotoxicity against MCF-7 breast cancer cells. title: Tracing soil–water signatures from contrasting land uses in low-flow streamwater of a mixed headwater catchment
abstract: Baseflow sustains water delivery from headwater catchments during non-event conditions and low flows. However, in mixed land-use headwater catchments, how land-use-related soil–water storage signatures are represented in low-flow streamwater and vary seasonally remain poorly understood. To address this gap, a two-year study involving monthly monitoring of a hilly purple-soil headwater catchment was conducted. title: Common genetic control for grain filling duration and kernel weight in grain sorghum
abstract: KEY MESSAGE: The genetic control of GFD in sorghum closely overlaps with that of grain size, is influenced by both pre- and post-anthesis processes, offering new opportunities for yield improvement through targeted breeding and inter-racial trait introgression. The duration of the grain filling period has been associated with yield increases in cereals including maize and sorghum. title: Global stability of leaning-type steel box arch bridges: mechanistic insights and quantitative evaluation of key design parameters
abstract: Leaning-type arch bridges are attractive for wide-deck urban applications, but their elastic global buckling mechanisms and parameter sensitivities remain insufficiently quantified. This study investigates a leaning-type steel box arch bridge using a three-dimensional finite element model validated against field-measured arch deflections and hanger forces. abstract: ABSTRACT Yellow is an established color category despite being generated by a mixture of primaries on RGB displays. We examined its lexical accessibility, representative‐color selections, and matching accuracy using two complementary tasks. A web‐based survey asked participants to list 10 color terms and select their best representatives from a 64‐field RGB grid. abstract: ATP-citrate lyase (ACLY) is a key enzyme in cellular metabolism that catalyses the cleavage of citrate to produce acetyl coenzyme A (acetyl-CoA), thereby bridging energy metabolism and epigenetic regulation. Acetyl-CoA serves as a common substrate for de novo lipogenesis (DNL) and histone acetylation. title: Dual‐Comb Spectroscopy With Fully Controlled Repetition Rate and Offset Frequency of Quantum Cascade Laser Frequency Combs
abstract: ABSTRACT Quantum cascade laser frequency combs (QCL‐FCs) are promising light sources for sensing applications, thanks to their convenient electrical pumping, chip‐scale footprint, high optical power, and relatively broadband emission in the mid‐infrared molecular fingerprint spectral region. abstract: Temperature is an important environmental factor influencing phenological development and productivity of sweet corn through heat unit accumulation. This study evaluated heat unit accumulation, heat use efficiency (HUE), yield components, and sweetness of seven commercial sweet corn cultivars grown under tropical lowland conditions during one growing season. abstract: Bone defects present significant clinical challenges worldwide, as conventional treatments such as autografts and allografts are constrained by limited supply, immune risks and insufficient bioactivity. Derived from the patient's own venous blood via centrifugation, autologous platelet concentrates (APCs) offer an autologous, readily accessible source of growth factors and immune-related cues that can support osteogenesis, angiogenesis, and regenerative microenvironment remodeling. title: Thermostability and pH Differentiation in Geobacillus Hydrolases: A Comparative Perspective
abstract: Thermostable enzymes are central to high-temperature industrial processes because they combine catalytic efficiency with structural resilience under demanding conditions. Among thermophilic bacteria, Geobacillus has emerged as a prominent source of industrially relevant enzymes, particularly hydrolases such as proteases, lipases, and carbohydrate-active enzymes. abstract: Spekboom (Portulacaria afra), a succulent viewed as both environmentally and socioeconomically acceptable, remains underutilized. This study investigated the culinary potential and consumer acceptability of spekboom across diverse flavour profiles and textures. title: From Approval to Occupancy: Regulatory Translation of Water-System Requirements in Lagos High-Rise Housing
abstract: High-rise residential buildings in Lagos rely heavily on water stored, pumped, and distributed within the building, because public supply is limited. Whether they deliver adequate pressure and continuous supply depends on design decisions that regulation could check. This study examined how far Lagos regulatory instruments translate the technical requirements of building water systems into criteria that can be assessed and verified. abstract: Planned events are increasingly recognized as important components of tourism development and destination promotion, whereas geotourism research has primarily focused on geoheritage, geodiversity, geoeducation, and geotourism products. The article conceptualizes geoevents as a new category of events that directly utilize geographical space, geodiversity, and geoheritage as their fundamental thematic and organizational components. title: Gendered landscapes of loss: climate change, disaster, and women's resilience in rural India
abstract: This article examines the gendered dimensions of climate-induced disasters in rural India through a systematic archival analysis of five community testimonies published by the People's Archive of Rural India (PARI). Drawing on stories from Odisha, Maharashtra, Assam, and Kerala, the study analyses how climate change manifesting as erratic monsoons, intensifying floods, accelerating riverbank erosion, and catastrophic landslides disproportionately impacts women in agrarian and indigenous communities. title: Angles of trust in transboundary water cooperation: Capturing the multidimensional and dynamic nature of trust in the Sava and Syrdarya river basins
abstract: Trust is frequently invoked to explain cooperation or conflict in interstate relations over shared water resources. Drawing on qualitative research in the Sava River Basin in Southeastern Europe and the Syrdarya River Basin in Central Asia, this article suggests three key dimensions through which trust can be better understood – its sources, levels, and intensities. title: Multi-scale connectivity and distribution: vulnerability in global food trade networks via static-dynamic integration
abstract: Abstract The global food trade network (FTN) is one of the key mechanisms for safeguarding national food supplies, and identifying its vulnerability is of considerable importance for maintaining global food security. This study develops a vulnerability assessment framework for the FTN that provides systematic analysis at the overall, cluster, and individual levels, integrating static and dynamic assessments within a unified analytical framework. abstract: Non-persistent phenolic endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs), bisphenols, parabens and triclosan, blood metals and ambient air pollutants are each linked to adverse neurodevelopment, but they are rarely analyzed together. abstract: Weed seed contamination of cattle feed can contribute to weed dispersal within crop–livestock systems when viable seeds survive digestion and are returned to fields through manure or slurry applications. However, the persistence of weed seeds from feed preservation to waste recycling remains poorly understood. This study aimed to evaluate the viability of common agricultural weed seeds after exposure to silage fermentation, simulated rumen digestion, and storage in cattle manure and slurry. abstract: Abstract Biological herbicides serve as highly efficient and eco-friendly weed control agents, which typically consist of natural secondary metabolites, such as phytotoxic metabolites produced by Streptomyces sp. However, the isolation of phytotoxic compounds from pathogenic Streptomyces strains has been insufficiently investigated. title: When heat hits: Short-run saving and withdrawal behavior among microfinance clients in Benin
abstract: Increased access to finance is widely viewed as a key driver to increase adaptive capacity in response to climate change. However, apart from limited studies on borrowing behavior, little is known about how exposure to extreme heat is associated with microfinance clients’ financial behavior. This study addresses this gap by investigating the short-run associations of unusual heat with microfinance clients’ saving and withdrawal behavior. In a case study, it combines geo-located temperature data with a unique dataset of around 50,000 clients of a leading Microfinance Institution (MFI) in Benin.

abstract: Los instrumentos estructurados de registro son centrales para la gestión sanitaria, pero su diseño y las condiciones organizacionales que lo rodean inciden fuertemente en la calidad de los datos producidos. abstract: Tropical floriculture is an economically relevant activity, particularly for family farming, because of the high added value of cut flowers and the potential for rapid financial returns. Among tropical ornamentals, Heliconia species are valued for their diversity of colors and forms. abstract: Historical knowledge of the landscape is essential to understand the current ecosystem. abstract: Efficient weed control in fallow fields prior to maize planting faces critical challenges due to herbicide resistance and the need to reduce reliance on glyphosate. This study evaluated non-selective and selective herbicide strategies in an on-farm strip-plot validation trial (6 ha) with nested subsampling (n = 6 quadrats per treatment plot). abstract: This study explored the integration of cognitive psychology into library space design, specifically examining how stochastic resonance where background noise enhances cognitive performance can inform acoustic zoning policies in academic libraries. Anchored in Ranganathan’s principles and the shifting demands of emotionally responsive users, the research critiqued the traditional silent library model. abstract: Early numeracy is central to school readiness and educational equity, yet national policies may be implemented unevenly across geographically and institutionally diverse early childhood education (ECE) settings. This study examined the implementation of Indonesia's 2024 early literacy-numeracy policy in urban, rural, and remote settings in West Nusa Tenggara and explored the feasibility of the LENTAS (Locally Contextualized Early Numeracy with Technology Support) model. abstract: Democratic accountability assumes that the citizens who bear the costs of government decisions can sanction the officials who make them. We identify a structural break in this assumption. When a city funds itself through taxes that fall partly on nonresidents (highway travelers, commuters, and regional shoppers who cannot vote in local elections) the electoral link between bearing costs and imposing sanctions weakens. abstract: Tour guide attributes’ roles have emerged as a crucial element affecting tourists’ memorable experiences and intention to revisit destinations along Thailand Andaman Coast, especially within the foreign tourist context. Based on the stimulus-organism-response (S-O-R) model, this study examined the influences of tour guide attributes (TGA) on memorable tourism experience (MTE) and revisit intention (RVI) among foreign tourists along Thailand's Andaman Coast. abstract: The number of EVs is increasing rapidly globally, and that means the need for more sustainable and economical charging. One of the possible solutions is a hybrid renewable energy system technology, which has wind and solar photovoltaic (PV) energy. abstract: Drawing on interviews with mid- and later-career teachers from primary and secondary schools in one region of England, this small-scale study examined why participants had chosen to stay. They described how their moral purpose and agency helped them manage multiple challenges over time, and how these had contributed to their sense of professional identity and decisions to stay. abstract: As public concern about food crises has risen, China faces the challenge of rebuilding confidence in its domestic food supply chains. This study examines how Confucian ethics are incorporated into the Chinese food documentary ‘A Bite of China’ and how the series constructs narratives of food safety and sustainability. title: Dietary nanoencapsulated A-Ghrelin improves growth performance and health status in juvenile Siberian sturgeon
abstract: This study evaluated a novel multi-functional feed supplement for juvenile Siberian sturgeon ( Acipenser baerii ), combining an acetylated ghrelin analog (A-Ghrelin) with a chitosan-alginate-iron oxide (Fe₂O₃) nanoparticle delivery system. Over 60 days, 240 fish (initial weight: 8.5 ± 0.9 g) were assigned to eight diets ( n = 3 tanks/treatment). The complete supplement (nanoencapsulated A-Ghrelin + 1 mg/kg nano-Fe₂O₃) yielded the best outcomes: weight gain increased 75.5% (73.9 vs. 42.1 g in control), feed conversion ratio improved from 4.1 to 1.8, and reduced ALT/AST. title: Molecular, agro-morphological, and phytochemical analysis of goldenrod (Solidago spp.) genotypes grown under two contrasting climates
abstract: Solidago , belonging to the Asteraceae family, is used as an herbal medicine and possess diuretic, anti-microbial, cytotoxic, anti-inflammatory, gastroprotective and immunobiological properties. However, the extent to which genetic differences among wild and cultivated Solidago materials contribute to variation in agronomic performance and phytochemical quality under contrasting environmental conditions remains insufficiently understood. title: Multi-factor assessment of future climate hazards to apple production across Switzerland’s growing regions
abstract: Abstract Apple production is likely to face increased climate hazards in the future resulting from climate change. The magnitude and relative importance of different climate hazards remain unclear, especially when considering multiple emissions scenarios. Here, we perform a multi-factor climate hazard assessment for apple-growing regions in Switzerland that considers summer heat, summer drought, spring frost, and insufficient winter chill as sources of climate hazard. title: What are pulsar companions made of? Using gravitational tides to probe their compositions
abstract: Low eccentricity, short orbital period pulsar companions may provide a probe to study novel dense and stable exoplanet internal compositions due to the potentially significant orbital evolution they experience caused by strong gravitational tides. We model the tidal characteristics such as apsidal motion constants, orbital precession, and tidal deformability for a variety of equations of state to be compared with values recovered via pulsar timing for a sample of four systems: PSR J1719-1438b, PSR J0636+5128b, PSR J2322+2650b, and PSR J1807-2459A b. title: Variety-Specific Responses of Mulberry to Copper-Induced Stress
abstract: Copper (Cu) is an essential plant micronutrient, but in excessive amounts it becomes phytotoxic, making Cu contamination of agricultural soils an important environmental concern. Because Cu tolerance mechanisms are complex and often genotype-specific, there is growing interest in multipurpose crops capable of thriving under metal stress. Mulberry is one of such species, which enables the combination of diverse agricultural uses with notable tolerance to heavy metals. title: Radiocarbon dating of wooden beams at Herodium palace-fortress: Modeling tree-felling events and their implications on site chronology
abstract: The site of Herodium is best known for its impressive, well-preserved palace fortress, built by Herod the Great, towards the end of the 1st century BC. The site's conical shape, artificially created to transform it into Herod's monumental burial complex, is clearly seen from afar. The impressive preservation of wooden beams and posts at the site has allowed for a rigorous radiocarbon study of the beams' felling dates and their potential implications for the timing of construction activities at the site. title: Effects of the Glycerol/Quercetin Ratio on the Structure and Tensile Behavior of PVA-Based Films
abstract: Poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)-based films containing glycerol and quercetin were prepared by casting as potential active-packaging materials. The effects of the glycerol/quercetin ratio on structural, thermal, mechanical, barrier, and antioxidant properties were investigated. Neat PVA and ternary formulations with PVA/glycerol/quercetin ratios of 70/20/10 (PVA+Gly+Q10) and 70/10/20 (PVA+Gly+Q20) by mass were characterized by FTIR, XRD, SEM, contact angle, TGA/DTG, tensile testing, water vapor permeability (WVP), total phenolic content, and DPPH assays. title: Phenolic Profiles of Nelumbo nucifera from Manipur Against Neurodegenerative Inflammation

title: Absorption and toxicity of mineral oil after dermal and mucosal surface exposure: a review
abstract: Dermal and mucosal surface exposure to mineral oils occurs in the occupational setting. To evaluate exposure levels at which toxicity occurs, we collected data on non-cancer toxicity of crude oil, refinery streams and refined mineral oils. This included extraction of no-observed-adverse-effect levels (NOAELs) and lowest-observed-adverse-effect levels (LOAELs). title: Macrophage- or neutrophil-expressed UPP1 drives tumor growth and immune suppression in the tumor microenvironment
abstract: Uridine phosphorylase 1 (UPP1) has recently emerged as a metabolic regulator with critical roles in tumor cell biology. However, its expression pattern and functional significance in nonmalignant components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) remain largely unexplored. Here, we performed a comprehensive pan-cancer single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealing that UPP1 is highly expressed not only in tumor cells but also in tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and neutrophils (TANs). title: Identification of Social Key Performance Indicators - A Case Study
abstract: Social Key Performance Indicators (SKPIs) and the competitiveness they can bring is studied and applied to a case in the energy sector (district heating). A case study has limited generalizability, but we argue that the case serves as a critical case, informing other companies on actions to take for increasing their competitive advantage by social value inclusion. title: Effect of substituting maize with newly released sorghum varieties on laying performance and egg quality of bovans brown
abstract: Rising maize prices and increasing competition caused by rising human food demand are forcing poultry producers to seek alternative energy sources. Newly released grain sorghum varieties in western Ethiopia may serve as a viable substitute, but their effects on laying hen performance and profitability need assessment. To assess the effects of replacing maize with a recently introduced sorghum variety (Assosa‑1) on feed intake, body weight change, feed conversion efficiency, egg production, egg quality, and economic return in Bovans Brown laying hens. title: Voltammetric studies of TiO2-nanographite based composites
abstract: Titanium dioxide (TiO 2 ) is a promising electrode material for use as an electrode in electrochemical energy storage. However, its low electrical conductivity limits its performance. This study investigated the influence of nanographite incorporation and ionic liquid (IL) addition on the structural and electrochemical properties of TiO 2 . title: Constraining Fault Kinematics and India‐Tarim Convergence Partitioning in Southwestern Tibet With Geodetic Block Modeling
abstract: Abstract How the convergent strain between the India Plate and the Tarim basin is partitioned by active faults and off‐fault deformation in southwestern Tibet is poorly understood due to limited knowledge of strain localisation and fault kinematics. In this study, we derive high‐resolution velocity fields for the southwestern Tibetan Plateau using both GNSS and InSAR observations. Using these velocity fields, we apply an improved block model to estimate the kinematics of major active faults in the region. title: Effects of organic and conventional management on morphophysiological parameters and antioxidant profile of tomato fruits (Solanum lycopersicum L.), ‘Big Río’ variety
abstract: Mexico is one of the main tomato-producing countries and relies heavily on synthetic chemical fertilizers, whose negative effects within and beyond production systems have already been described. In this context, organic agriculture offers an alternative to reduce chemical fertilizer use. The objective of the present study was to evaluate two management systems, organic and conventional, in terms of plant morphophysiological parameters, yield, and the antioxidant profile of fruits of the ‘Big Río’ variety of Solanum lycopersicum L. title: Review of educational interventions for patients requiring palliative care: A scoping review
abstract: BACKGROUND: Palliative care aims to improve the quality of life of individuals with serious, progressive illnesses. Therapeutic patient education is a key approach for enhancing patient autonomy and empowerment. However, structured educational interventions for patients receiving palliative care remain poorly documented in the literature, in contrast to the growing body of evidence regarding education for caregivers and healthcare professionals.
