title: Burned habitats facilitate predation and lead to long‐term reductions in prey success
abstract: Intensifying wildfire regimes under global change are expected to shift species interactions through changes in habitat structure and composition, vegetation productivity, and sensory cues. Yet there is little evidence of how burn-induced changes in habitat composition and structure modify predator-prey relationships. We investigated how wildfires influence relationships between mule deer (Odocoileus hemionus) and cougars (Puma concolor) in the US Intermountain West using high-resolution telemetry data, kill site locations, and annual measures of mule deer fawn production. title: Values of Villainy: A Typology of Antagonists in Superhero Films Through Schwartz’s Theory of Basic Human Values
abstract: This article investigates the motivational grammars of villains in Hollywood superhero films through the lens of Schwartz’s Theory of Basic Human Values. By analyzing the discourse of eight iconic antagonists, we identified three clusters: Ambiguous Tragedians, whose villainy emerges from wounded subjectivity and marginalization; Revolutionary Calculators, who justify domination through distorted appeals to justice and order; and the Chaotic Nihilist, represented solely by Heath Ledger’s Joker, who embodies systemic collapse and anarchic spectacle. title: Venom composition of the Iberian adder (Vipera seoanei) from northern Portugal reveals limited sex and size variation
abstract: Snake venom is a complex and dynamic ecological trait, with high potential for intraspecific variation. In this study, the venom composition of the Iberian adder ( Vipera seoanei ) from the Peneda Mountains of northern Portugal was investigated to explore whether venom varies with body size and sex. Venom proteomes from six individuals representing juvenile, subadult, and adult males and females were characterised using LC–MS/MS, while individual variation was assessed from SDS–PAGE profiles of 18 snakes. title: Dynamical features and dispersive soliton solutions of a fractional extended Schrödinger model incorporating cubic-quadratic nonlinear terms
abstract: This study is devoted to investigating soliton solutions and qualitative analysis of the M-fractional extended nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation with cubicquadratic nonlinear terms. This research is motivated by the significance of the extended NLS model in optics, quantum mechanics, plasma physics, electromagnetic wave propagation, and the approximate description of dense quasione- dimensional Bose–Einstein condensates (BECs) involving repulsive contact interactions and long-range dipole-dipole attraction. title: Quantifying assets for the geopolitics of climate change mitigation
abstract: Abstract Climate change mitigation reshapes the distribution of economic assets in the low-carbon transition. Here we quantify climate-related assets for 169 countries across four dimensions: fossil fuel production, climate change damages, renewable energy potential and land carbon sequestration capacity. We combine integrated assessment models, climate projections, economic damage functions and biosphere datasets to assess asset changes under multiple mitigation scenarios. title: Electrons Hopping Across a Molecular Network: Spectra and Symmetries
abstract: We investigate interacting spinless electrons on finite molecular networks described by a tight-binding Hubbard Hamiltonian. The interplay between network geometry, Coulomb interactions and discrete symmetries is analysed for rings with L=3,4,5, and 6 nodes, filled with one, two or three electrons. Special attention is devoted to the role of the network symmetries in determining the structure of the many-body spectrum and the Mulliken classification of the eigenstates. title: Naringenin Delays Aging in Drosophila through FoxO-Mediated Autophagy and Intestinal Homeostasis Preservation
abstract: Abstract Naringenin (NAE), a natural flavonoid with established geroprotective properties, has unclear mechanisms in intestinal aging. This study demonstrated that dietary NAE (0.5 mM and 1.5 mM) significantly extended Drosophila median lifespan by 8.27% and 14.41% (P < 0.05), and improved healthspan through improved locomotor capacity (26.79% and 37.49%, P < 0.05), elevated ATP production (92.60%, P < 0.001), and enhanced stress resistance. title: Aquatic vegetation promotes prey diversity but not the diversification of predator phenotypes
abstract: Freshwater fish have evolved to forage in a range of habitats, from open water in lakes to benthic shorelines and streams. Much research has focused on how prey differences, such as zooplankton versus benthic macroinvertebrates, might select for divergence in predator traits across this habitat gradient. title: The spillover effects and mechanisms of typhoon disasters on stock volatility: considering the heterogeneity of financial enterprises and non-financial enterprises
abstract: Extreme meteorological events, such as typhoons, constitute severe external shocks that significantly impact macroeconomic operations and fundamental corporate activities. Grounded in stakeholder theory, this study employs a two way fixed effects difference in differences model alongside the VaR-BEKK-MVGARCH-DUMMY-T framework. abstract: Small interfering RNA (siRNA) has achieved clinical success in liver-directed therapies, but its translation to solid tumors remains limited by heterogeneous delivery and context-dependent target dependence. This review compares non-small cell lung cancer, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, breast cancer, glioblastoma, and hepatocellular carcinoma across four interconnected dimensions: resistance networks, tumor microenvironmental reprogramming, metastatic progression, and delivery-system design. title: Is the Object Obsolescent? On Reuse Beyond Simondon
abstract: The article critically examines the status of the obsolescence of technical objects within the context of contemporary consumer society, taking Gilbert Simondon’s philosophy of technology as its central theoretical framework. The author argues that obsolescence is not primarily a technical phenomenon, but rather a social, symbolic, and economic one, produced by market dynamics, advertising, and the logic of permanent innovation, which detach the object from its structural durability. title: Design Approaches for Oxygen Reduction Systems for Warehouse Storage Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Oxygen reduction systems (ORS) are protection systems, with a design protection objective to limit fire spread beyond the point of ignition. Research has shown that the prescriptive design methods, in VdS 3527, EN 16750, and ISO 20338, are not appropriate as prescriptive design methods as they result in insufficient protection levels. In this paper, two design approaches for ORS for warehouse applications have been developed to address the lack of robust design methods. title: Assessing the genetic diversity in potato genotypes to enhance yield and quality in temperate region of Kashmir valley
abstract: Potato ( Solanum tuberosum L.) is a food crop of a global significance, and the production of high yielding cultivars that matches a specific agro-climate, is important to achieve food security. This study explored the genetic variability, association of traits and phylogenetic variation available in 53 genotypes of potato, which were grown in temperate environment of Kashmir valley in India. title: How much would egg and duckling predation need to be reduced to reverse declines of ground-nesting waterfowl in Finland? A demographic scenario analysis
abstract: Abstract Populations of water- and wetland-associated birds have declined globally due to multiple pressures, including habitat loss, climate change, and predation. Ground-nesting waterfowl are particularly vulnerable to predators, and the spread of invasive mammalian predators like raccoon dogs ( Nyctereutes procyonoides ) has intensified this threat in parts of Northern Europe. title: Influence of functional traits and trait syndromes on the vulnerability of amphibians and reptiles in the tropical dry forest of Oaxaca, Mexico
abstract: Abstract Tropical dry forests are among the most threatened ecosystems worldwide, yet their biodiversity remains understudied compared to humid tropical forests. We integrated functional trait ecology with environmental vulnerability assessments to evaluate multi‑causal disturbances affecting amphibians and reptiles in Oaxaca, Mexico, a hotspot of endemism and biodiversity loss. title: Optimization of pro-tray configuration, substrate composition, and seedling age for chili and brinjal plug seedlings intended for robotic transplanting
abstract: Labor scarcity has accelerated interest in robotic transplanting, whose reliability depends on seedling geometry and root plug cohesion. This study optimized pro-tray configuration, substrate composition, and seedling age for chili and brinjal plug seedlings. title: Genomic prediction of single cross families of perennial ryegrass under two nitrogen managements
abstract: Abstract The performance of a single cross is determined by the additive effects of the parents and their interactions, which can be estimated through general combining ability (GCA) and specific combining ability (SCA). With genome‐wide marker information, it is possible to predict GCA for new parents and the genetic value of unrealized crosses. title: Safety and Analgesic Effectiveness of Adding Butorphanol to Multimodal Intravenous Patient-Controlled Analgesia After Gynecologic Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Butorphanol is sometimes added to multimodal intravenous patient-controlled analgesia (PCA), but its incremental analgesic benefit and adverse symptom burden when combined with an established sufentanil-based regimen remain uncertain. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study used routinely collected perioperative, postoperative PCA follow-up, and hospital billing data from July 2022 to June 2025. title: Aging of Urban Traffic Fine Particles Modulates Toxicity Mechanisms and Oxidative Stress Responses
abstract: Abstract Vehicular emissions are an important source of urban air pollution that can age through atmospheric processes, but how their health effects change during atmospheric aging remains poorly understood. To simulate realistic urban emissions, we sampled air in a parking garage where cold-start and urban emissions coexist. Following aging in an oxidation flow reactor (OFR), we studied the cellular and acellular effects of the fresh and aged aerosols. abstract: ABSTRACT Accessing surface quantum transport in topological insulators is hampered by residual bulk conduction arising from lattice defects. Here, we demonstrate a novel synthesis pathway for realizing high‐mobility ‐ thin films in which surface transport is dominant. title: Reconstructed functional diversity and food-web structure reveal mammalian community shifts through the Oligo-Miocene in Oregon
abstract: Abstract Understanding how ecological communities respond to environmental change over long timescales is essential for predicting modern ecosystem dynamics. Here, we reconstructed functional community composition and trophic network structure of seven mammal communities from the eastern region of Oregon. We focused on fossil localities that span the past 32 million years. title: A 4-D spatio-temporal misfit function for waveform inversion of Distributed Acoustic Sensing data
abstract: Summary Standard Full-Waveform Inversion (FWI) objective functions often struggle to resolve deep structures when data are dominated by localised near-surface scattering. To address this, we develop a 4-D time-frequency-space-wavenumber (TFXK) objective function that explicitly enforces spatial coherence, leveraging the dense sampling of Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS). title: Provenance and environment jointly shape early regeneration in fir and beech: evidence from distributed participatory trials across Europe
abstract: Summary Forest regeneration is shaped by strong demographic filters during germination and early establishment, yet the relative contributions of seed provenance and environment remain poorly understood under natural conditions. We combined climate‐chamber trials with a continental‐scale, field‐based citizen science seed‐sowing experiment to quantify germination, early phenological development, and 3‐yr postgermination survival of fir ( Abies spp.) and beech ( Fagus spp.) provenances across Europe. title: Measuring innovation in local government: an Exploratory factor analysis of provincial administrative organizations in Thailand
abstract: Innovation has become a critical capability for local governments seeking to improve service delivery, organizational effectiveness, and responsiveness to community needs. However, empirical research on local government innovation remains fragmented, with limited attention to multidimensional measurement frameworks, particularly in decentralized governance contexts. title: Reprogramming tumor cells with LCOR mRNA nanotherapy to enhance immunotherapy
abstract: Transcription factors (TFs) are often considered undruggable due to their structural complexity. mRNA technologies can overcome this therapeutic limitation by enabling dynamic protein replacement therapies. Here, we explore the TF activity of LCOR (Ligand-dependent corepressor), which suppresses tumor growth, at least in part by inducing the antigen presentation machinery (APM) in tumor cells and constraining cellular plasticity. title: Travel time budgets and the potential to replace travel by car in urban regions: A case study from Finland
abstract: A shift towards sustainable modes of transport (walking, cycling, and public transport) is urgently needed to reduce the negative externalities of private car use. Whereas active travel is a feasible alternative for relatively short distances, public transport can substitute for a larger share of car use. City regions are often seen as the main targets for this mode shift given the availability of public transport options and the proximity of services. title: Ex situ thermal acclimation alters temperature selection with limited post-release effects in an endangered frog ( Rana muscosa )
abstract: Abstract Amphibian declines driven by the fungal pathogen Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd) pose major challenges for conservation, particularly for cold-adapted species occupying habitats where temperatures may be less limiting to Bd growth. Host thermal behaviour can influence infection dynamics, and thermal environments during developmental stages may shape disease susceptibility and performance. title: Niches in cancer: from primary tumors to metastatic disease
abstract: Cancer progression does not occur in isolation: malignant-cell states and fates are shaped by specialized microenvironments, or cancer niches. Within primary tumors, vascular, stromal, immune and neural interactions create local hypoxic, metabolic and mechanical conditions that together influence malignant-cell behavior. abstract: To address the inefficient gas extraction problem of high‑gas low‑permeability coal seams in Guizhou Province, this study investigates the permeability‑enhancing mechanism and field performance of liquid CO₂ phase‑change fracturing, taking local anthracite and bituminous coal as research objects. title: Tuning e-fuel product distribution by combining a Na-promoted Fe-based catalyst with BETA zeolites in CO2-modified Fischer-Tropsch synthesis
abstract: The integration of acidic zeolites with Fe-based catalysts provides a promising strategy to overcome the broad hydrocarbon distribution of CO 2 -modified Fischer-Tropsch synthesis (FTS) through in situ product upgrading. title: Beyond the outlet: How lateral seepage shapes controlled drainage performance in a sandy soil
abstract: Controlled drainage (CD) is used in temperate humid regions to reduce water and nutrient losses. Although CD effectiveness has been widely evaluated, the role of lateral seepage in sandy soils remains underexplored and neglecting it may overestimate reductions in water and nutrient losses. The objective was to evaluate CD performance in a sandy loam field prone to lateral seepage and quantify how lateral seepage alters estimates of water and nitrate losses from the field. title: REIMAGINING CLIMATE JUSTICE THROUGH THE LENS OF GREEN SOCIAL WORK: AN INTEGRATED CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK
abstract: Climate justice scholarship has converged on a trivalent model of distributive, procedural and recognition justice, yet this model remains largely anthropocentric, vulnerable to technocratic and market-based capture, and silent on both the epistemic marginalisation of Indigenous and Global South knowledge and the structural drivers of the crisis. title: Content associations with answer selection and engagement in supply chain community question answering
abstract: Community question-answering (cQA) platforms are important ecosystems for knowledge sharing, yet research on what makes an answer “best” or a question engaging has often focused on either individual lexical features or broad topics. This exploratory study examines both levels in Yahoo! Chiebukuro, asking which nouns and semantic noun clusters are associated with best-answer selection and question engagement. title: Recent trends in (commercial) power-to-methanol technology
abstract: Methanol based on CO 2 and H 2 produced from renewable energy is anticipated to be an important building block in a sustainable economy. While the synthesis of e-methanol looks similar to conventional methanol synthesis at a first view, important boundary conditions are different along the scale from catalyst to process level. abstract: Preterm birth is a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality worldwide, with ascending infection and inflammation at the fetal-maternal interface recognized as major contributors to its pathophysiology. abstract: The root meristem is essential for stem cell maintenance and root development in plants. abstract: Gamma irradiation is an effective mutagenesis approach for developing wheat lines with improved agronomic performance and enhanced nutritional quality. This study evaluated the effects of gamma irradiation on biological yield, protein content, iron (Fe), zinc (Zn), phytic acid concentration, and mineral bioavailability in mutant lines derived from three spring wheat cultivars (Zhenis, Almaken, and Eritrospermum-35). abstract: Background Improving the deployment of helitack crews is crucial for limiting the growth of newly ignited wildfires. Aims We evaluated whether an optimization model could improve deployment in areas where high-intensity fires could occur compared with the current heuristic approach. abstract: Multifunctional and environmentally friendly hydrogel materials were developed through the reaction of chemically crosslinking biocompatible polymers and natural crosslinkers present in grape pomace, a waste product left over during the wine making process. abstract: Within safety practice and science there are countless ideas, approaches and concepts to manage safety. Some of these safety concepts are picked up, discussed widely and spread, while others do not. Little is known about this subject. This paper provides a unique perspective on the development and adoption of safety concepts by using an evolutionary framework to explore reasons why. title: From molecular advances to limited clinical impact: The persistent gap in chromoblastomycosis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chromoblastomycosis (CBM) is a chronic implantation mycosis of considerable morbidity, first described more than a century ago, predominantly affecting rural populations in tropical and subtropical regions. Although historically associated with impoverished settings, an increasing number of cases have been reported in both endemic and non-endemic areas, including high-income countries, reflecting an underrecognized epidemiological landscape. abstract: Phosphorus (P) - zinc (Zn) interactions regulate nutrient acquisition, physiological function, productivity, and seed nutritional quality. abstract: Abstract Conventional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) require metallic current collectors such as copper for anodes and aluminum for cathodes, adding significant weight without contributing to the capacity. This is especially problematic for Si-dominant anodes, with mass loadings lower than 2 mg cm–2. Here, copper is replaced with lightweight, non-woven carbon nanotube fabrics (CNTfs) combined with high-capacity Si/PPAN active material to form a self-standing composite anode. title: Conservation agriculture optimizes soil nitrogen stabilization and availability to crops under rice-based cropping
abstract: Conservation agriculture (CA) is increasingly promoted in the Indo-Gangetic Plains to address sustainability challenges in soil-plant-environment system. Efficient nitrogen (N) management plan under CA is one of those challenges, which restricts its wider adoption. We hypothesized that appropriate CA management option optimizes the balance between soil N stabilization and N availability to crops. title: A study of the greenhouse gas emissions inventory and driving factors decomposition in Tongzhou, China
abstract: Abstract District-and county-level greenhouse gas (GHG) inventories remain insufficiently developed, limiting the formulation of targeted mitigation policies at the grassroots governance scale. Taking Tongzhou District, Beijing, as a representative rapidly urbanizing megacity sub-center, this study developed an integrated district-level GHG emissions inventory covering energy activities, agricultural production, LUCF, and waste treatment from 2018 to 2020, and applied the Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) method to identify sector-specific driving mechanisms. title: Predicting connectivity from movement trajectories and step selection
abstract: Predicting and mapping connectivity are essential for ecology and conservation in the face of environmental change. Yet connectivity modeling is challenging because it requires understanding how organisms successfully move across complex landscapes. GPS tracking increasingly produces detailed data on movement trajectories and fine‐scale resource selection, yet it remains unclear how to reliably link such data to connectivity models without relying on individual‐based simulations. title: Green synthesized silver nanoparticles from floral waste of Tagetes patula for mitigation of Meloidogyne incognita stress in tomato plants
abstract: Meloidogyne incognita ( M. incognita ) is a destructive plant parasitic nematode causing severe crop losses worldwide. This study aims to evaluate the potential of Tagetes patula - mediated silver nanoparticles (TP@Ag NPs) as an eco-friendly nematicidal and plant growth-promoting agent against M. incognita infection in Solanum lycopersicum L. seedlings. abstract: Reconstructing the dietary and habitat preferences of extinct taxa is essential to understand the selective pressures that drive morphological and behavioral evolution, which provides a necessary framework for understanding macroevolutionary patterns and how extinct lineages navigated ecological shifts across time and space. This study examines the degree to which environmental changes influence dietary intake by analysing dental microwear in Heteroxerus rubricati , an extinct xerine squirrel from the Middle Miocene (Aragonian) of the Iberian Peninsula. abstract: Coriander has become increasingly significant from both economic and nutritional perspectives owing to the biologically active compounds obtained from its powdered fruits, dried extracts, herbal infusions, tinctures, and decoctions. To identify high-quality coriander (Coriandrum sativum) genotypes, 160 genetic materials were grown under the same environmental conditions and comprehensively analyzed in terms of numerous morphological, agronomic, essential oil, and essential oil component characteristics. title: Sun Protection Behaviors of Adolescents Diagnosed with Cancer and Their Healthy Peers
abstract: Background: Skin cancer is a major public health problem worldwide. It is important to determine adolescents’ sun protection behaviors and develop protective behaviors to prevent skin cancer and sun-related skin problems that may occur in later life.Objectives: The aim of this study was to evaluate the sun protection self-efficacy, decision balance perceptions, and sun protection behaviors of adolescents diagnosed with cancer (ADC), the factors affecting these behaviors, and the difference between the variables in ADC and their healthy peers.Methods: This descriptive, cross-sectional, and comp

title: Uncorking Quantitative and Qualitative Seminal Traits in French-Alpine Bucks via Carbetocin Stimulation to Enhance Goat Production in Semi-Arid Environments
abstract: Optimizing semen collection is critical for maximizing genetic advancement and reproductive efficiency in livestock. While exogenous hormones can enhance ejaculate quantity and quality, short windows of biological activity often limit their efficacy. This study was conducted in northern-arid Mexico (25° N, 103 W) to evaluate the comparative effects of oxytocin (OXYT) and carbetocin (CARB) administration on semen quality in French-Alpine bucks. title: Heavy metal contamination in branded and non-branded turmeric powder from Khulna, Bangladesh: Exposure assessment and potential carcinogenic risk
abstract: Turmeric is vulnerable to heavy metal contamination due to metal uptake from contaminated soils, irrigation water, post-harvest processing or via adulteration. This research assessed the concentrations of heavy metals (Pb, Cr, Cd, Mn, Cu) alongside non-carcinogenic and carcinogenic risks in fifteen non-branded and five branded powdered turmeric samples acquired from eight sampling locations in Khulna, Bangladesh. abstract: Infectious disease severity, shedding, and within-host kinetics can vary substantially with exposure dose, inoculation route, and host factors. However, the relative contributions of these variables to infection heterogeneity remain poorly quantified because small sample sizes in controlled in vivo experiments limit their statistical power and scientific scope. abstract: BACKGROUND: Parents play a central role in shaping children's health behaviours and dietary habits. Previous research has provided insight into parents' feeding practices, especially regarding preschoolers. Less is known about how parents of 10-12-year-old children, whose fruit and vegetable (F&V) intake is particularly low relative to recommendations, perceive F&V and translate their intentions regarding F&V into everyday practices. title: The Genus Weissella: A Review of its Antimicrobial Potentials, Functional Characteristics and Uses in Food Biopreservation
abstract: Background and Aim: Heterofermentative lactic acid bacteria belonging to the Genus Weissella possess unique metabolic capabilities with distinct value for natural food preservation. This review has synthesized current insights into the physiological characteristics, antibacterial pathways and antifungal mechanisms of Weissella species, with their practical uses within diverse food systems and safety problems restricting their commercial adoption. abstract: Pink brinjal ( Solanum melongena L.) is a highly preferred and extensively cultivated vegetable crop in Jammu and Kashmir, yet its genetic improvement has been constrained by the limited availability of high-yielding cultivars and the paucity of genetic information for parental selection. abstract: Volcanic aquifers are globally important groundwater resources, but their pronounced heterogeneity arising from lava emplacement, volcanic facies, structural features, and differential weathering makes hydrogeological characterization challenging. This study presents a techno-economic and environmental assessment of the novel POTASSIAL process, an integrated, near-zero-waste flowsheet designed to recover potassium chloride (KCl), aluminum oxide (Al 2 O 3 ), and silicon carbide (SiC) from a K-feldspar concentrate. abstract: Abstract Transitioning to low-carbon sources is decisive for the sustainability of Green Silk Road economies, which are currently struggling with climate change and energy crises. This paper investigates the role of digital finance in advancing energy transformation across Green Silk Road economies, with a comparative focus on 76 advanced and 72 emerging economies from 2004 to 2023. abstract: Abstact Climate change education requires fostering students' skills in making informed decisions on climate-related actions. Thus, teacher education must equip teachers for such “climate action teaching” and may build on investigating teacher beliefs. abstract: Abstract The olive oil industry generates a significant amount of by-products during harvesting and oil extraction, creating environmental challenges while offering opportunities for valorization within livestock production systems. This review provides a structured synthesis of current knowledge on chemical composition, nutritional characteristics, bioactive properties, processing strategies, and feeding applications of major olive oil by-products, including olive pomace, olive cake, olive leaves, and olive mill wastewater. abstract: Hamlet, staged in Moscow on 8 January 1912, is one of the most celebrated and extensively studied theatrical productions of the twentieth century, as it brought together the co-director of the Moscow Art Theatre, Konstantin Sergeevich Stanislavsky, and the English director Edward Gordon Craig. abstract: The composition of a polyclonal antibody response is hard to measure experimentally but contains vital information about the robustness of immunity. abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) are fast becoming a general interface to sound, yet how far their broad pretraining carries into specialized domains remains largely open. abstract: We study the role of momentum fractionation in the development of chaos on smooth 3-charge supergravity solutions of D1-D5 theory, specifically momentum-fractionated superstrata. abstract: Magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) is an optical probe of orbital time reversal symmetry breaking. Although frequency integrated MCD is related to the self-rotation contribution to orbital magnetization at zero field, its magnetic response generally differs from the thermodynamic orbital susceptibility. abstract: We propose a protocol to prepare and probe dark states in a single-molecule electron spin resonance based on atomic force microscopy (ESR-AFM), thus extending existing techniques developed to address Rabi oscillations. abstract: Earthquake preparation involves progressive damage accumulation, strain localization, and changes in the organization of seismicity. We investigate preparatory processes preceding seven episodes of major earthquakes in the Kuril - Kamchatka subduction zone during 2014 - 2025, including the 29 July 2025 MW 8.8 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake. abstract: Lithium-rich cathodes boast a large specific capacity due to the presence of excess lithium per transition metal. abstract: Cooperative behavior can improve environmental quality, whereas selfish defection can degrade shared resources. abstract: EnRoute is an iOS application designed to support more sustainable everyday choices in transportation and fast fashion consumption. We describe three design iterations and the user research and field evaluations that shaped each one. abstract: We produce degenerate photon pairs called signal and idler via parametric down-conversion (PDC) in a Fabry-Pérot waveguide resonator having close to a 2GHz bandwidth in the telecom C-band. abstract: Epithelial tissues play a fundamental role in morphogenesis. Mechanically they can be viewed as thin soft materials exhibiting a solid-fluid duality. abstract: Large language models (LLMs) should abstain from scientific multiple-choice questions when no option is valid, but frequent abstention alone does not demonstrate sensitivity to answer availability. abstract: Hour-long videos, streaming feeds, and movie-length content are pushing vision-language models (VLMs) past their breaking point -- the standard recipe of encoding each frame into visual tokens yields sequences that grow linearly with video length, causing prohibitive memory consumption and inference latency. abstract: The 2026 measles resurgence in Bangladesh motivates a spatial modelling framework that accounts for heterogeneous local transmission, vaccination activity, and interdivisional connectivity. We formulate a multipatch susceptible-vaccinated-infectious-recovered model for the eight administrative divisions of Bangladesh. abstract: Internet Exchange Points (IXPs) operate from colocation facilities that draw power from regional grids and store limited backup fuel. abstract: Marine fishery and aquaculture processing generate substantial volumes of biological byproducts—fish skin, bone, scales, and viscera—that remain underutilized as feedstocks for higher-value bio-based materials. abstract: The marine environment absorbs the largest share of the ecological burden generated by international shipping, an industry that carries over eighty per cent of global trade by volume. The International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships, 1973, as modified by the Protocol of 1978 (MARPOL 73/78), is the principal treaty addressing operational and accidental pollution from vessels, structured around six technical Annexes covering oil, noxious liquid substances, harmful packaged substances, sewage, garbage, and air pollution. title: Ireland & the Ocean: a decade dive review into Ocean Literacy
abstract: Human and natural systems are deeply interconnected, influencing one another for centuries. In recent decades, the protection of the marine environment has gained prominence, particularly following several reports linking climate change, biodiversity loss and ocean pollution to human health. Ocean Literacy (OL), a framework that promotes education for sustainable development (ESD) focused on the ocean, is emerging as a strategic bridge between education, sustainability, and public policy. While global attention in OL has increased, Ireland’s efforts are still fragmented, low and inconsistent.

abstract: Abstract This article examines the legal implications of autonomous fishing vessels ( AFV s) under the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea ( LOSC ). abstract: We read with great interest the report describing the first robotic totally endoscopic coronary artery bypass (TECAB) in Southeast Asia. abstract: Access to safe and reliable water remains a persistent challenge for rural communities in Malaysia, where infrastructural limitations, spatial constraints, and governance fragmentation continue to undermine water security. abstract: The Huhu grub ( Prionoplus reticularis ; Order: Coleoptera, Family: Cerambycidae, Subfamily: Prioninae - hereafter referred to as P. reticularis ) is an edible beetle larva endemic to Aotearoa New Zealand and has long been part of Māori food traditions. title: A validation framework for translating ethnomicrobiology into microbiome-enabled desert restoration
abstract: Microbiome-based dryland restoration is promising but weakly validated. We develop ethnomicrobiology, the study of how human communities manage microbial processes, as a discovery-and-validation framework. A structured evidence map of 42 systems shows food fermentation is most mature, whereas restoration practices lag. abstract: Communities on the frontlines of climate change face disproportionate risks of multiple hazards. Although community resilience depends on effective risk communication, most research focuses on the information that individuals receive from authorities rather than that which they produce or exchange themselves—that is, “community-based risk communication”. abstract: Abstract Vladimir Peniakoff’s Popski’s Private Army remains one of the most influential published accounts of the Libyan Arab Force (LAF) during the Second World War. This archive-led article reassesses Vladimir Peniakoff as a problematic source for the LAF, showing how his memoir preserved valuable traces of LAF activity while distorting chronology, agency, reputational memory and attribution. abstract: This paper presents a case study of the entrepreneur and landowner Anton Kajfež and his successors, owners of one of the largest companies in Kočevje and Lower Carniola before World War I and during the interwar period. abstract: Peatlands store approximately 30% of global terrestrial soil carbon, yet how subalpine peatlands respond to extreme drought remains poorly understood. abstract: Social science on wildfire has garnered increased attention with scholarship particularly focused on pre-fire and near-term impacts. However, the long-term impacts of wildfire and long-term recovery are less well understood and less represented in scholarship. This article takes up the questions of long-term wildfire recovery with special attention to time. title: Necropolitics under competitive authoritarianism: martyrdom, fatalism and contested responsibility for death in Turkey
abstract: Blame avoidance is usually theorized through democratic institutions, where elections, opposition parties, courts and independent media can contest official accounts of failure. This article extends blame avoidance theory to competitive authoritarianism by developing the concept of necropolitical blame avoidance: the conversion of responsibility-threatening deaths into governable objects of meaning, distribution and credit. abstract: This study examines the factors influencing tourist satisfaction with street food experiences in Hanoi from the perspective of sustainable tourism development. Although street food is widely recognized as a key component of Vietnam’s culinary tourism, empirical evidence remains limited for Hanoi, where long-standing culinary heritage coexists with rapid urbanization, increasing tourist demand, and challenges related to service consistency, hygiene, space management, and price transparency. abstract: Background: Hotel swimming pools are widely used for leisure, yet inadequate disinfection and maintenance can turn them into vehicles for recreational water illness. title: The Right to Communicate: UNESCO and the politics of global communication, 1969–1987
abstract: Abstract The Right to Communicate (RtC) is the idea that individuals possess not only the freedom to ‘seek, receive and impart information’, as laid down in Article 19 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR), but also the right to communicate horizontally with their peers, using technologies new and old. The brainchild of Jean d’Arcy, a French broadcaster and official who argued in 1969 that Article 19 should be updated to reflect the new technological possibilities, the concept inspired an international effort to write the RtC into human rights law. abstract: This article analyzes the impact of transport infrastructure on agricultural market integration and spatial inequalities in Benin. The data comes from the National Institute of Statistics and Demography (INSTaD) of Benin, collected between November 2025 and January 2026 from a sample of 1,920 households distributed across the country's twelve departments. It employs a spatial econometric model of the SDM type. abstract: Abstract Technical variability in pre-analytical and analytical steps significantly hinders the reproducibility of gut metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS). To address this, we developed and validated a practical mNGS workflow. First, by evaluating three commercial preservation buffers at 37°C, we identified Buffer C as the most effective for maintaining microbiome integrity under simulated transport stress. abstract: Objective(s): To characterize the structural chemistry, physicochemical properties, skin bioactivities, formulation aspects, sustainability, therapeutic applications, commercialization, and regulatory aspects of sophorolipids, rhamnolipids, and mannosylerythritol lipids as biosurfactants with focus on their potential in leave-on cosmetic and topical pharmaceutical formulations, as well as highlight research and development gaps. abstract: Consumer behavior represents a critical foundation for enterprises navigating an increasingly dynamic and competitive market environment. Purchasing decisions are not merely single-factor outcomes, but rather the result of complex interplay between service quality, price perception, product quality, and promotional strategies. This research aims to analyze consumer behavior towards purchasing decisions through a mixed-perspective approach combining qualitative literature analysis with empirical quantitative evidence using multiple linear regression. title: A Comprehensive Review on the Phytochemistry, Traditional Uses and Pharmacological Activities of Aegle Marmelos: Current Evidence and Future Perspectives
abstract: Aegle marmelos (L.) Correa (Rutaceae), commonly known as bael, is a medicinally important tree widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. Almost every plant part has been used in Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani medicine. This review systematically examines the botanical profile, ethnomedicinal uses, phytochemical composition and experimental pharmacological evidence for A. marmelos. Major bioactive classes include alkaloids (aegeline, skimmianine), coumarins (marmelosin, imperatorin, marmin, and marmesin), flavonoids (rutin, quercetin), phenolic acids and terpenoids. Pre

title: From Tito's Yugoslavia to the Bolivarian republic: A history of diplomatic, economic, military, and non-aligned-movement-mediated relations between Serbia and Venezuela (1950- 2026)
abstract: Serbia and Venezuela maintain one of the oldest formally established relationships between Southeast Europe and Latin America — dating, by the Serbian foreign ministry's own record, to 13 April 1882 — yet no dedicated peer-reviewed study of the dyad exists in any lan- guage, a gap this review both documents and begins to fill (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Serbia, 2026; Simić, 2024). The aim of the article is to reconstruct the diplomatic, economic, military, and Non-Aligned-Movement-mediated history of the relationship across 1950–2026 and to explain its paradoxical structure

title: Ferroptosis in cancer: molecular mechanisms, tumour microenvironment, therapeutic resistance, and clinical translation
abstract: Ferroptosis is a distinct form of regulated cell death driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation and oxidative membrane damage, and it differs fundamentally from apoptosis, necroptosis, and pyroptosis in its molecular mechanisms and execution pathways. Increasing evidence indicates that ferroptosis plays a pivotal role in cancer biology by regulating tumour initiation, progression, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and interactions within the tumour microenvironment (TME). title: Singing Homer : Modern Greek songs, digital literacy, and the experiential reception of the epics in secondary education
abstract: Abstract This article reports on Singing Homer , a two-year cultural project (2021–2023) in a Greek lower-secondary school that engaged students with the Iliad and the Odyssey through modern Greek songs. The project addressed persistent challenges in teaching Homer – linguistic difficulty, cultural distance, and questions of curricular relevance – by introducing music as a medium of reception and reinterpretation, through which students connected modern musical narratives with Homeric figures and themes. abstract: Abstract Why do some regions achieve higher levels of economic development while others do not? This paper introduces the Agglomeration-Clustering-Knowledge Spillovers (AC-KS) model, a conceptual framework for better understanding the nature of such differences. We argue that the missing piece of this puzzle is the process by which localized anchors ignite dynamic triangular forces between agglomeration, clustering, and knowledge spillovers, setting in motion a life cycle of first- and second-generation knowledge spillover effects. title: "Aragwadhadi Avaleha as a Virechaka Yoga: a Comprehensive Review"
abstract: Virechana Karma (therapeutic purgation) represents one of the principal bio-purification procedures (Panchakarma) in Ayurvedic medicine, specifically designed to eliminate vitiated Pitta dosha and associated morbid substances through the anal route.Aragwadhadi Avaleha, a classical Ayurvedic formulation documented in the Charaka Samhita Kalpa Sthana, stands as a significant Virechaka Yoga (purgative preparation) that combines three potent ingredients: Aragwadha (Cassia fistula Linn.), Trivrut (Operculina turpethum Linn.), and Guda (jaggery).This comprehensive review aims to systematically analy

abstract: This study examined the physicochemical, mineral, and bacterial profiles of multifloral honeys from Apis mellifera L. collected from different agro-climatic zones of Himachal Pradesh, India. Of the total honey samples, 26 were identified as multifloral based on melissopalynological analysis. title: Iranophobia in Trump’s Social Media: Corpus-Assisted Critical Discourse Analysis
abstract: Strained diplomatic relations between Iran and the United States have historically been characterised by ongoing strife, involving sensitive issues like nuclear programs, economic penalties, and Middle Eastern power struggles. abstract: Frontline service workers and/or their supervisors delivering clearly inaccurate, bad, and/or unlawful service to customers or other “persons of interest” (POI) that causally precedes negative outcomes is one category of shitshow service-failure performance. abstract: Phenolic and flavonoid content extractions from Homalomena occulta are important ingredients in traditional Vietnamese medicine with bioactivities such as antiinflammatory, antibacterial, and antioxidant properties. abstract: Historians routinely put the 1926 British General Strike into a British historical context stretching back to the First World War and before. More rarely historians look forward to the consequences of the Strike and to how it has been remembered. This article puts the British Strike into an international context and considers its consequences and the memory of it into the twenty-first century. abstract: The compressive strength of concrete is a critical parameter that governs the safety and durability of reinforced concrete structures. In Nigeria, the frequent collapse of buildings has been largely attributed to the use of substandard construction materials, particularly poor quality concrete aggregates. This study presents a comparative analysis of the compressive strength of concrete produced with coarse aggregates obtained from different sources in Nigeria, with the aim of evaluating their suitability for structural applications. abstract: The present study investigated problematic exercise from a qualitative perspective. It critically examined the conventional primary-secondary addiction dichotomy’s conceptual validity and proposes alternative frameworks for a more nuanced understanding. abstract: Abstract We argue that Kant’s Formula of Humanity (FH) should be expanded to provide a more nuanced analysis of complex real-world cases of mistreatment. Migrants are not only mistreated due to their perceived instrumental value (as a mere means) but also by treating them as of no value (as a mere thing) or mistreating them due to perceived instrumental or intrinsic disvalue (as a mere threat). abstract: Central areolar choroidal dystrophy (CACD) is a rare monogenic hereditary retinal dystrophy characterised by progressive retinal pigment epithelium and choriocapillaris atrophy, photoreceptor loss, oxidative stress, and chronic inflammation. Emerging evidence suggests that the gut microbiota can modulate systemic inflammatory responses and may influence ocular health through the gut-eye axis. abstract: Consumer goods firms face a persistent tension between supply chain resilience and operating efficiency. Existing resilience research explains many of the capabilities firms require, but provides less guidance on when those capabilities should be activated as disruption conditions change. This study addresses that temporal gap by extending the Contextualized Resilience-Agility Architecture (CRAA) through a temporal ambidexterity perspective. abstract: This study examined the influence of respective factors of wealth creation on designated measures of entrepreneurial performance of pig farmers in South-South, Nigeria. Specifically, it established a nexus between financial capital and market share; human capital and turnover; social capital and customer satisfaction; and intellectual capital and customer loyalty; respectively. abstract: This study investigates the conflicting lenses through which Bible believers in the Bamenda Urban Sphere, Cameroon, interpret Scripture and the resulting implications for their spiritual, economic and sociopolitical life. abstract: Reliable bedrock-depth information is essential for foundation design and seismic site characterization, yet borehole-only investigations provide sparse coverage and active-source surface-wave surveys may lack the low-frequency energy needed to resolve deeper interfaces. Insufficient knowledge regarding the effects of herbal raw materials, as well as their potential adverse effects and interactions with medications and food, poses a considerable risk in therapies involving these products. abstract: Global dry land agricultural systems face intensifying structural and climatic pressures, demanding innovative soil management paradigms to sustain crop productivity and preserve scarce hydrological and nutritional resources. Conventional tillage (CT) practices, characterized by intensive mechanical soil inversion, accelerate the oxidation of soil organic matter, disrupt macro-pore continuity, and generate high subsoil bulk density that limits water permeability and exacerbates terminal drought vulnerability. abstract: This study investigates the relative influence of liquidity measures and traditional accounting variables used in the Ohlson model of equity valuation (earnings and book equity per share) on corporate valuation in the Nigerian capital market. To conduct the investigation, the study collected data for 38 listed Nigerian companies from 2014 to 2024, using FGLS for baseline regression, with the BC-MM and PCSE estimators for robustness and sensitivity analyses. abstract: Abstract Cacti develop spines instead of conventional leaves, which often serve as mechanical defence against herbivores and protection from excess sunlight. abstract: The Swedish Infrastructure for Medical Population-based Life-course and Environmental Research (SIMPLER) is a national research infrastructure that provides longitudinal data and biological samples to investigate how dietary, lifestyle, environmental, and genetic factors influence health and disease across the life course. title: Light as a control variable in the green synthesis of silver and gold nanoparticles: Phytochemical mechanisms, tunability, and applications
abstract: Plant-mediated synthesis has become a sustainable route to silver and gold nanoparticles, in which phytochemicals act as reducing and stabilizing agents under mild conditions. While pH, temperature, precursor concentration, and extract composition are well-characterized control variables, illumination is still typically treated as a fixed background condition rather than a tunable design parameter. title: The ubiquitin–proteasome system and proteostasis in the cochlea and sensorineural hearing disorders
abstract: The ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) is the major machinery for intracellular protein degradation, playing an indispensable role in maintaining proteostasis across all tissues. Sensorineural hearing loss affects billions of people worldwide and is characterized by the irreversible degeneration of cochlear hair cells and spiral ganglion neurons. However, effective treatments remain unavailable. Although UPS dysfunction has been increasingly recognized in aging and neurodegenerative diseases, its specific contributions to cochlear development, homeostasis, and hearing disorders have received re

title: Electrostatic control of chromatin compaction safeguards against apoptotic DNA release
abstract: Apoptosis involves extensive intracellular reorganisation to facilitate the clearance of dying cells. A key step in this process is the destruction of the genome through fragmentation by caspase-activated DNase (CAD). Rather than dispersing after CAD-mediated cleavage, DNA fragments are compacted into a dense chromatin compartment, but the underlying mechanism and biological relevance of this compaction remain unknown. title: Psychosocial Harm as an Inequality Regime at Work: Intersectional Accounts From Portugal
abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines psychosocial harm at work as a sociological problem of inequality rather than only an issue of individual stress. Drawing on Acker's concept of inequality regimes together with minority stress and intersectionality, and based on 60 in‐depth interviews with workers in Portugal, it analyses how overload, insecurity, work‐family conflict, poor leadership, and weak reporting systems are organized through gendered, heteronormative, racialized, and migration‐related relations of power. Reflexive thematic analysis developed three themes: the organization of harm through

title: Growth, biomass productivity, nitrogen uptake and use efficiency of selected enset clones in southern Ethiopia
abstract: Enset ( Ensete ventricosum ) is a staple food crop for over 20 million people in southern Ethiopia. As climate change intensifies, its importance for food security increases, and its cultivation is also expanding into new territories such as the warmer and drier lowlands. This study evaluated the responses of two enset clones (Ganticho and Nifo) to six different integrated soil fertility management (ISFM) alternatives on establishment, vegetative growth, biomass production, nitrogen uptake, nitrogen use efficiency (NUE), biomass partitioning, and soil chemical properties. A factorial experimen

title: Why 3D Reconstruction Breaks Down on Under-Ice AUV Video, and How to Predict It
abstract: Reconstruction of 3D structures using under-ice AUV video footage has been inaccurate, although it is not certain whether this is due to shortcomings in the methods or an inherent deficiency of the capture system. We test four different models for reconstruction on the same Antarctic under-ice AUV video (Icefin, Kamb Ice Stream): classical feature matching SfM, differentiable photometric splatting, volumetric depth fusion, and a pose-free feed-forward foundation model. All four fail, each in a distinct way: near-total registration yielding almost no structure, geometrically broken output despi

title: WorldBench: Evaluating LLMs on Three.js Voxel World Generation
abstract: Large language models can now write complete, interactive 3D worlds as code, but grading those worlds automatically is unreliable. Existing judges take one view of the output: a vision-language model scores a few rendered snapshots, or a language model reads the source. On worlds written by five frontier models we find that the two views disagree on 32% of required items, mostly code that no frame shows, and that fixed views miss small close-up contents. We present WorldBench, a benchmark and judge for open-ended, LLM-generated Three.js worlds. From one prompt describing a floating voxel islan

title: Magnonic cavity-enhanced quantum magnetometry with nitrogen-vacancy centre ensembles
abstract: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centre ensembles are leading room-temperature magnetometers, but their sensitivity is usually extracted from a single resonance and relies on external microwave and bias-field hardware. This work proposes a chip-scale NV magnetometer built around a one-dimensional YIG/CoFeB magnonic crystal, in which a single structural defect forms a passive magnonic cavity and integrated permanent magnets supply the bias field. Micromagnetic simulations show a defect-localised spin-wave mode at 2.910 GHz inside the 2.5-3.0 GHz magnonic band gap, 40 MHz from the NV zero-field splitting,

title: The grounded spirituality of mathematics
abstract: We propose that mathematics is done largely as a means of both coping with and celebrating our physicality in the natural world. Inspired by David Abram's "Becoming Animal", we suggest that -- in opposition to the popular image of an otherworldy Platonic realm-- the spiritual component of doing mathematics is grounded on and in the Earth. We explore this as a means of questioning the widespread adoption of AI in the workflows of research mathematics.

title: VulnBump: A Benchmark for Fixing Vulnerable Dependencies in Real Projects While Keeping the Build and Tests Green
abstract: Software composition analysis (SCA) tools report far more vulnerable dependencies than teams fix: in Snyk Open Source production data, 94% of vulnerability findings have a known fixed version, yet only about 10% are resolved. Agentic coding tools could close this gap, but no benchmark evaluates them on vulnerability-driven upgrades in real, runnable projects across ecosystems, verified independently of the agent. We present VulnBump: 307 upgrade tasks covering 2,066 fixable vulnerabilities in 43 repositories across six package managers, matched to Snyk Open Source production vulnerability dist

title: HGP:An on-device personalized agent memory via hybrid graph storage
abstract: LLM-based agents face challenges in personalized interactive tasks due to heterogeneous, multi-typed, and implicitly constrained long-term traces. Existing memory mechanisms struggle with accurate routing and retrieval, especially on-device where personalization is critical. Most methods use single-vector representations, blurring type distinctions and relational structure. We propose HGP, a hybrid graph memory framework. HGP employs a lightweight self-enhancement classifier for personalized memory routing and constructs episodic, semantic, and procedural memories as graphs. It also extracts w

Lumen-bench: Cross-Lingual Safety Gaps and the Say-Do Problem in Tool-Calling Large Language Models
abstract: When a large language model refuses an unethical request, what does refusal mean? In conversation, refusal is bounded by what the model says; once the model is equipped with executable tools, what it does can diverge from what it says, a failure mode that English-only evaluations cannot fully reveal. We introduce Lumen-bench, a behavioral benchmark of tool-calling ethics spanning 30 models, five languages (Portuguese, English, Spanish, Mandarin Chinese, Hindi), 108 Portuguese-authored scenarios, six social-pressure conditions, two system prompts (ethical and neutral), and 21 generic tools. title: Type $B$- and $C$- trigonometric weight functions
abstract: We introduce and study trigonometric weight functions of type $B$ and type $C$ arising from integrable lattice models. These functions give $q$-deformations of the factorial $K$-theoretic Schur $P$- and $Q$-functions of Ikeda and Naruse, with the $P$-functions specialized to the type $B$ case. We realize them as specializations of partition functions of a six-vertex model with triangular boundary conditions and derive their algebraic properties using the Yang-Baxter equation and properties of the $R$- and $K$-matrices. title: The Missile and the Toll: Two-Way Flow Through the Strait of Hormuz
abstract: Tolls for safe passage and attacks on shipping are usually treated as mutually exclusive: either ships pay or attacks happen. We argue they are complementary. In a Stackelberg escalation game for the Strait of Hormuz, the enforcer chooses an attack intensity and a toll schedule; the response is to pay, cross exposed, wait, reroute, or exit. Attacks create the willingness to pay; tolls harvest it. The model predicts asymmetry across trade forms: a toll where the cargo owner can pay and the vessel owner will consent, and none where either fails. Any such payment is clandestine, but the model's i

title: Adapting English Quality Classifiers for Multilingual LLM Pretraining Data Selection
abstract: Recent advances in large language model (LLM) pretraining highlight the role of high-quality training data in improving performance. While model-based filtering has proven effective in selecting high-quality subsets from web-scale corpora, especially for high-resource languages, low-resource languages face challenges due to limited availability of annotated data. This work explores extending quality filtering to over 100 languages by proposing a multilingual adaptation approach that converts an existing English quality classifier into a multilingual variant. Our approach proposes training a sm

title: Social Priors: Descriptions of AI Users Shape How Language Models Trust and Cooperate
abstract: Descriptions of how people use AI are becoming training data for the next generation of models. We ask whether what a model reads about its users changes how it treats people. Using contrastive synthetic-document finetuning, we train Qwen3-32B on four matched corpora built from the same 1,625 real-world usage scenarios. The corpora differ only in the predominant motive they attribute to users of AI chatbots: helping others (prosocial), exploiting others (antisocial), legitimate self-advancement, or task completion. Finetuning shifts the models' stated beliefs about users, how true those belief

title: From Product Evidence to Access Rights: Auditing and Routing Non-Firm Grid Connections
abstract: Non-firm connection products can accelerate grid access while reinforcements are delayed, but their planning value depends on evidence supporting the contractual promise. We develop a one-way evidence-to-access framework for calendarized products. Stage A constructs and fixes directional restriction calendars from public residual-load and day-ahead price-timing signals. Stage B audits the submitted calendar and one bounded common repair, tests joint threshold attainability under the shared annual budget, and applies an aggregation-aware Power Transfer Distribution Factor (PTDF) certificate. title: The Curse of Knowledge in Role-Playing Language Models
abstract: Role-playing language models speak as characters in games and agent simulations, where the system records what each character can hear, see and understand. We test whether characters respect these boundaries in 480 scenes, each with a counterfactual twin that changes only the hidden fact, so mentions of the twin's fact measure guessing. Across 11 open-weight models, characters use content from speech they cannot understand or hear at 67 and 72 percentage points (pp) above this baseline, although most models correctly state what the character perceives. title: Sociotechnical Aspects of Tor Relay Rejection
abstract: In 2019, the Tor Project enforced an end-of-life (EoL) policy for Tor versions, leading to the rejection of outdated relays, amounting to a notable fraction of consensus weight. While this policy aids network maintenance, reduces backporting efforts, and shortens vulnerability exposure, its sociotechnical implications remain unstudied.

title: Electromagnetic isospin breaking in hadronic vacuum polarization within a VMD model
abstract: One of the challenging components of modern lattice-QCD computations of the leading hadronic vacuum polarization contribution to the muon $(g-2)_μ$ is the isospin-breaking correction due to electromagnetism. Dominated by long distances, this correction suffers from severe signal-to-noise issues and finite-volume effects. To provide infinite-volume benchmarks for various quark-level Wick contractions, we estimate their sizes phenomenologically at the physical point, using a previously developed vector-meson-dominance model. title: Which Knowledge Should LLMs Trust? Uncovering a Generalizable Steering Direction Across Knowledge Conflicts
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) frequently encounter conflicts between internal parametric knowledge and external contextual knowledge, yet the mechanisms governing this selection remain unclear. We show that the choice between context and parametric knowledge is linearly represented and can be controlled along a single direction in the model's residual stream. We first demonstrate that this direction generalizes across factual-conflict settings, including context formats, knowledge categories, and datasets, while consistently shifting behavior between parametric and contextual answers. title: SoK: Privacy-Preserving Order Matching
abstract: Privacy-preserving order matching enables traders to discover and execute compatible orders while limiting disclosure of sensitive trading information. Existing systems span financial markets and blockchain-based asset exchanges and employ diverse market structures, privacy mechanisms, and trust assumptions, making their privacy guarantees difficult to compare. We present a systematization of privacy-preserving order matching covering 22 protocol families. title: A low-cost compact muon detector for millikelvin operation
abstract: Ionizing radiation produces correlated errors in superconducting qubits, posing some challenges to quantum error correction. In addition, it causes background events in other superconducting cryogenic devices, such as kinetic inductance detectors and superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors. Cosmic muons are a component of this background that can only be partly shielded against at ground level, but can be tagged by an independent detector inside the cryostat, so that the affected data can be vetoed, or the muon tags incorporated into error correction. We present a low-cost, compact mu

title: The Constitution Speaks Nheengatu: An Open MT System and Reproducible Corpus Pipeline for the Amazonian Língua Geral
abstract: Nheengatu (yrl), the Amazonian Língua Geral, has 6--10 thousand speakers and is co-official in São Gabriel da Cachoeira (Brazil), yet remains poorly served by evaluated Portuguese--Nheengatu MT resources. We present the largest parallel corpus assembled for the language (14.5k Portuguese--Nheengatu pairs), anchored by the 2023 official translation of the Brazilian Federal Constitution; the first MT evaluation set built from transcribed spontaneous speech; and, to our knowledge, the first open-weight MT models dedicated to bidirectional Portuguese--Nheengatu translation. title: ALP interactions with mesons and baryons at $\mathcal{O}(1/f_a)$: a general field redefinition invariant approach
abstract: We develop a field-redefinition-invariant description of hadronic amplitudes outside the WZW sector at $\mathcal{O}(1/f_a)$, including general flavour-conserving and flavour-changing quark couplings. Starting from the most general CP-conserving Lagrangian for ALP interactions with the QCD sector, we identify invariant Wilson coefficient combinations and match them onto the $U(3)$ chiral theory. title: Constrained Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning in Imagination
abstract: Predicting cost in a multi-agent world model moves most constrained policy updates into imagination: the stronger model-free baseline needs $10$ to $20$ times CA-MAMBA's interactions on the median SMAC configuration, and CA-MAMBA earns $2.8$ to $12$ times the baselines' MAMuJoCo reward at equal budget. In controlled tests on one task per benchmark, pricing the model's cost advantages at parity more than halves a cost-blind learner's cost and meets a tight continuous-control limit the learned multiplier misses, suggesting the model's cost estimates are not the bottleneck.

title: Translation Tag Team: Formal Rules and LLMs Translate More Macros Together Than Apart
abstract: Modern critical software infrastructure is largely written in C. Since C lacks memory safety, researchers are investigating automatic translation of C to safer languages like Rust. But real-world C software consists of more than just C code, often using named code fragments called macros which are not part of the C language proper. State-of-the-art techniques avoid translating macros by preprocessing C code first before translating it. title: A Comprehensive Interpretation of the LZ High-Energy Recoil Event: A Minimal $U(1)_B$ Dark Sector and Its Experimental Tests
abstract: The $248$ keV nuclear-recoil candidate reported by LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) motivates an inelastic dark matter (DM) interpretation, in which scattering converts the DM particle into a slightly heavier state. We provide a comprehensive study of this interpretation in an anomaly-free model of gauged baryon number, where a new vector boson, $Z_B$, mediates interactions between DM and quarks. Breaking the baryonic gauge symmetry generates the new particle masses and a small splitting between two DM states, while a residual symmetry keeps the lighter state stable. title: ENSO-Flavor Differences in Indonesian Marine Heatwaves: Satellite SST, Physical Covariates, and Coral Habitat Suitability
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) in the Indonesian Seas develop within a long-term rise in sea surface temperature and strong interannual climate variability. We analyze daily NOAA Optimum Interpolation Sea Surface Temperature version 2.1 for 1982–2022 and compare five Eastern-Pacific (EP) with five Central-Pacific (CP) El Niño events. MHWs are detected against a fixed 1982–2011 baseline, and each event is represented by the common 1 July–30 June window spanning its developing and decaying phases. title: Phenology of spring phytoplankton bloom in the marine waters around Kamchatka
abstract: Timing and other phenological parameters of the spring phytoplankton bloom in the waters around Kamchatka are determined on long-term satellite-derived data for chlorophyll a concentration obtained in 1998–2024. Three methods of the timing determining are compared, as the biomass threshold, the cumulative biomass threshold, and the maximum biomass growth rate; finally, a modified threshold method is proposed, more suitable for the study area. title: Microbial deamination of peptides and proteins as a source of persistent marine dissolved organic matter
abstract: Abstract Refractory dissolved organic nitrogen is a major component of the ocean's nitrogen pool, yet the mechanisms producing and preserving it remain poorly understood. Here, we show that deaminated peptides (DAPs), derived from microbial processing of proteinaceous material, are ubiquitous across oxygenated marine environments—from productive coastal waters to the oligotrophic ocean—and persist from surface to bathypelagic depths. title: UAV-based super-resolution instance segmentation enables ecological monitoring of sea cucumbers in shallow coral reef habitats
abstract: Accurate monitoring of sea cucumbers from UAV imagery remains challenging because submerged individuals often exhibit low contrast, camouflage against coral-rubble backgrounds, and weak boundary information under water-surface disturbance. In particular, key visual cues such as body contours, surface texture, and papillae-like structures can be severely blurred in aerial images, limiting the reliability of automated recognition. abstract: Creating high-precision bathymetric models continues to be a major challenge, especially in complex environments where numerous factors restrict data gathering. To address these issues, this study introduces and evaluates a weighted average data fusion method. The approach was implemented during a comprehensive measurement campaign, in which weights were assigned to each dataset according to its estimated accuracy. title: Species-specific phenological indicators reveal topographic–climatic associations with evergreen-tree phenology in subtropical hilly regions
abstract: Evergreen-tree phenology is an important ecological indicator of forest responses to climate change and local environmental heterogeneity. In subtropical hilly regions, frequent cloudy and rainy conditions, complex terrain, and weak seasonal greenness signals hinder species-level phenological retrieval and interpretation. Here, we evaluated the ecological indicator value of the start of season (SOS), end of season (EOS), and length of season (LOS) for eight representative evergreen tree species in Xiamen, Fujian Province, China. title: Improved low-noise waveform feature purification processing for low-signal-to-noise ratio sub-bottom profile data and its application in marine placer exploration
abstract: Sub-bottom profile (SBP) measurement is a widely used hydroacoustic geophysical method for continuous imaging of submarine stratigraphy. Conventional processing pipelines rely on basic filtering and envelope extraction, which fail to handle field data with waveform clipping, repeated navigation coordinates, and heavy background noise. Existing commercial seismic software and published algorithms are mainly designed for conventional seismic data and lack customized processing frameworks adapted to high-frequency SBP signals with instrument-specific distortions. abstract: Developing fully reprocessable engineered wood composites (EWCs) with high mechanical strength under mild fabrication conditions remains a significant challenge. Here, a hyperbranched adhesive with complementary imine-bond and hydrogen-bond networks was designed and combined with wood particles to fabricate a wood composite (WP/HTP) by hot pressing at 120°C. title: Development of a Towing System Design Program Based on the U.S. Navy Towing Manual
abstract: Marine towing is required for transporting ships and floating structures and for salvage operations of damaged vessels. Safe towing operations require the estimation of towing resistance, selection of an appropriate tug and towing equipment, and verification of the towing system. However, the design procedure based on the U.S. Navy Towing Manual involves repeated manual calculations using tables, curves, and empirical criteria, which can be time-consuming and prone to reading errors. title: Multiobjective Optimization of Cross-Flow Membrane Channel Geometry via Integrated CFD Modeling and RSM-Desirability Function Analysis
abstract: Abstract Pressure-driven membrane separation processes are pivotal for seawater desalination and wastewater recovery. However, the geometric configuration of the flow channel strongly influences mass-transfer performance and energy consumption. This study applies an integrated three-dimensional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and response surface methodology (RSM) framework to optimize length-to-height (L/H) and length-to-width (L/W) ratios of cross-flow membrane channels for concentration polarization (CP) mitigation and hydraulic pressure drop (ΔP) reduction. title: A new piece in the puzzle: The palaeoecological significance of bryozoans over 7000 years in Daidokutsu Cave (Okinawa, Japan)
abstract: ABSTRACT Submarine caves are cryptic, climatically sensitive habitats with long‐term ecological dynamics that are poorly understood. We present the first palaeoecological analysis of bryozoans from Daidokutsu Cave (Okinawa, Japan), based on a sediment core spanning approximately the last 7000 years. We quantify temporal changes in bryozoan diversity, taxonomic and functional composition, and community turnover, comparing these with published records for ostracods, foraminifera and bivalves, as well as independent environmental proxies, that are, δ 18 O as a proxy for East Asian Winter Monsoon

abstract: The methods used in monitoring the increasing drought are vitally significant. In order to determine and monitor drought, many scientific studies have been carried out in our country, especially using the standardized precipitation index (SPI). However, due to increasing temperatures and evaporation, there is a need for studies showing the spatio-temporal change of drought at the country scale according to the standardized precipitation evapotranspiration index (SPEI), which also takes evaporation into account. abstract: Migration into Sahul is one of the earliest migrations which required open-sea voyages. Two primary routes from Sunda-the northern and southern routes-have been proposed, yet the details of human dispersal into and within Sahul remain unclear. title: Institutional Strengthening of Mama-Mama Papua in the Development of Ikan Asar Businesses Based on Local Resources: A Study of the Kampung Bright Gas Program in Imbi Village, Jayapura
abstract: Ikan asar (smoke fish) processing industry is one of the growing local economic sectors in the coastal area of Dok 8, Imbi Village, Jayapura City. For the local community, particularly coastal women known as the “Mama-Mama Papua,” smoked fish holds not only economic value but also serves as a distinctive feature of the local community, representing food processing knowledge passed down through generations and forming an integral part of the social and cultural life of the coastal community. title: Enabling global prediction of marsh vegetation survival during extreme storms
abstract: Flood protection by coastal vegetated systems depends on the persistence of vegetation structures, but it is currently impossible to predict vegetation survival during extreme storms. Using the largest artificially generated waves in the world, we here quantified the persistence of tidal marsh vegetation by measuring stem breakage of winter-state vegetation (3 species and mimics) during extreme storms with up to 2.0 m significant wave height, 4 m water level and 8 s peak period waves. title: Inside or out? Modeling climate effects on western Atlantic bluefin tuna distribution
abstract: The rapidly changing ocean environment is driving shifts in fish distribution, fishing effort, catch, and catch rates. Previous assessments of western Atlantic bluefin tuna have struggled to reconcile conflicting trends in US and Canadian catch per unit effort (CPUE) indices in the northwest Atlantic, likely due to changes in bluefin distribution in recent decades. The most recent stock assessment addressed this by using a time series of the Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation to modulate catchability for these indices and account for changes in fish availability.
