title: Super Warm Early Eocene Simulations With HadGEM3‐GC31‐LL
abstract: Abstract The early Eocene Climatic Optimum (EECO; 53.3–49.1 million years ago) represents the period of greatest sustained warmth in the Cenozoic (last 66 million years), with proxy‐data indicating global‐mean temperatures 10–16°C above preindustrial and atmospheric concentrations of 1,200–2,500 ppmv. This extreme greenhouse climate provides insights into Earth's climate sensitivity and feedback mechanisms and offers a stress‐test for evaluating climate models under vastly different boundary conditions. Here we present the first application of the HadGEM3‐GC31‐LL model to the super‐warm EECO.

title: Educating character, difference and the “great questions” curriculum
abstract: Purpose This article examines difference in interdisciplinary character education programs in higher, secondary and elementary education. Such successful “classical education” curricula focus on “Great Books” or “classics,” but their canon-based approaches have drawn criticism for difficulties with incorporating difference. The innovative, inquiry-driven “Great Questions” curriculum of Villanova University's Humanities major represents a “classical” approach that remains grounded within its formative Augustinian tradition while reflectively opening to noncanonical texts. title: Sai số nội suy hình học và khoảng cách tuyến trong khảo sát địa hình đáy
abstract: Khảo sát địa hình đáy là cơ sở quan trọng cho thiết kế và khai thác các công trình hàng hải. Tuy nhiên, độ chính xác của mô hình địa hình đáy không chỉ phụ thuộc vào sai số đo tại điểm mà còn chịu ảnh hưởng của sai số nội suy giữa các tuyến khảo sát, trong khi mối quan hệ này chưa được lượng hóa đầy đủ. Nghiên cứu này xây dựng một mô hình giải tích mô tả cơ chế hình thành sai số nội suy hình học trong khảo sát địa hình đáy. title: Lubricant-Engine Suitability Evaluation for Fuel Efficiency in Fishing VesselUsing Temperature and Color Degradation
abstract: Engine performance in fishing vessel depends on the reliability and efficiency of diesel engine, in which the lubrication system plays a key role in reducing friction, controlling operating temperature, and minimizing component wear. However, field observations in small-scale fisheries indicate that many fishermen select lubricants based on habit, price, or availability rather than manufacturer specifications, which may reduce engine efficiency and increase fuel consumption. title: PHOTOCHEMICAL DEGRADATION PATHWAYS OF LINEAR LOW DENSITY POLYETHYLENE REVEALED BY INTEGRATED FTIR, RAMAN, AND AI-ASSISTED SEM ANALYSIS
abstract: Linear low-density polyethylene (LLDPE) is the dominant polymer in agricultural films, mulch covers, and packaging throughout Ecuador and Latin America, where intensive agricultural economies drive high per-capita consumption. Its prolonged outdoor use under intense equatorial UV radiation accelerates photooxidative degradation, generating microplastic particles that have been detected in remote ecosystems including the Antarctic region, underscoring the global reach of local plastic degradation. title: Brief communication: Mass balance of glaciers in the Eastern Hindu Kush from 1979 to 2002 using KH-9 panoramic and SPOT-5 stereo imagery
abstract: Abstract. Glaciers exhibit region-specific mass loss patterns in response to ongoing climate change. In this study, we provide a geodetic mass balance assessment for glaciers within the Hindu Kush region spanning the period 1979–2002, utilizing KH-9 panoramic imagery and SPOT-5 stereo satellite imagery. Our analysis reveals a moderate mass loss of −0.13 ± 0.12 m w.e. a−1, a rate similar to post-2000 observations given their uncertainties. title: eDNA metabarcoding reveals invertebrate diversity in the blackwater pools of southeast Queensland peatlands
abstract: Despite harbouring a disproportionate diversity of rare and endemic species, the pyrophilic peatlands of southeast Queensland remain poorly characterized, particularly regarding their invertebrate communities. In the physically and chemically extreme blackwater pools, meiofaunal assemblages likely form critical trophic links but have never been described due to their small size and low public profile. abstract: The Horseshoe Canyon Formation in southern Alberta, Canada, preserves abundant plant fossils from the upper Campanian to upper Maastrichtian. However, studies describing the macroflora are taxonomically out of date, and limited work has been done to utilise the flora for palaeoclimatic reconstruction. Fifty-eight plant taxa are documented from the Morrin Bridge locality within the lower Maastrichtian Horsethief Member of the Horseshoe Canyon Formation. title: Dual Single Atoms Boosting Photocatalytic Upcycling of Raw Polyvinylidene Fluoride Plastic
abstract: ABSTRACT Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) is a highly recalcitrant fluorinated polymer that is highly resistant to chemical degradation, making its sustainable recycling and upcycling challenging. Despite its widespread use as a binder in the lithium‐ion battery industry, effective strategies for converting PVDF waste into value‐added chemicals remain limited. abstract: Abstract. Nitrous oxide (N2O) is the most dominant precursor of ozone-depleting substances and the third most important anthropogenic greenhouse gas, with agriculture contributing the largest share of emissions (56 %). Over the past two decades, airborne in-situ measurements have become increasingly important for studying emission and transport of N2O in the atmosphere, also driven by the development of more precise and simultaneously faster Quantum Cascade Laser (QCL)-based spectrometers. title: Necessity or Indulgence: Reconsidering Space Exploration
abstract: Taking the debate over whether space exploration constitutes a necessity or a mere indulgence as its starting point, this essay adopts a philosophical and interdisciplinary perspective to re-examine the value of human space activities inspired by the Pale Blue Dot photograph. The study breaks down the binary opposition between necessity and indulgence, arguing that this distinction is not purely economic but hinges on definitions of resource purposes and human civilisational goals. title: 3D crustal seismic structure of southern mainland Portugal from combined local earthquake and active source tomography
abstract: Summary We present P- and S-wave seismic tomographic models for southern mainland Portugal, specifically for the region south of the 39° N parallel. These models were obtained using local seismicity and wide-angle refracted and reflected seismic profiles, considering a spatial resolution of approximately 10 km in latitude and longitude, and 3 km in depth, the highest spatial resolution so far compared to previous models of similar or broader regional scope. title: Life Cycle Assessment of Virgin and Recycled Polypropylene Kitchenware in the UK: Impacts of Domestic Recycling, International Supply Chains, and Consumer Use
abstract: This study evaluates the cradle-to-grave environmental performance of polypropylene (PP) kitchenware in the United Kingdom (UK), addressing critical gaps in understanding how material choices, global supply chains, domestic recycling, and consumer use-phase practices interact. Four scenarios were assessed using life cycle assessment (LCA) modelling: virgin PP (vPP) manufactured in China and Germany, recycled PP (rPP) produced in the UK, and a 50:50 vPP–rPP blend. title: MONKI: a three-dimensional Monte Carlo simulator for transfer of polarised light in planetary atmospheres
abstract: Abstract. Spectropolarimetry is a powerful tool for characterising planetary atmospheres and surfaces. For the design and operation of spectro(polari)metric instrumentation, numerically simulated signals of the measured radiation are essential. Here we present MONKI (Monte Carlo KNMI), an efficient and accurate radiative transfer code written in Fortran, based on the Monte Carlo method. title: A dual role of precipitation amount and temperature determines precipitation isotopic trends in Southeast Alaska
abstract: Southeast Alaska is one of the wettest places in the world, with some locations within the region receiving upwards of 6 metres of precipitation annually. Given the region's abundant precipitation, it is important to understand the mechanisms controlling the hydrologic cycle to better constrain past and future trends in climate. Accomplishing this requires the evaluation of isotopes in precipitation, as this is key to untangling the many drivers of the water cycle. abstract: Abstract. Post-launch characterization of the receiver telescope of the laser altimeter is essential for achieving precise georeferenced planetary measurements and for radiometric calibration to passively measure surface reflectance. For the Ganymede Laser Altimeter (GALA) aboard the Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (Juice), such in-flight calibration was originally planned during a lunar flyby but could not be performed due to an unexpected reboot of the instrument. title: Entanglement and apparent thermality in simulated black holes
abstract: We investigate the apparent thermality of Hawking radiation in the semi-classical limit of quantum black holes using the mean-field limit of a chiral spin-chain simulator, which models fermions propagating on a black hole space-time in the continuum. In this free-theory regime, no genuine thermalisation occurs. title: Flyway-scale migration phenology identifies mismatches between migration timing and European hunting regulations
abstract: The study of bird migration timing is pivotal for the identification of the onset of pre-breeding migration, when, according to the European regulatory framework, the hunting seasons should end following Article 7.4 of the EU Birds Directive. Member States may use different data sources, including citizen science platforms, to determine this onset. Here, we used data from eBird, a citizen science platform, to describe the timing of pre- and post-breeding migration of the Song Thrush (Turdus philomelos) across the Western Palearctic. abstract: Continental brine deposits hosted in salar-type systems of the Central Andean Lithium Triangle (Argentina, Bolivia, and Chile) account for more than 60% of known global lithium resources, making the accurate spatial characterization of lithium concentration a matter of paramount importance for resource evaluation and investment decision-making. title: Metastable and Stable States in Covalent Organic Frameworks Controlled by Synthetic Selection Pressure
abstract: The synthesis of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) has long followed a thermodynamics-driven approach, aiming to obtain highly ordered stable crystalline materials while overlooking metastable structures with unique dynamic characteristics. Inspired by the biological concept of "selection pressure," we propose that the harshness of synthetic conditions serves as a key selection pressure governing the final state of COFs. title: Chromium Removal from Wastewater Using Phosphorylated Fish Bone Char
abstract: Hexavalent chromium is a toxic and highly leachable contaminant associated with several environmental hazards. A phosphoric acid-functionalized fish bone char has been synthesized by chemical impregnation and researched for the treatment of hexavalent chromium from water. The surface area of the synthesized material is found to be 19.79 m2/g by nitrogen adsorption-desorption isotherm having pore volume and diameter of 0.049 cm3/g and 13.7–14.9 nm, respectively. title: Análise integrada do comportamento não estacionário de fenómenos hidrológicos extremos: caso de estudo da bacia hidrográfica do rio Muriaé (sudeste do Brasil)
abstract: O estudo analisou o comportamento não estacionário de eventos hidrológicos extremos na bacia do rio Muriaé (8,126 km2, sudeste do Brasil), uma região propensa a inundações fluviais. Foi utilizada uma metodologia que combina a técnica das séries de picos acima de um limiar, POT (do inglês Peaks Over Threshold), e a estimativa da taxa de ocorrência por Kernel (KORE). title: Numerical calculations of neutron star mountains supported by crustal lattice pressure
abstract: Abstract Gravitational waves may set the spin frequencies of neutron stars in low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs). One mechanism for facilitating such emission is the formation of a mass asymmetry - or ‘mountain’ - supported by elastic strains driven by thermal gradients. Most studies have focused either on the origin of the elastic strains or the temperature asymmetry in isolation, and have not considered the entire formation process. abstract: ABSTRACT Standardised sampling protocols are essential for improving biodiversity assessments, particularly for indicator groups such as fruit‐feeding butterflies. Although fermented banana is the most widely used bait in tropical regions, rotten fish is the best bait for catching fruit‐feeding butterflies in high‐altitude sites. title: An analytical model for rotors in confined flow across operating regimes
abstract: Rotors operating in confined flows, or blockage, are commonly encountered in wind and water tunnels, as well as in shallow or dense deployments of hydrokinetic turbines. Confinement induces a streamwise pressure gradient in the channel, modifying the rotor induction, thrust and power. title: The Promise and Perils of Private Enforcement under EU Law: The Digital Services Act in Context
abstract: Abstract This article offers a conceptual account of private enforcement under EU law, focusing on the DSA. It argues that the damages action under the DSA derives directly from Union law and cannot be reduced to a declaratory reference to national law. Situated within regulatory theory, it shows how private enforcement may complement public enforcement while raising concerns about access to justice, compliance incentives, and democratic legitimacy. abstract: The persistent housing deficit, indoor thermal discomfort, and rising energy demand in Nigeria’s humid-tropical climate have triggered a search for innovative building components that advance energy efficiency and sustainability in the construction industry. abstract: Abstract The transpressive plate boundary between the Caribbean and North American plates in Hispaniola is a complex system of strike-slip faults, subduction zones, fold-and-thrust belts, and normal faulting. title: Improved desalination by polymer grafting
abstract: Freshwater scarcity demands desalination technologies that are efficient, scalable, and sustainable. Capacitive deionisation (CDI) is promising but remains limited by inefficient ion adsorption and poor charge utilisation. abstract: Introduction: Ecotourism can alter wildlife behavior without affecting species diversity, but this is a poorly known subject. Objective: To evaluate the influence of tourist access on medium- and large-bodied mammals in Manuel Antonio National Park, Costa Rica. title: Cellulose-based bioplastics for a circular bioeconomy: Properties, applications, market potential, consumer acceptance, and future perspectives
abstract: Cellulose-based bioplastics have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional petroleum-derived plastics, offering a sustainable and eco-friendly solution to the growing environmental concerns associated with plastic waste. Derived from renewable resources such as wood, cotton, and agricultural residues, cellulose bioplastics exhibit biodegradability, biocompatibility, and low environmental impact. title: Rural place leadership across the Anglo-Scottish border: analysing the evolution, resilience and success of the Borderlands partnership
abstract: This paper explores the evolution of the Borderlands Partnership, a cross-border initiative seeking to address common challenges in the Anglo-Scottish rural periphery. Utilising a path-tracing methodology, a timeline was constructed to identify key events in the evolution of the Borderlands Partnership which created opportunity spaces for institutional entrepreneurship and generative place leadership. title: Forward self-similar solutions to the MHD-Boussinesq system with Newtonian gravitational field
abstract: This paper is concerned with the existence of forward self-similar solutions to the three-dimensional Magnetohydrodynamic-Boussinesq (MHD-Boussinesq) system with a Newtonian gravitational field. By employing a blow-up argument and the Leray-Schauder theorem, we construct a forward self-similar solution to this system without imposing any smallness assumptions on the self-similar initial value.

abstract: Groundwater underpins India's water and food security but faces growing stress from overexploitation and climate change. This study evaluates the hydrologic performance of small-scale, pond-based Managed Aquifer Recharge (MAR) interventions implemented under government development programs, in the context of India's plan to construct 14 million additional recharge structures. abstract: The pervasive environmental presence of microplastics (MPs) raises concerns regarding their potential impacts on reproductive health, particularly in the context of prenatal exposure. This study aimed to establish a polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs) exposure model in pregnant rats and to investigate the subsequent effects on the growth, hormonal profiles, steroidogenic enzyme expression, and testicular histology of male offspring from birth to adulthood. abstract: Polypropylene production relies predominantly on fossil resources for process energy and carbon feedstock. This study compares fossil primary production, renewable-carbon primary routes based on biomass, renewable hydrocarbons, or CO2 and hydrogen, and recycling pathways under German industrial cost conditions within the European carbon-pricing framework. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper develops careless assemblages as a concept to explore the failures to care for men after sexual violence and abuse. We draw upon data from the Men's Unwanted Sexual Experience (MUSE) project, which included semi‐structured interviews and arts‐based workshops with 40 self‐identifying men in Northeast and Southeast England. title: H–D Exchange in Ultraviolet-irradiated Water: Methane Ice Mixtures
abstract: Abstract The deuterium-to-hydrogen (D/H) ratio in solar system volatiles is commonly used to diagnose volatile formation conditions. This ratio may be altered by a range of processes under solar nebula conditions, however, including energetic processing of icy grains. title: Environmental Perception and Intelligent Navigation for Autonomous Delivery Robots in Complex Scenarios
abstract: Autonomous delivery robots (ADRs) face perception and navigation challenges in complex scenarios. When operating in real world urban environments, ADRs have trouble negotiating upturned streets, uneven terrain, and moving obstacles. This review covers three key areas: environmental perception, navigation techniques, and mechanical adaptability of delivery vehicles. abstract: This study aims to examine the eco-theological interpretation of the story of the Saba’ people in Q.S. Saba’ [34]: 15–17 to minimize the food waste crisis in Indonesia. title: Thermal resilience under climate extremes: simulation-based assessment of heatwave impacts in informal buildings in Cairo
abstract: Abstract Climate change and rapid urbanization are increasing the frequency and intensity of heatwaves. Informal settlements are particularly vulnerable to heat stress due to inadequate housing conditions and socioeconomic constraints. In Egypt, informal housing accounts for 38.6% of the national housing stock, yet the risk of indoor heat stress remains underexplored. abstract: The relevance of this study stems from the fact that the transition of farms from traditional tillage to minimum and no-till techniques requires seed drills capable of operating consistently under varying conditions of crop residue, soil moisture and field micro-relief. abstract: Abstract This study improves the operational eclipse-season yaw attitude model for Global Positioning System (GPS) Block IIF satellites by using Reverse Kinematic Precise Point Positioning (RKPPP) yaw estimates as an observation-driven reference. Using a 7.5-year global GPS tracking dataset, we reconstruct yaw attitude time series over eclipse season maneuvers and compare them with the current operational attitude model. title: Complex-valued modified Zakharov-Kuznetsov equation
abstract: Motivated by the introduction of the Zakharov-Kuznetsov equation as a higher dimensional generalization of the Korteweg-de Vries equation, in this paper we introduce the modified Zakharov-Kuznetsov (mZK) equation as a 2-dimensional generalization of the complex-valued modified Korteweg-de Vries equation. abstract: The Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC) is currently undergoing drastic economic income development and some of the most rapid landuse changes in Thailand. title: Performance degradation and failure mechanisms of pultruded carbon/glass-fiber hybrid sucker rods after long-term downhole service
abstract: Pultruded carbon/glass-fiber hybrid composite rods are increasingly used as sucker rods, yet the relationship between degradation accumulated during long-term downhole service and subsequent longitudinal splitting during retrieval and drum winding remains insufficiently understood, particularly for rods containing a carbon/glass hybrid transition region. This study compared five specimens sectioned from a pristine 22 mm-diameter parent rod with five specimens sectioned from a service-aged parent rod retrieved after 435 days of actual downhole service. title: Beyond wind-sector management: optimal wind farm operational planning for balancing fatigue damage and extending lifetime
abstract: Abstract. We present an optimization framework for long‑term wind farm operation that balances fatigue loads and energy yield to extend turbine and farm lifetime. The approach plans per‑turbine derating setpoints for discrete wind conditions using an engineering wake model and surrogate models for power and damage. We formulate the problem as a nonlinear program and solve it either for the full farm in a single run or iteratively per turbine. title: Signatures of photospheric convection throughout the solar atmosphere: the EVE Sun-as-a-star mHz continuum
abstract: Abstract Convectively driven motions in the solar photosphere can generate broadband Doppler variability across the chromosphere, transition region and corona. Here we investigate this variability using “Sun-as-a-Star” observations from the Extreme Ultraviolet Variability Experiment (EVE) aboard the Solar Dynamics Observatory, constructing high signal-to-noise Doppler power spectra by incoherently averaging spectra from 3-hour sequences of the centroid wavelengths of emission lines that span wavelengths 35–104 nm. title: Distributed Observation Scheduling and Sensor Fusion For Large Agile Constellations
abstract: With the rapid increase in interest towards large scale earth observing satellite constellations, the problem of properly commanding and utilizing these systems has become increasingly relevant. This work focuses on a complete distributed approach to this problem, incorporating an observation task allocation and scheduling algorithm in addition to a sensor data fusion algorithm for end-to-end target coverage and processing. title: Gen-EBM: an energy balance model for terrestrial planets. Climate multistability from snowball to post-runaway greenhouse climates
abstract: Climate multistability and tipping points are fundamental properties of planetary climates that depend sensitively on climate feedbacks. We introduce the Geneva Energy Balance Model (Gen-EBM), a new 1-D latitudinal EBM for rapid exploration of terrestrial planet climates, and use it to investigate how planetary rotation, eccentricity, and thermal inertia shape climate attractors and multistability. abstract: With a 35-day orbital period and $\sim$0.5 eccentricity, TOI-2257 b occupies a sparsely populated corner of transiting mini-Neptune parameter space and may lie near the orbital distance at which tidal and atmospheric escape process become negligible. abstract: We study the three-dimensional primitive equations with full viscosity and horizontal thermal diffusion in bounded domains. We establish global well-posedness for admissible $H^1$ initial data and persistence of $H^2$ regularity on the flat-bottom cylinder. The higher regularity analysis combines fractional hydrostatic Stokes regularity with anisotropic estimates of the vertical transport. title: Testing the inelastic dark matter interpretation of the LZ event with heavy-element experiments
abstract: We consider the inelastic dark matter interpretation of the recent 248 keV event observed by LZ and identify different experiments that could test it. Details of the underlying model and the ability of complementary experiments to test it depend significantly on the high-velocity tail of the dark matter distribution. We consider several example velocity distributions motivated by the impact of the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) in order to map out the effects of this dependence. title: A ghost-cell immersed boundary method for the shallow water equations on Cartesian grids: mass conservation and wetting and drying over variable topography
abstract: A ghost-cell immersed boundary method is proposed for the two-dimensional shallow water equations with a variable bed (topography), solved with an explicit Godunov-type finite volume scheme (unsplit second-order MUSCL, HLLC flux, hydrostatic reconstruction) on Cartesian grids. Ghost-cell methods leak mass through the wall. title: Global stability and sharp decay for the two-dimensional non-rotating primitive equations without thermal diffusion
abstract: We study the two-dimensional non-rotating primitive equations with positive horizontal and vertical viscosity and without thermal diffusion. Our main results are fourfold. First, for every integer \(s\ge4\), we prove that sufficiently small, compatible, doubly periodic \(H^s\) perturbations of a stably stratified rest state with an affine temperature profile generate unique global strong solutions; the horizontal velocity and temperature remain uniformly small at the initial Sobolev order despite the derivative loss in the full diagnostic vertical velocity, and strict stratification persists.

title: Asymptotic stability and Rayleigh-Taylor instability of stratified states for the three-dimensional rotating primitive equations with gravity
abstract: We study the 3D rotating primitive equations with gravity in a horizontally periodic channel, with viscous horizontal velocity and no density diffusion. For every Coriolis parameter, stably stratified equilibria are asymptotically stable. Small compatible \(H^4\) perturbations yield global classical solutions with uniform \(H^4\) bounds. abstract: Understanding the origin and evolution of planetary atmospheres, and the connection between their lower and upper atmospheric layers, remains a fundamental challenge in exoplanet science. Addressing these questions requires observations spanning a broad wavelength range, from the ultraviolet to the near-infrared, together with the ability to simultaneously characterise planetary and stellar variability. abstract: We study global regularity and the infinite Prandtl number limit for temperature patches of the two-dimensional nondiffusive Boussinesq system on $\mathbb R^2$, with velocity dissipation $Λ^{2α}$, $\frac12<α\leq1$. title: Excited-State Effects in Nucleon Sigma Terms from a Variational Analysis
abstract: We investigate excited-state effects in nucleon sigma-terms in lattice QCD using twisted-mass clover-improved fermion ensembles. We study correlation functions with nucleon and multihadron nucleon-$σ$-meson interpolating operators. title: Preferential concentration of cloud droplets: Coupled effects of phase change and gravitational settling
abstract: Cloud droplets respond to turbulent motion with finite inertia and settle under gravity, while condensation and evaporation change their sizes. The nonuniform accumulation of cloud droplets in turbulent flows, known as preferential concentration, has attracted sustained interest because it affects droplet collision and coalescence rates. We develop an analytical theory that quantifies the coupled effects of droplet inertia, gravitational settling, and phase change on concentration changes. title: Model-Order-Adaptive Channel Estimation for AFDM Systems with Fractional Delay and Doppler
abstract: Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) has emerged as a promising waveform for high-mobility communications owing to its ability to exploit multipath diversity. However, channel state information (CSI) acquisition remains challenging in channels with fractional delay and Doppler and an unknown number of propagation paths. In this paper, we investigate the channel estimation for AFDM systems. We first analyze the AFDM response in the presence of fractional-delay-induced frequency wrapping. abstract: We study a class of periodic NLS-Dysthe (NLS-Dy) equations, also referred to as higher-order nonlinear Schrödinger equations (HNLS), of the form $i\partial_t u+a\partial_x^2u+b|u|^2u+i\varepsilon(c\partial_x^3u+d|u|^2\partial_xu+eu^2\partial_x\overline{u})=0$ with $ x\in\mathbb T$, $a,b,c,d,e\in\mathbb R$, $abc\neq0$, and $\varepsilon>0$. title: Spin textures at the Fermi surface of ferromagnets and associated torque
abstract: We establish theoretically that transverse spin textures are generically induced by the spin-orbit interaction at the Fermi surface of centrosymmetric ferromagnetic metals. We confirm this prediction with {\em ab initio} computations for Fe, Co and Ni. By symmetry, this cannot be associated with spin-orbit torques under a uniform current. title: MUNITE: Unified Multimodal Latent Inference for Any-to-Any Multimodal Generation
abstract: We introduce MUNITE, a latent-variable framework for flexible any-to-any multimodal generation that treats encoding and latent generation as the same inference problem under different amounts of observed evidence. Given any subset of modalities, MUNITE models the conditional distribution over the latent representation associated with the complete observation. abstract: We present and analyze a spatially and temporally adaptive high-order method for the one-dimensional Richards equation describing vertical water transport in unsaturated soil, with an emphasis on resolving sharp wetting fronts while satisfying a fully discrete water mass balance. The spatial discretization uses an arbitrary-order local discontinuous Galerkin spectral-element formulation with collocated Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto quadrature, and the time integration is based on a high-order Rosenbrock-Wanner method. abstract: The introduction of two-body XX interactions has been shown to improve the performance of quantum annealing in solving certain combinatorial optimisation problems and would enable the simulation of a broader class of many-body Hamiltonians. Due to experimental constraints, such interactions are typically not natively available on analogue quantum devices. To overcome this limitation we introduce the truss gadget. abstract: This paper develops theoretical and numerical extensions of Birkhoff pseudospectral transcription for aerospace optimal control problems. Building on the recently proposed body of knowledge, a Birkhoff integration operator is derived for flipped Legendre Gauss Radau (fLGR) grids, drawing connections to regular LGR grids and to the favorable conditioning properties that make Birkhoff interpolants particularly appealing. title: Optimal Gating for Dead-Time-Constrained Single-Photon Detectors
abstract: We develop a Fisher-information framework for optimizing single-photon detector gating in periodic experiments, in contrast to previous more empirical or heuristic gating choices. After each photon detection, such a detector is insensitive for a dead time, so that an early background detection can obscure a later signal. abstract: Characterizing intermediate quantum chaos in systems with mixed phase spaces requires probing spectral correlations across multiple scales. Here, we present a multi-scale statistical analysis of the resonance spectra of ultracold 166Er and 168Er atoms using higher-order spacing ratios, spacing increments, and the accumulated power spectral density of decimated level sequences. abstract: Neutrinos and muons produced in the forward direction of LHC collisions and detected by the FASER and SND@LHC experiments enable a comprehensive deep-inelastic scattering (DIS) programme, covering both neutral and charged currents, at TeV energies. This programme aims to provide stringent constraints on proton and nuclear structure as well as on hadron fragmentation, and to offer novel insight into neutrino interactions at the highest energies achieved in a laboratory. abstract: Marine data management in developing countries faces structural challenges such as institutional fragmentation, lack of regulatory frameworks, and capacity limitations, hindering the adoption of FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable). This study, with a qualitative approach complemented by a descriptive quantitative component, aimed to design a national marine data network model based on FAIR principles for Panama, articulated within the framework of the IOC-UNESCO IODE programme and OBIS. title: Chinese Botany at the 1873 Vienna World’s Fair
abstract: This article examines the Chinese botanical exhibits at the 1873 Vienna World’s Fair as part of global knowledge formation within Austro-Hungarian Empire. It argues that these exhibits were not static displays but dynamic objects mediating trade, science, and imperial representation. abstract: Acoustic Doppler Current Profilers (ADCPs) are widely deployed to characterise tidal currents in energetic marine environments. While instruments and deployment techniques have improved reliability, data usability remains constrained by workflow, metadata, and archival practices. This study draws lessons from a multi-decadal archive of ADCP deployments across tidal energy sites in the Orkney and Pentland Firth region. abstract: This research analyzes the dynamics of halal tourism and the implementation of Islamic values in key Southeast Asian destinations, namely Malaysia, Indonesia, and Thailand. This research uses a qualitative approach to explore how Islamic values, such as halalness, sustainability, and inclusiveness, are implemented in halal tourism policies and practices. abstract: Coastal environments worldwide are subject to rapid transformations, including to mitigate against climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution. abstract: This study examined the legal and ethical challenges associated with genomic data sharing in Nigeria with focused on issues of consent, privacy, data ownership and international collaboration. abstract: Adolescents’ environmental responsibility is shaped by both individual and contextual factors, including life goal orientation and family communication processes. abstract: This study explores the empowerment of coastal communities through the development of ecotourism as a sustainable approach to improving local livelihoods and environmental stewardship. title: A blueprint for Vibrio surveillance and risk reduction in Europe
abstract: Vibrio bacteria, long regarded as pathogens of tropical waters, are now emerging across numerous European coastlines as rising sea surface temperatures and extreme weather reshape microbial ecologies. Wound and foodborne infections caused by Vibrio vulnificus , Vibrio parahaemolyticus and other non-cholera species are increasing in frequency and latitude. Recent heat-related outbreaks in the Baltic and North Seas demonstrate that climate change is already expanding the suitable habitat for these bacteria. title: Reforming Institutional Design for Fairness: Evictions from Toronto Community Housing, 2002–2014
abstract: Abstract This article examines institutional safeguards for fairness in rent-arrears evictions from the Toronto Community Housing Corporation (TCHC). It reconstructs the reform sequence that led to the adoption of a novel—possibly unique—institutional mechanism: the Office of the Commissioner for Housing Equity (OCHE), an independent accountability mechanism for procedural fairness in evictions. It was a contingent institutional response to tragic administrative failings, not a response to judges’ or legislatures’ external oversight. abstract: The Absheron Peninsula contains a dense network of Caspian ports and industrial terminals where vertical land motion (VLM) may affect infrastructure performance. abstract: In Last 3 Days , players investigate unusual marine animal deaths by examining samples and comparing test results with collection locations and reports. This paper analyses how the game's evidence chain develops from these comparisons, with particular attention to clues that suggest an incomplete explanation. abstract: Purpose: Indonesia and Tanzania, linked across the Indian Ocean, share textile traditions that reflect cultural interconnectedness and soft power. Batik from Indonesia and kitenge from East Africa are globally recognized fabrics that have evolved into dynamic fashion industries. Kitenge, widely believed to have originated from Indonesian batik before undergoing adaptations in East Africa through innovations such as kanga, kikoi, and shuka, has emerged as a cultural icon alongside batik. abstract: Summary This teaching case examines why post-pandemic tourism recovery should not automatically be equated with destination resilience. abstract: Amisos, situated in the Pontic region of northern Anatolia, was one of the most significant ancient urban centers of the Black Sea basin. abstract: Teluk Bintuni Regency is dominated by rivers, estuaries, swamps, and coastal areas, so water transport is the main mode connecting communities across districts. Nevertheless, community accessibility to water transport remains low, allegedly because of high transportation costs and long travel times. This study analyzes the partial and simultaneous effects of transportation cost (X1) and travel time (X2) on water transport accessibility (Y). title: The just price: a market-process account
abstract: Abstract When is a price just? This paper develops a new theory of justice in pricing, grounded in the Austrian market process tradition. Prices, I argue, are not merely outcomes to be evaluated against an external standard of fairness. They are instruments through which the competitive process performs morally significant functions: communicating information, generating incentives and coordinating the plans of millions under pervasive ignorance. abstract: We present a comprehensive DNA barcode reference library of invertebrate species samples from chameleon habitats in South Africa. The dataset was developed to support dietary metabarcoding assessments of dwarf chameleons (Bradypodion spp.) and to strengthen national invertebrate sequence resources. title: Restoration in the Anthropocene: reconsidering the primacy of “native ecosystems”
abstract: Abstract The third edition of the Society for Ecological Restoration's International Principles and Standards for the Practice of Ecological Restoration places recovery of “native ecosystems” at the center of what counts as legitimate ecological restoration. Here I argue that, in the Anthropocene, this emphasis reflects a value‐based choice rather than an ecological inevitability. abstract: This article asks whether elections, even if they are not free and fair, might still have important consequences for authoritarian ruling coalitions, testing the theory that dictators avoid destabilizing their coalition before an election, but can afford to do this once the vote has passed. Fossilised bones, characteristics of their preservation, and their sedimentary infill can serve as a basis for unravelling the origin of fossil bonebeds. Assessing the taphonomic data thereby allows for deciphering the genesis of multitaxic mass accumulations of elements of organisms from different habitats. abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines Japanese perceptions of the European Union's Indo‐Pacific Strategy through interviews with government officials and foreign policy influencers. Respondents considered the EU to be a highly important actor in the Indo‐Pacific context. Three‐quarters of respondents considered the Indo‐Pacific Strategy document to be sufficiently important that it constitutes an upgrade or a positive transformation of the existing relationship. abstract: ABSTRACT Floods rank among the most frequent and widely managed hazards worldwide. While considerable research has examined public perceptions of flood risk, less attention has been paid to how people interpret institutional presence, action, and responsibility in flood‐prone settings shaped by infrastructure and governance systems. abstract: Purpose: This study examines how economic, social, and environmental sustainability influence tourists’ revisit intentions at destinations in Madura, focusing on the mediating roles of perceived value and destination image. Research Method: A survey was conducted among tourists who had visited cultural, religious, marine, and natural attractions in Madura. abstract: Legal protection for Traditional Cultural Expressions (TCEs) in Indonesia, particularly the Gambang Semarang performance, remains inadequate despite formal recognition under Article 38 of Law No. 28 of 2014 on Copyright. The core gap lies in the absence of a sui generis protection regime and the ambiguous formulation of Article 38, which fails to specify ownership, benefit-sharing, or registration mechanisms for communal cultural expressions. title: Citizen-science data reveal drivers of PFAS variability in backyard chicken eggs
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widespread synthetic contaminants that can accumulate in food, such as chicken eggs. Although European Union maximum levels for PFOS, PFOA, PFNA and PFHxS apply to commercialised eggs, backyard chicken egg concentrations frequently exceed these limits. Consequently, in the Netherlands, the national health authority advised against consuming backyard eggs. abstract: Irregular migration to Europe by sea, though risky, remains one of the most popular migration options for many Sub-Saharan Africans. This study examines the drivers of irregular migration decisions using an incentivized lab-in-the-field experiment in rural Gambia, the African country with the highest per-capita rate of irregular migration to Europe. abstract: Background and aim A One Health–focused Community Health Needs Assessment (CHNA) identifies animal and environmental risk factors affecting human health. This cross-sectional descriptive study assessed the health needs of Bomaa, a rural town in Ghana, using a One Health approach. Methods A cross-sectional design with convenience sampling recruited 271 residents. abstract: This study aimed to identify and document the ethnic meat products of Borno State, Nigeria, addressing a critical gap in the documentation of Nigeria's intangible culinary heritage. abstract: The Moon is becoming a realistic site for scientific missions, permanent research facilities, and commercial activity. One resource has become especially important: water ice near the lunar south pole. Lunar water is extremely valuable for future commercial space operations. abstract: Abstract. The tectonics of Colombia is characterised by the interaction of multiple oceanic plates subducting beneath the continent, generating active transpressional deformation and a wide range of subduction-related and crustal earthquakes. We present a flatfile containing ground-motion intensity measurements from 694 shallow earthquakes. The dataset includes 8,086 three-component acceleration records that were uniformly processed. abstract: Maritime cargo claims in the Gulf Cooperation Council arise within a tightly knit shipping environment, yet they are decided under six national legal systems. This article examines the fragmentation and harmonisation of cargo claims law in the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman and Qatar. abstract: Artificial light at night (ALAN) is increasingly recognised as an important anthropogenic pressure affecting nocturnal biodiversity, particularly in oceanic islands with high endemism levels. Arthropods, especially moths (Lepidoptera), are key components of nocturnal ecosystems, yet their distribution and abundance patterns in Madeira Island remain insufficiently documented and their responses to ALAN are poorly understood. abstract: This article analyzes the notary’s responsibility and the legal consequences for the parties when false information is provided regarding a collateral object that has already been encumbered with a prior mortgage. abstract: BackgroundEuthanasia remains a highly debated issue in end-of-life care because it raises ethical concerns surrounding patient autonomy, relief of suffering, professional responsibilities, and the sanctity of life. abstract: The primary objective of this study is to explore the role of Blue Accounting in flood disaster mitigation, with a particular focus on addressing persistent gaps in water resource management and fostering transparent, data-driven governance within flood-prone regions. title: Accelerated weathering of limestone for CO 2 capture and storage: a critical review of unbuffered, buffered, and modified pathways
abstract: Accelerated weathering of limestone (AWL) converts CO2 into dissolved bicarbonate by reacting calcium carbonate and water, an alternative to geological storage. This review examines AWL as a branching family spanning the unbuffered concept, buffered AWL (BAWL), and modified routes (potable-water, construction-grade waste limestone, promoter-assisted, utilization-based, ship-based, and electrochemical AWL), grouped into six classes covering reactor configuration, feedstock, dissolution promotion, effluent conditioning, downstream utilization, and electrochemically driven alkalinity generation.

abstract: This study focuses on the shade-grown coffee agroforestry system of the Cacahuatique Mountain Range in Ciudad Barrios, El Salvador, a region with a long tradition of coffee cultivation under tree cover. All Salvadoran coffee is produced under shade, a practice that preserves greater biodiversity than sun-grown systems. abstract: Seafaring is a demanding occupation characterized by prolonged periods away from home, long and irregular working hours, physical workload, fatigue, confined living conditions, limited shore leave, and reduced social interaction. These conditions can negatively affect the mental and physical health of seafarers and increase their vulnerability to psychological difficulties. abstract: For most of the post-Cold War era, the Arctic was governed as an exception to great-power politics: a “zone of peace” in which scientific cooperation, not strategic rivalry, set the tone. As Arctic Amplification strips away the ice that once made the region marginal, it is exposing a geography rich in shipping lanes, hydrocarbons, and critical minerals, and drawing the United States, Russia, and China into overlapping contests for military advantage, economic access, and legal control. abstract: Cultural tourism refers to the mutual motivation of the visitors toward learning and appreciating historic places. It is closely connected to the sustainable approach, efficient management of heritage sites, built environment and social customs of these locations. title: The prince and the scientists
abstract: Scientific institutions pose a peculiar leadership challenge: their ultimate purpose, scientific discovery, cannot be commanded or predicted. I argue that scientific leadership is less about exercising authority than about cultivating the trust, diversity, interactions and intellectual freedom from which scientific excellence can emerge.

abstract: Agriculture increasingly requires interventions that improve yield stability, resource-use efficiency and stress resilience without proportionally increasing chemical or energetic inputs. abstract: The Salt-Medina-Mecca telegraph project began in 1900 with the aim of building a continuous overland connection under Ottoman administrative control and reducing reliance on the foreign submarine cable via Jeddah. abstract: This study examines how Social Safety Net Programs (SSNPs) in Bangladesh generate spatially differentiated welfare outcomes within a unitary governance system. abstract: Vocabulary assessment in Indonesian EFL higher education remains predominantly focused on discrete-item tests, prioritizing individual receptive knowledge. To address limitations of such tests, this study examined collaborative, digital, multimodal vocabulary projects in a pre-service teacher class in Indonesia and explored students’ perceptions. abstract: Public services such as healthcare, schools, and transport constitute the infrastructure essential for a functioning and productive society. abstract: Conservation areas are critical for tackling the global environmental crisis1. abstract: Targets 1 and 3 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF) require actions to focus on areas of importance for biodiversity-a prerequisite for reversing biodiversity loss and halting human-induced extinctions as set out in the Mission and Goals of the KMGBF. abstract: The Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) posits that environmental degradation increases during the early stages of economic development and decreases once a certain income level is reached. Ecuador and Mexico illustrate contrasting patterns within this framework: the former relies heavily on natural resources, while the latter has a more diversified economy, albeit with persistent environmental challenges. abstract: The booming fast fashion industry fuels a throwaway consumer culture that has negative environmental impacts. Sustainability branding of fast fashion is like solving a paradox. abstract: This paper explores the gender dynamics within the Opobo Kingdom of Rivers State, Nigeria, from its founding in 1870 to 2022 focusing on the diverse roles and contributions of women from the pre-colonial period to the post-colonial era. It critically examines how women have navigated the intersecting forces of tradition, modernity, and socio-political structures to serve as agents of change. abstract: Within his Grain-Tax Law, Agyrrhios regulates bidders and bidding for the grain-tax assessed annually upon Lemnos, Imbros, and Skyros. abstract: ABSTRACT Anaerobic speed reserve (ASR) and critical speed (CS) offer practical, performance‐based estimates of physiological tolerances, and can be derived from maximal aerobic speed (MAS) and maximal sprint speed (MSS) in swimming. abstract: This study focuses on the socio-economic history of cattle breeding in Thrace from the mid-1920s to the late 1940s. title: Highly pathogenic avian influenza as a systemic risk - implications for control and preparedness
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) has evolved from episodic outbreaks into a globally entrenched, multi-host panzootic, with recurrent spillover into mammals. The expanding host range and increasing wildlife–livestock interfaces challenge traditional control strategies, increase opportunities for viral adaptation, and thereby elevate zoonotic risk. We therefore propose that HPAI should be reframed as a long-term systemic risk requiring resilience-based governance, and strengthened One Health control and preparedness.

abstract: Spiritual tourism increasingly encompasses contemplative encounters with nature and culture, yet the development of spiritually themed products in protected-area destinations raises questions about cultural authority, conservation, and commercialisation. This study explores whether an ecotourism destination in Tanjung Puting, Central Kalimantan, Indonesia, could support a community-sensitive spiritual tourism offer without transforming sacred practices into visitor performances. abstract: Purpose - This study maps the spatial structure of Italy’s tourism economy across the 20 regional capitals. title: Modern pollen rain of an upland area: implications of pollen dispersal for interpreting palaeoenvironmental records
abstract: A long‐term perspective on landscape evolution is critical for understanding past land‐use activity, land cover–climate feedbacks and, notably, for establishing a factual basis for conservation. Fossil pollen analysis provides a means to achieve this. Biases pertaining to pollen productivity, pollination processes and basin size, however, mean there is not a one‐to‐one relationship between pollen and plant presence. Upland pollen recruitment is poorly understood, and existing studies of pollen dispersal have yielded conflicting results, making interpreting past landscape character challenging.

abstract: Elementary classrooms are formative social spaces in which children learn how to interpret difference, regulate responses, participate fairly, and handle disagreement. This qualitative needs analysis examined how culturally grounded mindful learning could be designed to support social moderation in upper-grade elementary classrooms in Jember, East Java, Indonesia. abstract: This essay argues that Bengali literature emerged from a continuous process of religious and cultural interweaving, shaped by Bengal’s multi-ethnic origins and centuries-long Hindu–Muslim coexistence. abstract: Abstract Shipboard hybrid AC/DC microgrids (MGs) are increasingly deployed to integrate advanced propulsion systems and pulsed power loads while maintaining high power quality and reliability. abstract: Global environmental politics is a field that combines the analysis and evaluation of environmental politics and policies with their practical application. abstract: Abstract Intellectual property (IP) is frequently approached through its codified forms and formal institutions, with less attention to the deeper social foundations from which protection of intangible creations arose. abstract: While infrastructure is widely acknowledged as a catalyst for economic growth and national development, its role in promoting equity, citizenship, and social justice remains underexplored. abstract: Background: Employee retention is increasingly challenging as Generation Z enters the corporate workforce with distinct expectations regarding career growth, compensation, supervisory support, organizational culture, and work–life balance. title: Beyond the Stage: Economic Impact and Tourism Multipliers of Music Festivals in Emerging Indian Destinations
abstract: In recent years, the consumption patterns of live music in India have broken out of conventional metropolitan hubs and found an eager, mobile audience across smaller towns, rural valleys, and scenic regional getaways. While traditional music business scholarship primarily focuses on recorded music, streaming royalties, catalog publishing, and copyright litigation, this study shifts critical attention to the broader macroeconomic spillovers generated by live concerts and multi-day music festivals in non-metropolitan environments. title: How Does the Issue of Social Forestry Affect the Knowledge of the Young Generation? Case Studies from Universities in Indonesia
abstract: Social forestry has emerged as a key agenda for the Indonesian government, aimed at reducing inequality in forest land tenure, enhancing community welfare, and minimizing conflict. Despite the many challenges of issuing social forestry management permits, specific issues, such as transdisciplinary science, regeneration, and youth engagement as drivers and actors at the site level, have yet to receive adequate attention. title: Reward System and Employees’ Effectiveness in Deposit Money Banks of Southeast, Nigeria
abstract: This study examined the relationship between reward system and employees’ effectiveness of deposit money banks in south east, Nigeria. Three research objectives, research questions and hypotheses were formulated. The study adopted survey research design and Pearson correlation coefficient was used to test the stated hypotheses and the findings showed that there is significant relationship between pay raise, profit sharing and employee productivity, innovativeness and Initiative. abstract: Investasi rendah karbon menjadi fokus transisi energi global, termasuk pengembangan Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) lintas negara antara IndonesiaSingapura. Kerja sama ini menimbulkan kebutuhan kepastian hukum bagi investor asing karena melibatkan lebih dari satu yurisdiksi. title: Morocco's nuclear option readiness (2026–2050): A governance-first approach aligned with the IAEA milestones framework
abstract: This study examines the public evidence available for assessing Morocco's nuclear power decision readiness across the 19 infrastructure issues of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) Milestones Approach. A documentary assessment separates established institutional foundations, evidence of preparatory activity, and matters that remain unverified. An author-developed Level 0–3 scale describes the maturity of the documented arrangements within their stated scope; it is neither an IAEA scoring system nor a test of Milestone 1 attainment. title: Legal Pluralism and Building Permit Enforcement in Tanzania: Contradictions of the Dual Land Tenure System
abstract: Tanzania operates a dual land tenure system. It recognises granted and customary rights of occupancy. The statute treats the two forms as equal, as set out in section 18(1) of the Village Land Act. The Constitution and the Court of Appeal confirm that customary rights are property. Yet building permit enforcement is built around granted title. A landholder in a declared planning area must obtain a permit before development. Regulation 124(1) of the Local Government (Urban Authorities) (Development Control) Regulations (2008) imposes this duty. In practice, the permit route presupposes a survey
journal: East African Journal of Law and Ethics

title: Where Commitment Dissipates: An Attenuation Cascade Theory of Gender in Climate Resilience Policy
abstract: Climate policy increasingly recognises that unequal social relations shape climate risk, yet this recognition has not consistently changed budgets, eligibility rules, or outcomes. This article examines where near-universal gender commitments weaken and what determines the scale of that loss. Using theory-building thematic synthesis, it integrates feminist political ecology, intersectionality, social vulnerability theory, the capabilities approach, and transformative resilience with research on policy evaporation and gradual institutional change. title: Assessing A Rural Community-Based Entrepreneurship in Malaysia: Are we there yet?
abstract: This article draws upon research undertaken in two rural communities in Malaysia under the program My Village My Future, a community-based entrepreneurship program initiated by the government to develop rural areas. Little is known about the success of rural community-based entrepreneurship. The paper uses various community-based entrepreneurship models to explore rural community-based entrepreneurship's roots, challenges, and issues. This study aims to explore the suitable model of community-based entrepreneurship in rural areas. This paper follows a case study method of a narrative approach

title: Christian Missions and Educational Growth of Ogbomoso Land 1960-1990
abstract: The general opinion is that education is an instrument of ensuring positive changes in the society however; positive changes have not been achieved in Ogbomoso prior to the arrival of Christian Mission. Traditional education was then characterized with vocational training such as basketry, blacksmithing, carving, arts, crafts, sculptures, painting and decoration. This education is not formal because there are no lesson notes, curriculum, school register and school buildings as in the western sense. title: Data infrastructure fragmentation and policy failure: Evidence from Indonesia’s food security governance
abstract: Indonesia’s food security governance faces a structural paradox: a 2025 budget allocation of IDR 155.5 trillion coexists with 23.28 million undernourished citizens and a 13-year absence of a National Food Plan. This study argues that data infrastructure fragmentation is the principal structural barrier underlying this paradox. We propose a three-dimensional typology (horizontal, vertical, and temporal) as an analytical framework for diagnosing this barrier. Using a qualitative explanatory single-case study design, this study analyzes 11 BPK audit reports published in 2026, covering audit perio
journal: Jurnal Tata Kelola dan Akuntabilitas Keuangan Negara

title: Operationalizing Litvinenko’s Assessment Criteria For Intertextual Units In Literary Translation: Cross-Linguistic Verification And Pragmatic Trajectories
abstract: Intertextuality constitutes one of the most intellectually stimulating yet methodologically challenging frontiers in modern linguistics and descriptive translation studies. While post-structuralist semiotics envisioned textuality as an infinite labyrinth of prior cultural fragments, applied translation research demands operational clarity to differentiate deliberate, source-anchored intertextual allusions from atmospheric socio-cultural realia, phraseological idioms, and archetypal motifs. journal: International Journal of Language Learning and Applied Linguistics

title: Community-Based Event Management Model for Community Empowerment and Sustainable Rural Tourism in Tua Tourism Village
abstract: Background: Rural tourism becomes more durable when residents can transform local culture, social networks, and community resources into visitor experiences without weakening local identity. In Tua Tourism Village, village events offer this possibility, yet their continuity is affected by limited managerial skills, financing, digital communication, and formal operating procedures. journal: Journal of Business Social and Technology

title: Policy-Robust Space Investment Strategies: A Multi-Criteria Evaluation under Competing Societal Paradigms
abstract: Although competing societal needs have intensified pressure on public budgets, public investment in space has expanded considerably. Decision-makers must prioritize space investments while considering economic, social, environmental, and strategic objectives. However, the relative importance of these objectives may vary across different policy perspectives. This study frames the prioritization of space investments as a multidimensional decision-making problem and develops a method for evaluating the robustness of space investment strategies under different societal paradigms. journal: Journal of Expert Systems and Sustainable Development

title: Coupling microalgal bioremediation of recirculating aquaculture effluents with photobiological hydrogen production
abstract: Abstract Recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) effluents contain substantial nitrate and phosphate loads, posing a significant eutrophication risk to aquatic ecosystems if left untreated. While microalgal bioremediation is a promising strategy, expanding opportunities for valorisation is crucial for its successful implementation. This study couples the cultivation of nitrate-utilizing Chlamydomonas reinhardtii strain CC-1690 in RAS effluent with photobiological hydrogen (H 2 ) production to achieve nutrient removal, bioenergy production, and high-quality biomass. title: Contribuições de Michel Foucault para a análise do discurso político
abstract: This paper examines Michel Foucault´s most relevant theoretical and methodological contributions to contemporary approaches of political discourse analysis within the French tradition. Based on the analysis of The archaeology of knowledge and The order of discourse, the article provides an overview of his main analytical contributions, it modes of reception, and some of their uses in poststructuralist and socio-semiotic perspectives in Latin American. In this way, it helps to show the wide range of readings and receptions of his work in our region.

title: Assessing the Influence of Tourism Development on Wildlife Conservation In GISHWATI-MUKURA National Park, Rwanda
abstract: This study examined the influence of tourism development on wildlife conservation in Gishwati-Mukura National Park, Rwanda. It specifically assessed the influence of income creation, community-based tourism activities, and ecotourism activities on wildlife conservation. A descriptive research design was employed, targeting a population of 475 individuals, from whom a sample of 217 respondents was selected. journal: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Management

title: The Nigerian Civil War: Causes, Resolution, And Post-War Reconciliation Efforts
abstract: The Nigerian Civil War, which ranged from 1967 to 1970, stands as a pivotal moment in the nation's history, marked by intense ethnic tensions and a profound struggle for control over resources and power. This abstract explores the multifaceted problems that led to the outbreak of the Nigerian Civil War, the approaches taken to resolve the conflict, and the subsequent efforts to foster reconciliation among the warring factions. This study employs a historical research approach, drawing upon secondary sources, including archival documents and academic literature. It employs a chronological analy
journal: JOURNAL OF HUMANITIES AND SOCIAL POLICY

title: Extinguishment and Revocation of Abandoned Land Rights under Indonesia’s Government Regulation No. 48/2025: A Land-law Perspective
abstract: This study aims to examine and investigate the controversy surrounding the extinguishment and revocation of rights to abandoned land under Indonesia’s Government Regulation No. 48/2025, viewed from the perspective of Indonesian land law. The research employs a literature review methodology, encompassing relevant legislation and academic literature. The findings indicate that the provisions regarding the extinguishment and revocation of rights to abandoned land in Indonesia’s Government Regulation No. 48/2025 grant the state broad authority to extinguish and revoke such rights and transfer them
journal: International Journal of Business Ecosystem and Strategy (2687-2293)

title: ‘I Have Been There Too’: motivations and expectations of young people with previous experience of being in a NEET situation becoming peer mentors- a qualitative study
abstract: This study explores how young people with previous experience of being in a NEET situation describe their motivation and expectations for serving as mentors for peers who are not in education, employment, or training. Using a qualitative, inductive design, five mentors aged 18–24 participated in individual in-depth interviews before beginning mentor training. Thematic analysis identified two overarching themes: Inspiring meaning for others and oneself and Providing support fosters resilience and growth. title: An Investigation into the Impact of Education-related Policies and Teaching Methods, School Infrastructure, and Student Performance on the Quality of Primary Education in Bangladesh
abstract: The study focuses to investigate the impact of educational policy, method, and school climate on the quality of primary education in Bangladesh. All this in the face of these abiding challenges – the fact that students come from social-economically diverse backgrounds, non-uniform, diverse pedagogical systems impart their education, and infrastructure is a barrier to the quality of education in a developing country. title: Retórica, enunciação e política
abstract: O trabalho analisa o papel do significante “mudança” no discurso político de Mauricio Macri em campanha e durante seu governo (2015-2019). Argumentamos que a “mudança” se constituiu em um significante primordial. title: Unpacking climate justice rhetoric: a comparative content analysis of international city networks
abstract: Purpose The rising membership and influence of international city networks have positioned cities as important actors in global policy debates on climate change and sustainability. This study aims to clarify how these networks frame and incorporate justice in their climate actions. Design/methodology/approach The study selected four prominent city networks (C40, CityNet, ICLEI and UCLG) and applied a content analysis method to examine how they interpret justice in 64 documents published by them between 2016 and 2022. title: CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY (CSR) DALAM KAITANNYA DENGAN PELESTARIAN LINGKUNGAN DAN MASYARAKAT WILAYAH PESISIR DAN PULAU-PULAU KECIL DI INDONESIA
abstract: Wilayah pesisir dan pulau-pulau kecil di Indonesia memiliki potensi sumber daya alam yang melimpah, namun sekaligus sangat rentan terhadap degradasi lingkungan dan masalah ketimpangan sosial-ekonomi. Kehadiran berbagai aktivitas industri dan korporasi di sekitar kawasan ini membawa dampak ekologis dan sosial yang signifikan, sehingga menuntut optimalisasi pelaksanaan Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR). Artikel ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji dan menganalisis implementasi program CSR dalam kaitannya dengan pelestarian lingkungan serta pemberdayaan masyarakat di kawasan pesisir dan pulau-pulau k

title: Drivers of Employee Engagement in Nepal's Private Sector: A PLS-SEM Analysis of Recruitment, Training, Performance Appraisal, and Compensation Practices in Kathmandu Valley
abstract: Background: Employee engagement is a key driver of a company's competitive advantage and performance. Employee engagement creates opportunities for employees to connect with their managers, employees, and organizations through the human resource management practices. Purpose: The objective of this research is to study the impact of human resource management practices on employee engagement in private sector of Kathmandu valley. title: LEXICAL-SEMANTIC FEATURES OF ENGLISH AND UZBEK TRADE TERMS
abstract: The article is devoted to the lexical-semantic features of trade terms in English and Uzbek languages. Trade terminology is one of the oldest and most dynamic layers of economic vocabulary in both languages. The study covers polysemy, synonymy, antonymy, hyponymy and homonymy, as well as semantic changes and borrowings. The article material consists of English trade terms and their Uzbek equivalents drawn from explanatory and bilingual dictionaries, legal and normative documents and commercial texts. Definitional, componential, etymological and comparative methods were applied in the article.

title: Policy Pathways Across the Tasman: A Comparative Analysis of Rural Education Policies and Practices in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand
abstract: Abstract This paper provides a critical comparative analysis of rural education policy as a means of addressing the special issue question of how educational theories and practices travel across borders and may be reshaped here in Aotearoa New Zealand. Data from Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand are part of a wider collaborative Royal Society of New Zealand- Te Apārangi Catalyst grant which positions the need to understand the unique context of New Zealand rural education as a key educational equity issue. title: Exploring the Rule-of-Law Approach to Collaborative Data Security Governance in BRICS
abstract: Data has become a foundational strategic resource in the digital age, and data security has emerged as a crucial issue that aﬀects national security, economic development, and social stability. With the expansion of data sovereignty approach and the collective rise of the “Global South,” the BRICS countries have initiated their respective data legislation processes and changed the passive position of developing countries in the formulation of international data rules through coordinated governance. title: Urban commons in a contested trajectory of new municipalism: rethinking public–common partnerships in the case of Kültürpark İzmir
abstract: Within the contested terrains of post-neoliberal urbanism, what are the possibilities (and limits) of urban commons? The article focuses on the case of Kültürpark in İzmir to provide critical answers by highlighting its counter-hegemonic potential of public–commons partnerships. Established as a cultural and ecological landmark, the park has recently become a site of intense struggles over urban futures: municipal projects seeking market-oriented valorization have clashed with civic mobilizations defending its ecological, cultural, and symbolic significance. title: Application of a Naegele’s Formula Adapted to the Long Count Mayan Calendar to Calculate the Expected Date of Birth During a Leap Year
abstract: Objective: To evaluate whether the Naegele formula applied to the Mayan calendar can improve the accuracy of due date prediction. Methods: A database of pregnant women who gave birth during the leap year 2016 was analyzed (post hoc analysis). The date of the last menstruation (confirmed by ultrasound) was converted to the Mayan date using an online converter. The Naegele formula was adapted to the Mayan calendar and applied to the date of the last menstruation on the Mayan calendar. title: Caste as Ecology: The Mangrove Archive, Slow Violence and the Labouring Dalit Body in the Sundarbans Stories of Shyamal Kumar Pramanik
abstract: The Sundarbans has been written, mapped, legislated and lamented into international visibility, yet almost never from the vantage of caste.This article reads five short stories by the Bangla Dalit writer Shyamal Kumar Pramanik-"In Dakshin Rai's Land," "Bhajahari and His Family," "Champaburi, or the Story of a Village," "Homeland" and "Life in the Forest"-to argue that in his fiction caste is not a social variable located within an environment but the mechanism by which that environment is distributed, priced, permitted and made lethal.Reading these stories together through Ritam Dutta's "Dalit

title: From representation to equitable participation: An overview of multicultural education research published in 2025
abstract: Multicultural education research has expanded rapidly, but its definitions remain varied and the distinction between representation and equitable participation remains unresolved. This thematic-bibliometric review of one publication year examines 210 English-language articles published in 2025 and classified in the field of Social Sciences in Scopus, the sole database. title: Empowering risky choices: care ethics and risk management in participatory immersive performance
abstract: This article examines audience engagement in immersive theatrical productions, focusing on why some participants thrive while others feel fearful or reluctant. It critiques traditional risk management systems for overlooking psychological and social risks in participatory art. Using insights from Joan Tronto’s care ethics and Paul Slovic’s risk perception, this study proposes that grounded risk management in care ethics can enhance audience experiences. title: Unlocking Employee Performance Through Internal Marketing: A PLS-SEM Analysis of Organizational Commitment in Nepal's Service Industry
abstract: Background: Employee performance is critical to service organizations, where employee attitudes and organizational support can directly shape service delivery. Internal marketing practices such as empowerment, rewards, supportive supervisor relationships, and career opportunities can strengthen organizational commitment and enhance employee performance. However, limited evidence exists on these relationships in Nepal’s service industry, particularly regarding the mediating role of organizational commitment. title: Evaluating the association between household water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) and selected placenta-related complications in The Gambia, Kenya and Mozambique
abstract: Placenta-related complications contribute substantially to maternal and perinatal mortality globally, with the greatest burden in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). However, the potential influence of inadequate household water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) on these outcomes remains poorly characterised. We investigated associations between household WASH conditions and selected placenta-related complications, including pre-eclampsia, small-for-gestational-age (SGA) and stillbirth, in The Gambia, Kenya and Mozambique. title: Indigenous Women’s Wisdom in Sustainable Natural Resource Management: A Participatory Environmental Justice Perspective
abstract: Sustainable natural resource management has yet to adequately recognize and integrate indigenous women’s traditional knowledge. This article examines its legal status, the challenges to its recognition, and the legal reforms needed to strengthen it from a participatory environmental justice perspective. title: Necrocities as Borderscapes: Necropolitics and the Production of Refugee Life in Offshore Detention
abstract: This paper examines refugee narratives to illustrate how necropower is exercised within borderscapes where life is presented at its extreme limit. Using Behrouz Boochani’s No Friend But the Mountains, I explore refugee camps as necrocities embedded within broader borderscapes that deny refugees free movement, access to civic life, and the status of being full human beings. Simultaneously, this paper examines refugees’ resistance within these spaces, focusing on testimony, narration, and epistemic resistance that challenge their subjugation. title: Demographic effects of earthquakes in Central and Southern Italy
abstract: This paper evaluates the demographic effects of two major earthquakes – L’Aquila 2009 and Central Italy 2016 – that struck a large area in Central and Southern Italy. Using municipality-level data (2002–2023) and a difference-in-differences design with multiple groups and periods, we estimate causal impacts on several demographic outcomes. title: Teacher Empowerment in Relation To SchoolBased Management Participation of The Teachers in Sta. Cruz North District, Davao Del Sur
abstract: Fundamentally, teacher empowerment is a measure expected to improve the school-based management participation of teachers. In this study, the researcher selected the 197 elementary school teachers in Sta. Cruz North District, Davao del Sur as the respondents of the study. Stratified random sampling technique was utilized in the selection of the respondents. Non-experimental quantitative research design using descriptive-correlational method was employed. title: Income Stability and Financial Resilience as Determinants of Well-Being Among Cruise Line Employees
abstract: This study examined income stability and financial resilience as determinants of well-being among cruise line employees residing in Pampanga, Philippines. A descriptive-correlational design was used with 128 respondents who met the study eligibility criteria and were selected through purposive screening followed by simple random sampling. Data were gathered through a structured online questionnaire containing demographic items and modified assessment scales for income stability, financial resilience, and employee well-being, rated on a four-point Likert scale.
