title: A Southern European Portrait of Learning Outcomes
abstract: This article draws on interviews with educators, employment services officers, and young people conducted in three localities of Southern Europe in 2024. It contributes to the comparative literature on education, training, and youth transition regimes through an analysis of interactions between these actors in three local contexts. The fieldwork was conducted in Castelló (Spain), Pesaro- Urbino (Italy), and the rural areas and tourist resorts in the district of Thessaloniki (Greece). title: Global warming and the National Cattlemen’s Association 1986–1996
abstract: In the mid-1980s, scientific studies first highlighted the role of anthropogenic methane in global warming and emissions from cows as an important source. This knowledge expanded views of responsibility for global warming beyond the fossil fuel sector. Using scientific studies, archival documents, media interviews, and various government reports, we analyzed how the National Cattlemen’s Association (NCA), a trade association for the U.S beef industry, reacted to news about its products’ impacts on global warming between 1986 and 1996. title: Beyond "Special Interest": Reconciling Historical Claims, Territorial Rights, and Political Economy of Urban Governance in Finfinnee/Addis Ababa
abstract: The intersection of municipal governance, state-building, and regional territorial rights in multinational federations frequently generates deep institutional, spatial, and political-economic friction. In Ethiopia, this friction is rooted in 19th-century imperial state expansion, which initiated the systematic displacement of indigenous Tulema Oromo communities to establish the garrison town (katama) at Finfinnee (Addis Ababa). title: Evaluating the impact of triple-drug mass drug administration using human and mosquito-based indicators of lymphatic filariasis in Samoa, 2019 – 2024
abstract: BACKGROUND: For lymphatic filariasis (LF) elimination, the World Health Organization recommends multiple rounds of mass drug administration (MDA) to interrupt transmission. While LF antigen (Ag) is routinely used to monitor progress, recent evidence suggests more time-sensitive indicators are needed during the immediate post-MDA period. In Samoa, triple-drug MDA was distributed in 2018 and 2023. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of Samoa's second round of triple-drug MDA on human and mosquito-based indicators of transmission. title: Anthropocentric and Ecocentric Discourses in Bangladesh’s EFL Textbooks: Implications for Pedagogies of Resilience
abstract: In the Anthropocene, the epoch of profound human impact on Earth, Bangladeshi ELT textbooks are not passive tools of language learning but active carriers of eco-political ideologies. Employing an eco-linguistic framework, this study investigates the eco-political discourses within Bangladeshi secondary-level English textbooks (Grades 6-10) through critical discourse analysis technique. abstract: Climate change demands systems and critical thinking competences in teacher education to foster transformative sustainability education. Against this backdrop, empirical evidence is needed to better understand how future educators internalize and operationalize these competences, particularly in relation to their readiness to enact transformative sustainability practices in educational contexts. abstract: Article 534 of the Comprehensive Organic Criminal Code requires indications that non-custodial measures are insufficient, but it does not specify which facts allow flight risk or risk of obstruction to be inferred. The study analysed that indeterminacy and its effects on exceptionality, proportionality and legal certainty. title: The Source(s) of Miguel de Unamuno’s ‘El buen bandolero’
abstract: Abstract Miguel de Unamuno’s oeuvre comprises a substantial number of texts whose main scope is religion, almost exclusively Christianity. This should come as no surprise in a person who had a very idiosyncratic creed, and whose “agonic” take on faith and transcendence dominated much of his life. Precisely because he was so invested in and knowledgeable about religion, it is surprising to find that he used “el buen bandolero” to refer to “el buen ladrón” (“the good thief”)—the latter being a phrase with long-standing idiomatic status to refer to one of the criminals crucified next to Jesus. title: Sanctions and the Use of Force in International Relations: Exploring a Multifaceted Nexus
abstract: This article explores the complex relationship between sanctions and the use of force. It reveals a multifaceted interrelationship that, to some extent, reflects the complex nature of sanctions themselves. After reviewing and assessing the key issues arising in relation to sanctions – particularly the legality and legitimacy of autonomous (i.e. non-UN) sanctions – the article examines a selection of concrete situations illustrating four distinct ways in which sanctions interact with, or otherwise become relevant to, the use of armed force. title: Transformational Leadership Styles of Secondary School Administrators and Their Effects on Teachers' Self-Efficacy in Balamban District I
abstract: This study examined the transformational leadership styles of secondary school administrators and their relationship with teachers’ self-efficacy in Balamban District I during School Year 2025–2026 as a basis for developing a Leadership Enhancement Program. Employing a descriptive-correlational research design, the study involved 65 secondary school teachers selected as respondents. Data were collected using standardized instruments, namely the Multifactor Leadership Questionnaire (MLQ Form 5X) and the Teachers’ Sense of Efficacy Scale (TSES Long Form). title: A Comparative Conceptual Analysis of “bənê hā’ĕlōhîm” (“Sons of God”) in the Qur’ān and Jewish Texts: Examining the Attribution of Polytheism to Jews in the Story of ‘Uzayr in Qur’ān
abstract: This paper offers a comparative conceptual analysis of the expression bənê hā’ĕlōhîm (בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים, “Sons of God”) within Jewish theology and the Qur’ānic reference to ʿUzayr in verse Q 9:30. abstract: Abstract The debate between different versions of teleosemantics has largely centered around which alternative offers the most plausible account of the contents of simple animal representations. A serious issue is that theorists not only disagree on which proposal best explains the contents of these representations but also on what the contents actually are. title: Putting place first: towards a new vision for UK industrial strategy
abstract: This paper challenges the longstanding dominance of agglomeration theory in shaping the UK’s approach to industrial and regional strategy. While agglomeration thinking, rooted in urban economics, has played an influential role in government policy for two decades, persistent spatial inequalities, institutional fragmentation and the underperformance of the UK’s largest cities raise serious questions about its suitability as a universal framework for national industrial policy. The paper argues that the UK economy is better understood as comprising three distinct types of firm–place relationship

title: The Long Trajectory of Rubber Physics: 3500+ Years and Counting
abstract: ABSTRACT Natural rubber has followed an extraordinary trajectory from an indigenous Mesoamerican technology to an industrially essential material. This selective history begins with processing Castilla elastica latex more than three and a half millennia ago to produce durable ceremonial and practical objects. title: EU Values and the Demise of Constitutional Prudence
abstract: Abstract This article presents two interconnected arguments. First, a method other than the doctrinal method is needed to study EU constitutional law. Using the ruling in Commission v Hungary as the central example, the article demonstrates that EU constitutional law is not just legal but also political in nature. Following Martin Loughlin, the article therefore argues that the method of EU constitutional law is ‘the method of prudence’. title: Institutions, legitimacy, and divergent regime trajectories after political openings: a comparative analysis of Tunisia, Egypt, Turkey, and Indonesia
abstract: Why do similar political openings produce divergent regime trajectories? This article develops a comparative institutional framework to explain variation in post-authoritarian outcomes through a structured comparison of Tunisia, Egypt, Turkey and Indonesia. It argues that political openings generate uncertainty but do not determine political outcomes. Instead, divergent trajectories emerge through the interaction of three analytically distinct but causally interdependent elements: contingent political openings, institutional mediation and legitimacy narratives. title: Does power-sharing facilitate memory-sharing? Bosnian Croat narratives in post-war Bosnia and Herzegovina
abstract: This study examines how Bosnian Croat wartime narratives intersect with perspectives on post-war power-sharing in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Drawing on media, NGO reports and semi-elite interviews, it shows that despite shared wartime narratives, particularly those depicting Serbs as aggressors, competition within the consociational system has led to narrative divergence between Bosnian Croats and Bosniaks. title: A familiarização da mandioca nos agroecossistemas dos povos indígenas do Oiapoque
abstract: Frente às aceleradas mudanças nos contextos agrícolas mundiais, com tendência ao monocultivo, à homogeneização e à perda da variabilidade genética das espécies cultiva das, o presente estudo teve como objetivo demonstrar a importância dos conhecimentos dos povos indígenas no manejo da agrobiodiversidade, com ênfase na familiarização da mandioca. title: Unpacking Service Quality and Student Satisfaction in Nepal's Private Higher Education: A PLS-SEM Analysis of the SERVQUAL Dimensions in Pokhara University Affiliated Colleges
abstract: Background: Student satisfaction is an important indicator of educational service quality and can influence students’ perceptions of institutional performance, engagement, and continued affiliation with an institution. In an increasingly competitive higher education environment, private colleges must understand which dimensions of service quality most strongly shape students’ experiences. title: Does Green Supply Chain Partnership Governance Pay Off? An Investigation of the Impact on Corporate Financial Performance
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines whether governance of green supply chain partnerships (GSCPs) using environmental criteria for supplier selection and termination is positively associated with corporate financial performance of focal firms. Drawing on the social capital theory, this study highlights the dichotomous nature of social capital in GSCPs, showing whether firms can gain corporate reputation and then financial benefits while proactively managing GSCPs. title: From Exclusion to Protection: Chinese Merchant Capital in the Philippines Under US Law and Empire, 1921–1926
abstract: Abstract Scholarship about the Chinese Question has largely understood it as a “coolie” question, but what if it was reframed in terms of merchants? Well-studied US anti-Chinese laws like the 1882 Chinese Exclusion Act targeted working-class rather than elite Chinese, like merchants and students. But in 1921, the US-controlled Insular Government in the Philippines enacted a statute known as the Chinese Bookkeeping Act (Act No. 2972), marking a moment when US Chinese exclusion laws were directed toward businessowners. title: O AVANÇO DO PODER JUDICIAL : EFEITOS EM PARTE DA GLOBALIZAÇÃO, DO PLURALISMO DAS FONTES JURÍDICAS E DA COMPLEXIDADE DOS FENÔMENOS SOCIAIS
abstract: Il contributo tratta del progressivo avanzamento del potere giudiziale (c.d. giudiziarizzazione), che negli ultimi decenni ha guadagnato decisamente terreno rispetto al principio di legalità (legale), sempre più indebolito da fattori sia endogeni che esogeni al mondo del diritto. In particolare, lo scritto evidenzia come, tra le cause storico-sociali lato sensu extra-giuridiche, la globalizzazione e il pluralismo delle fonti giuridiche, insieme alla complessità dei fenomeni sociali, abbiano contribuito e contribuiscano all’affermarsi della giuristocrazia.

title: Governments or facilitators? Power and politics of multi-level sustainable energy governance in Surat, Gujarat
abstract: Urban areas are becoming strategic sites in the ongoing sustainable energy transition, driven by the new opportunities and imperatives presented by decentralized sustainable energy technologies. However, the presence of cities in the global clean energy landscape remains underwhelming. Despite national programs encouraging urban energy transition in India, the response has largely failed to meet the goals. title: Creativity, Psychological Capital, and Stress Resistance as Predictors of Academic Achievement: Evidence from Postgraduate Fine Arts Students
abstract: This study investigates the relationships among creativity, psychological capital, stress resistance, and academic achievement within Fine Arts education. Using product-of-coefficients (delta-method) tests of the indirect effects, it examines how psychological capital and stress resistance mediate the impact of creativity on academic performance among postgraduate Fine Arts students. title: Hospitality for the Truth in 3 John and Its Implications for Contemporary Christians
abstract: Hospitality has been a veritable tool widely used to achieve certain purposes, good or bad in human endeavours. It is a virtue Jesus enjoyed from different persons while on earth and recommends same. The church after him continues to use hospitality to alleviate people’s suffering and support itinerant preachers and missionaries. title: Modern grass phytolith assemblages from the Maloti-Drakensberg Mountains, southern Africa
abstract: Montane grasslands dominate the Maloti-Drakensberg mountain range in southern Africa and rank among the region's most biodiverse and sensitive ecosystems. Reconstructing their long-term dynamics remains challenging, as widely used palaeoecological proxies such as pollen offer limited taxonomic resolution for distinguishing grasses. title: Between reconciliation and peace making and brutalization: The Israeli case
abstract: Abstract This article examines the relationship between peacemaking, reconciliation, and brutalization in violent conflicts. It argues that these processes are deeply interconnected: effective peacemaking and reconciliation can interrupt or reverse brutalization, whereas unsuccessful or incomplete peacemaking may allow brutalization to persist, deepen, and become normalized, even alongside formal reconciliation initiatives. abstract: ABSTRACT The problem of heavy metal pollution in aquatic ecosystems is becoming increasingly critical. ZIF ‐8 is a representative metal–organic framework ( MOF ) that exhibits exemplary Cu 2+ adsorption characteristics and is amenable to large‐scale synthesis. However, the inherent crystalline powder morphology of MOF materials has led to great difficulty in recycling them for use as adsorbents in practical applications. abstract: Hemagglutinin (HA) is the principal immunologic target of most licensed seasonal influenza vaccines. Targeting both HA and neuraminidase (NA) might improve vaccine effectiveness. This randomized phase 1/2 study evaluated an investigational mRNA-based quadrivalent seasonal influenza vaccine, encoding HA and NA of A/H1N1, A/H3N2, B/Victoria, and B/Yamagata (FLUm4HA-4NA). title: How Do (Mis-)Perceptions of Refugee Gender Composition Shape Attitudes? Evidence from a Survey Experiment
abstract: Abstract People’s perceptions of others, particularly those from other countries, can shape their attitudes and willingness to offer solidarity. We study public beliefs about the gender composition of forcibly displaced populations in a large online survey experiment. Participants ( n = 13,008) representative of the adult population of six EU countries, consistently underestimated the share of women among the people displaced by the Russian war on Ukraine. title: From policy proliferation to coherence: Translating agroecological evidence into subnational food-systems governance in Vihiga County, Kenya
abstract: Sustainable agriculture in Kenya is governed by numerous policies addressing crops, soils, livestock, water, agroforestry, climate change, biodiversity, nutrition, marketing and social inclusion. Yet the existence of many broadly supportive instruments has not produced coherent agroecological implementation at the subnational level. This study examined how policy proliferation, fragmented mandates, and weak coordination affect the translation of agroecological evidence into county food-systems governance, using Vihiga County as a case study. title: Linguistic Sciences in Andalusia During the Emirate and Caliphate Periods Through the Book Al-Muqtabis by Ibn Hayyan al-Qurtubi (d. 469 AH / 1076 CE)
abstract: This study examines the development and flourishing of linguistic sciences in Andalusia during the Emirate and Caliphate periods, as documented in Ibn Hayyan al-Qurtubi's seminal historical work, Al-Muqtabis.The research explores how Andalusia emerged as a prominent center for linguistic scholarship, attracting scholars from across the Islamic world and fostering the study of Arabic grammar, lexicography, philology, and the linguistic analysis of the Qur'an.Key figures such as Ibn al-Qutiyya, Ibn al-Sayyid al-Batalyawsi, and others are discussed in the context of their contributions to the int

title: Rethinking body partonymy: transverse analogous paradigms across world languages
abstract: The part-whole relations of body-part lexemes, or “body partonymy,” might seem like a key source of evidence for shared conceptual systems in support of embodiment theories of cognition, but widespread variation in this lexical field across world languages calls this assumption into question. Recent studies focus on radical mismatches and random overlap relative to isolated frames of contrast such as body joints, reference languages, and ad hoc hierarchies. title: Framing of nationalism in climate reporting in the Global South: The case of India
abstract: Climate change and nationalism have traditionally been viewed as opposing forces because nationalism is often territorially bounded, while climate change transcends borders. This study examines the intersection of climate reporting and three forms of nationalism – that is, economic, resource and green nationalism – in India by analysing the coverage of Conference of the Parties (COP) summits in The Hindu and The Times of India before and after the Narendra Modi government’s rise in 2014. title: Revisión y discusión sobre la presencia y distribución del Taguató Negro (Parabuteo leucorrhous) en el noreste argentino
abstract: El Taguató Negro (Parabuteo leucorrhous) presenta poblaciones regulares y de mayor densidad en las selvas montanas de las Yungas del noroeste de Argentina. La población del nordeste tendría una densidad muy baja y, en los últimos 65 años, solo se conocen dos registros documentados en Misiones y pocos reportes de observación. title: Distribución dinámica probatoria en el delito de enriquecimiento ilícito: ponderación entre presunción de inocencia y tutela judicial efectiva
abstract: El presente estudio aborda la compatibilidad constitucional de la distribución dinámica de la prueba frente a la presunción de inocencia en el delito de enriquecimiento ilícito. La problemática radica en que el juzgamiento de este tipo penal enfrenta una marcada asimetría informativa entre la Fiscalía y el procesado, donde la aplicación rígida de la carga estática genera impunidad debido a la opacidad financiera; sin embargo, la dinamización probatoria es severamente cuestionada por la doctrina garantista por presuntamente vulnerar el estado de inocencia y el derecho a la no autoincriminación

title: Claudin-6 (CLDN6) and Folate Receptor Alpha (FRα) Targeted Antibody-Drug Conjugates: Bypassing Platinum Resistance and Tumor Heterogeneity in High-Grade Serous Ovarian Carcinoma

title: Illness perceptions, treatment attitudes, and social relationships among clinic-attending adults with bipolar disorder in Kerman, Iran: a qualitative study
abstract: Abstract Background Bipolar disorder is a chronic psychiatric condition in Iran; however, little is known about how patients in non-Western, collectivistic contexts – particularly in southeastern Iran – perceive their illness, form treatment attitudes, and manage social relationships. This qualitative study therefore explored illness perceptions, treatment attitudes, and social relationships among clinic-attending adults with bipolar disorder in Kerman, Iran. title: Strengthening the Paris Agreement Through Collective Decisions: Achievements and Limitations
abstract: ABSTRACT Due to its bottom‐up architecture, the Paris Agreement succeeded in securing broad participation but remained vulnerable to challenges concerning both the adequacy of national mitigation commitments and their implementation. This paper assesses the extent to which Parties to the Paris Agreement have succeeded in ensuring the effective functioning of the Paris framework through their collective decisions. It analyses two dimensions: the operationalisation of the Paris mechanisms and rules and the coordination of national efforts in the areas of mitigation pathways and climate finance.

title: Cohortes poblacionales sobre salud y bienestar en la infancia y la adolescencia: una revisión sistemática descriptiva y análisis comparado
abstract: FUNDAMENTOS // Las cohortes poblacionales permiten estudiar trayectorias de salud y bienestar en la infancia y la adolescencia, así como sus determinantes y su utilidad para orientar políticas públicas. El objetivo de este trabajo fue identificar, comparar y sintetizar cohortes de base poblacional sobre salud y bienestar infantil y adolescente en el ámbito nacional e internacional. title: TESTING THE IMPACT OF REFUGEE IMMIGRATION ON INFLATION SUB-GROUPS IN THE WORLD’S LEADING REFUGEE HOST COUNTRY: FOURIER CAUSALITY APPROACH
abstract: This study investigates the causal relationship between the refugee population in Türkiye and sub-categories of inflation. Employing econometric analysis on data spanning the period from 2003 to 2024, the research first utilizes the Fourier ADF unit root test to determine the stationarity properties of the variables. title: Informalisation Within IO s Under Geopolitical Pressure? WTO Negotiations on Development, Environment and Inclusiveness
abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines whether and how the informalisation of negotiations within international organisations (IOs) affects the effectiveness of particular negotiation agendas. Moving beyond broad‐brush diagnoses of multilateral gridlock, it develops a differentiated account of how pockets of effectiveness can be maintained under conditions of intensifying geopolitical contestation. title: The Sources of Normativity in World Politics: Identity, History and Moral Obligation Towards Refugees
abstract: Why do states facing the same international norms arrive at radically different interpretations of the morally right course of action? This article examines the sources of normativity in world politics through the lens of the 2015 European refugee crisis. abstract: The vision of the best form of government which Alfonso de Cartagena (1384–1456) defends in his writings is shaped by the character of the kingdom of Castile. He is keenly aware of the need to articulate a moral programme adapted to the circumstances of his time. title: Between Treaty Signature and Ratification: France and the 1961 Convention on the Reduction of Statelessness
abstract: Abstract This article investigates the legal consequences of treaty signature not followed by ratification, focusing on France’s 64-year-old signature of the 1961 Convention on the Reduction of Statelessness. France’s engagement with the 1961 Convention is unusual, raising multiple questions. One question relates to the customary status of Article 18(a) of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties (VCLT). abstract: This paper explores these connections- boxing, boxers of leadership, the ring, drama and knockout effects. It enunciates a metaphorical framework that equates leadership to boxing. title: When and How Do Women Directors Matter for Corporate Sustainability? The French Case
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines when and how board gender diversity matters for corporate sustainability. Using a sample of French listed firms over 2006–2024, we combine dynamic system GMM estimations with difference‐in‐differences tests around France's phased board gender quotas. The results show that greater female board representation is associated with stronger ESG performance, but that this relationship is highly contingent. title: A Paired RGB-Sonar Dataset for Fish Monitoring with Consumer Sonar
abstract: Imaging sonar enables underwater observation in conditions where optical imaging is ineffective due to darkness and turbid water. However, imaging-sonar systems previously used for ecological monitoring have typically been expensive, limiting their accessibility. Consumer forward-looking sonar has the potential to make fish monitoring more accessible, but its noisy imagery makes annotation and the development of automated methods challenging. title: A Solvable Model in the Half-filled Landau Level
abstract: A solvable microscopic model of interacting electrons in a half-filled Landau level is presented. The Hamiltonian is a well-defined limit of the electron-electron interaction. The low energy sector consists of a set of independent, spatially interlaced, one-dimensional systems of non-interacting fermionic dipoles, each system with a Fermi sea ground state. title: From Video Clips to Creation Trajectory: Sora100K for AI-Native Video Creation
abstract: AI-Native video creation is shifting from isolated video clips toward iterative video creation workflows. However, existing datasets remain largely video clips, representing video generation and editing as separate tasks rather than connected stages of a video creation workflow. In this paper, we introduce Sora100K, a dataset that represents the AI-Native video creation workflow as a structured video creation trajectory. title: Incremental Open-Ended Deep Research with Structured Harness
abstract: Existing Open-Ended Deep Research (OEDR) systems primarily generate reports from scratch, making them inefficient for scenarios where research reports need to be continuously maintained as new information emerges. We introduce \textbf{Incremental Open-Ended Deep Research (Incremental-OEDR)}, a research setting that treats a report as an evolving research state and incrementally updates it by preserving valid knowledge, revising outdated or incomplete content, and incorporating newly available information. abstract: The Model Context Protocol provides a shared interaction substrate for the agentic web, allowing heterogeneous services to expose capabilities through a standardized interface. Learning to use this ecosystem entails a hierarchy of capabilities: tool-format skills, server-level transfer, and cross-server composition. We present MCPDisCo, an ecosystem-scale reinforcement learning framework for MCP-native agents. abstract: This contribution reviews CT25, a new generation of CTEQ--TEA parton distribution functions (PDFs) for precision QCD. title: Debug2Fix: Can Interactive Debugging Help Coding Agents Fix More Bugs?
abstract: While significant progress has been made in automating various aspects of software development through coding agents, there is still significant room for improvement in their bug fixing capabilities. abstract: Geopolitical and strategic intelligence reports constitute a rich source of expert knowledge and have increasing value in the current political climate, but their heterogeneity and analytical complexity pose challenges for retrieval-augmented question answering. abstract: Agentic approaches for automated test generation can reach high-quality results, but they improve a given test suite incrementally, so a weak starting point may lead to many iterations or insufficient tests. abstract: This work presents a low-cost acoustic sensing framework for underwater localization and perception using single-beam sonars (SBS) and a forward-looking sonar (FLS). abstract: Critical raw materials (CRMs) are emerging inorganic pollutants because of their technological use and release into remote marine environments. However, their occurrence, distribution, and ecological significance in Antarctic waters remain poorly understood, and existing risk indices have not been adapted for CRMs in these systems. abstract: The second species of the African genus Ocinaropsis Aurivillius, 1905, Ocinaropsis tinubu sp. n., is described from West Africa. abstract: Many of the key dynamics that shape predator-prey interactions are governed by the physical and physiological principles which determine how animals move and perform in their environments. This opinion paper outlines the foundations underlying marine vertebrate predator-prey encounters within the context of pelagic habitats. Variables, such as maximum swimming speed, acceleration and manoeuvrability, play crucial roles in dictating the outcome of predator-prey encounters. abstract: Abstract Background The purpose of this paper is to examine the scale and importance of Indigenous cultural burning in precolonial times on the Central California Coast. abstract: There is growing evidence of environmental degradation in the Arctic, reflected in rising temperatures, ice melt, and more frequent extreme weather events. In this context, tourism development in Spitsbergen must be balanced with nature conservation. This study aims to examine experiences of tourism and opinions on sustainable activities, as well as to explore the potential for establishing a geopark on Svalbard. title: Upper Palaeolithic mariners? Evaluating experimental evidence for intentional early seafaring
abstract: Brought to popular consciousness by Thor Heyerdahl in the 1940s, the role of seafaring in human migration has been intensely debated. Aiming to stimulate discussion around the ways in which experimental archaeology is used to support such grand narratives, the authors of this debate critically assess a recent claim for Upper Palaeolithic seafaring in the Japanese archipelago. Here, they argue that creating a boat for which there is no archaeological evidence with generic tools that were not widely available in the region risks a confounding circularity of logic.

abstract: Pemphis acidula J.R.Forst. and G. Forst. or santigi is a plant native to Indonesia, widely recognized for its high economic value. Although listed as Least Concern by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), its existence in the wild is increasingly threatened by land degradation, climate change, and it suffers from low natural seed germination rates. title: Human Plunder: Slaving Raids, Economic Warfare, and Mercantilism in the French Caribbean, 1665-1713
abstract: Abstract Between 1665 and 1713, at a time of almost perpetual warfare in Europe, privateers frequently assaulted and seized enslaved people from rival colonies all over the Caribbean. Following mercantilistic principles, the French in particular sought to increase the labour force in their colonies while undermining their enemies’ plantation economies. Of the about 14,000 to 16,000 slaves captured in inter-colonial raids, more than 10,000 were forcibly taken to French colonies. These raids not only came at a high human cost but also led to shifting economic fortunes in the Caribbean.

abstract: This study examines the ecocritical dimension and the potential of ecotourism in the lyrics of Ebiet G. Ade, an Indonesian musician known for his sensitivity to humanitarian and environmental issues. Using an ecocritical approach, this study aims to explore how Ebiet's songs represent the ecological crisis, the relationship between humans and nature, and spiritual reflections on natural disasters that occur in Indonesia. abstract: A burgeoning microbiology field, sociovirology is the study of how viruses interact with one another and the effects such interactions have on social evolution. Challenging dominant narratives that viruses are individualistic pathogens, sociovirologists explore the social interaction of viruses through the language of cooperation, altruism, and cheating, social concepts with biological definitions. abstract: ABSTRACT Despite efforts by critical scholars of development to centre race in their analysis, Development Studies remains entangled in its racist history and contemporary imperialism. title: Further revisions to the catalogue of skeletal material from megatooth sharks, with a response to Sternes et al. (2024)
abstract: One specimen of Otodus auriculatus and three specimens of O. megalodon are added to the catalogue of skeletal material from megatooth sharks. Criticisms of the Lamnoidea hypothesis and reconstruction of Cretalamna sp. by Sternes et al. (2024) are responded to. abstract: The Indonesian government's commitment to achieving Net Zero Emissions (NZE) by 2060. abstract: Camels have been companions to humans since ancient civilizations, being a preferred animal because of their multipurpose nature. They were commonly used for long-distance transportation, favored over other animals like horses and donkeys due to their patience and ability to endure long journeys through harsh deserts with minimal water. title: Pre-Colonial Trade in a Border Region: A Case Study of Illela-Konni Trade Relations, 1700-1900 A.D
abstract: This paper examines Illela and Konni trade relations from 1700 to 1900 and argued that the relations are influenced by geographical and historical factors. The objective of the paper is to analyse how these factors shaped trade between the two towns. Through a critical analysis of oral interviews, archival records, travellers' accounts, and relevant secondary literature, the paper found out that variations in climate, soil, vegetation and resource endowments created patterns of comparative production that encouraged sustained exchange in grains and livestock which in turn developed the trade.

abstract: The Western media's depiction of Africa has long been entrenched in a narrow and conclusively negative narrative. title: Taxonomic revision of Vaccinium myrtillus (Ericaceae)
abstract: Vaccinium myrtillus has commonly been recognized as encompassing plants from Eurasia, Japan, and North America. abstract: Abstract The “composite nature of early Chinese texts” is a familiar way of thinking about textual formation in early China. It highlights how a text is comprised of small, movable textual units called “building blocks,” how an assemblage of building blocks stands either on its own or as part of a larger whole, and how a composite structure is the “norm” rather than exception in early Chinese writings. abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) commonly rely on inertial navigation systems (INS) aided by Doppler velocity logs (DVLs) for reliable underwater navigation. abstract: Thermodynamic cycles are the foundation of energy conversion across natural and engineered systems, transforming heat into useful work. abstract: Deep-sea skates are among the primary bycatch species in Southern Ocean demersal fisheries, yet their behavioural ecology and three-dimensional space use remain poorly understood due to their inaccessible habitat. This knowledge gap is particularly important because post-release survival in deep-set fisheries can be relatively low, making improved understanding of activity patterns critical for mitigating fisheries-induced mortality. title: Ultraviolet radiation lowers upper thermal limits in marine diatoms
abstract: Abstract Escalating ultraviolet radiation (UVR) and ocean warming are expected to interactively shape phytoplankton performance, yet their combined effects on diatom thermal plasticity remain poorly resolved. We quantified how UVR alters growth‐based thermal performance curves in three model marine diatoms grown across species‐specific temperature gradients (5–28°C) under UV‐excluded (PAR) and UV‐present (PAB) solar radiation. title: Ontogeny of settlement behaviours in response to Grammatophora marina diatom biofilms in the marine polychaete, Platynereis dumerilii
abstract: Abstract Settlement, the transition of a swimming planktonic larva to a benthic juvenile, is a key process during the development of many marine invertebrates. Microbial biofilms act as positive cues for larval settlement across species, yet the behavioural processes preceding settlement are poorly understood. Here, we investigated age-dependent changes in settlement behaviour in marine polychaete Platynereis dumerilii larvae in response to Grammatophora marina diatom biofilms. title: Nitrogen-Dependent Regulation of Nitrate Reductase in Coral Symbioses
abstract: The nutritional symbiosis between corals and their photosynthetic dinoflagellate partners underpins the ecological success of reef-building corals in nutrient-poor environments. Although coral holobionts can assimilate the abundant yet highly variable environmental nitrate, direct insight into how nitrate reductase is regulated in these symbiotic algae has been lacking. Here, nitrate reductase protein abundance and gene expression were characterized in cultured Symbiodiniaceae exposed to different nitrogen regimes and light conditions, revealing the multifactorial nature of its regulation. title: Interactive effects of ocean warming and higher irradiances on the Southern Ocean diatom Pseudo-nitzschia subcurvata
abstract: Abstract Diatoms are the dominant primary producers south of the Antarctic Polar Front (~60°S) and play a central role in Southern Ocean food webs and the biological carbon pump. Although models project that climate change will enhance primary productivity in the Southern Ocean, the interactive effects of environmental drivers, particularly temperature and light, on diatom productivity and physiology remain poorly understood. title: State of the stock for West Kamchatka coho salmon Oncorhynchus kisutch as a cumulative result of environmental impact in the freshwater and early marine periods of life
abstract: Two phases are revealed in the stock dynamics for the West Kamchatka coho salmon over the past five decades (since 1971) with almost fivefold difference in reproductive efficiency, independently of the number of spawners. In each of the phases, age of smoltification and abundance of return for the year-classes were determined by total abundance of the pacific salmon spawners, mostly pink and chum salmon, as a source of marine derived nutrients (MDN) transported to the rivers in their bodies. title: Hidden in historical sources: Rediscovering the thorny oyster (Spondylus gaederopus Linnaeus, 1758) in art, archives, and cultural knowledge
abstract: The thorny oyster (Spondylus gaederopus), a Mediterranean bivalve prised during prehistoric times for its distinctive spiny purple shell, has since been overlooked in cultural and scientific records. Frequently depicted in Early Modern still-life paintings, particularly in Italian works of the seventeenth century, its representations were historically misidentified as scallops or common oysters. This participated in obscuring the visual evidence of occurrence and human use of this species during this period. title: Genetic diversity of an invader: Percnon gibbesi in the Mediterranean Sea
abstract: Invasive alien species pose significant threats to marine biodiversity by altering ecosystem structure and function, outcompeting native species, transmitting diseases, or interbreeding with local fauna. The Mediterranean Sea is among the regions most affected by biological invasions and hosts one of the highest diversities of invasive crab species. One of the most widespread alien species is Percnon gibbesi, that has colonized and spread throughout the Mediterranean Sea over the last 25 years. title: Sustainable Utilization Challenges and Opportunities of the Blue Economy Resources in Bangladesh
abstract: Bangladesh’s Blue Economy, emphasizing the sustainable use of ocean and coastal resources, presents both immense opportunities and pressing challenges. Following maritime boundary settlements with India and Myanmar, the country gained an exclusive economic zone of 118,813 km² and an extended continental shelf of 37,000 km² in the Bay of Bengal, offering substantial potential in fisheries, aquaculture, renewable energy, tourism, shipping, and marine biotechnology. title: Assessing and quantifying variations in the functioning of marine food webs across scales
abstract: The mismatch between the scale of ecological processes and management decisions represents a significant challenge in marine conservation. This misalignment can result in ineffective conservation measures and compromise the sustainability of marine ecosystems. The large spatial resolution commonly used to analyze food webs may obscure key ecological processes and their functioning, leading to inaccurate conclusions with important consequences for management and governance. title: The Social Service Activities for Coastal Communities Affected by Coastal Erosion in Karawang Regency
abstract: Some coastal areas of Karawang Regency are affected by severe coastal erosion. This condition worsens the socio-economic life of coastal communities in Karawang Regency, particularly those in remote areas, amidst their relatively poor conditions. For this reason, Universitas Singaperbangsa Karawang and other universities held community service activities in the form of social service involving students. title: Atlas of Holocene organic-walled dinoflagellate cysts of the Mar Piccolo (Taranto, Southern Italy)
abstract: Dinoflagellates are one of the major components of modern plankton. Some of them produce a preservable organic-walled resting cyst, known as a dinocyst, which represents a direct link between the organism, its environment, and the sedimentary record. Dinocysts provide a unique window into key palaeoecological and palaeoenvironmental factors, such as past sea-surface conditions. Analyzing dinocyst assemblages, essential for deciphering such factors, requires a robust taxonomy and consistent nomenclature for accurate taxa identification. title: Ecological and radiological risk assessment of natural radioactivity from phosphate industry by-products used in construction: a case study from Crotone, Italy
abstract: Phosphogypsum (PG), a by-product of phosphate fertilizer production, has been widely considered for reuse in construction materials in line with the principles of the circular economy. However, PG and associated secondary compounds such as metasilicate phosphate often contain naturally occurring radionuclides, including 226 Ra, 238 U and 232 Th, which may pose radiological hazards. title: Evidence of Seagrass-Saltmarsh Connectivity, and their Role in Coastal Seascapes – a Review
abstract: Abstract Seagrass beds and saltmarshes are two of the most ecologically valuable coastal habitats globally, providing a wide range of ecosystem services including carbon sequestration, coastal flood defence, and habitat provision for fauna. While both systems can co-occur within the same intertidal zone, they have often been studied in isolation, with less consideration given to how their functional connectivity may influence the continued ecological and geomorphological development of either system. title: Atlas of pollen and spores from forests and wetlands in the mid-Atlantic Coastal Plain, USA
abstract: This atlas includes descriptions and illustrations of pollen and spores from plant species found in the mid-Atlantic Coastal Plain of the United States of America, with a focus on taxa that grow in or near riparian wetlands. It includes light micrographs and detailed descriptions of 141 species spanning 105 genera and 68 families of plants. This atlas was compiled to facilitate the identification of palynomorphs from sedimentary archives in the mid-Atlantic region. It includes both wetland taxa and those from surrounding uplands that may be deposited in wetland sediments.

abstract: Most ocean general-circulation models face the persistent challenge that the simulated summer ocean mixed layers are too shallow, indicating a lack of mixing; climate models coupled to them simulate too hot sea-surface temperatures (SSTs). Global wind energy input to the oceans supplies a great amount of energy to the surface waves. It is commonly thought that wave-induced turbulence mixing occurs only through wave breaking, but that turbulence, though intense, is injected only to a depth of the order of a wave height. title: Design for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Data Processing and Analysis Model for Seaport Based Surveillance in Maritime Narcotics. 'A Case Dar Es Salaam Sea Port'
abstract: This study presents the design and evaluation of an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-based facial recognition system that utilizes a police photo archive for real-time suspect identification at maritime seaports. The system processes real-time images captured by UAVs and compares them against a curated database of 669 known suspects. A total of 2,355 UAV-captured images from Ununio and Kigamboni seaports were used to evaluate the system. abstract: Animal observations can reveal ecological change in marine protected areas, but their conservation importance and their ability to diagnose climatic causes are different properties. This critical narrative synthesis examines how those two properties differ across four observation classes: benthic condition, coastal fish composition, seabird reproduction and unusual animal occurrences. abstract: Elemental geochemistry provides an effective tool for reconstructing sediment provenance and tracing the evolution of coastal depositional systems. This study investigates the geochemical composition of relict sands, Holocene beach-ridge deposits and modern beach sediments along the Emilia–Romagna coast (Northern Adriatic Sea) using X-ray fluorescence (XRF) analyses and selected elemental ratios. title: Temporary carbon storage can mitigate slow-responding climate changes
abstract: Abstract Carbon removal and storage is central to many net-zero commitments, yet its durability, particularly for nature-based methods, is uncertain due to disturbance risks. Previous work shows that carbon storage-years (the time-integrated quantity of carbon storage) are proportional to time-integrated avoided warming, which in turn causes avoided changes in slow-responding climate variables. Here, we show that temporary carbon storage results in avoided changes in inertial climate variables. title: Physicochemical characteristics of Nigerian estuaries and their patterns, drivers, and implications for environmental management
abstract: Estuaries are dynamic coastal ecosystems that provide essential ecological, biogeochemical, and socio-economic services. Despite their importance, Nigerian estuaries remain underrepresented in global scientific literature, with existing studies fragmented and spatially uneven. This study systematically reviewed the physicochemical characteristics of surface waters and sediments in selected Nigerian estuaries, including Lagos Lagoon, Awoye, Bonny River, Imo River, and Qua Iboe River. title: Geochemical clustering reveals cryptic eruptions and tephra correlations from Antarctic fumarolic ice-cave archives
abstract: Abstract Volcanic deposits preserved within Antarctic fumarolic ice caves provide rare access to sub-ice eruptive records hidden beneath the ice cap. Here we present the first integrated textural, petrological, and geochemical characterisation of 21 tephra samples from three summit ice caves at Mount Melbourne (Northern Victoria Land, Antarctica). Major and trace-element glass compositions, combined with published datasets, were analysed using multivariate statistical workflows. title: Seasonal long-distance migration of striped marlin associated with sea surface temperature in the western North Pacific
abstract: Abstract Striped marlins ( Kajikia audax ) are broadly distributed in tropical and temperate waters. However, their long-term movements in the western North Pacific remain poorly understood. To investigate these movements, 10 individuals (162–191 cm eye-to-fork length) were equipped with pop-up satellite archival transmitting tags and released in the northern East China Sea in August 2023. Nine tags successfully transmitted data after 9–241 days at liberty, including five that remained at liberty for 118–241 days. title: Development Of A Behavior Change Module To Reduce Microplastic Exposure In Coastal Communities
abstract: Background: Coastal communities face high vulnerability to microplastic exposure due to widespread environmental contamination and limited risk awareness, prompting this study to develop, validate, and evaluate a behavior-change–oriented educational module to reduce such exposure. Methods: This study applied a Research and Development (R&D) approach comprising the stages Analyze, Design, Develop, Implement, and Evaluate. abstract: The adjacency effect introduces spatial biases in high-resolution satellite imagery through atmospheric scattering of radiance from adjacent surfaces, particularly near sharp albedo contrasts such as ice-ocean boundaries. This study presents a data-driven approach for estimating the atmospheric point spread function directly from spaceborne observations over marine environments in both polar regions. title: Leaning left: how turn bias and habitat complexity shape spatial cognition in a coral-reef fish
abstract: In coral reef ecosystems, anthropogenic change is rapidly altering habitat structure, but the consequences for fish cognition remain poorly understood. We tested whether structural habitat complexity influences spatial learning and strategy use in the humbug damselfish (Dascyllus aruanus). Juveniles were reared in aquaria containing either high- or low-complexity coral structures and trained in a T-maze task, requiring the use of egocentric (turn-based) and/or allocentric (landmark-based) strategies to locate a reward. title: Measuring the nutritional benefits of fisheries adaptations in the Pacific Islands region
abstract: Fish are an important source of dietary protein 1 and essential nutrients 2 . However, efforts to sustain these benefits across the global south are increasingly challenged by population growth, habitat degradation and climate change 3 , 4 , 5 . These pressures are particularly acute in several Pacific Small Island Developing States (SIDS), where gaps have emerged between the recommended level of fish consumption needed for good nutrition and the supply of fish from coral reefs and other coastal habitats 6 , 7 , 8 ̶ the source of most fish consumed in the region 8 , 9 , 10 . title: Ibn Khaldûn as a Colonial Archive: Toward an Epistemic Decolonization
abstract: Abstract This article examines Ibn Khaldûn not as a stable, timeless precursor of modern social science but as a figure constituted through colonial translation and reception. Focusing on nineteenth- and twentieth-century French and English translations of the Muqaddimah , it argues that Ibn Khaldûn emerged in modern scholarship as a colonial archive—a site where translation, race, and epistemic authority intersected to produce new forms of historical and sociological knowledge. title: Temporal trends of dengue exposure among children in coastal Kenya
abstract: Abstract Background Serosurveys suggest widespread dengue virus (DENV) transmission in Africa but there is limited information on the temporal patterns of exposure. Methods Using repeated cross-sectional serosurvey data, we estimated the prevalence and incidence of DENV infections in coastal Kenya over 20 years (1998–2018). Stored sera ( n = 8025), collected annually from an open longitudinal cohort of 1834 children aged 15 years and below, were screened for anti-DENV IgG antibodies. abstract: ABSTRACT Compound‐specific stable isotope analysis (CSIA) has been widely applied to modern and archaeological samples of animal and human body tissues to evaluate food habits and/or physiological conditions. However, these techniques have rarely been applied to aquatic mammals, for which further study is required to evaluate their utility. abstract: Climate change in coastal areas threatens the survival of family archives, a category of vital records that hold legal, administrative, and historical value for families. The city of Pekalongan has experienced tangible impacts in the form of land subsidence and chronic tidal flooding; however, studies linking the preservation of family archives to community adaptation strategies for climate change remain limited. title: Corporate Social Responsibility Program Planning for Labuhan Coastal Ecotourism by PX Company
abstract: Corporate social responsibility in extractive industries is increasingly expected to address community welfare and environmental sustainability, particularly in coastal areas where livelihoods depend on natural resources. Coastal vulnerability is associated with mangrove degradation, limited alternative livelihoods, and environmental pressures. This study examines the planning process of Company PX’s Labuhan Coastal Ecotourism CSR Program and identifies the factors supporting and constraining its development. title: Reduced size of larvae and small fish linked to warming and reduced prey density
abstract: Abstract Body size is a integrative trait that has declined across ecological assemblages in the last decades. Changes in body size of early life stages and small-bodied fish are driven by complex interactions between size-dependent mortality, and temperature- and food dependent growth, and can have consequences for recruitment to the adult stock and food availability to predators. abstract: Preventing safety of navigation (SN) deficiencies is of critical importance in waterborne transport since the SN Code constitutes one of the most recurrent deficiency categories that serve as a basis for detention under port state controls (PSC). In pursuit of this objective, this study initially delineates and critically evaluates the interdependencies between a spectrum of influential determinants and deficiency types, as well as their respective contributions to detention occurrences attributable to the SN code. title: Morphological and molecular characterization of Pseudo-nitzschia species from the Levantine Basin (Northeastern Mediterranean) and assessment of domoic acid production
abstract: Domoic acid (DA) is a water-soluble neurotoxin mainly produced by the diatom genus Pseudo-nitzschia. While several potentially toxic species of Pseudo-nitzschia have been reported in Turkish coastal waters, toxicity studies have remained localized to the Sea of Marmara. In this study, three Pseudo-nitzschia species; P. arenysensis (non-toxic), P. brasiliana, and P. galaxiae (both potentially toxic), were isolated from the Levantine Basin of the northeastern Mediterranean Sea. abstract: Oyster reefs are critical interfacial habitats that underpin coastal and marine bio-diversity, and enhance multiple ecosystem services of blue carbon habitats, including water filtration and shoreline stabilization. However, despite this ecological value, oyster reefs have suffered dramatic global declines. The absence of a systemic economic valuation of oyster reef ecosystem services introduces deep uncertainty in the prioritization of restoration areas, thereby constraining coordinated large-scale transboundary conservation, restoration, eco-engineering efforts, and policy. abstract: ABSTRACT Direct seawater oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is critically hampered by chloride‐induced competitive oxidation, corrosion, and active‐site poisoning, driving the urgent need for highly active and chlorine‐tolerant electrocatalysts. Herein, a surface‐engineered electrocatalyst comprising osmium nanoparticles (Os NPs) anchored onto CoFe layered double hydroxide (Os/CoFe LDH) was prepared. title: The Concept of the Maritime, or How to Decolonize the Uncolonizable with Hegel and Coleridge
abstract: This essay interrogates the maritime as a concept and principle of colonization in Hegel’s philosophy of history and seeks to interrupt this imperializing logic with an alternative conception of the maritime from Coleridge’s The Rime of the Ancient Mariner . Examining the sea as history in Hegel and as archive in Coleridge, I argue that, for the latter, the maritime is no mere object of conquest, but throws the human back upon herself and discloses an unexplored psychic landscape. abstract: ABSTRACT Successive waves of extraction in the Caribbean—from plantation monocultures to oil and gas—have reshaped overlapping agrarian, coastal and marine environments, undermining the socio‐ecological foundations of small‐scale fisher livelihoods and generating ongoing conflict between the state, energy sector and fishing communities. abstract: Sea buckthorn fruit is nutrient-rich, and its encapsulated bioactive compounds may provide health benefits. title: Culture of Tulunadu: Traditions, Practices and Modern Transformations - A Critical Review

abstract: Furan fatty acids (FuFAs) are an important family of fatty acids with health-promoting effects, which are especially present in marine sources but also found in other food categories, albeit only at low amounts. Hence, only six or fewer FuFAs were regularly measured in samples. However, some studies, carried out with great effort, demonstrated the existence of many more (uncommon) FuFAs (in total 42). abstract: The tectonic evolution of the Tethyan oceans and the subsequent accretion of East Asian blocks to Eurasia are central to deciphering the geodynamic assembly of the Asian continent. title: Exploitable limits of osmotic energy recovery from Japanese rivers and brine
abstract: This study estimates comparative upper bounds on pressure-retarded osmosis (PRO) power and specific energy for five Japanese river estuaries and desalination-brine scenarios. abstract: The article examines oneiric modality as a stylistic dominant in Neil Gaiman’s novel “The Ocean at the End of the Lane”. title: Understanding how local public policies influence blue food systems. The case of Barcelona
abstract: Abstract Cities are increasingly important actors in food governance, yet their role in blue food systems remains poorly understood, particularly because they generally lack authority over fisheries management. This study examines how municipal policies shaped Barcelona’s blue food system between 1940 and 2023 and asks how local governments influence seafood provisioning through powers exercised beyond production. abstract: Abstract Sub-Neptunes’ molten interiors are expected to accommodate large quantities of volatiles, potentially altering their radius evolution. abstract: ABSTRACT This study evaluates the long‐term corrosion of copper canisters in a deep geological disposal repository, focusing on the environmental transition from oxic to anoxic conditions. abstract: This world literature review presents the current systematics, ecology and toxicology of snakes of the subfamily Hydrophiinae – a genetic clade including the most toxic Australian terrestrial elapids and sea snakes. abstract: Coastal ecotourism destinations are particularly vulnerable to environmental disturbances, including floods, which may disrupt tourism activities and weaken tourists’ perceptions and willingness to visit. abstract: In a laboratory in San Marcos, Texas, is a box containing a small stuffed lion and a luchadore’s mask. abstract: Thyroid nodules are among the most frequently detected endocrine abnormalities, with a considerably higher prevalence in women. abstract: As embedded devices grow more complex, running multiple operating systems on a single device—and deploying virtualization beyond data centers into embedded systems—has become standard. abstract: Previous genetic studies of skeletal variation in threespine stickleback fish (Gasterosteus aculeatus) have focused primarily on striking morphological differences. abstract: Lawallu Village Unit Cooperative (KUD), located in Barru Regency, South Sulawesi, is a community-based economic institution with strong social capital, yet it still faces limited digital leadership capacity in managing services, administration, and data-based decision-making. Most service processes remain manual, archives are not yet digitized, and internal communication lacks standardization. This community service program aimed to strengthen the digital leadership capacity of the cooperative's management board and key members through flexible, self-paced web-based learning. abstract: On Friday, September 26, 2025, the Arts Criticism Area of the National University of the Arts (Argentina) hosted a roundtable discussion on Esto es Teatro and Máquina Teatro, exhibitions held at the Modern Museum of Buenos Aires between 2025 and 2026. title: Mediaciones, medialidades y testimonios: entre cinedocumental, arte y memoria. Un análisis de Lemebel, Cicatrices en la tierra y Este arte que abraza
abstract: This article examines how documentary cinema establishes relationships between art and memory in three documentaries: Lemebel, Cicatrices en la tierra, and Este arte que abraza. The analysis identifies three distinct forms of mediation, mediality, and testimonial practice. Lemebel is an authorial and didactic documentary centered on the recovery of the artist’s archive and the reconstruction of his life and work. title: Network Pharmacology Exploration of Ubidecarenone (Coenzyme Q10): An In Silico, Hypothesis-Generating Study
abstract: Ubidecarenone (coenzyme Q10, CoQ10) is a widely used lipophilic quinone whose therapeutic associations beyond mitochondrial electron transport remain incompletely mapped. This in silico study applied network pharmacology to explore its therapeutic potential. Targets were predicted with SwissTargetPrediction (100 targets; probability 0.014-0.424, only six ≥ 0.10), the Similarity Ensemble Approach (SEA) and PharmMapper; six SwissTargetPrediction targets (ALOX5, ALOX15, PPARG, PPARA, PTGES, APEX1) were also supported by SEA at p < 0.05. title: From national to global: Mapping global center-pivot irrigated cropland with knowledge-guided data augmentation
abstract: Center-pivot irrigated cropland (CPIC) is a large-scale, intensive agricultural irrigation practice with high water-use efficiency. This characteristic enables CPIC to increase crop yields and promote agricultural development, while simultaneously causing groundwater overexploitation and subsequent environmental issues. Mapping the global distribution of CPIC is critical for enhancing water resource management, guiding agricultural policies, and assessing ecological impacts. title: A 500 m deep multipurpose research borehole and monitoring station in Delft, the Netherlands
abstract: The 500 m deep DAPGEO-02 multifunctional research borehole and monitoring station was drilled in Delft in spring 2022. Dinoflagellate biostratigraphy reveals that the borehole goes through the Neogene Upper North Sea Group, including the Waalre, Maassluis, Oosterhout, Diessen, and Groot Heide formations. Below, a stratigraphic gap exists between the late Miocene Diessen and the middle Miocene Groote Heide formations, followed by a much larger gap between the Groote Heide and the lower Eocene Dongen formations. title: A new Caribbean species of the giant isopod genus Bathynomus (Crustacea, Isopoda, Cirolanidae) with notes on its evolutionary history
abstract: Abstract The new species Bathynomus tuebingoborikensis sp. nov., discovered in an historic museum collection, is described. We provide preliminary phylogenetic analyses of the genus, including extant and fossil species, using morphological characters. We reconstruct the evolutionary origin of the genus in the Caribbean, and suggest ten different migration waves all over the world oceans, including multiple recolonizations of the Americas. institutions: Senckenberg Centre for Human Evolution and Palaeoenvironment

title: Villa Ögel: A Vanishing Example of Modern Heritage at Şaşkınbakkal
abstract: This study investigates Villa Ögel, a rare surviving example of Suadiye’s modernist garden-villa era (1940s–1950s), to illuminate its architectural, historical, and socio-cultural significance amid Istanbul’s rapid urban transformation. Suadiye is a coastal residential district on the Anatolian side of Istanbul, with Villa Ögel located in Şaşkınbakkal, a smaller micro-geographical area within the broader Suadiye neighborhood, representing a specific locality within its wider urban and historical context. As neoliberal policies and post-1999 earthquake “renewal” initiatives erased nearly all tr

title: Olinto Dini ( 1805–1866 ) physicist by choice, naturalist by fate
abstract: The naturalist Olinto Dini (18051866) is known within the Tuscan scientific panorama of the 19th century for his studies of the geology of the Garfagnana Valley in Northern Tuscany (Italy).He retired from a teaching position in physics at the University of Pisa, for family reasons, at a very early stage of his scientific career.Nevertheless, he maintained close contacts with the academic world in Pisa, as testified by the correspondence preserved within the "Olinto Dini" collection, housed at the library of the Domus Galilaeana in Pisa.This paper gives a brief overview of his main contributio

title: Review of Salmonid Alphavirus: Focus on Viral Survival, Shedding, Detection and Effects of Vaccination
abstract: This review of salmonid alphavirus provides a collection of the most recent knowledge on the factors relevant for the transmission and control of the virus including updates on SAV survival, viral shedding, detection, and effects of vaccination as reported in peer-reviewed literature, presentations, theses, and annual reports. SAV can survive in all water types, being the longest in colder marine waters without organic loading. The biophysical properties of SAV indicate a moderate to high robustness. abstract: 23-Demethylgorgosterol is an unusual marine sterol scaffold characterized by an atypical 22,23-cyclopropyl-containing side chain and an uncommon sterol substitution pattern. Its recent access through an efficient semi-synthetic route enables systematic structural diversification. In this study, we completed the semi-synthesis and prepared the unnatural diastereomer together with a series of structurally diverse intermediates and derivatives. title: An Energy Integration Free Kubo-Bastin Formula Decomposition
abstract: Kubo formulae play a central role in modern spintronics and condensed matter physics, serving as the foundational ground for studying transport responses in the linear regime. In this work, we propose a reformulation of the widely used Kubo-Bastin decompositions that eliminates the need for numerical energy integration. title: Indian MAHASAGAR and the Evolution of India's Maritime Diplomacy
abstract: India's maritime diplomacy has undergone a decisive transformation over the past decade, evolving from a continental-focused posture toward a proactive, maritime-centric vision for the Indo-Pacific. This article examines that evolution and assesses the operational relevance of minilateral architectures in advancing India's strategic objectives. title: Cytochalasins are a fascinating class of natural compounds: advances in the chemistry, biological activities, mode of action, and structure-activity relationships of novel cytochalasins isolated in the last decade are described
abstract: Cytochalasins are a very intriguing group of natural compounds. Since the first isolation of the well-known cytochalasins A and B in 1966, over 300 analogues have been described as metabolites, primarily produced by various fungal genera. Their bioactivities, targets, total syntheses, and biosyntheses had been also extensively investigated. After the review of Scherlach et al., 2010 several other cytochalasins, isolated from different fungal sources, their biological activities and potential applications, were extensively described. title: Structural Design Strategies of Lead-Free Ternary Metal Halide Scintillators for Advanced X-ray Imaging
abstract: Conspectus The ever-increasing demand for advanced X-ray detection technologies calls for a revolution in conventional inorganic scintillators. In recent years, ternary metal halides (TMHs) have attracted extensive attention from both the scientific and industry communities owing to their strong X-ray absorption, high luminescence efficiencies, and structurally tunable characteristics, positioning them as promising candidates for next-generation scintillation materials. Macroevolutionary insights into the range limits of species and lineages
abstract: Understanding the intrinsic and extrinsic factors that determine the range limits of species is an important goal in biology. Much work has focused on understanding the range limits of populations and individual species, whereas the factors that determine the distributions of evolutionary lineages have received less attention in the range limits literature. In this review I highlight recent macroscale insights into the range limits of flowering plant lineages, and briefly compare these to findings from other taxa. title: EFFECTS OF INVASIVE FISH SPECIES ON NATIVE SPECIES AND AQUATIC ECOSYSTEMS
abstract: Biological invasions have emerged as one of the major drivers of global biodiversity loss, threatening native species, ecosystem functioning, and human well-being. This review examines the impacts of invasive species on native fish species and aquatic ecosystems, with emphasis on mechanisms of invasion, pathways of introduction, ecological consequences, and management strategies. Deliberate and accidental introductions facilitated by globalization, aquaculture, trade, and transportation have accelerated the spread of invasive organisms across freshwater and marine environments. journal: KEBBI JOURNAL OF AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL SCIENCES

title: Pedro Carrere. Un japonista español en el México finisecular: colección, mediación y práctica artística
abstract: Historiography of Japonisme in Latin America has logically prioritized the study of prominent figures such as José Juan Tablada, leaving the role of cultural mediators whose influence proved decisive yet to be examined. Among them, Pedro Carrere stands out; however, his diplomatic career and collecting activities have lacked a systematic reconstruction until now. title: NEUROPROTECTIVE AND MEMORY-ENHANCING EFFECTS OF SARGASSUM TENERRIMUM ETHANOLIC EXTRACT IN SCOPOLAMINE-INDUCED AMNESIA IN WISTAR RATS
abstract: Objectives: The present study aimed to assess the neuroprotective properties and memory enhancement of the ethanolic extract of Sargassum tenerrimum (ST) with regard to the scopolamine-induced amnesia model in Wistar rats and explore the underlying mechanism involved in cholinergic neurotransmission. Methods: The extract was administered orally once daily for 14 consecutive days at doses of 50, 100, and 200 mg/kg. title: Genealogies of protest and resistance in the Scottish Highlands and islands after 1750
abstract: Abstract Histories of protest in the Highlands and Islands have been largely limited to the study of dramatic and large-scale events driven by issues of possession of and access to land after 1850. Most research to date has tended to focus on the crofting counties of the north-west of the region and the paradigmatic land raid, with alternate forms of protest and at different times often relegated to little more than a footnote. title: Crítica de artes latinoamericana, identidad y modernidad: la reunión de Quito (1970)
abstract: The article analyzes the meeting of experts in Latin American arts held in Quito in June 1970, which was part of the study project on the cultures of Latin America proposed in 1966 during the Fourteenth General Conference of UNESCO. Based on a documentary analysis of the sources related to this initiative from UNESCO’s digital archive, the article identifies the project’s objectives, phases, and methodology, highlighting the proposals made at the Quito meeting within this framework. title: The worth of high-resolution inventories: disparities between monthly and annual emission trends in the cement industry
abstract: Abstract Distinctive emissions from individual plants are pivotal for unraveling net-zero paths in the cement industry, as aggregated figures obscure substantial plant-specific variation. We estimated the high spatiotemporal emissions broken down from national to plant levels and from yearly to monthly scales using the Tier 2 bottom-up approach based on the 2006 IPCC Guidelines. Monthly estimates revealed clear seasonal patterns, with spring emissions up to 10.1% higher and winter emissions 12.5% lower than the annual average, driven by plant-level operational variations. title: Prevalence and multimorbidity patterns of thyroid dysfunction in Chinese adults
abstract: The risk of thyroid dysfunction (TD) persists in the Chinese population. However, large-scale epidemiological studies investigating TD prevalence and its geographic disparities are limited. Previous studies have mostly focused on associations between TD and individual organ systems or single medical conditions. This nationwide, large-scale study utilized data from the Meinian Health Check-up database across all 31 provinces of the Chinese mainland. A total of 10,748,391 adults who had health check-ups between 2017 and 2023 and had complete thyroid function results for serum thyroid-stimulating
institutions: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

title: Declines in the diversity of fish represented in British domestic recipes over the past 100 years
abstract: Abstract Fish and shellfish are nutritionally important foods, yet consumption in many high‐income countries remains low and concentrated on a narrow set of environmentally costly species. In the United Kingdom, fish consumption is dominated by a small group of fish, the ‘Big Five’, which is often treated as an inevitable outcome of supply, convenience and ingrained consumer preferences. However, little empirical evidence exists on how and when such preferences emerged, or whether present‐day patterns reflect historical continuity or cultural loss. title: Ecological considerations for reintroducing Chinook salmon upstream of Shasta Dam
abstract: Abstract In this assessment, we reviewed existing literature to assess the ecological risks, benefits, and uncertainties associated with reintroducing Chinook salmon ( Oncorhynchus tshawytcha ) into the McCloud River, a tributary of the Sacramento River, California. Two source populations are being considered for reintroduction by co‐managers in the basin (the Winnemem Wintu Tribe, California Department of Fish and Wildlife, and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration): existing winter‐run Chinook salmon (WRCS) from the mainstem Sacramento River, and Chinook salmon from New Zealand (NZ

title: Facies and paleogeographic conditions of the Late Paleozoic flora burial and preservation in the Southern Tien Shan (based on the Karachatyr Mountains localities)
abstract: The article examines the facies and paleogeographic conditions of flora fossil burial and preservation in the Upper Paleozoic deposits of the Karachatyr Mountains (Southern Fergana, Southern Tien Shan). The study aims to reconstruct the sedimentary environments which controlled the terrestrial vegetation transport, accumulation, and preservation in the Late Carboniferous — Early Permian. title: Energy Efficiency Measures vs. Biofuels - Implications for Vessel Operational Performance
abstract: The purpose of this study is to determine the relative importance of energy saving measures (ESMs) and alternative biofuels for the improvement of ship efficiency and for compliance with new regulations imposed on the maritime transport sector. In light of the fact that ESMs have proven that they are capable of providing a significant fuel saving potential by enhancing the hull condition, propulsion, and internal combustion efficiency as well as through operational optimization, the aim of this study is to investigate the advantages and disadvantages of ESMs compared to biofuels. title: Nutrient legacies from elephant megacarcasses create coldspots of biodiversity and hotspots of ecosystem processes
abstract: Terrestrial megafauna (animals >1,000 kg) have substantial impacts on ecosystems while alive; yet, we know little about the impacts of these ecosystem engineers after they die. Like whale carcasses in the ocean, terrestrial megacarcasses may leave ecological legacies via the nutrient pulses they create on the landscape. Here, we investigated the impact of elephant megacarcasses on savanna ecosystems in Kruger National Park, South Africa. title: Sacralisation and Monumentalisation of World War I in the Isonzo/Soča Region
abstract: This article examines the monumentalisation of World War I in the Isonzo/Soča region (today divided between Italy and Slovenia), promoted by the Italian government and local authorities during the interwar period. Following Italy’s victory in the war, the liberal state – and even more emphatically Mussolini’s regime – fostered a patriotic cult that supported the dictator’s efforts to present Fascism as the rightful heir to that victory. title: Drainage Management by the Department of Public Works and Spatial Planning (PUPR) in Flood Prevention in Padang City
abstract: Background Padang City is vulnerable to flooding because of its coastal and low-lying areas, high rainfall, and drainage systems that are not yet fully optimal. Drainage management is therefore an important part of government efforts to prevent and reduce flood risk. This study aims to describe and analyze drainage management by the Padang City Department of Public Works and Spatial Planning (PUPR) in flood prevention. title: The Efraim Berkovici Collection: Poesiealbum and Diary Writing in "Ilaniah" Children's Village
abstract: In September 1947, a train traveling under the auspices of the Red Cross departed Romania carrying over 420 Jewish children, via Prague, to the Netherlands. The children, among them Holocaust survivors from Transnistria, had been gathered from different parts of Romania, including orphanages, and were taken to the “Ilaniah” children’s village, located on the grounds of a former Jewish psychiatric hospital in Apeldoorn. A smaller group of over thirty Jewish child survivors from Germany arrived a few weeks later. In October 1948, these children boarded a ship, the Negba, and departed for Israel.
