title: From Curaçao to Coro: A Reexamination of Transimperial Marronage in the Eighteenth Century
abstract: This article reassesses the transimperial flight of enslaved Afro-Curaçaoans from the Dutch island of Curaçao to the Spanish mainland of Tierra Firme, particularly Coro, during the eighteenth century. Owing to Spain's policy of royal asylum, enslaved Afro-Curaçaoans could obtain freedom upon entering Spanish territory. Drawing on a detailed 1775 runaway register and colonial correspondence, the article reconstructs who fled, how they escaped, and why they undertook the maritime crossing. abstract: Abstract The insidious collapse of a 38‐year‐old businessman’s hyper‐rational life into a midlife marital crisis compels his psyche to demand a terrifying return to its origins. This paper maps his psychological rebirth by tracing the explicit structural parallels between the stages of the analytical process and the ancient Egyptian solar myth of transformation, illustrating how dream imagery shapes the analytic process. title: Coping with Life’s Challenges in Ottoman Sarajevo: Freed Slaves and Agency in an Early Modern Borderland Society
abstract: This paper aims to fill in the gaps in the social history of the Ottoman borderlands by exploring the social integration and agency of freed slaves in Early Modern Ottoman Sarajevo. Recent scholarship has made considerable advances in evaluating the agency of freed slaves in the Ottoman Empire by using the collective biography approach. However, with few exceptions, attention has mostly been paid to materials relating to the inner parts of the Ottoman world, particularly to the Sharia court protocols of the Istanbul Region. title: The Natural Tourism Riches of Manyu Division, Cameroon: An Inventory of An Exceptional but Underexploited Ecological Endowment
abstract: Manyu Division, in the South-West Region of Cameroon, possesses one of the richest natural tourism endowments in Central Africa, anchored by Korup National Park among the oldest and most bio-diverse rainforests on the continent. It extends across the Takamanda highlands, the Cross River and its tributaries, a landscape of waterfalls, wildlife corridors, and geological formations that together constitute a natural capital of world-class quality. This article presents a systematic inventory of Manyu's natural touristic assets, drawing on archival records, conservation science, government reports
journal: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF HUMANITIES AND CULTURAL STUDIES

title: Dissecting the urban anatomy: modernist layers, institutional landmarks, and the Heritage-City Synergy in Cartagena
abstract: Cartagena, Spain, is a unique Mediterranean coastal city defined by its transition from a rigid 18th-entury military stronghold to a dynamic modern center. While its ancient ruins are well-documented, the city’s later layers – specifically its modernist architecture and institutional landmarks – are often overlooked in urban discourse. This neglect creates a gap between heritage preservation and the living city, risking a “museumification” that disconnects historical sites from contemporary social life. title: Conjunción de Venus y la Luna en la pintura rupestre de Las Peñitas, Hidalgo, México
abstract: En este trabajo se propone que el conjunto rupestre localizado en el sitio Las Peñitas sea la representación de una conjunción lunar con el planeta Venus en su faceta como estrella vespertina, fenómeno que ocurre en el cielo del poniente en dos fechas del año relacionadas con la temporada de lluvias. title: An Investigation into the Protection of Investor Rights of Tsingtao Brewery During the German Occupation Period (1903-1914)
abstract: In 1903, British and German merchants jointly funded the establishment of the Germania Brewery. In accordance with the British law, the Hong Kong Companies Ordinance, they registered the Anglo-German Brewing Company in Hong Kong and then set up a branch in Qingdao. This corporate organizational model, together with the colonial legal environment, jointly constituted the institutional foundation for the protection of investor rights of Tsingtao Brewery. title: Political Ecology of Agrarian Change in Social Forestry among the Tana Ai Community in Sikka Regency, East Nusa Tenggara
abstract: This paper examines how the dynamics of Social Forestry, which serves as a means of establishing new spaces/territories, trigger agrarian, social, economic, and ecological changes in communities, and even give rise to socio-territorial conflicts between the state and local communities. Building on the political ecology perspective, this article addresses two interrelated questions. title: The Imprint of a Few: Editorial Authority and Epistemic Inequalities in Elite Biology Journals
abstract: As scholarly publishing becomes increasingly commodified, market-oriented definitions of excellence are reshaping the organization and hierarchization of scientific knowledge. Using a sociology of elites framework, this article examines how the social conditions under which knowledge is produced, evaluated, and circulated shape epistemic inequalities. It focuses on journal editors—who play a central role in defining legitimate knowledge—but remain understudied as holders of scientific and editorial authority. title: «Ad usum discipulorum». Justo Florian Lobeck y el mercado bibliográfico del latín en Chile durante la década de 1860
abstract: This article examines the participation of Justo Florian Lobeck in the Chilean typographic space in the mid-nineteenth century; in particular, it explores his forms of intervention in the configuration of a structured and functional bibliographic corpus to the requirements of Chilean secondary education for Latin studies. title: “A Vile Character”
abstract: Alfons Sutter was perhaps the most notorious German police agent in the Łódź ghetto. A native of Łódź, he and dozens of other Volksdeutsche (ethnic Germans) were hired by the criminal police (Kriminalpolizei, or Kripo) after Nazi Germany conquered and annexed the city. As a Kripo employee from 1940 to 1945, he took part in the arrest and torture of countless Jews. title: The Amphistegina bleaching index as a tool for evaluating reef-ecosystem health: new data from the Maldives & Australia provide updated insights
abstract: Abstract The Amphistegina bleaching index (ABI) provides a simple, low-cost method for assessing photo-oxidative stress in reef-dwelling foraminifera. The ABI, developed for Florida reefs, has been applied to assess the extent of such stress in several regions globally, including the Maldives, and now in Australia. Here, we assess the application of the ABI for capturing variability in photo-inhibitory stress across contrasting reef settings and temporal scales. title: Condition and Durability Evaluation of Reinforced-Concrete Bridge Girders in the Surabaya Container Terminal Environment
abstract: An access bridge at PT Terminal Petikemas Surabaya has operated since 1992 in a chloride-bearing marine environment and carries repetitive heavy operational vehicles. The reinforced-concrete girders were repaired by epoxy injection and strengthened with carbon-fibre-reinforced polymer between 2010 and 2014; however, cracks were identified again in 2021. abstract: Malaria control in Ghana's coastal savannah is constrained by outdoor biting and insecticide resistance, yet controlled evidence on environmental management is scarce. This study estimated the effect of an integrated environmental management (IEM) package on malaria parasitaemia among adults. title: A Study of Artistic Training for Chinese Women at the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts de Lyon (1921–1946)
abstract: During the early twentieth century, increasing numbers of Chinese students travelled to France to pursue artistic education. Among the institutions that received these students, the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts de Paris has attracted substantial scholarly attention, while the contribution of the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts de Lyon has been investigated less extensively. title: Tendencias y ausencias en el estudio de la migración colombiana a Chile: Una revisión de alcance para proyectar la investigación
abstract: Over the past two decades, Chile has become one of the top five destinations for Colombian migrants (DANE, 2022). This phenomenon has spurred a significant increase in research aimed at understanding various dimensions of these migrations. This study aims to analyze academic research on Colombian migration to Chile from 2005 to 2024, examining the main themes addressed, knowledge about places of origin, motivations for migration, reflections on the role of the Colombian internal armed conflict in these migrations, and the challenges arising from these studies. title: Petagram‐Scale Dissolved Organic Carbon Stocks in Alaskan Permafrost Soils
abstract: Abstract The pan‐Arctic permafrost region hosts vast amounts of soil organic carbon, a pool increasingly susceptible to climate‐driven changes. Dissolved organic carbon (DOC) is a key component of this carbon pool. However, its stocks and fluxes remain poorly understood due to limited measurements and challenges of tracking subsurface fluxes across landscapes. abstract: This study aimed to analyse the spatial distribution and spatiotemporal clustering of AIDS notifications among men in all 5570 Brazilian municipalities between 2014 and 2023. Using an ecological design, data on AIDS notifications among men (≥ 13 years) were retrieved from Brazil’s Notifiable Diseases Information System database. Spatial analysis included global autocorrelation via Moran’s I and the identification of local clusters via the Local Indicators of Spatial Association applied to Empirical Bayes smoothed rates. title: A comprehensive review on the phytochemical constituents and bioactivities of Jatropha curcas L.
abstract: Jatropha curcas L., belonging to the family Euphorbiaceae, is a multifunctional medicinal plant with extensive ethnopharmacological relevance. Various parts of the plant are used to treat a wide range of ailments. Traditionally, it has been used for the treatment of cancer, digestive disorders, skin diseases, and infectious diseases. abstract: Introduction: The arteriovenous fistula is the vascular access of choice for many patients undergoing hemodialysis, due to its importance in ensuring effective and continuous treatment. However, its functionality can be compromised by complications such as thrombosis, stenosis, infection, aneurysms, hematomas, and issues associated with puncture. In this context, nursing interventions are essential for monitoring, maintenance, and preservation of the vascular access. title: Weatherlands for Sky & Bones
abstract: This two-breathed essay emerges from the convergence of Indigenous and settler practices of knowing, feeling, and moving. Written from Aotearoa (New Zealand) and Naarm (Melbourne), Weatherlands for Sky & Bones draws from a cross-cultural, transdisciplinary collaboration in performance philosophy. As an experimental mode for thinking through performance, we explore a praxis of weatherlands. abstract: Aim . To analyze primary disability due to cardiovascular diseases (CVD) and the need for vocational rehabilitation and habilitation among working-age individuals who were granted disability status in the Arkhangelsk Region between 2019 and 2023. Material and methods . The study was based on individual rehabilitation programs for working-age people recognized as disabled for the first time due to CVD (n=1982). abstract: The Great Nicobar project carries a reported cost of ₹72,000 crore, and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change informed the Rajya Sabha in August 2023 that an estimated 9.64 lakh trees would be felled for it. The Great Nicobar Mega Project is one of India’s largest and most ambitious infrastructure projects. abstract: Doping among competitive athletes remains a persistent threat to the integrity of sport, athlete health, and the legitimacy of sporting achievement. This study aims to analyze the causal factors, impacts, and prevention efforts related to doping cases among athletes in competitive sport through a literature review. A narrative literature review was conducted using scientific journal articles, official reports of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA), and Indonesian sports legislation retrieved from Google Scholar, PubMed/PMC, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, Garuda, and legal databases. title: Multidisciplinary insights into Late Pleistocene-Holocene palaeoenvironment at the archaeo-palaeontological Loltún Cave site in Yucatán, Mexico
abstract: Abstract A lack of well-dated archaeological and palaeontological sequences containing proxy-based palaeoenvironmental information has hindered the reconstruction of long-term human-biodiversity interactions in Mexico. Here, we re-evaluate the stratigraphy of the Huechil Chamber in Loltún Cave, a key Yucatán site whose archaeo-palaeontological sequence, dating from the Pleistocene to the Late Holocene, provides critical insights into the environmental conditions that shaped human settlement from near the onset of our species’ presence in this part of the world. abstract: Endophytic microorganisms residing within mangrove plants endure extreme abiotic stresses, making them valuable candidates for bioprospecting. This study evaluated the phenotypic diversity, biochemical characteristics, and metabolic capabilities of cultivable endophytic microorganisms associated with Avicennia marina from the mangrove ecosystem of Navsari, Gujarat, India. title: Assessing the potential and cost of enhanced rock weathering in China
abstract: Large-scale carbon dioxide removal is essential for carbon neutrality, but current options face constraints. Enhanced rock weathering is a promising alternative, yet its viability at a national scale in China remains unquantified. Here we show, using a spatially explicit analysis across China’s croplands, that a single-year basalt application could remove 0.44–0.79 billion tonnes of CO2 by 2100, at a net life-cycle-adjusted cost of 127–226 US dollars per tonne of CO2 removed. title: Seakeeping Comparison of FPSO Hulls with and Without a Moonpool at Forward Speed
abstract: Moonpool openings can alter vessel motions through interactions between the external wave field, hull motion and the enclosed water column. This study compares two floating production, storage and offloading hull configurations, with and without a moonpool, at a reported speed of 13.45 knots and wave headings of 90°, 120° and 150°. title: Purification of Water Bodies from Heavy Metals using Biotechnology in the Absheron Peninsula
abstract: One of the pressing environmental problems in Azerbaijan's arid regions is the management of lakes and reservoirs, most of which are man-made. The Absheron industrial region contains over 200 water bodies contaminated with heavy metals — lead, copper, and zinc — at levels significantly exceeding the maximum permissible concentration. Research was conducted to identify approaches and principles for the biotechnological treatment of water bodies in the Absheron industrial region contaminated with heavy metals. title: Trace metals contamination in freshwater fish in Brazil: related factors, environmental impacts, and risks to human health
abstract: Freshwater fish are essential components of the aquatic food chain and an important source of protein and nutrients for various communities, especially riverine populations. However, water pollution is one of the main causes of metal bioaccumulation in the organs of these animals. This study conducted a systematic review of the scientific literature on trace metal contamination in freshwater fish in Brazil. title: Water Quality in Relation to Phytoplankton Abundance and Diversity of Selected Reservoirs in Kazaure, Jigawa State, Nigeria
abstract: This study investigates the composition of phytoplankton species as bio-indicators of water quality in Wawan Rafi Reservoir and Kazaure, Jigawa State, Nigeria. A total of 962 and 1262 organisms/litre were recorded for Kazaure Reservoir and Wawan Rafi Reservoir respectively. abstract: Highlights Nurse-led primary care interventions play a central role in harm reduction strategies for people who use drugs. This approach provides a comprehensive and effective response to the needs of people who use drugs, promoting equity and inclusion. By raising awareness among nursing professionals about their role in implementing strategies for this population, we can help reduce the stigma associated with drug use. abstract: Thousands of microfauna remains, predominantly amphibian, were recovered from an Iron Age/Roman site near Cambridge, England by MHI Ltd (MOLA-Headland infrastructure), creating considerable media speculation about how and when these animals died and why so many were concentrated in one gully. We investigated the taxonomy, taphonomy, dating, and period of mortality, of specimens sub-sampled from the original samples. Results showed this was the debris left by a community of predators. title: Lead Weight Production and Use in Fishing Gear at the Deltaic Settlement of Antic (Amposta, Tarragona, Catalonia) during the Late Iron Age (Third–Second Centuries BCE)
abstract: Abstract The archaeological investigations conducted at the Iberian site of l’Antic (Amposta, Catalonia), located in the Ebro delta region, have identified a domestic sector associated with the production of fishing lead weights. These artifacts, together with other lead elements linked to their manufacture, are documented in stratigraphic contexts dated to the Late Iron Age (third–second centuries BCE). title: Magnetite sandstones of the Haghartsin Fe-Ti deposit (Armenia): mineralogical and geochemical features
abstract: The Haghartsin deposit of ferruginous sandstones (Armenia) is hosted by Middle Eocene sedimentary rocks. A productive horizon is composed of alternating beds of volcanic sandstones and gravelites with magnetite interbeds and massive strata. Five ferruginous sandstone beds with cross-bedding extend for 5.5 km with an average thickness of 2.5 m. The chemical composition of rocks have elevated Fe, Ti, V, Zn, As, and Ge contents relatively to the clarke value and are depleted Rb, Cs, and Ba. title: Coffin tree-ring δ¹⁸O reveals prolonged drought contributing to the collapse of the Northern Song Dynasty
abstract: The Northern Song Dynasty (960–1127 CE) was one of the most prosperous dynasties in Chinese history. In its final years, the Fang La Rebellion (1120–1122 CE), the most severe peasant rebellion of the period, erupted in the lower Yangtze River basin (LYRB) and contributed to the dynasty’s collapse. However, the role of climate in the rise of this rebellion remains unclear due to the lack of high-resolution paleoclimate records in the LYRB over this critical epoch. title: Reconstructing the aqueous environment of the Ryugu parent body through the speciation of multiple elements
abstract: The parent body of the C-type asteroid Ryugu experienced aqueous alteration. The past aqueous environments have been reconstructed using mineralogies and geochemical modeling, often assuming Na-Cl-rich fluid compositions. Here, we reconstruct Ryugu’s aqueous environment using chemical equilibrium modeling constrained by Electron Probe Microanalyzer (EPMA) and X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectroscopy. abstract: Abstract Applying a Science and Technology Studies (STS) lens and building on Rancièrian philosophy and the aesthetic turn in International Relations (IR), the article explores the possibilities that the mobilisation of knowledge from the artistic field holds for the pluralisation of expert knowledge-making in the global governance of sustainable development. title: Mō Tātou, Ā, Mō Kā Uri Ā Muri Ake Nei: Visioning Mokopuna Futures Through Climate Change Adaptation Strategies
abstract: In Murihiku Southland in Aotearoa New Zealand, Māori are already responding and adapting to the impacts of climate change. Drawing on twenty interviews with Māori leaders, environmental practitioners, and knowledge holders, this kaupapa Māori (Māori-led) study examines perspectives on adapting to climate disruption. Interviewees identified a range of whakapapa (ancestry)-based adaptation strategies rooted in intergenerational care, cultural continuity, and relational governance. title: The Great American Novel Revisited: Myth, Memory, and Morality in Moby-Dick
abstract: Herman Melville’s Moby-Dick; or, The Whale (1851) occupies an anomalous position in the American literary canon: largely misunderstood and commercially unsuccessful upon publication, it was subsequently elevated during the twentieth-century "Melville Revival" to the preeminent status of the Great American Novel. title: Vibrio cholerae non-O1/non-O139 Serotype O27 septicemia in a patient with decompensated chronic liver disease - A Case Report
abstract: Vibrio cholerae serotypes that belong to the non-O1 and non-O139 category, especially O27, are emerging opportunistic pathogens being increasingly associated with severe septicemia, particularly in immunocompromised individuals. Most non-O1 or non-O139 serogroups cause sporadic infections, but certain strains of Vibrio cholerae, including the O27 serotype, have acquired additional virulence factors, raising concerns about their potential for more invasive disease. We report a case of septic shock due to NOVC (serotype O27) in a patient suffering from decompensated chronic liver disease (DCLD).

title: Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for Integrated Liner Shipping Route and Schedule Optimization with Weekly Port Time Windows
abstract: Designing an efficient and cost-effective port network requires accounting for practical constraints, such as port time operation windows. Ignoring these constraints can lead to impractical schedules. This paper presents a method for optimizing liner shipping routes and schedules while accommodating multiple weekly port time windows. A mathematical model is developed to minimize overall costs by optimizing the sequence of port calls, schedules, and sailing speeds. title: Local Prey Use by Invasive European Green Crabs in a New England Salt-Marsh Estuary
abstract: Abstract Impacts of generalist invaders are often discussed as species-level effects, but the trophic interactions that produce those effects are local. We dissected and visually examined stomach contents from 271 European green crabs ( Carcinus maenas ) collected from 21 sampling groups in the Plum Island estuary, Massachusetts, during June–July 2025. We compared the occurrence of foods across marsh-associated primary creeks, main-stem channels, and the open sound. title: Teaching for resilience in university outdoor education fieldwork: a poetic inquiry
abstract: Outdoor education is a well-established and growing field in Australia. University courses are vital for preparing outdoor educators and outdoor education teachers to work with school-aged students across various outdoor roles. These courses offer more than the preparation to instruct outdoor activities; they also prepare graduates to teach in, through, about and with outdoor environments. Outdoor education programs in schools regularly claim to develop ‘resilience’ among participating students. title: Socio-Environmental Controversies in Chile’s Peatland Governance: From Global Climate Discourses to Local Extractivist Realities
abstract: This article analyzes the legislative process that culminated in Chile’s 2024 Peatland Protection Law (Law 21.660), employing critical discourse analysis to examine the parliamentary debates that shaped this regulatory framework. Unlike previous studies on environmental governance in Chile—which have focused on identifying specific conflicts, characterizing extractivist patterns, or diagnosing institutional fragility—this work exposes the socio-technical controversies underlying peatland governance. title: Potential for Carotenoid and Other Bioproducts Production by a Brazilian Dunaliella salina Isolate Using a High Photon Flux Density Strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT Dunaliella species are among the most significant biological sources of carotenoids, notably beta‐carotene. Given that chemical synthesis offers a more cost‐effective alternative to biotechnological cultivation, optimizing production strategies is essential for economic viability. This study investigated the optimization of bioproduct synthesis in a Brazilian strain of Dunaliella salina by evaluating the effects of high photon flux density (PFD) and temperature under low‐salinity conditions (1 mol L −1 NaCl) to facilitate downstream processing. title: Evaluation of Iron Ore Dust Emission Rates and Associated Bacterial Load
abstract: The National Industrial and Mining Company (SNIM) is facing significant dust emissions, raising serious environmental and public health concerns. This study aimed to characterize airborne dust emissions from mining activities and to assess their physicochemical and microbiological composition. Dust samples were analyzed and found to contain hazardous heavy metals, including lead, copper, nickel, and cobalt. title: Plant invasions threaten a critically imperiled inland salt marsh ecosystem
abstract: Abstract Inland salt marshes (ISM) form in non-arid regions when mineral soil is infiltrated by salt-saturated groundwater that rises to the surface in natural saltwater springs or seeps. ISMs were historically found across the eastern USA but presently the few remaining intact are critically imperiled natural communities. Due to their highly saline conditions, ISMs support regionally rare halophytic plants, and they are also susceptible to invasion by salt-tolerant invasive plants. abstract: El estudio tuvo como objetivo caracterizar los patrones histopatológicos hepáticos en peces fluviales de la Amazonía ecuatoriana y explorar su asociación con estructuras morfológicamente compatibles con microplásticos. abstract: The oropharyngeal cavity of turtles exhibits considerable morphological diversity associated with differences in habitat, diet, and feeding strategies. abstract: ABSTRACT Interactions between microbes shape the structure and function of microbial communities. While studying interactions is key to understanding microbial communities as a whole, gaining a detailed mechanistic view is challenging due to the number of co-occurring interactions. Here, we focus on a single class of shared nutrients, the cobalamin (vitamin B 12 ) family of enzyme cofactors known as cobamides, to study nutrient interactions in laboratory consortia of increasing complexity. title: The Eastern Flank as NATO’s Geopolitical Code
abstract: This article focuses on NATO’s Eastern Flank. It addresses the identified research gap in literature concerning the insufficient conceptualisation of NATO’s Eastern Flank. Specifically, the authors attempt to answer two fundamental questions: what geographical area constitutes NATO’s Eastern Flank, and which member states should be considered part of it? The analysis adopts a geopolitical perspective, with particular consideration of the concept of geopolitical codes. title: Phytochemical Profiling, In Vitro Antioxidant, and Anticancer Activities of Ethanolic Extract of Salicornia Europaea L. Flowers
abstract: Salicornia europaea L. is a salt-tolerant halophyte of increasing scientific interest because of its nutritional value and potential as a source of bioactive phytochemicals. This study investigated the phytochemical composition, in vitro antioxidant capacity, and anticancer activity of an ethanolic extract from S. europaea L. flowers. Dried flowers were extracted with ethanol and subjected to qualitative phytochemical screening and chromatographic profiling to identify major secondary metabolites. title: Hydropeaking Catalyzes Redox Reactions in Impacted Aquifers: A First Field Evidence
abstract: Abstract Hydropeaking indicates the sudden and frequent fluctuation of river stage caused by the operation of hydropower plants. This river alteration affects numerous physical, chemical, biological, and ecohydrological processes in surface water bodies. The impact of hydropeaking on groundwater hydraulics has been investigated only recently through modeling and experimental studies at multiple spatial scales. title: Market Trends and Challenges for Alabama's Emerging Oyster Aquaculture Industry
abstract: Different marketing channels influence farm profitability by affecting the costs that producers incur and the prices they receive. This article quantifies oyster sales volume and price by market channel in Alabama's commercial oyster aquaculture sector and assesses challenges to expanding farm businesses. The results show that many oyster producers are selling exclusively through one channel, which raises questions about their resiliency and their capacity to adapt to a dynamic single market. title: Genome report: sequencing of Helicoverpa- infecting Ophryocystis sp. confirms cryptic diversity and changes in gene content of Lepidoptera-infecting apicomplexan parasites
abstract: Apicomplexan parasites of insects represent a largely unexplored branch of the tree of life. Their small size and lack of informative phenotypic traits can obscure their diversity and many lineage-specific adaptations to different host species. To better understand how these parasites have evolved, we have sequenced and annotated the genome of a neogregarine parasite of moths in the family Noctuidae, including Helicoverpa armigera. title: Omni-Directional Wall-Climbing Robot: A Novel Mechatronic System with Propulsion-Based Adhesion
abstract: This paper presents the design, implementation, prototype development, and qualitative evaluation of an omni-directional wall-climbing robot using a propulsion-based adhesion mechanism.

title: Spatio-temporal patterns of diversity and distribution of common Megachile bees across agroclimatic gradients in Eastern India
abstract: Abstract Bees of the genus Megachile (Megachilidae; Hymenoptera) are among the most efficient pollinators of wild and cultivated plants, yet their diversity, distribution, and seasonal dynamics remain inadequately documented across varied agroclimatic landscapes in India. Despite their recognized contribution to crop pollination, previous studies have largely overlooked spatial and seasonal variation in Megachile assemblages, especially in Eastern India. title: Actinomycetota-Derived Metabolites in Pancreatic Cancer: Chemical Diversity, Metabolic Vulnerability, and Translational Barriers
abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma remains among the deadliest malignancies worldwide, and effective therapies are still lacking. Actinomycetota are among the richest microbial sources of bioactive secondary metabolites, and three agents in clinical use against pancreatic malignancy derive from them — streptozotocin, everolimus and doxorubicin — though all three are indicated for neuroendocrine rather than ductal tumors. title: Movement ecology of post-breeding gulls reveals wetland connectivity in northwestern Africa
abstract: Wetlands are among the most threatened ecosystems worldwide, and their loss increasingly compromises landscape connectivity essential for persistence of waterbird populations. In the Mediterranean region, and particularly in northwestern Africa, conservation prioritisation has largely focused on sites supporting high bird numbers, while the role of wetlands in maintaining functional connectivity remains poorly understood. title: Colonial Alien: House Crows, Disposability and Necropolitics in Urban Tanzania
abstract: ABSTRACT Which lives are allowed to flourish in the city, and which are rendered excessive, alien, or disposable? This article examines kunguru (a Swahili term for crows/ravens, commonly referring to the house crow, Corvus splendens , in urban Tanzania) in Dar es Salaam as a lens through which to analyze colonial afterlives, urban waste infrastructures, and the biopolitics of multispecies life in a postcolonial African city. title: Two-dimensional calculations for the novel axial turbo-vapor compressor
abstract: Abstract Turbo-vapor compressors (TVCs) are critical for generating vacuum pressure in a novel combined cycle for electricity and freshwater production. This paper presents a new TVC design comprising a single axial compressor rotor directly driving a single axial turbine rotor, aiming to improve efficiency, increase allowable mass flow rate, and reduce cost and losses. title: The role of local governance and financial capacities in the effectiveness of international environmental agreements: Evidence from the Ramsar convention
abstract: ABSTRACT Wetlands are critical components of natural water infrastructure, delivering hydrological regulation, biodiversity support, and climate resilience, yet they continue to deteriorate globally. This article provides new causal evidence on the effectiveness of International Environmental Agreements (IEAs) by examining the impacts of wetland designation under the Ramsar Convention. title: BEYOND CHARON’S OBOL: COIN AND COIN-LIKE DEPOSITIONS IN FUNERARY ASSEMBLAGES AT PARION FROM THE CLASSICAL TO THE ROMAN PERIOD
abstract: This article examines funerary monetary deposition in 75 documented contexts from the South/Tavşandere Necropolis of Parion, dated from the Late Classical/Early Hellenistic to the Roman Imperial period. The dataset is analysed at context level and distinguishes ordinary struck coins, coin-like objects, and modified monetary deposits, while keeping coin issue date separate from grave/context date. title: The vegetation associations and flora of Hi’Tara, a shell cay, Te Whanga, Rēkohu / Wharekauri / Chatham Island
abstract: The islands of Te Whanga Lagoon, Rēkohu / Wharekauri / Chatham Island are scarcely documented. Two of the islands are shell cays, Moturangaranga and Hi’Tara. In this paper the geology, physiography, landforms, vegetation associations and some of the biota of Hi’Tara are documented. Hi’Tara has a vascular flora of 50 taxa and four fungi (two rusts, one leaf spotting fungus and a mildew). Fifty-two percent of the vascular plants and fungi are naturalised to the Chatham Islands. title: Field Preparation, Sampling Protocols, and Pilot Study of Amoebae in Freshwater Bodies
abstract: Free-living amoebae, living in freshwater ecosystems, constitute an important ecological group among microscopic eukaryotic organisms. Various amoebae belonging to the order (Adl et al.) can be used as potential bioindicators in assessing the trophic state, organic matter loading, microhabitat characteristics, and ecological variability of water bodies. Since most of these organisms are microscopic in size, their study requires proper field preparation, standardized sampling, preservation of living material, and laboratory microscopic analysis. title: The Maghribi Scholars and the Development of Islam in Bilad al-Sudan up to 1900 AD
abstract: From the emergence of Islam in the Arabian Peninsula in the 7th century AD, to its expansion and development across continents of the world, series of factors have come into play to make the religion distinct among other forms of religions. This is in terms of ideology, ideals and practices. On the other hand, its mode of dispersion as well as expansion from the Arabian Peninsula to other parts of the world became distinct and have resulted to its wide acceptance as well as resurgence of its decayed ideals centuries after another. title: Classification of mobile robots for rescue operations
abstract: Search and rescue operations in case of disasters are typically time-sensitive and are conducted under hazardous conditions, with limited access to the affected area. Despite the advances in disaster risk management, events such as earthquakes continue to cause significant loss of life, underscoring the need for more effective rescue techniques. In this context, mobile rescue robots are emerging as a promising tool to support traditional search and rescue operations and to reduce the risk to rescue teams. abstract: The eruption of the Tonga submarine volcano on January 15, 2022 generated a strong pressure wave, so-called Lamb wave, which orbited the Earth a few times. title: Assessment of Sustainable Indigenous Building Materials in Selected Resorts in Lagos State, Nigeria
abstract: In Nigeria, the move towards sustainable construction has spurred growing interest in locally sourced building materials that meet climatic and cultural needs while minimising environmental impact. This study examines the use and perceived adoption of five sustainable indigenous building materials (compressed earth blocks, bamboo, laterite, timber and stone) in three case-study resorts in Lagos State, Nigeria: La Campagne Tropicana Resort, Ibeju-Lekki (Case 1); Whispering Palms Resort, Iworo, Badagry (Case 2); and Rosh Beach Resort, Badagry (Case 3). title: Swietenia mahogani Fruit Shell-Based Carbon as a Filter Medium for Domestic Liquid Waste: A Preliminary Evaluation
abstract: Domestic wastewater generated from daily household activities can degrade environmental water quality if discharged without adequate treatment. Filtration is one of the most widely applied preliminary treatment methods due to its simplicity and effectiveness in increasing water quality. Activated wood carbon (AWC) is widely used as an adsorbent in filtration systems. However, commercially produced AWC can be expensive, prompting interest in developing carbon from lignocellulosic waste such as mahogany fruit shells. title: The Impact of Synthetic Osmoprotectants and Salsola vermiculata on Growth of Streptomyces sp.AH1 Isolated from an Arid-Soil
abstract: Soil salinity is a major environmental constraint that adversely affects microbial growth and plant productivity. Actinomycetes are recognized as important producers of phytohormones, particularly indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), while halophytes possess the ability to produce and accumulate osmoprotective compounds. title: Influence of Nonpolar Amino Acids on Phase Transitions of Atmospheric Aerosol Particles
abstract: Abstract The fate of aerosol particles in the atmosphere depends, in part, on their composition, morphology, and phase transitions. Studies of aerosol phase transitions have focused on aerosol particles with organic compounds consisting of C, H, and O atoms, although a substantial fraction of organic compounds contains heteroatoms such as sulfur and nitrogen. In this study, nonpolar amino acids were used to study the effect of organonitrogen compounds on phase transitions of droplets using optical microscopy. title: Postcolonial perspectives on neoliberal humanitarian governance and the Rohingya refugee crisis in Bangladesh
abstract: The global refugee crisis situation is increasingly being subsumed under the humanitarian-development nexus (HDN), which, otherwise, informs humanitarian interventions within the normative framework of northern stakeholders including development agencies. While refugee studies have already explored HDN, there is still a lack of critical research on HDN, especially in the context of neoliberal governance. title: Invasive or non-invasive trapping of otters and the use of scent lures and baits: a review
abstract: Abstract Animals are often trapped to learn more about a species’ behavioural ecology, either invasively with live traps or non-invasively with hair- or camera traps. The use of scent lures or baits can help to attract animals to the trap site. The aim of this study was to identify the best and most efficient trapping techniques and scent lure or bait for research on Eurasian otters ( Lutra lutra ). abstract: Abstract Although the Tatun Volcanic Group (TVG) looms over the metropolitan capital region of Taiwan, the threats it poses are only vaguely known. Here, as a first step toward improving understanding those threats, we investigate the Shamao complex, one of the youngest and smallest features of the TVG. title: Production and Characterization of Polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) from an Agricultural By-Product Using Bacillus thuringiensis CICIM (B2031)
abstract: The widespread overuse of petroleum plastics has led to serious environmental challenges. This has necessitated the pursuit of greener alternatives that would reduce or eliminate mankind’s unsustainable and toxic dependence on the recalcitrant petroleum plastics. Polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) is a potential substitute candidate for the production of biodegradable plastics. title: Municipal Libraries as Community Learning Spaces: A Model for Educational Resource Management in Western Visayas
abstract: This mixed-methods study used a triangulation design to evaluate municipal libraries in Western Visayas as vital community learning spaces. The paper emphasized libraries' transformative role in supporting lifelong learning and social engagement in the digital age. Thirty-seven librarians and library staff participated in quantitative data collection, while fifteen librarians took part in qualitative interviews. abstract: This study investigates the primary and secondary buckling behavior of thin-walled composite cylinders subjected to external pressure using analytical formulations and finite element (FE) modeling. title: Implementation of OHS Internal Audit as Hazard Control at Semarang Container Terminal
abstract: The rapid growth of global maritime trade has increased the risk of occupational accidents at container terminals, necessitating a strong Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) system. This study aims to examine the relationship between the implementation of internal OHS audits, communication patterns, and hazard control at container terminals in Semarang City. title: Patronage and Accounting Between the Philippines and China, 1733–1797
abstract: Abstract Missionary efforts followed the expansion of the Old World’s frontiers, often entwined with trade. This article reviews the accounts of the Franciscan mission in China and of the obras pías of Manila during the eighteenth century to analyse how local conditions and empire-wide structures translated into specific actions on the ground. title: Halophytes-associated endophytic fungi for sustainable development
abstract: Abstract Halophytes, naturally adapted to survive and grow under high-salinity conditions, harbour complex internal microbiomes composed of endophytic microorganisms that persist within plant tissues without causing disease. Among these, endophytic fungi play a crucial role in enhancing host plant growth and stress tolerance. Halophytes host a diverse community of endophytic fungi that are naturally adapted to extreme saline and arid environments. abstract: The estimation of Post-Mortem Interval (PMI) remains a global challenge, but the estimation of Post-Mortem Submersion Interval (PMSI) in cases of drowning or those submerged from aquatic ecosystems is still particularly difficult. abstract: Urban-tree controversies often arise when evidence measured at one biological or geographical scale is used to justify management decisions at another. Conocarpus erectus L. provides a useful test case because it is valued for stress tolerance and restoration in parts of its native range, while large introduced plantings have attracted concern over pollen, roots, water use, biodiversity, allelopathy and naturalization. abstract: Understanding how risk perception relates to self-protection is essential for improving emergency preparedness within higher education institutions. This study analyses these two dimensions among members of the University of Macerata (Italy) through a case study based on 174 questionnaires. abstract: The increasing complexity of maritime logistics activities requires an integrated information system to support efficient container movement management. PT. Perusahaan Pelayaran Nusantara Panurjwan (Samudera Indonesia Group) utilizes the Shipping Information System (SIS) as a digital solution to improve operational effectiveness, information accuracy, and coordination among stakeholders involved in container transportation. abstract: This study investigated associations among sexual self-schemas, attachment-related anxiety and avoidance in close relationships, and sexual compulsivity among young adults. abstract: Hydropower infrastructures are central to sustainability transitions but are also embedded in historically layered landscapes of meaning, identity, and governance. This article examines how cultural heritage is mobilised and constrained in the relicensing of Swedish hydropower facilities under the National Plan for Modern Environmental Conditions (NAP). abstract: Hutan mangrove di Kelurahan Jenebora, Kabupaten Penajam Paser Utara, mengalami degradasi akibat tumpahan minyak tahun 2018 dan tekanan pembangunan Ibu Kota Nusantara, sehingga upaya pemulihannya memerlukan pembiayaan dan dukungan masyarakat. abstract: This study investigated the length–weight relationship and condition factors of ichthyofauna species in Okamini Stream, a segment of the New Calabar River, Rivers State, Nigeria. Fish samples were assessed for length, weight, length–weight relationships and condition factors across sampling Stations and Months and analysed following standard method using identification keys and measuring instruments. title: The Identification and Morphological Description of Parmarion martensi in The Protected Forest Area of The Southern Tip of Tarakan
abstract: This study aims to identify and describe the morphology of shell-less snails (slugs) in the Gunung Selatan Protected Forest area of ​​Tarakan City. The research used a descriptive qualitative approach with a purposive sampling method. Sampling was conducted from November to December 2025 at four observation stations, each using a 20 x 20 meter plot. The results showed that one shell-less snail species was found at all observation stations, namely Parmarion martensi. This species has unique morphological characteristics in the form of a reduced shell as a form of adaptation to its environment.

title: Spatial and Social Mechanisms for Urban Development through Community Festival:
abstract: Abstract: This paper explores the social and spatial mechanisms of two community festivals regarded as cultural capitals through a comparative lens. One is the floating Hikiyama in the Karatsu Kunchi festival in Karatsu City, Japan; the other is the revival of the creation and procession of Sapao in Chiang Mai, Thailand. title: PLACE-BASED INTERPRETATION OF ORANG ASLI LIFE-COURSE HERITAGE
abstract: This study reframes Orang Asli (OA) cultural practices as a life-course and spatial system within Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) Domain 3. It connects them to care settings, households, Adat institutions, burial boundaries and ancestral sites. Studies emphasise festive events, weakening recognition of continuity across life phases. The research combined interviews with OA knowledge holders and representatives with ethnographic, academic and heritage sources. Content analysis coded manifestations by social role, ritual purpose, symbolic meaning, participation pattern and community context.

abstract: This study analyzes the representation and function of smong narrative in the children's book "Itam and U" as a disaster literacy media based on local culture. Smong is an oral tradition from Simeulue that functions as a tsunami early warning system through poetry and collective memory. Using a computer-aided qualitative content analysis approach, the study extracted and analyzed text from 48 pages of the book to identify patterns of smong representation, nature signs, and disaster risk reduction education. The results of the study show that smong is not presented as a separate exotic element

title: Effect of Selected Food Crop Outputs on Poverty Level of Farm Households in Rivers State
abstract: This study examined the effect of selected food crop outputs on poverty level of farm households in Rivers State. The primary data of the study were collected from a sample of 820 respondents based on the copies of questionnaires completed and returned. The data collected were analyzed using binary logit regression involving the odd ratios and marginal effects. The estimated binary logit results showed that yam production decreases the probability of poverty reduction by 0.028%. The results showed that an increase in cassava production increases the probability of poverty reduction by 0.034%.

title: Boreal Peatland 24-hour Solar-induced Chlorophyll Fluorescence Measurements under Continuous Daylight Conditions during the Summer Period
abstract: Continuous ground-based observations of solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) from northern peatlands remain uncommon, despite their potential to complement ecosystem carbon flux measurements and support satellite-based monitoring of vegetation activity. Here, we present continuous SIF estimates using data acquired with the Fluorescence Box (FloX) at two boreal peatland sites in northern Finland during the 2023 and 2025 growing seasons. title: Challenging the Terra Mamaizinha–Terra Longe dichotomy: Migration, Gender, and islandness in Nha Fala, Vitalina Varela, and Hanami
abstract: This article examines how contemporary films from and about Cape Verde articulate new poetics of islandness at the intersection of migration and gender. Focusing on Nha Fala (Flora Gomes, 2002), Vitalina Varela (Pedro Costa, 2019), and Hanami (Denise Fernandes, 2024), it combines perspectives from Island, Migration, and Gender Studies to analyse how islandness is shaped by mobility, absence, and return. By contrasting modes of return–performative, impossible and cyclical–the films challenge linear migration narratives such as the binary opposition between Terra Mamaizinha and Terra Longe. Givi

title: Regional economic impacts and emission responses under solar radiation modification
abstract: Abstract Solar Radiation Modification (SRM) has been proposed as a potential tool to limit increases in global or regional temperatures caused by anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions. While previous research has extensively examined the climate system's response to various SRM strategies, as well as their aggregate economic consequences, the spatial distribution of economic impacts has received less attention. title: Subspecific identity of channel-billed cuckoos (Scythrops novaehollandiae) vagrant to Aotearoa New Zealand
abstract: The channel-billed cuckoo Scythrops novaehollandiae is an occasional vagrant to Aotearoa New Zealand, with eight confirmed records. There are three described subspecies: the nominate form from Australia; S. n. fordi from Sulawesi; and S. n. schoddei from the Bismarck Archipelago. No previous studies have identified the subspecific identity of any channel-billed cuckoos in New Zealand. title: Hauntological ecologies and temporalities of post-socialism: Disco Elysium between Estonia and China
abstract: This paper examines the video game Disco Elysium (ZA/UM, 2019) as a pivotal cultural text for understanding the hauntological dimensions of post-socialist experience. The game’s transnational journey and profound reception from Estonia to China reveal a shared, yet differentially articulated, structure of feeling shaped by the aftermath of collapsed socialist projects and the ascendancy of neoliberal capitalism. title: Citizen Science and Environmental DNA Reveals Site of an Invasive Paropsisterna beata (Newman) (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae) Population in New Zealand
abstract: More than a decade after being declared eradicated, a population of the Australian blessed leaf beetle Paropsisterna beata (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae) was located in New Zealand in 2026. The pest has been found and photographed three times by citizen scientists approximately 25 km north of the original Wellington infestation and reported on iNaturalist. An environmental DNA (eDNA) match from a water sample then directed searching to Eucalyptus trees visible on Google Earth upstream. title: Economic, environmental and public health impacts of gas flaring in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria
abstract: Over the past six decades, billions of cubic feet of gases associated with crude oil exploration have been flared. Unfortunately, gas flaring has continued despite successive legislative interventions, with limited implementation of effective remediation strategies in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria. Gas flaring involves the combustion of associated gases produced during oil extraction, which contain particulate matter (soot), carbon dioxide, sulfur oxides (SOx), nitrogen oxides (NOx), and volatile organic compounds. title: HOUSEHOLD PRACTICES AND PERCEPTIONS OF BOREHOLE WATER IN LAMBANYI MUNICIPALITY GUINEA
abstract: Domestic boreholes are essential for self-supply in cities with inadequate public water services. This study examines household practices and perceptions of borehole water in Lambanyi, Conakry, Guinea. A descriptive cross-sectional survey covered 383 households in four neighbourhoods from 5 to 25 June 2024. Data collected through a Microsoft Forms questionnaire were processed in Microsoft Excel using descriptive statistics and thematic analysis of open-ended responses. title: The Philosophy of Sambulu in the Life of the Kaili People
abstract: This research article is motivated by the culture of the Kaili community regarding the existence of Sambulu as a traditional custom (adat) that embodies philosophical meanings and values in community life. The research questions are: (1) what is the status of the Sambulu tradition in Kaili culture? (2) what is the philosophical meaning of Sambulu in the life of the Kaili people? and (3) why is the application of Sambulu's philosophical values needed in Kaili community life? This article aims to describe the status of the Sambulu custom, explain its philosophical meaning, and analyze the philos
journal: Journal of Education and Teaching Learning

title: Regional and Temporal Dynamics of Dengue in Mexico (2020–2024): A Comprehensive Epidemiological Analysis
abstract: Dengue remains a major public health concern in Mexico, with incidence and clinical burden increasing substantially in recent years. Using national surveillance data from 2020 to 2024, this study provides a comprehensive overview of the changing epidemiological landscape, with an emphasis on geographic distribution, temporal trends, serotype dynamics, and disease severity. Over this period, Mexico saw an almost fivefold increase in dengue cases, reaching over 123,000 confirmed infections and 426 deaths in 2024, the highest annual number recorded. title: Geographic and host-associated morphometric variation in Gyrodactylus atratuli Putz and Hoffman, 1963 and Gyrodactylus mediotorus King, Marcogliese, Forest, Mclaughlin and Bentzen, 2013 (Monogenea: Gyrodactylidae) from leuciscid fishes, with first records from Mexico
abstract: Abstract The present study reports the first records of the viviparous monogeneans Gyrodactylus atratuli and Gyrodactylus mediotorus from leuciscid fishes in Mexico, providing new insights into intraspecific haptoral sclerite variability across hosts and geographic regions in North America. Nuclear rDNA (ITS region) genetic analyses confirmed species identities; Mexican G. atratuli sequences showed a 0.7% divergence from Canadian specimens, while Mexican G. mediotorus sequences exhibited a 0.2–0.8% divergence from other North American populations, including those from Texas and Canada. title: Hydrogel application as a soil amendment to mitigate water deficiency effects on flaxseed cultivars grown in sandy soils
abstract: Abstract Water scarcity is a major constraint for flax production in Egypt’s sandy soils. This research aims to investigate the use of hydrogels, as water-absorbing polymers can enhance soil moisture retention and improve crop performance under water deficit conditions, thereby increasing flax yield and seed quality. Two field experiments were conducted during the 2022/2023 and 2023/2024 winter seasons at the National Research Centre, Al Nubaria, Egypt, to evaluate the effects of hydrogel (0 and 80 kg/ha) on three flax cultivars (Giza-11, Giza-12, Sakha-3) under full water irrigation quantity

title: The taxonomic status of Eurypterus podolicus Chernyshev, 1947 (Arthropoda: Eurypterida), from the Silurian of Podillia, Ukraine
abstract: This article presents the results of an investigation into the complex history of the eurypterid species "Eurypterus podolicus Chernyshev, 1947", for which neither an original description nor a type series is known. The study confirms that this species is a nomen nudum, as it was never formally described. Moreover, the specimens of "Eurypterus podolicus" from the Borys Chernyshev's collection lack distinct morphological features that would justify recognizing it as a separate species.

title: Sacred Grove as a Community-Oriented Biodiversity Preservation: A Research in the Shekhawati Terrain of Thar Desert
abstract: Sacred Groves, commonly known as Orans or Devbanis in local vernacular, exemplify community-driven biodiversity preservation within the Shekhawati region of the Thar Desert. The community firmly prohibits hunting, logging, and farming in these village commons, which are governed by the residents and dedicated to local deities. Environmental and Biological Importance Sacred forests act as "mini biosphere reserves" and provide refuge for fauna in this arid region. In Shekhawati, the preservation of heritage is more deeply embedded in socioreligious traditions than in formal legislation. Communit

title: Floristic Diversity and Ethnomedicinal Importance of Vaatangi Sacred Grove, Rajavommangi Mandal, Alluri Sitaramaraju District, Andhra Pradesh, India
abstract: Sacred groves are patches of forest under community based protection, revered as the abode of local deities and maintained through indigenous cultural beliefs. The present study documents the floristic diversity and ethnomedicinal significance of the Vaatangi Sacred Grove located in Rajavommangi Mandal, Alluri Sitaramaraju District, Andhra Pradesh, India. The grove, presided over by Lord Shiva, encompasses one hectare of dry deciduous forest with a documented history exceeding 100 years. journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Beyond two alleles: multiallelic genotypic selection and its estimation from time-series data
abstract: Genetic diversity is central to evolutionary change, with both natural selection and random genetic drift depending on variation within a population. An individual in a diploid population carries two alleles per locus, yet the population as a whole can harbour many alleles, giving rise to a rich spectrum of homozygous and heterozygous genotypes. Such multiallelic variation is common at biologically and medically important loci such as the major histocompatibility complex, the ABO blood group system, and genes underlying monogenic diseases. title: Egyptian Blue Production and Lead Metallurgy in a Late Hellenistic Workshop on Kos (Greece): A Case of Multicrafting
abstract: Abstract A well-preserved late Hellenistic workshop in the agora of Kos provides a rare opportunity to examine pigment production embedded in a multicrafting setting. Excavations of a room in the eastern stoa have revealed fire-structures, Egyptian blue pellets, a range of mineral earth pigments, litharge rods, lead slag, tools and other production debris, demonstrating both pigment manufacture and lead metallurgy within a single workshop space. title: The geometry of gametic dispersal in a flying mammal, Rhinolophus hipposideros
abstract: Abstract Dispersal influences population and evolutionary dynamics, in a manner that depends on by which dispersal strategies gene flow occurs. In some species, mating partners move exclusively for mating, dispersing genes but not individuals. This is the case in many bat species, of which the lesser horseshoe bat ( Rhinolophus hipposideros ) shows a genetic structure at a fine spatial scale suggesting restricted dispersal. title: In What Ways Does Technology-enhanced Teacher Professional Development Change Learning Outcomes in Numeracy, in Marginalised Rural Schools in Bangladesh? A Coarsened Exact Matching Study
abstract: This paper addresses gaps in the international evidence base on the impacts of technology-enhanced Teacher Professional Development (TPD). In particular, it addresses the ways in which teachers’ participation in technology-enhanced TPD changes learning outcomes, in the contexts of marginalised rural schools. Examples of such evidence, arising from large scale studies and conducted by researchers from the global south, are rare. The paper also contributes to the small but growing evidence base on foundation numeracy skills in rural schools in Bangladesh, with a particular focus on marginalised

title: Efficient Propranolol Delivery Enabled by Manganese‐Based Bioactive Metal–Organic Frameworks With High Loading Capacity
abstract: A green and efficient method was developed for propranolol delivery utilizing manganese‐based bioactive metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) as biocompatible drug carriers. Mn‐based bioactive MOFs with a high aspect ratio were synthesized and characterized for size (average, 17 µm), morphology, stability, elemental composition, crystallinity, functionality, charge character, and biocompatibility (a protein adsorption capacity of 0.03 µg µg −1 (5 h) and a hemolysis ratio of < 0.5%). title: An agenda for plastics crisis research in the synthetic age
abstract: This survey synthesizes insights from environmental social sciences to recast the plastics crisis as a structural feature of growth-dependent economies instead of a problem solvable by consumer choice or incremental technologies. Rather than a within-field review of ecological economics, it maps adjacent literatures to specify what this field could study and how, clarifying researchable questions, suitable methods, and tractable indicators. title: TRANSFORMING THE IMAGE: REFUGEEHOOD, AESTHETICS AND THE POLITICS OF EQUALITY
abstract: At the centre of the image representing refugeehood are bodies forced to leave their homelands. Yet the political significance of refugee images cannot be inferred from visibility alone: visual representations may document suffering while also fixing refugeehood within recognizable figures of tragedy, victimhood, and helplessness. This article asks how different visual regimes configure the relation between the refugee, the image, and the spectator, and under what aesthetic conditions that relation may become a site of political subjectivation rather than the reproduction of victimhood. title: Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices in School Disaster Risk Reduction and Management of Elementary School Heads in Fourth Congressional District of Quezon: Basis for Development of School Safety Manual
abstract: This study assessed the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of elementary school heads in School Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (SDRRM) in the Fourth Congressional District of Quezon, Philippines, during School Year 2024–2025, as a basis for developing a School Safety Manual. Anchored on the Knowledge–Attitude–Practice Theory and Comprehensive School Safety Framework, the study employed a quantitative descriptive–correlational design involving 38 elementary school heads selected through cluster sampling. Data were collected using an expert-validated, researcher-developed questionnaire

title: Bodies in Motion: Images of Women in the Magazine Frou-Frou (Rio de Janeiro, 1923–1927)
abstract: In the 1920s, Rio de Janeiro emerged as a cosmopolitan capital marked by rapid urban development and profound social change. During this period, women experienced greater freedom of movement and expanded opportunities for participation in social life outside the home. At the same time, fashion underwent radical change: while Paris remained an important reference point, North American influences—circulating primarily through cinema—gained increasing prominence. title: Studies in the vascular flora of the Southeastern United States. XI.
abstract: Hexastylis viridistylis (Aristolochiaceae) is described as a novel species distinguished from other species in the genus by a unique combination of morphological characters including style and ovary color and dimensions, stamen morphology, calyx tube dimensions, and fruiting characteristics. The range, habitat, phenology, and potential affinities to other species in the group are discussed in detail. title: Developing Sustainable Tourism Through Ecotourism: Theoretical Foundations and Practical Directions for Uzbekistan
abstract: This article analyses, from both theoretical and practical perspectives, the role of ecotourism in shaping sustainable tourism. Drawing on a review of international literature, it examines the three pillars of ecotourism (nature conservation, local community well-being, and environmental education) and synthesises their interrelationships. It then identifies the potential of ecotourism in Uzbekistan, the problems currently constraining it, and the mechanisms through which it can be developed. title: Hybrid Energy System for Off-Grid Electrification of Koluama Communities, Bayelsa State, Nigeria
abstract: This study investigates the technical, economic and environmental feasibility of a hybrid solar photovoltaic (PV), wind, battery storage and diesel-generator system for supplying Koluama 1 and Koluama 2 communities in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, Nigeria. A bottom-up electricity load assessment was conducted using household appliance inventories and estimated electricity requirements for residential, educational, healthcare and commercial consumers. title: Environmentally Relevant Concentrations of Nanomaterials Drive Photochemical Production of Reactive Species and Pollutant Degradation in Surface Waters
abstract: Reactive intermediates in surface waters are widely attributed to dissolved organic matter (DOM). Natural, incidental, or engineered nanomaterials simultaneously occur at parts per billion and can function as photocatalysts, yet the photochemical role of nanomaterials at environmentally relevant concentrations remains overlooked in surface water photochemistry. Here, we quantify reactive intermediates from TiO2 nanomaterials (1–100 μg L−1) and DOM (1–5 mgC L−1) under 222, 265, and 365 nm. title: Equity in the Technology Sector for Pasifika Learners in Aotearoa New Zealand
abstract: Pasifika peoples remain significantly underrepresented in Aotearoa New Zealand’s technology sector; despite comprising 8.9% of the population they make up less than 3% of those in digital and IT pathways. This disparity reflects structural inequities that constrain access, progression and representation, with clear impacts on workforce participation, education and economic outcomes. Using Pacific research methodologies, this qualitative study evaluates the effectiveness of micro-credentials and Pasifika-led IT programmes in addressing these inequities. title: Entangled Naturalisms: : Drawing nature beyond media.
abstract: This paper presents practice-based and theoretical contributions exploring how field drawing, site-specific practice, environmental humanities, walking and durational practices, and embodied experience can extend architectural drawing methodologies beyond medium-specificity and dualistic culture. Drawing as a situated and embodied practice — entangled with analogue, digital, and hybrid media, on-site, in motion, with collected data, images, traces, memories, and matter — can shift practice toward drawing from within an environment in intra-action, with all actors active in the drawing process.
journal: BBDS - Black Book: Drawing and Sketching

title: Monsters of finance
abstract: Abstract An anthropology of horror can serve as a vernacular critique of financial speculation. Drawing on fieldwork in San Pedro, Paraguay, I track horror across three registers: pombero tricksters; plata yvyguy (buried money) as a founding myth of postwar finance; and obligations binding sesame farmers to monsters, patrones , and creditors. Horror—a critical ontology and distinctive wonder—arises when obligation becomes undecidable: when one cannot tell whether the forces manipulating time and the future are persons who stand in relation, or how far the liability extends. title: Shifting Alignments in India’s Southeast Asia Policies
abstract: Drawing on historical and contemporary sources, this research argued that India’s policies toward Southeast Asia have been shaped by the interplay of three primary drivers: security maximization, economic maximization, and power maximization. The dominance of one driver or a combination of drivers varies across temporal phases, producing shifting alignments in India’s policy orientation and its regional engagement with Southeast Asia. This research applied neo-classical realism to examine the evolution of India’s foreign policy towards Southeast Asia from the Cold War through the post-Cold War

title: Voluntary Migration and Internal Displacement: A Study of Unhomeliness in Thrity Umrigar’s The Museum of Failures
abstract: Migration in today’s world is the most debatable topic that involves the movement of people from one place to another both individually or collectively. The traditional notions of voluntary migration often highlight the movement undertaken by an individual as a search for a better lifestyle, a better job offer, or for educational purposes. This study attempts to break this traditional notion of voluntary migration by stating that movement is also triggered by pain. title: Readers of the Living: Interpretive Mastery and Natural Thinking in Plutarch, Celsus, Origen, and Porphyry
abstract: Abstract This article examines the intersection between imperial writings on animals and post-Hellenistic debates about exegesis. It is the first study to argue that interpreters drawing on Aristotelian theories of voice and Hellenistic ideas of natural sympathy treated the meaningful but non-verbal animal as a test case of nature’s availability to reading, and as an opportunity to reflect on how exegetes transfer their skills between literature and the natural world. title: Niallia Circulans mediated Bio-fabrication of ZnO nanoparticles: Synthesis, characterization, and multifunctional applications
abstract: The current study addresses increasing global problems (agricultural sustainability, environmental contamination, and antimicrobial resistance) by means of sustainable and multifunctional biosynthesized Zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs). The study utilized a cell-free supernatant of a novel endophytic bacterial strain (Niallia Circulans) to synthesize ZnO NPs. title: Integrating the Diverse Values of Nature Into Environmental Law and Policy: Insights From Scottish Peatland Restoration
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper aims to arrive at a better understanding of the integration of the diverse values of nature (instrumental, intrinsic, relational) into (environmental) law and policy, using peatland restoration in Scotland as a case study. It argues that adopting a pluri‐value approach is a useful tool for both the design and implementation of environmental law and policy. title: Steel robots and space turtleships: the divergence of Korean animation and Japanese anime
abstract: During the Park Chung-hee military dictatorship, Korea shadowed Japanese industrial upgrading at every stage. The same was true in animation, in which Korea took Japanese animations, indigenized them, and imbued them with a techno-nationalism that positioned Korean animation as both dependent on Japan and destined to overcome it. Instead, the opposite happened: today South Korean animation is a pale shadow of Japanese anime’s global success. title: A case for empire: Why the United States intervened in Venezuela in 2026?
abstract: This research article analyzes the U.S. military operation “Absolute Resolve” on Janu- ary 3, 2026, which resulted in the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife by Delta Force units supported by air and naval assets. Employing a qualitative interpretive case- study design, the study examines the event through five analytical levels: civilizational, geopoliti- cal, international relations, political philosophy, and military. The findings show that the inter- vention reflects persistent imperial logic, thalassocratic geopolitical imperatives, a shift toward offensive realism
journal: Military Studies Journal for Strategy Technology and Defense Sciences

title: Temporal shifts in insect cuticular hydrocarbons in response to experimental desiccation
abstract: Insects are vulnerable to desiccation as they are small and have a high surface area-to-volume ratios. Over 80% of their body water is lost through the cuticle, but insects possess specialised cells that synthesize cuticular hydrocarbons (CHCs) to form a hydrophobic waxy barrier that reduces water loss. However, how rapidly CHCs are synthesized and transported across the cuticle under desiccating conditions remains poorly understood. title: An Innovative Approach for Estimating Coseismic Surface Uplifts Using Ionospheric Observations From Remote GNSS Stations: First Application for the 2025 Myanmar Earthquake
abstract: Abstract The M w 7.7 Myanmar earthquake on 28 March 2025 ruptured ∼480 km of the Sagaing Fault. Its fault slip distribution remains poorly constrained by three‐dimensional surface displacement data due to sparse GNSS‐coverage near the fault. Satellite‐based synthetic aperture radars capture meters of right‐lateral displacements but isolating vertical crustal movements from these measurements is challenging. institutions: Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research

title: Travel history and occupation among diagnosed Cutaneous Leishmaniasis cases in Guyana: A multi-site retrospective case series, 2017–2021
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (CL) in Guyana has not been systematically characterised in the peer-reviewed literature for several decades. This study aimed to describe the demographic, occupational, geographic, and clinical profile of diagnosed CL cases at Guyana's principal diagnostic sites, and to test, within this case series, whether field-based occupation is associated with reported interior travel and whether travel history is associated with time to presentation. METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: Retrospective case series (chart review) of CL diagnoses recorded at three facilities

title: Multi-criteria assessment of bio-based construction on circularity, environmental impact and feasibility
abstract: Over the past decade, the construction industry has increasingly prioritized climate neutrality. In line with this, the EU Green Deal and its ‘Fit-for-55’ legislative package aim to reduce total emissions by 55% by 2030. A major challenge in achieving this goal is addressing the embodied carbon of building materials, which arises from production, transportation, and end-of-life stages. Reaching such targets requires a fundamental shift from the current linear construction model toward a circular and low-carbon approach. journal: GRID - Architecture Planning and Design Journal

title: From “common sense” to “good sense” climate adaptation: extreme heat in the austere city
abstract: This paper challenges the assumption that ‘common sense’ provides an adequate framework for understanding how people respond to climate change. Appeals to ‘common sense’ naturalize individual responsibility, obscuring the structural conditions that shape adaptive capacity, and we propose ‘good sense’ as a more accurate account of how people actually reason about and adapt to climate change. The paper draws on ethnographic fieldwork to examine everyday responses to extreme heat in a low-income neighbourhood in Manchester, UK. title: Evaluation of the Plant Growth-Promoting Potential of Bacillus subtilis Isolated from the Rhizosphere of Berberis aristata for Improving Drought Stress Tolerance in Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum)
abstract: The rhizosphere is a very favourable environment for the presence of a wide range of microorganisms, which allow many beneficial interactions between the plants and microorganisms. Bacillus species are known as plant growth promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) to improve the growth and productivity of plants, among these microbes. abstract: The processing of cassava for human consumption leads to the generation of large quantities of cassava peel waste. The continuous accumulation of these peels has contributed to environmental pollution, thereby placing significant pressure on waste management systems. This study aimed to assess the biodegradation potentials of Aspergillus niger and Bacillus subtilis, individually and in combination, using cassava peels as the substrate. title: Ungrievable lives: State and non-state authoritarianism in the making of Uyghur foreign fighters
abstract: While there is a broad literature on the policies of authoritarian regimes toward their populations abroad, we know far less about the inclusionary and exclusionary policies of authoritarian host states toward displaced populations residing within their own territories. This article examines how Uyghur refugees who fled China and arrived in Turkey via third countries between 2014 and 2016 were channelled into conflict zones in Syria through the interaction of state institutions, diaspora organisations, and armed non-state actors. title: Oportunidades y Barreras de la Economía Social, Popular y Solidaria frente al Desarrollo Sostenible en América Latina: Una Revisión Exploratoria
abstract: Introducción: La Economía Social, Popular y Solidaria (ESPS) abarca una serie de prácticas colectivas que parecen contribuir al Desarrollo Sostenible (DS) pero cuya evidencia se encuentra dispersa en América Latina. title: Traditional preservation practices of asala fish (Schizothorax spp.) among Himalayan communities of Darjeeling, India
abstract: Abstract Traditional fish preservation practices are an important part of the cultural heritage and food systems of the Darjeeling Himalayas. In this study, the traditional methods used by local communities to preserve asala fish ( Schizothorax spp.) have been documented. Data were collected from the 50 respondents over the age of 18 including fish farmers, hatchery operators, fish processors, traders, and household members engaged in fish production, preservation, and marketing. title: Depresión psicótica: una revisión sistemática de su clínica, diagnóstico y tratamiento
abstract: Psychotic depression (PD) is a severe manifestation of major depressive disorder characterized by the presence of psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations and delusions, alongside the typical signs and symptoms of depression. This condition poses significant challenges in both diagnosis and treatment due to the complexity of its clinical presentation. abstract: Abstract Montane and cloud forests are high-elevation ecosystems dependent on specific environmental conditions and increasingly threatened by fragmentation, isolation, and climate change in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest. We quantified changes in climatic suitability for two characteristic tree species of these ecosystems, Drimys angustifolia and Ilex microdonta , under future climate scenarios, assessing range contraction and expansion, potential losses of suitable areas, and opportunities for ecological restoration.
