title: Tablewares and Ten-Footers: The Materiality of Irish Immigrant Life in Nineteenth-Century Lowell, Massachusetts
abstract: Abstract The Irish immigrant experience in 19th-century North America is often framed in terms of processes of oppression and racialization. However, archaeological and documentary evidence from the industrial city of Lowell, Massachusetts, complicates this narrative, because Lowell’s Irish population transcended the initial trauma of immigration and the challenge of anti-Irish prejudice by leveraging the powers of the Catholic Church and of community-building mechanisms, such as residential clustering and voluntary associations, to become a major political force in the city. abstract: Most cobitid loaches (Cypriniformes: Cobitidae) exhibit pronounced sexual dimorphism associated with mating behaviour. abstract: There has been no dearth of interest in the politics of IPTA in Indian intellectual circles. title: Cadmium and lead: genotoxic effects on the broodstock of the fish Prochilodus magdalenae (Characiformes: Prochilodontidae)
abstract: Introduction: Heavy metals such as cadmium (Cd) and lead (Pb) pose a significant threat to aquatic ecosystems due to their persistence, capacity for bioaccumulation, and genotoxic potential. These contaminants are of particular concern in tropical freshwater systems, where they may impact native species of ecological, economic, and nutritional importance, such as Prochilodus magdalenae, a migratory fish endemic to the Magdalena–Cauca River basin in Colombia. abstract: We present an update to the 2023 U.S. 50‐state National Seismic Hazard Model, based on questions and comments received from a range of users, as well as additional internal and building code reviews since its initial release. title: Risk and Cost Assessment of Suez Canal Transit Compared with Alternative Multimodal Corridors for Container Shipping between Abu Dhabi and Constanța
abstract: This paper quantifies the operational risk and the transport cost of a 10,000 TEU shipment between Abu Dhabi and Constanța South and compares the Suez Canal route with the Cape of Good Hope detour and with two multimodal corridors through Iran. title: Climate at the Apex: The Emerging Role of Apex Courts in Global Climate Governance
abstract: Abstract This article offers the first global mapping and comparative analysis of climate litigation reaching domestic apex courts. Drawing on a novel dataset, it identifies more than 360 cases decided between 1995 and 2024, with a sharp rise since 2015. Apex courts are defined as the highest domestic judicial bodies with final jurisdiction over climate-relevant matters. title: Habitat Use, Resource Acquisition, and Risk Management of Raccoons in Human-Modified Landscapes across North America
abstract: Urbanization creates concentrated food sources, artificial habitats and fragmented living environments for adaptable medium-sized carnivores. However, ecological studies of raccoons mostly carry out separately on habitat utilization and so on, which hinders the understanding of their continued existence in human-altered landscapes. abstract: Abstract Background Liver fibrosis is a progressive pathological disease characterised by excessive deposition of extracellular matrix and damage to hepatocellular architecture. Despite increasing therapeutic requirements, existing antifibrotic therapies are limited. Amaranthus spinosus , an ethnomedicinal plant used by many tribal groups in India, exhibits antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties; however, its antifibrotic effectiveness remains unknown. abstract: This article examines mosque tourism as a spatial and cultural mechanism shaping urban cultural identity in Malaysian cities. Focusing on Kuala Terengganu, Melaka, George Town, and Putrajaya, it investigates how mosques function beyond religious institutions to contribute to urban placemaking, heritage representation, and tourism development. abstract: Purpose: This study analyses how Nahdlatul Ulama’s (NU) cultural da’wah strategy and the role of religious leaders build religious harmony in Jepara Regency, Central Java, a post-conflict area that experienced religiously charged unrest in 1998 and a church-construction dispute lasting nearly two decades. title: Patients’ and Health Care Workers’ Perspectives on Barriers to Hypertension Care in a Pastoralist Setting
abstract: Hypertension affects about one in four Kenyan adults, yet only 15.5% of those affected are aware of their status. No measured prevalence estimate exists for Mandera County, where pastoral mobility, 77% absolute poverty and sparse health services are likely to compound underdetection, while evidence from transitioning pastoralist populations shows that their historically low cardiovascular risk is rising. abstract: Abstract Positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) services from low Earth orbit (LEO) present an important alternative or complement to established global satellite navigation systems (GNSSs). title: Hepatitis aguda de origen desconocido: Revisión narrativa sobre el potencial rol del Adenovirus F41
abstract: La hepatitis de origen desconocido (HOD), reportada en más de 1,000 casos en 35 países hasta julio de 2022, representa un desafío en salud pública, especialmente en niños, con una posible asociación al adenovirus humano (HAdV), subtipo F41, aunque su papel etiológico sigue siendo debatido. abstract: This study examines the Sufi teachings of Sheikh Yusuf Al-Makassary as a form of resistive literature, namely a spiritual discourse that functions as a resistance against physical colonization, cultural domination, and epistemic oppression during the colonial period. abstract: The main challenges of every Filipino migrant are sociocultural adaptation and psychological distress when living abroad. With this, strong emotional quotient is needed to survive. This study investigated the moderating role of emotional quotient on the relationship between sociocultural adaptation and psychological distress among Filipino migrants. abstract: South Africa’s deepening electricity crisis, marked by persistent load-shedding and escalating tariffs, has accelerated private solar photovoltaic (PV) installations. This rapid transition has raised concerns about municipal revenue erosion, cross-subsidisation and energy inequality. The City of Johannesburg Metropolitan Municipality (CoJ) is at the centre of this transition, and is grappling with the implications for its business model and how private solar PV can be leveraged to support a just energy transition. abstract: Organisms that make up the soil fauna are involved in several activities related to the functioning of the soil ecosystem. They present high diversity and are distributed throughout the world, in different conditions, and can be used as bioindicators of soil quality among different management conditions. There are few studies carried out on soil fauna in South America, mainly involving mountainous regions, which are suffering strong anthropogenic impacts. abstract: Cileungsi River water is susceptible to biological contaminants in the form of bacteria from industrial and domestic waste, one of which is coliform bacteria. abstract: Brettanomyces bruxellensis is a major wine spoilage yeast responsible for the production of volatile phenols, including 4-ethylphenol (EP) and 4-ethylguaiacol (EG), from grape-derived hydroxycinnamic acids. abstract: Abstract Subcortical vascular cognitive impairment (SVCI) is a risk factor for dementia. White matter hyperintensity (WMH) lesions are considered a hallmark of SVCI. title: From Foraging to Dairy Pastoralism: Indigenous Transformation Among Sami in Early Modern Northern Fennoscandia
abstract: Aboriginal societies worldwide have independently transformed their modes of production. In northern Eurasia, this included a shift from transport-oriented reindeer herding toward a pastoral economy between the sixteenth and nineteenth centuries. This article examines whether this transition among the Indigenous Sami of northern Fennoscandia was accompanied by intensified milking and a more elaborate dairy culture. abstract: Objective: Acinetobacter lwoffii is an environmental organism and skin commensal with low intrinsic virulence. abstract: Abstract Climate change increasingly generates conditions of persistent governance turbulence, placing growing demands on local authorities as frontline risk managers while simultaneously exposing them to new forms of vulnerability. title: Considering Culinary Use of Lavender: Sensory and Cultural Factors
abstract: Lavender is a Mediterranean herb that is used relatively infrequently in the kitchen compared to other Mediterranean herbs, despite growing interest in its culinary applications. The question to be addressed in this narrative historical review is why that should be so. Several alternative hypotheses (historical, chemical, perceptual, psychological, physiological, and antimicrobial) are outlined and critically evaluated. title: Secretome-dependent antimicrobial and immunomodulatory activity of Lactobacillus johnsonii against multidrug-resistant Enteroaggregative Escherichia coli
abstract: Abstract Background: Enteroaggregative Escherichia coli (EAEC) is a leading cause of persistent diarrhea in children in low- and middle-income countries, and the emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains necessitates non-antibiotic therapeutic strategies. This study evaluated Lactobacillus johnsonii , previously characterized by our group, as a probiotic candidate against a clinically confirmed MDR EAEC isolate resistant to ampicillin, ciprofloxacin, azithromycin, amoxicillin, and gentamicin. title: Olivine-hosted melt inclusions provide insights into primitive magma compositions driving young eruptions from Red Crater, Tongariro (New Zealand)
abstract: Abstract Volcanism at continental arcs is ultimately driven by mantle-derived magmas; however, erupted compositions are typically overprinted by crustal interactions during ascent, obscuring deeper signatures. We target olivine and their melt inclusions (MI) in basaltic andesite scoria erupted from Red Crater (Tongariro, New Zealand) to capture primitive melt compositions prior to upper crustal processing. title: Active and passive reference panels for the validation of solar-induced fluorescence
abstract: With the preparation of the FLEX satellite mission and other platforms providing quantitative measurements of solar-induced fluorescence (SIF), the calibration and validation (Cal/Val) of SIF products is becoming increasingly relevant. Owing to the dynamic nature of SIF, cross-validation requires synchronous data acquisition when performed on vegetated targets. This study investigates two new concepts for artificial SIF reference targets—active and passive—tested for airborne and proximal validation and designed for potential satellite applications. institutions: European Space Research and Technology Centre

title: Microbial Primer: Mirror bacteria
abstract: Mirror bacteria are hypothetical synthetic organisms built from molecules of opposite chirality to those used throughout nature. This primer discusses their potential dangers: because of their chiral mismatch to the natural environment, mirror bacteria could plausibly evade predation, immunity and other ecological control mechanisms to a degree never seen before. This property could simultaneously make them unprecedented invasive species and dangerous pathogens.

title: Asymptotic behavior of lidar scattering properties of absorbing dust aerosols across Rayleigh and geometrical-optics regimes: theory and implications
abstract: Lidar ratio (S), linear depolarization ratio (δ), and single-scattering albedo (ω) are central quantities for dust typing and property retrieval in lidar remote sensing. We investigate their dependence on size parameter (x) and iron oxide fraction of mineral dust using TAMUdust2020 and triaxial-ellipsoid calculations. Results show a consistent asymptotic structure that is weakly sensitive to particle shape in both limits of scattering theory. abstract: Abstract Interest in the topic of geodetic co-location in space and space ties has recently intensified within the geodetic community, particularly following the approval of the European Space Agency’s Genesis mission. From the perspective of very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), observations of Earth-orbiting satellites are not standard practice yet. To enable VLBI support for future co-location satellite missions, such observations must be integrated into the VLBI processing chain. title: Bodies in tension: embodied persistence and change in meat-eating
abstract: This article examines how embodied knowledge contributes to both the reproduction and possible reorientation of meat consumption. Drawing on household interviews and a dietary experiment with consumers in Norway, we analyze three interconnected dimensions of embodied meat-eating: shared cultural understandings of meat as healthy and nutritious; habituated routines of shopping, cooking, and eating; and interpreted bodily experiences of taste, satiety, craving, and discomfort. title: La Orden del Hospital y las minorías en el Oriente latino en los siglos XII-XIII
abstract: Las órdenes militares en el Oriente latino ejercieron un control sobre una población diversa que comprendía tanto a cristianos orientales de diferentes denominaciones como a musulmanes, judíos y francos. abstract: The study investigated the influence of capital market on infrastructure development in Nigeria, which utilized a quasi-experimental research design and time series yearly data from 1981 to 2025. Autoregressive distributed lag model (ARDL) was employed and the data of gross capital formation was proxy for infrastructure development, while instrument of capital market such as all share indexes, government stocks equity and corporate bond are utilized as independent variable in the study in order to determine the influence of capital market on infrastructure development in the country. title: Electromagnetic Compatibility Testing of Military Ships
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) testing of military ships is an essential process for ensuring the correct and safe operation of electrical and electronic systems under complex operational conditions. This paper presents a methodology for assessing electromagnetic compatibility at the ship level, considering the vessel as an integrated system. The objectives include determining overall electromagnetic susceptibility, optimizing operations by reducing interference, and verifying the self-compatibility of installed equipment. abstract: Autobiografía del algodón (2020) de Cristina Rivera Garza articula una escritura que entrelaza investigación archivística, memoria familiar y trabajo literario para reconstruir la historia del auge algodonero en el noreste mexicano, una huelga campesina borrada de los registros oficiales y la genealogía de una familia fronteriza. Este artículo propone leer la novela a partir del concepto de relato de filiación de Dominique Viart, no sólo como una búsqueda de ascendencia familiar o literaria, sino como una operación situada que vincula archivo, territorio y genealogía en el espacio del noreste

title: Factors Affecting Tax Revenues in Five ASEAN Countries from 2014 to 2024
abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the impact of economic factors such as growth, inflation, and tourism flows on tax revenues in five ASEAN countries. The study was conducted from 2014 to 2024 and used secondary data on variables such as economic growth, inflation, number of tourists, and tax revenues. abstract: Abstract The low-velocity impact response of hybrid glass/carbon filament-wound composite pipes with a nominal outside diameter of 24 mm was investigated experimentally, analytically and numerically. title: Questões ambientais
abstract: The article aims to analyze the moderating effect of re-election on the relationship between environmental spending behavior and forward-looking policies (health, education, safety, infrastructure) in Brazilian municipalities, filling a gap by examining how the quest to remain in power influences the manipulation of spending to improve the image of managers, with implications for expenditure selection. Both venoms trigger human platelet activation and aggregation sensitive to snake venom metalloproteases (SVMPs) inhibitors, potentially through protease-activated receptor 1 (PAR-1) activation; however, B. erythromelas exhibits significantly higher potency. title: Una nueva población del taxón vulnerable Centaurea seridis L. revela procesos de hibridación con Centaurea aspera L. en Cataluña
abstract: Este trabajo documenta la presencia de Centaurea seridis en Montjuïc, que representa la única población confirmada de la especie conocida actualmente en la provincia de Barcelona. La población fue detectada por primera vez en los alrededores del Museu Nacional d’Art de Catalunya (MNAC) durante el VI Biomaratón de Flora Española, un evento destinado a promover el registro fotográfico de plantas silvestres mediante iNaturalist. title: Metals as energy carriers: Unlocking a hydrogen economy through established logistics
abstract: A future energy system centred on renewables and hydrogen requires reliable, high-density storage and cost-effective transport at scale. Metals (and metal oxides) offer a compelling pathway for a fast integration of hydrogen into a sector coupled energy system: circular energy carriers that provide safe and dispatchable energy. This review discusses the role of hydrogen in metal reduction processes for renewable energy storage, with subsequent metal oxidation delivering heat and hydrogen for industry and grids. title: Dynamics of abundance for chum salmon of Russian origin
abstract: Periods of high and low abundance are revealed in dynamics of the Russian chum salmon population in 1907–2025. The period of high abundance with recorded annual catches from 58,000 to 185,000 tons lasted from the mid-1920s to the mid-1960s, followed by the low abundance one with the catches from 21,000 to 70,000 tons lasting until the mid-2000s. Currently, the stocks are at a high level again.
institutions: All-Russian Research Institute Fisheries and Oceanography

title: Petal infrared transmission warms flowers and reduces microbial abundance
abstract: Flowers create distinct internal microclimates, yet how these conditions filter microbial abundance remains poorly understood. We tested whether petal light transmission and internal floral temperature influence microbial abundance in two co-occurring species, Lyonia lucida and Lyonia fruticosa (Ericaceae), which have translucent petal 'windows' that modify internal light environments. We measured internal and external floral temperatures, quantified culturable microbial abundance (yeasts, molds, bacteria), and assessed ultraviolet (UV) and infrared (IR) petal transmission using spectrometry.

These strategies are now the area of concern of coal mining entrepreneurs responsible for saline discharges into environment, which should be significantly reduced or eliminated to meet legal requirements. abstract: La obesidad sarcopénica es un síndrome geriátrico caracterizado por la coexistencia de exceso de tejido adiposo y disminución de la masa y función muscular. abstract: The present study aimed to develop a Ciclopirox olamine-loaded calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) vaterite nanoparticle hydrogel as an enhanced topical antifungal delivery system. abstract: Contamination of surface waters by potentially toxic metals represents an important environmental concern due to their persistence, bioaccumulation, and potential effects on aquatic ecosystems and human health. This study aimed to analyze scientific evidence on the occurrence of these elements in Brazilian surface waters, considering the main metals detected, their sources, temporal distribution, quality standards, environmental risks, and monitoring gaps. abstract: Acid affected soils have been expanding in the Ethiopian highlands, and caused serious yield decline. Organic amendments and lime have been used to manage soil acidity. This study aimed at investigating the effects of four manure rates (0, 4, 8, and 12 t ha-1), with three lime rates (0, 1.5 and 3 t ha-1 CaCO3) on maize yield, and selected soil chemical properties. abstract: The paper focuses on the prehistoric rock art as a symbolic communication method, by conducting a comparative study of the Lascaux cave paintings in France and the Bhimbetka rock shelters in India. title: Arabic Journalism in India: Historical Development and Contemporary Trends
abstract: Arabic journalism in India occupies a distinctive position in the history of Indian journalism and Indo-Arab intellectual relations. Although Arabic is not a major vernacular language of India, it has enjoyed a long and distinguished history as a language of religion, scholarship, education, literature, and international communication. abstract: This study examines the role of the Besoekisch Proefstation as a colonial agricultural research centre that supported the plantation industry in the Besuki Residency in the early 20th century. title: A debate for inclusive community development: Uncovering marginalized perspectives
abstract: The paper draws on participatory development, social justice, and decolonization frameworks, emphasizing inclusive development as a tool to address historical and ongoing exclusions. title: Canalised Urban Waterways, Palimpsest Landscapes and Climate Adaptation: Comparison of Ecomorphological Trajectories from Isparta and Chelmsford
abstract: This paper examines canalised urban waterways as active ecomorphological agents in the Anthropocene city through a comparative study of Isparta, Türkiye, and Chelmsford, United Kingdom. Focusing on Isparta’s Çayboyu canal and associated stream system, and Chelmsford’s canalised corridor shaped by the Rivers Chelmer and Can, the paper investigates how urban waterways form and modify relationships between urban morphology, spatial memory and public space. title: Biophilic Architecture for Psychological Recovery and Biodiversity Conservation in Nigerian Rehabilitation Environments: Advancing Sustainable Development Goal 15
abstract: Biophilic architecture has gained increasing attention as an evidence-based approach in enhancing human well-being through the intentional integration of natural elements into the built environment. In Nigerian rehabilitation settings, where psychological recovery is a primary objective amid rapid urbanization and mental health challenges, the role of biophilic design extends beyond therapeutic outcomes to include environmental stewardship. title: Effects of Fecal Subsampling on Dietary DNA Metabarcoding in Wild Boars (Sus scrofa)
abstract: Using DNA metabarcoding, we examined dietary components of the wild boar (Sus scrofa) and tested a common but rarely examined assumption that a small fecal subsample represents the dietary signal of an entire fecal mass. We analyzed multiple subsamples taken from the same fecal mass as well as already separated fecal pieces collected on Shodoshima Island, Japan, in May, July, and September, using chloroplast trnL and mitochondrial COI markers to infer plant and animal dietary taxa, respectively. title: Mutant Bacteria in Bioremediation: Harnessing Modified Microbes for Cleanup of Environmental Pollutants
abstract: Environmental pollution threatens global ecosystems and public health, while driving global climate change. Although bioremediation is a sustainable and cost-effective alternative to traditional chemical treatments, natural bacteria are often limited by slow degradation rates and an inability to break down highly resilient materials. To overcome these limits, genetic engineering and targeted mutation are used to improve bacterial metabolism and increase the production of key degrading enzymes. This review examines recent progress in genetically altering established pollutant-degrading bacteria

title: Doble suicidio (1969) de Masahiro Shinoda: una enunciación sobre la historia y las formas del cine en Japón
abstract: This article analyzes the film Double Suicide (1969), directed by Masahiro Shinoda, as an aesthetic and critical proposal that repositions cinema within a continuum of visuality in Japan. Based on a dialogue between historical-cultural analysis and film analysis, the study is organized into two sections: “The Edo Period: Its History and Culture as the Foundation of Symbolism in Double Suicide” and “Performing and Visual Arts in Double Suicide: Resource and Memory.” The first section examines how the historical-cultural references of the Edo period—including ukiyo-e and calligraphy—shape the fi

title: As geoestratégias formativas de Grandes Potências Regionais e o caso brasileiro recente (2003-2022)
abstract: The objective of this study is to contribute to the understanding of Brazilian geostrategy focused on extra-regional deterrence as it was shaped in the twenty-first century. To this end, the paper first defines some fundamental concepts of Geostrategy and Great Power status, following a Structural Realist approach. It then identifies key elements shared by the two successful trajectories of Regional Great Power formation in the last multipolar conjuncture of the interstate system, between 1815 and 1945. title: THE CASBAH OF ALGIERS: A LIVING URBAN LANDSCAPE OF CULTURAL MEMORY, RESILIENCE, AND HERITAGE CONSERVATION
abstract: This study examines the Casbah of Algiers as a living urban landscape, emphasizing its historical, architectural, and cultural significance in the Mediterranean context. Rather than treating the Casbah solely as a preserved monument, the research conceptualizes it as a dynamic, resilient cultural system shaped by successive Amazigh, Arab-Islamic, Andalusian, Ottoman, and European influences. title: Содержание полихлорированных бифенилов в мышечной ткани налима (Lota lota) и щуки (Esox lucius) из реки Пясина
abstract: Несмотря на глобальный запрет полихлорированных бифенилов (ПХБ) в рамках Стокгольмской конвенции 2001 года, эти стойкие органические загрязнители продолжают выявляться в арктических экосистемах, удалённых от территорий их потенциального использования в прошлом. title: Institutional Transformation and Electoral Pragmatism in Indonesian Islamic Organisations
abstract: This article examines how Nahdlatul Wathan (NW), a pesantren-based Islamic organisation in West Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, has transformed from a religious educational institution into an electoral actor since 2004. It asks how this reflects tensions between religious authority and electoral pragmatism in post-1998 Indonesia, and what conditions enable or constrain pesantren-based organisations to maintain religious legitimacy while competing electorally. title: We Have Always Been Here: Xinka Resistance in the Face of Extractivist Projects
abstract: On October 22, 2017, a peaceful Xinka community protest against the Escobal extractivist mining project was met with brutal repression by the Guatemalan state, revealing enduring patterns of colonial governance and Indigenous dispossession. This article examines Indigenous Xinka resistance to extractivist megaprojects in the southeastern region of Guatemala as an expression of cosmological continuance, rather than merely a reaction to external violence. title: The economic and environmental potential of sustainable food packaging: an empirical study using modified starch films with wasabi extract
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of starch-based biopolymers as innovative and sustainable food packaging materials, enabling the achievement of economic and environmental benefits. An empirical study was conducted to assess the effects of incorporating wasabi powder and paste into starch matrices, with the goal of improving antimicrobial properties and functional performance. The findings demonstrate the feasibility of these biopolymers as eco-friendly alternatives to conventional plastics, contributing to waste reduction and promoting circular economy models within the food industry. title: JWST MIRI Reveals a Potential Atmosphere on the Ultrahot Rocky Planet TOI-431b
abstract: Abstract An open question in exoplanet science is whether rocky exoplanets extremely close in to their host stars, “lava worlds,” can retain significant atmospheres. Thermal emission observations via secondary eclipse can be used to determine whether a rocky exoplanet possesses an atmosphere. It is expected that an atmosphere could increase the planet’s albedo and/or redistribute heat away from the dayside, reducing the secondary eclipse depth measured. abstract: Cyanobacteria are recognized as promising sources of diverse metabolites with potential applications in pharmaceutical, nutraceutical and biotechnological fields. The present study investigated the bioactive compound profile of an axenically cultured isolate Microcystis aeruginosa through solvent extraction, quantitative estimation and gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC-MS) analysis. abstract: The name of Arsinoe II, or Philadelphus , occurs very often in documents related to Ptolemaic imperial agendas throughout the Mediterranean. title: Assessing Environmental Behaviour Among Residents in Chosen Barangays of Concepcion, Tarlac: Towards an Integrated Ecological Management Plan
abstract: The study aimed to develop an integrated ecological management action plan by analyzing the environmental behavior of residents in selected barangays of Concepcion, Tarlac. Using a quantitative survey approach, it examined attitudes, practices, and perceptions related to waste management, energy use, water conservation, and other green practices. title: Silenced Flesh, Sanctioned Hunger: The Predicament of Women in Prostitution in Jayanta Mahapatra’s Calcutta Poems
abstract: Between the lyric hush of the imagist poem and the clamour of a society that trades in hunger, Jayanta Mahapatra’s “Hunger” and “The Whorehouse in a Calcutta Street” stage some of the most disquieting encounters in Indian poetry in English. This paper investigates how the two poems render women ensnared in the sex trade, and whether their austere, image-driven art exposes the economic and patriarchal machinery of exploitation or quietly reproduces the silence it seeks to indict. title: Des musiques populaires enregistrées sur le terrain. Notes sur la prise directe et l’enregistrement de terrain dans la captation des voix populaires au début du xx e siècle
abstract: Cet article étudie les prémices de l’enregistrement de terrain dans le champ des musiques folk traditionnelles à la faveur de la mise en circulation des premiers phonographes (dès la fin du xix e siècle). Revenant sur les premières pratiques de captation permises par l’enregistrement sonore, puis suivant les collectes « équipées » de Bela Bartók en Europe, de Frances Densmore et de John et Alan Lomax aux États-Unis, l’analyse aboutit à discerner un « delta » entre documentation ethnographique des pratiques musicales folkloriques et création musicale.

abstract: Water source nodes within water network are subject to dual pressures: the propagation of failure risks and reverse feedback from fluctuations in user demand. As the connectivity of water network and the relationship between water supply and consumption become increasingly complex, there is an urgent need to elucidate the patterns of bidirectional risk transmission in complex water network and to effectively manage water source nodes. abstract: La investigación básica constituye un componente fundamental de los sistemas científicos; sin embargo, los modelos de financiamiento y evaluación orientados hacia resultados de corto plazo pueden desfavorecer actividades cuyos beneficios son inciertos, acumulativos y diferidos. title: HOW WILL CHINA’S ADOPTION OF GENETICALLY MODIFIED SOYBEANS AFFECT GLOBAL SOYBEAN MARKETS?
abstract: China began commercial planting of genetically modified (GM) soybeans in 2024 after two decades of regulatory caution. Because China buys about two-thirds of the soybeans traded worldwide, exporters ask whether higher domestic yields will cut its imports and depress world prices. This paper works through three channels: yield gains on existing soybean land, land reallocation between corn and soybeans, and slower structural change in the countryside. title: Evidence for funerary behaviour and lethal trauma in a new Neanderthal individual from Shanidar Cave
abstract: Abstract Shanidar Cave has long featured in debates concerning Neanderthal cognitive capacity and behaviour, including evidence for care and intentional burial. By identifying additional individuals, including Shanidar A reported here, new excavations have expanded a burial cluster first identified in 1960. Shanidar A, an older adult, was deposited around 75,000 years ago, decayed, and their skeletal remains were subsequently disturbed by a flash flood. title: The Astronomical Language of James 1:17 Revisited
abstract: There is general agreement among scholars that παραλλαγὴ and τροπῆς ἀποσκίασμα in James 1:17 refer to astronomical phenomena, but little agreement as to the nature of these phenomena. The present article returns to the writings of the Greek astronomers to gain a scientifically precise understanding of these terms, and argues that astronomical terms such as these diffused from the academy into everyday Greek and Jewish life, and were both meaningful to James’s readers and useful for James’s argument.

title: Production Risk and Productivity of Smallholder Onion Farmers in Taraba State, Nigeria
abstract: This study examined the production risks and productivity of smallholder onion farmers in Taraba State, Nigeria. The study specifically analyzed the production risk associated with onion production for each input, assessed the contribution of major production inputs to onion output, and estimated the returns to scale in onion production. A multistage sampling procedure was used to select 254 onion farmers from Jalingo, Ardo-Kola, and Wukari Local Government Areas of Taraba State. title: La instrumentalización del diseño gráfico en la industria musical: de la experiencia material al consumo digital.
abstract: Este artículo analiza la transformación del diseño gráfico dentro de la industria musical a partir del desplazamiento de los soportes físicos hacia los entornos digitales. Desde una perspectiva histórica y critica, mediante una revisión documental cualitativa, se examina el trayecto de la portada musical como objeto material y comercial hacia su condición contemporánea de imagen integrada en interfaces digitales y sistemas de recomendación. title: Notes on the natural history of the carpet python (Morelia spilota) at the northern tip of Australia
abstract: As part of a broader study, we gathered data on the natural history of carpet pythons (Morelia spilota) from the Lockerbie Scrub in Cape York. Between 2013 and 2016, we detected 37 carpet pythons during nocturnal road surveys across 28.8 km of woodland and rainforest. All specimens were in woodland, unlike rainforest-dwelling carpet pythons in the Atherton Tablelands. Our sample was dominated by small individuals. title: Experimentos Mentales y Racionalismo Modal: una evaluación crítica del enfoque de Chalmers
abstract: “Thought experiments” are common in many scientific disciplines and can have significant theoretical consequences. However, we know they can fail, which leads to the question of how to establish that a thought experiment legitimately achieves its result. Given the modal dimension of thought experiments, one plausible option is to address this question within the framework of a particular modal epistemology. abstract: The article presents calculations of the estimated safety factor F and the overdesign factor, ODF, for the front embankment body of the Lake Druzno reservoir in Nowe Dolno. title: Optimization of Zn(II)-Diethyldithiocarbamate (DDTC) Complex Formation for UV–Vis Spectrophotometric Determination
abstract: Direct UV–Vis spectrophotometric determination of Zn(II) is limited by the absence of a suitable intrinsic chromophore, necessitating complex formation to obtain an analytical absorption response. However, comprehensive optimization of the Zn(II)–diethyldithiocarbamate (DDTC) extraction system remains limited. title: The Kārṣāpaṇa and the King's Share: Currency, Taxation and Fiscal Administration in the Empire of Aśoka
abstract: Aśoka's empire rested on two fiscal instruments that the epigraphic and archaeological record allows us to see with unusual clarity: a silver punch-marked currency denominationed in kārṣāpaṇas and paṇas, and a land-based revenue system whose central levy, bali, is named by the emperor's own inscription at Lumbinī. title: Savannah elephant family dynamics: short- and long-term responses to environmental and social changes
abstract: Multilevel societies offer flexibility in short-term association patterns for individual members while retaining valuable long-term relationships with conspecifics. Using a long-term data set on free-ranging African elephants, Loxodonta africana , in Amboseli, Kenya, we illustrate the complexity of decisions about associates in elephant multilevel societies on annual and longer-term timescales, spanning over 50 years. title: Leveraging Cultural Events for Destination Branding: Assessing the Impact of the Radin Jambat Festival on the Image of Way Kanan Regency, Indonesia
abstract: This study investigates the strategic role of cultural festivals in shaping destination image within the context of emerging tourism regions in Indonesia. Specifically, it examines the influence of the Radin Jambat Festival on the destination image of Way Kanan Regency, Lampung Province. Utilizing a quantitative approach, this research surveyed 95 respondents who attended the festival. Data were analyzed using Simple Linear Regression via SPSS. abstract: Abstract Pseudomonas aeruginosa ( P. aeruginosa ), an opportunistic bacterial pathogen, causes severe respiratory infections. Rapid detection of bacterial species is important for switching from broad-spectrum to narrow-spectrum antibiotics when antimicrobial resistance is present. Here, we designed paper-based hydrophilic-lipophilic balance/divinylbenzene/polydimethylsiloxane polymer-coated TF-SPME patches and integrated them into a bacterial culture to extract volatile emissions associated with the P. aeruginosa (ATCC 27853) strain. title: Marriage in Central Asia During The Soviet Period: State Policy, Traditional Practices, and Social Transformation
abstract: This article examines the transformation of marriage and wedding practices in Central Asia during the Soviet period, with particular attention to the interaction between Soviet state policy, Islamic institutions, customary law, and local traditions. Marriage represented one of the most important spheres in which Soviet modernization encountered deeply rooted social and cultural practices. Following the establishment of Soviet power, marriage was progressively transferred from the religious and customary sphere into the sphere of secular state legislation. abstract: The paper is an examination of thetraditions of the exoteric performance of the Igbabonnenlimi acrobatic dance of the Esan people of Edo state, Nigeria. It is an attempt to study what ordinarily cannot be comprehended through the orthodox Western scholarly tradition, an art, which nonetheless was experienced by a privileged group of initiates, that you may consider to be adherents of ancestral religion. abstract: Focussing on the period from 1970 to 1990, this article examines how gay men, many of whom moved from Ireland to London, adapted their activism in the face of evolving housing pressures. It pays particular attention to how housing reforms, the AIDS crisis and notions of national identity shaped gay politics during this period and how the social crises of the 1980s transformed gay radicalism as conflict over identities and AIDS redefined gay activism and interactions with the state. abstract: This study investigates the mechanical performance, workability, and durability of sisal fibre-reinforced mortar (SFRC) modified through alkali treatment (NaOH) and combined alkali-paraffin treatment. abstract: Iodine is an essential micronutrient, and iodine deficiency remains an important public-health concern worldwide. Although universal salt iodization is an effective strategy for improving iodine intake, food manufacturers have raised concerns regarding the possible effects of iodized salt on sensory quality, fermentation, spoilage, shelf life, and iodine stability. abstract: Despite the rapid expansion of rigid road pavements in Nepal, their lifecycle environmental impacts remain largely unquantified. abstract: How do governing parties regulate informal miners and what explains regulatory response variations? Drawing on Ghana and leveraging original and secondary data, this paper shows that National Democratic Congress (NDC) incumbents tolerated most local miners even when President Mahama raided the informal mining sector. title: Environmental impact ramifications of replacing added sugar with non-nutritive sweeteners in a high-calorie Dutch diet: the SWEET project
abstract: Abstract Purpose Growing concern about excess added sugar intake and associated adverse health effects has increased interest in non-nutritive sweeteners (NNS) as low-calorie alternatives that preserve sweetness. abstract: Este artículo de reflexión analiza la nostalgia como una estructura de sentido recurrente en la obra de Rubén Blades. Aunque la recepción crítica ha privilegiado, con razón, el carácter urbano, narrativo y político de sus composiciones, la nostalgia constituye uno de los principios que articulan esas dimensiones. title: Optimizing Stocking Density for Enhanced Tilapia and Lettuce Production in NFT Aquaponics
abstract: Water is an essential resource in arid regions; therefore, its management and use must be rational. Aquaponics, which integrates aquaculture and hydroponics, represents an innovative approach to efficient water use, particularly in arid environments. abstract: The occurrences of three invasive Rubus species, namely Rubus ellipticus Smith, Rubus rosifolius Smith and Rubus niveus Thunb. are analysed in three locations in Colombia. (olive) has been acknowledged for its therapeutic properties, especially in addressing illnesses associated with oxidative stress.This study examines the hepatoprotective efficacy of flavonoid-rich extracts derived from Olea europaea L. in the context of chemically induced liver damage.Phytochemical analysis confirmed the presence of bioactive substances such as flavonoids, phenolic acids, and secoiridoids, noted for their significant antioxidant and antiinflammatory properties.Hepatic injury was generated experimentally with hepatotoxic chemicals, resulting in substantial inc

title: Effect of Accruals Quality on the Firm Value of Construction and Allied Firms Listed at the Nairobi Securities Exchange, Kenya
abstract: Accruals quality is a dimension of financial reporting quality because reliable accrual information enables investors to assess reported earnings and firm performance. However, evidence on whether accruals quality translates into higher firm value remains limited among construction and allied firms listed at the Nairobi Securities Exchange. The study examined the effect of accruals quality on firm value. title: Harnessing the ion transportome to treat cancer
abstract: Abstract Despite significant advances in early detection and therapeutic opportunities, cancer remains a critical global health challenge. The greatest barrier to reducing cancer‐associated mortality is the persistent problem of therapeutic resistance and metastasis. Standard treatment approaches, including surgery combined with chemotherapy and radiation, are effective for many patients with localised disease. However, a substantial proportion of patients will experience recurrence and therapy resistance, leading to treatment failure and poor outcomes. This adverse prognosis for patients high

title: Visions of the Future and the Problem of the Cold War Past
abstract: Using Mike Davis’ City of Quartz , Leslie Marmon Silko's Almanac of the Dead , and Octavia Butler's Parable of the Sower as an entry point, this article reconstructs the career of the concept of the Cold War, tracing the decline of its paradigm in favor of a shift to the more capacious category of imperialism.

title: Cross-protection of wildtype and vaccine-derived chikungunya virus antibodies against chikungunya and Mayaro viruses in mice
abstract: Abstract The live-attenuated vaccine IXCHIQ against chikungunya virus (CHIKV) was approved in 2023, with its efficacy evaluated using human neutralizing antibody titers as surrogate effectiveness criterion. Previous in vivo studies assessed its efficacy at high CHIKV-specific antibody titers, whereas its efficacy and antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) risks at suboptimal levels mimicking long-term immunity remain poorly characterized. abstract: Interlayer stacking modes dictated by noncovalent interactions play a pivotal role in influencing pore structures and emergent properties of 2D covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs), yet precise control over stacking modes remains challenging. title: Conditions and implications of participation in semiotics (and elsewhere)
abstract: AbstractThis paper examines the conditions of possibility for semiotics to engage with the notion of participation and, through it, with participatory sciences. After tracing the genealogy of participation as a concept—from participant observation and action research to actor-network theory—the paper analyses the political requalification of this sociological notion into an institutional project for science. title: Ecological and functional value of nativebees in Avocado (Persea americana) pollination.
abstract: Although bees provide essential ecosystem services, the contribution of native bee functional groups to avocado pollination remains poorly quantified. We aimed to (1) evaluate the effect of distance from semi-natural vegetation on native bee visitation rates and (2) compare pollen transfer potential and fruit production among native bee functional groups. We surveyed bee visitation along a 6–72 m gradient from semi-natural vegetation in two commercial Hass avocado (Persea americana Mill.) orchards in central Chile (20 trees each; 2018). title: Lifestyle factors and clustered patterns of body shape change in Korean adults: A longitudinal observational study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Obesity is a major health problem driven by lifestyle habits and changes in body composition, particularly increased body fat mass and reduced skeletal muscle mass. Body mass index alone cannot fully characterize adiposity distribution or changes in muscle mass. Body-shape indicators such as waist circumference, waist-to-hip ratio, and waist-to-height ratio predict metabolic and cardiovascular disease risk; however, few studies have assessed longitudinal changes in these measures together with lifestyle factors. title: Valorizing palm date wastes for supercapacitor electrode synthesis and evaluation
abstract: Abstract Climate and energy issues continue to drive researchers to develop fossil-free energy technologies that are both sustainable and scalable. In this work, date seeds (DS) are used to produce activated carbon (DSAC), which is then used as a supercapacitor electrode. The synthesis method uses KOH activation coupled with argon-gas flow calcination at 950 °C. The produced DSAC has a high specific surface area of 1374 m 2 /g and a turbostratic microporous structure (pore size = 1.14 nm), in addition to oxygen-containing functional groups (–C–O–, –OH). title: Social Cultural Dynamics of Iruekpen Community and Its Neighbors
abstract: This article examines the social –cultural relations between Iruekpen community and its neighbours in Esan society, Edo State, Nigeria. The study explores the social Cultural dynamics of Iruekpen community. Through a qualitative research approach, the study examines the historical, cultural, and geographical contexts of inter-village settlement, festivals, intermarriages, joint worship, and linguistic affinity between Iruekpen community’s relationships with its neighbours. The findings highlight the significance of these social cultural dynamics in promoting social cohesion, cultural identity

abstract: This article aims to examine the practice of the application of jus cogens by international judicial institutions, including the Permanent Court of International Justice, the International Court of Justice, international criminal justice bodies, and regional judicial bodies (such as the European Court of Human Rights and the Inter-American Court of Human Rights), as well as to explore the development of the jus cogens concept in the practice of national courts, with particular reference to the United States, Argentina, and Ukraine. title: An immunomodulatory hydrogel activates dual NF-κB and cGAS-STING pathways to suppress osteosarcoma growth and recurrence
abstract: Abstract Osteosarcoma is the most common primary malignant bone tumor in adolescents, significantly impacting their quality of life. The difficulty in removing all residual tumor cells during surgery contributes to the recurrence of osteosarcoma. To provide an alternative strategy, we developed an iron-based polysaccharide hydrogel (gIONPs@CMOT) with immunomodulatory capabilities to activate antitumor immunity and remodel the postoperative tumor immune microenvironment. title: LINGUISTIC STRUCTURE OF RESTAURANT MENUS: A COMPARATIVE CORPUS STUDY OF WESTERN AND UZBEK MENU TEXTS
abstract: Restaurant menus constitute a distinct text type whose linguistic architecture remains under-described for most languages outside English. This article reports a comparative corpus study of two balanced menu corpora: a Western corpus of twenty menus from Ireland, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, Australia, France, Germany, and Spain (9,481 tokens), and an Uzbek corpus of twenty menus from restaurants in Tashkent, Samarkand, Bukhara, and Khiva, written in the Uzbek language (3,677 tokens). title: Study on the possibility of optimizing technology for repairing aircraft skin using riveting according to strength criteria
abstract: Flight safety plays a decisive role in passenger comfort and security. It mostly depends on the reliability of the aircraft. During operation, this reliability is maintained by the effectiveness of repair technology and the quality of the repair. The implementation of new repair technologies and the optimization of existing ones is a key aspect of this process. For this reason, this study examines the possibility of optimizing a well-known technology for aircraft structural repair, namely the repair of the aircraft fuselage using riveting. title: Absorb the Doom: Depression and Alienation in the Lyric Sketchbooks of Gabby Schulz
abstract: In this article, I propose a new category of autobiographical writing I call the ‘lyric sketchbook’. Drawing on Emma Winsor Wood’s conceptualisation of the ‘lyric diary’, I define the lyric sketchbook as a multimodal work consisting of fundamentally non-narrative fragments, rooted in a visual-verbal comics aesthetic and committed to representing a sense of self that is equal parts alienated and depressive. title: Volatile-mediated microbiome enrichment by Streptomyces albidoflavus G1 enhances suppression of apple ring rot pathogen Botryosphaeria dothidea
abstract: Abstract Background Apple ring rot, caused by the fungal pathogen Botryosphaeria dothidea , is a devastating disease affecting apple production. It causes extensive damage to fruit and branches, leading to significant economic losses within the apple industry in China and across the globe. While the volatile organic compound G1-VOC has demonstrated remarkable efficacy in suppressing B. dothidea and reducing fruit decay, its internal biocontrol mechanism and the host transcriptional response remain largely unexplored. abstract: Purpose Organizations are currently confronted with agile external dynamics, and achieving sustainable organizational performance requires the appropriate method. Therefore, this study aims to explain how innovation can achieve sustainable organizational performance, tracing the antecedents to produce a comprehensive model. abstract: The article analyses the scientific literature on the bioecological characteristics, distribution range, chemical composition and medicinal properties of wild bog bilberry (Vaccinium uliginosum L.), which grows in the cold regions of the Northern Hemisphere, and of the closely related cultivated species, highbush blueberry (V. corymbosum L.). title: Genotype × Environment Interaction and Yield Stability of UiTM Advanced Rice Lines Across Two Malaysian Environments
abstract: Genotype × Environment (G×E) interaction is a key determinant of yield stability and adaptability in rice under varying agro-ecological conditions. This study evaluated five gamma-irradiation-derived UiTM advanced rice mutant lines alongside six commercial varieties across two Malaysian locations to assess yield performance, phenotypic variability, and preliminary adaptability. title: Trauma maxilofacial para cirujanos generales: Una revisión sistemática
abstract: Introducción. El trauma maxilofacial puede convertirse en una amenaza para la vida por compromiso de la vía aérea o hemorragia masiva, así como por las lesiones asociadas. title: Education Reform as Organized Abandonment? A Spatial Analysis of School Consolidation in Remote Aboriginal Communities of the Northern Territory of Australia, 2014–2018
abstract: Over the past four decades, neoliberal reforms have reshaped education systems globally. Among these, school consolidation remains a popular policy instrument promising efficiency, consistency, and scale. In some urban contexts, however, consolidation has produced uneven impacts along racial and socioeconomic lines. This study shifts attention from the global metropole to small, diverse Indigenous communities using the case of a high-school consolidation process continuing to affect Aboriginal communities across the sparsely populated Northern Territory of Australia. title: Drivers of invertebrate community structure in a high-volume Neotropical cave system: a newly recognized subterranean biodiversity hotspot
abstract: Understanding how niche-based and neutral processes shape biological communities is a central objective in ecology, particularly in extreme and poorly explored environments such as large subterranean systems. Here, we investigated the mechanisms structuring terrestrial invertebrate communities in the one of the most extensive and voluminous cave systems in South America. Sampling across 56 sectors (30 m²) and 168 quadrats (1 m²) revealed 123 terrestrial invertebrate species. title: Une synthèse des pelouses dunaires maritimes de l’Europe occidentale
abstract: Cet article concerne une tentative de synthèse sur les végétations de pelouses maritimes arrière-dunaires plus ou moins fixées de l’Europe occidentale, de la Norvège au Portugal. Outre une description synthétique des alliances et des associations, ces dernières sont placées dans deux schémas systémiques combinant l’ensemble des vingt géosigmetums des dunes sèches de la zone d’étude concernée.

title: Corrosion Control in Oil Pipeline Infrastructure Using Gmelina Arborea and Wire Croton Extracts
abstract: This research explores the sustainable application of Gmelina arborea and Wire Croton plant extracts as green corrosion inhibitors for oil pipeline infrastructure. Steel samples were exposed to different corrosive environment (acidic, alkaline, saline, and neutral) to simulate the diverse conditions faced by pipelines. Three different concentration ratios of the extract (50:50, 60:40, and 40:60) were applied into the corrosive environment to determine their efficacy in inhibiting pipeline corrosion. title: Activación epigenética del gen SERPINA3 como estrategia compensatoria para la deficiencia de alfa-1 antitripsina: propuesta de un modelo con CRISPRa
abstract: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) is an inherited disorder mainly associated with pathogenic variants in SERPINA1, which cause misfolded protein accumulation in the liver and reduced pulmonary antiprotease protection. This article reviews recent advances in gene therapies for AATD and proposes an alternative model based on epigenetic activation of SERPINA3 using CRISPRa. title: TENDINOPATÍAS: ACTUALIZACIÓN SOBRE MÉTODOS DE TRATAMIENTO Y PROTOCOLOS TERAPÉUTICOS ACTUALES
abstract: Las tendinopatías son trastornos musculoesqueléticos frecuentes que pueden ocasionar dolor, limitación funcional y disminución de la capacidad para realizar actividades cotidianas, laborales y deportivas. El objetivo fue analizar y actualizar la evidencia científica sobre los principales métodos terapéuticos utilizados actualmente en su tratamiento. title: Computational Study of Gas-Phase Reactions to Produce Sulfite Esters: A New Class of Sulfur Containing Molecules in the Atmosphere?
abstract: Abstract We use computational quantum chemistry to study gas-phase reactions of aldehydes with water and sulfur dioxide. We find that a new reaction leading to the formation of previously nearly unstudied sulfite esters is possible with a comparatively low barrier. The reaction can be catalyzed by the presence of additional hydrogen bonding molecules, including water, nitric acid, and sulfuric acid. title: RICE FARMERS' PERCEPTIONS OF THE CAUSES OF CLIMATE CHANGE AND ASSOCIATED SOCIOECONOMIC FACTORS IN BEKWARRA LOCAL GOVERNMENT AREA, CROSS RIVER STATE, NIGERIA.
abstract: This study investigated the rice farmers’ perceptions of the causes of climate change and associated socioeconomic factors in Bekwarra Local Government Area, Cross River State, Nigeria. Literature was duly reviewed under. A multistage sampling technique was used to select 98 respondents, and data were collected through structured questionnaire and analyzed using percentage, mean and regression analysis. title: Validity of the comprehensive assessment of psychopathic personality–self‐report Korean version ( CAPP ‐ SR ) in a sample of Korean prison inmates
abstract: Given the theoretical and clinical importance of psychopathy, numerous assessment instruments have been developed, including the Comprehensive Assessment of Psychopathic Personality (CAPP). Although the CAPP has received increasing empirical support across cultures, research examining the validity of the Korean self-report version remains limited. The current study examined the validity of the Comprehensive Assessment of Psychopathic Personality-Self Report Korean Version (CAPP-SR) in Korea. title: The Contributions of Historian Mohamed-Seghir Ghanem to the Establishment of the Foundations of the Algerian Historical School
abstract: Following independence, historical studies in Algeria witnessed the emergence of a distinguished group of researchers and historians specialising in ancient, medieval, modern, and contemporary history. Among the most prominent scholars of the ancient history of the Maghreb was Dr Mohamed-Seghir Ghanem, who, despite his passing, left a rich scholarly legacy that helped reinterpret the region’s ancient history beyond the French colonial perspective that had long dominated most of its subjects. title: Inclusión financiera en Ecuador: Expansión del Acceso, Morosidad Sistémica y Presión sobre las Provisiones en la Banca Privada, Pública y el Sector Cooperativo
abstract: Existe una paradoja en la evolución reciente del sistema financiero ecuatoriano: el mismo proceso que permitió incorporar a millones de personas a productos y servicios financieros también contribuyó, en parte, al deterioro de la calidad de la cartera y a nuevas formas de exclusión. title: Vegetation cover dynamics across presidential terms in Brazil
abstract: Abstract National-level politics play important roles in shaping environmental policies. We provide a synthetic and integrative analysis of vegetation cover changes across presidential terms between 1990 and 2025 in Brazil, focusing on the Amazon, Atlantic Forest, and Cerrado. Our results show marked temporal differences in rates of habitat loss across biomes. title: The Tourism–Poverty Paradox in Jamaica: A Parish-Level Mathematical Examination of Hotel Concentration, Tourism Employment, and Poverty
abstract: Tourism is one of Jamaica's principal economic sectors, yet the geographical coexistence of internationally competitive hotel enclaves and economically disadvantaged communities raises questions about the extent to which tourism development translates into local poverty reduction. title: Subnational spatial co-distribution of tuberculosis and diabetes mellitus across Ghana’s 16 regions following administrative reorganisation: An ecological analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: National administrative boundary reorganisations, increasingly common across sub-Saharan Africa, create discontinuities in surveillance data alignment that complicate subnational burden estimation for infectious and non-communicable diseases alike. abstract: El acoso y la violencia escolar comprometen el derecho a aprender en condiciones de seguridad y afectan la participación, el bienestar y la trayectoria educativa de niñas, niños y adolescentes. Este artículo analiza críticamente las estrategias de prevención pertinentes para instituciones de Educación General Básica y Bachillerato en Ecuador. title: Soft Shell, Hard Core: Peach Culture and The Paradox of Immigrant Integration in Italy
abstract: To the international observer, Italy is the archetype of a Peach Culture, as a society characterized by a soft, approachable exterior where interpersonal warmth and informality facilitate initial social contact. This reputation for La Dolce Vita and warmth is often cited as a primary pull factor for newcomers. However, this commentary argues that this very cultural flexibility functions as a structural trap for economic migrants. title: Vaginal formulations selectively target Lactobacillus iners and Candida spp. while preserving Lactobacillus crispatus
abstract: Vaginal eubiosis is associated with low bacterial diversity and Lactobacillus crispatus dominance, whereas Lactobacillus iners often persists after antibiotics. We evaluated complementary approaches to inhibit L. iners and Candida spp. while preserving L. crispatus. title: Navigating Bureaucratic Hurdles: Fostering an FTZ-minded Investment Climate in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand
abstract: Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand are reported to foster regional and international cooperation, as well as compete in attracting domestic and international investments, particularly within the context of FTZs. Bureaucratic hurdles remain the biggest issues responsible for stifling investment growth, which contrasts with the nature of FTZs and the designation as areas for rapid economic growth. abstract: Terrorism in West Africa and the Sahel has evolved from isolated criminal acts into organised and sustained violence that increasingly resembles armed conflict. Groups such as Boko Haram, the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal Muslimin (JNIM) and the Islamic State in the Greater Sahara (ISGS) have established command structures, exercised territorial influence, conducted prolonged military operations and engaged state armed forces on a continuing basis. abstract: Emergency department visits are common among patients with advanced cancer and may increase during the final stages of disease. Although many visits are related to acute complications requiring urgent assessment, others may potentially be managed through anticipatory symptom control, outpatient care, or timely access to palliative care services. abstract: The container and domestic glass (CDG) industry is one of the most energy-intensive sectors in China. To analyse the life cycle carbon emissions and the potential for carbon reduction of the CDG industry in China, we developed a carbon-emission accounting model based on life cycle assessment (LCA) and conducted an empirical analysis using 2023 as the baseline year. title: Development Strategy of E-Government in Village Governance in Banda Sub-District
abstract: Background: E-government is intended to improve transparency, accountability, efficiency, and public participation using information technology. However, its implementation in village governance in Banda Sub-district, Central Maluku Regency, remains uneven because of limitations in institutional readiness, human resources, infrastructure, and policy support. abstract: El artículo analiza el modo en que las cartas de Pedro de Valdivia convierten la adversidad, la fragilidad de la gobernación y la lealtad imperial en capital de autoridad. abstract: This article focuses on translations and rewritings of classical Chinese poetry in a group of early twentieth-century modernist little magazines. abstract: Our duoethnographic inquiry, grounded in Intersectionality, addresses the following questions: How do intersectionality and internationalization complicate Black diasporic dynamics within the United States? What communal responsibilities do Black international/immigrant people hold toward Black American people within the U.S. academy? abstract: La construcción teórica del pensamiento numérico es objeto de controversia entre la didáctica de las matemáticas y las neurociencias cognitivas. abstract: This article examines the evolution of Brazilian migration policy from a historical and critical perspective, tracing its trajectory from the colonial period to the enactment of Law No. 13,445/2017 — the Migration Law. abstract: PURPOSE: Although the Mediterranean diet has been widely studied in relation to depression, less is known about the associations between other diets, such as the Nordic Diet, and depressive symptoms and clinical depression. abstract: The load capacity factor (LCF) is a preferred sustainability indicator due to its ability to measure the ecological footprint and the biocapacity to support both. abstract: Applying Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) methods to the online output of climate change contesters, this article examines how their discursive strategies are accommodated within counter-disinformation frameworks. abstract: Dry Afromontane forests are important carbon sinks, yet the influence of topographic gradients on their carbon stocks remains insufficiently understood. This study assessed aboveground carbon (AGC), belowground carbon (BGC), litter carbon (LC), soil organic carbon (SOC), and total carbon (TC) stocks along altitude, slope, and aspect gradients in Bela Mountain Forest, northern Ethiopia. abstract: Las extradiciones de personas desde México hacia Estados Unidos se han intensificado en las últimas décadas como parte de la cooperación bilateral en materia de seguridad y persecución penal. abstract: Antibiotic accumulation in discharged water is a growing global public health concern that demands high-performance membrane materials to mitigate it. abstract: Human activities have transformed landscapes through habitat loss and fragmentation, and species responses depend on their tolerance to these changes. Such responses can be gradual or abrupt, with critical points—thresholds—where abundances shift sharply. abstract: Bone is a type of specialized connective tissue that forms the skeleton. It´s solid, resistant, vascularized, and provides support, movement, protection, mineral storage, hematopoiesis, among other characteristics. abstract: Abstract Agricultural systems face the critical challenge of providing sufficient, healthy nutrition for a growing population while operating within planetary boundaries and conserving biodiversity. abstract: Abstract Black chickpea is a subgroup of desi chickpeas characterized by its black-colored seeds. abstract: Several large scabies outbreaks have occurred in the Amhara region of Ethiopia since 2015, and biomedical interventions focused on mass drug administration are often deployed to contain the disease. abstract: Competence Based Curriculum (CBC) arose in Rwandan education as indispensable ingredient to foster quality education for producing knowledgeable and competent citizens. title: Melanin as a Multifunctional Molecular System: Biosynthesis, Genetics, and Functional Roles in Livestock Species
abstract: Melanin is the primary pigment found in the skin, hair, wool and feathers of many vertebrates and plays a crucial role in determining the physical appearance and physiological performance of livestock species. Melanin functions in thermoregulation as well as coloration, photoprotection, and adaptation to diverse environmental conditions. This review examines the biosynthesis of melanin and the genetics of melanogenesis in major livestock species such as cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, horses, and poultry, and the roles of melanin-based pigmentation within different systems of animal production. title: The Role Of Gastronomy Image in the Effect Of Brand Awareness and Perceived Service Quality on Willingness To Pay More in Restaurants
abstract: Tourists seeking to move away from standardized tourist experiences due to globalization are increasingly turning to experiencing local culture and daily life practices in the destinations they visit. In this context, gastronomy tourism has become a significant element in the development and competitiveness of destinations. This study examines the role of gastronomy image in the influence of brand awareness and perceived service quality on the willingness to pay more in restaurants. title: Sustainable finance taxonomies from a human rights perspective
abstract: This article examines the human rights compatibility of 15 sustainable finance taxonomies issued by private transnational and international institutions as of June 2025. Addressing a gap in the literature, it derives the human rights responsibilities of taxonomy issuers based on the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights and the OECD Due Diligence Guidance, viewing these issuers as business entities and collaborative governance initiatives (CGI). title: Modelo predictivo de la intención de actuar sostenible: Actitud y conciencia ambiental como impulsores en universitarios
abstract: The sustainable behavior of younger generations has generated interest among academics and decision-makers given their importance in the development of global solutions. The objective of this study is to analyze the effect of environmental attitude and awareness on the intention to act sustainably among college students in Mexico. The methodology was quantitative, using structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), with a sample of 192 students (46.9% male, 53.1% female) with an average age of 19 years (standard deviation 1.967) from Tamaulipas, Yucatán, and Hidalgo. title: European Catfish Establishment and Long‐Term Deterioration of a Traditional Cyprinid Recreational Fishery
abstract: ABSTRACT The effects of invasive apex predators on inland recreational fisheries remain poorly quantified. We used standardised angling competition records from Iznájar Reservoir, southern Spain (2008–2025), to test whether establishment of European catfish ( Silurus glanis ) was associated with deterioration of a traditional cyprinid fishery. title: Through Our Eyes: Visualising the Stories We Think Journalists Are Missing or Aren’t Covering Well
abstract: Societies around the world have seen a decrease over the past decade in news engagement as audiences increasingly report feeling “fatigued” or overwhelmed by the news, feeling that news is untrustworthy or poorly represents “people like me”; and/or feeling that the news isn’t relevant or valuable. Amidst this decline, movements and models, including civic journalism, community-centred journalism, and solidarity journalism, have emerged to try to counter this trend. title: One Health as a contemporary paradigm in health policy
abstract: The One Health concept is defined as an integrated approach to health based on the interdependence of humans, animals, and ecosystems. Within this framework, the High-Level Expert Panel identified six key areas representing major challenges for current health policy, including the reduction of epidemic and pandemic risks associated with zoonotic diseases, the control of endemic, tropical, and vector-borne diseases, the prevention of antimicrobial resistance, and the improvement of food safety and security. title: Informalidad laboral como mecanismo de exclusión crediticia en México (2021)
abstract: Este artículo analiza la relación entre la informalidad laboral y el acceso al crédito formal en México en 2021 desde el enfoque de la exclusión social. A partir de los microdatos de la Encuesta Nacional de Inclusión Financiera (ENIF 2021), se examina en qué medida la inserción laboral informal opera como un mecanismo estructural de exclusión crediticia, más allá de las diferencias individuales de ingreso y de las características sociodemográficas. title: Intervención o marginación institucional: relaciones cívico-militares en Latinoamérica a partir de Argentina y Ecuador
abstract: Este artículo compara las relaciones cívico-militares en Argentina y Ecuador tras la tercera ola de democratización, aplicando el institucionalismo histórico y el método comparado para explicar dichas relaciones en la actualidad. Pese a compartir un siglo XX marcado por golpes de Estado, gobiernos autoritarios y el "juego de doble moneda", ambos países divergieron radicalmente tras sus transiciones. title: Dieback Disease Increases Short-Term Spatial Heterogeneity and Litterfall Inputs in Forests Dominated by a Long-Lived Foundation Species
abstract: Abstract Litterfall, a key ecosystem process linking vegetation dynamics, carbon flux, and nutrient cycling, can be substantially altered by disease. However, effects of disease on both its production and spatial distribution are not well understood. We examined the effects of a dieback disease on leaf litterfall in forests dominated by a susceptible foundation tree species Agathis australis (kauri). title: Influenza vaccine effectiveness against hospitalization in children aged 6–72 months: a test-negative study in the Southern Italy, 2022–2026
abstract: BACKGROUND: Seasonal influenza is an important cause of hospitalization in young children, yet real-world evidence on vaccine effectiveness (VE) against severe outcomes remains limited in Italy. We estimated influenza VE against influenza-associated hospitalization among children aged 6-72 months in the district of Foggia, Southern Italy. title: Eviction, Home and the Spatiality of Shame
abstract: ABSTRACT Rooted in the scene of residential evictions, the present article examines the intersection of shame and eviction through intimate group interviews with family members in gentrifying Mexico City. It makes three contributions: highlighting the role of shame in facilitating evictions, presenting a spatial theory of shame and offering strategies for resolving shame and restoring political agency and connection. title: ASESMEN AUTENTIK STORYTELLING DALAM PENGUKURAN KETERAMPILAN BERBICARA SISWA JENJANG SD/MI
abstract: Speaking skills are one of the important competencies in Indonesian language learning at the elementary/Islamic elementary school level that need to be developed through contextual and meaningful assessment. However, speaking skills assessment in schools is still dominated by conventional assessments so that students' speaking abilities have not been measured optimally. title: “Technology and science are, by definition, non-discriminatory”- narratives of the performance of sex and gender dimensions in European climate project proposals
abstract: Abstract The integration of sex and gender dimensions (SGDs) in European research and innovation (R&I) funding has become a central policy priority, yet its practical implementation in grant proposals remains underexplored. This study investigates how SGDs are framed, negotiated, and operationalised in technology-oriented proposals addressing the climate crisis, submitted to Horizon 2020 and Horizon Europe between 2014 and 2022. title: Acne: epidemiology, risk factors, pathogenesis, management and cutting-edge research
abstract: Acne vulgaris is a widespread chronic inflammatory skin condition particularly affecting the pilosebaceous unit, with its pathogenesis intricately linked to excessive sebum production, abnormal follicular keratinization, overcolonization by Cutibacterium acnes (C. acnes), and dysregulated host immune responses. Beyond its dermatological manifestations, the disorder is frequently associated with psychological comorbidities such as anxiety and depression, significantly impacting patients' quality of life. title: Identifying intercalation electrodes for electrochemical ion recovery and desalination
abstract: Water sources serve as a requirement for human consumption, industrial, and agricultural needs and a resource for valuable ions. Appropriate treatment of water that captures ions from the aqueous solution can give rise to suitable `products', such as critical ions (such as Li$^+$) in selective ion recovery and usable water in the case of desalination (i.e., removal of non-essential ions). title: BIER-DC: Stateless Multicast for In-Orbit Space Data Centers in LEO Constellations
abstract: Emerging data-intensive space applications generate large volumes of data that must be processed, stored, replicated, and delivered efficiently. However, relying on terrestrial cloud regions can expose satellite data to high delivery latency and loss of timeliness due to intermittent satellite-to-ground visibility and limited access to ground infrastructure. title: Hurricane recovery gaps lie in reconnection, not local restart
abstract: Climate-intensified hurricanes disrupt urban mobility, yet whether recovery is equitable across the rural-urban gradient is unclear. Analyzing device-based mobility for Hurricanes Helene and Milton, we find local activity restarted within approximately 4.5 days in both storms, whereas reconnection to the outside world took 5 days in coastal-urban Florida but 11 in inland-rural Appalachia. The gap lies in external reconnection, not local restart, implying planners should target rural isolation.

title: Building Macroeconomically Relevant Climate Indices via the Assemblage VAR
abstract: What should a macroeconomically relevant climate index contain? The composition is inherently ambiguous, and aggregation choices affect structural inference. We introduce the Assemblage VAR, which jointly estimates nonnegative aggregation weights and VAR parameters by maximizing the system likelihood-gain criterion, effectively outsourcing aggregation to observed macroeconomic dynamics. Two variants operate in component-space and rank-space, reweighting named subcomponents or emphasizing regions of the cross-sectional distribution.
