title: Changing Geographies of Violence in North and West Africa
abstract: This paper analyses spatial trends in armed conflicts in North and West Africa. It shows that all types of violence saw a significant increase in 2025. However, these violent incidents are distributed very unevenly across the region: while conflict is at its lowest in North Africa, the vast majority of violent incidents and victims are concentrated in five West African countries: Nigeria, Cameroon, Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger. abstract: We calculate the sea-level cosmic-ray muon flux with CORSIKA and develop CorsikaAgent, an auditable large-language-model-based system for configuring, executing, and validating air-shower simulations, and for predicting particle fluxes in unexplored environments. The physics calculation uses proton primaries described by the solar-minimum spectrum of Papini et al., with UrQMD at low interaction energies and either Sibyll 2.3e or QGSJET-III at high energies. title: Constraints on pion parton distributions at small $x$ from leading-neutron electroproduction data
abstract: We revisit the extraction of parton distribution functions (PDFs) in the pion in a global QCD analysis of pion--nucleus Drell--Yan and leading-neutron (LN) electroproduction data, in view of recent suggestions that uncertainties on the pion PDFs at small parton momentum fraction $x$ are dramatically underestimated. title: Stochastic Snowball States in Planetary Climate
abstract: Motivated by the recent finding of Ji and Abbot (2025) that at moderate eccentricity (0.2--0.3) the planetary Snowball bistability vanishes, we have introduced stochasticity of the orbital eccentricity into a simplified version of the energy balance model of Eisenman and Wettlaufer (2009) to study a general Earth-like planet. abstract: Excitation of carbon and oxygen ions is the primary mechanism by which collapsing gas clouds dissipate heat to form new stars. At early cosmic times, in galaxies with chemically pristine gas, many stars are expected to have masses far larger than the mass of our sun due to the deficit in these elements. We searched for ultra-metal-poor galaxies using their spectroscopic absorption signatures in front of bright background quasars, employing the new GHOST high-resolution spectrograph. abstract: Artificial warming via engineered aerosols presents a novel pathway to bypass volatile scarcity on modern Mars. Utilizing the Generic Planetary Climate Model, we evaluate the physical feasibility of aerosol-induced terraforming over a full Martian year (669 Sols). abstract: Amino acid enantiomeric excess (EE) is a potential biosignature, but its measurement requires sufficient surviving material as well as preserved chirality. We derive a criterion that separates abundance-limited from racemization-limited preservation and apply it to the Mars Organic Molecule Analyzer (MOMA) on the ExoMars Rosalind Franklin rover. title: Personality Without Persons? A Psychometric Critique of Big Five Testing in Large Language Models
abstract: Human personality inventories are increasingly used to characterize large language models (LLMs), compare systems, and inform downstream governance claims. Yet, these inventories were developed and validated for humans, and it remains unclear whether they are valid for non-human systems. We present a systematic psychometric evaluation of Big Five personality measurement in LLMs. We ask three research questions: Do Big Five inventories a) appropriately describe LLMs, b) capture meaningful differences between models, and c) reflect internal factors consistent with human personality? abstract: Detecting biosignatures on Earth-like exoplanets from the Proterozoic era requires instrumentation capable of probing near-ultraviolet (NUV) spectral features, particularly ozone (\ce{O3}), which serves as an indirect proxy for molecular oxygen (\ce{O2}) when direct detection is challenging. abstract: The strong Szegő theorem and the Fisher-Hartwig formula describe the asymptotic behavior of determinants obtained by restricting translationally invariant operators to large finite regions. abstract: Non-equilibrium electron and phonon populations govern heat generation and dissipation in nanoscale devices, yet their direct characterization remains challenging. Anti-Stokes Raman scattering provides a sensitive probe of phonon populations and local temperatures, although its interpretation becomes more complex when electronic and phononic populations are driven out of equilibrium. abstract: Feature caching has become a mainstream training-free strategy for accelerating video diffusion models by reusing intermediate outputs across denoising steps. abstract: Universal, equation-of-state (EOS) insensitive relations among the global properties of compact stars are well established for hadronic neutron stars and for self-bound strange stars. abstract: The shipping industry faces increasing pressure to reduce greenhouse gas emissions while maintaining operational efficiency. This study evaluates the energy-saving potential of an Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC) system for waste heat recovery from a 21,840 kW MAN 8S65ME-C8.6 main marine diesel engine during a realistic 1,610.7-nautical-mile coastal voyage from Dalian to Qinzhou, China. abstract: The sediment plume resulting from the breach of the Kakhovka Dam on 06 June 2023 could lead to severe, long-term environmental pollution in the northwestern Black Sea (NWBS), as the floodwater transported contaminated sediments, chemicals, and polluted water from the reservoir and upstream sections of the Dnieper River. title: In situ enhancement of coral larval settlement using acoustic enrichment, engineered habitats and living materials
abstract: Worldwide reef ecosystem degradation is inspiring efforts to enhance in-situ coral larvae settlement onto degraded or artificial reefs. Here we simultaneously test three approaches for enhancing settlement over two weeks in Kāne'ohe Bay, O'ahu, Hawai'i. Nineteen artificial structures, mimicking natural reef mesoscale roughness, were deployed along two transect lines at distances between 1 and 42 m from an "acoustic enrichment" underwater speaker broadcasting healthy reef sound. title: Probabilistic tsunami hazard assessment and flood modeling: a case study of Manzanillo, Colima, Mexico
abstract: This study presents a site-specific seismic-source probabilistic tsunami hazard assessment for Manzanillo, Colima, a coastal city in Mexico vulnerable to local tsunamis due to its proximity to the subduction zone along the Mesoamerican Trench. Historical records show that the region has been affected by significant tsunamis, most notably in 1932 and 1995. title: A unified numerical method based on added momentum source terms for hydrodynamic prediction of underwater vehicles
abstract: Classical numerical methods for predicting hydrodynamic coefficients of underwater vehicles typically rely on repeated grid generation, dynamic mesh techniques, and complex physical models, resulting in high computational cost and operational complexity. In this study, a unified numerical method combining added momentum source terms with the Wray-Agarwal 2018 Rotation/Curvature turbulence model (WA-2018 RC model) is developed to address these limitations. abstract: Abstract Lightweight aggregate concrete has become a popular material in hydraulic engineering and coastal and offshore engineering, and understanding its durability under underwater rotational abrasion is critical. abstract: This article examines how the Yemeni Houthi movement transformed its missile, drone, and maritime capabilities into a source of regional instability and economic disruption in the Bab al-Mandab area. Rather than reconstructing the Yemeni war, it analyzes the development of the Houthi arsenal since the 2015 regionalization of the conflict and its intensified use following October 2023. abstract: Abstract Chlorine electro-oxidation represents the primary anode side reaction during direct seawater electrolysis, causing corrosion and permanent deactivation of catalyst and thereby insufficient stability. title: Environmental and geographic predictors of seed plant diversity across South American terrestrial coastal lomas
abstract: Understanding the predictors of plant diversity gradients remains a major challenge in biogeography, particularly in understudied arid ecosystems where water availability is highly constrained. Coastal lomas—isolated, fog-fed vegetation oases distributed across the Peruvian and Chilean coastal deserts of South America–provide a unique system for examining how climate, topography, and geography shape plant diversity under extreme aridity. abstract: As a core component of the offshore floating photovoltaic (OFPV) system, connectors exert a decisive influence on the stable operation of the entire multi-float structure. title: Transcriptional Profiling and Co-expression Integration for the Filtering of Relevant Bacterial sRNA–mRNA Interactions: Application to Staphylococcus aureus Biofilm
abstract: Abstract Small regulatory ribonucleic acids coordinate bacterial gene expression and contribute to biofilm development, virulence, and stress adaptation. We characterized these regulators across six Staphylococcus aureus strains by integrating newly generated transcriptome data from strain Bmb9393 with public datasets from five additional strains. abstract: Abstract Non-diffracting light beams have exceptional self-healing and propagation characteristics that make them unique for free-space optical communication, atmospheric optics, and remote sensing. Tricomi beams are a novel type of diffraction-free, structure-shaped beam whose scattering characteristics in humid maritime aerosol environments remain mostly unexplored. abstract: Igneous centres across the Taranaki Peninsula represent the southwestern limit of arc volcanism associated with the Tonga–Kermadec–Hikurangi subduction system. Taranaki Maunga, the youngest and largest of three andesitic stratovolcanoes, dominates the geomorphology of the Taranaki Peninsula along with the eroded remnants of the Kaitake and Pouakai edifices. abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines drug cartels as creative, innovation‐driven organizations rather than solely violent criminal enterprises. abstract: Abstract The under-development NASA Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) aims to provide breakthroughs in exoplanet science, yet the most effective approaches to modeling the detection and characterization of potentially Earth-like worlds with HWO remain uncertain despite being essential considerations for mission design. In this work, we aim to better model and understand detection metrics through the use of Exoplanet Open-Source Imaging Mission Simulator (EXOSIMS), an exoplanet yield modeling tool. title: Arctic Grayling, scared to death: Are Brown Trout an impediment to Arctic Grayling reintroduction success in Michigan?
abstract: Abstract Introduction Arctic Grayling Thymallus arcticus were extirpated from Michigan in 1936. Their demise was likely caused by overfishing, habitat destruction from large-scale logging, and the introduction of Brook Trout Salvelinus fontinalis and Brown Trout Salmo trutta. Subsequently, Brook Trout and Brown Trout have become the dominant salmonid species in Michigan streams. Past attempts to restore Arctic Grayling to Michigan have been unsuccessful, perhaps due to competition with these now-resident salmonids. title: Position of the Lhasa Terrane and Two‐Stage Crustal Shortening During the India–Asia Collision
abstract: Abstract The paleolatitudinal change of the Lhasa Terrane is critical for estimating the timing of the India–Asia collision and associated syn‐to post‐collisional crustal shortening, but its paleoposition is highly debated. Here we present integrated geochronologic and paleomagnetic results from the Lower Eocene Nianbo Formation in the Linzhou Basin. Two SIMS U−Pb zircon ages of 54.59 ± 0.68 Ma and 53.97 ± 0.43 Ma were obtained from the strata. The magnetostratigraphy spans chrons C24r–C23r, estimating deposition from ∼55.37 to ∼52.54 Ma. title: Coupled U–Pb geochronology of inherited and detrital zircon in the Iberian Massif: insights into its deep structure and geodynamic evolution
abstract: Abstract The combined use of detrital and inherited zircon U-Pb age spectra provides new insights into the crustal evolution of the Iberian Massif as part of the North Gondwana margin. In the Ossa–Morena Zone (OMZ), Ediacaran detrital zircon populations are dominated by Pan‑African ages, whereas inherited zircons overwhelmingly record Cadomian signatures, implying that Cadomian crust remained largely unexposed during the Cadomian event itself. title: Compact low-frequency optomechanical triaxial inertial sensor
abstract: Triaxial optomechanical accelerometers offer a compact, ground-testable complement to free-fall electrostatic accelerometers used in satellite geodesy, alongside applications in seismometry and precision metrology. We demonstrate a compact triaxial inertial sensor using monolithic fused-silica resonators with dual heterodyne interferometric readout. title: Probing soft signals of gravitational-wave memory with space-based interferometers
abstract: Gravitational-wave displacement memory is a remarkable, ubiquitous prediction of general relativity that has not yet been detected. Unlike the oscillatory components of gravitational waveforms, displacement memory is associated with soft gravitons and provides the leading low-frequency observable of its parent event. Analogous soft signals may also be associated with velocity and integrated-displacement memory. title: Decade-long data highlight medium-sized, fast-flowing cold-water streams as important recruitment habitats for European river and brook lampreys
abstract: European river lamprey Lampetra fluviatilis is a migratory (anadromous) species, spawning in freshwater rivers where it co-occurs with its non-migratory paired species, European brook lamprey L. planeri . Both species are listed under Annex II of the EU Habitats Directive, requiring habitat protection and sustainable management across their distribution ranges. Yet, both species have experienced declines and spatial drivers of larval recruitment remain poorly quantified. title: Sulfide‐Ene Reactions by Visible‐Light‐Mediated Phosphine Redox Catalysis
abstract: Sulfur‐containing compounds play a crucial role in many biological processes. The important gasotransmitter hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) can be metabolized by cellular enzyme system for the biosynthesis of amino acids and regulatory effects related to diseases. Although the photocatalytic thiol‐ene reactions have been widely developed, a general H 2 S‐ene reaction by organic photocatalysis remains elusive. abstract: Objective: This study aimed to investigate the potential of Resveratrol in reversing promoter hypermethylation of LATS1/2 genes, key components of the Hippo Signaling Pathway, in OSCC cell lines. Materials and Methods: In vitro investigation was conducted after getting encouraging outcomes from consensus molecular docking & molecular dynamics (MD) simulations upto 100 nanoseconds. title: Adakitic Permian magmatism along the eastern Gondwana margin: constraints on deep crustal processes and metallogenesis in northeastern Queensland
abstract: The Kennedy Igneous Association (KIA) of northeastern Queensland provides an opportunity to investigate links between granitoid magmatism, deep crustal processes and metallogenesis along the eastern Gondwana margin. This study integrates whole-rock geochemistry with new zircon U–Pb geochronology to constrain the timing, sources and tectonic significance of granitoids from the Georgetown region (Kidston subprovince). title: Gaussian process inference of stochastic magneto-active dynamics and viscosity in Swift J1727.8-1613
abstract: Linking X-ray variability to the underlying magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) dynamics of black hole X-ray binaries remains challenging. We systematically investigate the stochastic and oscillatory variability of the black hole X-ray binary candidate Swift J1727.8-1613 during its 2023 outburst using Gaussian process (GP) regression applied to Insight-HXMT multi-band light curves. title: Owned dog population profile, dog ownership and bite risk determinants: Key steps to rabies control in Antananarivo, Madagascar
abstract: Rabies remains a significant public health threat in Madagascar, with dog-mediated transmission causing approximately 1,000 human deaths annually. In Antananarivo, the capital city, control efforts are hindered by limited up to date knowledge on the dog population. This study aims to provide updated estimates of the owned dog population characteristics, identify determinants of ownership, and assess dog bite incidence and risk factors to guide effective vaccination and prevention strategies. abstract: The Cunqian Cu-Pb-Zn deposit is a significant skarn-porphyry deposit located at the junction of the eastern and central segments of the Qin-Hang metallogenic belt (QHMB) in China. However, ore prospecting in this area has been hindered by insufficient research on ore-related intrusions relative to adjacent areas. To constrain the emplacement timing and magma sources of the ore-related intrusions, this study presents systematic zircon U-Pb ages, trace element compositions, and Lu-Hf isotopic data. abstract: This article reflects on the critical inquiry that shapes the Darkness Reframed issue and, from a decolonial perspective, problematizes the possible assumptions attached to the category of darkness. Unpacking coloniality not only as a historical legacy but as a living force that continues to shape ways of thinking, the reflection points to the plurality of futures to be reframed in order to embrace a multilayered understanding of darkness(es). abstract: Comprehensive Summary Notwithstanding the importance of the hexafluoroisopropyl group (CH(CF 3 ) 2 ) in medicinal and agricultural chemistry, convenient access to hexafluoroisopropylthiolated (SCH(CF 3 ) 2 ) compounds remains challenging, limiting their exploration. title: Spontaneous ferromagnetic Fe–La geminal atoms with spin and coordination modulation for acidic oxygen reduction
abstract: Synergistic spin-state and local coordination engineering offers a promising strategy for enhancing the acidic oxygen reduction reaction performance of Fe–N–C electrocatalysts, yet the precise control and stabilization of active sites remain challenging. Here we report a Fe–La geminal-atom electrocatalyst (Fe1-La1/NC) with spontaneous ferromagnetic spin ordering for acidic oxygen reduction reaction. abstract: Abstract Dietary choice of seed-consuming rodents potentially determines the survival and dispersal success of shade-tolerant forest herbs – a group at risk in post-agricultural landscapes of eastern North America. Optimal foraging theory predicts that large, energy-rich seeds will be most attractive and seed consumption will be greater in structurally complex habitats, which provide protection from predators. abstract: Photoacoustic sensing has emerged as a promising technique for detecting polymeric particles suspended in liquids through the conversion of absorbed optical energy into acoustic signals. Here, we present a multiscale computational study of the photoacoustic response of polystyrene (PS) beads suspended in water under pulsed optical excitation. abstract: O presente estudo teve como objetivo realizar o inventário florístico das espécies de Piperaceae ocorrentes no município de Vitória da Conquista, Bahia. O trabalho foi desenvolvidocom base na análise de exsicatas provenientes de herbários, consultas a bases de dados virtuais e expedições de campo realizadas em fragmentos de floresta estacional decidual e floramentos rochosos. title: Numerical Solutions of Inelastic Compressible Fluid Flow in Two Dimensional Square Cavity
abstract: In this study, inelastic compressible flow within a two-dimensional square cavity is investigated using the Galerkin finite element method. The main goal is to investigate the effect of lid-driven boundary conditions on the flow characteristics. We apply two types of boundary conditions, a constant lid velocity and a given analytical velocity profile. title: HFIP-promoted Lewis acid-free one-pot synthesis of pyran derivatives under mild conditions
abstract: A one-pot, three-component reaction of aromatic aldehyde, malononitrile, dimedone or ethyl acetoacetate was developed in which the reaction medium and promoter was 1,1,1,3,3,3-hexafluoro-2-propanol (HFIP). abstract: Soil is an essential and strategic resource for the sustainability of agricultural production on the planet; however, it faces progressive degradation derived from unsustainable management practices and the effects of climate change. Within this context, climate-smart agriculture emerges as an approach to try to increase productivity by strengthening the resilience of agricultural systems. title: Multiple stressor effects of hypoxia and metals on ventilation, activity, bioaccumulation, and loss of equilibrium in fathead minnows
abstract: Hypoxia is an increasing concern in freshwater ecosystems, driven by warming, stratification, and nutrient enrichment. Fish cope with hypoxia through behavioural and ventilatory adjustments, yet growing evidence suggests that certain metals can impair these critical compensatory mechanisms. It is currently unknown whether lead (Pb) and nickel (Ni), released in part through expanding mining operations, may alter these critical survival responses. abstract: Abstract Production, sale, manufacturing and mounting of engineered stone kitchen countertops, tiles and sheets have been banned in Australia as at 2024. This type of change can be a point of concern with respect to other products which may also have reduced emissions throughout its life cycle, as well as decreasing the exposure of workers to respirable crystalline silica. abstract: La Informática Forense es una rama del conocimiento que trabaja con evidencia digital, información almacenada en un medio digital que es relevante para una investigación. title: Comparative efficacy of new-generation fungicides against major fungal diseases of rice
abstract: A field study was conducted during the kharif seasons of 2023 and 2024 at the Rice Research Unit, Agricultural Research Institute, Rajendranagar, using a randomised block design (RBD) with 8 treatments and 4 replications to evaluate the efficacy of seven multi-active combination fungicides against three predominant fungal diseases of rice in Telangana, namely sheath blight, blast and grain discolouration, which limit rice productivity and grain quality under intensive production systems. title: Weak and inconsistent associations between birch-feeding insects and pollution levels around two industrial towns during substantial emission decline (1988–2025)
abstract: Industrial emissions have historically altered terrestrial ecosystems, but their long-term effects on insect herbivores remain insufficiently understood, particularly during ecosystem recovery following emission decline. We analysed a dataset on the densities of 24 Recognisable Taxonomic Units (RTUs) of birch-feeding insects collected from 1988 to 2025 around two industrial towns in northwestern Russia previously identified as pollution hotspots. title: Functionalization of Peptides via Radical Arylation
abstract: Among the manifold methods for the functionalization of peptides known today, radical chemistry has so far only rarely been exploited to introduce structural modifications on this challenging type of substrate. In this short review, we give an overview showing that, especially, radical arylation reactions can represent attractive and powerful tools to access functionalized peptides under mild and biocompatible conditions where no protecting group strategy is required. title: A Cost-Illness Analysis of Economic Burden of Unimproved Water Use on Households: Empirical Evidence from Dhaka Urban Riparian Areas
abstract: The rapid urbanization and increasing industrial establishment near Dhaka’s rivers are creating environmental pressure on nearby communities. And people due to several factors are forced to use unimproved water from the nearby waterbodies. This study looks at how using unsafe water affects the health, health expenditure and poverty of 1,826 families living near the Turag River in Dhaka. title: Party Membership Rolls on the Open Web
abstract: Enmarcado en el campo de la Computación y Sociedad, este artículo analiza la difusión reciente de padrones de afiliados a partidos políticos en Argentina, a partir de casos masivos detectados en 2026. abstract: Abstract This article argues that taking Article 2 values seriously as a cornerstone of EU constitutional law requires analysing domains beyond the rule of law and judicial independence. It investigates the role of values in migration management by taking the EU–Turkey Statement and temporary reintroduction of border checks within Schengen as examples through which to tease out how values interact with non-values-based priorities, the indeterminacy of divergent interpretations of values, and the value of freedom. abstract: Various biotic constraints affect the cultivation of aromatic rice in India, especially in the North-West Plain Zone and bakanae disease is responsible for high economic losses ranging from 3.0–95.4 %. It occurs in Haryana and the adjoining states, particularly in early-transplanted rice crops. Weather influences all stages of the host and pathogen life cycle, as well as disease progression. abstract: La adquisición forense de dispositivos móviles en campo presenta desafíos en integridad, trazabilidad y control metodológico, especialmente cuando se utilizan métodos descentralizados o documentación manual. abstract: The concept of vertical greening systems has gained considerable attention in recent years as an innovative approach to enhancing thermal comfort within various built environments. This growing interest is rooted in the recognition of the substantial influence that greenery can exert on the microclimate of structures. The design of student hostels in general faces a significant challenge on thermal discomfort, intensified by high solar gain in the tropical savannah climate. title: Recent advances and emerging mechanisms in graphene-based materials for cartilage tissue engineering
abstract: Graphene-based materials offer tunable mechanical, electrical, and biochemical properties that address longstanding challenges in cartilage tissue engineering. This review synthesizes recent advances in graphene derivatives, scaffold fabrication strategies, and emerging mechanisms governing cell-graphene interactions. title: Luxury hospitality meets sustainability: crafting impactful stories on social media
abstract: Purpose Luxury is synonymous with quality, exclusivity and rarity, characteristics which do not hold sustainability as a core consideration in service provision. This study aims to investigate how luxury service brands craft stories on social media around their sustainability practices. title: A deeper look into the diversity of suckermouth catfishes (Mochockidae: Chiloglanis Peters 1868) of southern Africa, with the description of four new species
abstract: Suckermouth catfishes of the genus Chiloglanis Peters 1868 are small and predominantly rheophilic fishes endemic to Africa. This genus is quite diverse, with over 70 species distributed across most river systems on the continent, except for the Cape Fold ecoregion and most of northern Africa. The present study undertook detailed genetic and morphological examination of suckermouth catfishes collected from multiple localities across the Zambezi River system. abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional tin perovskites are attracting increasing attention for coherent light emission, yet the impact of organic cations on their properties remains poorly understood. title: Poking the cell surface: mechanics, remodeling, and what force reveals
abstract: Abstract What happens when you poke a living cell, applying a localized external force to its surface? The answer depends, in part, on how long you keep poking. The plasma membrane and the actomyosin cortex beneath it form a mechanically active interface that changes in disease and can itself be reshaped by force. abstract: Glacial Isostatic Adjustment (GIA) models solve the gravitationally self-consistent sea-level equation for the response of the solid Earth and the oceans to changing ice loads. abstract: Stagnation in the summation of floating-point numbers occurs when the running sum, or the accumulator, does not change its value despite addends being greater than zero. abstract: We perform direct numerical simulations of rotating turbulence to investigate the mechanisms responsible for the maintenance of large-scale geostrophic vortices. abstract: User simulators are gaining attention as environments to train LLM assistants that can better cope with the nuances of multi-turn conversations with real users. Prior work on user simulation has emphasized generating realistic user utterances, leaving unexplored their potential as a source of direct feedback on the assistant's responses. abstract: We present a two-year homogeneous optical monitoring campaign of three TeV-emitting high-synchrotron-peaked BL Lac objects, 1ES 1959+650, H 1426+428, and PG 1553+113, carried out with the Asiago Schmidt 67/92 cm telescope. TeV blazars are key targets in high-energy astrophysics, relevant for relativistic jet physics, particle acceleration, multiwavelength variability studies, and, in selected cases, multimessenger programmes. abstract: Crystallisation of calcium carbonate (CaCO$_3$) in aqueous solutions is essential for carbon dioxide sequestration and the sustainable production of calcium carbonate materials, which are widely used in industry and increasingly explored for novel applications. While crystallisation is often analysed within the framework of classical nucleation theory, CaCO$_3$ and other ionic crystals often form through amorphous precursor phases, motivating the need for alternative descriptions. title: Measurement of Born cross sections of $e^+e^-\to pK^{-}\barΣ^{0}$ + c.c. at $\sqrt{s}$ = 3.5-4.9 GeV and partial wave analysis at $\sqrt{s}$ = 3.773 GeV
abstract: Using $e^+e^-$ collision data collected by the BESIII detector at BEPCII corresponding to a total integrated luminosity of 44.6 $\rm fb^{-1}$, we present the first measurement of the Born cross sections for the process $e^+e^-\to pK^{-}\barΣ^{0}$ + c.c. at fifty-six center-of-mass energies between 3.51 and 4.95~GeV. title: GLIO2: A GPU-Parallelized Tightly-Coupled LiDAR-Inertial-GNSS System for Robust and Real-Time Global Localization and Mapping
abstract: Globally consistent, real-time state estimation in large-scale, perceptually degraded environments is essential for autonomous vehicles and aerial robots, and requires fusing LiDAR, inertial, and GNSS measurements. Existing fusion methods, however, share a scan-to-map front-end with two failure modes. First, each scan is aligned to an incrementally built map that drifts under degeneracy, and once the estimate diverges the error is irrecoverable.
